topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: AI in Daily Life
topics.description: Spotting AI in daily life: face unlock on a phone, video recommendations, spelling auto-correct, automatic doors that detect people; technology that seems to 'know' things
evidence: Identify at least five examples of AI in their daily life
Explain that these technologies use patterns and data, not magic or real thinking
Describe one way AI makes their life easier and one time it might not work perfectly
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} point out several things they use every day — like auto-correct or face unlock — and explain that these are examples of AI?
topics.descriptionZh: 发现生活中的AI（人工智能）：手机面部解锁、视频推荐、拼写自动纠错、感应行人的自动门；这些看似能够“懂得”事物的技术。
evidenceZh: 识别日常生活中至少五个AI（人工智能）的例子
解释这些技术使用的是模式与数据，而不是魔法或真正的思考
描述一种AI让生活更便利的方式，以及一次它可能无法完美运作的情况
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否指出他们每天使用的几样事物——比如自动纠错或面部解锁——并解释这些都是AI（人工智能）的例子？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: Computers in Everyday Life
topics.description: Identifying computers in everyday life — not just laptops but phones, tablets, smart speakers, traffic lights, washing machines; what makes something a computer
evidence: Point out at least five everyday objects that contain computers
Explain what all computers have in common (they follow instructions and process information)
Sort a set of objects into 'contains a computer' and 'does not contain a computer'
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} look around your home and point out at least five things that have a computer inside them, including ones that don't look like traditional computers?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别日常生活中的计算机——不仅仅是笔记本电脑，还包括手机、平板电脑、智能音箱、交通信号灯、洗衣机等；探讨是什么让一个物体成为计算机。
evidenceZh: 指出至少五件包含计算机的日常物品
解释所有计算机的共同点（它们遵循指令并处理信息）
将一组物品分类为‘包含计算机’和‘不包含计算机’
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否环顾一下你的家，指出至少五件内部有计算机的物品，包括那些看起来不像传统计算机的物品？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: Real-World Robots
topics.description: What a robot really is — not the sci-fi version; robots in factories, robot vacuum cleaners, robot arms in surgery; that robots follow instructions given by people
evidence: Describe what a robot is (a machine that follows instructions to do a task)
Name at least three real robots and what they do
Explain that robots are not alive and do not have feelings — they follow instructions people wrote
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a robot vacuum cleaner, could they explain how it's different from a person cleaning — that it follows instructions rather than thinking for itself?
topics.descriptionZh: 机器人真正的样子——不是科幻作品中的版本；工厂里的机器人、扫地机器人、手术中的机械臂；机器人是按照人类给出的指令来工作的。
evidenceZh: 描述什么是机器人（一种按照指令完成任务的机器）
列举至少三种真实的机器人并说明它们的作用
解释机器人不是活的，也没有感情——它们只是执行人们编写的指令
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到一个扫地机器人，他们能解释它和人打扫卫生的区别吗——即它是按照指令工作，而不是自己思考？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: Smart Versus Not-Smart Devices
topics.description: Sorting objects into 'smart' (can sense and respond) and 'not smart' (just sits there); a toaster vs a smart speaker; introduction to the idea that some machines can sense and respond to the world
evidence: Sort a set of objects into 'smart' (responds to input) and 'not smart' (does the same thing every time)
Explain what makes a smart speaker different from a regular radio
Give an example of a machine that senses something and responds (automatic door, motion-sensor light)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain the difference between a normal light switch and one that turns on automatically when you walk into a room?
topics.descriptionZh: 将物品分为“智能”（能感知并做出反应）和“非智能”（只能待在那里不动）两类；对比烤面包机和智能音箱；初步引入一些机器能够感知并对周围世界做出反应的概念。
evidenceZh: 将一组物品分为“智能”（能对输入做出反应）和“非智能”（每次都做同样的事情）两类
解释智能音箱与普通收音机有什么不同
举出一个能感知事物并做出反应的机器的例子（自动门、感应灯）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能解释一下普通电灯开关和走进房间时会自动亮起的开关有什么区别吗？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: Step-by-Step Instructions
topics.description: Step-by-step instructions for everyday tasks (making a sandwich, brushing teeth); that if instructions are wrong or missing, things go wrong; computers follow instructions exactly
evidence: Write or describe step-by-step instructions for a simple everyday task
Predict what goes wrong if a step is missing or in the wrong order
Explain that a computer follows instructions exactly — it cannot guess what you meant
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} had to write instructions for making a jam sandwich so precise that even a robot could follow them, could they include every single step?
topics.descriptionZh: 日常任务的逐步指令（如制作三明治、刷牙）；如果指令错误或遗漏，事情就会出错；计算机会严格按照指令（算法 / Algorithms）执行
evidenceZh: 编写或描述完成一项简单日常任务的逐步指令
预测如果遗漏某个步骤或顺序错误会导致什么问题
解释计算机严格按照指令执行——它无法猜测你的真实意图
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 必须写出制作果酱三明治的指令，精确到连机器人也能照着做，他们能包含每一个微小的步骤吗？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: Voice Assistants and How They Work
topics.description: What happens when you talk to Alexa, Siri, or Google Assistant; they listen, try to understand, look up answers; sometimes they get it wrong; they are tools, not alive
evidence: Describe the steps that happen when you ask a voice assistant a question (it listens, processes words, finds an answer, speaks back)
Give an example of a time a voice assistant might get something wrong
Explain that a voice assistant is a computer program, not a person — it doesn't understand or feel
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} asked Alexa or Siri a question and got a wrong answer, could they explain why the voice assistant sometimes makes mistakes?
topics.nameZh: 语音助手及其工作原理
topics.descriptionZh: 当你和 Alexa、Siri 或 Google 助理（Google Assistant）说话时会发生什么；它们会倾听、尝试理解并查找答案；有时它们会出错；它们是工具，没有生命
evidenceZh: 描述向语音助手提问时发生的步骤（它会倾听、处理词语、寻找答案并用语音回复）
举一个语音助手可能会出错的例子
解释语音助手是一个计算机程序，不是真人——它不会真正理解事物，也没有感情
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 向 Alexa 或 Siri 提问却得到了错误的答案，他们能解释为什么语音助手有时会犯错吗？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: AI in Computer Games
topics.description: How computer game characters 'decide' what to do; simple rule-based AI vs learning AI; NPCs, difficulty adjustment; AI as the opponent in chess or board games
evidence: Explain how a computer opponent in a game decides its moves
Describe the difference between a game character that follows fixed rules and one that learns from the player
Give an example of AI making a game more fun (adjusting difficulty, generating levels)
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} plays a video game against the computer, could they explain how the game's characters 'decide' what to do?
topics.nameZh: 电子游戏中的AI（人工智能）
topics.descriptionZh: 电脑游戏角色如何“决定”它们的行动；简单的基于规则的AI（人工智能）与学习型AI（人工智能）的对比；非玩家角色（NPC），难度调整；AI（人工智能）作为国际象棋或棋盘游戏中的对手
evidenceZh: 解释游戏中的电脑对手是如何决定其走法的
描述遵循固定规则的游戏角色与能从玩家那里学习（进行学习）的游戏角色之间的区别
举一个AI（人工智能）让游戏变得更有趣的例子（如调整难度、生成关卡）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}玩电子游戏并与电脑对战时，他们能解释游戏中的角色是如何“决定”该做什么的吗？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: AI Mistakes and Limitations
topics.description: Machines make mistakes; they only know what they've been shown; bad training data leads to bad results; AI is not magic — just maths on data; showing edge cases and failures
evidence: Give an example of AI making a mistake (voice assistant mishearing, auto-correct error, wrong recommendation)
Explain that AI mistakes happen because of gaps or errors in training data
Describe why AI is not magic — it follows mathematical rules applied to data
topics.assessmentPrompt: If an AI incorrectly identified a picture of a muffin as a chihuahua, could {{name}} explain why that kind of mistake happens?
topics.nameZh: 人工智能的错误与局限性
topics.descriptionZh: 机器也会犯错；它们只认识学过的内容；糟糕的训练数据会导致糟糕的结果；人工智能不是魔法——它只是对数据进行数学（Maths）运算；展示一些边缘情况和失败的案例。
evidenceZh: 举一个人工智能犯错的例子（语音助手听错、自动纠错错误、推荐错误）
解释人工智能犯错是因为训练数据（Training data）存在缺失或错误
描述为什么人工智能不是魔法——它遵循应用于数据的数学（Mathematical）规则
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果人工智能把一张玛芬蛋糕的图片错误地识别成了吉娃娃，{{name}}能解释一下为什么会发生这种错误吗？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: Data and Information for Computers
topics.description: What data is: information that computers use — numbers, words, pictures, sounds; everything a computer knows comes from data that people give it
evidence: Define data as information stored in a computer (numbers, text, images, sounds)
Give at least three examples of data they create every day (photos, messages, search queries)
Explain that a computer only knows what it has been given — it has no knowledge of its own
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what 'data' means and give examples of data they create every time they use a phone or computer?
topics.descriptionZh: 什么是数据：计算机使用的信息——数字、文字、图片、声音；计算机所知道的一切都来自于人类提供给它的数据（data）。
evidenceZh: 将数据定义为存储在计算机中的信息（数字、文本、图像、声音）
举出至少三个他们每天产生的数据实例（照片、消息、搜索查询）
解释计算机只知道被输入给它的内容——它本身没有任何自主知识
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释一下“数据（data）”是什么意思，并举例说明他们每次使用手机或电脑时都会产生哪些数据吗？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: Humans Versus Machines
topics.description: Comparing human and machine capabilities: creativity, empathy, common sense vs speed, memory, repetition; the Turing Test (simplified); what makes humans unique
evidence: Name at least three things humans are better at than computers (creativity, empathy, common sense)
Name at least three things computers are better at than humans (speed, memory, repetitive tasks)
Describe the Turing Test in simple terms (can a computer fool a person into thinking it's human?)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what humans are still better at than computers and what computers can do that humans can't?
topics.descriptionZh: 比较人类和机器的能力：创造力、同理心、常识，对比速度、记忆力、重复性工作；简化版图灵测试（Turing Test）；让人类与众不同的独特之处
evidenceZh: 至少说出三件人类比电脑擅长的事情（创造力、同理心、常识）
至少说出三件电脑比人类擅长的事情（速度、记忆力、重复性任务）
用简单的话描述图灵测试（Turing Test）（电脑能不能骗过人类，让人以为它是真人？）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释一下人类在哪些方面依然比电脑强，以及电脑能做哪些人类做不到的事情吗？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: Machine Learning Basics
topics.description: How machine learning works at a conceptual level: show the computer many examples, it finds patterns, then it makes predictions about new things; hands-on experience with Teachable Machine or similar tool
evidence: Describe the three steps of machine learning in simple terms (give examples, find patterns, make predictions)
Train a simple model using a tool like Teachable Machine and describe what happened
Explain why showing more and better examples makes the model more accurate
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe how you teach a computer to recognise something — by showing it lots of examples until it spots the pattern?
topics.descriptionZh: 从概念层面了解机器学习 (Machine Learning) 是如何工作的：给计算机展示许多例子，让它寻找规律，然后对新鲜事物做出预测；使用 Teachable Machine 或类似工具进行动手实践。
evidenceZh: 用简单的语言描述机器学习的三个步骤（提供例子、寻找规律、做出预测）
使用 Teachable Machine 等工具训练一个简单的模型，并描述发生了什么
解释为什么展示更多、更好的例子能让模型变得更准确
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能描述一下你是如何教计算机识别事物的吗——通过给它展示大量例子，直到它发现其中的规律？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: Patterns and Classification
topics.description: Humans are great at spotting patterns; computers can learn to spot patterns too, but they need lots of examples; sorting and classification activities as the basis of machine learning
evidence: Sort a set of items into categories and explain the rules they used
Explain that computers learn patterns by looking at many examples
Describe why a computer needs more examples than a human to learn the same pattern
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you showed {{name}} pictures of cats and dogs, could they explain how a computer could learn to tell them apart — and why it would need many more pictures than a person would?
topics.descriptionZh: 人类非常擅长发现规律（Patterns）；计算机也能学习发现规律，但它们需要大量的示例；排序和分类活动是机器学习（Machine Learning）的基础。
evidenceZh: 将一组物品分门别类，并解释他们所使用的分类规则
解释计算机是如何通过观察大量示例来学习规律的
描述为什么计算机在学习同一规律时，需要比人类更多的示例
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你给 {{name}} 看一些猫和狗的图片，他们能解释计算机是如何学习区分它们的吗？——以及为什么计算机需要的图片数量比人多得多？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: Recommendation Systems and Filter Bubbles
topics.description: How recommendation systems work: YouTube, Netflix, and shop websites track what you click and find patterns; filter bubbles; the difference between helpful suggestions and manipulation
evidence: Explain how YouTube or Netflix decides what to suggest next
Describe what a 'filter bubble' is (only seeing things similar to what you already like)
Give one benefit and one risk of recommendation systems
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} understand why YouTube keeps suggesting similar videos to ones they've watched, and could they explain how the recommendation system works?
topics.nameZh: 推荐系统与过滤气泡 (Recommendation Systems and Filter Bubbles)
topics.descriptionZh: 推荐系统（Recommendation Systems）的工作原理：YouTube、Netflix 和购物网站会追踪您的点击行为并寻找规律；过滤气泡（Filter Bubbles）现象；以及有益的建议与操纵（Manipulation）之间的区别。
evidenceZh: 解释 YouTube 或 Netflix 是如何决定接下来推荐什么内容的
描述什么是“过滤气泡”（Filter Bubble）（即只能看到与自己已经喜欢的事物相似的内容）
说出推荐系统（Recommendation Systems）的一个益处和一个风险
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否理解为什么 YouTube 会不断推荐与他们看过的相似的视频，并且能否解释推荐系统（Recommendation System）的工作原理？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: AI and Fairness in Decisions
topics.description: Whether AI should make important decisions about people: jobs, loans, justice; who is responsible when AI makes unfair decisions; introduction to algorithmic fairness
evidence: Give an example of an important decision that AI might help make (hiring, medical diagnosis, loan approval)
Explain why letting AI make decisions about people can be risky if the system is biased
Suggest who should be responsible if an AI system makes an unfair decision
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learned that a computer program was deciding who gets a job interview, could they explain why that might be unfair and who should be responsible?
topics.nameZh: 人工智能与决策公平性
topics.descriptionZh: 人工智能是否应该对人们做出重要决策：就业、贷款、司法；当人工智能做出不公平决策时谁应承担责任；算法公平性（Algorithmic Fairness）简介
evidenceZh: 举一个人工智能可能协助做出的重要决策的例子（如招聘、医疗诊断、贷款审批）
解释如果系统存在偏见，让人工智能对人们做出决策为什么会存在风险
提出如果人工智能系统做出了不公平的决策，应该由谁来承担责任
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}得知一个计算机程序正在决定谁能获得工作面试机会，他们能否解释这为什么不公平，以及应该由谁来承担责任？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: AI and the Environment
topics.description: AI needs huge amounts of energy and water to train; data centres and their environmental cost; but AI can also help — predicting weather, monitoring deforestation, optimising energy; trade-offs
evidence: Explain that training AI models uses a lot of electricity and water
Give at least two examples of AI being used to help the environment
Describe the trade-off between AI's environmental cost and its environmental benefits
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain that AI needs a lot of energy to work but can also be used to help protect the environment, and discuss whether the trade-off is worth it?
topics.descriptionZh: 训练人工智能需要消耗大量的能源和水资源；数据中心 (data centres) 及其环境代价；但人工智能也能提供帮助——预测天气、监测森林砍伐 (deforestation)、优化能源；权衡利弊 (trade-offs)。
evidenceZh: 解释训练人工智能模型需要消耗大量的电力和水资源
列举至少两个利用人工智能保护环境的例子
描述人工智能的环境代价与环境效益之间的权衡 (trade-off)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释人工智能运行需要大量能源，但也能用于保护环境，并讨论这种权衡是否值得？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: AI and the Future of Work
topics.description: How AI is changing the world of work: some jobs disappear, new ones are created, many change; jobs AI can't do (yet); what skills matter in an AI world
evidence: Name at least two jobs that AI is changing or replacing and two new jobs AI has created
Explain why creativity, empathy, and problem-solving are skills that matter more in an AI world
Describe how AI might change a specific job they know about (teacher, doctor, farmer) without replacing it
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how AI might change the way people work in the future and which human skills will still be important?
topics.descriptionZh: 人工智能（AI）如何改变工作世界：一些工作消失，新工作产生，许多工作发生改变；人工智能（目前）还无法胜任的工作；在人工智能时代哪些技能至关重要
evidenceZh: 说出至少两种正在被人工智能改变或取代的工作，以及两种由人工智能创造的新工作
解释为什么在人工智能时代，创造力、同理心和解决问题的能力变得更加重要
描述人工智能将如何改变他们熟悉的一项具体工作（如教师、医生、农民），而不会完全取代它
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释人工智能将如何改变未来人们的工作方式，以及哪些人类技能仍然重要？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: AI Data Collection and Privacy
topics.description: What data AI systems collect about you; who has it and why it matters; cookies, tracking, smart speakers always listening; your data is valuable
evidence: Name at least three types of personal data that AI systems collect
Explain why personal data is valuable to companies
Describe one step they can take to protect their privacy online
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} understand that apps and websites collect information about what they do online, and could they explain why that matters?
topics.nameZh: 人工智能（AI）数据收集与隐私
topics.descriptionZh: 人工智能系统会收集你的哪些数据；谁拥有这些数据以及为什么这很重要；Cookie（网络追踪器）、网络追踪（Tracking）、智能音箱（Smart Speakers）随时监听；你的数据非常有价值
evidenceZh: 至少说出三种人工智能系统收集的个人数据类型
解释为什么个人数据对公司很有价值
描述一项他们可以在网上保护隐私的措施
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否理解应用程序和网站会收集他们在网上的行为信息，并且能否解释这为什么很重要？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: Bias in AI Systems
topics.description: If training data is biased, AI will be biased; examples: facial recognition working better for some skin tones, translation assuming gender; where bias comes from and whether we can fix it
evidence: Explain what bias in AI means using a real-world example
Describe how biased training data leads to biased AI results
Suggest one way to reduce bias in an AI system (use more diverse data, test with different groups)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain why an AI trained mostly on photos of light-skinned faces might not work as well for people with darker skin?
topics.nameZh: 人工智能系统中的偏见
topics.descriptionZh: 如果训练数据存在偏见，人工智能（AI）也会产生偏见；例如：人脸识别对某些肤色的识别效果更好，翻译软件会默认假设性别；探讨偏见的来源以及我们是否能够消除它。
evidenceZh: 用现实生活中的例子解释人工智能偏见是什么意思
描述存在偏见的训练数据是如何导致人工智能产生偏见结果的
提出一种减少人工智能系统偏见的方法（例如使用更多样化的数据，或对不同群体进行测试）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能解释一下为什么主要用浅色皮肤人脸照片训练出来的人工智能，在识别深色皮肤的人时效果可能没那么好吗？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: Deepfakes and AI-Generated Content
topics.description: Deepfakes, AI-generated images and text; how to spot them and why they matter; the importance of checking sources; not everything online is real
evidence: Explain what a deepfake is and give an example of AI-generated content
Describe at least two clues that might reveal an image or text was AI-generated
Explain why it matters that AI can create realistic fake content
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw an amazing photo online, would they think to question whether it might have been created by AI rather than captured by a camera?
topics.nameZh: 深度伪造与人工智能生成内容
topics.descriptionZh: 深度伪造、AI生成的图像和文本；如何识别它们及其重要性；核实信息来源的重要性；并非网络上的所有内容都是真实的
evidenceZh: 解释什么是深度伪造（Deepfake），并举一个AI生成内容的例子
描述至少两个可能表明图像或文本是AI生成的线索
解释为什么AI能够创建逼真的虚假内容是一件重要的事情
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在网上看到一张令人惊叹的照片，他们会想到质疑这张照片可能是由AI生成的，而不是用相机拍摄的吗？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: Designing Fair AI Rules
topics.description: Design thinking applied to AI ethics: if you were designing an AI system, what rules would you give it? Who should it help? What should it not be allowed to do?
evidence: Propose at least three rules for a hypothetical AI system they are designing
Explain why AI designers need to think about who might be harmed, not just who benefits
Describe one real example of AI being used responsibly and one where it was not
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was designing an AI assistant for their school, could they think of rules to make sure it was fair and helpful for everyone?
topics.descriptionZh: 将设计思维应用于人工智能伦理 (AI ethics)：如果你在设计一个AI系统，你会给它制定什么规则？它应该帮助谁？它不应该做什么？
evidenceZh: 为他们正在设计的假设性AI系统提出至少三条规则
解释为什么AI设计者需要考虑谁可能会受到伤害，而不仅仅是谁会受益
描述一个负责任地使用AI的真实案例，以及一个没有负责任地使用AI的案例
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 正在为学校设计一个AI助手，他们能想出规则来确保它对每个人都公平且有帮助吗？

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: The Future of AI
topics.description: What AI might do in 10 years; what we want it to do and what we're worried about; children as future designers and decision-makers about AI; hopeful, empowered framing
evidence: Describe at least two ways AI might be used in the future that don't exist yet
Explain one thing they would want AI to do and one thing they would want it not to do
Describe why it matters that young people understand AI — because they will shape how it is used
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} have a thoughtful conversation about what they'd want AI to do in the future and what they'd be worried about?
topics.descriptionZh: 探讨人工智能在未来10年可能会做什么；我们希望它做什么以及我们担忧什么；儿童作为人工智能未来的设计师和决策者；采用充满希望且赋能的视角。
evidenceZh: 描述至少两种未来可能应用但目前尚不存在的AI（人工智能）使用方式
解释一件他们希望AI（人工智能）去做的事，以及一件他们不希望AI去做的事
描述为什么年轻人理解AI（人工智能）很重要——因为他们将塑造AI的使用方式
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否就他们希望AI（人工智能）在未来做什么以及他们担忧什么进行深思熟虑的对话？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Reading for Meaning
topics.description: Understand that reading is about making meaning, not just saying words correctly — a text that can be decoded but not understood has not been read
evidence: Simple View of Reading (Gough & Tunmer)
reading comprehension research on comprehension-decoding separation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads something aloud correctly but then can't tell you what it was about, do they recognise that reading means understanding — not just saying the words?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解阅读的核心在于建构意义，而不仅仅是正确地朗读单词——一篇能够解码（decode）但无法理解的文章，就不能算是真正读过。
evidenceZh: 阅读的简单观（Simple View of Reading，Gough & Tunmer）
关于理解与解码（comprehension-decoding）分离的阅读理解研究
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 能正确地大声朗读一段内容，但随后却无法告诉你文章讲了什么，他们是否认识到阅读意味着理解——而不仅仅是读出单词？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Monitoring Comprehension
topics.description: Notice the difference between decoding words and actually understanding them — recognise when you've read the words but not grasped the meaning, and do something about it
evidence: comprehension monitoring research
Metacognitive Monitoring in Reading Comprehension (MDPI 2024)
topics.assessmentPrompt: After {{name}} reads a paragraph or listens to an explanation, do they notice when they haven't really understood it — rather than just carrying on as if they had?
topics.descriptionZh: 注意解码字词与真正理解其含义之间的区别——识别出何时只是读出了字词却未理解其意义，并采取相应的补救措施。
evidenceZh: 理解监控研究
阅读理解中的元认知监控 (Metacognitive Monitoring) (MDPI 2024)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}读完一段话或听完一段解释后，他们是否能察觉到自己并没有真正理解，而不是假装懂了继续往下进行？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Author's word choices
topics.description: Recognise how an author's deliberate choices — of words, structure, tone, and perspective — create particular effects on you as a reader
evidence: authorial awareness research
Understanding Author's Purpose (Firkins)
collaborative multilayered text interpretation in 5-8 year olds
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads a book or article, do they ever notice and comment on why the author chose to write it a certain way — and what effect that has on them as a reader?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解作者的刻意选择（如用词、结构、语气和视角）如何对读者产生特定的影响。
evidenceZh: 作者意识研究（authorial awareness research）
理解作者意图（Firkins）
5-8岁儿童的合作式多层文本解读（collaborative multilayered text interpretation in 5-8 year olds）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}阅读书籍或文章时，他们是否会注意到并谈论作者为什么选择以特定的方式进行写作，以及这种写作方式对他们作为读者产生了怎样的影响？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Inference vs Explicit Meaning
topics.description: Distinguish between what a text explicitly says and what you have inferred, assumed, or read in — knowing which is which is fundamental to honest comprehension
evidence: inference vs literal comprehension development research
online inference making and comprehension monitoring (PMC 2021)
topics.assessmentPrompt: After {{name}} reads a story or article, can they tell you which parts they actually read in the text and which parts they worked out or assumed for themselves?
topics.nameZh: 推理与明确含义 (Inference vs Explicit Meaning)
topics.descriptionZh: 区分文本字面上明确表达的内容与你所推理、假设或自行代入的内容——弄清两者的区别是达成客观理解 (honest comprehension) 的基础。
evidenceZh: 推理与字面理解 (literal comprehension) 发展研究
在线推理生成与阅读理解监控 (online inference making and comprehension monitoring, PMC 2021)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在{{name}}读完一个故事或文章后，他们能告诉你哪些部分是文本中实际写明的，哪些部分是他们自己推理或假设出来的吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Knowing What You Don't Know
topics.description: Monitor your own vocabulary gaps — notice words you half-know, distinguish confident from uncertain knowledge, and develop strategies to resolve the uncertainty
evidence: Noticing Unfamiliar Words Assessment research (grade 2+)
word consciousness and vocabulary metacognition research
Building Word Knowledge e-Book (PMC 2019)
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} comes across a word they half-know — where they can guess the meaning but aren't sure — do they notice that gap and do something about it, like looking it up or asking?
topics.descriptionZh: 监测自身的词汇盲区——察觉一知半解的单词，区分确定掌握与不确定理解的知识，并制定策略以消除不确定性
evidenceZh: “察觉生词”评估研究（Noticing Unfamiliar Words Assessment research, 二年级及以上）
词汇意识（word consciousness）与词汇元认知（vocabulary metacognition）研究
《构建词汇知识》电子书（Building Word Knowledge e-Book, PMC 2019）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 遇到一个一知半解的单词——能猜出意思但不完全确定时，他们是否会注意到这个知识缺口并采取行动，比如查阅词典或向他人请教？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Reviewing Own Writing
topics.description: Evaluate whether your own writing achieves the effect you intended on a reader — go beyond checking for correctness to asking whether it actually works
evidence: writing self-evaluation research grades 3-5
metacognitive awareness of writing (Frontiers 2025)
topics.assessmentPrompt: After {{name}} writes something — a story, a letter, a persuasive piece — do they think about whether it would have the effect they wanted on a reader, not just whether the spelling is right?
topics.descriptionZh: 评估自己的写作是否达到了对读者预期的效果——不仅要检查正确性，还要思考它是否真正起作用。
evidenceZh: 3-5年级写作自我评估研究 (writing self-evaluation research grades 3-5)
写作元认知意识 (metacognitive awareness of writing, Frontiers 2025)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在{{name}}写完一些内容（如故事、信件或劝说性文章）之后，他们是否会思考这是否会对读者产生他们想要达到的效果，而不仅仅是检查拼写是否正确？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Reflecting on Your Language Use
topics.description: Reflect on yourself as a language user — how your reading, writing, and speaking shift across audiences, purposes, and contexts, and where you want to develop further
evidence: metalinguistic awareness development
register and audience awareness research
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} notice how they communicate differently in different situations — writing for school versus texting a friend, or speaking in a debate versus chatting at home — and can they explain why those differences matter?
topics.descriptionZh: 反思自己作为语言使用者的表现——思考你的阅读、写作和口语表达如何因受众、目的和语境的不同而发生变化，以及你希望在未来进一步发展哪些方面。
evidenceZh: 元语言意识发展 (metalinguistic awareness development)
语域与受众意识研究 (register and audience awareness research)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否能注意到他们在不同情境下的沟通方式有所不同——例如为学校写作业与给朋友发短信，或者在辩论中发言与在家里聊天——并且能否解释这些差异为何重要？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Building sentences
topics.description: Understand that words combine to make sentences — a sentence expresses a complete thought; produce and expand complete sentences in speech and writing
evidence: Distinguish between complete sentences and fragments
Compose a complete sentence with a subject and verb
Expand a simple sentence by adding detail
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} says something like "The dog", can they tell you that's not a complete sentence — and add words to make it say something like "The dog ran fast"?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解词语可以组合成句子——句子能够表达一个完整的意思；能够在口语表达和书面写作中生成并扩充完整的句子
evidenceZh: 区分完整句子与句子片段（残缺句）
使用主语和谓语构造完整的句子
通过添加细节扩充简单句
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}说了类似“那只狗”（The dog）这样的话，他们能指出这不是一个完整的句子，并添加词语使其变成类似“那只狗跑得很快”（The dog ran fast）这样的完整句子吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Spaces Between Words
topics.description: Separate words with spaces in writing; understand that spaces mark word boundaries in print
evidence: Leave clear finger-spaces between words when writing
Count the number of words in a written sentence by identifying spaces
Correct writing that has missing spaces between words
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is writing a short message, can they leave a space between each word — so the reader can tell where one word ends and the next begins?
topics.descriptionZh: 在书写时使用空格分隔单词；理解在书面印刷中，空格标志着单词的边界
evidenceZh: 书写时在单词之间留出清晰的“一指宽”空格
通过识别空格来数出书写句子中的单词数量
改正书写中单词之间缺失空格的情况
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 正在写一条短信息，他们能在每个单词之间留出空格吗——以便读者能分辨出一个单词在哪里结束，下一个单词在哪里开始？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Basic Nouns & Verbs
topics.description: Use frequently occurring nouns (people, places, things) and verbs (action words) appropriately in speech and writing
evidence: Use common nouns accurately in sentences (e.g. 'dog', 'school', 'book')
Use action verbs appropriately (e.g. 'run', 'eat', 'play')
Identify nouns and verbs in simple sentences when prompted
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} talks or writes about everyday things — like "the dog runs" or "Mum cooks dinner" — do they use the right kind of words for things (nouns) and actions (verbs) without mixing them up?
topics.descriptionZh: 在口语和写作中正确使用常见的名词（Nouns，即人物、地点、事物）和动词（Verbs，即动作词）
evidenceZh: 在句子中准确使用普通名词（例如“狗”、“学校”、“书”）
恰当地使用动作动词（例如“跑”、“吃”、“玩”）
在提示下识别简单句中的名词和动词
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 谈论或书写日常事物时——比如“狗在跑”或“妈妈做晚饭”——他们能否正确使用表示事物（名词）和动作（动词）的词汇而不混淆？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Capitals for Names, Days and I
topics.description: Use capital letters for proper nouns (names of people, places) the days of the week, and the personal pronoun 'I'
evidence: Capitalise names of people and places consistently in writing
Write the pronoun 'I' as a capital letter
Capitalise days of the week (e.g. 'Monday')
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is writing their friend's name or the name of a town, do they automatically start it with a capital letter — and do they write the word 'I' with a capital when talking about themselves?
topics.nameZh: 人名、星期和“I”的大写字母
topics.descriptionZh: 对专有名词（人名、地名）、星期以及人称代词“I”使用大写字母。
evidenceZh: 在书写中始终将人名和地名首字母大写
将代词“I”写为大写字母
将星期名称首字母大写（例如“Monday”）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}写朋友的名字或城镇名称时，他们会自动将首字母大写吗？在谈论自己时，他们会把“I”写成大写吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Grammar words: letter, word, sentence
topics.description: Use basic grammatical terminology when discussing reading and writing: letter, capital letter, word, singular, plural, sentence, punctuation, full stop, question mark, exclamation mark
evidence: Name punctuation marks correctly when pointed out in text
Use terms like 'capital letter' and 'full stop' when editing writing
Explain what a 'sentence' is using the correct term
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you point to a full stop or a question mark in a book, can {{name}} tell you what it's called and what it's for — and do they know the difference between a word and a sentence?
topics.nameZh: 语法词汇：字母、单词、句子
topics.descriptionZh: 在讨论阅读和写作时使用基本的语法术语：字母（letter）、大写字母（capital letter）、单词（word）、单数（singular）、复数（plural）、句子（sentence）、标点符号（punctuation）、句号（full stop）、问号（question mark）、感叹号（exclamation mark）
evidenceZh: 在文本中被指出时，能正确说出标点符号的名称
在修改写作内容时，能使用“大写字母”和“句号”等术语
能使用正确的术语解释什么是“句子”
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果您在书中指着一个句号或问号，{{name}}能告诉您它叫什么名字以及它的用途吗——并且他们知道单词和句子之间的区别吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Joining Words with 'And'
topics.description: Join words and clauses using the conjunction 'and' to create longer sentences
evidence: Combine two simple sentences using 'and' (e.g. 'I like cats and dogs')
Join two related clauses with 'and' (e.g. 'We went to the park and we played')
Use 'and' in lists of items within a sentence
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is telling you about their day, can they write two ideas joined together with the word 'and' — like "I had lunch and then we played outside"?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用连词“和”（and）连接词语和分句，以构建更长的句子
evidenceZh: 使用“和”（and）组合两个简单句（例如：“我喜欢猫和狗”）
用“和”（and）连接两个相关的分句（例如：“我们去了公园并且玩耍了”）
在句中列举多项事物时使用“和”（and）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 向你讲述他们的一天时，他们能用“和”（and）把两个想法连起来写吗——比如“我吃了午饭并且我们在外面玩”？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Prepositions
topics.description: Understand and use the most frequently occurring prepositions of location and direction (e.g. to, from, in, out, on, off, for, by, with)
evidence: Use prepositions correctly in sentences (e.g. 'on the table', 'under the bed')
Follow instructions involving prepositions (e.g. 'Put the book on the shelf')
Describe positions using prepositional phrases
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} to describe where something is — like where the cup is on the table — can they use little words like "on", "under", "next to", or "by" correctly?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解并运用最常见的表示位置和方向的介词（如 to, from, in, out, on, off, for, by, with）
evidenceZh: 在句子中正确使用介词（例如：'on the table' 在桌上，'under the bed' 在床下）
遵循包含介词的指令（例如：'把书放在书架上'）
使用介词短语描述位置
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你让 {{name}} 描述某个物品的位置——比如杯子在桌子上的哪里——他们能正确使用 'on'（在……上面）、'under'（在……下面）、'next to'（在……旁边）或 'by'（靠近）这类词吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Question Words
topics.description: Understand and use question words (who, what, where, when, why, how) to form and answer questions
evidence: Ask questions using appropriate question words
Answer who, what, where, when questions about familiar topics
Recognise that question words signal a question is being asked
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to find out something — like where you put their shoes or why the sky is blue — can they start their question with the right word, like "where" or "why"?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解并运用疑问词（who, what, where, when, why, how）来提出和回答问题。
evidenceZh: 使用恰当的疑问词进行提问
能够回答关于熟悉话题的 who（谁）、what（什么）、where（哪里）、when（何时）等疑问句
能够识别出疑问词代表正在提出一个问题
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 想要弄清楚某件事——比如你把他们的鞋子放在哪里（where），或者为什么天空是蓝色的（why）——他们能用正确的疑问词（如“哪里”或“为什么”）来开头提问吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Regular Plural Nouns
topics.description: Form and use regular plural nouns orally and in writing by adding -s or -es; understand that plural means more than one
evidence: Say and write correct plural forms (e.g. 'one cat, two cats'; 'one wish, two wishes')
Choose -s or -es correctly based on the ending sound
Explain that plural nouns name more than one
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you point to a picture of one cat and then several cats, can {{name}} tell you the correct word for more than one — and write it with the right ending, like "cats" or "boxes"?
topics.nameZh: 规则复数名词 (Regular Plural Nouns)
topics.descriptionZh: 通过在词尾添加 -s 或 -es，在口语和书面表达中正确构成并使用规则复数名词；理解复数 (plural) 表示“不止一个”的含义。
evidenceZh: 能说出并写出正确的复数形式（例如：'one cat, two cats'；'one wish, two wishes'）
能根据词尾发音正确选择添加 -s 或 -es
能解释复数名词 (plural nouns) 用来表示“不止一个”的事物
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果您指着一只猫的图片，然后再指着几只猫的图片，{{name}} 能告诉您表示“不止一个”的正确单词吗——并且能用正确的词尾拼写出来，比如 'cats' 或 'boxes'？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Starting and Ending Sentences
topics.description: Begin sentences with a capital letter and end them with the appropriate mark (full stop, question mark, or exclamation mark); recognise and name end punctuation
evidence: Write sentences beginning with a capital letter
Choose and use the correct end punctuation for statements, questions, and exclamations
Identify and name full stops, question marks, and exclamation marks when reading
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes a sentence like "the cat sat on the mat", do they remember to use a capital letter at the start and a full stop at the end — without needing a reminder?
topics.descriptionZh: 句子开头使用大写字母，结尾使用适当的标点符号（句号、问号或感叹号）；识别并说出句末标点的名称
evidenceZh: 书写以大写字母开头的句子
为陈述句、疑问句和感叹句选择并使用正确的句末标点
在阅读时识别并说出句号、问号和感叹号的名称
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 写出像 "the cat sat on the mat" 这样的句子时，他们能否记住在句首使用大写字母，并在句末使用句号——而无需他人提醒？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Apostrophes: Contraction and Possession
topics.description: Use apostrophes in writing for both contraction (marking omitted letters) and singular possession, distinguishing the two uses
evidence: Use apostrophes correctly in both 'don't' and 'Sam's bag' within the same piece of writing
Explain the difference between apostrophe for contraction and apostrophe for possession
Correct misplaced or missing apostrophes in a set of sentences
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes a word like "don't" or "it's", do they put the apostrophe in the right place — and can they also write something like "the dog's bowl" to show the bowl belongs to the dog?
topics.descriptionZh: 在写作中使用撇号来表示缩写（标记省略的字母）和单数所有格，并能区分这两种用法。
evidenceZh: 在同一篇写作中，能正确使用撇号拼写“don't”和“Sam's bag”。
解释用于缩写的撇号和用于表示所有格的撇号之间的区别。
纠正一组句子中放错位置或缺失的撇号。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 写下像“don't”或“it's”这样的词时，他们能把撇号放在正确的位置吗？他们还能写出像“the dog's bowl”这样的词组，以表明碗是属于狗的吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Commas in lists
topics.description: Use commas to separate items in a list within a sentence (e.g., 'I bought apples, bananas, and oranges')
evidence: Write a sentence containing a list of 3+ items separated by commas: 'I bought apples, bananas, and oranges'
Identify where commas should go in an unpunctuated list sentence
Explain that commas separate items in a list so the reader knows each item
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} writes a sentence listing three or more things — like the items they'd pack for a picnic — do they put commas between each item in the list?
topics.descriptionZh: 在句子中使用逗号（commas）分隔列举的各项（例如英文中的 'I bought apples, bananas, and oranges'）
evidenceZh: 写一个包含3个或更多项目的句子，并用逗号分隔这些项目（例如：'I bought apples, bananas, and oranges'）
找出在缺少标点的列举句中逗号应该加在什么位置
解释在列举时逗号的作用是分隔各项，以便读者能清楚分辨出每一个项目
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 写了一个列举三件或更多事物的句子——比如他们去野餐要打包的物品——他们是否会在每一项之间加上逗号（commas）？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Determiners and articles
topics.description: Use determiners (articles a/an/the and demonstratives this/that/these/those) correctly before nouns
evidence: Use 'a' before consonant sounds and 'an' before vowel sounds correctly: 'a ball', 'an apple'
Distinguish 'this/these' (near) from 'that/those' (far) when pointing to objects
Select the correct article (a/an/the) to complete a sentence
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes about something nearby versus something far away, do they use the right word — saying "this book" for one in their hand and "that book" for one across the room?
topics.descriptionZh: 在名词前正确使用限定词（包括冠词 a/an/the 和指示词 this/that/these/those）
evidenceZh: 在辅音发音前正确使用 'a'，在元音发音前正确使用 'an'：'a ball'，'an apple'
指代物体时，能区分近处的 'this/these' 和远处的 'that/those'
选择正确的冠词（a/an/the）来补全句子
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 描写附近的事物与远处的事物时，他们是否使用了正确的词——对于手中的书说“this book”，对于房间另一头的书说“that book”？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Expanded noun phrases
topics.description: Use expanded noun phrases to describe and specify, adding adjectives and other modifiers before a noun (e.g., 'the blue butterfly', 'the old, creaky door')
evidence: Expand 'the cat' into 'the fluffy black cat' by adding adjectives
Use noun phrases with two or more modifiers in independent writing
Choose precise adjectives to make a noun phrase more vivid: e.g., 'a tiny, shivering kitten'
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} describes something in writing — like a pet or a toy — do they add extra describing words, such as "the small, fluffy rabbit" rather than just "the rabbit"?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用扩展名词短语进行描述和具体说明，在名词前添加形容词和其他修饰语（例如：‘蓝色的蝴蝶’、‘破旧且吱呀作响的门’）
evidenceZh: 通过添加形容词将‘猫’扩展为‘毛茸茸的黑猫’
在独立写作中使用带有两个或更多修饰语的名词短语
选择精准的形容词使名词短语更加生动：例如‘一只娇小的、瑟瑟发抖的小猫’
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}在写作中描述某物（如宠物或玩具）时，他们是否会添加额外的描述性词语，例如说‘那只小小的、毛茸茸的兔子’而不是仅仅说‘那只兔子’？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Four Types of Sentences
topics.description: Understand and use the four sentence types — statement, question, exclamation, and command — recognising how grammatical patterns indicate sentence function
evidence: Write or identify a statement, question, exclamation, and command from a set of sentences
Match each sentence type to its correct end punctuation mark
Transform a statement into a question or command on request
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} spot the difference between a question ("Are you hungry?") and a command ("Eat your dinner!") — and write each type of sentence using the right punctuation at the end?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解并使用四种基本句型——陈述句（statement）、疑问句（question）、感叹句（exclamation）和祈使句（command）——并认识语法模式如何体现句子功能。
evidenceZh: 从一组句子中写出或识别出陈述句、疑问句、感叹句和祈使句
将每种句型与其正确的句末标点符号进行匹配
根据要求将陈述句转换为疑问句或祈使句
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否分辨疑问句（“你饿了吗？”）和祈使句（“快吃晚饭！”）的区别——并写出每种句型，在句末使用正确的标点符号？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Grammar Terms: Nouns, Verbs and Tense
topics.description: Use and understand Year 2 grammatical terminology in discussion: noun, noun phrase, statement, question, exclamation, command, compound, suffix, adjective, adverb, verb, tense (past/present), apostrophe, comma
evidence: Use the term 'noun phrase' when discussing expanded noun phrases in own writing
Identify adjectives, adverbs, and verbs in sentences using correct terminology
Explain what 'tense' means and give an example of past and present tense
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} to point out a noun, a verb, or an adjective in a sentence from their reading book, can they find one and explain what it does in the sentence?
topics.nameZh: 语法术语：名词、动词与时态
topics.descriptionZh: 在讨论中使用并理解二年级（Year 2）语法术语：名词（noun）、名词短语（noun phrase）、陈述句（statement）、疑问句（question）、感叹句（exclamation）、祈使句（command）、复合词/复合句（compound）、后缀（suffix）、形容词（adjective）、副词（adverb）、动词（verb）、时态（tense）（过去时/现在时）、撇号（apostrophe）、逗号（comma）
evidenceZh: 在讨论自己写作中的扩展名词短语时，使用“名词短语”（noun phrase）这一术语
使用正确的术语识别句子中的形容词（adjective）、副词（adverb）和动词（verb）
解释“时态”（tense）的含义，并给出过去时（past tense）和现在时（present tense）的例子
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你让{{name}}指出他们阅读书中某句话里的一个名词（noun）、动词（verb）或形容词（adjective），他们能找出来并解释它在句子中的作用吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Past, Present and Progressive Tense
topics.description: Use verbs to convey past and present tense correctly and consistently, including the progressive form (e.g., she is drumming, he was shouting), understanding how tense indicates time
evidence: Write a passage consistently in past tense without switching to present
Use progressive forms correctly: 'was running', 'is jumping' to show ongoing actions
Identify verbs in a sentence and change them from past to present tense or vice versa
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is writing about something that happened yesterday versus something happening right now, do they change the verb — for example, writing "she jumped" for the past and "she is jumping" for right now?
topics.nameZh: 过去时、现在时与进行时
topics.descriptionZh: 正确且连贯地使用动词来表达过去时和现在时，包括进行时（Progressive tense）形式（例如：she is drumming, he was shouting），并理解时态如何表示时间。
evidenceZh: 连贯地使用过去时撰写段落，不切换至现在时
正确使用进行时形式：'was running'、'is jumping'来表示正在进行的动作
识别句子中的动词，并将其从过去时改为现在时，或反之
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 描写昨天发生的事情与此时此刻正在发生的事情时，他们是否会改变动词——例如，用“she jumped”表示过去，用“she is jumping”表示现在？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Pronouns
topics.description: Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns correctly (e.g., I/me/my, they/them/their, anyone/everything), replacing nouns to avoid repetition
evidence: Replace a repeated noun with a pronoun: 'The dog was happy. He wagged his tail.'
Use I/me correctly in subject and object position in a sentence
Choose the correct possessive pronoun (my/his/her/their) to match the noun it replaces
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} retells a story or describes what a friend did, do they use words like "he", "she", "they", or "his" correctly — instead of repeating the person's name every single time?
topics.descriptionZh: 正确使用人称代词 (personal pronouns)、物主代词 (possessive pronouns) 和不定代词 (indefinite pronouns)（例如：I/me/my、they/them/their、anyone/everything），通过替代名词来避免重复。
evidenceZh: 用代词替换重复的名词：‘小狗很开心。它摇了摇它的尾巴。’
在句子中正确使用‘我’ (I/me) 作主语和宾语。
选择正确的物主代词 (possessive pronoun)（my/his/her/their）以匹配其所替代的名词。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 复述故事或描述朋友做了什么时，他们是否能正确使用‘他’ (he)、‘她’ (she)、‘他们’ (they) 或‘他的’ (his) 等词——而不是每次都重复那个人的名字？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Subject-verb agreement
topics.description: Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in sentences, maintaining subject-verb agreement (e.g., 'He hops' vs 'We hop')
evidence: Write 'The dog runs' (singular) and 'The dogs run' (plural) with correct verb agreement
Correct subject-verb agreement errors in sentences: fix 'The children plays' to 'The children play'
Choose the correct verb form to match a singular or plural subject in a gap-fill exercise
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} writes "she hop" or "we hops", do they catch the mistake — and can they fix it to "she hops" and "we hop" so the subject and verb match?
topics.descriptionZh: 在句子中使用单数和复数名词并搭配相应的动词，保持主谓一致（例如，'He hops' 与 'We hop' 的区别）。
evidenceZh: 正确搭配动词，写出 'The dog runs'（单数）和 'The dogs run'（复数）。
纠正句子中的主谓一致错误：将 'The children plays' 修改为 'The children play'。
在填空题中选择正确的动词形式，以匹配单数或复数主语。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 写出 'she hop' 或 'we hops'，他们能发现这个错误吗？并且能将其修改为 'she hops' 和 'we hop' 以确保主谓一致吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Subordinate clauses
topics.description: Use subordination (when, if, that, because) and co-ordination (or, and, but) to join clauses and create compound and complex sentences
evidence: Write 'I stayed inside because it was raining' using a subordinating conjunction
Use 'but' and 'or' to join ideas: 'I wanted to play but it was raining'
Use 'when' and 'if' clauses in writing: 'If it stops raining, we can go outside'
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes a story or a message, can they join two ideas with words like "because", "but", "when", or "if" — rather than writing every thought as a short separate sentence?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用从属连词（when, if, that, because）和并列连词（or, and, but）来连接分句，从而构建并列句（compound sentences）和复合句（complex sentences）。
evidenceZh: 使用从属连词（subordinating conjunction）造句：‘我待在室内，因为下雨了’（I stayed inside because it was raining）。
使用‘but’（但是）和‘or’（或者）连接想法：‘我想出去玩，但是下雨了’（I wanted to play but it was raining）。
在写作中使用‘when’（当……时）和‘if’（如果）引导的从句：‘如果雨停了，我们就可以去外面’（If it stops raining, we can go outside）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 写故事或留言时，他们能否使用像‘因为’（because）、‘但是’（but）、‘当……时’（when）或‘如果’（if）这样的词语将两个想法连接起来，而不是将每个想法都写成简短的独立句子？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Adjectives vs adverbs
topics.description: Use adjectives and adverbs correctly, choosing between them depending on whether a noun or verb/adjective is being modified (e.g., 'She ran quickly' vs 'She is quick')
evidence: Choose the correct form: 'The dog is (slow/slowly)' vs 'The dog walks (slow/slowly)'
Identify whether a word is modifying a noun (adjective) or a verb (adverb) in a given sentence
Expand sentences by adding both an adjective and an adverb: 'The tall boy ran quickly'
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} writes "she ran quick" instead of "she ran quickly", can they spot that they need an adverb to describe the running — and fix it themselves?
topics.descriptionZh: 正确使用形容词和副词，根据被修饰的是名词还是动词或形容词来准确选择（例如：'She ran quickly' 与 'She is quick' 的区别）
evidenceZh: 选择正确的形式：'The dog is (slow/slowly)' 与 'The dog walks (slow/slowly)'
在给定的句子中，识别某个词是修饰名词（形容词）还是修饰动词（副词）
通过同时添加形容词和副词来扩展句子：'The tall boy ran quickly'
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 写了 "she ran quick" 而不是 "she ran quickly"，他们能发现描述跑步动作需要使用副词，并自己纠正过来吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Choosing A or An
topics.description: Use the correct form of the indefinite article — 'a' before words beginning with a consonant sound and 'an' before words beginning with a vowel sound (e.g., a rock, an open box, an hour, a unicorn)
evidence: Choose 'a' or 'an' correctly before nouns beginning with consonant or vowel sounds (e.g., 'a ball', 'an egg', 'an umbrella')
Apply the rule to tricky words where spelling and sound differ (e.g., 'an hour' because /h/ is silent, 'a uniform' because /juː/ starts with a consonant sound)
Correct errors in a/an usage in given sentences (e.g., change 'a orange' to 'an orange')
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes, do they automatically choose "a" before a word that starts with a consonant sound and "an" before a vowel sound — like "a cat" but "an apple" or "an hour"?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用正确的不定冠词形式——在辅音音素开头的单词前使用 'a'，在元音音素开头的单词前使用 'an'（例如：a rock, an open box, an hour, a unicorn）。
evidenceZh: 在以辅音或元音音素开头的名词前正确选择 'a' 或 'an'（例如：'a ball', 'an egg', 'an umbrella'）
将规则应用于拼写和发音不同的易错词（例如：'an hour' 因为 /h/ 不发音，'a uniform' 因为 /juː/ 以辅音音素开头）
纠正给定句子中 'a' 或 'an' 用法的错误（例如：将 'a orange' 改为 'an orange'）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 写作时，他们是否能自动在以辅音音素开头的单词前选择 'a'，在元音音素开头的单词前选择 'an'——比如 'a cat' 但 'an apple' 或 'an hour'？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Expressing Time, Place and Cause
topics.description: Use conjunctions (when, before, after, while, so, because), adverbs (then, next, soon, therefore) and prepositions (before, after, during, in, because of) to express time, place and cause within and across sentences
evidence: Use time conjunctions to connect clauses (e.g., 'We went inside because it was raining', 'After the bell rang, we lined up')
Use adverbs of time and cause within sentences (e.g., 'First, she opened the door. Then, she stepped outside. Therefore, she got wet.')
Use prepositions of time and cause in phrases (e.g., 'during the lesson', 'before lunch', 'because of the rain')
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes a story, do they use time words like "after", "while", or "soon" to show the order things happened — rather than starting every sentence with "then"?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用连词（conjunctions，如 when, before, after, while, so, because）、副词（adverbs，如 then, next, soon, therefore）和介词（prepositions，如 before, after, during, in, because of）在句内和跨句表达时间、地点和原因
evidenceZh: 使用时间连词（time conjunctions）连接分句（例如：'We went inside because it was raining / 因为下雨，我们走进了室内'，'After the bell rang, we lined up / 铃响之后，我们排好了队'）
在句子中使用时间和原因副词（例如：'First, she opened the door. Then, she stepped outside. Therefore, she got wet. / 首先，她打开了门。接着，她走到外面。因此，她弄湿了。'）
在短语中使用时间和原因介词（例如：'during the lesson / 在上课期间'，'before lunch / 午餐前'，'because of the rain / 因为下雨'）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 写故事时，他们是否使用了诸如 'after'、'while' 或 'soon' 之类的时间词来表明事情发生的顺序，而不是每句话都以 'then' 开头？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Grammar Terms: Clauses and Conjunctions
topics.description: Use and understand Year 3 grammatical terminology accurately when discussing reading and writing: preposition, conjunction, word family, prefix, clause, subordinate clause, direct speech, consonant letter, vowel letter, inverted commas/speech marks
evidence: Use the terms 'clause' and 'subordinate clause' to identify parts of a multi-clause sentence (e.g., point to the subordinate clause in 'I stayed inside because it rained')
Use the terms 'conjunction', 'preposition', and 'prefix' correctly when explaining word/sentence choices in own writing
Distinguish between consonant letters and vowel letters and use the terms 'direct speech' and 'inverted commas' when discussing punctuation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} to find a "subordinate clause" or a "preposition" in a sentence from their book, can they point one out and explain what it means?
topics.descriptionZh: 在讨论阅读和写作时，准确使用并理解三年级语法术语：介词（preposition）、连词（conjunction）、词族（word family）、前缀（prefix）、分句（clause）、从属分句（subordinate clause）、直接引语（direct speech）、辅音字母（consonant letter）、元音字母（vowel letter）、引号（inverted commas/speech marks）
evidenceZh: 使用“分句（clause）”和“从属分句（subordinate clause）”术语来识别多分句句子的组成部分（例如，指出“我待在室内，因为下雨了”这句话中的从属分句）
在解释自己写作中的词语或句子选择时，正确使用“连词（conjunction）”、“介词（preposition）”和“前缀（prefix）”术语
区分辅音字母（consonant letters）和元音字母（vowel letters），并在讨论标点符号时使用“直接引语（direct speech）”和“引号（inverted commas）”术语
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你让{{name}}在书中的句子里找出一个“从属分句（subordinate clause）”或“介词（preposition）”，他们能指出来并解释其含义吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Irregular past tense verbs
topics.description: Form and use the past tense of frequently occurring irregular verbs correctly (e.g., sat, hid, told, went, came, ran), recognising that these do not follow the regular -ed pattern
evidence: Supply the correct past tense of common irregular verbs: go→went, see→saw, run→ran, tell→told
Correct over-regularised forms in writing (e.g. change 'goed' to 'went', 'hided' to 'hid')
Write a short recount using at least five irregular past-tense verbs accurately
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes about something that happened in the past with an irregular verb — like "run" or "sit" — do they write "ran" and "sat" rather than "runned" and "sitted"?
topics.nameZh: 不规则过去式动词 (irregular past tense verbs)
topics.descriptionZh: 正确构成并使用常见不规则动词的过去式（例如：sat, hid, told, went, came, ran），并认识到这些动词不遵循常规的 -ed 规则变化模式。
evidenceZh: 提供常见不规则动词的正确过去式：go→went, see→saw, run→ran, tell→told
纠正写作中过度规则化的形式（例如，将 'goed' 改为 'went'，将 'hided' 改为 'hid'）
写一段简短的记叙文，准确使用至少五个不规则过去式动词
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 描写过去发生的事情并使用不规则动词（如 'run' 或 'sit'）时，他们是否会写 'ran' 和 'sat'，而不是 'runned' 和 'sitted'？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Irregular Plural Nouns
topics.description: Form and use irregular plural nouns (e.g., children, teeth, mice, geese) in addition to regular plurals, recognising that some nouns have irregular plural forms that do not follow the -s/-es pattern
evidence: Form and use irregular plural nouns correctly (e.g. child→children, tooth→teeth, mouse→mice, goose→geese)
Identify collective nouns that name a group (e.g. 'a flock of birds', 'a group of children', 'a pack of wolves')
Correct over-regularised plurals in writing (e.g. change 'mouses' to 'mice', 'foots' to 'feet')
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you point to a picture of several mice or a group of children, can {{name}} write the correct plural — knowing it's "mice" not "mouses" and "children" not "childs"?
topics.descriptionZh: 除了规则复数外，掌握并使用不规则复数名词（如 children, teeth, mice, geese），认识到有些名词的不规则复数形式不遵循加 -s/-es 的规律
evidenceZh: 正确构成并使用不规则复数名词（例如：child→children, tooth→teeth, mouse→mice, goose→geese）
识别表示群体的集合名词（例如：a flock of birds, a group of children, a pack of wolves）
在写作中纠正过度规则化的复数错误（例如：将 mouses 改为 mice，将 foots 改为 feet）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你指着一张多只老鼠或一群孩子的图片，{{name}} 能否写出正确的复数形式——知道是 mice 而不是 mouses，是 children 而不是 childs？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Pronouns for clarity
topics.description: Choose pronouns for clarity and cohesion, avoiding ambiguity and repetition; use reflexive pronouns correctly (e.g., myself, ourselves, himself)
evidence: Replace repeated nouns with pronouns to improve cohesion: rewrite 'Sam picked up Sam's bag' as 'Sam picked up his bag'
Use reflexive pronouns correctly in sentences (e.g. 'I made it myself', 'They helped themselves')
Identify and fix ambiguous pronoun references (e.g. 'Tom told Jack he was late' — who was late?)
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes a paragraph about two people — like two characters in a story — do they use "he", "she", and "they" clearly enough that you always know who is being talked about?
topics.descriptionZh: 选择合适的代词以确保表达清晰和连贯，避免歧义和重复；正确使用反身代词（例如：我自己 myself、我们自己 ourselves、他自己 himself）
evidenceZh: 用代词替换重复的名词以提高连贯性：将‘萨姆拿起了萨姆的包’改写为‘萨姆拿起了他的包’
在句子中正确使用反身代词（例如：‘我自己做的 (myself)’、‘他们自己动手 (themselves)’）
识别并修正指代不明的代词（例如：‘汤姆告诉杰克他迟到了’——谁迟到了？）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}写一段关于两个人的话时——比如故事里的两个角色——他们使用‘他’、‘她’和‘他们’时是否足够清晰，让你总能清楚地知道在说谁？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Punctuating Direct Speech
topics.description: Punctuate direct speech using inverted commas (speech marks), understanding that direct speech records the exact words spoken and must be enclosed in punctuation marks
evidence: Place inverted commas around the spoken words in a sentence (e.g., "Let's go!" shouted Tom.)
Write a sentence containing direct speech with correct punctuation including a reporting clause (e.g., Mum said, "Time for bed.")
Identify direct speech in a text and explain what the inverted commas show
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes down something a character said in a story, do they put speech marks around the exact words — like "Come here," she called — and use the correct punctuation inside?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用引号（speech marks）为直接引语添加标点，理解直接引语记录的是人物所说的原话，并且必须使用标点符号将其括起来。
evidenceZh: 在句子中的说话内容外加上引号（例如：“Let's go!” shouted Tom.）
写出一个包含直接引语和正确标点符号的句子，包括提示语（例如：Mum said, "Time for bed."）
在文本中识别直接引语，并解释引号的作用
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}写下故事里某个角色说的话时，他们是否会在原话外加上引号（speech marks）——就像“过来，”她喊道这样——并在内部使用正确的标点符号？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: The Present Perfect Tense
topics.description: Use the present perfect form of verbs in contrast to the simple past tense, understanding how the present perfect indicates an action completed at an unspecified time or with ongoing relevance (e.g., 'He has gone out' vs 'He went out')
evidence: Form the present perfect using 'has/have' + past participle (e.g., 'She has eaten', 'They have finished')
Choose between simple past and present perfect to match the intended meaning (e.g., 'I ate lunch' vs 'I have eaten lunch')
Identify the present perfect form in a text and explain why the author used it instead of simple past
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between "I ate breakfast" (simple past) and "I have eaten breakfast" (present perfect) — knowing one means a finished action and the other links the past to right now?
topics.descriptionZh: 对比一般过去时 (Simple Past Tense)，使用动词的现在完成时形式，理解现在完成时如何表示在不确定时间完成的动作或具有持续相关性的动作（例如：‘He has gone out’ 与 ‘He went out’ 的区别）。
evidenceZh: 使用‘has/have + 过去分词 (past participle)’来构成现在完成时（例如：‘She has eaten’，‘They have finished’）
根据想要表达的意思，在一般过去时和现在完成时之间做出正确选择（例如：‘I ate lunch’ 与 ‘I have eaten lunch’ 的区别）
在文本中识别出现在完成时形式，并解释作者为什么使用它而不是一般过去时
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释‘I ate breakfast（一般过去时）’和‘I have eaten breakfast（现在完成时）’之间的区别——知道前者表示一个已经完成的动作，而后者将过去与现在联系了起来？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Abstract nouns
topics.description: Understand and use abstract nouns to name ideas, qualities, and states that cannot be perceived by the senses
evidence: Sort words like 'freedom', 'table', 'courage', 'pencil', 'childhood' into abstract and concrete noun categories
Complete sentences using appropriate abstract nouns: 'Her _____ (brave → bravery) inspired the whole team'
Write three sentences each containing a different abstract noun (e.g. 'honesty', 'friendship', 'happiness')
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} write a sentence using an abstract word like "kindness", "freedom", or "happiness" — knowing these are nouns even though you can't touch or see them?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解并使用抽象名词（Abstract nouns）来命名无法通过感官直接感知的想法、品质和状态。
evidenceZh: 将“freedom（自由）”、“table（桌子）”、“courage（勇气）”、“pencil（铅笔）”、“childhood（童年）”等单词分别归入抽象名词（Abstract nouns）和具体名词（Concrete nouns）类别。
使用合适的抽象名词完成句子：“她的_____（brave 变为 bravery，勇气）鼓舞了整个团队”。
写出三个句子，每个句子包含一个不同的抽象名词（例如“honesty（诚实）”、“friendship（友谊）”、“happiness（快乐）”）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否使用像“kindness（善良）”、“freedom（自由）”或“happiness（快乐）”这样的抽象词写一个句子，并明白即使看不见、摸不着，它们也是名词呢？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Agreement in sentences
topics.description: Ensure subject-verb agreement and pronoun-antecedent agreement within and across sentences
evidence: Correct 'The group of children were laughing' to 'The group of children was laughing' and explain the singular subject
Choose the correct pronoun in 'Each student must bring ____ (his or her / their) book' and explain the antecedent link
Identify and fix three agreement errors in a short paragraph, explaining each correction
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} writes "Each of the players have their own locker", can they spot the error and fix it to "has their own locker" — making sure the verb matches the subject?
topics.descriptionZh: 确保单句内及跨句之间的主谓一致（subject-verb agreement）和代词与先行词一致（pronoun-antecedent agreement）。
evidenceZh: 将“The group of children were laughing”纠正为“The group of children was laughing”，并解释其单数主语（singular subject）
在“Each student must bring ____ (his or her / their) book”中选择正确的代词，并解释代词与先行词（antecedent）的联系
识别并修正一段短文中的三个一致性错误，并解释每处修改
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}写出“Each of the players have their own locker”，他们能否找出错误并将其修正为“has their own locker”——以确保动词与主语保持一致？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Comparatives & Superlatives
topics.description: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs, choosing correctly between them
evidence: Form comparatives and superlatives for 'big' (bigger/biggest), 'beautiful' (more/most beautiful), and 'good' (better/best)
Choose the correct form in 'She runs _____ (faster/more fast) than her brother' and explain the rule
Write sentences using both a comparative adverb ('more carefully') and a superlative adjective ('tallest') correctly
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is comparing three things — like three books they've read — can they correctly say one is "good", another is "better", and the best one is "the best"?
topics.descriptionZh: 掌握形容词和副词比较级与最高级的构成及用法，并能正确区分和使用它们。
evidenceZh: 能正确写出 'big' (bigger/biggest)、'beautiful' (more/most beautiful) 和 'good' (better/best) 的比较级与最高级。
能在 'She runs _____ (faster/more fast) than her brother' 中选择正确的形式，并解释其中的语法规则。
能正确使用比较级副词 (如 'more carefully') 和最高级形容词 (如 'tallest') 进行造句。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 正在比较三件事物——比如他们读过的三本书——他们能否正确地说出一本 'good'（好），另一本 'better'（更好），而最好的一本则是 'the best'（最好）？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Expanded noun phrases (age 8+)
topics.description: Expand noun phrases with modifying adjectives, nouns, and preposition phrases to add detail
evidence: Expand 'the teacher' to 'the strict maths teacher with curly hair' using adjective, noun, and preposition phrase
Write a sentence containing a noun phrase with at least three modifiers, e.g. 'the old stone bridge over the river'
Identify the head noun and its modifiers in 'the tiny grey kitten under the table'
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} describes something in a piece of writing, do they build up a rich description — like "the tall man with the grey coat" rather than just "the man"?
topics.nameZh: 扩展名词短语（8岁及以上）
topics.descriptionZh: 使用修饰性形容词、名词和介词短语来扩展名词短语，以增加细节
evidenceZh: 使用形容词、名词和介词短语，将‘老师’扩展为‘那位留着卷发的严厉数学老师’
写一个包含至少三个修饰语的名词短语的句子，例如‘河上那座古老的石桥’
识别‘桌子下那只极小的灰色小猫’中的中心名词及其修饰语
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 在写作中描述某物时，他们是否会构建丰富的描述——比如‘那个穿着灰色外套的高个子男人’而不仅仅是‘那个男人’？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Fronted Adverbials and Commas
topics.description: Use fronted adverbials to vary sentence openings and punctuate them with commas
evidence: Write a sentence beginning with a time adverbial, e.g. 'Later that day, the children ran home'
Rewrite 'The fox crept through the garden at midnight' with the adverbial fronted and a comma placed correctly
Identify and correct a missing comma after a fronted adverbial in 'Before breakfast she packed her bag'
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes a story or a report, do they sometimes start a sentence with a phrase like "After lunch," or "Quietly, the fox moved closer," — and put a comma after that opening phrase?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用句首状语（fronted adverbials）来变换句首，并正确使用逗号进行标点。
evidenceZh: 写一个以时间状语开头的句子，例如：“那天晚些时候，孩子们跑回了家。”
改写“狐狸在半夜悄悄穿过花园”（The fox crept through the garden at midnight），将状语移至句首并正确放置逗号。
找出并纠正“早饭前她收拾好了书包”（Before breakfast she packed her bag）中句首状语后缺失的逗号。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}写故事或报告时，他们是否会偶尔用像“午饭后，”或“悄悄地，狐狸靠近了，”这样的短语开头，并在该开头短语后加上逗号？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Grammar Terms: Pronouns and Determiners
topics.description: Know and use Year 4 grammar terminology including determiner, pronoun, possessive pronoun, and adverbial
evidence: Label the determiner, pronoun, and adverbial in 'She quickly opened her present on the table'
Explain the difference between a possessive pronoun ('mine', 'theirs') and other pronouns ('I', 'they')
Use the terms 'determiner' and 'adverbial' accurately when discussing a classmate's writing
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} to find a "determiner" or a "possessive pronoun" in a sentence, can they point one out and explain what job it does?
topics.nameZh: 语法术语：代词与限定词
topics.descriptionZh: 掌握并使用四年级语法术语，包括限定词 (determiner)、代词 (pronoun)、物主代词 (possessive pronoun) 和状语 (adverbial)。
evidenceZh: 在句子“She quickly opened her present on the table”中标注出限定词 (determiner)、代词 (pronoun) 和状语 (adverbial)。
解释物主代词 (possessive pronoun)（如 'mine'、'theirs'）与其他代词 (pronoun)（如 'I'、'they'）之间的区别。
在讨论同学的作文时，准确使用“限定词 (determiner)”和“状语 (adverbial)”这两个术语。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你让{{name}}在句子中找出一个“限定词 (determiner)”或“物主代词 (possessive pronoun)”，他们能指出来并解释它在句子中起什么作用吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Plural vs Possessive in Nouns
topics.description: Distinguish between the plural -s suffix and the possessive -'s suffix in nouns
evidence: Sort words like 'dogs', 'dog's', and 'dogs'' into plural, singular possessive, and plural possessive categories
Explain why 'the cats bowl' is incorrect and supply the correct form ('the cat's bowl' or 'the cats' bowl') for a given meaning
Write two sentences using the same noun — one as a plural and one as a possessive
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell the difference between "the girls' coats" (belonging to many girls) and "the girls are coming" (just a plural) — and write each one correctly without mixing up the apostrophe?
topics.descriptionZh: 区分名词中表示复数的“-s”后缀和表示所有格的“-'s”后缀
evidenceZh: 将“dogs”、“dog's”和“dogs'”等单词分类到复数 (plural)、单数所有格 (singular possessive) 和复数所有格 (plural possessive) 类别中
解释为什么“the cats bowl”是错误的，并根据特定含义提供正确的形式（“the cat's bowl”或“the cats' bowl”）
使用同一个名词造两个句子——一个用作复数，一个用作所有格
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否区分“the girls' coats”（属于多个女孩的所有格）和“the girls are coming”（仅为复数）的区别，并在书写时正确使用撇号 (apostrophe) 而不混淆？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Simple Past, Present and Future
topics.description: Form and use the simple past, present, and future verb tenses consistently in writing
evidence: Rewrite 'I walk to school' in past tense ('I walked') and future tense ('I will walk')
Identify and correct inconsistent tense in 'Yesterday she walks to the shop and bought milk'
Write a three-sentence paragraph maintaining consistent future tense throughout
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes about something that happened yesterday, something happening now, and something that will happen tomorrow, do they change the verb correctly for each time — like "I walked", "I walk", and "I will walk"?
topics.nameZh: 一般过去时、现在时和将来时
topics.descriptionZh: 在写作中正确、连贯地构成并使用一般过去时、现在时和将来时动词时态
evidenceZh: 将“I walk to school”改写为过去时（“I walked”）和将来时（“I will walk”）
识别并纠正“Yesterday she walks to the shop and bought milk”中不一致的时态
写一个包含三句话的段落，并在全篇保持一致的将来时态
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 描写昨天发生的事、现在发生的事以及明天将要发生的事时，他们能否根据每个时间正确地变换动词——例如使用“I walked”、“I walk”和“I will walk”？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Standard English Verbs
topics.description: Use Standard English verb inflections in place of non-standard local forms
evidence: Correct 'we was playing' to 'we were playing' and explain why the standard form is needed in writing
Choose the standard form in pairs such as 'I did / I done', 'she has / she have', 'they were / they was'
Rewrite a short passage replacing three non-standard verb forms with their Standard English equivalents
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sometimes says "we was" or "they done it" in conversation, do they know to write "we were" and "they did it" in their schoolwork — using standard written English?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用标准英语动词的屈折变化（verb inflections）来替代非标准的当地方言形式
evidenceZh: 将 "we was playing" 纠正为 "we were playing"，并解释在书面写作中为何需要使用标准形式
在给定的词对中选择标准形式，如 "I did / I done"、"she has / she have"、"they were / they was"
重写一段短文，将其中三个非标准动词形式替换为对应的标准英语形式
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在日常交谈中有时会说 "we was" 或 "they done it"，他们是否知道在学校的作业中应该写 "we were" 和 "they did it"——即使用标准书面英语（Standard Written English）？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Adjective Order in Sentences
topics.description: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional English patterns (opinion-size-age-shape-colour-origin-material-purpose) to produce natural-sounding descriptions
evidence: Arrange multiple adjectives before a noun in conventional order, e.g. 'a lovely little old rectangular green French silver whittling knife' simplified to classroom examples like 'a small red bag' not 'a red small bag'
Identify when adjective order sounds unnatural and rearrange to match English conventions, e.g. correct 'the wooden big table' to 'the big wooden table'
Apply the size-before-colour-before-material pattern in descriptive writing, e.g. 'a tall grey stone castle' rather than 'a stone grey tall castle'
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} uses several describing words together — like "a tiny old wooden box" — does the order sound natural, or do they mix up the adjectives so it sounds odd?
topics.nameZh: 句子中形容词的排列顺序
topics.descriptionZh: 按照英语习惯模式（opinion-size-age-shape-colour-origin-material-purpose）在句子中对形容词进行排序，以生成自然流畅的描述。
evidenceZh: 按照习惯顺序将多个形容词排列在名词前，例如将'a lovely little old rectangular green French silver whittling knife'简化为课堂示例，如使用'a small red bag'而不是'a red small bag'
识别形容词顺序听起来不自然的情况，并重新排列以符合英语习惯，例如将'the wooden big table'纠正为'the big wooden table'
在描述性写作中应用'大小在颜色前、颜色在材料前'的顺序规律，例如使用'a tall grey stone castle'而不是'a stone grey tall castle'
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 连用多个描述性词语时——比如“a tiny old wooden box”——顺序听起来自然吗，还是他们把形容词的顺序弄混了，导致读起来很奇怪？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Brackets and dashes for parenthesis
topics.description: Use brackets, dashes, and commas to indicate parenthesis — additional information inserted into a sentence that could be removed without changing the sentence's core meaning
evidence: Insert a parenthetical phrase using paired brackets, e.g. 'The oldest building (built in 1642) stands in the town square'
Use paired dashes to add an aside or extra detail within a sentence, e.g. 'My brother — who is older than me — lives in London'
Choose between brackets, dashes, and commas for parenthesis based on how much emphasis the aside should receive, recognising that dashes give most prominence and brackets give least
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} adds a little extra detail inside a sentence — like "The teacher, who is very strict, gave us homework" — do they correctly use brackets, dashes, or commas around that added bit?
topics.nameZh: 括号与破折号表示插入语 (Parenthesis)
topics.descriptionZh: 使用括号、破折号和逗号来表示插入语 (Parenthesis) ——即插入句子中的附加信息，即使删除也不会改变句子的核心意思。
evidenceZh: 使用成对的括号插入补充短语，例如：‘最古老的建筑（建于1642年）矗立在城镇广场上’
使用成对的破折号在句子中添加补充说明或额外细节，例如：‘我的哥哥——他比我大——住在伦敦’
根据补充说明需要强调的程度，在括号、破折号和逗号之间进行选择，要知道破折号的强调效果最强，而括号最弱
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 在句子中添加一点额外细节时——比如‘那位非常严格的老师给我们布置了作业’——他们是否正确地在添加的内容周围使用了括号、破折号或逗号？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Cohesion within paragraphs
topics.description: Use cohesive devices within a paragraph — including pronouns, adverbials (then, after that, firstly), and synonyms — to link sentences and build a coherent flow of ideas
evidence: Replace repeated nouns with pronouns or synonyms to maintain cohesion without ambiguity, e.g. 'The explorer found a cave. She examined it carefully'
Use adverbials of sequence (firstly, then, next, finally) and cause (therefore, as a result, consequently) to connect ideas within a paragraph
Identify where cohesion breaks down in a paragraph and insert appropriate linking devices to improve the flow
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes a paragraph, do the sentences flow together smoothly — using words like "however", "after this", or "in contrast" to link ideas, rather than every sentence starting with "And then"?
topics.descriptionZh: 在段落中使用衔接手段（包括代词、副词（如 then、after that、firstly）和同义词）来连接句子，构建连贯的思路。
evidenceZh: 用代词或同义词替换重复的名词，以保持连贯且无歧义，例如：'The explorer found a cave. She examined it carefully.'（探险家发现了一个洞穴。她仔细地检查了它。）
使用表示顺序的副词（firstly、then、next、finally）和表示因果的连接词（therefore、as a result、consequently）来连接段落内的观点。
找出段落中连贯性中断的地方，并插入适当的衔接词（linking devices）以改善文章的流畅度。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 写段落时，句子之间是否流畅连贯——使用诸如 'however'、'after this' 或 'in contrast' 等词语来连接观点，而不是每句话都以 'And then' 开头？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Commas Before Joining Words
topics.description: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction (and, but, or, so, yet) when joining two independent clauses in a compound sentence
evidence: Place a comma before the coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence, e.g. 'I wanted to go outside, but it was raining'
Distinguish compound sentences (two independent clauses) from simple sentences with compound predicates, e.g. 'She sang and danced' needs no comma but 'She sang a song, and he played the piano' does
Edit writing to insert missing commas before coordinating conjunctions in compound sentences
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} joins two complete thoughts with a word like "but" or "so" — like "I wanted to go, but it was raining" — do they put a comma before that joining word?
topics.descriptionZh: 在并列句（compound sentence）中连接两个独立分句（independent clauses）时，请在并列连词（coordinating conjunction，如 and, but, or, so, yet）前使用逗号。
evidenceZh: 在并列句中，将逗号放在并列连词之前，例如：'I wanted to go outside, but it was raining'（我想出去玩，但是下雨了）。
区分包含两个独立分句的并列句与带有复合谓语的简单句，例如：'She sang and danced'（她又唱又跳）不需要逗号，但'She sang a song, and he played the piano'（她唱了一首歌，而他弹了钢琴）需要逗号。
修改写作内容，在并列句的并列连词前补上缺失的逗号。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}用“but”（但是）或“so”（所以）等词连接两个完整的想法时——比如“I wanted to go, but it was raining”（我想去，但是下雨了）——他们会在连接词前面加逗号吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Commas to avoid ambiguity
topics.description: Use commas to clarify meaning and avoid ambiguity in sentences where the absence of a comma could cause misreading
evidence: Insert a comma to prevent ambiguity, e.g. 'Let's eat, Grandma' vs 'Let's eat Grandma' or 'Most of the time, travellers worry about their bags'
Identify sentences where a missing comma changes the meaning and explain the two possible readings
Use commas after introductory elements (adverbial phrases, subordinate clauses) to prevent misreading of the main clause
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why "Let's eat, Grandma" and "Let's eat Grandma" mean very different things — and use that kind of comma in their own writing to avoid confusion?
topics.descriptionZh: 在可能因为漏掉逗号而产生误解的句子中，正确使用逗号来澄清句意、消除歧义。
evidenceZh: 插入逗号以避免歧义，例如：'Let's eat, Grandma'（我们吃饭吧，奶奶）和 'Let's eat Grandma'（我们把奶奶吃了吧），或者 'Most of the time, travellers worry about their bags'（大多数时候，旅行者担心自己的行李）
找出因为缺少逗号而改变意思的句子，并解释这句话可能产生的两种不同理解
在引导成分（如状语短语 (adverbial phrases)、从句 (subordinate clauses)）之后使用逗号，以防止对主句 (main clause) 产生误读
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么 'Let's eat, Grandma' 和 'Let's eat Grandma' 这两句话的意思截然不同，并且在自己的写作中也能正确使用这类逗号来避免别人产生误解呢？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Converting Words into Verbs
topics.description: Convert nouns and adjectives into verbs by adding suffixes -ate, -ise (-ize), and -ify, understanding how word class changes affect sentence construction
evidence: Add -ate, -ise, or -ify to nouns or adjectives to form verbs, e.g. pollen → pollinate, advert → advertise, simple → simplify
Choose the correct verb-forming suffix for a given root and use the resulting verb in a sentence, e.g. 'They needed to classify the animals' from 'class'
Identify the word-class change when a suffix converts a noun or adjective into a verb and explain how this affects the sentence structure
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} take a word like "active" or "sharp" and turn it into a verb by adding a suffix — knowing that "activate" and "sharpen" are the verb forms?
topics.descriptionZh: 通过添加后缀 -ate、-ise (-ize) 和 -ify，将名词 (nouns) 和形容词 (adjectives) 转换为动词 (verbs)，并理解词性 (word class) 变化如何影响句子构建。
evidenceZh: 在名词或形容词后添加 -ate、-ise 或 -ify 来构成动词，例如：pollen → pollinate，advert → advertise，simple → simplify。
为给定的词根选择正确的动词后缀，并将生成的动词用在句子中，例如：从词根“class”派生出动词，并造出句子“They needed to classify the animals”。
识别后缀将名词或形容词转换为动词时的词性 (word-class) 变化，并解释这种变化如何影响句子结构。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否通过添加后缀将像“active”或“sharp”这样的词转换为动词，并知道“activate”和“sharpen”是它们的动词形式？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Expanded noun phrases (age 9+)
topics.description: Form and use prepositional phrases (preposition + noun phrase) to add detail about time, location, or direction within sentences, recognising how they function as adjective or adverb phrases
evidence: Identify the preposition and noun phrase within a prepositional phrase, e.g. in 'under the old bridge', 'under' is the preposition and 'the old bridge' is the noun phrase
Add prepositional phrases to expand sentences with detail about where, when, or how, e.g. 'The cat slept' → 'The cat slept on the warm windowsill throughout the afternoon'
Distinguish prepositional phrases functioning as adjectives (modifying nouns: 'the house on the hill') from those functioning as adverbs (modifying verbs: 'she ran across the field')
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes directions or descriptions of a place — like "behind the old tree" or "near the top of the hill" — do they use prepositional phrases naturally to show where or when something is?
topics.nameZh: 扩展名词短语（9岁及以上）
topics.descriptionZh: 构建并使用介词短语（prepositional phrases，即介词 + 名词短语）来为句子中的时间、地点或方向添加细节，并认识它们如何作为形容词短语或副词短语发挥作用。
evidenceZh: 识别介词短语中的介词和名词短语，例如在 'under the old bridge' 中，'under' 是介词，'the old bridge' 是名词短语
添加介词短语来扩展句子，提供关于地点、时间或方式的细节，例如：'The cat slept' → 'The cat slept on the warm windowsill throughout the afternoon'
区分作为形容词功能的介词短语（修饰名词：'the house on the hill'）和作为副词功能的介词短语（修饰动词：'she ran across the field'）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 写下路线指示或地点描述时——例如 'behind the old tree' 或 'near the top of the hill'——他们是否能自然地使用介词短语（prepositional phrases）来表示某物在哪里或何时存在？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Fixing Fragments & Run-Ons
topics.description: Recognise and correct sentence fragments (incomplete sentences lacking a subject or predicate) and run-on sentences (two or more independent clauses joined without proper punctuation or conjunctions)
evidence: Identify a sentence fragment by checking whether it has both a subject and a predicate, e.g. recognise 'Running through the park' as a fragment and correct to 'The dog was running through the park'

Identify a run-on sentence where two independent clauses are fused without punctuation or a conjunction, e.g. 'I like cats I also like dogs' and correct using a full stop, comma + conjunction, or semicolon
Edit a paragraph to fix fragments and run-ons, choosing the most effective correction strategy for each error
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s writing has a sentence like "Running down the street." or two ideas jammed together without any punctuation, can they spot that something's wrong and fix it?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别并纠正残缺句（缺乏主语或谓语的不完整句子，sentence fragments）和连写句（两个或多个独立分句在没有正确标点或连词的情况下连接在一起的句子，run-on sentences）。
evidenceZh: 通过检查句子是否同时包含主语（subject）和谓语（predicate）来识别残缺句（sentence fragment），例如识别出“Running through the park”是一个残缺句，并将其纠正为“The dog was running through the park”。
识别两个独立分句（independent clauses）在没有标点或连词（conjunction）的情况下直接相连的连写句（run-on sentence），例如“I like cats I also like dogs”，并使用句号、逗号加连词或分号（semicolon）进行纠正。
编辑段落以修复残缺句和连写句，为每个错误选择最有效的纠正策略。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}的作文中出现了像“Running down the street.”这样的句子，或者把两个想法毫无标点地挤在一起，他们能发现哪里不对劲并把它改对吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Grammar Terms: Modal Verbs and Clauses
topics.description: Know and use Year 5 grammar terminology accurately when discussing reading and writing: modal verb, relative pronoun, relative clause, parenthesis, bracket, dash, cohesion, ambiguity
evidence: Label a relative clause in a sentence and identify the relative pronoun that introduces it, using correct terminology
Explain why a pair of brackets or dashes creates a parenthesis and describe its function using the term 'parenthesis'
Use the terms 'modal verb', 'cohesion', and 'ambiguity' when discussing how a writer has achieved particular effects in a text
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} what a "modal verb" or a "relative clause" is, can they give you a clear explanation and point to an example in a sentence?
topics.nameZh: 语法术语：情态动词（Modal Verbs）与从句（Clauses）
topics.descriptionZh: 在阅读和写作讨论中，准确了解并使用五年级语法术语：情态动词（modal verb）、关系代词（relative pronoun）、关系从句（relative clause）、插入语（parenthesis）、括号（bracket）、破折号（dash）、连贯性（cohesion）、歧义（ambiguity）。
evidenceZh: 在句子中标出关系从句（relative clause），并使用正确的术语指出引导它的关系代词（relative pronoun）。
解释为什么一对括号或破折号会构成插入语（parenthesis），并使用‘插入语’一词描述其功能。
在讨论作者如何在文本中实现特定效果时，使用‘情态动词’（modal verb）、‘连贯性’（cohesion）和‘歧义’（ambiguity）等术语。
