topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你问 {{name}} 什么是“情态动词”（modal verb）或“关系从句”（relative clause），他们能给出清晰的解释并在句子中指出例子吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Linking paragraphs with adverbials
topics.description: Link ideas across paragraphs using adverbials of time (later, meanwhile, after a while), place (nearby, far away, beyond the wall), and number (secondly, finally, in addition) to guide the reader through a multi-paragraph text
evidence: Begin a new paragraph with an adverbial of time to signal a shift in time or sequence, e.g. 'Meanwhile, back at the castle...' or 'Several hours later, the storm finally passed'
Use adverbials of place to move the reader to a new location between paragraphs, e.g. 'Beyond the forest, the land was flat and dry'
Use numbering or addition adverbials to structure non-fiction across paragraphs, e.g. 'The first reason... The second reason... In addition...'
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes a multi-paragraph story or report, do they use linking phrases — like "Meanwhile, far away…" or "By the following morning…" — to guide the reader smoothly from one section to the next?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用时间（如 later, meanwhile, after a while）、地点（如 nearby, far away, beyond the wall）和顺序（如 secondly, finally, in addition）等副词（adverbials）来连接不同段落的内容，引导读者顺畅地阅读多段落文本。
evidenceZh: 以时间副词（adverbials of time）开启新段落，以提示时间或顺序的转换，例如：'Meanwhile, back at the castle...（同时，回到城堡……）'或'Several hours later, the storm finally passed（几个小时后，风暴终于过去了）'
使用地点副词（adverbials of place）在段落间将读者的视角转移到新地点，例如：'Beyond the forest, the land was flat and dry（穿过森林，土地平坦而干燥）'
使用序号或递进副词（numbering or addition adverbials）跨段落构建非虚构类文本的结构，例如：'The first reason...（第一个原因是……）The second reason...（第二个原因是……）In addition...（此外……）'
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 撰写多段落故事或报告时，他们是否使用连接短语（linking phrases）——例如'Meanwhile, far away…（同时，在遥远的地方……）'或'By the following morning…（到了第二天早上……）'——来引导读者顺畅地从一个部分过渡到下一个部分？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Modal Verbs and Possibility
topics.description: Understand and use modal verbs (can, may, must, might, shall, will, could, should, would) and modal adverbs (perhaps, surely, certainly) to indicate degrees of possibility, necessity, and permission
evidence: Select a modal verb to express certainty, probability, or possibility in a sentence, e.g. 'It will rain' vs 'It might rain' vs 'It could rain'
Replace a modal verb with a modal adverb to achieve a similar effect, e.g. 'He might come' → 'Perhaps he will come'
Distinguish between modals expressing permission (may, can), obligation (must, should), and possibility (might, could) in context
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes, do they choose between words like "must", "might", "could", and "should" to show whether something is certain, possible, or just an idea — rather than treating every action as definite?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解并使用情态动词（can, may, must, might, shall, will, could, should, would）和情态副词（perhaps, surely, certainly）来表达可能性、必要性和允许的不同程度。
evidenceZh: 在句子中选择合适的词来表达确定性、概率或可能性，例如区分“天会下雨 (It will rain)”、“天可能会下雨 (It might rain)”和“天也许会下雨 (It could rain)”。
用情态副词替换情态动词以达到相似的表达效果，例如将“他可能会来 (He might come)”替换为“也许他会来 (Perhaps he will come)”。
在语境中区分表达许可（may, can）、义务（must, should）和可能性（might, could）的情态动词。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 写作时，他们是否会选择使用“must”、“might”、“could”和“should”等词，来表明某件事是确定的、有可能的，还是仅仅是一个想法——而不是把每个动作都当成绝对确定的事实？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Progressive and Continuous Tenses
topics.description: Form and use the progressive (continuous) verb tenses — past progressive (was walking), present progressive (am walking), and future progressive (will be walking) — to convey ongoing actions at different times
evidence: Write sentences using past progressive to describe an action that was ongoing at a particular time, e.g. 'She was reading when the phone rang'
Distinguish present progressive from simple present, e.g. 'I am eating lunch' (right now) vs 'I eat lunch at noon' (habitual)
Form the future progressive using 'will be' + present participle to describe an action that will be ongoing, e.g. 'Tomorrow at 3pm I will be travelling'
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to describe an action that was happening over a period of time in the past — like "I was reading when the phone rang" — can they write the verb in the right ongoing-past form?
topics.nameZh: 进行时与持续时态（Progressive and Continuous Tenses）
topics.descriptionZh: 构建并使用进行时（持续时态）动词时态——过去进行时（was walking）、现在进行时（am walking）和将来进行时（will be walking）——来表达在不同时间正在持续进行的动作
evidenceZh: 使用过去进行时造句，描述在特定时间正在持续进行的动作，例如：'电话响时她正在读书（She was reading when the phone rang）'
区分现在进行时与一般现在时，例如：'我正在吃午饭（I am eating lunch）'（此刻正在发生）与'我中午吃午饭（I eat lunch at noon）'（习惯性动作）
使用'will be + 现在分词（present participle）'构成将来进行时，描述将来某时正在持续进行的动作，例如：'明天下午3点我将正在旅行（Tomorrow at 3pm I will be travelling）'
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}想要描述过去某段时间内正在持续发生的动作——比如'电话响时我正在读书（I was reading when the phone rang）'——他们能否用正确的过去进行形式写出动词？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Relative Clauses
topics.description: Form and use relative clauses beginning with relative pronouns (who, whose, whom, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when, why) to add detail, qualify nouns, and create complex sentences
evidence: Combine a main clause with a relative clause using 'who' or 'which' to add information about a noun, e.g. 'The dog, which had a red collar, barked loudly'
Choose the correct relative pronoun (who for people, which for things, where for places, when for times) and identify the noun it refers back to
Recognise that a relative clause beginning with 'that' can often replace 'who' or 'which' in defining clauses, e.g. 'The book that I read' vs 'The book which I read'
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes to add detail about a noun — like describing a friend "who loves football" or a place "where we always go on holiday" — do they build that into the same sentence using a relative clause?
topics.descriptionZh: 学习构建并使用由关系代词（who, whose, whom, which, that）和关系副词（where, when, why）引导的定语从句，以补充细节、修饰名词并构建复合句。
evidenceZh: 使用‘who’或‘which’将主句与定语从句结合，为名词添加信息，例如‘The dog, which had a red collar, barked loudly’（那条戴着红项圈的狗大声吠叫）
选择正确的关系代词（who指代人，which指代事物，where指代地点，when指代时间），并识别其所指代的名词（先行词）
认识到在限定性定语从句（defining clauses）中，以‘that’开头的定语从句通常可以替换‘who’或‘which’，例如‘The book that I read’与‘The book which I read’
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}写作需要补充名词的细节时——比如描述一个‘热爱足球的朋友（who loves football）’或一个‘我们总是去度假的地方（where we always go on holiday）’——他们是否会使用定语从句将这些内容融入同一个句子中？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Verb Prefixes and Meaning
topics.description: Use verb prefixes (dis-, de-, mis-, over-, re-) to change verb meaning, understanding how each prefix modifies the action expressed by the root verb
evidence: Add verb prefixes to change meaning, e.g. dis- (disagree, disappear), de- (decompose, defrost), mis- (misunderstand, misbehave), over- (overlook, overreact), re- (redo, reconsider)
Select the appropriate verb prefix to express a specific meaning shift such as negation (dis-/mis-), reversal (de-/un-), repetition (re-), or excess (over-)
Distinguish verb prefixes from noun/adjective prefixes and explain how adding a prefix to a verb changes the action described
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you give {{name}} a verb like "appear" and ask them to use a prefix to change its meaning, can they produce words like "disappear", "reappear", or "misrepresent" and explain what the prefix does?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用动词前缀（如 dis-、de-、mis-、over-、re-）来改变动词的含义，理解每个前缀如何修饰词根动词所表达的动作。
evidenceZh: 添加动词前缀以改变词义，例如：dis-（disagree, disappear）、de-（decompose, defrost）、mis-（misunderstand, misbehave）、over-（overlook, overreact）、re-（redo, reconsider）
选择合适的动词前缀来表达特定的词义转变，如否定（dis-/mis-）、反转（de-/un-）、重复（re-）或过度（over-）
区分动词前缀与名词/形容词前缀，并解释在动词上添加前缀是如何改变所描述的动作的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你给 {{name}} 一个像 "appear" 这样的动词，并要求他们使用前缀来改变其含义，他们能否说出 "disappear"、"reappear" 或 "misrepresent" 等词，并解释这些前缀的作用？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Active and passive voice
topics.description: Use the passive voice to shift focus from the agent to the action or recipient, understanding how passive constructions affect the presentation of information in formal and objective writing
evidence: Convert active sentences to passive voice and explain the change in emphasis
Identify passive constructions in news reports and scientific writing
Choose between active and passive voice based on purpose and audience
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} wants to write about something without saying who did it — like in a science report — can they switch the sentence round to say "The experiment was carried out" instead of "We carried out the experiment"?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用被动语态将焦点从动作执行者（agent）转移到动作或动作承受者（recipient）上，理解被动结构（passive constructions）如何影响正式和客观写作中的信息呈现方式。
evidenceZh: 将主动句转换为被动语态（passive voice），并解释强调重点的变化
在新闻报道和科学写作中识别被动结构（passive constructions）
根据写作目的和受众在主动语态（active voice）和被动语态（passive voice）之间进行选择
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}想要描述某件事而不指明是谁做的——比如在科学报告中——他们能转换句子结构，说“实验已被完成”而不是“我们完成了实验”吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Bullet Point Punctuation
topics.description: Punctuate bullet points consistently to list information clearly, applying conventions for capitalisation, end punctuation, and parallel structure across items
evidence: Create bullet point lists with consistent capitalisation and punctuation throughout
Use full stops for bullet points that are complete sentences and no punctuation for fragments
Maintain parallel grammatical structure across all items in a bulleted list
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} uses bullet points to list information — like in a school project — are all the bullets punctuated the same way, with matching capitalisation and consistent end punctuation?
topics.descriptionZh: 统一使用项目符号标点以清晰列出信息，遵循大小写、句末标点以及各项平行结构的规范。
evidenceZh: 创建大小写和标点符号始终一致的项目符号列表
完整句子的项目使用句号，短语或不完整句子则不加标点
在项目符号列表的所有项目中保持平行的语法结构
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 使用项目符号列出信息时——例如在学校项目中——所有项目是否都采用了相同的标点方式，大小写一致且句末标点统一？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Choosing Tenses for Precise Meaning
topics.description: Use verb tense to convey various times, sequences, states, and conditions, selecting tenses deliberately to express the precise timing and nature of actions and events
evidence: Write a paragraph using multiple tenses to show the sequence of past, present, and future events
Choose between simple, progressive, and perfect tenses to express duration or completion
Explain why a specific tense is appropriate for expressing a condition or hypothetical situation
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes a story that jumps between past events and present thoughts, do they shift verb tenses deliberately and accurately — so the reader always knows exactly when each event is happening?
topics.nameZh: 选择时态以表达精确含义
topics.descriptionZh: 使用动词时态（verb tense）来表达各种时间、顺序、状态和条件，有意识地选择时态以准确表达动作和事件的精确发生时间及其性质。
evidenceZh: 撰写一段话，使用多种时态来展示过去、现在和未来事件的顺序
在一般时态（simple tenses）、进行时态（progressive tenses）和完成时态（perfect tenses）之间进行选择，以表达动作的持续或完成
解释为什么特定的时态适合用来表达条件或假设情况（hypothetical situation）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}写一个在过去事件和现在想法之间跳跃的故事时，他们是否能有意且准确地转换动词时态——让读者始终能确切地知道每个事件发生的时间？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Colons and Semicolons in Lists
topics.description: Use a colon to introduce a list and semi-colons to separate items within lists, particularly when list items contain internal commas or are complex phrases
evidence: Introduce a list with a colon after an independent clause such as 'You will need the following items:'
Use semi-colons to separate list items that contain commas such as locations with city and country
Punctuate complex lists in formal writing maintaining clarity and consistency
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes a list of things that are themselves quite long or contain commas — like a list of ingredients with measurements — do they use a colon to introduce it and semi-colons to separate the items?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用冒号（Colon）引出列表，并使用分号（Semicolon）分隔列表中的各项，尤其是当列表项内部包含逗号（Commas）或为复杂短语时。
evidenceZh: 在独立分句（Independent clause）后使用冒号引出列表，例如‘你需要以下物品：’
使用分号分隔包含逗号的列表项，例如包含城市和国家的地点
在正式写作中对复杂列表进行标点处理，以保持清晰和一致性
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 编写一个本身较长或包含逗号的列表时——例如带有计量单位的配料表——他们是否会使用冒号来引出列表，并使用分号来分隔各项？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Commas After Introductory Elements
topics.description: Use a comma to separate an introductory element from the rest of the sentence, including introductory words, phrases, and clauses
evidence: Place commas after introductory adverbs such as 'However' or 'Therefore' at the start of sentences
Use commas after introductory prepositional phrases like 'In the morning' or 'After the game'
Punctuate introductory dependent clauses correctly such as 'When the bell rang, we left'
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} begins a sentence with a phrase or clause — like "Despite the rain," or "If you look closely," — do they put a comma after that opening part before the main sentence begins?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用逗号将句首的引导成分（introductory element）与句子其余部分隔开，包括引导词、引导短语和引导从句。
evidenceZh: 在句首的引导副词（如 'However' 或 'Therefore'）后使用逗号。
在句首的引导介词短语（如 'In the morning' 或 'After the game'）后使用逗号。
正确标点引导性从句（dependent clauses），例如 'When the bell rang, we left'。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 使用短语或从句（如 'Despite the rain,' 或 'If you look closely,'）开始一个句子时，他们会在主句开始前，在这个开头部分后面加上逗号吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Commas with yes, no, and names
topics.description: Use commas to set off the words yes and no, to set off tag questions, and to indicate direct address in sentences
evidence: Write sentences using commas with yes and no at the beginning such as 'Yes, I understand'
Punctuate tag questions correctly such as 'It's cold today, isn't it?'
Use commas to set off names in direct address such as 'Sarah, please pass the salt'
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes dialogue or a letter and addresses someone by name — like "Yes, Mum, I did tidy my room" — do they use commas correctly around the name and around words like "yes" or "no"?
topics.descriptionZh: 学习使用逗号来隔开“yes（是的）”和“no（不是）”，隔开附加疑问句（tag questions），以及在句子中标示直接称呼（direct address）。
evidenceZh: 在句首的“yes”或“no”后面正确使用逗号造句，例如：“是的，我明白了（Yes, I understand）”。
为附加疑问句（tag questions）正确使用标点符号，例如：“今天很冷，不是吗（It's cold today, isn't it?）？”
在直接称呼（direct address）他人时，用逗号隔开人名，例如：“莎拉，请把盐递给我（Sarah, please pass the salt）”。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 写对话或信件并直接称呼某人名字时——例如“是的，妈妈，我确实整理房间了（Yes, Mum, I did tidy my room）”——他们是否能正确地在名字以及“yes”或“no”等词语周围使用逗号？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Conjunctions, Prepositions and Interjections
topics.description: Explain the function of conjunctions, prepositions, and interjections in general and in particular sentences, understanding how each word class contributes to meaning
evidence: Identify conjunctions, prepositions, and interjections in sentences and explain their function
Explain how removing a preposition or conjunction changes the meaning of a sentence
Use interjections appropriately to convey emotion in dialogue or informal writing
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} what the word "although" or "ouch!" does in a sentence, can they explain one is a conjunction that joins ideas and the other is an interjection that expresses feeling?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释连词、介词和感叹词在一般情况及具体句子中的功能，理解各词类对句子含义的贡献。
evidenceZh: 识别句子中的连词、介词和感叹词，并解释其功能
解释去掉介词或连词后句子含义会发生怎样的变化
在对话或非正式写作中恰当使用感叹词来传达情感
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你问{{name}}“although”（虽然）或“ouch!”（哎哟！）在句子中起什么作用，他们能解释前者是连接思想的连词，而后者是表达情感的感叹词吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Consistent verb tense
topics.description: Recognise and correct inappropriate shifts in verb tense within and across sentences and paragraphs, maintaining consistency unless a shift is required by meaning
evidence: Identify and correct unnecessary tense shifts in a given paragraph
Edit own writing to ensure consistent tense use throughout a narrative
Explain when a tense shift is appropriate such as when describing a flashback
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you read back a paragraph {{name}} has written and it unexpectedly switches from past tense to present tense mid-way through, can they spot the shift and correct it so the tense stays consistent?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别并纠正句子内部、句间以及段落间不恰当的动词时态（verb tense）转换，保持时态一致，除非语义需要时态转换
evidenceZh: 识别并纠正给定段落中不必要的时态转换（tense shift）
修改自己的写作，以确保在整个故事叙述中保持时态一致
解释何时进行适当的时态转换，例如在描述倒叙（flashback）时
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你重读{{name}}写的一段话，发现它在中途意外地从过去时（past tense）切换到了现在时（present tense），他们能发现这种时态转换并纠正它，从而保持时态一致吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Correlative Conjunctions
topics.description: Use correlative conjunctions correctly in sentences, pairing words such as either/or, neither/nor, both/and, not only/but also, and whether/or
evidence: Write sentences using each pair of correlative conjunctions correctly
Ensure parallel structure when using correlative conjunctions in complex sentences
Identify and correct errors in correlative conjunction usage in given sentences
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} wants to say that two things are equally true — like "both cats and dogs make good pets" — do they know to use "both…and" together, rather than just "and" on its own?
topics.descriptionZh: 在句子中正确使用关联连词，将诸如 either/or (要么/要么)、neither/nor (既不/也不)、both/and (...和...都)、not only/but also (不仅/而且) 以及 whether/or (是否/或者) 等词语成对使用。
evidenceZh: 正确使用每对关联连词造句
在复杂句中使用关联连词时，确保平行结构 (Parallel structure)
识别并纠正给定句子中关联连词使用的错误
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 想要表达两件事同样成立时——比如“猫和狗都是好宠物”——他们是否知道要将“both…and”搭配使用，而不是单独使用“and”？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Grammar Terms: Voice and Punctuation
topics.description: Know and use Year 6 grammatical terminology accurately: subject, object, active voice, passive voice, synonym, antonym, ellipsis, hyphen, colon, semi-colon, bullet points
evidence: Define and give examples of subject and object in sentences
Explain the difference between active and passive voice using correct terminology
Use terms such as ellipsis, colon, and semi-colon accurately when discussing punctuation choices
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} to find the "subject" and "object" in a sentence, or to explain what a "semi-colon" or "ellipsis" does, can they give you a confident and accurate answer?
topics.descriptionZh: 准确了解并使用六年级语法术语：主语 (subject)、宾语 (object)、主动语态 (active voice)、被动语态 (passive voice)、同义词 (synonym)、反义词 (antonym)、省略号 (ellipsis)、连字符 (hyphen)、冒号 (colon)、分号 (semi-colon)、项目符号 (bullet points)
evidenceZh: 定义并举例说明句子中的主语 (subject) 和宾语 (object)
使用正确的术语解释主动语态 (active voice) 和被动语态 (passive voice) 之间的区别
在讨论标点符号的选择时，准确使用省略号 (ellipsis)、冒号 (colon) 和分号 (semi-colon) 等术语
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你让 {{name}} 找出句子中的“主语 (subject)”和“宾语 (object)”，或者解释“分号 (semi-colon)”或“省略号 (ellipsis)”的作用，他们能给出自信且准确的回答吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Hyphens in Prefixed Words
topics.description: Use hyphens to avoid ambiguity in compound modifiers and prefixed words, distinguishing between meanings that change based on hyphen placement
evidence: Distinguish between 'man eating shark' and 'man-eating shark' by adding or removing hyphens
Use hyphens with prefixes to clarify meaning such as 'recover' versus 're-cover'
Apply hyphens correctly in compound adjectives before nouns such as 'well-known author'
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why "a man-eating shark" and "a man eating shark" mean completely different things — and use a hyphen correctly in their own writing to avoid that kind of confusion?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用连字符来避免复合修饰语和前缀词中的歧义，区分因连字符位置不同而改变的含义。
evidenceZh: 通过添加或移除连字符来区分“man eating shark”（男人吃鲨鱼）和“man-eating shark”（食人鲨）
在前缀中使用连字符以明确含义，例如区分“recover”（恢复）和“re-cover”（重新覆盖）
在名词前的复合形容词中正确使用连字符，例如“well-known author”（著名作家）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么“a man-eating shark”（食人鲨）和“a man eating shark”（一个正在吃鲨鱼的男人）意思完全不同——并且能在自己的写作中正确使用连字符以避免这种混淆？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Paragraph Cohesion
topics.description: Link ideas across paragraphs using a wider range of cohesive devices including word repetition, grammatical connections such as adverbials, and ellipsis to create coherent extended texts
evidence: Use adverbials such as 'on the other hand' and 'as a consequence' to connect paragraphs
Apply ellipsis to avoid repetition while maintaining clarity across sentences
Create cohesion by repeating key words or using synonyms to link ideas between paragraphs
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes a long piece across several paragraphs, do the sections feel connected — with repeated key words, linking phrases, and occasional gaps (ellipsis) used deliberately to hold the whole text together?
topics.descriptionZh: 运用更丰富的衔接手段（包括词语重复、状语等语法连接以及省略）来串联段落间的想法，从而写出连贯的长篇文章。
evidenceZh: 使用诸如“另一方面”和“因此”之类的状语（adverbials）来连接各个段落
运用省略（ellipsis）来避免重复，同时保持句子之间的清晰易懂
通过重复关键词或使用同义词来建立连贯性，将不同段落的思想联系起来
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 撰写跨越多段的长篇文章时，各部分内容是否感觉紧密相连——是否通过重复关键词、使用连接短语，以及有意识地运用偶尔的省略（ellipsis）来将整篇文章凝聚在一起？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Punctuating Clauses
topics.description: Use semi-colons, colons, and dashes to mark boundaries between independent clauses, choosing the appropriate punctuation based on the relationship between the clauses
evidence: Join two related independent clauses using a semi-colon in place of a conjunction
Use a colon to introduce an explanation or elaboration of the first clause
Replace commas with dashes to create stronger pauses between clauses for emphasis
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes two closely related sentences, can they join them with a semi-colon or colon — like "It was late; the streets were empty" — rather than always using a full stop or "and"?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用分号（semi-colons）、冒号（colons）和破折号（dashes）来标记独立分句（independent clauses）之间的界限，并根据分句之间的关系选择合适的标点符号
evidenceZh: 使用分号代替连词来连接两个相关的独立分句
使用冒号引出对第一个分句的解释或详细说明
用破折号代替逗号，在分句之间制造更强的停顿以起到强调作用
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 写两个关系密切的句子时，他们能使用分号或冒号来连接吗——例如‘天色已晚；街道空无一人’——而不是总是使用句号或连词‘和’（and）？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Punctuating Titles of Works
topics.description: Use underlining, quotation marks, or italics to indicate titles of works, applying conventions for different types of works such as books, stories, poems, songs, and articles
evidence: Use italics or underlining for titles of books, films, and albums
Use quotation marks for titles of short works such as poems, songs, and articles
Apply title formatting conventions consistently in a piece of writing
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} refers to a book title or a film name in their writing, do they know to put it in inverted commas or italics — like writing *Charlotte's Web* or "Charlotte's Web" — rather than just leaving it as plain text?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用下划线（underlining）、引号（quotation marks）或斜体（italics）来标示作品标题，并针对不同类型的作品（如书籍、故事、诗歌、歌曲和文章）应用相应的格式规范。
evidenceZh: 对书籍、电影和专辑的标题使用斜体或下划线
对诗歌、歌曲和文章等短篇作品的标题使用引号
在一篇文章中一致地应用标题格式规范
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}在写作中提到书名或电影名时，他们是否知道使用引号或斜体——比如写成 *Charlotte's Web* 或 "Charlotte's Web"——而不是仅仅保留为纯文本？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: The subjunctive mood
topics.description: Use the subjunctive form in formal writing and speech to express wishes, demands, suggestions, or hypothetical situations (e.g., 'If I were you', 'I suggest that he go', 'Were they to arrive')
evidence: Write sentences using 'If I were' to express hypothetical conditions
Transform informal sentences into formal equivalents using subjunctive forms such as 'I recommend that she attend'
Identify subjunctive mood in formal texts such as legal documents or formal letters
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes a formal letter or a persuasive essay, can they use phrases like "If I were in charge…" or "The school suggests that every pupil attend…" to sound more formal and precise?
topics.descriptionZh: 在正式写作和口语中使用虚拟语气（subjunctive mood）来表达愿望、要求、建议或假设情况（例如：'If I were you'（如果我是你）、'I suggest that he go'（我建议他去）、'Were they to arrive'（要是他们到来））。
evidenceZh: 使用 'If I were' 造句来表达假设条件
使用虚拟语气（subjunctive mood）形式（如 'I recommend that she attend'）将非正式句子转换为正式的对应句
在法律文件或正式信函等正式文本中识别虚拟语气（subjunctive mood）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 撰写正式信件或议论文时，他们能否使用诸如 'If I were in charge...'（如果由我负责……）或 'The school suggests that every pupil attend...'（学校建议每位学生都出席……）这样的短语，以使其表达更加正式和精确？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Varying Sentence Structure
topics.description: Expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, reader interest, and style, using techniques such as embedding clauses, using appositives, and varying sentence length
evidence: Combine two simple sentences into one complex sentence using subordination
Expand a simple sentence by adding descriptive phrases and clauses
Reduce wordy sentences by removing redundant words while preserving meaning
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} revises their writing, can they take a very long sentence and split it up, or take three short choppy sentences and combine them into one — choosing the version that reads best for the audience?
topics.descriptionZh: 运用嵌入从句（embedding clauses）、使用同位语（appositives）以及变换句子长度等技巧，对句子进行扩充、合并与精简，从而更准确地表达意义、提升读者的阅读兴趣并优化文章风格。
evidenceZh: 运用从属关系（subordination）将两个简单句合并为一个复合句
通过添加描述性短语和从句来扩充简单句
在保持原意不变的前提下，通过删减冗余词汇来精简冗长的句子
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 修改作文时，他们能否把一个特别长的句子拆分开来，或者把三个短促零碎的句子合并成一句——并从中选出读起来最顺畅、最适合读者阅读的版本？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Advanced Punctuation for Clarity
topics.description: Use punctuation confidently and accurately for effect and clarity — including semicolons to link related clauses, colons to introduce lists or explanations, dashes and parentheses for parenthetical information, ellipsis for omission or suspense, and commas for coordinate adjectives and nonrestrictive elements
evidence: Use a semicolon to link two closely related independent clauses without a conjunction
Set off a nonrestrictive clause with commas and explain why the commas are needed
Use a colon to introduce an explanation or elaboration, and a dash for a dramatic aside
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes a complex piece — like an essay or a detailed story — do they use advanced punctuation like semi-colons, colons, dashes, and ellipses confidently and accurately to shape meaning and style?
topics.nameZh: 高级标点符号提升表达清晰度
topics.descriptionZh: 自信且准确地使用标点符号以增强表达效果和清晰度——包括使用分号连接相关从句，使用冒号引出列表或解释，使用破折号和括号插入补充信息，使用省略号表示省略或制造悬念，以及使用逗号分隔并列形容词和非限制性成分。
evidenceZh: 使用分号连接两个密切相关且无连词的独立分句
使用逗号分隔非限制性从句（nonrestrictive clause），并解释为什么需要这些逗号
使用冒号引出解释或详细说明，并使用破折号插入强调性的补充说明
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 撰写复杂文章（如论文或详细故事）时，他们是否能自信、准确地使用分号、冒号、破折号和省略号等高级标点符号来塑造意义和风格？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Grammar for Effect
topics.description: Analyse the effectiveness and impact of grammatical features in texts read — understanding how authors make deliberate grammatical choices (sentence length, passive voice, fronted adverbials, listing) to create specific effects on the reader
evidence: Explain how an author's use of short, simple sentences creates tension or urgency in a passage
Analyse why an author uses a list of three (tricolon) in a persuasive text and evaluate its impact
Identify a grammatical choice in a text (e.g., present tense for immediacy) and explain the effect on the reader
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads a piece of writing they admire, can they point to specific grammatical choices the author made — like very short sentences for tension, or a list of three for rhythm — and explain why those choices work?
topics.descriptionZh: 分析所读文本中语法特征的有效性与影响力——理解作者如何刻意进行语法选择（句子长度 (sentence length)、被动语态 (passive voice)、句首状语 (fronted adverbials)、排比列举 (listing)）来为读者营造特定的表达效果。
evidenceZh: 解释作者如何使用简短、简单的句子在段落中营造紧张感或紧迫感
分析作者在劝说性文本中为何使用三项排比 (tricolon)，并评估其产生的影响
识别文本中的一种语法选择（例如使用现在时态 (present tense) 以增强即时感），并解释其对读者产生的影响
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 阅读他们欣赏的文章时，他们能否指出作者所做的具体语法选择——比如为了营造紧张感而使用极短的句子，或者为了节奏感而使用三项排比 (tricolon)——并解释这些选择为何有效？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Literary and Language Terminology
topics.description: Discuss reading, writing, and spoken language with precise and confident use of linguistic and literary terminology — including terms for word classes, sentence types, clause types, literary devices, and text-level features
evidence: Use terms like 'subordinate clause', 'relative pronoun', 'metaphor', 'alliteration' accurately in discussion
Explain the difference between a simile and a metaphor using correct terminology
Use metalanguage (e.g., 'the author employs enjambment to...') confidently when writing about texts
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} discusses a book or piece of writing with a teacher, do they use precise language — like "the author uses a compound-complex sentence here" or "that's a non-restrictive relative clause" — rather than just saying "this bit is good"?
topics.descriptionZh: 在讨论阅读、写作和口语时，能够准确且自信地使用语言学和文学术语——包括词类 (word classes)、句型 (sentence types)、从句类型 (clause types)、文学修辞手法 (literary devices) 以及语篇层面特征 (text-level features) 的术语。
evidenceZh: 在讨论中准确使用诸如“从句” (subordinate clause)、“关系代词” (relative pronoun)、“暗喻” (metaphor)、“头韵” (alliteration) 等术语
使用正确的术语解释“明喻” (simile) 和“暗喻” (metaphor) 之间的区别
在撰写文本分析时，自信地使用元语言 (metalanguage)（例如：“作者运用跨行连续 (enjambment) 来……”）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 与老师讨论一本书或一篇文章时，他们是否会使用精准的语言——比如“作者在这里使用了一个并列复合句 (compound-complex sentence)”或“这是一个非限制性定语从句 (non-restrictive relative clause)”——而不是仅仅说“这部分写得很好”？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Phrases & Clauses
topics.description: Understand and analyse the function of phrases (noun, verb, adjectival, adverbial, prepositional) and clauses (main, subordinate, relative) in general and in specific sentences, including recognising and correcting misplaced and dangling modifiers
evidence: Identify a prepositional phrase acting as an adverbial and explain its role in the sentence
Distinguish between a main clause and a subordinate clause and explain their relationship
Spot a dangling modifier in a sentence and rewrite it to remove the ambiguity
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads a sentence like "Walking home from school, the rain soaked her backpack" and something feels grammatically off, can they identify the dangling modifier and explain how to rewrite it correctly?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解并分析短语（名词短语 noun phrase、动词短语 verb phrase、形容词短语 adjectival phrase、副词短语 adverbial phrase、介词短语 prepositional phrase）和从句（主句 main clause、从句 subordinate clause、关系从句 relative clause）在句子中的功能，包括识别并纠正错位修饰语（misplaced modifiers）和悬垂修饰语（dangling modifiers）
evidenceZh: 识别在句子中充当状语的介词短语（prepositional phrase），并解释其在句子中的作用
区分主句（main clause）和从句（subordinate clause），并解释它们之间的关系
找出句子中的悬垂修饰语（dangling modifier），并重写该句子以消除歧义
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 读到像“Walking home from school, the rain soaked her backpack”这样的句子，并感觉语法上有些不对劲，他们能识别出悬垂修饰语（dangling modifier）并解释如何正确地重写它吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Standard English
topics.description: Know and understand the differences between spoken and written language — including differences in formality, register, grammar, and vocabulary — and between Standard English and other varieties of English, using Standard English confidently in writing and speech
evidence: Explain three differences between how we speak informally and how we write formally (e.g., contractions, slang, sentence completeness)
Identify features of Standard English and explain why it is used in formal contexts
Rewrite an informal spoken passage (e.g., a text message) in formal written Standard English
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} understand that the way they speak with friends is different from how they should write in school — and can they adjust their language for formal situations, using standard grammar and vocabulary?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解并理解口语和书面语之间的差异——包括正式程度、语域 (register)、语法和词汇方面的不同——以及标准英语与其他英语变体之间的区别，并能在写作和口语中自信地使用标准英语。
evidenceZh: 解释我们在非正式口语和正式书面语表达时的三个不同之处（例如：缩略形式、俚语、句子完整性）
找出标准英语的特征，并解释为什么在正式场合要使用它
将一段非正式的口语内容（例如：一条短信）改写为正式的书面标准英语
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否明白与朋友交谈时的说话方式与在学校里的写作方式不同，并且能否在正式场合调整自己的语言，使用标准的语法和词汇？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Types of Sentences
topics.description: Choose among and construct simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex sentences to signal different relationships among ideas, varying sentence patterns deliberately for meaning, interest, and style
evidence: Combine short sentences into a complex sentence using a subordinating conjunction for effect
Rewrite a passage of monotonous simple sentences using a mix of sentence types for variety and flow
Identify the sentence type (simple, compound, complex, compound-complex) of given examples and explain the effect of each
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is writing for effect — like building tension in a story or structuring an argument — do they deliberately vary their sentence types, mixing short punchy sentences with longer, more complex ones?
topics.descriptionZh: 选择并构建简单句（simple sentences）、并列句（compound sentences）、复合句（complex sentences）和并列复合句（compound-complex sentences），以表达观点之间的不同逻辑关系，并有意识地变换句式，从而提升表达的意义、趣味性和风格。
evidenceZh: 使用从属连词（subordinating conjunction）将短句合并为复合句，以达到特定的表达效果
运用混合句式重写由单调简单句组成的段落，以增加文章的多样性和流畅度
识别给定例句的句子类型（简单句、并列句、复合句、并列复合句），并解释每种句式的表达效果
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 为了达到特定效果而写作时——例如在故事中营造紧张感或构建论点——他们是否有意识地变换句子类型，将简短有力的短句与更长、更复杂的句子混合使用？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Verb Voice and Mood
topics.description: Understand and use active and passive voice deliberately, and recognise verb moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, conditional) and their effects — choosing the appropriate voice and mood for purpose and audience
evidence: Rewrite an active sentence in the passive voice and explain when the passive is more appropriate
Identify the subjunctive mood in a formal text (e.g., 'If I were...', 'It is essential that he be...')
Explain why a scientific report typically uses passive voice while a personal narrative uses active
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes a formal report or analysis, can they choose between active and passive voice deliberately — for example, using passive voice in a science write-up to sound objective and impersonal?
topics.nameZh: 动词语态与语气（Verb Voice and Mood）
topics.descriptionZh: 理解并刻意使用主动语态（active voice）和被动语态（passive voice），识别动词语气（verb moods：陈述语气 indicative、祈使语气 imperative、虚拟语气 subjunctive、条件语气 conditional）及其表达效果——能够根据写作目的和受众选择合适的语态与语气。
evidenceZh: 将主动语态（active voice）句子改写为被动语态（passive voice），并解释在何种情况下使用被动语态更为合适
在正式文本中识别虚拟语气（subjunctive mood）（例如：'If I were...'、'It is essential that he be...'）
解释为什么科学报告通常使用被动语态，而个人叙事通常使用主动语态
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}撰写正式报告或分析时，他们能否刻意在主动语态和被动语态之间进行选择——例如，在科学报告中使用被动语态以显得客观且不带个人色彩？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Sitting and holding a pencil
topics.description: Sit correctly at a table holding a pencil comfortably and correctly; form lower-case letters in the correct direction starting and finishing in the right place
evidence: Hold a pencil with a comfortable tripod or near-tripod grip
Write all 26 lowercase letters with correct starting points and direction
Maintain consistent letter size on lined paper
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} sits down to write, do they hold their pencil comfortably and form each letter the right way — starting from the right place and going in the right direction?
topics.descriptionZh: 在桌前保持正确的坐姿，舒适且正确地握笔；以正确的方向书写小写字母，起笔和收笔位置准确。
evidenceZh: 以舒适的三指握笔法（tripod grip）或近似三指握笔法握笔
正确起笔并按正确方向书写全部26个小写字母
在横线纸（lined paper）上保持字母大小一致
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 坐下来写字时，他们是否舒适地握着铅笔，并以正确的方式书写每个字母——从正确的位置起笔，并按正确的方向运笔？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Forming Capital Letters
topics.description: Form capital letters correctly; print many upper- and lowercase letters legibly
evidence: Write all 26 capital letters with correct formation
Distinguish between uppercase and lowercase forms in own writing
Use appropriate sizing so capitals are taller than lowercase letters
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} write all the capital letters clearly and legibly so that someone reading their work can easily tell which letter is which?
topics.descriptionZh: 正确书写大写字母；清晰、规范地书写许多大写和小写字母
evidenceZh: 以正确的书写方式写出全部26个大写字母
在自己的书写中正确区分大写和小写字母
保持合适的大小比例，使大写字母比小写字母更高
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否清晰、工整地写出所有大写字母，让阅读其作品的人能轻松分辨出每个字母？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Letter Formation Families
topics.description: Understand which letters belong to which handwriting families based on similar formation patterns and practise letters in groups
evidence: Group letters by similar strokes (e.g. c, a, d, g, o family — all start with a curve)
Explain why certain letters are practised together
Form letters within the same family consistently using the shared movement pattern
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} understand that certain letters are formed in similar ways — for example, "c," "a," "d," and "g" all start with the same curved stroke — and practise those families together?
topics.descriptionZh: 根据相似的书写规律，理解哪些字母属于同一个书写家族，并分组练习这些字母。
evidenceZh: 根据相似笔画对字母进行分组（例如 c、a、d、g、o 家族——都以曲线起笔）
解释为什么某些字母需要一起练习
使用相同的运笔规律，连贯地书写同一家族内的字母
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否理解某些字母的书写方式相似——例如，“c”、“a”、“d”和“g”都以相同的曲线起笔——并且能够将这些同家族的字母放在一起练习？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Writing digits 0-9
topics.description: Form digits 0-9 correctly and legibly
evidence: Write all digits 0-9 clearly with correct starting points
Form digits the appropriate size relative to letter height
Write numbers legibly so they can be read by others
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes numbers like 3, 5, and 7, are they formed the right way and clearly readable — not reversed or written in an unusual direction?
topics.descriptionZh: 正确且清晰地书写数字0-9
evidenceZh: 以正确的起笔位置清晰地书写所有数字0-9
按照与字母高度相适应的合适比例书写数字
清晰地书写数字，以便他人能够轻松辨认
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}书写如3、5和7等数字时，字形是否正确且清晰易读——没有反向或书写方向异常？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Joining Letters
topics.description: Begin to join letters using diagonal and horizontal strokes, understanding which letter pairs are best left unjoined, forming letters of correct size relative to one another
evidence: Join 'in', 'un', 'it' with a diagonal stroke connecting the letters
Leave letters like 'b' unjoined when followed by certain letters, explaining why
Write with consistent letter sizing on lined paper, ascenders and descenders in proportion
topics.assessmentPrompt: Is {{name}} starting to join up their letters when writing, so that their handwriting flows more smoothly rather than each letter standing completely separate?
topics.descriptionZh: 开始使用斜向和横向笔画（diagonal and horizontal strokes）连接字母，了解哪些字母组合最好保持断开，并能写出大小比例协调的字母。
evidenceZh: 使用斜向笔画连接字母来连写 'in'、'un'、'it'
在 'b' 等字母后接某些特定字母时保持不连写，并能解释原因
在横格纸（lined paper）上保持字母大小一致，上伸部分（ascenders）和下延部分（descenders）比例协调
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 在书写时是否开始将字母连写，使书写更加流畅，而不是让每个字母完全孤立？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Blending Sounds to Read Words
topics.description: Apply phonic knowledge to blend sounds in unfamiliar words containing taught grapheme-phoneme correspondences; respond speedily to graphemes for all 40+ phonemes
evidence: Sound out and blend unfamiliar phonically regular words (e.g. /sh/-/o/-/p/ → 'shop')
Read words containing taught GPCs without excessive sounding out
Distinguish between similarly spelled words by identifying differing letter sounds (e.g. 'big' vs 'bag')
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} comes across a word they haven't seen before, can they sound it out bit by bit and blend the parts together to read it — even if it takes a moment?
topics.descriptionZh: 运用自然拼读知识，将包含已学字素-音素对应关系（grapheme-phoneme correspondences）的生词中的音素进行连音拼读；对所有40多个音素的字素（graphemes）做出快速反应。
evidenceZh: 发音并拼读不熟悉的符合拼读规律的单词（例如 /sh/-/o/-/p/ → 'shop'）
阅读包含已学字素-音素对应关系（GPCs）的单词，无需过度逐音拼读
通过识别不同的字母发音来区分拼写相似的单词（例如 'big' 与 'bag'）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 遇到没见过的单词时，他们能否逐音拼读并将各部分连起来读——即使这需要花一点时间？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Consonant Digraphs
topics.description: Read and spell words containing consonant digraphs and less common consonant spellings (ch, sh, th, ck, tch, ng, ph, wh, k for /k/)
evidence: Read words with consonant digraphs (e.g. 'shop', 'chip', 'that')
Identify the sound made by ph (/f/) and wh (/w/) in words
Spell words ending in -ck (e.g. 'duck') and -tch (e.g. 'match')
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} sees words like 'shop', 'chip', 'ring', or 'photo', can they spot that two letters together make one sound and read the whole word correctly?
topics.descriptionZh: 阅读和拼写包含辅音字母组合以及较少见辅音拼写方式的单词（ch, sh, th, ck, tch, ng, ph, wh, 以及发 /k/ 音的 k）
evidenceZh: 阅读包含辅音字母组合的单词（例如 'shop', 'chip', 'that'）
识别单词中 ph (/f/) 和 wh (/w/) 发出的音
拼写以 -ck（例如 'duck'）和 -tch（例如 'match'）结尾的单词
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 看到像 'shop'、'chip'、'ring' 或 'photo' 这样的单词时，他们能发现两个字母组合在一起发一个音，并正确读出整个单词吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Knowing all letters
topics.description: Recognise and name all uppercase and lowercase letters of the alphabet; name the letters in order and use letter names to distinguish between alternative spellings
evidence: Name all 26 letters in both cases when shown in random order
Recite the alphabet from A to Z
Use letter names to explain spelling choices (e.g. 'Is it c or k in cat?')
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} point to any letter — capital or small — and tell you its name? And can they say the alphabet in order from A to Z?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别并说出字母表中所有的大写和小写字母（uppercase and lowercase letters）；按顺序说出字母，并利用字母名称来区分不同的拼写方式。
evidenceZh: 在随机打乱顺序的情况下，能说出大写和小写两种形式的所有26个字母的名称
能从A到Z按顺序背诵字母表
能使用字母名称来解释拼写选择（例如：‘cat 里面是用 c 还是 k？’）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能指出任意一个字母（无论大写还是小写）并说出它的名称吗？他们能从A到Z按顺序说出整个字母表吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Onsets & Rimes
topics.description: Blend and segment onsets and rimes in single-syllable words; isolate and pronounce individual phonemes (initial, medial, final) in CVC words; add or substitute phonemes to make new words
evidence: Blend onset and rime to say a word (e.g. /c/ + /at/ → 'cat')
Identify the first, middle, or last sound in a CVC word
Change one sound to make a new word (e.g. change /c/ in 'cat' to /b/ → 'bat')
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you slowly say the sounds '/d/ /o/ /g/', can {{name}} blend them together and say 'dog'? And if you say 'cat', can they tell you the three separate sounds: /k/ /a/ /t/?
topics.descriptionZh: 拼读和拆分单音节词中的首音与尾音 (Onsets & Rimes)；分离并准确发音辅音-元音-辅音 (CVC) 词中的单个音素（首音、中音、尾音）；添加或替换音素以构成新词
evidenceZh: 拼合首音和尾音来读出一个单词（例如：/c/ + /at/ → 'cat'）
识别辅音-元音-辅音 (CVC) 单词中的第一个、中间或最后一个音
改变一个音来构成一个新单词（例如：将 'cat' 中的 /c/ 改为 /b/ → 'bat'）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你缓慢地读出 '/d/ /o/ /g/' 这几个音，{{name}} 能把它们拼合在一起并说出 'dog' 吗？如果你说出 'cat'，他们能告诉你这三个独立的音吗：/k/ /a/ /t/？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Rhyming words
topics.description: Recognise and produce rhyming words; join in with predictable phrases and rhymes in stories and poems; learn to appreciate and recite poems by heart
evidence: Identify which words rhyme from a set (e.g. cat, bat, dog)
Generate a word that rhymes with a given target
Join in with repeated refrains and rhyming patterns during shared reading
topics.assessmentPrompt: When you read a rhyming book to {{name}}, do they join in and predict the rhyming words — and can they come up with their own rhyme for a simple word like 'cat'?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别并生成押韵词；在故事和诗歌中参与可预测的短语和押韵；学习欣赏并背诵诗歌
evidenceZh: 从一组词中识别哪些词是押韵的（例如：cat, bat, dog）
生成一个与给定目标词押韵的词
在共读过程中，参与重复的叠句和押韵模式
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当你给 {{name}} 读押韵绘本时，他们是否会跟着念并预测押韵词——并且他们能否为像“cat”这样简单的词自己想出一个押韵词？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Single Letter Sounds
topics.description: Know the primary sound for each consonant and the short and long sounds for the five major vowels; respond speedily to single-letter graphemes
evidence: Say the most common sound for each consonant when shown the letter
Distinguish short vowel sounds in CVC words (e.g. /a/ in 'cat' vs /e/ in 'bed')
Associate long and short vowel sounds with common single-letter spellings
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} look at a letter and quickly say its sound — like 's' makes /s/, 'a' can make a short /a/ as in 'apple' or a long /ā/ as in 'cake'?
topics.descriptionZh: 掌握每个辅音（consonant）的主要发音以及五个主要元音（vowel）的长短音；能够对单字母字素（grapheme）做出快速反应。
evidenceZh: 看到字母时，能说出每个辅音最常见的发音
区分CVC（辅音-元音-辅音）单词中的短元音（例如，'cat'中的/a/与'bed'中的/e/）
将长短元音与常见的单字母拼写联系起来
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否看到一个字母并快速说出它的发音——比如's'发/s/音，'a'在'apple'中发短音/a/，在'cake'中发长音/ā/？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Understanding print
topics.description: Demonstrate understanding that print carries meaning, follows left-to-right top-to-bottom directionality, and is organised page by page in books
evidence: Track words with a finger moving left to right across the page
Turn pages in the correct sequence when handling a book
Point to where reading starts on a page
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} looks at a page in a picture book, do they know to start at the top-left and follow the words left to right, then move down to the next line?
topics.descriptionZh: 能够理解印刷文字承载意义，遵循从左到右、从上到下的方向性 (directionality)，并理解书籍中的文字是按页顺序组织的
evidenceZh: 用手指在书页上从左向右移动来追踪文字
拿书时按正确的顺序翻页
指出书页上开始阅读的位置
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}看图画书的一页时，他们是否知道从左上角开始，从左到右跟随文字，然后再移到下一行？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Vowel Digraphs
topics.description: Read and spell words containing common vowel digraphs (ai, ay, ee, ea, oa, oe, oo, oi, oy) including where a digraph can represent more than one sound
evidence: Read words with vowel digraphs (e.g. 'tree', 'boat', 'rain', 'coin')
Distinguish between different sounds for the same digraph (e.g. 'oo' in 'book' vs 'moon')
Spell words using common vowel digraph patterns
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads a word like 'rain', 'boat', or 'moon', can they recognise the vowel pair that makes a special sound and read the whole word correctly?
topics.descriptionZh: 阅读和拼写包含常见元音字母组合（ai, ay, ee, ea, oa, oe, oo, oi, oy）的单词，包括同一个字母组合可以代表不同发音的情况。
evidenceZh: 阅读包含元音字母组合的单词（例如 'tree'、'boat'、'rain'、'coin'）
区分同一个字母组合的不同发音（例如 'book' 中的 'oo' 与 'moon' 中的 'oo'）
使用常见的元音字母组合模式拼写单词
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 阅读像 'rain'、'boat' 或 'moon' 这样的单词时，他们能否识别出发出特殊声音的元音字母对，并正确读出整个单词？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Compound Words
topics.description: Recognise and spell compound words by identifying the two component words that combine to form a single word
evidence: Identify the two words in a compound (e.g. 'sunshine' = 'sun' + 'shine')
Spell compound words by combining known words
Create compound words from given word pairs
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} look at a word like 'sunshine' or 'football' and spot the two smaller words hiding inside it?
topics.descriptionZh: 通过识别组合成单个词的两个组成部分，来认读并拼写复合词
evidenceZh: 识别复合词中的两个单词（例如：'sunshine' = 'sun' + 'shine'）
通过组合已知单词来拼写复合词
根据给定的单词对创建复合词
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否看着像 'sunshine' 或 'football' 这样的词，并找出里面藏着的两个小单词呢？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Diphthongs and complex vowels
topics.description: Read and spell words containing diphthongs and complex vowel patterns (ow, ou, ew, ue, ie, aw, au) and words ending in -y as a vowel sound
evidence: Read words with variable vowel sounds (e.g. 'ow' in 'cow' vs 'snow')
Decode words with diphthongs (e.g. 'cloud', 'blue', 'pie')
Read words ending in -y pronounced as /ee/ or /igh/ (e.g. 'happy', 'my')
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} read words like 'town', 'cloud', 'flew', 'claw', or 'pie' — spotting the special vowel combinations and saying the right sound for each one?
topics.descriptionZh: 阅读和拼写包含双元音和复杂元音模式（ow, ou, ew, ue, ie, aw, au）的单词，以及以-y结尾发元音的单词
evidenceZh: 阅读具有可变元音发音的单词（例如，'cow' 和 'snow' 中的 'ow'）
拼读包含双元音的单词（例如，'cloud'、'blue'、'pie'）
阅读以-y结尾且发音为 /ee/ 或 /igh/ 的单词（例如，'happy'、'my'）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否读出像 'town'、'cloud'、'flew'、'claw' 或 'pie' 这样的单词——准确识别特殊的元音组合并读出每个组合的正确发音？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: R-Controlled Vowel Sounds
topics.description: Read and spell words containing r-controlled vowels (ar, er, ir, ur, or, ore) and vowel-r patterns where 'r' modifies the vowel sound
evidence: Read words with r-controlled vowels (e.g. 'car', 'bird', 'fork', 'her')
Recognise that 'r' changes the vowel sound (e.g. 'cat' vs 'cart')
Spell words with common r-controlled patterns
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads words like 'car', 'bird', 'nurse', or 'fork', can they recognise that the 'r' after the vowel changes its sound, and read the word correctly?
topics.nameZh: 受 R 控制的元音发音 (R-controlled vowel sounds)
topics.descriptionZh: 阅读和拼写包含受 R 控制元音（ar, er, ir, ur, or, ore）以及“元音+r”组合（其中 'r' 改变元音发音）的单词。
evidenceZh: 阅读包含受 R 控制元音的单词（例如 'car'、'bird'、'fork'、'her'）
认识到 'r' 会改变元音的发音（例如 'cat' 与 'cart' 的对比）
拼写具有常见 R 控制模式的单词
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 阅读像 'car'、'bird'、'nurse' 或 'fork' 这样的单词时，他们能否认识到元音后的 'r' 改变了它的发音，并正确地读出该单词？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Reading Contractions
topics.description: Read and understand contractions with apostrophes, knowing the apostrophe represents omitted letters
evidence: Read common contractions in text (e.g. 'I'm', 'we'll', 'don't')
Match contractions to their expanded forms (e.g. 'I'm' = 'I am')
Explain that the apostrophe shows where letters are missing
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} understand that 'can't' means 'cannot' and 'it's' means 'it is' — knowing the apostrophe stands for the missing letter or letters?
topics.descriptionZh: 阅读并理解带有撇号的缩略形式，知道撇号代表被省略的字母
evidenceZh: 阅读文本中常见的缩略形式（例如：“I'm”、“we'll”、“don't”）
将缩略形式与其完整形式进行匹配（例如：“I'm” = “I am”）
解释撇号表示哪些字母被省略了
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否理解 “can't” 的意思是 “cannot” 以及 “it's” 的意思是 “it is”——并且知道撇号代表被省略的一个或多个字母？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Reading fluently
topics.description: Read aloud books matched to phonic ability accurately and with growing fluency; reread familiar texts to build confidence, speed, and expression
evidence: Read a phonically appropriate text with 90%+ accuracy
Reread familiar texts with improved pace and expression
Read emergent-reader texts with purpose and understanding
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads a book aloud at their level, can they get through most words without stumbling — sounding less like they're decoding and more like they're telling a story?
topics.descriptionZh: 准确且日益流畅地大声朗读与自然拼读(phonics)能力相匹配的书籍；重读熟悉的文本以建立自信、提升速度和表现力
evidenceZh: 以90%以上的准确率朗读符合自然拼读(phonics)水平的文本
以更佳的节奏和表现力重读熟悉的文本
带着目的和理解阅读启蒙读者(emergent-reader)文本
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}大声朗读适合其水平的书籍时，他们能否顺畅地读通大部分单词而不卡顿——听起来不像是在生硬地解码(decoding)，而更像是在讲述一个故事？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Reading High-Frequency Words by Sight
topics.description: Read common high-frequency and exception words automatically by sight, including words with irregular spelling patterns
evidence: Read common exception words instantly without sounding out (e.g. 'the', 'said', 'was', 'you')
Note unusual correspondences between spelling and sound in exception words
Recognise at least 20-30 high-frequency words in connected text
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} instantly recognise everyday words like 'said', 'was', 'they', 'come', and 'because' without needing to sound them out every time?
topics.descriptionZh: 能够通过视觉自动认读常见的高频词和例外词（exception words），包括拼写不符合常规发音规律的单词
evidenceZh: 无需拼读即可瞬间认读常见例外词（例如 'the', 'said', 'was', 'you'）
注意例外词中拼写与发音之间的不规则对应关系
在连贯文本中至少能认出20到30个高频词
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否无需每次拼读，就能瞬间认出 'said'、'was'、'they'、'come' 和 'because' 等日常词汇？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Reading Inflectional Endings
topics.description: Read words containing taught GPCs with common inflectional endings (-s, -es, -ing, -ed, -er, -est) and the prefix un-; read multi-syllable words with taught patterns
evidence: Read suffixed words fluently (e.g. 'jumping', 'wanted', 'faster')
Identify the root word when a suffix is added
Read words with prefix un- (e.g. 'unhappy', 'undo')
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} sees familiar words with different endings — like 'jumped', 'running', 'biggest', or 'unhappy' — can they spot the root word and read the whole thing correctly?
topics.descriptionZh: 阅读包含已学字母-音素对应关系 (GPCs) 并带有常见屈折词尾 (-s, -es, -ing, -ed, -er, -est) 及前缀 un- 的单词；阅读具有已学拼读模式的多音节单词
evidenceZh: 流利地阅读带有后缀的单词（例如 'jumping', 'wanted', 'faster'）
在添加后缀时识别词根 (root word)
阅读带有前缀 un- 的单词（例如 'unhappy', 'undo'）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 看到带有不同词尾的熟悉单词时——比如 'jumped'、'running'、'biggest' 或 'unhappy'——他们能否识别出词根 (root word) 并正确读出整个单词？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Split Digraphs and Magic E
topics.description: Read and spell words containing split digraphs (a-e, e-e, i-e, o-e, u-e) where a final 'e' makes the preceding vowel long
evidence: Read words with split digraphs (e.g. 'cake', 'bike', 'home', 'cube')
Compare minimal pairs showing the effect of the split digraph (e.g. 'cap' vs 'cape')
Spell words with split digraphs correctly
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that the 'e' at the end of words like 'cake', 'bike', or 'home' changes the vowel sound in the middle — making it say its name instead of its short sound?
topics.nameZh: 分离双字母组合 (Split Digraphs) 与魔法E (Magic E)
topics.descriptionZh: 阅读和拼写包含分离双字母组合 (Split Digraphs)（如 a-e, e-e, i-e, o-e, u-e）的单词，其中词尾的字母 'e' 使前面的元音 (Vowel) 发长音。
evidenceZh: 阅读包含分离双字母组合的单词（例如：'cake', 'bike', 'home', 'cube'）
对比展示分离双字母组合作用的最小对立词对 (Minimal pairs)（例如：'cap' 与 'cape'）
正确拼写包含分离双字母组合的单词
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否知道像 'cake'、'bike' 或 'home' 这样单词词尾的 'e' 会改变中间元音 (Vowel) 的发音——使其发字母本音（长音）而不是短音？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Syllables
topics.description: Count, blend, and segment syllables in spoken words; divide written words into syllables as an aid to reading and spelling
evidence: Clap out syllables in spoken words (e.g. 'butterfly' = 3 claps)
Blend syllables to form words (e.g. 'rain' + 'bow' → 'rainbow')
Segment a word into its syllable parts orally
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} clap out the syllables in words — two claps for 'pen-cil' or three for 'com-pu-ter' — and split a spoken word into its parts?
topics.descriptionZh: 计算、拼合和切分口语单词中的音节 (syllables)；将书面单词划分为音节，以辅助阅读和拼写。
evidenceZh: 拍手打出单词中的音节（例如：'butterfly' = 拍3次手）
拼合音节以组成单词（例如：'rain' + 'bow' → 'rainbow'）
口头将单词切分为音节部分
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否通过拍手来数单词中的音节——例如 'pen-cil' 拍2次手，或 'com-pu-ter' 拍3次手——并将口语单词拆分为各个音节部分？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Trigraphs
topics.description: Read and spell words containing trigraphs — three-letter graphemes representing a single sound (igh, air, ear, are)
evidence: Read words with trigraphs (e.g. 'night', 'chair', 'near')
Distinguish between different sounds for 'ear' (e.g. 'hear' vs 'bear')
Identify the single phoneme represented by three letters in a word
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} recognise three-letter combinations like 'igh' in 'night', 'air' in 'chair', and 'ear' in 'hear' — knowing that all three letters together make just one sound?
topics.descriptionZh: 阅读和拼写包含三合字母的单词——即代表单一发音的三个字母图素（graphemes）（如 igh, air, ear, are）
evidenceZh: 阅读包含三合字母的单词（例如 'night', 'chair', 'near'）
区分 'ear' 的不同发音（例如 'hear' 与 'bear' 中的发音区别）
识别单词中由三个字母代表的单一音素（phoneme）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否识别像 'night' 中的 'igh'、'chair' 中的 'air' 以及 'hear' 中的 'ear' 这样的三个字母组合——并知道这三个字母结合在一起只发一个音？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Alternative Spellings for Known Sounds
topics.description: Recognise alternative grapheme-phoneme correspondences for known phonemes (e.g., /dʒ/ as ge/dge/g, /s/ as c, /n/ as kn/gn, /r/ as wr, /ʒ/ as s), reading words with less common spellings for familiar sounds
evidence: Read words with less common spellings for familiar sounds: 'badge', 'giraffe', 'city', 'knock', 'gnaw', 'write', 'treasure'
Identify that the same phoneme can be represented by different graphemes (e.g., /dʒ/ spelled g, ge, dge)
Select the correct alternative GPC to decode an unfamiliar word in context
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that the /j/ sound can be spelled different ways — like in 'jump', 'cage', and 'bridge' — and can they read words with these less common spellings?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别已知音素（phonemes）的替代字素-音素对应关系（grapheme-phoneme correspondences）（例如，/dʒ/ 对应 ge/dge/g，/s/ 对应 c，/n/ 对应 kn/gn，/r/ 对应 wr，/ʒ/ 对应 s），能够阅读包含常见发音但拼写较少见的单词。
evidenceZh: 能够阅读包含常见发音但拼写较少见的单词：'badge'、'giraffe'、'city'、'knock'、'gnaw'、'write'、'treasure'
能够识别同一个音素可以由不同的字素（graphemes）表示（例如，/dʒ/ 拼写为 g、ge、dge）
能够在语境中选择正确的替代字素-音素对应关系（GPC）来解码生词
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否知道/j/音可以有不同的拼写方式——例如在'jump'、'cage'和'bridge'中——并且他们能阅读这些拼写较少见的单词吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Reading with Expression and Accuracy
topics.description: Read aloud with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression (prosody), re-reading familiar texts to build fluency and confidence, and using context to self-correct
evidence: Read a grade-level passage aloud with expression and appropriate pacing
Self-correct miscues during oral reading by re-reading or using context cues
Re-read a familiar book demonstrating increased fluency and confidence
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads a story aloud, do they vary their voice to match the mood — pausing at punctuation, slowing for sad parts, speeding up for excitement?
topics.nameZh: 富有感情且准确地朗读
topics.descriptionZh: 准确、以适当的语速和富有表现力（韵律，prosody）地大声朗读，通过重读熟悉的文本来提升流利度（fluency）和自信心，并利用上下文进行自我纠正
evidenceZh: 富有表现力且以适当的节奏大声朗读符合其年级水平的段落
在朗读过程中通过重读或利用上下文线索来自我纠正误读（miscues）
重读熟悉的书籍，展现出更高的流利度（fluency）和自信心
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 大声朗读故事时，他们是否会调整声音以契合故事情节的情绪——在标点符号处停顿，悲伤的部分放慢语速，激动人心的部分加快语速？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Syllables (age 6+)
topics.description: Decode words of two or more syllables by breaking them into syllable chunks, applying knowledge that every syllable must contain a vowel sound, and blending the parts together
evidence: Read 'rabbit', 'thunder', 'fantastic' by breaking into syllable chunks and blending
Clap or tap syllables in a multi-syllable word, then read each chunk before blending
Identify that every syllable must contain a vowel sound
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} encounters a long word like 'fantastic' or 'umbrella', can they break it into syllables and blend the parts together to read the whole word?
topics.descriptionZh: 通过将两个或更多音节的单词拆分为音节块，运用每个音节必须包含元音 (vowel sound) 的知识，并将各部分连读来解码单词。
evidenceZh: 通过将 'rabbit'、'thunder'、'fantastic' 拆分成音节块并连读来阅读这些单词
拍手或敲击多音节词中的各个音节，然后在连读前先读出每个音节块
识别出每个音节都必须包含元音 (vowel sound)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 遇到像 'fantastic' 或 'umbrella' 这样的长单词时，他们能将其拆分成音节并将各部分连读以读出整个单词吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Decoding unfamiliar words
topics.description: Read Y3-4 exception words with unusual spelling-sound correspondences, applying growing knowledge of morphology and etymology to decode unfamiliar exception words
evidence: Read exception words from the Y3-4 statutory word list accurately (e.g. 'business', 'caught', 'knowledge', 'different')
Identify unusual letter-sound correspondences in exception words and explain why the word does not follow common GPC rules
Use growing knowledge of morphology and etymology to attempt unfamiliar exception words (e.g. recognise the root 'know' in 'knowledge')
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} read trickier exception words — like 'ordinary', 'promise', 'recent', or 'island' — without being thrown off by the parts that don't follow the usual spelling rules?
topics.descriptionZh: 朗读3-4年级的例外词（exception words），这些词具有不寻常的形音对应关系（spelling-sound correspondences），并运用不断积累的构词法（morphology）和词源学（etymology）知识来解码陌生的例外词。
evidenceZh: 准确朗读3-4年级法定词汇表中的例外词（例如：'business', 'caught', 'knowledge', 'different'）
识别例外词中不寻常的字母与发音对应关系（letter-sound correspondences），并解释为什么该词不符合常见的字素-音素对应（GPC）规则
运用不断积累的构词法（morphology）和词源学（etymology）知识来尝试拼读陌生的例外词（例如：识别出 'knowledge' 中的词根 'know'）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否朗读更复杂的例外词（trickier exception words）——例如 'ordinary'、'promise'、'recent' 或 'island'——而不会被不符合常规拼写规则的部分所干扰？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Prefixes and suffixes
topics.description: Read words containing common prefixes and suffixes from the Y3-4 programme, applying knowledge of root words, prefixes and suffixes (morphology and etymology) to read aloud and understand new words
evidence: Read words with common prefixes (dis-, mis-, re-, pre-) and suffixes (-ation, -ous, -ly) by identifying the root word first
Apply morphological knowledge to attempt unfamiliar words (e.g. recognise 'happy' inside 'unhappiness')
Explain how a prefix or suffix changes the meaning or word class of a root word (e.g. 'care' → 'careless' → 'carelessly')
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} sees a word like 'disappear' or 'comfortable', can they spot the root word and figure out what the prefix or suffix is adding to its meaning?
topics.descriptionZh: 阅读3-4年级课程中包含常见前缀和后缀的单词，运用词根、前缀和后缀（形态学(morphology)和词源学(etymology)）知识来朗读并理解新词。
evidenceZh: 通过先识别词根来阅读带有常见前缀（dis-, mis-, re-, pre-）和后缀（-ation, -ous, -ly）的单词
运用形态学(morphology)知识尝试理解生词（例如，识别出'unhappiness'中的'happy'）
解释前缀或后缀如何改变词根的意义或词类（例如：'care' → 'careless' → 'carelessly'）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 看到像 'disappear' 或 'comfortable' 这样的单词时，他们能找出词根并弄清楚前缀或后缀为其添加了什么含义吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Predicting what happens next
topics.description: Predict what might happen next in a story based on what has been read so far; discuss the significance of titles and events
evidence: Make a prediction before turning the page and explain reasoning
Discuss why a title fits or hints at the story content
Revise predictions as new information is encountered in the text
topics.assessmentPrompt: When you stop midway through a story, can {{name}} make a reasonable guess about what might happen next — and explain why they think so based on what's happened so far?
topics.descriptionZh: 根据已读内容预测故事接下来可能发生的情节；探讨标题和事件的意义
evidenceZh: 在翻页前做出预测并解释理由
探讨书名为何贴切或如何暗示故事内容
在阅读中遇到新信息时修正预测
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当在故事中途暂停阅读时，{{name}} 能否对接下来可能发生的情节做出合理猜测，并根据已发生的内容解释其理由？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Book Features and Author's Reasons
topics.description: Identify front cover, back cover, and title page of a book; identify the reasons an author gives to support points in informational text
evidence: Point to and name parts of a book (front cover, back cover, title page)
Use the title page to find the title, author, and illustrator
Identify a reason the author gives for a claim in a simple non-fiction text
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find the contents page or index in a non-fiction book and use it to locate specific information — and do they understand why the author included those features?
topics.nameZh: 书籍特征与作者的理由
topics.descriptionZh: 识别书籍的封面（front cover）、封底（back cover）和书名页（title page）；识别作者在信息类文本中为支持观点而给出的理由。
evidenceZh: 指出并说出书籍各部分的名称（封面、封底、书名页）
利用书名页查找书名、作者和插画师
识别作者在简单的非虚构文本（non-fiction text）中为支持主张（claim）而给出的理由
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否在非虚构类图书中找到目录（contents page）或索引（index）并利用它们查找特定信息——同时理解作者为何要包含这些图书特征（features）？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Characters, settings, and events
topics.description: Identify characters, settings, and major events in stories; become familiar with key stories, fairy tales, and traditional tales and retell them with key details in sequence
evidence: Name the main characters in a story
Describe where and when a story takes place
Retell a familiar story including beginning, middle, and end events
topics.assessmentPrompt: After reading a fairy tale or story together, can {{name}} retell it to you in order — saying who was in it, where it happened, and what the main events were?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别故事中的角色、场景和主要事件；熟悉经典故事、童话和传统故事，并按顺序复述其中的关键细节。
evidenceZh: 说出故事中的主要角色
描述故事发生的时间和地点
复述熟悉的故事，包括开端、发展和结局事件
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在共同阅读完一个童话或故事后，{{name}} 能否按顺序为您复述——说明故事里有哪些角色、故事发生在哪里，以及主要事件是什么？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Comparing Characters Across Stories
topics.description: Compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in familiar stories; identify similarities and differences between two texts on the same topic
evidence: Identify what two stories have in common (e.g. 'Both have a bear character')
Compare information from two books about the same topic
Discuss how characters' experiences are similar or different across stories
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has read two stories with similar themes — like two tales about a brave hero — can they tell you what was the same and what was different between them?
topics.descriptionZh: 比较和对比熟悉故事中角色的冒险与经历；识别同一主题的两篇文本（texts）之间的异同
evidenceZh: 识别两个故事的共同点（例如，‘都有熊这个角色’）
比较两本关于同一主题的书籍中的信息
讨论不同故事中角色的经历有哪些相似或不同之处
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 阅读了两篇主题相似的故事——比如两个关于勇敢英雄的故事——他们能说出这两篇故事有什么相同和不同之处吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Connecting reading to experience
topics.description: Link what is read or heard to own experiences; draw on background knowledge and vocabulary to support understanding of texts
evidence: Make text-to-self connections (e.g. 'This reminds me of when I...')
Use personal experience to understand a character's feelings
Relate events in a story to own life to deepen comprehension
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} hears or reads a story about something familiar — like going to school or visiting a grandparent — do they connect it to their own life and use that to help understand what's happening?
topics.nameZh: 将阅读与个人经验相联系
topics.descriptionZh: 将所读或所听的内容与自身经验相联系；利用背景知识和词汇来辅助理解文本
evidenceZh: 建立文本与自我的联系（text-to-self connections，例如：‘这让我想起了我……的时候’）
利用个人经验来理解角色的感受
将故事中的事件与自己的生活相联系以加深理解
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 听到或读到关于熟悉事物的故事——比如去上学或看望祖父母——时，他们是否会将其与自己的生活联系起来，并利用这些联系来帮助理解所发生的故事？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Different Types of Texts
topics.description: Recognise common types of texts (storybooks, poems, non-fiction); name the author and illustrator and define the role of each in telling or presenting a text
evidence: Distinguish between a story, a poem, and a non-fiction book
Point to and name the author and illustrator on the cover
Explain that the author writes the words and the illustrator makes the pictures
topics.assessmentPrompt: When you hand {{name}} a book, can they tell you whether it's a story or a fact book — and point out the author's name on the cover?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别常见的文本类型（故事书、诗歌、非虚构类读物）；说出作者（author）和插画师（illustrator）的名字，并说明他们在讲述或展示文本时各自的作用。
evidenceZh: 区分故事、诗歌和非虚构类书籍（non-fiction book）
指出并说出封面上的作者（author）和插画师（illustrator）的名字
解释作者负责撰写文字，插画师负责绘制插图
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当你把一本书递给 {{name}} 时，他们能告诉你这是一本故事书还是事实类书籍，并指出封面上作者的名字吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Discussing Texts as a Group
topics.description: Participate in discussions about what is read, taking turns and listening to others; explain understanding clearly; actively engage in group reading activities
evidence: Share ideas about a book in a group discussion
Listen to and respond to others' opinions about a text
Take turns speaking and build on what classmates have said about a book
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}}'s class discusses a book they've all read, does {{name}} join in — sharing their own ideas and listening to what others think, even if their view is different?
topics.descriptionZh: 参与关于阅读内容的讨论，轮流发言并倾听他人；清晰地表达自己的理解；积极参与小组阅读活动
evidenceZh: 在小组讨论中分享对一本书的想法
倾听并回应他人对文本的观点
轮流发言，并在同学发言的基础上进行补充
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}的班级讨论大家都读过的一本书时，{{name}}是否会参与其中——分享自己的想法并倾听他人的看法，即使观点不同？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Listening to Texts Read Aloud
topics.description: Listen to and discuss poems, stories, and non-fiction at a level beyond independent reading; confirm understanding of texts read aloud by asking and answering questions about key details
evidence: Answer questions about a story or non-fiction text read aloud by the teacher
Discuss events, characters, or ideas from chapter books read to the class
Ask for clarification when something in a read-aloud is not understood
topics.assessmentPrompt: After you read a story aloud to {{name}}, can they answer questions about what happened — like who the main character was, where the story took place, and what the problem was?
topics.descriptionZh: 聆听并讨论超出其独立阅读水平的诗歌、故事和非虚构类文本；通过提问和回答关于关键细节的问题，来确认对朗读文本的理解。
evidenceZh: 回答关于老师朗读的故事或非虚构文本的问题
讨论课堂上朗读的章节书（chapter books）中的事件、人物或主题
当对朗读内容有不理解之处时，主动提问以澄清
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当您给{{name}}大声朗读完一个故事后，他们能回答关于故事情节的问题吗——比如主角是谁、故事发生在哪里，以及遇到了什么问题？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Main Topic of Informational Texts
topics.description: Identify the main topic and retell key details of informational texts; describe connections between individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information
evidence: State what a non-fiction text is mostly about in one sentence
List two or three important facts learned from an informational text
Explain how two events or ideas in a text are connected
topics.assessmentPrompt: After {{name}} reads a short fact book — like one about animals or space — can they tell you what the main topic was and give you a few key facts they learned from it?
topics.nameZh: 信息类文本的主要主题
topics.descriptionZh: 识别信息类文本（informational texts）的主要主题并复述关键细节；描述文本中人物、事件、观点或信息片段之间的联系。
evidenceZh: 用一句话说明非虚构类文本（non-fiction text）的主要内容
列出从信息类文本中学到的两到三个重要事实（facts）
解释文本中的两个事件或观点是如何产生联系的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在 {{name}} 阅读了一本简短的知识类读物（例如关于动物或太空的书籍）后，他们能告诉你主要主题是什么，并说出从中学到的几个关键事实吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Pictures and Text Working Together
topics.description: Describe the relationship between illustrations and the text in which they appear; use pictures to support and extend comprehension
evidence: Use pictures to predict or confirm story events
Describe what is happening in an illustration and how it relates to the text
Explain how an illustration adds information not stated in words
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is reading a picture book, do they look at the illustrations to help them understand what's happening in the story — and can they explain how a picture connects to the words on the page?
topics.nameZh: 图片与文本的协同作用
topics.descriptionZh: 描述插图与其所在文本之间的关系；利用图片来支持和拓展理解
evidenceZh: 利用图片预测或确认故事事件
描述插图中发生的事情及其与文本的关系
解释插图如何补充文字中未提及的信息
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}阅读图画书时，他们是否会看插图以帮助理解故事中发生的事情——并且他们能否解释图片与页面上的文字是如何联系起来的？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Reading between the lines
topics.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in literary and informational texts; make simple inferences based on what characters say and do
evidence: Answer 'who', 'what', 'where' questions about a text using evidence
Infer a character's feelings from their actions (e.g. 'She's sad because she's crying')
Make logical guesses about unstated information using text clues
topics.assessmentPrompt: While reading a story, can {{name}} answer questions like "Why did the character do that?" or "How do you think they felt?" — using clues from the text rather than just guessing?
topics.nameZh: 领会言外之意 (Reading between the lines)
topics.descriptionZh: 针对文学类和信息类文本中的关键细节提问并作答；根据角色的言行进行简单的推断。
evidenceZh: 结合文本证据，回答关于文章内容的“谁”、“什么”、“在哪里”等问题
根据角色的行为推断其内心感受（例如：“她很难过，因为她哭了”）
利用文本线索，对文中未直接说明的信息进行合理猜测
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在阅读故事时，{{name}} 能否利用文本中的线索（而不是凭空猜测）来回答诸如“角色为什么这么做？”或“你觉得他/她当时感觉如何？”等问题？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Self-Correcting While Reading
topics.description: Check that text makes sense while reading and self-correct inaccurate reading by re-reading or using context
evidence: Notice when reading does not make sense and stop to re-read
Self-correct errors mid-sentence (e.g. 'Wait, that doesn't sound right')
Use meaning, sentence structure, and visual cues together to monitor reading
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is reading and something doesn't quite make sense, do they go back and re-read that part — or use the surrounding words to work out what a tricky word or sentence means?
topics.nameZh: 阅读中的自我纠正 (Self-Correcting While Reading)
topics.descriptionZh: 在阅读时检查文本是否通顺合理，并通过重读或利用上下文来纠正阅读错误。
evidenceZh: 察觉到阅读内容不合理时，停下来重新阅读
在读句子中途自我纠正错误（例如：‘等等，这听起来不对’）
结合词义、句子结构和视觉提示（visual cues）来监控阅读过程
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 在阅读时遇到不太通顺或合理的内容，他们是否会回头重读那一部分，或者利用周围的词语来推测生词或句子的意思？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Characters' Viewpoints and Responses
topics.description: Identify and compare characters' points of view, recognise who is narrating a story, describe how characters respond to events and challenges, and compare characters' experiences across different stories or versions of the same story
evidence: Identify who is telling a story and explain how you know (e.g. 'The wolf is telling the story because he says I')
Describe how a character responds to a problem or challenge using evidence from the text (e.g. 'When the bridge broke, she decided to swim across')
Compare how two characters from different stories react to a similar situation (e.g. how two heroes show bravery in different ways)
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads a story told from one character's point of view, can they think about how a different character in the same story might have seen events differently?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别并比较人物的观点，辨认故事的叙述者，描述人物对事件和挑战的反应，并比较人物在不同故事或同一故事不同版本中的经历
evidenceZh: 识别讲故事的人并解释你是如何知道的（例如，‘是狼在讲故事，因为他说了“我”’）
使用文本中的证据描述人物如何对问题或挑战做出反应（例如，‘当桥断了时，她决定游过去’）
比较不同故事中的两个人物对相似情况的反应（例如，两位英雄如何以不同的方式展现勇敢）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 阅读以某一人物视角讲述的故事时，他们能否思考故事中的其他人物可能会以怎样的不同视角看待这些事件？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Expressive and Sensory Language
topics.description: Recognise recurring literary language in stories and poetry, identify words and phrases that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses, and discuss favourite words and phrases
evidence: Spot recurring story language such as 'Once upon a time' and 'happily ever after'
Identify sensory words and phrases in a poem: 'the icy wind howled'
Share a favourite word or phrase from a story and explain why it appeals
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads a poem or a story with vivid language, can they pick out a phrase they really liked — and tell you why it works well or how it made them feel?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别故事和诗歌中反复出现的文学语言，找出暗示情感或唤起感官体验的词语和短语，并讨论最喜欢的词语和短语。
evidenceZh: 找出故事中反复出现的文学用语，如‘从前’和‘从此幸福地生活在一起’
识别诗歌中的感官词语和短语，如‘寒风呼啸’
分享故事中喜欢的一个词或短语，并解释它为何吸引人
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 阅读语言生动的诗歌或故事时，他们能挑出一个自己非常喜欢的短语——并告诉你它为什么写得好，或者它让他们有什么样的感受吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Main Topic & Key Details
topics.description: Identify the main topic of a multi-paragraph informational text, determine the focus of specific paragraphs, and explain how key details support the main idea
evidence: Identify the main topic of a multi-paragraph informational text and state the focus of individual paragraphs
Describe how specific details and facts in the text support the main idea
Explain how events, ideas, or steps in a text are connected (e.g. cause-effect, sequence, comparison)
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads a multi-page article — like a school text about a historical event — can they tell you the main idea and then explain what each section was specifically about?
topics.nameZh: 主旨与关键细节 (Main Topic & Key Details)
topics.descriptionZh: 识别多段落说明文（informational text）的主旨，确定特定段落的重点，并解释关键细节如何支撑主旨。
evidenceZh: 识别多段落说明文的主旨，并说明各个段落的重点
描述文本中的具体细节和事实如何支撑主旨（main idea）
解释文本中的事件、观点或步骤是如何相互关联的（例如：因果关系（cause-effect）、顺序（sequence）、对比（comparison））
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}阅读一篇多页的文章——例如关于历史事件的课文——时，他们能说出文章的主旨，并解释每个部分具体讲了什么吗？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Non-Fiction Text Features
topics.description: Recognise different non-fiction text structures and features (headings, contents, glossary, index), understanding how texts are organised to present information
evidence: Use a contents page to find information on a specific topic in a non-fiction book
Identify the purpose of headings, glossary, and index in an information text
Recognise that non-fiction books can be structured as lists, time order, or question-and-answer
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is using a non-fiction book for a school project, do they know how to use the headings, contents page, and index to find what they need quickly?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别不同的非虚构类文本结构和特征（标题 (headings)、目录 (contents)、词汇表 (glossary)、索引 (index)），理解文本如何组织以呈现信息
evidenceZh: 使用目录 (contents page) 在非虚构类图书中查找特定主题的信息
识别信息文本中标题 (headings)、词汇表 (glossary) 和索引 (index) 的作用
认识到非虚构类图书可以按列表 (lists)、时间顺序 (time order) 或问答 (question-and-answer) 结构进行组织
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 为学校项目使用非虚构类图书时，他们是否知道如何使用标题、目录和索引来快速找到所需内容？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Retelling Stories with Structure
topics.description: Retell stories including key details in sequence, describe characters, settings, and major events using evidence from the text, and describe the overall structure of a story (beginning, middle, ending)
evidence: Retell a familiar story in order, including at least three key details from beginning, middle, and end
Describe a character's appearance, actions, or personality using details from the text
Explain how the beginning of a story introduces the characters and setting, and how the ending concludes the action
topics.assessmentPrompt: After reading a story, can {{name}} describe the main character — including what kind of person they are, what they wanted, and how they felt at the end — using details from the book?
topics.descriptionZh: 按顺序复述故事并包含关键细节，运用文本证据描述人物、场景和重大事件，并描述故事的整体结构（开头、中间、结尾）
evidenceZh: 按顺序复述熟悉的故事，至少包含开头、中间和结尾的三个关键细节
运用文本细节描述人物的外貌、行为或性格
解释故事的开头如何介绍人物和场景，以及结尾如何收束情节
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 读完一个故事后，{{name}} 能否运用书中的细节来描述主角——包括他/她是个什么样的人、他/她的愿望是什么，以及最后他/她的感受如何？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Story Sequence and Central Message
topics.description: Discuss the sequence of events in narrative texts and how items of information are related in non-fiction, retelling stories including key details and demonstrating understanding of central message or lesson
evidence: Retell a story in correct sequence with beginning, middle, and end
Identify the central message or lesson of a story
Explain how two pieces of information in a non-fiction text are connected
topics.assessmentPrompt: After {{name}} finishes a chapter book, can they explain the beginning, middle, and end in their own words — and describe what the story was really about at its heart?
topics.descriptionZh: 讨论文本中事件的先后顺序以及非虚构类文本（non-fiction）中信息之间的关联，复述包含关键细节的故事，并展示对中心思想（central message）或寓意的理解。
evidenceZh: 按照正确的顺序复述故事，包括开头、中间和结尾
识别故事的中心思想或寓意
解释非虚构类文本（non-fiction）中两条信息是如何关联的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在{{name}}读完一本章节书后，他们能否用自己的话讲述故事的开头、中间和结尾——并描述这个故事的核心究竟讲了什么？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Forms of Poetry and Performance
topics.description: Recognise different forms of poetry (free verse, narrative poetry, haiku) and discuss their features; prepare poems and play scripts to read aloud and perform with understanding through intonation, tone, volume and action
evidence: Name at least two different forms of poetry and describe a feature of each (e.g., 'narrative poetry tells a story', 'free verse does not have a regular rhyme or rhythm')
Recognise the form of a given poem and explain how you identified it (e.g., 'This is a narrative poem because it has characters and a plot')
Prepare and perform a poem or play script extract showing understanding through changes in intonation, volume, and expression
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads a poem aloud, do they change their voice to match the mood — reading excitedly for a lively poem or quietly for a sad one — rather than reading it flat?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别不同的诗歌形式（自由诗、叙事诗、俳句）并讨论其特征；准备诗歌和剧本进行朗读和表演，通过语调、语气、音量和动作来展现对作品的理解。
evidenceZh: 说出至少两种不同的诗歌形式，并描述它们各自的一个特征（例如，‘叙事诗讲述故事’，‘自由诗没有固定的押韵或节奏’）
识别给定诗歌的形式，并解释你是如何辨认出来的（例如，‘这是一首叙事诗，因为它有人物和情节’）
准备并表演一首诗歌或剧本片段，通过语调、音量和表情的变化来展现对作品的理解
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}大声朗读诗歌时，他们是否会改变声音以契合诗歌的情感——比如用兴奋的语气朗读欢快的诗，或用轻柔的声音朗读悲伤的诗——而不是平淡无味地朗读？

topics.subject: English
topics.name: Inferring Characters' Feelings and Motives
topics.description: Draw inferences from independently-read texts, such as inferring characters' feelings, thoughts and motives from their actions, and justifying inferences with evidence from the text
evidence: Infer a character's feelings or motives from their actions and dialogue (e.g. 'She slammed the door — how is she feeling?')
Justify an inference by quoting or pointing to specific evidence in the text
