topics.description: Evaluate the lasting contributions of Greek and Roman civilisations to modern life — democracy, law, language (Latin roots), architecture (columns, arches, domes), sport (Olympics), philosophy, literature, and theatre — and understand that Greek ideas reached us through Rome, and then through later European civilisations, in a chain of cultural transmission
evidence: List at least five ways ancient Greece and Rome still influence modern life
Explain how Greek culture spread to Rome and then from Rome across Europe
Give a specific modern example of a Greek or Roman legacy such as democratic voting or architectural columns
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} list several things we still have today because of the ancient Greeks and Romans — like democracy, the Olympics, Latin words, and building styles — and explain how those ideas reached us?
topics.nameZh: 希腊与罗马的当代遗产
topics.descriptionZh: 评估希腊和罗马文明对现代生活的持久贡献——民主、法律、语言（拉丁语词根）、建筑（柱子、拱门、圆顶）、体育（奥运会）、哲学、文学和戏剧——并理解希腊的思想是如何先传给罗马，再通过后来的欧洲文明，沿着文化传承的链条传到我们今天的。
evidenceZh: 列出至少五种古希腊和古罗马至今仍影响现代生活的方式
解释希腊文化是如何传播到罗马，然后又从罗马传播到整个欧洲的
举出一个具体的现代希腊或罗马遗产的例子，如民主投票或建筑柱子
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否列出我们今天仍享有的源于古希腊和古罗马的几项事物——比如民主、奥运会、拉丁语词汇和建筑风格——并解释这些思想是如何传承到我们今天的？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Greek Philosophers and Medicine
topics.description: Know that Greek thinkers called philosophers developed ways of understanding the world that still influence us today — Socrates asked challenging questions to test ideas (the Socratic method), Plato imagined the ideal society, Aristotle observed and classified the natural world — and that Hippocrates is called the father of medicine for insisting on natural causes of illness rather than blaming the gods
evidence: Describe what Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle each contributed to thinking and learning
Explain the Socratic method as learning by asking questions rather than just being told answers
Say why Hippocrates is called the father of medicine
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell you about Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle — what each one was famous for — and explain why Greek thinkers still matter today?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解被称为哲学家的希腊思想家们发展出了理解世界的方法，这些方法至今仍影响着我们——苏格拉底通过提出具有挑战性的问题来检验思想（苏格拉底式提问法 / Socratic method），柏拉图构想理想社会，亚里士多德观察并对自然界进行分类——同时了解希波克拉底被称为“医学之父”，因为他坚持从自然原因寻找疾病成因，而不是归咎于神灵。
evidenceZh: 描述苏格拉底、柏拉图和亚里士多德各自对思维和学习做出的贡献
解释苏格拉底式提问法（Socratic method）是如何通过提问来学习，而不是仅仅被告知答案
说明为什么希波克拉底被称为“医学之父”
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能给你讲讲苏格拉底、柏拉图和亚里士多德吗——他们各自因何而闻名——并解释为什么希腊思想家至今仍具有重要意义？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Roman Law, Latin, and Christianity
topics.description: Understand that Roman law became the basis for legal systems across Europe and beyond, that Latin is the root of French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, and Romanian and gave English hundreds of words (e.g. exit, video, annual, education), and that Christianity spread throughout the Roman Empire, eventually becoming its official religion under Emperor Constantine
evidence: Give examples of English words that come from Latin
Explain that Roman law influenced modern legal systems in Europe and beyond
Describe how Christianity spread through the Roman Empire and became its official religion
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} give you examples of English words that come from Latin and explain how Roman law and Christianity spread across Europe through the Roman Empire?
topics.nameZh: 罗马法、拉丁语与基督教
topics.descriptionZh: 了解罗马法如何成为欧洲乃至世界其他地区法律体系的基础，了解拉丁语是法语、西班牙语、意大利语、葡萄牙语和罗马尼亚语的基础，并为英语贡献了数百个单词（例如：exit出口、video视频、annual每年的、education教育），以及了解基督教如何在罗马帝国传播，并最终在君士坦丁大帝时期成为国教。
evidenceZh: 举出一些源自拉丁语的英语单词的例子
解释罗马法如何影响了欧洲及世界其他地区的现代法律体系
描述基督教是如何在罗马帝国传播并成为其国教的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能给你举一些源自拉丁语的英语单词的例子，并解释罗马法和基督教是如何通过罗马帝国传播到欧洲各地的吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Roman Republic and Empire
topics.description: Explain how Rome was first governed as a republic — with elected consuls, a powerful Senate, and a distinction between patricians and plebeians — before becoming an empire ruled by emperors like Augustus (who brought peace, the Pax Romana) and Nero, and compare republican government with Athenian direct democracy
evidence: Describe the Roman Republic's structure: consuls, Senate, patricians, and plebeians
Explain how Rome changed from a republic to an empire under Augustus
Compare Athenian direct democracy (citizens vote on decisions) with Roman republican government (citizens elect representatives)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain the difference between the Roman Republic and the Roman Empire, and compare how Rome and Athens each let people have a say in government?
topics.nameZh: 罗马共和国与罗马帝国
topics.descriptionZh: 解释罗马最初如何作为一个共和国（republic）进行统治——设有选举产生的执政官（consuls）、强大的元老院（Senate），以及贵族（patricians）和平民（plebeians）的区分——后来如何转变为由奥古斯都（Augustus，他带来了“罗马和平” Pax Romana）和尼禄等皇帝统治的帝国，并将共和制政府与雅典的直接民主制（direct democracy）进行比较。
evidenceZh: 描述罗马共和国的结构：执政官（consuls）、元老院（Senate）、贵族（patricians）和平民（plebeians）
解释罗马在奥古斯都（Augustus）统治下如何从共和国转变为帝国
比较雅典的直接民主制（direct democracy，公民对决策进行投票）与罗马的共和制政府（公民选举代表）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释罗马共和国和罗马帝国的区别，并比较罗马和雅典各自是如何让人民在政府中拥有发言权的吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Hidden Voices of Greece and Rome
topics.description: Examine the lives of people usually left out of the Greek and Roman story — enslaved people who made up roughly 30% of Athens and powered Rome's economy, women whose lives varied dramatically between Athens (largely confined to the home) and Sparta (physical training, property ownership), and conquered peoples across both empires — and evaluate whose voices are missing from the historical record and why
evidence: Describe the daily life of an enslaved person in Athens or Rome using available evidence
Compare the lives of women in Athens and Sparta, explaining key differences
Explain why the historical record favours elite men and what this means for our understanding
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell you about the lives of enslaved people or women in ancient Greece and Rome, and explain why we know less about them than about famous leaders?
topics.nameZh: 古希腊与古罗马的隐藏之声
topics.descriptionZh: 探索那些通常被排除在古希腊和古罗马故事之外的人们的生活——包括占雅典人口约30%并推动罗马经济发展的奴隶（被奴役者），生活差异巨大的女性（在雅典主要局限于家庭，而在斯巴达则参与体育训练并拥有财产），以及两大帝国被征服的民族——并评估哪些人的声音在历史记录中缺失了，以及为什么会这样。
evidenceZh: 利用现有证据，描述雅典或罗马奴隶的日常生活
比较雅典和斯巴达女性的生活，解释其中的主要区别
解释为什么历史记录更关注精英男性（精英阶层），以及这对我们的历史认知有什么影响
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能给你讲讲古希腊或古罗马奴隶或女性的生活，并解释为什么我们了解他们的故事比了解著名领袖的故事要少吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Inclusion and Exclusion in Athens
topics.description: Analyse who was included and excluded from Athenian democracy — only free adult male citizens (roughly 30% of adults) could participate, while women, enslaved people (who may have made up a third of the population), and foreign residents (metics) were excluded — and evaluate whether Athens truly deserves the title 'birthplace of democracy' by comparing it with modern representative democracies
evidence: Calculate approximately what fraction of the Athenian population could participate in democracy
List the groups excluded from Athenian democracy and explain why each was excluded
Construct an argument for or against calling Athens a true democracy, using evidence
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain who was left out of Athenian democracy and make a reasoned argument about whether it really deserves to be called the birthplace of democracy?
topics.descriptionZh: 分析谁被纳入或排斥于雅典民主之外——仅有自由成年男性公民（约占成年人口的30%）能够参与，而女性、奴隶（可能占总人口的三分之一）以及外邦居民（metics）均被排斥在外——并通过与现代代议制民主（representative democracies）进行比较，评估雅典是否真正配得上“民主发源地”的称号。
evidenceZh: 估算雅典人口中大约有多大比例（fraction）的人能够参与民主
列出被排斥在雅典民主之外的群体，并解释每个群体被排斥的原因
使用证据构建支持或反对将雅典称为真正民主政体的论点
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释谁被排斥在雅典民主之外，并有理有据地论证其是否真的配得上被称为“民主发源地”？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Troy: Myth or History?
topics.description: Explore how Heinrich Schliemann's excavation at Hisarlik in modern Turkey raised questions about whether the Trojan War described in Homer's Iliad was historical, partly historical, or entirely mythical — understanding that archaeology and literary sources can support or contradict each other, and that the line between myth and history in the ancient world is often blurred
evidence: Describe Schliemann's excavation at Hisarlik and what he claimed to have found
Explain how archaeological evidence at Troy both supports and complicates Homer's story
Discuss why the boundary between myth and history is difficult to draw for the ancient world
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} discuss whether the Trojan War really happened, explaining what archaeology has found at Troy and why the answer isn't simple?
topics.descriptionZh: 探索海因里希·施里曼 (Heinrich Schliemann) 在现代土耳其的希沙利克 (Hisarlik) 进行的考古发掘，是如何引发人们对荷马《伊利亚特》(Iliad) 中描述的特洛伊战争 (Trojan War) 究竟是真实历史、部分真实还是纯粹神话的疑问的——理解考古学 (archaeology) 和文献资料 (literary sources) 可以相互印证或相互矛盾，并且了解在古代世界中，神话与历史的界限往往是模糊的。
evidenceZh: 描述施里曼在希沙利克的发掘工作以及他声称发现的文物。
解释特洛伊的考古证据 (archaeological evidence) 是如何既印证又使荷马的故事变得复杂的。
探讨为什么在古代世界中很难划定神话与历史之间的界限。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能讨论一下特洛伊战争是否真的发生过吗？请解释考古学在特洛伊发现了什么，以及为什么这个问题的答案并不简单。

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Fall of the Roman Republic
topics.description: Trace how Roman political violence — the murder of the Gracchi brothers, civil wars between Marius and Sulla, Caesar's crossing of the Rubicon and assassination on the Ides of March, and the final war between Octavian and Antony — destroyed the Republic and led to one-man rule under Augustus, and debate whether the fall of the Republic was inevitable or a series of choices
evidence: Describe at least three key events in the collapse of the Roman Republic in chronological order
Explain what 'crossing the Rubicon' meant and why it was a point of no return
Construct an argument about whether the Republic's fall was inevitable or could have been prevented
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain the chain of events that destroyed the Roman Republic — from the Gracchi to Caesar's assassination to Augustus — and discuss whether it could have been avoided?
topics.descriptionZh: 追溯罗马政治暴力——格拉古兄弟（Gracchi brothers）遇刺、马略（Marius）与苏拉（Sulla）之间的内战、凯撒（Caesar）跨越卢比孔河（Rubicon）及在三月十五日（Ides of March）遇刺，以及屋大维（Octavian）与安东尼（Antony）之间的最后战争——是如何摧毁共和国并导致奥古斯都（Augustus）一人独裁统治的，并探讨共和国的覆灭是必然的还是由一系列选择造成的。
evidenceZh: 按时间顺序描述罗马共和国崩溃过程中的至少三个关键事件
解释‘跨越卢比孔河（crossing the Rubicon）’的含义以及为什么它是一个无法回头的转折点
论证共和国的覆灭是必然的还是本可避免的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释摧毁罗马共和国的一系列事件——从格拉古兄弟（Gracchi）到凯撒（Caesar）遇刺再到奥古斯都（Augustus）——并探讨这一切本是否可以避免？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Different Accounts of the Same Event
topics.description: Recognise that different people can give different accounts of the same event — and that both can be genuine while still disagreeing
evidence: Wineburg corroboration heuristic
Initiating Historical Thinking in Elementary Schools
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard two different versions of the same historical event, would they understand that both people might be telling the truth from their own point of view — and want to know why the versions differ?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识到不同的人可以对同一事件给出不同的叙述——并且即使存在分歧，双方的说法都可能是真实的。
evidenceZh: Wineburg交叉印证启发法（Wineburg corroboration heuristic）
在小学阶段开启历史思维（Initiating Historical Thinking in Elementary Schools）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}听到关于同一历史事件的两种不同说法，他们能否理解这两人可能都是从各自的视角讲述事实，并且想要探究这两种说法为何存在差异？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Evidence from the Past
topics.description: Understand that everything we know about the past comes from evidence — objects, buildings, pictures, documents, and stories that have survived
evidence: Wineburg historical thinking framework
Historical Thinking in the Elementary Years (ERIC)
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} learns about something that happened long ago, do they ask how we know about it — and understand that someone had to find or leave behind that evidence?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解我们所知道的关于过去的一切都来源于证据——那些幸存下来的物品、建筑、图片、文献和故事
evidenceZh: 温伯格历史思维框架 (Wineburg historical thinking framework)
小学阶段的历史思维 (Historical Thinking in the Elementary Years (ERIC))
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 学习很久以前发生的事情时，他们会问我们是如何知道这些的——并且理解必须有人发现或留下了这些证据吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Vocabulary: historical thinking
topics.description: Know and use the vocabulary of historical thinking — source, evidence, primary source, secondary source, artefact, chronology, chronological order, BC/BCE, AD/CE, century, decade, era, period, timeline, excavation, archaeologist, interpretation, corroborate, bias, perspective — and apply these terms when discussing how we know about the past and how reliable our knowledge is
evidence: Correctly use BC/BCE and AD/CE to place events in time and explain what the letters stand for
Distinguish between a primary source and a secondary source with an example of each
Use 'evidence', 'interpretation', and 'bias' correctly in a sentence about a historical source
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you asked {{name}} whether something they read in a history book was definitely true, could they explain why it might not be — using words like 'source', 'evidence', or 'bias'?
topics.descriptionZh: 掌握并运用历史思维的专业词汇——史料 (source)、证据 (evidence)、一手史料 (primary source)、二手史料 (secondary source)、文物 (artefact)、年代学 (chronology)、时间顺序 (chronological order)、公元前/纪元前 (BC/BCE)、公元/纪元 (AD/CE)、世纪 (century)、年代 (decade)、时代 (era)、时期 (period)、时间线 (timeline)、发掘 (excavation)、考古学家 (archaeologist)、诠释 (interpretation)、印证 (corroborate)、偏见 (bias)、视角 (perspective)——并在探讨我们如何认知过去以及认知的可靠性时运用这些词汇。
evidenceZh: 正确使用公元前/纪元前 (BC/BCE) 和公元/纪元 (AD/CE) 将事件按时间定位，并解释这些字母缩写代表什么
区分一手史料 (primary source) 和二手史料 (secondary source)，并为两者各举一个例子
在关于历史史料的句子中正确使用“证据 (evidence)”、“诠释 (interpretation)”和“偏见 (bias)”
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你问 {{name}} 他们在历史书中读到的内容是否绝对真实，他们能否解释为什么可能并非如此——并运用“史料 (source)”、“证据 (evidence)”或“偏见 (bias)”等词汇？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Checking Sources Against Each Other
topics.description: Corroborate: check whether multiple sources agree on the same facts — and investigate why they might not
evidence: Wineburg corroboration heuristic
Historical Thinking in the Elementary Years (ERIC)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was trying to find out what really happened in a historical event, would they know to look at more than one source and compare what they say?
topics.descriptionZh: 相互印证（Corroborate）：检查多个信息来源是否认同相同的事实——并调查它们不一致的原因。
evidenceZh: 温伯格交叉印证启发法（Wineburg corroboration heuristic）
小学阶段的历史思维（Historical Thinking in the Elementary Years (ERIC)）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}想要弄清楚一个历史事件的真实情况，他们是否知道要查阅多个信息来源并比较它们的说法？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Questioning Historical Sources
topics.description: Before trusting a historical source, ask: who made this, when, and why? — the answers shape how much weight the source should carry
evidence: Wineburg sourcing heuristic
Teaching Historical Thinking Using Primary Sources (Library of Congress)
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} looks at a historical document, photograph, or account, do they ask who created it and what that person's reasons or point of view might have been?
topics.descriptionZh: 在相信一份历史史料之前，请先思考：这是谁留下的？什么时候留下的？为什么留下？——这些答案决定了该史料应被赋予多大的参考价值。
evidenceZh: 温伯格溯源启发法 (Wineburg sourcing heuristic)
利用一手史料教授历史思维（美国国会图书馆）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 查看历史文献、照片或记述时，他们是否会追问是谁创作了它，以及该创作者的可能动机或观点是什么？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Understanding People in Their Own Time
topics.description: Understand that people in the past saw the world very differently from us — judge their actions by the context they lived in, not only by today's values
evidence: Historical Empathy: A Cognitive-Affective Theory (ERIC)
Year 4-6 historical empathy research
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learns that people in the past did something that seems wrong today, can they think about why those people might have believed it was normal or right at the time?
topics.nameZh: 理解历史人物所处的时代
topics.descriptionZh: 明白过去的人们看待世界的方式与我们大不相同——要根据他们所处的时代背景来评价他们的行为，而不仅仅是用今天的价值观去评判。
evidenceZh: 历史共情：一种认知-情感理论 (Historical Empathy: A Cognitive-Affective Theory) (ERIC)
4-6年级历史共情研究 (Year 4-6 historical empathy research)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 了解到过去的人们做了一些在今天看来似乎是错误的事情，他们能否思考一下为什么那些人当时会认为这是正常或正确的？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Evidence Versus Interpretation
topics.description: Distinguish between historical evidence and historical interpretation — evidence is what survived, interpretation is the argument a historian builds from it, and the same evidence can support different arguments
evidence: Development of historical understanding among 9-14 year olds
Ways of Seeing: Evidence and Learning in the History Classroom (RRCHNM)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} understand that two historians can look at the same evidence and reach different conclusions — and that history involves argument and judgment, not just facts?
topics.descriptionZh: 区分历史证据（historical evidence）与历史诠释（historical interpretation）——证据是留存下来的史料，诠释是历史学家基于这些史料构建的论点，且相同的证据可以支持不同的论点。
evidenceZh: 9-14岁儿童历史理解能力的发展
观察方式：历史课堂中的证据与学习（Ways of Seeing: Evidence and Learning in the History Classroom）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否理解两位历史学家面对相同的证据可以得出不同的结论——并且历史不仅关乎事实，还涉及论证与判断？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Kings & Queens
topics.description: What medieval kings and queens did: ruling the land, making laws, collecting taxes; the crown and throne as symbols of power; the Tower of London
evidence: Explain what a medieval king or queen did (ruled, made laws, led armies, collected taxes)
Describe at least one symbol of royal power (crown, throne, sceptre)
Name one famous medieval monarch or describe the Tower of London's role
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what a king or queen actually did in medieval times, beyond just wearing a crown?
topics.descriptionZh: 中世纪国王与王后的职责：统治土地、制定法律、征收税赋；王冠（crown）与王座（throne）作为权力的象征；伦敦塔（Tower of London）。
evidenceZh: 解释中世纪国王或王后做了什么（统治、制定法律、统帅军队、征收税赋）
描述至少一种皇室权力的象征（王冠、王座、权杖（sceptre））
说出一位著名的中世纪君主，或者描述伦敦塔的作用
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能解释一下在中世纪，国王或王后除了戴王冠之外，实际上还要做哪些事情吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Knights & Armour
topics.description: What knights were: trained warriors who served a lord; armour, shields, swords, and lances; the code of chivalry as rules for how knights should behave
evidence: Describe what a knight wore and carried (armour, helmet, shield, sword, lance)
Explain that knights trained from a young age and served a lord
Name one rule of the code of chivalry (be brave, be honest, protect the weak)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe what a knight looked like, what they did, and at least one rule they were supposed to follow?
topics.descriptionZh: 骑士的定义：经过训练、为领主服务的武士；盔甲、盾牌、长剑和长矛；骑士精神（Chivalry）作为骑士行为规范的准则。
evidenceZh: 描述骑士的穿着和携带的物品（盔甲、头盔、盾牌、长剑、长矛）
解释骑士从小接受训练并效忠于领主
说出骑士精神（Chivalry）的一条准则（勇敢、诚实、保护弱小）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否描述骑士的外貌、他们的职责，以及他们应遵守的至少一条准则？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Medieval Clothing
topics.description: What people wore in medieval times: peasant clothes (wool, linen) vs noble clothes (silk, fur, bright colours); no zippers or buttons; how clothes showed your place in society
evidence: Describe what a medieval peasant would typically wear
Explain how noble clothing was different from peasant clothing
Give one way that what you wore showed your place in society
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw pictures of different medieval people, could they tell you which ones were rich and which were poor just by looking at their clothes?
topics.descriptionZh: 中世纪人们的穿着：农民服装（羊毛、亚麻）与贵族服装（丝绸、毛皮、鲜艳的颜色）的对比；没有拉链或纽扣；服装如何显示你的社会地位
evidenceZh: 描述中世纪农民通常穿什么
解释贵族服装与农民服装有什么不同
举出一个例子说明你的穿着如何显示你的社会地位
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到不同中世纪人物的图片，他们能仅仅通过看衣服分辨出哪些人富有、哪些人贫穷吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Medieval Food & Feasts
topics.description: What people ate in medieval times: bread and pottage for ordinary people, grand feasts for the rich; no forks, eating with hands; the great hall as the centre of castle life
evidence: Describe what ordinary people ate most days (bread, pottage, vegetables, ale)
Explain how a feast in a great hall was different from everyday meals
Name one surprising table manner from medieval times (no forks, shared cups, food thrown on the floor)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} went to a medieval banquet, could they describe what food would be served and which table manners would surprise them?
topics.descriptionZh: 中世纪人们的饮食：普通人日常吃面包和浓汤（pottage），富人则享用盛大的宴会；没有叉子，直接用手进食；大厅（great hall）是城堡生活的中心。
evidenceZh: 描述普通人大多数日子吃什么（面包、浓汤（pottage）、蔬菜、麦芽酒（ale））
解释大厅（great hall）里的宴会与日常饮食有何不同
说出一个中世纪令人惊讶的餐桌礼仪（不用叉子、共用杯子、把食物扔在地上）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 去参加一场中世纪的宴会，他们能描述出会上什么菜，以及哪些餐桌礼仪会让他们感到惊讶吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Robin Hood & King Arthur
topics.description: The legends of Robin Hood (Sherwood Forest, stealing from the rich, Merry Men) and King Arthur (Round Table, Excalibur, Camelot); that these are stories, not proven history, but reflect medieval values
evidence: Retell the basic story of Robin Hood or King Arthur
Name at least two characters from one of these legends
Explain that these are legends (stories) rather than proven facts
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell you the story of Robin Hood or King Arthur and explain that these are legends rather than definitely true history?
topics.descriptionZh: 罗宾汉（舍伍德森林、劫富济贫、快乐好汉）与亚瑟王（圆桌、王者之剑、卡美洛）的传说；知道这些是故事而非被证实的历史，但它们反映了中世纪的价值观。
evidenceZh: 复述罗宾汉或亚瑟王的基本故事
说出其中一个传说中至少两个人物的名字
解释这些是传说（故事）而不是被证实的事实
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能给你讲讲罗宾汉或亚瑟王的故事，并解释这些是传说而不是绝对真实的历史吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: The Vikings
topics.description: Who the Vikings were: seafaring warriors and traders from Scandinavia; longships; Viking raids on Britain; that Vikings also settled and farmed
evidence: Describe who the Vikings were and where they came from
Explain what made longships special (fast, could sail in shallow water, dragon prows)
State that Vikings were not just raiders but also farmers, traders, and settlers
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell you who the Vikings were, where they came from, and that they did more than just raid and fight?
topics.descriptionZh: 维京人是谁：来自斯堪的纳维亚（Scandinavia）的航海勇士和商人；长船（longships）；维京人对不列颠的袭击；维京人也是定居者和农夫。
evidenceZh: 描述维京人是谁以及他们来自哪里
解释长船（longships）的特殊之处（速度快、能在浅水区航行、带有龙头船首）
说明维京人不仅是掠夺者，还是农夫、商人和定居者
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能告诉你维京人是谁、他们来自哪里，以及他们不仅会掠夺和战斗，还会做其他事情吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Village Life
topics.description: Daily life for ordinary people in a medieval village: thatched houses, farming, baking bread, fetching water; how different life was from today
evidence: Describe what a typical medieval village looked like (thatched cottages, fields, church)
Name at least three daily tasks a medieval villager would do
Give two differences between life in a medieval village and life today
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe what a normal day would be like for a child living in a medieval village, and how it would differ from their own life?
topics.descriptionZh: 中世纪乡村里普通人的日常生活：住茅草屋、种地、烤面包、打水；以及那时的生活与今天有多么不同。
evidenceZh: 描述一个典型的中世纪村庄看起来是什么样子的（茅草屋、农田、教堂）
说出中世纪村民每天至少会做的三项日常任务
给出中世纪乡村生活与今天生活的两个不同之处
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否描述一下生活在中世纪村庄的孩子普通的一天会是怎样的，以及这与他们自己的生活有什么不同？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: What Is a Castle?
topics.description: What a castle is: a fortified building used as both a home and a defence; key parts including towers, moat, drawbridge, and thick walls; why castles were built
evidence: Name at least four parts of a castle (tower, moat, drawbridge, walls, gatehouse)
Explain that castles were both homes and defences
Describe why someone in medieval times would need a castle
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visited a ruined castle, could they point out the main parts and explain why it was built that way?
topics.descriptionZh: 什么是城堡：一种兼具居住与防御功能的防御性建筑（fortified building）；关键部分包括塔楼（tower）、护城河（moat）、吊桥（drawbridge）和厚重的城墙；以及建造城堡的原因。
evidenceZh: 至少说出城堡的四个组成部分（塔楼、护城河、吊桥、城墙、城门楼）
解释城堡既是居住地也是防御工事
描述中世纪时期的人为什么需要城堡
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}参观一座废弃的城堡，他们能指出主要部分并解释当时为什么这样建造吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Anglo-Saxon Britain
topics.description: Who the Anglo-Saxons were: Germanic peoples who settled in Britain after the Romans left; their kingdoms, villages, place names, art, and eventual conversion to Christianity
evidence: Explain who the Anglo-Saxons were and when they came to Britain (after the Romans left)
Name at least two Anglo-Saxon kingdoms (e.g. Wessex, Mercia, Northumbria)
Give an example of Anglo-Saxon influence still visible today (place names ending in -ton, -ham, -bury)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain who the Anglo-Saxons were and point out that many English place names come from Anglo-Saxon words?
topics.descriptionZh: 盎格鲁-撒克逊人是谁：在罗马人离开后定居不列颠的日耳曼民族；他们的王国、村庄、地名、艺术，以及最终皈依基督教的过程
evidenceZh: 解释盎格鲁-撒克逊人是谁，以及他们何时来到不列颠（在罗马人离开之后）
说出至少两个盎格鲁-撒克逊王国的名字（例如威塞克斯、麦西亚、诺森布里亚）
举出一个今天仍可见的盎格鲁-撒克逊人影响的例子（如以 -ton、-ham、-bury 结尾的地名）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释一下盎格鲁-撒克逊人是谁，并指出许多英国地名都源自盎格鲁-撒克逊语词汇？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Battle of Hastings and 1066
topics.description: The events of 1066: the death of Edward the Confessor, three claimants to the throne, the Battle of Hastings, William the Conqueror, and the Bayeux Tapestry as a historical source
evidence: Explain why there was a crisis when Edward the Confessor died in 1066
Describe the Battle of Hastings and its outcome
Explain what the Bayeux Tapestry is and why it is important as a historical source
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell you what happened in 1066, why it mattered, and what the Bayeux Tapestry shows us about those events?
topics.nameZh: 黑斯廷斯战役与1066年 (Battle of Hastings and 1066)
topics.descriptionZh: 1066年的重大事件：忏悔者爱德华 (Edward the Confessor) 的逝世、三位王位争夺者、黑斯廷斯战役 (Battle of Hastings)、征服者威廉 (William the Conqueror)，以及作为历史重要史料的贝叶挂毯 (Bayeux Tapestry)。
evidenceZh: 解释为什么在1066年忏悔者爱德华 (Edward the Confessor) 去世时会出现王位继承危机
描述黑斯廷斯战役 (Battle of Hastings) 的过程及其最终结果
解释什么是贝叶挂毯 (Bayeux Tapestry)，以及为什么它作为历史史料非常重要
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能告诉你1066年发生了什么、为什么这些事件很重要，以及贝叶挂毯 (Bayeux Tapestry) 向我们展示了关于这些事件的哪些内容吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Castle Design Through the Ages
topics.description: How castles were built and evolved: from wooden motte-and-bailey to stone keeps to concentric castles; rooms and their uses; how castle design responded to new attack methods
evidence: Describe the difference between an early motte-and-bailey castle and a later stone castle
Name at least three rooms or areas in a medieval castle and their purpose
Explain one way castle design changed to resist new attack methods
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how castles changed over time and describe what different rooms inside a castle were used for?
topics.descriptionZh: 城堡是如何建造和演变的：从早期的木制土墩与外庭（motte-and-bailey）城堡，到石制主楼（stone keeps），再到同心圆城堡（concentric castles）；各个房间及其用途；城堡设计如何应对新的攻击方式
evidenceZh: 描述早期的木制土墩与外庭（motte-and-bailey）城堡和后来的石制城堡之间的区别
说出中世纪城堡中至少三个房间或区域及其用途
解释一种城堡设计为了抵御新攻击方式而做出的改变
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能解释一下城堡随着时间推移发生了哪些变化，并描述一下城堡内部不同房间的用途吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Medieval Pyramid of Power
topics.description: How medieval society was organised: king at the top, then lords, then knights, then peasants/serfs; who owed what to whom; the pyramid of power and mutual obligations
evidence: Draw or describe the feudal pyramid showing king, lords, knights, and peasants
Explain what each level owed to the level above (loyalty, military service, labour)
Describe what a serf's life was like and why they couldn't easily leave
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain the medieval class system — who was at the top, who was at the bottom, and what each group had to do for the others?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解中世纪社会是如何组织的：国王在最顶端，往下依次是领主（lords）、骑士（knights），最底层是农民和农奴（peasants/serfs）；各个阶层之间互相承担什么义务；认识权力金字塔以及他们之间的相互责任。
evidenceZh: 画出或描述展示国王、领主、骑士和农民的封建金字塔（feudal pyramid）
解释每一层级对上一级负有什么义务（如忠诚、兵役、劳役）
描述农奴（serf）的生活是什么样的，以及为什么他们不能轻易离开
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能解释一下中世纪的阶级制度（class system）吗——谁在最顶层，谁在最底层，每个群体都需要为其他群体做些什么？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Siege Warfare
topics.description: How castles were attacked and defended: siege weapons (trebuchets, battering rams, siege towers), boiling liquids, arrow slits, murder holes; the drama of a medieval siege
evidence: Name at least three siege weapons or attack methods
Describe at least two ways a castle was designed to resist attack
Explain what a siege was and why it could last weeks or months
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was reading about a medieval siege, could they explain the weapons used to attack a castle and the clever ways defenders fought back?
topics.descriptionZh: 城堡是如何被攻打和防守的：包括各种攻城武器（投石机 trebuchets、攻城槌 battering rams、攻城塔 siege towers）、倾倒滚烫液体、射箭孔（arrow slits）、杀人洞（murder holes）；以及中世纪围城战中惊心动魄的故事。
evidenceZh: 说出至少三种攻城武器或攻击方法
描述至少两种城堡用来抵御攻击的设计方法
解释什么是围城战，以及为什么它可能会持续数周或数月
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 正在阅读关于中世纪围城战的内容，他们能解释用来攻打城堡的武器以及防守方巧妙反击的方法吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: The Black Death
topics.description: The Black Death of 1348-49: what the plague was, how it spread, its devastating death toll; how it changed society by giving surviving workers more power and higher wages
evidence: Describe what the Black Death was and at least two symptoms
Explain how the plague spread (fleas on rats, person to person)
Describe one major way the Black Death changed society (fewer workers led to higher wages, peasants gained power)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell you what the Black Death was, how it spread, and why it actually ended up changing society in unexpected ways?
topics.descriptionZh: 1348至1349年的黑死病：这场瘟疫究竟是什么，它是如何传播的，以及它造成的惨重死亡人数；它又是如何通过让幸存的工人获得更多权力和更高工资来改变社会的。
evidenceZh: 描述黑死病（Black Death）是什么，并指出至少两种症状
解释瘟疫是如何传播的（老鼠身上的跳蚤、人与人之间的传播）
描述黑死病改变社会的一个主要方式（工人减少导致工资上涨，农民获得了更多权力）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能告诉你黑死病是什么、它是如何传播的，以及为什么它最终以意想不到的方式改变了社会吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: The Crusades
topics.description: A simplified account of the Crusades: why Europeans travelled to the Holy Land, what they found there, the cultural exchange between Christian Europe and the Islamic world
evidence: Explain in simple terms why European armies travelled to the Holy Land
Describe at least one thing Europeans learned from the Islamic world during the Crusades
Acknowledge that the Crusades involved violence and suffering on both sides
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what the Crusades were and describe something that Europeans learned about the wider world through these journeys?
topics.descriptionZh: 十字军东征的简单概述：欧洲人为什么要前往圣地，他们在那里发现了什么，以及基督教欧洲与伊斯兰世界之间的文化交流。
evidenceZh: 用通俗易懂的语言解释欧洲军队前往圣地的原因
描述至少一件欧洲人在十字军东征期间从伊斯兰世界学到的知识或事物
认识到十字军东征给交战双方都带来了暴力与苦难
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释一下什么是十字军东征，并描述一件欧洲人通过这些旅程了解到的关于更广阔世界的事物吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: The Medieval Church
topics.description: The enormous power of the medieval Church: monasteries and the daily life of monks and nuns; building great cathedrals; pilgrimage as a religious journey; the Church's influence over everyday life
evidence: Explain why the Church was so powerful in medieval times (owned land, controlled education, people feared God's punishment)
Describe what daily life was like for a monk or nun
Explain what a pilgrimage was and give one reason people went on them
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain why the Church was such a big part of everyone's life in medieval times and what monks and nuns actually did all day?
topics.descriptionZh: 中世纪教会的巨大权力：修道院（monastery）以及修士和修女的日常生活；建造宏伟的大教堂（cathedral）；作为宗教旅程的朝圣（pilgrimage）；教会对日常生活的影响。
evidenceZh: 解释为什么教会在中世纪时期如此强大（拥有土地、控制教育、人们害怕受到上帝的惩罚）
描述修士（monk）或修女（nun）的日常生活是什么样的
解释什么是朝圣（pilgrimage），并给出一个人们去朝圣的原因
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释一下为什么教会在中世纪是每个人生活中如此重要的一部分，以及修士和修女们每天实际上都在做些什么吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Vikings vs Anglo-Saxons
topics.description: The conflict between Vikings and Anglo-Saxons for control of England: Viking raids, Alfred the Great's resistance, the Danelaw, Athelstan as first king of all England, Edward the Confessor
evidence: Describe the Viking raids on Anglo-Saxon England and their impact
Explain who Alfred the Great was and why he was important
Describe what the Danelaw was (the area of England under Viking control)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell you about the struggle between the Vikings and Anglo-Saxons for control of England, and who Alfred the Great was?
topics.nameZh: 维京人与盎格鲁-撒克逊人的较量 (Vikings vs Anglo-Saxons)
topics.descriptionZh: 维京人（Vikings）和盎格鲁-撒克逊人（Anglo-Saxons）为了争夺英格兰的控制权而发生的冲突：包括维京人的突袭、阿尔弗雷德大帝（Alfred the Great）的抵抗、丹麦法区（Danelaw）的建立、阿瑟尔斯坦（Athelstan）成为第一位统治全英格兰的国王，以及忏悔者爱德华（Edward the Confessor）。
evidenceZh: 描述维京人对盎格鲁-撒克逊英格兰的突袭及其影响
解释阿尔弗雷德大帝（Alfred the Great）是谁以及他为何重要
描述丹麦法区（Danelaw）是什么（即英格兰受维京人控制的地区）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能给你讲讲维京人（Vikings）和盎格鲁-撒克逊人（Anglo-Saxons）为争夺英格兰控制权而进行的斗争，以及阿尔弗雷德大帝（Alfred the Great）是谁吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Art & Architecture
topics.description: Medieval cultural achievements: illuminated manuscripts, Gothic cathedrals (flying buttresses, stained glass), Gregorian chant, the Bayeux Tapestry; art and architecture as expressions of faith and power
evidence: Describe what an illuminated manuscript is and who made them
Name at least two features of Gothic cathedral architecture (pointed arches, flying buttresses, stained glass)
Explain how medieval art and buildings were connected to the Church and religious belief
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visited a Gothic cathedral, could they point out features like stained glass windows and flying buttresses and explain why medieval people built such impressive buildings?
topics.descriptionZh: 中世纪的文化成就：泥金装饰手抄本（illuminated manuscripts）、哥特式大教堂（飞扶壁 flying buttresses、彩色玻璃 stained glass）、格里高利圣咏（Gregorian chant）、贝叶挂毯（Bayeux Tapestry）；艺术与建筑作为信仰和权力的表达。
evidenceZh: 描述什么是泥金装饰手抄本（illuminated manuscript）以及是由谁制作的
说出哥特式大教堂建筑的至少两个特征（尖拱 pointed arches、飞扶壁 flying buttresses、彩色玻璃 stained glass）
解释中世纪的艺术和建筑是如何与教会及宗教信仰联系在一起的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 参观一座哥特式大教堂，他们能指出彩色玻璃窗和飞扶壁（flying buttresses）等特征，并解释为什么中世纪的人们要建造如此令人惊叹的建筑吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Crime & Punishment
topics.description: How justice worked in medieval times: trial by ordeal, trial by combat, the role of the sheriff; punishments including stocks, pillory, and dungeons; how different it was from modern justice
evidence: Describe at least two medieval methods of deciding guilt (trial by ordeal, trial by combat)
Name at least two medieval punishments and explain what they involved
Compare one aspect of medieval justice to how justice works today
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe how criminals were caught and punished in medieval times and explain what seems unfair by today's standards?
topics.descriptionZh: 中世纪时期的司法运作方式：神明裁判（trial by ordeal）、决斗审判（trial by combat）、治安官的角色；惩罚方式包括足枷（stocks）、示众柱（pillory）和地牢（dungeons）；以及它与现代司法的巨大差异。
evidenceZh: 描述至少两种中世纪判定有罪的方法（神明裁判、决斗审判）
说出至少两种中世纪的惩罚方式并解释其具体内容
将中世纪司法的某一方面与现代司法的运作方式进行比较
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否描述中世纪时期罪犯是如何被捕和受罚的，并解释按照今天的标准哪些做法显得不公平？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Magna Carta and Limiting Royal Power
topics.description: King John, the barons' revolt, and the sealing of the Magna Carta in 1215; what the Magna Carta said about limiting the king's power; its lasting importance for democracy and rights
evidence: Explain why the barons rebelled against King John
Describe what the Magna Carta said (the king must follow the law too, fair trial rights)
Explain why the Magna Carta still matters today (foundation of democracy and human rights)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell you what the Magna Carta is and why a document from 1215 is still considered important today?
topics.descriptionZh: 约翰国王、贵族反叛以及1215年《大宪章》的签署；《大宪章》关于限制国王权力的规定；它对民主和权利的持久重要性
evidenceZh: 解释贵族们为什么反叛约翰国王
描述《大宪章》的内容（国王也必须遵守法律，保障公平审判的权利）
解释为什么《大宪章》至今仍然重要（它是民主和人权的基础）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能告诉你《大宪章》是什么，以及为什么一份1215年的文件今天仍然被认为很重要吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Medieval Legacy in Modern Life
topics.description: What the Middle Ages gave us: Parliament, universities, common law, Gothic architecture, the English language (Anglo-Saxon + Norman French), place names, surnames; why we are still fascinated by the medieval world
evidence: Name at least three things from the Middle Ages that still affect our lives today
Explain how the English language was shaped by Anglo-Saxon and Norman French
Give a reason why people today are still fascinated by the medieval period (castles, knights, fantasy literature, games)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name several things we still have today — from Parliament to English words to university degrees — that actually began in the Middle Ages?
topics.nameZh: 中世纪在现代生活中的遗产
topics.descriptionZh: 中世纪留给我们的遗产：议会、大学、普通法（common law）、哥特式建筑（Gothic architecture）、英语（盎格鲁-撒克逊语 + 诺曼法语）、地名、姓氏；以及为什么我们今天仍然对中世纪的世界着迷。
evidenceZh: 列举至少三件来自中世纪且至今仍影响我们生活的事物
解释英语是如何在盎格鲁-撒克逊语（Anglo-Saxon）和诺曼法语（Norman French）的影响下发展形成的
给出一个现代人依然对中世纪着迷的原因（如城堡、骑士、奇幻文学、游戏等）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否说出几件我们今天仍在拥有的事物——从议会到英语词汇，再到大学学位——而这些事物实际上都起源于中世纪？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Medieval Worlds Beyond Europe
topics.description: The medieval world beyond Europe: the Islamic Golden Age (maths, medicine, architecture), the Mali Empire and Mansa Musa, Song Dynasty China; how the medieval world was connected through trade routes like the Silk Road
evidence: Name at least two achievements of the Islamic Golden Age (algebra, hospitals, architecture)
Describe who Mansa Musa was and why he is remembered
Explain how the Silk Road connected distant parts of the medieval world through trade
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell you about important civilisations outside Europe during the Middle Ages and explain how the Silk Road connected different parts of the world?
topics.nameZh: 欧洲以外的中世纪世界
topics.descriptionZh: 欧洲以外的中世纪世界：伊斯兰黄金时代（数学、医学、建筑）、马里帝国与曼萨·穆萨、中国宋朝；中世纪世界如何通过丝绸之路等贸易路线紧密相连
evidenceZh: 列举伊斯兰黄金时代至少两项成就（代数、医院、建筑）
描述曼萨·穆萨是谁以及他为何被世人铭记
解释丝绸之路如何通过贸易将中世纪世界的遥远地区连接起来
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能告诉你中世纪欧洲以外的重要文明，并解释丝绸之路是如何将世界不同地区连接起来的吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Printing Press & Renaissance
topics.description: The invention of the printing press by Gutenberg and its arrival in England with William Caxton; how printed books changed everything; the transition from the Middle Ages to the Renaissance
evidence: Explain what the printing press was and why it was revolutionary
Describe William Caxton's role in bringing printing to England
Give at least one way printed books changed society (more people could read, ideas spread faster)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain why the invention of the printing press was one of the most important moments in history and how it changed the world?
topics.descriptionZh: 古腾堡（Gutenberg）发明了印刷机，随后威廉·卡克斯顿（William Caxton）把它带到了英国；看看印刷书籍是如何改变一切的；了解人类是如何从中世纪（Middle Ages）过渡到文艺复兴（Renaissance）时期的。
evidenceZh: 解释什么是印刷机，以及为什么它的出现具有革命性（revolutionary）
描述威廉·卡克斯顿（William Caxton）在把印刷术引进英国时发挥的作用
说出至少一种印刷书籍改变社会的方式（比如：让更多人学会了阅读，思想传播得更快了）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能解释一下为什么印刷机的发明是历史上最重要的时刻之一，以及它是如何改变世界的吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Towns & Trade
topics.description: The growth of medieval towns: markets, guilds, the merchant class; how towns won charters of self-governance; the shift from purely rural to partly urban life
evidence: Describe how medieval towns were different from villages (markets, walls, guilds, more people)
Explain what a guild was and why it mattered for tradespeople
Describe one way towns changed medieval society (new merchant class, more freedom for townspeople)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain why medieval towns grew and how the rise of markets and guilds changed the way people lived and worked?
topics.descriptionZh: 中世纪城镇的发展：市场、行会（guilds）、商人阶层；城镇如何获得自治特许状（charters of self-governance）；从纯粹的乡村生活向部分城市生活的转变
evidenceZh: 描述中世纪的城镇与村庄有什么不同（有市场、城墙、行会，人口更多）
解释什么是行会（guild），以及它为什么对手工业者（tradespeople）很重要
描述城镇改变中世纪社会的一种方式（出现了新的商人阶层，城镇居民获得了更多自由）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释一下为什么中世纪的城镇会发展壮大，以及市场和行会（guilds）的兴起是如何改变人们的生活和工作方式的吗？

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Women in the Middle Ages
topics.description: The lives of medieval women: noblewomen managing estates, peasant women's hard daily work, nuns and abbesses, notable figures like Eleanor of Aquitaine and Joan of Arc
evidence: Describe the different lives of noblewomen, peasant women, and nuns
Name at least one notable medieval woman and explain what she did
Explain one way women's lives in medieval times were more restricted than today
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell you about what life was like for women in medieval times and name a famous medieval woman who made her mark on history?
topics.descriptionZh: 中世纪女性的生活：管理庄园的贵族女性、从事繁重日常劳作的农妇、修女与女修道院长（abbesses），以及阿基坦的埃莉诺（Eleanor of Aquitaine）和圣女贞德（Joan of Arc）等著名历史人物。
evidenceZh: 描述贵族女性、农妇和修女的不同生活
说出至少一位著名的中世纪女性并解释她的主要事迹
举例说明中世纪女性的生活在某一方面比今天受到更多限制
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能给你讲讲中世纪女性的生活是什么样的，并说出一位在历史上留下印记的著名中世纪女性吗？

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Asking for Help
topics.description: Ask for help when you've had a go yourself and are still stuck — knowing when to ask is a skill in itself
evidence: Hattie visible learning
self-regulated learning research
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has tried something and is still stuck, do they come and ask for help rather than sitting frustrated or giving up?
topics.descriptionZh: 当你自己尝试过后依然遇到困难时，请主动寻求帮助——知道何时求助本身就是一项重要的技能。
evidenceZh: 哈蒂可见学习 (Visible Learning)
自我调节学习研究 (Self-Regulated Learning)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 尝试了某件事却依然遇到困难，他们是会主动寻求帮助，而不是坐在那里感到沮丧或直接放弃吗？

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Checking Your Own Work
topics.description: After finishing a task, look back at what you did and ask yourself: does this seem right?
evidence: After finishing a piece of work, re-read or review it without being asked to
Spot and correct at least one error in their own work by checking back through it
Describe what they checked for — e.g. 'I re-read each line to make sure my answers matched the question'
topics.assessmentPrompt: After {{name}} finishes a piece of work or activity, do they look it over themselves to check it seems right before saying they're done?
topics.descriptionZh: 完成任务后，回头看看自己做的内容，并问问自己：这样做对吗？
evidenceZh: 完成作业后，无需提醒便能主动重新阅读或检查
通过回头检查，发现并纠正自己作业中的至少一处错误
描述自己检查的内容——例如：‘我重读了每一行，以确保答案与题目要求相符’
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 在完成作业或活动后，会在宣布完成前自己检查一遍，确认做得对不对吗？

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Persisting When It's Hard
topics.description: Keep trying when something feels hard — making mistakes and trying again is how learning happens
evidence: Keep working on a difficult task for a sustained period without giving up or asking someone else to do it
After making a mistake, try again with a different approach rather than saying 'I can't do it'
Talk about difficulty positively — e.g. 'This is hard but I'm getting better' rather than 'I'm no good at this'
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} finds a puzzle or activity really tricky, do they keep trying different ways rather than giving up straight away?
topics.descriptionZh: 当感到困难时继续尝试——犯错并重新尝试是学习发生的过程。
evidenceZh: 持续专注于困难的任务，不放弃也不求助他人代劳。
犯错后，尝试用不同的方法再次挑战，而不是说“我做不到”。
以积极的态度谈论困难——例如说“这很难，但我正在进步”，而不是说“我不擅长这个”。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 觉得某个拼图或活动非常棘手，他们是否会不断尝试不同的方法，而不是立刻放弃？

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Feeling of not understanding
topics.description: Notice the feeling of not understanding — recognise when something is confusing rather than reading or listening past it
evidence: comprehension monitoring research
Flavell metacognitive monitoring
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is reading or listening and something doesn't make sense, do they notice and say so — rather than carrying on as if they understood?
topics.descriptionZh: 察觉不理解的感觉——识别出令人困惑之处，而不是在阅读或听讲时直接略过。
evidenceZh: 理解监控研究 (comprehension monitoring research)
弗拉维尔元认知监控 (Flavell metacognitive monitoring)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在阅读或倾听时遇到不理解的内容，他们能注意到并表达出来，而不是装作理解了继续往下进行吗？

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Planning a Task
topics.description: Make a simple plan before starting a task: what do I need to do, and what should I do first?
evidence: Before starting a task, describe what they need to do and what order to do it in
Break a larger task into smaller steps without being prompted — e.g. 'First I'll read the question, then I'll draw a diagram'
Gather the materials or information they need before beginning, rather than starting and then stopping to find things
topics.assessmentPrompt: Before {{name}} starts a bigger task — like writing a story or making something — do they take a moment to think about what they'll do first?
topics.descriptionZh: 在开始一项任务前制定一个简单的计划：我需要做什么，以及首先应该做什么？
evidenceZh: 在开始任务前，能描述需要做什么以及做的顺序
无需提示即可将较大的任务分解为较小的步骤——例如，“首先我会读题目，然后我会画个图表”
在开始前收集所需的材料或信息，而不是开始后再停下来寻找
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在{{name}}开始一项较大的任务（如写故事或制作东西）之前，他们会花点时间思考首先要做什么吗？

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Thinking Before Starting
topics.description: Before starting something new, stop and think: what do I already know about this topic?
evidence: prior knowledge activation research
Ausubel meaningful learning
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is about to learn something new — say a new topic in science or a new type of word problem — do they first think about what they already know?
topics.descriptionZh: 在开始新事物之前，停下来想一想：关于这个主题，我已经知道了什么？
evidenceZh: 先验知识激活研究 (prior knowledge activation research)
奥苏贝尔有意义学习 (Ausubel meaningful learning)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 准备学习新内容时——比如科学的新主题或新型应用题 (word problem)——他们会先思考自己已经知道了什么吗？

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Connecting New & Old Ideas
topics.description: Look for connections between new ideas and things you already know — how does this fit with what I've learned before?
evidence: elaborative encoding
schema theory (Bartlett, Rumelhart)
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} learns something new, do they ever say things like 'oh, that's like...' and connect it to something they already knew?
topics.descriptionZh: 寻找新知识与已知事物之间的联系——这如何与我之前学过的知识相契合？
evidenceZh: 精细编码 (elaborative encoding)
图式理论 (schema theory) (Bartlett, Rumelhart)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}学习新事物时，他们有没有说过类似‘哦，这就像……’的话，并将其与已知的事物联系起来？

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Spotting Patterns
topics.description: Spot patterns and recurring structures — in numbers, words, nature, sounds, or events — and use them to make sense of new information
evidence: Spot a pattern in a set of numbers, shapes, or facts without being told to look for one
Use a pattern they noticed to make a prediction — e.g. 'The next one should be 16 because it's doubling each time'
Explain the pattern they found and why they think it works
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} notices a pattern — like a number pattern, a word ending, or something that keeps recurring — do they use it to figure out what comes next or predict something new?
topics.descriptionZh: 发现数字、词语、自然、声音或事件中的规律（Patterns）和重复结构（Recurring structures），并利用它们来理解新信息。
evidenceZh: 在未被提示的情况下，主动发现一组数字、图形或事实中的规律
利用发现的规律进行预测——例如："下一个应该是16，因为每次都在翻倍"
解释他们发现的规律，并说明为什么认为该规律成立
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 注意到某种规律——例如数字规律、单词词尾或不断重复的现象时——他们会利用该规律来推断接下来是什么，或预测新事物吗？

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Teaching It Back
topics.description: After learning something new, explain it in your own words — to yourself, a family member, or even a toy
evidence: Explain a concept they've learned to someone else in their own words, not just repeating what the teacher said
After teaching something to a friend or sibling, identify a gap in their own understanding that they only noticed through explaining
Summarise a lesson by pretending to teach it back, using examples they made up themselves
topics.assessmentPrompt: After {{name}} learns something at school, can they explain it back to you in their own words — not just repeat what they were told?
topics.descriptionZh: 学习新知识后，用自己的话将其解释出来——可以是对自己、家人，甚至是对玩具说。
evidenceZh: 用自己的话向他人解释学到的概念，而不是仅仅重复老师说的话
在教朋友或兄弟姐妹后，发现自己理解中的知识盲区，这些盲区只有在讲解时才会被察觉
通过模拟教学来总结课程内容，并使用自己构思的例子
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}在学校学到新知识后，他们能用自己的话向您复述吗——而不是仅仅重复被告知的内容？

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Trying a New Approach
topics.description: When your first approach isn't working, try a different one — being flexible about strategies is part of being a good learner
evidence: When stuck on a problem, try a completely different approach rather than repeating the same method — e.g. drawing a picture instead of writing equations
Describe a time they changed strategy mid-task and explain why the new approach worked better
Accept that their first idea might not work and show willingness to start over with a fresh plan
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} tries one way to solve a problem and it isn't working, do they try a different approach rather than just repeating the same thing?
topics.descriptionZh: 当你的第一种方法行不通时，尝试另一种方法——灵活运用策略 (strategies) 是成为优秀学习者的重要品质。
evidenceZh: 遇到难题卡住时，尝试完全不同的方法，而不是重复同一种方法——例如，用画图代替列方程式 (equations)
描述一次在任务中途改变策略的经历，并解释为什么新方法效果更好
接受自己的初步想法可能行不通，并表现出愿意制定全新计划重新开始的积极态度
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 尝试了一种解决问题的方法但行不通，他们会尝试换一种方法，而不是仅仅重复同样的做法吗？

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Describing Rules & Patterns
topics.description: When you notice a pattern repeating, describe it as a rule that works every time — then test whether the rule holds in new cases
evidence: Describe a pattern or rule they've noticed in their own words — e.g. 'Every time you add 0 to a number, it stays the same'
Test whether a rule they've described holds for new examples they haven't seen before
Explain the difference between noticing a pattern and proving it always works
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} spots a pattern — like a grammar rule or a number pattern — can they describe it as a general rule and then check whether it works in new examples?
topics.descriptionZh: 当你注意到某种规律（pattern）在重复时，将其描述为一条每次都能适用的规则（rule），然后测试这条规则在新的情况中是否依然成立。
evidenceZh: 用自己的话描述他们注意到的规律或规则——例如：‘每次给一个数加0，结果都保持不变’
测试他们描述的规则在他们以前没见过的新例子中是否依然成立
解释发现规律（noticing a pattern）和证明它始终成立（proving it always works）之间的区别
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 发现了一个规律——比如语法规则或数字规律——他们能否将其描述为一条通用规则，然后检查它在新的例子中是否依然有效？

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Learning from Mistakes
topics.description: When you get something wrong, investigate why — what did you misunderstand or overlook? Analysing errors is one of the most powerful ways to learn
evidence: error analysis research
Hattie feedback effect size
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} gets something wrong on a test or activity, do they look at the mistake to understand what went wrong — rather than just moving on?
topics.descriptionZh: 当你做错时，要探究原因——是哪里没理解对，还是忽略了什么？分析错误（error analysis）是最有效的学习方法之一。
evidenceZh: 错误分析研究（error analysis research）
哈蒂的反馈效应量（Hattie feedback effect size）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 在考试或活动中做错时，他们会去研究这个错误以了解出错的原因，而不是直接略过吗？

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Transferring Skills
topics.description: Recognise when a skill or strategy learned in one subject or situation can be applied in a completely different one
evidence: transfer of learning research
Perkins & Salomon transfer taxonomy
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} ever spotted that something they learned in one subject — like a way of organising information — could help them in a completely different one?
topics.descriptionZh: 能够意识到在一个学科或情境中学到的技能或策略，可以应用到完全不同的其他学科或情境中
evidenceZh: 学习迁移研究 (transfer of learning research)
珀金斯与萨洛蒙迁移分类法 (Perkins & Salomon transfer taxonomy)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否曾经发现，他们在某个学科中学到的东西——比如一种整理信息的方法——能够在一个完全不同的学科中帮到他们？

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Understanding Why
topics.description: Go beyond knowing *that* something is true — ask *why* it is true and *how* it works
evidence: Ask 'why?' or 'how does that work?' about something they've been told, rather than just accepting it
Explain the reason behind a rule or method — e.g. 'We carry the ten because 13 ones is the same as 1 ten and 3 ones'
Show deeper understanding by connecting a new idea to something they already know — e.g. 'Oh, that's like when we...'
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} often ask 'but why?' when they learn a fact — wanting to understand the reason behind it rather than just accepting it?
topics.descriptionZh: 不满足于仅仅知道某件事是真的——还要追问为什么它是真的，以及它是如何运作的。
evidenceZh: 对被告知的内容追问‘为什么？’或‘这是怎么运作的？’，而不是盲目接受
解释规则或方法背后的原因——例如：‘我们要满十进一（carry the ten），因为13个一等于1个十和3个一’
通过将新想法与已知事物联系起来展示更深入的理解——例如：‘哦，这就像我们之前……’
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 学习一个事实时，他们是否经常追问‘但为什么呢？’——想要理解背后的原因，而不是仅仅接受它？

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Choosing a Strategy
topics.description: Before starting a study task, choose a deliberate strategy; after finishing, evaluate honestly whether that strategy actually helped
evidence: Before starting a task, name the strategy they plan to use and explain why — e.g. 'I'll make a mind map first because there's a lot to organise'
After finishing, honestly evaluate whether their chosen strategy helped or whether a different one would have been better
Describe at least three different learning strategies and explain when each works best
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} ever talk about *how* they're going to study or practise something — and afterwards think about whether that approach worked?
topics.descriptionZh: 在开始学习任务前，有意识地选择一种策略；完成后，诚实地评估该策略是否真的有帮助。
evidenceZh: 在开始任务前，说明计划使用的策略并解释原因——例如，‘我会先画思维导图，因为有很多内容需要整理’
完成后，诚实地评估所选策略是否有帮助，或者换一种策略是否会更好
描述至少三种不同的学习策略，并解释每种策略在何时最有效
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否会谈论他们打算*如何*学习或练习某件事——并在事后思考这种方法是否奏效？

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Reflecting After Learning
topics.description: After completing a piece of learning, reflect on the process: what helped most, what was confusing, and what would you do differently next time?
evidence: Kolb reflective learning cycle
Hattie & Timperley feedback model
topics.assessmentPrompt: After {{name}} finishes a project or topic at school, do they reflect on how the learning went — not just whether the result was good, but what worked and what didn't?
topics.descriptionZh: 在完成一段学习后，对学习过程进行反思：什么最有帮助，什么令人困惑，以及下次你会采取哪些不同的做法？
evidenceZh: 库伯反思学习循环 (Kolb reflective learning cycle)
哈蒂和廷珀利反馈模型 (Hattie & Timperley feedback model)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 在学校完成一个项目或主题后，他们是否会反思学习的过程——不仅仅是结果是否好，而是哪些方法有效，哪些无效？

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Finding Knowledge Gaps
topics.description: Survey your own understanding of a whole topic — identify where your knowledge is solid, where it is shaky, and what still needs work
evidence: metacognitive monitoring research
Flavell metacognition framework
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} how well they understand a whole topic, can they tell you honestly which parts they feel confident on and which parts need more work?
topics.descriptionZh: 评估自己对整个主题的理解程度——明确哪些知识掌握得扎实，哪些地方还比较薄弱，以及哪些部分还需要继续学习。
evidenceZh: 元认知监控研究 (metacognitive monitoring research)
弗拉维尔元认知框架 (Flavell metacognition framework)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你问 {{name}} 对整个主题的理解程度，他们能诚实地指出哪些部分自己很有把握，哪些部分还需要多加练习吗？

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Setting Learning Goals
topics.description: Set a specific learning goal, work towards it with a deliberate plan, then honestly assess whether you achieved it and what you would change
evidence: Set a specific, achievable learning goal for themselves — e.g. 'By Friday I want to know all my 7-times tables' rather than just 'get better at maths'
Make a simple plan for how to reach their goal and follow through on it over several days
After the deadline, honestly assess whether they achieved the goal and describe what they would do differently next time
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} ever set themselves a specific learning goal — like 'I want to get better at times tables by the end of the week' — and then honestly judge whether they met it?
topics.descriptionZh: 设定一个具体的学习目标，制定明确的计划并为之努力，然后诚实地评估自己是否达成了目标，以及思考下次会做出哪些改变。
evidenceZh: 为自己设定一个具体且可实现的学习目标——例如‘到周五我想熟练背诵所有7的乘法口诀（7-times tables）’，而不仅仅是‘提高数学成绩’
制定一个简单的计划来达成目标，并在接下来的几天里坚持执行
在截止日期后，诚实地评估自己是否达成了目标，并描述下次会采取哪些不同的做法
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否曾为自己设定过具体的学习目标——比如‘我想在周末前提高乘法口诀（times tables）的掌握程度’——然后诚实地评估自己是否达成了目标？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Buyers & Sellers
topics.description: When someone makes or has something, they can sell it; when someone wants something, they can buy it; introduction to the concept of exchange and transactions
evidence: Explain what a buyer does and what a seller does
Act out a simple buying and selling transaction with a partner
Describe a time they or a family member bought something from a person (market stall, car boot sale, bake sale)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} set up a stall at a school fair, could they explain who the buyers and sellers are and what each person does?
topics.descriptionZh: 当某人制作或拥有某件物品时，他们可以出售它；当某人想要某件物品时，他们可以购买它；这是对交换（exchange）和交易（transaction）概念的初步介绍。
evidenceZh: 解释买家和卖家分别做什么
与同伴角色扮演一次简单的买卖交易
描述一次自己或家人从他人那里购买物品的经历（如市场摊位、旧货市场、烘焙义卖）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在学校游园会上设立一个摊位，他们能解释谁是买家、谁是卖家，以及每个人分别做什么吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Goods & Services
topics.description: Some people make things (goods) and some people do things for others (services); recognising both in everyday life and understanding that both have value
evidence: Sort a set of pictures into goods (things you can touch) and services (things people do for you)
Give three examples of goods and three examples of services from their everyday life
Explain that both making things and helping people are valuable kinds of work
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell you the difference between a product you buy in a shop and a service like getting a haircut, and give examples of each?
topics.descriptionZh: 有些人制造物品（商品），有些人为他人提供服务（服务）；在日常生活中识别这两者，并理解它们都具有价值。
evidenceZh: 将一组图片分类为商品（你能触摸到的物品）和服务（人们为你做的事情）
举出日常生活中的三个商品例子和三个服务例子
解释制造物品和帮助他人都是有价值的工作
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能告诉你商店里购买的商品和像理发这样的服务之间有什么区别，并分别举例吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Making Something to Sell
topics.description: The experience of creating a product to sell — a craft, a drawing, baked goods; what makes something worth buying; pride in making something others want
evidence: Create a simple product (craft, drawing, baked item) that could be sold
Explain what makes their product good enough for someone to want to buy it
Suggest a fair price for their product and give a reason
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} made something at home — like friendship bracelets or decorated biscuits — could they explain why someone might want to buy them?
topics.descriptionZh: 体验创造待售产品的过程——如手工艺品、画作或烘焙食品；理解什么特质让物品值得购买；体会因制作出他人喜爱的物品而产生的自豪感。
evidenceZh: 制作一件可供出售的简单物品（如手工艺品、画作或烘焙食品）
解释自己的物品好在哪里，能让别人产生购买意愿
为物品建议一个合理的价格并说明理由
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}在家里制作了物品——比如友谊手环或装饰饼干——他们能解释一下为什么别人可能会想买吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Who Is a Customer?
topics.description: Understanding that a customer is someone who buys what you make or do; thinking about what customers want and need; the idea that businesses serve people
evidence: Define what a customer is in their own words
Suggest what a customer might look for when deciding whether to buy something (quality, price, looks nice)
Explain why it matters to think about what the customer wants, not just what you want to make
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was planning to sell lemonade at a school event, could they think about what would make people want to buy their lemonade rather than someone else's?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解顾客就是购买你制作的产品或享受你提供服务的人；思考顾客想要和需要什么；明白企业是为人们服务的。
evidenceZh: 用自己的话定义什么是顾客
提出顾客在决定是否购买某物时可能会看重什么（质量、价格、外观好看）
解释为什么思考顾客的需求很重要，而不仅仅是考虑自己想做什么
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 计划在学校活动中卖柠檬水，他们能否思考一下，怎样才能让人们想买他们的柠檬水，而不是别人的？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Being a Good Seller
topics.description: Customer service, fairness, and honesty in business; keeping promises to customers; why being trustworthy matters for repeat business and reputation
evidence: Explain why being honest about what you're selling matters
Describe what good customer service looks like (being polite, helpful, keeping promises)
Give an example of how being unfair or dishonest could hurt a business
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sold something to a friend and it broke the next day, would they understand why it's important to make it right rather than ignore it?
topics.descriptionZh: 商业中的客户服务、公平与诚实；信守对顾客的承诺；为什么值得信赖对于吸引回头客和建立信誉非常重要
evidenceZh: 解释为什么对你所卖的商品保持诚实很重要
描述良好的客户服务是什么样的（有礼貌、乐于助人、信守承诺）
举一个例子说明不公平或不诚实会如何损害一门生意
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 把一件东西卖给了朋友，结果第二天就坏了，他们会明白为什么弥补过失比视而不见更重要吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Costs & Revenue
topics.description: It costs money to make things (costs/expenses); you earn money by selling them (revenue); if revenue is more than costs, that's profit; if costs are more, that's a loss
evidence: Explain what costs, revenue, and profit mean using a simple example
Calculate profit from a given scenario (e.g. spent £3 on ingredients, sold cakes for £8, profit = £5)
Explain what happens if costs are higher than revenue (you make a loss)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} spent £4 on supplies for a lemonade stand and earned £10 selling lemonade, could they tell you how much profit they made?
topics.descriptionZh: 制作物品需要花钱（成本/支出）；通过出售物品可以赚钱（收入/营收）；如果收入大于成本，那就是利润；如果成本大于收入，那就是亏损。
evidenceZh: 用一个简单的例子解释成本、收入和利润的含义
根据给定场景计算利润（例如：花3英镑买原料，卖蛋糕收入8英镑，利润=5英镑）
解释如果成本高于收入会发生什么（即产生亏损）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 花了4英镑购买柠檬水摊的物资，卖柠檬水赚了10英镑，他们能告诉你他们赚了多少钱（利润）吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Having a Business Idea
topics.description: Where business ideas come from; spotting everyday problems and thinking of solutions; the difference between inventing something new and improving something that exists
evidence: Identify a simple everyday problem and suggest a product or service that could solve it
Explain the difference between an invention (something new) and an innovation (making something better)
Describe where one real entrepreneur got their business idea from
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you asked {{name}} to think of a problem at school or home that they could solve by making or selling something, could they come up with an idea?
topics.descriptionZh: 商业想法的来源；发现日常问题并思考解决方案；发明（invention，即创造全新事物）与创新（innovation，即改进现有事物）之间的区别。
evidenceZh: 识别一个简单的日常问题，并建议一种能够解决该问题的产品或服务
解释发明（invention）与创新（innovation）之间的区别，即创造全新事物与改进现有事物的不同
描述一位真实的企业家（entrepreneur）是如何获得其商业想法的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你让{{name}}想一个在学校或家里遇到的问题，并且他们可以通过制作或销售某种东西来解决这个问题，他们能想出一个点子吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Learning from Failure
topics.description: Not every business idea works; entrepreneurs try, fail, learn, and try again; iteration and resilience as core entrepreneurial skills; famous failure-to-success stories
evidence: Give an example of a famous entrepreneur who failed before succeeding
Explain what they would do differently if a business idea didn't work the first time
Describe why failing and trying again is better than giving up
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s first attempt at a project or business idea didn't work out, would they see it as a chance to improve rather than a reason to give up?
topics.descriptionZh: 并不是每个商业点子都能立刻成功；创业者（entrepreneurs）会尝试、失败、学习，然后再试一次；不断迭代（iteration）和保持韧性（resilience）是核心的创业技能；我们还会学习那些从失败走向成功的著名创业故事。
evidenceZh: 举一个著名创业者在成功之前经历过失败的例子
解释如果商业点子第一次没有成功，他们会做些什么不同的尝试
描述为什么失败后再次尝试比直接放弃更好
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 第一次尝试某个项目或商业点子没有成功，他们会把它看作是改进的机会，而不是放弃的理由吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Making a Simple Plan
topics.description: Before starting a business, making a simple plan: what will I make or do, who will buy it, what do I need, how much will it cost, and what price will I charge?
evidence: Write or draw a simple business plan covering: product, customer, materials needed, and price
Identify at least three things they would need before they could start selling
Explain why planning ahead is better than just starting without thinking
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wanted to run a small business at a school fair, could they write a simple plan covering what they'd sell, what they'd need, and what they'd charge?
topics.descriptionZh: 在开始做生意之前，制定一个简单的计划：我要做或卖什么？谁会买？我需要准备什么？要花多少钱？我要定什么价格？
evidenceZh: 写下或画出简单的商业计划，包括：产品、顾客、所需材料和价格
找出在开始售卖前至少需要准备的三样东西
解释为什么提前计划比想都不想就直接开始要好
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 想在学校游园会上做点小生意，他们能写一个简单的计划，说明他们要卖什么、需要准备什么以及定什么价格吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Marketing Basics
topics.description: How people find out about what you're selling; signs, posters, social media, word of mouth; being persuasive; the basics of advertising and promotion
evidence: Design a simple poster or advert for a product or service
Name at least three ways to let people know about something you're selling
Explain why a catchy name or eye-catching design helps sell more
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wanted to advertise a car wash or bake sale, could they design a poster that would make people want to come?
topics.descriptionZh: 人们如何了解你售卖的商品；招牌、海报、社交媒体、口口相传；如何说服别人；广告与推广的基础知识
evidenceZh: 为某款产品或服务设计一张简单的海报或广告
说出至少三种让人们知道你在卖东西的方法
解释为什么响亮的名字或吸睛的设计能帮你卖出更多商品
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}想为洗车或烘焙义卖活动做宣传，他们能设计出一张吸引大家来参加的海报吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Teamwork in Business
topics.description: Most businesses need more than one person; working together, dividing tasks, and using different people's strengths; the value of teamwork in business
evidence: Describe how they would divide tasks in a team business project (one person makes, one sells, one designs)
Explain why using people's different strengths makes a business better
Give an example of a problem that could happen if a team doesn't work well together
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was working with friends to run a stall at a fair, could they suggest how to divide up the jobs so everyone plays to their strengths?
topics.descriptionZh: 大多数企业需要多人协作；通过共同努力、分配任务并发挥每个人的优势；体会团队合作在商业中的重要价值。
evidenceZh: 描述在团队商业项目中他们将如何分配任务（一个人负责制作，一个人负责销售，一个人负责设计）
解释为什么发挥每个人不同的优势能让企业变得更好
举例说明如果团队配合不好可能会引发什么问题
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 和朋友们一起在集市上经营一个摊位，他们能提出如何分配工作的建议，让每个人都能发挥自己的优势吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Ethics in Business
topics.description: Being honest, being fair, treating workers well, not harming the environment; what makes a 'good' business; whether businesses should care about more than profit
evidence: Name at least two things that make a business ethical (fair wages, honest advertising, environmentally responsible)
Explain why a business that only cares about profit might cause problems
Describe a situation where a business owner faces an ethical choice and suggest what they should do
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard about a company paying its workers very little to make bigger profits, could they explain why that's unfair and suggest a better approach?
topics.descriptionZh: 诚实守信，公平公正，善待员工，保护环境；探讨什么造就了一家“好”企业；以及企业是否应该关心利润以外的事情
evidenceZh: 至少说出两件让企业符合道德的事情（如：公平的工资、诚实的广告、对环境负责）
解释为什么一个只关心利润的企业可能会引发问题
描述一个企业主面临道德选择的情境，并建议他们应该怎么做
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 听说一家公司为了赚取更多利润而给工人支付极低的工资，他们能解释为什么这是不公平的，并建议一个更好的做法吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Pitching an Idea
topics.description: Presenting a business idea to others convincingly; explaining what makes it good and why people should support it; building confidence in public speaking about ideas
evidence: Deliver a 1-2 minute pitch for a business idea covering: what it is, who it helps, and why it's good
Answer at least two questions about their idea from an audience
Explain why being able to explain your idea clearly matters for getting support
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} had to stand up in front of the class and explain a business idea in two minutes, could they do it confidently and persuasively?
topics.descriptionZh: 有说服力地向他人展示商业创意（business idea）；解释它的优势以及人们为何应该支持它；培养在公众面前表达想法的自信心
evidenceZh: 进行1至2分钟的商业创意推介（pitch），内容需涵盖：它是什么、它能帮助谁、以及它为什么好
回答观众针对其创意提出的至少两个问题
解释为什么能够清晰地表达想法对于获得他人支持至关重要
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}必须站到全班面前，用两分钟时间说明一个商业创意，他们能够自信且有说服力地完成吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Real Entrepreneurs
topics.description: Stories of real entrepreneurs who started young: Mikaila Ulmer (Me & the Bees), Moziah Bridges (Mo's Bows), Cory Nieves (Mr. Cory's Cookies); what makes someone an entrepreneur
evidence: Retell the story of at least one real entrepreneur who started as a child
Identify three qualities that helped that entrepreneur succeed (creativity, persistence, passion)
Explain what the word 'entrepreneur' means in their own words
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell you about a real person who started a business as a kid and explain what qualities helped them succeed?
topics.descriptionZh: 讲述从小开始创业的真实企业家的故事：米凯拉·乌尔默（Me & the Bees）、莫齐亚·布里奇斯（Mo's Bows）、科里·尼夫斯（Mr. Cory's Cookies）；探讨是什么让一个人成为企业家（entrepreneur）。
evidenceZh: 复述至少一位从小开始创业的真实创业者的故事
找出帮助该创业者取得成功的三个品质（创造力、毅力、热情）
用自己的话解释“企业家”（entrepreneur）这个词的含义
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能给你讲一个小时候就开始创业的真实人物的故事，并解释是哪些品质帮助他们取得成功的吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Scaling Up
topics.description: What happens when a small business grows; making more products, hiring people, reaching more customers; the challenges and opportunities of scaling
evidence: Describe what 'scaling up' means for a business
Identify at least two challenges of growing a business (need more money, more people, more materials)
Explain how a lemonade stand could grow into a bigger business step by step
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what would need to change if their small school-fair business became so popular that lots more people wanted to buy from them?
topics.descriptionZh: 当小型企业发展壮大时会发生什么；生产更多产品、雇佣员工、接触更多客户；扩大规模（scaling up）带来的挑战与机遇
evidenceZh: 描述“扩大规模”（scaling up）对企业意味着什么
找出企业发展过程中面临的至少两个挑战（需要更多资金、更多人员、更多原材料）
逐步解释一个柠檬水摊位如何一步步发展成更大的企业
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释一下，如果他们的小型校园义卖生意变得非常受欢迎，有更多人想要购买他们的产品，那么需要做哪些改变吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Social Enterprise
topics.description: Using business skills to help others or solve social and environmental problems; making money AND making a difference; examples of social enterprises
evidence: Explain what a social enterprise is in their own words (a business that helps people or the planet)
Give an example of a real social enterprise or charity shop
Suggest a social enterprise idea that could help their school or community
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} come up with an idea for a business that both makes money and helps people or the environment?
topics.descriptionZh: 运用商业技能帮助他人或解决社会与环境问题；既能赚钱又能创造积极改变；社会企业的实例。
evidenceZh: 用自己的话解释什么是社会企业（即一家帮助人类或保护地球的企业）
举出一个真实的社会企业或慈善商店的例子
提出一个能帮助自己学校或社区的社会企业创意
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否想出一个既能赚钱，又能帮助他人或保护环境的商业创意？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Supply Chains
topics.description: Where products come from before they reach the customer; raw materials, making, transporting, and selling; the journey of a product from start to finish
evidence: Trace the journey of a familiar product (e.g. chocolate bar) from raw material to shop shelf
Identify at least three stages in a supply chain
Explain why a long supply chain can make a product more expensive
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you asked {{name}} how a chocolate bar gets from a cocoa farm to a shop shelf, could they describe the main steps in the journey?
topics.descriptionZh: 产品在到达顾客手中之前的来源；包括原材料、制造、运输和销售；产品从起点到终点的整个旅程
evidenceZh: 追溯一种常见产品（例如巧克力棒）从原材料到商店货架的旅程
识别供应链（Supply Chain）中的至少三个环节
解释为什么较长的供应链会使产品的价格更高
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你问{{name}}一块巧克力是如何从可可农场运到商店货架上的，他们能描述出这趟旅程的主要步骤吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Buying Things
topics.description: How buying and selling works: prices, paying for items, receiving change; the basic transaction process in shops and markets
evidence: Explain what happens when you buy something in a shop (choose, pay, get change)
Read a price label and say whether they have enough money to buy the item
Act out a simple buying scenario using real or play coins
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} had a £2 coin and wanted to buy a snack for 80p, could they work out roughly how much change they'd get back?
topics.descriptionZh: 买卖的运作方式：价格、付款、找零；商店和市场的基本交易过程
evidenceZh: 解释在商店购物时会发生什么（挑选、付款、找零）
阅读价格标签，并判断是否有足够的钱购买该物品
使用真实硬币或玩具硬币模拟简单的购物场景
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 有一枚2英镑（£2）的硬币，想买一份80便士（80p）的零食，他们能大致算出能找回多少零钱吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Coins & Notes
topics.description: Recognising common coins and notes, knowing their values, and understanding that different combinations can make the same amount
evidence: Sort a handful of mixed coins into groups by value
State the value of common coins and notes when shown them
Find two different ways to make the same amount using different coins
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you tipped out a jar of coins, could {{name}} sort them and tell you how much each type is worth?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识常见的硬币和纸币，知道它们的币值，并理解不同的组合可以凑成相同的金额
evidenceZh: 将一把混合的硬币按币值分组
看到常见的硬币和纸币时，能说出它们的面值
找出用不同硬币凑出相同金额的两种不同方法
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你把一罐硬币倒出来，{{name}}能把它们分类并告诉你每种硬币的面值是多少吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Jobs People Do
topics.description: Different kinds of work people do; that people earn money by working; how jobs help the community; linking personal interests to possible jobs
evidence: Name at least five different jobs and describe what each person does
Explain that people get paid money for the work they do
Connect a personal interest to a job (e.g. 'I like animals so I could be a vet')
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell you about different jobs people do in your community and explain that people get paid for their work?
topics.descriptionZh: 人们从事的各类工作；人们通过工作赚钱；工作如何帮助社区；将个人兴趣与可能从事的工作联系起来
evidenceZh: 至少说出五种不同的职业，并描述每种职业的具体工作内容
解释人们通过工作获得报酬
将个人兴趣与某种职业联系起来（例如：‘我喜欢动物，所以我可以当兽医’）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能向你介绍你们社区里人们从事的不同工作，并解释人们通过工作获得报酬吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Looking After Money
topics.description: Keeping money safe; not losing coins or notes; understanding that money has real value and should be treated carefully; basic money responsibility
evidence: Describe at least two ways to keep money safe (purse, wallet, money box, giving to a grown-up)
Explain why it matters if you lose money
Show that they treat real coins and notes carefully rather than leaving them lying around
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you gave {{name}} some coins to look after at a shop, would they keep them safe and know where they put them?
topics.descriptionZh: 安全保管金钱；不丢失硬币（coins）或纸币（notes）；理解金钱具有实际价值并应谨慎对待；培养基本的金钱责任感
evidenceZh: 描述至少两种妥善保管金钱的方法（如使用钱包（wallet）、存钱罐（money box）或交给成年人）
解释丢失金钱会带来什么影响
表现出能小心对待真实的硬币（coins）和纸币（notes），而不是随手乱放
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果在商店里给 {{name}} 一些硬币（coins）让其保管，他们能把钱妥善保管好并清楚记得存放位置吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Needs & Wants
topics.description: The difference between things we need (food, shelter, clothing) and things we want (toys, treats); that we sometimes have to choose because money is limited
evidence: Sort a set of pictures into 'need' and 'want' categories and explain their choices
Give an example of something everyone needs and something that is a want
Explain why a family might choose to buy a need before a want
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you showed {{name}} pictures of a winter coat, a toy robot, and a loaf of bread, could they tell you which ones are needs and which is a want?
topics.descriptionZh: 区分我们必需的物品（如食物、住所、衣物）和我们想要的物品（如玩具、零食）；理解由于金钱（资源）有限，我们有时必须做出取舍。
evidenceZh: 将一组图片分类为“需要（need）”和“想要（want）”两类，并解释他们的选择理由
举出一个每个人都需要（need）的物品和一个想要（want）的物品的例子
解释为什么家庭可能会选择先购买必需品（need）而不是想要的物品（want）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你给{{name}}看一件冬装外套、一个玩具机器人和一条面包的图片，他们能分辨出哪些是需要（need）的物品，哪个是想要（want）的物品吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Saving Money
topics.description: Why people save money; piggy banks and saving jars; setting a savings goal; the idea that not spending now means having more later
evidence: Explain why someone might save money instead of spending it straight away
Describe a savings goal they could set and how they would work towards it
Tell you what delayed gratification means in their own words (waiting to get something better)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} received some birthday money, could they explain why it might be smart to save some of it rather than spending it all at once?
topics.descriptionZh: 人们为什么要存钱；存钱罐和储蓄罐；设定储蓄目标；理解现在不花钱意味着以后会有更多钱的理念
evidenceZh: 解释为什么有人会选择存钱而不是立刻把钱花掉
描述他们可以设定的一个储蓄目标，以及他们将如何努力实现这个目标
用自己的话解释延迟满足 (delayed gratification) 是什么意思（即等待以获得更好的东西）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 收到了一些生日红包，他们能解释为什么存下其中一部分比一次性全部花掉更明智吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: What Money Is
topics.description: What money is and why we use it; that money is exchanged for goods and services; brief history from barter to coins to digital payments
evidence: Explain that people use money to pay for things they need or want
Give an example of how buying worked before money existed (swapping or bartering)
Name at least two forms money can take (coins, notes, card, phone payment)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you asked {{name}} why people use money instead of just swapping things, could they give you a sensible answer?
topics.descriptionZh: 金钱的概念及我们使用它的原因；金钱用于交换商品和服务；从物物交换到硬币再到数字支付的简要历史
evidenceZh: 解释人们用金钱购买所需或想要的物品
举例说明在金钱出现前是如何进行交易的（物物交换）
列举金钱至少存在的两种形式（硬币、纸币、银行卡、手机支付）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你问{{name}}为什么人们使用金钱而不是直接物物交换，他们能给出合理的解释吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Advertising & Spending
topics.description: How advertising tries to influence what we buy; being a critical consumer; understanding 'value for money'; the difference between emotional and rational spending
evidence: Spot at least two persuasion techniques in a real advert (bright colours, celebrity, special offer)
Explain what 'value for money' means and compare two similar products at different prices
Describe a time when advertising made them want something they didn't really need
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} sees an advert for a toy or game, can they recognise that the advert is trying to make them want to buy it?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解广告如何试图影响我们的购买决定；学会做明智的消费者；理解“物有所值”（value for money）的概念；区分冲动消费与理性消费
evidenceZh: 在真实的广告中找出至少两种说服技巧（如鲜艳的色彩、名人代言、特价优惠）
解释“物有所值”（value for money）的含义，并比较两款价格不同的相似产品
描述一次广告让他们想要某件其实并不真正需要的物品的经历
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 看到玩具或游戏的广告时，他们能意识到这个广告是试图让他们产生购买欲望吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Banks & Saving
topics.description: What banks do and why people use them; bank accounts as safe places for money; that savings in a bank can earn interest; children's savings accounts
evidence: Explain what a bank does in simple terms (keeps money safe, lets you save)
Describe what interest means (the bank pays you a little extra for keeping money there)
Name one reason a bank account is safer than keeping all your money at home
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what a bank does and why people put their money there instead of keeping it all at home?
topics.descriptionZh: 银行的作用及人们使用银行的原因；银行账户是安全存放钱财的地方；在银行存钱可以赚取利息（Interest）；儿童储蓄账户。
evidenceZh: 用简单的语言解释银行的作用（保管钱财、让你存钱）
描述利息（Interest）的含义（银行为你把钱存那里而支付的一点额外报酬）
说出一个为什么银行账户比把钱全放在家里更安全的原因
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释一下银行是做什么的，以及为什么人们要把钱存进银行而不是全部放在家里吗？

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Budgeting Pocket Money
