topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} flips a coin 10 times and gets 7 heads, do they understand why this doesn't mean heads is "more likely" — and that the more times you flip, the closer the results get to 50:50?
topics.descriptionZh: 进行重复的概率实验，并将实验相对频率（relative frequency）结果与理论预测进行比较；理解并证明随着试验次数的增加，实验概率（experimental probability）会趋向于理论概率（theoretical probability）——并且少量试验可能会得出差异很大的结果。
evidenceZh: 掷骰子60次，并将每个数字出现的实验频率与预期的10次进行比较
解释为什么实验结果不会与理论预测完全一致，但随着试验次数的增加会越来越接近
预测如果将实验重复600次而不是60次，会发生什么情况
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 抛硬币10次得到了7次正面，他们是否理解这并不意味着正面“更有可能”出现——并且抛的次数越多，结果就越接近50:50？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Probabilities Sum to One
topics.description: Understand that when all possible outcomes of a trial are listed, their probabilities must add up to 1; use this to find the probability of an event NOT happening: P(not A) = 1 − P(A); apply this shortcut to avoid counting all unfavourable outcomes directly
evidence: List all outcomes of spinning a 4-colour spinner and verify their probabilities add up to 1
Calculate P(not rolling a 3) as 1 − 1/6 = 5/6 using the complement rule
Spot an error in a probability table where the values don't sum to 1 and explain what's wrong
topics.assessmentPrompt: If the probability of it raining tomorrow is 0.3, can {{name}} work out the probability of it NOT raining — and explain why all probabilities in a situation must add up to 1?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解当列出一次试验的所有可能结果时，它们的概率总和必须等于1；利用此规律求事件不发生的概率：P(非A) = 1 − P(A)；应用这一简便方法来避免直接计算所有不利的结果
evidenceZh: 列出转动4色转盘的所有可能结果，并验证它们的概率之和等于1
利用对立事件规则（complement rule），计算“不掷出3”的概率为 P(非3) = 1 − 1/6 = 5/6
发现概率表中数值之和不为1的错误，并解释错误的原因
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果明天下雨的概率是0.3，{{name}}能算出不下雨的概率吗——并解释为什么在一个情境中所有概率的总和必须等于1？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: The 0-to-1 Probability Scale
topics.description: Understand probability as a measure expressed as a number between 0 (impossible) and 1 (certain); place events on the probability scale; express probabilities as fractions, decimals, and percentages
evidence: Place events on a number line from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain), expressing positions as fractions or decimals
Explain that a probability of 0.5 means 'even chance' and connect this to the informal word 'likely'
Convert between informal language ('very unlikely') and a numerical position on the 0-to-1 scale
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} write the same probability as a fraction, a decimal, and a percentage — for example, knowing that an even chance is ½, 0.5, and 50%?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解概率 (probability) 是一种度量，用0（不可能 impossible）到1（必然 certain）之间的数值来表示；将事件放置在概率标尺上；用分数 (fractions)、小数 (decimals) 和百分比 (percentages) 来表示概率。
evidenceZh: 将事件标记在从0（不可能）到1（必然）的数轴 (number line) 上，并用分数或小数表示其所处位置
解释0.5的概率意味着“机会均等” (even chance)，并将其与“可能” (likely) 等日常非正式用语联系起来
在“极不可能” (very unlikely) 等非正式用语与0到1标尺上的数值位置之间进行转换
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否将同一个概率分别表示为分数、小数和百分比——例如，知道“机会均等”即是½、0.5和50%？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Complementary events
topics.description: Understand and apply the rule that probabilities of all mutually exclusive outcomes sum to one; use this to find the probability of a complementary event (P(not A) = 1 − P(A))
evidence: Verify that probabilities of all outcomes listed for a spinner sum to 1
Calculate the probability of NOT rolling a 6 as 1 − 1/6 = 5/6
Identify an error in a probability distribution where the values do not sum to 1
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a spinner has three sections and one has a probability of 0.4 and another has 0.35, can {{name}} work out the probability of landing on the third section without being told?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解并应用所有互斥结果的概率之和为1的规则；利用该规则求对立事件的概率（P(非A) = 1 − P(A)）
evidenceZh: 验证转盘上列出的所有结果的概率之和是否为1
计算掷出非6点的概率为 1 − 1/6 = 5/6
识别概率分布中各项数值之和不等于1的错误
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果一个转盘有三个区域，其中一个区域停在上面的概率是0.4，另一个是0.35，{{name}} 能在不被告知的情况下算出停在第三个区域的概率吗？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Experimental probability
topics.description: Record, describe, and analyse the frequency of outcomes from probability experiments to develop an understanding of relative frequency as an estimate of probability
evidence: Conduct a coin-toss experiment, record results in a frequency table, and calculate relative frequencies
Compare experimental results with theoretical probability and explain discrepancies
Predict that relative frequency approaches theoretical probability as the number of trials increases
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} rolls a die 60 times and records the results, can they compare how often each number came up with what they'd expect in theory — and explain why they might not match perfectly?
topics.descriptionZh: 记录、描述和分析概率实验结果的频率，以理解相对频率 (relative frequency) 作为概率估计值的概念。
evidenceZh: 进行抛硬币实验，将结果记录在频数表 (frequency table) 中，并计算相对频率 (relative frequencies)
将实验结果与理论概率 (theoretical probability) 进行比较，并解释其中的差异
预测随着试验次数的增加，相对频率会趋近于理论概率
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 掷骰子 60 次并记录结果，他们能否将每个数字出现的次数与理论预期进行比较——并解释为什么它们可能不会完全吻合？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: The Probability Scale
topics.description: Understand probability as a measure on a scale from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain); use the language of probability including likely, unlikely, certain, and impossible
evidence: Place everyday events on a 0-to-1 probability scale with justification
Explain why a fair six-sided die gives each number a probability of 1/6
Distinguish between equally likely outcomes (fair coin) and unequally likely outcomes (biased spinner)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that probability goes from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain), place events on that scale as numbers, and tell you whether a game is fair or not?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解概率是从0（不可能）到1（必然）尺度上的一种度量；使用概率语言，包括很可能（likely）、不太可能（unlikely）、必然（certain）和不可能（impossible）
evidenceZh: 将日常事件放置在0到1的概率尺度上并说明理由
解释为什么公平的六面骰子（fair six-sided die）每个数字出现的概率都是1/6
区分等可能结果（公平硬币/fair coin）和不等可能结果（有偏转盘/biased spinner）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释概率的范围是从0（不可能）到1（必然），将事件用数字表示并放置在该尺度上，以及判断一个游戏是否公平？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Sets & Venn Diagrams
topics.description: Enumerate sets and their unions and intersections systematically using tables, grids, and Venn diagrams to organise and count outcomes
evidence: List the elements in the union and intersection of two sets using a Venn diagram
Use a two-way table to enumerate all possible outcomes of two combined events
Shade regions of a Venn diagram to represent A ∪ B, A ∩ B, and A′ (complement)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} use a table or Venn diagram to systematically list all the possible outcomes of two events — like rolling two dice — and use it to count favourable outcomes?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用表格、网格和维恩图（Venn diagrams）系统地列举集合及其并集（unions）和交集（intersections），以组织和计算可能的结果。
evidenceZh: 使用维恩图列出两个集合的并集和交集（intersection）中的元素
使用双向表格（two-way table）列举两个组合事件的所有可能结果
在维恩图中对区域进行涂色，以表示 A ∪ B（并集）、A ∩ B（交集）和 A′（补集，complement）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否使用表格或维恩图系统地列出两个事件（例如掷两个骰子）的所有可能结果，并以此来计算有利结果（favourable outcomes）的数量？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Tree diagrams
topics.description: Generate theoretical sample spaces for single and combined events using listing, tables, and tree diagrams, and calculate theoretical probabilities as the number of favourable outcomes divided by the total number of equally likely outcomes
evidence: List all 36 outcomes when rolling two dice and find P(total = 7)
Draw a tree diagram for two successive events and multiply along branches for combined probabilities
Calculate the probability of a combined event using a sample space diagram and simplify the fraction
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw a tree diagram to map out all possible outcomes of a two-step probability situation — like flipping a coin and then rolling a die — and calculate the probability of any particular combination?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用列表、表格和树状图来生成单个和复合事件的理论样本空间 (sample spaces)，并通过有利结果 (favourable outcomes) 数量除以等可能结果总数来计算理论概率 (theoretical probabilities)。
evidenceZh: 列出掷两个骰子时的所有36种结果，并计算P(总和 = 7)
为两个连续事件绘制树状图，并沿分支相乘来计算复合概率 (combined probabilities)
使用样本空间图 (sample space diagram) 计算复合事件的概率并化简分数
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否绘制树状图来展示两步概率情境（例如先抛硬币再掷骰子）的所有可能结果，并计算任何特定组合的概率？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Venn Diagrams and Counting Outcomes
topics.description: Construct and interpret Venn diagrams with two or three sets to organise and count outcomes; use systematic listing and the product rule for counting to enumerate all possible outcomes of combined events
evidence: Draw a two-circle Venn diagram to sort 30 students by whether they like football, like cricket, or like both
Shade the intersection A ∩ B and the union A ∪ B on a Venn diagram and explain what each region represents
Use a completed Venn diagram to calculate P(A), P(B), P(A ∩ B), and P(A ∪ B)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} surveys a class about which sports they play and draws a Venn diagram to show the results, can they use it to find out how many students play both sports — and calculate the probability of picking one of those students at random?
topics.nameZh: 韦恩图（Venn Diagrams）与结果计数
topics.descriptionZh: 构建和解释包含两个或三个集合的韦恩图（Venn diagrams）以组织和计算结果；使用系统列举法和乘法计数原理（product rule for counting）来枚举组合事件的所有可能结果
evidenceZh: 绘制一个双圆韦恩图，根据30名学生是否喜欢足球、喜欢板球或两者都喜欢对他们进行分类
在韦恩图上为交集（intersection）A ∩ B 和并集（union）A ∪ B 涂上阴影，并解释每个区域代表什么
使用已完成的韦恩图计算 P(A)、P(B)、P(A ∩ B) 和 P(A ∪ B)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 调查全班同学参加哪些运动并绘制韦恩图来展示结果，他们能否利用该图找出同时参加这两项运动的学生人数——并计算出随机抽取其中一名学生的概率（probability）？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Bar Models for Ratios
topics.description: Represent ratio and proportion problems using bar models (rectangular strips divided into equal parts labelled with quantities) and tape diagrams (segmented strips showing part-to-part and part-to-whole relationships); use these visual models to set up and solve unequal sharing, scaling, and percentage problems — drawing the diagram first, then reading off the answer
evidence: Draw a bar model to represent a ratio problem — e.g. sharing £20 in the ratio 3:2 by drawing 5 equal blocks
Use a bar model to solve a proportion problem and explain each step
Compare bar models with other representations (tables, double number lines) and explain when each is most useful
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} needs to share 30 stickers between two friends in a 2:3 ratio, can they draw a bar model — splitting a strip into 5 equal boxes — and use it to work out each share without just guessing?
topics.nameZh: 比例条形模型 (Bar Models for Ratios)
topics.descriptionZh: 使用条形模型 (Bar Models，即划分为等份并标有数量的矩形条) 和纸带图 (Tape Diagrams，即展示部分与部分、部分与整体关系的分段条) 来表示比 (Ratio) 和比例 (Proportion) 问题；利用这些直观的视觉模型来建立和解决不等分配、按比例缩放以及百分比问题——先绘制图表，再根据图表得出答案。
evidenceZh: 绘制条形模型来表示比例问题——例如，通过绘制5个相等的方块，将20英镑按3:2的比例进行分配。
使用条形模型解决比例问题，并解释每一个步骤。
将条形模型与其他表示方法（表格、双数轴 (Double Number Lines)）进行比较，并解释在什么情况下每种方法最为有效。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 需要把30张贴纸按2:3的比例分给两个朋友，他/她能画出条形模型——将一条纸带分成5个相等的格子——并借此算出每人分得的数量，而不是靠盲目猜测吗？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Percentages (age 9+)
topics.description: Know and use the vocabulary of ratio and proportion — ratio, proportion, percentage, scale, equivalent, unequal, relative size, part-to-part, part-to-whole, and out of — and understand the difference between ratio (comparing parts to parts) and proportion (comparing a part to the whole)
evidence: Explain the difference between a 'ratio' and a 'proportion' using a concrete example like mixing paint
Use 'per cent' correctly and convert between fractions, decimals, and percentages in context
Define 'scale factor' and use it to describe how a shape has been enlarged or reduced
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is sharing something 3 ways and 2 ways, can they explain the difference between a ratio (like 3:2) and a proportion (like 3 out of 5) — showing they know what each word means?
topics.descriptionZh: 掌握并运用比和比例（ratio and proportion）的相关词汇——比（ratio）、比例（proportion）、百分数（percentage）、比例尺（scale）、等价（equivalent）、不等（unequal）、相对大小（relative size）、部分与部分（part-to-part）、部分与整体（part-to-whole）以及“……之中有……”（out of）——并理解比（比较部分与部分）和比例（比较部分与整体）之间的区别。
evidenceZh: 使用具体的例子（如混合颜料）来解释“比”（ratio）和“比例”（proportion）之间的区别。
正确使用“百分数”（per cent），并在具体情境中进行分数（fractions）、小数（decimals）和百分数（percentages）之间的转换。
定义“比例因子”（scale factor），并用它来描述图形是如何被放大或缩小的。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 要把某物按 3 份和 2 份来分配，他们能否解释“比”（如 3:2）和“比例”（如 5 份中的 3 份，即 3 out of 5）之间的区别——从而证明他们理解每个词的含义？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Calculating Percentages
topics.description: Solve problems involving the calculation of percentages of amounts (e.g. 15% of 360) and the use of percentages for comparison
evidence: Calculate 15% of 360 by finding 10% and 5% and combining
Compare two discounts given as percentages of different original prices
Explain a strategy for finding any percentage of an amount using known percentage facts
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a jumper originally costs £40 and is 15% off, can {{name}} work out how much the discount is and what the sale price would be?
topics.descriptionZh: 解决涉及计算数值的百分比（例如360的15%）以及使用百分比进行比较的问题。
evidenceZh: 通过先计算10%和5%再相加的方法，求出360的15%
比较基于不同原价的两种百分比折扣
解释一种利用已知百分比知识求任意数量百分比的策略
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果一件毛衣原价40英镑，现降价15%，{{name}}能算出折扣金额是多少，以及折后售价是多少吗？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Ratio Problems
topics.description: Solve problems involving the relative sizes of two quantities where missing values can be found by using integer multiplication and division facts
evidence: If the ratio of red to blue beads is 3:5 and there are 15 blue beads, find the number of red beads
Use multiplication facts to find the missing value: 'For every 2 apples there are 5 oranges; if there are 20 oranges, how many apples?'
Explain the multiplicative relationship between two quantities in a ratio context
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a recipe uses 3 eggs for every 200g of flour, can {{name}} work out how many eggs would be needed for 600g of flour?
topics.descriptionZh: 解决涉及两个数量相对大小的问题，其中缺失值可通过整数乘除法（integer multiplication and division）求解。
evidenceZh: 如果红珠子与蓝珠子的比例（ratio）是3:5，且有15颗蓝珠子，求红珠子的数量
运用乘法口诀（multiplication facts）求缺失值：‘每2个苹果对应5个橘子；如果有20个橘子，有多少个苹果？’
在比例（ratio）情境中解释两个数量之间的乘法关系（multiplicative relationship）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果一个食谱中每200克面粉需要3个鸡蛋，{{name}}能算出600克面粉需要多少个鸡蛋吗？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Scale and similar shapes
topics.description: Solve problems involving similar shapes where the scale factor is known or can be found
evidence: Find the missing side of a similar rectangle given a scale factor of 3
Determine the scale factor between two similar triangles from given side lengths
Use a scale factor to enlarge or reduce a shape and verify that all sides are in the same ratio
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has a scale drawing where 1 cm represents 5 m, and a room measures 3.5 cm on the plan, can they work out the real length of the room?
topics.descriptionZh: 解决涉及相似图形（similar shapes）的问题，其中比例因子（scale factor）已知或可以求出。
evidenceZh: 已知比例因子（scale factor）为3，求相似矩形（similar rectangle）的缺失边长
根据给定的边长，确定两个相似三角形（similar triangles）之间的比例因子（scale factor）
使用比例因子（scale factor）放大或缩小图形，并验证所有边长是否保持相同的比例
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 有一张按比例绘制的图纸（scale drawing），其中1厘米代表5米，且图纸上的房间长3.5厘米，他们能算出房间的实际长度吗？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Understanding fractions
topics.description: Solve problems involving unequal sharing and grouping using knowledge of fractions and multiples
evidence: Share 40 sweets between two children in the ratio 3:5
Solve: 'Tom gets twice as many as Sam and Sam gets three times as many as Jo. If there are 30 altogether, how many does each get?'
Use fraction knowledge to explain why sharing in ratio 2:3 means one person gets 2/5 of the total
topics.assessmentPrompt: If three friends share a bag of 24 sweets so that one person gets twice as many as each of the others, can {{name}} work out how many each person receives?
topics.descriptionZh: 运用分数和倍数知识，解决涉及不平均分与分组的问题
evidenceZh: 将40颗糖果按3:5的比例分给两个孩子
解答：‘汤姆得到的数量是山姆的两倍，山姆得到的是乔的三倍。如果总共有30颗，每个人各得多少？’
运用分数知识解释为什么按2:3的比例分配意味着其中一人得到总数的2/5
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果三个朋友分一袋24颗糖果，其中一人得到的数量是另外两人各自的两倍，{{name}}能算出每个人分得多少颗吗？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Compound Units
topics.description: Use compound units such as speed (distance ÷ time), unit pricing (cost ÷ quantity), and density (mass ÷ volume); solve problems involving compound units
evidence: Calculate average speed given distance and time, converting between km/h and m/s if needed
Compare unit prices of two products sold in different quantities to find the better deal
Use the density formula to find mass, volume, or density given the other two values
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a car travels 150 miles in 2.5 hours, can {{name}} work out its average speed — and use the same idea to solve problems about price per kilogram or density of a material?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用复合单位，如速度 (speed，距离 ÷ 时间)、单价 (unit pricing，成本 ÷ 数量) 和密度 (density，质量 ÷ 体积)；解决涉及复合单位的问题。
evidenceZh: 根据距离和时间计算平均速度，必要时在千米/小时 (km/h) 和米/秒 (m/s) 之间进行换算
比较以不同数量出售的两种商品的单价 (unit price)，找出更划算的交易
使用密度 (density) 公式，在已知另外两个值的情况下求出质量、体积或密度
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果一辆汽车在2.5小时内行驶了150英里，{{name}}能计算出它的平均速度吗——并且能用同样的思路解决关于每公斤价格或材料密度的问题吗？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Dividing Quantities by Ratio
topics.description: Divide a given quantity into two parts in a given part:part or part:whole ratio, and express the division as a fraction of the whole
evidence: Share £60 between two people in the ratio 2:3 by finding the value of one part
Express the result of sharing 24 sweets as 10 and 14 in ratio form as 5:7
Solve problems involving three-part ratios (e.g. divide 180 in the ratio 1:2:3)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If £60 is shared between two people in the ratio 2:3, can {{name}} work out how much each person gets?
topics.descriptionZh: 将给定数量按给定的部分:部分 (part:part) 或部分:整体 (part:whole) 比例分成两部分，并将分配结果表示为占整体的分数。
evidenceZh: 通过求出一份的价值，将60英镑按2:3的比例分给两个人
将24颗糖果分为10颗和14颗的分配结果，用比例形式表示为5:7
解决涉及三部分比例的问题（例如，将180按1:2:3的比例进行分配）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果将60英镑按2:3的比例分给两个人，{{name}}能算出每个人得到多少吗？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: One Quantity as a Fraction
topics.description: Express one quantity as a fraction of another where the result may be less than 1 or greater than 1, and interpret the meaning in context
evidence: Express 45 minutes as a fraction of 2 hours (= 3/8)
Express a larger quantity as a fraction of a smaller one and explain why the result exceeds 1
Simplify the resulting fraction and interpret its meaning in the original context
topics.assessmentPrompt: If there are 15 boys and 20 girls in a class, can {{name}} express the number of boys as a fraction of the whole class and say whether that fraction is less than or greater than a half?
topics.nameZh: 一个量占另一个量的分数
topics.descriptionZh: 将一个量表示为另一个量的分数（fraction），结果可能小于1或大于1，并结合具体情境解释其含义
evidenceZh: 将45分钟表示为2小时的分数（= 3/8）
将较大的量表示为较小量的分数（fraction），并解释为什么结果大于1
化简所得的分数，并在原情境中解释其含义
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果一个班有15名男生和20名女生，{{name}}能否将男生人数表示为全班总人数的分数，并说明该分数是小于二分之一还是大于二分之一？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Percentages as Fractions
topics.description: Define percentage as 'number of parts per hundred'; interpret percentages and percentage changes as a fraction or a decimal; express one quantity as a percentage of another; compare quantities using percentages; work with percentages greater than 100%
evidence: Convert fluently between percentages, fractions, and decimals
Express one quantity as a percentage of another
Calculate percentage increases and decreases and interpret percentages greater than 100%
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a shop says a TV is 130% of its original price, does {{name}} understand what that means — and can they work out the new price from the original?
topics.nameZh: 百分比作为分数 (Percentages as Fractions)
topics.descriptionZh: 将百分比定义为'每一百份中的份数'；将百分比及百分比变化理解为分数 (fraction) 或小数 (decimal)；将一个量表示为另一个量的百分比；使用百分比比较数量；处理大于100%的百分比
evidenceZh: 在百分比、分数和小数之间熟练转换
将一个量表示为另一个量的百分比
计算百分比的增加和减少，并理解大于100%的百分比
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果商店说一台电视机的价格是其原价的130%，{{name}}能理解这意味着什么吗——他们能根据原价计算出新的价格吗？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Proportional Reasoning Vocabulary
topics.description: Know and use advanced vocabulary of multiplicative reasoning — direct proportion, inverse proportion, ratio, rate, unit rate, compound unit, scale factor — accurately in problem-solving contexts
evidence: Distinguish between 'direct proportion' and 'inverse proportion' with real-world examples
Use 'rate', 'speed', and 'density' correctly and explain what units they are measured in
Calculate using compound measures — e.g. work out the speed of a car that travels 120 miles in 2 hours
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is solving a problem about speed or density, can they explain what 'compound unit' means and tell the difference between direct proportion (more of one means more of the other) and inverse proportion (more of one means less of the other)?
topics.nameZh: 比例推理词汇 (Proportional Reasoning Vocabulary)
topics.descriptionZh: 了解并能在解决问题的语境中准确使用乘除法推理的高级词汇——正比例 (direct proportion)、反比例 (inverse proportion)、比 (ratio)、速率 (rate)、单位速率 (unit rate)、复合单位 (compound unit)、比例因子 (scale factor)。
evidenceZh: 能结合现实生活中的例子区分“正比例” (direct proportion) 和“反比例” (inverse proportion)。
能正确使用“速率” (rate)、“速度” (speed) 和“密度” (density)，并解释它们的计量单位。
能使用复合量度进行计算——例如，计算一辆汽车在2小时内行驶120英里的速度。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 正在解决关于速度或密度的问题，他们能解释“复合单位” (compound unit) 的含义，并区分正比例（一个量增加，另一个量也随之增加）和反比例（一个量增加，另一个量反而减少）吗？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Proportion Graphs
topics.description: Represent proportional relationships using double number lines (two parallel number lines aligned at 0) and ratio tables; recognise that equivalent ratios generate straight lines through the origin when graphed
evidence: Plot pairs of proportional values on a coordinate grid and draw the straight line through the origin
Explain why a directly proportional relationship always passes through (0,0)
Read a proportion graph to find an unknown value — e.g. 'If 3 kg costs £6, how much does 5 kg cost?'
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is comparing the cost of buying different numbers of cinema tickets, can they sketch a proportion graph — a straight line through zero — and use it to read off the cost of any number of tickets without recalculating each time?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用双线数轴 (double number lines，即两条在0处对齐的平行数轴) 和比例表来表示正比例关系；认识到在绘制图形时，等价比例 (equivalent ratios) 会生成穿过原点的直线。
evidenceZh: 在坐标网格上绘制成比例的数据对，并画出穿过原点的直线
解释为什么正比例关系 (directly proportional relationship) 的图像总是经过原点 (0,0)
读取比例图以求出未知值——例如：‘如果3千克花费6英镑，那么5千克花费多少？’
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 正在比较购买不同数量电影票的成本，他们能否画出一个比例图——一条穿过零点的直线——并利用它直接读出任意数量电影票的成本，而无需每次都重新计算？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Ratio Notation
topics.description: Use ratio notation to describe the relationship between two or more quantities, simplify ratios to their simplest form, and convert between ratio and fraction representations
evidence: Write a ratio from a word problem and simplify it (e.g. 12:8 = 3:2)
Convert a ratio to equivalent fractions of a whole (e.g. 3:2 means 3/5 and 2/5)
Simplify ratios involving decimals or fractions by finding a common multiplier
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a smoothie recipe uses orange juice and mango juice in the ratio 3:2, can {{name}} simplify that ratio, express it as a fraction, and work out how much of each is needed for a given total amount?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用比的表示法 (Ratio Notation) 描述两个或多个数量之间的关系，将比化简为最简比，并在比与分数的表示形式之间进行转换。
evidenceZh: 根据应用题写出比并将其化简（例如 12:8 = 3:2）
将比转换为总量的等价分数（例如 3:2 表示 3/5 和 2/5）
通过寻找公乘数 (common multiplier) 来化简包含小数或分数的比
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果一份冰沙食谱中橙汁和芒果汁的配比是 3:2，{{name}} 能够化简这个比，把它表示为分数，并计算出在给定总量下每种果汁各需要多少吗？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Scale and similar shapes (age 11+)
topics.description: Use scale factors to interpret and create scale diagrams and maps, calculating real-life distances from map measurements and vice versa
evidence: Calculate a real-life distance from a map measurement using a given scale (e.g. 1:25,000)
Draw a scale diagram of a room using a chosen scale factor
Convert between map distance and actual distance in problems involving different units
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looks at a map where 1 cm = 50 km, can they work out the real distance between two cities that are 4.5 cm apart on the map?
topics.nameZh: 比例尺与相似图形（11岁及以上）
topics.descriptionZh: 运用比例因子（scale factors）解读并绘制比例图（scale diagrams）和地图，能够根据地图上的测量值计算实际距离，或根据实际距离计算地图上的距离。
evidenceZh: 使用给定的比例尺（如1:25,000）根据地图上的测量值计算实际距离
使用选定的比例因子（scale factor）绘制房间的比例图（scale diagram）
在涉及不同单位的问题中，进行地图距离与实际距离之间的换算
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看一张地图，上面标明 1 厘米 = 50 千米，他们能算出地图上相距 4.5 厘米的两个城市之间的实际距离吗？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Unit Conversions
topics.description: Convert freely between related standard units of measurement (time, length, area, volume/capacity, mass) using decimal notation to up to three decimal places where appropriate
evidence: Convert between area units such as cm² and m² using the square of the linear scale factor
Perform multi-step conversions (e.g. convert 2.5 hours to seconds via minutes)
Convert volume units such as cm³ to litres and explain the relationship
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} convert between units confidently — for example, changing kilometres to metres, kilograms to grams, or hours and minutes to just minutes — including multi-step problems?
topics.descriptionZh: 在相关标准测量单位（时间、长度、面积、体积/容积、质量）之间进行自由换算，并在适当时使用最多保留三位小数的十进制表示法 (decimal notation)。
evidenceZh: 使用线性比例因子 (linear scale factor) 的平方在 cm² 和 m² 等面积单位之间进行换算
执行多步换算（例如，通过分钟将 2.5 小时换算为秒）
将 cm³ 等体积单位换算为升 (litres)，并解释它们之间的关系
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否自信地在不同单位之间进行换算——例如，将千米换算为米、千克换算为克，或将小时和分钟换算为单纯的分钟数——包括多步换算问题？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Percentages (age 12+)
topics.description: Solve problems involving percentage increase, percentage decrease, finding the original value after a percentage change, and calculating simple interest
evidence: Calculate a 15% increase on £240 using a decimal multiplier (× 1.15)
Find the original price before a 20% discount resulted in a sale price of £64
Calculate simple interest on £500 at 3% per annum for 4 years
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a bike originally costs £250 and its price goes up by 8%, can {{name}} work out the new price — and if a savings account earns 3% simple interest per year, how much interest would £500 earn in 4 years?
topics.descriptionZh: 解决涉及百分比增加（percentage increase）、百分比减少（percentage decrease）、求百分比变化后的原始值，以及计算单利（simple interest）的问题
evidenceZh: 使用小数乘数（decimal multiplier）× 1.15，计算240英镑增加15%后的结果
已知降价20%后的售价为64英镑，求打折前的原价
计算单利：本金500英镑，年利率3%，期限4年
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果一辆自行车原价250英镑，价格上涨了8%，{{name}}能算出新价格吗？另外，如果储蓄账户每年产生3%的单利（simple interest），500英镑存4年能赚取多少利息？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Proportion
topics.description: Recognise and solve problems involving direct proportion (as one quantity increases, the other increases at a constant rate) and inverse proportion (as one increases, the other decreases), including graphical and algebraic representations
evidence: Identify whether a real-world relationship is direct or inverse proportion and justify the choice
Set up and solve a direct-proportion equation (e.g. if 4 pens cost £6, find the cost of 10)
Sketch graphs showing direct proportion (straight line through origin) and inverse proportion (curve)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} understand the difference between quantities that grow together at the same rate (direct proportion) and ones where one goes up as the other goes down — like more workers meaning fewer days to finish a job (inverse proportion)?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识并解决正比例（一个量增加，另一个量按固定速率增加）和反比例（一个量增加，另一个量减少）的问题，包括图形和代数表示方法。
evidenceZh: 判断现实生活中的关系是正比例还是反比例，并说明理由
列出并求解正比例方程（例如：如果4支笔6英镑，求10支笔的价格）
绘制正比例（经过原点的直线）和反比例（曲线）的图像
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否理解正比例（两个量按相同比例共同增长）和反比例（一个量增加，另一个量就减少，比如工人越多，完成工作所需的天数越少）之间的区别？

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Ratio Notation and Relationships
topics.description: Understand that a multiplicative relationship between two quantities can be expressed as a ratio; use ratio notation; simplify ratios
evidence: Explain why 'for every 2 red beads there are 5 blue beads' can be written as 2:5 or as 2/5 of the blue count
Identify the multiplicative relationship in a table of values (e.g. y is always 3 times x)
Connect the ratio a:b to the fraction a/b and to the linear function y = (a/b)x
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a ratio like 3:4 is really the same as the fraction ¾ — and show how that relationship connects to a straight-line graph through the origin?
topics.nameZh: 比的表示法与关系 (Ratio Notation and Relationships)
topics.descriptionZh: 理解两个量之间的乘性关系 (multiplicative relationship) 可以用比 (ratio) 来表示；使用比的记法 (ratio notation)；化简比 (simplify ratios)
evidenceZh: 解释为什么“每2颗红珠子对应5颗蓝珠子”可以写成2:5，或者写成蓝珠子数量的2/5
识别数值表中的乘性关系 (multiplicative relationship)（例如，y总是x的3倍）
将比 (ratio) a:b 与分数 (fraction) a/b 以及线性函数 (linear function) y = (a/b)x 联系起来
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么像 3:4 这样的比 (ratio) 实际上与分数 (fraction) 3/4 是相同的——并展示这种关系如何连接到一条经过原点的直线图 (straight-line graph through the origin)？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Expressing Feelings with Words
topics.description: Express their own feelings appropriately using words rather than actions — saying 'I feel angry because...' instead of hitting, shouting, or withdrawing
evidence: Use an 'I feel ___ when ___' statement during a disagreement
Choose to tell an adult how they feel instead of acting out physically
Describe their feelings about a difficult situation using at least two emotion words
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is frustrated — say a sibling takes their toy — do they use words to say how they feel rather than snatching it back or crying?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用语言而非行动来恰当地表达自己的感受——说“我感到生气，因为……”而不是打人、大喊大叫或退缩
evidenceZh: 在发生争执时使用“当……时，我感到……”的句式进行表达
选择向成年人表达自己的感受，而不是采取肢体动作发泄
使用至少两个情绪词汇来描述自己对困难处境的感受
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}感到沮丧时——比如兄弟姐妹拿走了他们的玩具——他们会用语言表达自己的感受，而不是把玩具抢回来或哭泣吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Feelings Change and Differ
topics.description: Understand that everyone has feelings, that feelings change throughout the day, and that the same event can make different people feel different things
evidence: Give an example of a time their feelings changed during a single day
Explain why two children might feel differently about the same event
Recognise that feelings are temporary and can change
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you and {{name}} watch the same film and you find it funny but {{name}} finds it scary, can they understand why you both felt differently?
topics.nameZh: 情绪会变化且因人而异
topics.descriptionZh: 理解每个人都有情绪，情绪在一天中会发生变化，并且同一件事可能会让不同的人产生不同的感受。
evidenceZh: 举出一个自己在一天中情绪发生变化的例子
解释为什么两个孩子可能会对同一件事有不同的感受
认识到情绪是暂时的，并且是可以改变的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你和{{name}}看同一部电影，你觉得很搞笑但{{name}}觉得很害怕，他们能理解为什么你们俩的感受不同吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Naming Basic Emotions
topics.description: Name and recognise basic emotions — happy, sad, angry, scared, excited, and surprised — in themselves and in others by looking at facial expressions and body language
evidence: Label at least five basic emotions from pictures or real situations
Match facial expressions to emotion words in a sorting activity
Say 'I feel ___' using a correct emotion word when asked about their own day
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a friend crying at a birthday party, can they tell you what that friend might be feeling and name the emotion?
topics.descriptionZh: 通过观察面部表情和肢体语言，命名并识别自己和他人的基本情绪——快乐、悲伤、愤怒、害怕、兴奋和惊讶
evidenceZh: 根据图片或真实情境，至少识别并命名五种基本情绪
在分类活动中，将面部表情与相应的情绪词汇进行匹配
当被问及自己的一天时，能使用正确的情绪词汇说出‘我感觉___’
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}在生日派对上看到朋友在哭，他们能告诉你朋友可能有什么感觉，并说出这种情绪的名称吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Triggers and Causes of Feelings
topics.description: Understand that feelings have causes — something happens (a trigger) and that makes us feel a certain way — and begin to identify what triggers their own emotions
evidence: Describe a trigger for at least three different emotions from their own experience
Complete 'I felt ___ because ___' sentences accurately
Identify what made a character in a story feel a particular way
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} gets upset about something at school, can they explain to you what happened that made them feel that way?
topics.nameZh: 情绪的触发因素与起因
topics.descriptionZh: 理解情绪是有起因的——发生某件事（触发因素）会让我们产生某种感受——并开始识别是什么触发了自己的情绪。
evidenceZh: 结合自身经历，描述至少三种不同情绪的触发因素
准确完成‘我感到___，因为___’的造句
识别故事中角色产生特定情绪的原因
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 在学校因为某事感到心烦时，他们能向您解释发生了什么事让他们产生这种感受吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Emotion Vocabulary
topics.description: Use a wider vocabulary of emotion words beyond the basics — including frustrated, worried, anxious, embarrassed, jealous, proud, disappointed, grateful, and lonely — and distinguish between similar emotions
evidence: Use at least five emotion words beyond the basic six in everyday conversation
Explain the difference between two similar emotions such as angry and frustrated
Choose a precise emotion word that fits a described scenario
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} doesn't get invited to a classmate's party, can they describe whether they feel disappointed, jealous, lonely, or a mix — rather than just saying 'sad'?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用超越基础词汇的更广泛的情绪词汇——包括沮丧（frustrated）、担忧（worried）、焦虑（anxious）、尴尬（embarrassed）、嫉妒（jealous）、自豪（proud）、失望（disappointed）、感激（grateful）和孤独（lonely）——并能区分相似的情绪。
evidenceZh: 在日常对话中，至少使用五个基础六种情绪之外的情绪词汇
解释两种相似情绪之间的区别，例如生气（angry）和沮丧（frustrated）
选择一个准确的情绪词汇来匹配所描述的场景
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 没有被邀请参加同学的聚会，他们能否描述自己是感到失望（disappointed）、嫉妒（jealous）、孤独（lonely），还是这些情绪的混合，而不是仅仅说“伤心（sad）”？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Hidden and Masked Feelings
topics.description: Recognise that people sometimes hide or mask their true feelings — smiling when they're actually sad, or saying 'I'm fine' when they're not — and understand why someone might do this
evidence: Give an example of a time someone might hide their feelings and explain why
Identify mismatches between someone's words and their body language
Explain that hiding feelings is common but that it's usually better to share with someone trusted
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a friend at school says 'I'm fine' but looks upset and is being very quiet, can {{name}} recognise that the friend might not actually be fine?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识到人们有时会隐藏或掩饰自己的真实情绪——比如明明很难过却面带微笑，或者明明感觉不好却说“我没事”——并理解人们为什么会这样做
evidenceZh: 举出一个人们可能会隐藏情绪的例子，并解释原因
识别某人的言语与其肢体语言之间的不一致
解释隐藏情绪是很常见的现象，但通常最好与信任的人分享
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果在学校里，一个朋友说“我没事”，但看起来很难过且非常安静，{{name}}能认识到这位朋友可能实际上并没有“没事”吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: How Emotions Feel in Your Body
topics.description: Understand the connection between emotions and the body — recognising physical signals like butterflies in the stomach (nervous), clenched fists (angry), racing heart (scared or excited), and tight shoulders (stressed)
evidence: Name at least three body sensations and match them to the emotions they signal
Notice a physical feeling in their own body and identify the emotion behind it
Explain why the body reacts physically when we have strong emotions
topics.assessmentPrompt: Before a school performance or sports day, can {{name}} notice and tell you about the physical feelings in their body — like butterflies in their tummy — and connect them to being nervous or excited?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解情绪与身体之间的联系——识别身体发出的生理信号，例如肚子里像有蝴蝶在飞（紧张）、握紧拳头（生气）、心跳加速（害怕或兴奋）以及肩膀紧绷（压力大）
evidenceZh: 说出至少三种身体感觉，并将它们与所对应的情绪匹配起来
注意到自己身体上的某种生理感觉，并识别出背后的情绪
解释为什么当我们有强烈的情绪时，身体会产生生理反应
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在学校演出或运动会之前，{{name}} 能否注意到并告诉你他们身体上的感觉——比如肚子里像有蝴蝶在飞——并将其与紧张或兴奋的情绪联系起来？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Mild to Strong Emotions
topics.description: Understand that emotions come in different intensities — from mild to strong — and that the same emotion can feel very different depending on how intense it is (e.g., annoyed → angry → furious, or nervous → anxious → panicked)
evidence: Place three related emotion words in order from mild to strong
Rate their own emotion on a simple scale (e.g., 1-5) in a real situation
Explain why recognising intensity matters for choosing how to respond
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell the difference between being a bit annoyed about losing a game and being truly furious — and explain that they're different levels of the same feeling?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解情绪具有不同的强度——从轻微到强烈——并且同一种情绪根据强度的不同，感受也会大不相同（例如：烦躁 → 生气 → 暴怒，或紧张 → 焦虑 → 恐慌）
evidenceZh: 将三个相关的情绪词汇按从轻微到强烈的顺序排列
在真实情境中，使用简单的量表（例如1-5分）为自己的情绪强度打分
解释为什么识别情绪强度对于选择如何应对很重要
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否区分因输掉游戏而感到有点烦躁与真正感到暴怒之间的区别——并解释它们是同一种情绪的不同强度级别？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Culture and Experience Shape Emotions
topics.description: Understand that emotional responses are shaped by personal experiences, culture, and context — the same situation triggers different emotions in different people because of their backgrounds and past experiences
evidence: Explain why two people might have very different emotional reactions to the same event
Give an example of how a past experience shaped someone's emotional response
Describe how cultural background might influence what makes someone feel proud or embarrassed
topics.assessmentPrompt: If one child in {{name}}'s class gets very scared during a thunderstorm while others think it's exciting, can {{name}} understand that the scared child might have had a frightening experience with storms before?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解情绪反应是由个人经历、文化和情境背景塑造的——由于背景和过往经历的不同，相同的情境会在不同的人身上引发不同的情绪。
evidenceZh: 解释为什么两个人对同一事件可能会有截然不同的情绪反应
举例说明过往经历如何塑造某人的情绪反应
描述文化背景如何影响让人感到自豪或尴尬的因素
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}班上的一个孩子在雷雨天感到非常害怕，而其他孩子却觉得很兴奋，{{name}}能否理解这个害怕的孩子以前可能有过关于风暴的可怕经历？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Emotional Patterns Over Time
topics.description: Reflect on their own emotional patterns over time — noticing recurring triggers, understanding their typical responses, and recognising how their emotional awareness has grown
evidence: Identify a recurring emotional trigger and their typical response to it
Describe how their emotional understanding has changed compared to when they were younger
Set a personal goal related to emotional awareness, such as noticing when stress is building
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you something like 'I always get stressed before tests but I've learned that's normal for me' — showing they understand their own emotional patterns?
topics.nameZh: 随时间变化的情绪模式
topics.descriptionZh: 反思自己随时间推移的情绪模式——留意反复出现的情绪触发因素，了解自身典型的应对反应，并认识到情绪觉察能力的成长
evidenceZh: 识别一个反复出现的情绪触发因素及其典型反应
描述与年幼时相比，自身的情绪认知发生了怎样的变化
设定一个与情绪觉察相关的个人目标，例如察觉压力正在逐渐累积
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能说出类似这样的话吗：‘我考试前总是感到有压力，但我已经明白这对我来说很正常’——以此表明他们理解自己的情绪模式？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Emotions and Decision-Making
topics.description: Understand how emotions influence thinking and decision-making — that strong feelings can cloud judgement, that we often make different choices when calm versus when upset, and that recognising this gives us more control
evidence: Give an example of a time a strong emotion led them or someone else to a poor decision
Explain the idea of 'cooling off' before making an important choice
Describe how the same situation looks different when you're calm versus upset
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sends an angry message to a friend during an argument and later regrets it, can they explain how their anger affected their decision and what they might do differently next time?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解情绪如何影响思考和做决定——强烈的情绪可能会蒙蔽判断（cloud judgement），我们在平静和生气时往往会做出不同的选择，而认识到这一点能让我们更好地掌控自己。
evidenceZh: 举一个例子，说明强烈的情绪如何导致自己或他人做出糟糕的决定
解释在做重要决定前“冷静一下（cooling off）”的做法
描述在平静和生气（upset）时，看待同一件事情会有什么不同
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在争吵时给朋友发了一条带着怒气的信息，事后又感到后悔，他们能解释自己的愤怒是如何影响这个决定的吗？下次他们可能会采取什么不同的做法？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Mixed and Conflicting Emotions
topics.description: Understand that people can experience mixed or conflicting emotions at the same time — feeling excited and nervous about starting a new school, or happy for a friend who won but disappointed for yourself
evidence: Describe a personal situation where they felt two emotions simultaneously
Explain why mixed feelings are normal and not something to worry about
Identify mixed emotions in a character from a book or film
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}}'s best friend gets picked for the team and they don't, can {{name}} explain that they feel happy for their friend AND disappointed for themselves at the same time?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解人们可以同时体验混合或冲突的情绪——例如对开始新学校生活感到既兴奋又紧张，或者为获胜的朋友感到高兴，但同时为自己感到失落。
evidenceZh: 描述一个自己同时感受到两种情绪的个人经历
解释为什么混合情绪是正常的，无需为此担忧
识别书本或电影中角色所表现出的混合情绪
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}的好朋友被选入团队而自己落选时，{{name}}能否解释自己同时为朋友感到高兴，又为自己感到失落？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Brain Science of Emotions
topics.description: Understand how the amygdala triggers emotional responses and how the prefrontal cortex (still developing in adolescence) regulates them; explain why stress hormones (cortisol, adrenaline) affect thinking and memory; understand that the adolescent brain's dopamine system makes feelings more intense; distinguish between emotion regulation (managing feelings effectively) and emotion suppression (pushing feelings down, which is counterproductive); introduce cognitive reappraisal as a research-backed technique for changing how we interpret a situation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain, in basic terms, why teenagers tend to feel emotions more intensely than adults — what's happening in the developing brain that makes feelings so powerful during adolescence, and what's the difference between managing a feeling and suppressing it?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解杏仁核（amygdala）如何触发情绪反应，以及前额叶皮层（prefrontal cortex，在青春期仍在发育中）如何对其进行调节；解释为什么压力荷尔蒙（皮质醇 cortisol、肾上腺素 adrenaline）会影响思考和记忆；理解青春期大脑的多巴胺（dopamine）系统会使情绪感受变得更加强烈；区分情绪调节（emotion regulation，有效管理情绪）与情绪压抑（emotion suppression，强行压制情绪，往往会适得其反）；介绍认知重评（cognitive reappraisal），这是一种有科学研究支持的方法，能帮助我们改变对特定情境的解读方式。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否用通俗易懂的语言解释，为什么青少年体验到的情绪往往比成年人更强烈——正在发育的大脑中究竟发生了什么，使得青春期的情绪感受如此强烈，以及管理情绪和压抑情绪之间有什么区别？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Identity and Belonging in Adolescence
topics.description: Understand that adolescence involves active construction of identity, leading to emotional complexity around questions of 'who am I?'; explore the emotional dynamics of belonging to multiple groups simultaneously (family, peer group, cultural or religious identity); understand social comparison and its intensification through social media; recognise that identity is not fixed and that uncertainty about identity is normal, not a sign of failure; develop language for navigating emotions tied to group membership and personal values
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} goes through a phase of feeling unsure about who they are or where they belong, can they explain why this kind of uncertainty is a completely normal and even necessary part of adolescence — not a sign that something is wrong?
topics.nameZh: 青春期的身份认同与归属感
topics.descriptionZh: 理解青春期涉及身份认同（identity）的主动建构，从而在思考“我是谁？”时产生复杂的情感体验；探索同时归属于多个群体（家庭、同辈群体、文化或宗教群体）的情感动态；理解社会比较（social comparison）及其在社交媒体环境下的加剧效应；认识到身份认同并非固定不变，对身份的不确定性是完全正常的，绝非失败的标志；培养能够妥善处理与群体归属感及个人价值观相关情感的表达语言。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 经历了一段对自己是谁或属于哪里感到不确定的时期，他们能否解释为什么这种不确定性是青春期完全正常甚至必要的一部分，而不是出了什么问题的信号？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Emotional Intelligence
topics.description: Introduce Goleman's emotional intelligence model (self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy, social skills); develop vocabulary for complex emotional states (ambivalence, ennui, schadenfreude, awe, nostalgia, cognitive dissonance); understand the evidence linking emotional intelligence to wellbeing, relationship quality, and long-term life outcomes; reflect on personal emotional growth over the secondary school years; explore the relationship between emotional literacy and mental health, and know when to seek professional support
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe a real situation where being aware of their own emotions — knowing what they were feeling and why — helped them handle a difficult moment better than if they had just reacted automatically?
topics.descriptionZh: 介绍戈尔曼的情绪智力模型（自我意识 self-awareness、自我调节 self-regulation、动机 motivation、同理心 empathy、社交技能 social skills）；培养用于描述复杂情绪状态的词汇（矛盾心理 ambivalence、倦怠 ennui、幸灾乐祸 schadenfreude、敬畏 awe、怀旧 nostalgia、认知失调 cognitive dissonance）；理解将情绪智力与幸福感、人际关系质量和长期生活结果联系起来的证据；反思在中学阶段个人情绪的成长；探索情绪素养与心理健康之间的关系，并了解何时应寻求专业支持。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否描述一个真实的情境：在其中，觉察到自身的情绪——清楚自己当下的感受及原因——帮助他们比单纯依靠自动反应更好地度过了一个艰难时刻？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Everyday Kindness and Care
topics.description: Show kindness and care towards others in simple everyday ways — comforting a friend who is upset, helping someone who has dropped their things, sharing without being asked, and saying kind words
evidence: Spontaneously offer comfort to someone who is visibly upset
Help another person with a practical task without being asked
Use kind words to encourage or cheer up someone who is struggling
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a younger child at school falls over in the playground, does {{name}} go over to help or comfort them without being told to by an adult?
topics.descriptionZh: 以简单的日常方式向他人表达友善与关爱——安慰难过的朋友，帮助掉落物品的人，主动分享，以及说出友善的话语
evidenceZh: 主动安慰明显情绪低落的人
无需提醒，主动帮助他人完成具体事务
用友善的话语鼓励或宽慰遇到困难的人
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果在学校操场上有年纪较小的孩子摔倒了，{{name}} 会在没有大人吩咐的情况下主动去帮忙或安慰他们吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Other People's Feelings and Thoughts
topics.description: Understand that other people have their own feelings and thoughts, and that these might be different from your own — a foundational awareness that not everyone sees or feels things the same way
evidence: State that other people can feel differently about the same thing
Give an example of a time someone felt differently from them about the same situation
Accept another child's feeling as valid even when it differs from their own
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} loves dogs but their friend is scared of dogs, can {{name}} understand that their friend's fear is real even though they don't feel it themselves?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解他人有自己的感受和想法，并且这些可能与自己的想法不同——这是一种基础的认知（foundational awareness），即并非每个人看待或感受事物的方式都一样。
evidenceZh: 能够说出他人对同一件事可能会有不同的感受
能够举出一个例子，说明在某件事情上他人的感受与自己不同
即使其他孩子的感受与自己不同，也能认可并接纳其感受的合理性
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 喜欢狗，但他们的朋友害怕狗，{{name}} 能否理解朋友的恐惧是真实的，即使他们自己并没有这种感觉？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Similarities & Differences
topics.description: Notice and appreciate ways that people are similar to and different from each other — including appearance, family structures, languages spoken, foods eaten, and celebrations observed — and understand that differences make communities interesting
evidence: Name several ways people in their class or community are different from each other
Describe at least one thing they have learned from someone who is different from them
Express a positive attitude about differences rather than judging them
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} talk positively about how families in their class are different — some have two mums, some speak another language at home, some celebrate different holidays — and see this as interesting rather than strange?
topics.descriptionZh: 观察并欣赏人们之间的相似与差异之处——包括外貌、家庭结构、使用的语言、饮食习惯以及庆祝的节日——并理解正是这些差异让社区变得更加有趣。
evidenceZh: 列举班级或社区中人们彼此不同的几个方面
描述至少一件他们从与自己不同的人身上学到的东西
对差异抱有积极的态度，而不是加以评判
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否积极地谈论班级里不同家庭之间的差异——比如有些家庭有两位妈妈，有些家庭在家里说另一种语言，有些家庭庆祝不同的节日——并认为这些差异很有趣，而不是觉得很奇怪？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Vocabulary: understanding others
topics.description: Know and use the key vocabulary for understanding others — empathy, perspective, kind, fair, community, similar, different, and care — and understand that these words describe real habits of thinking and feeling
evidence: Use the word 'empathy' correctly and distinguish it from 'sympathy' — e.g. 'Empathy means I try to feel what they feel'
Explain what 'perspective' and 'point of view' mean and demonstrate by describing how two people might see the same event differently
Use words like 'community', 'belonging', and 'inclusion' accurately when talking about their school or neighbourhood
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} sees someone who seems sad or left out, can they describe what that person might be feeling using words like 'empathy' or 'perspective' — showing they're thinking about the other person, not just themselves?
topics.descriptionZh: 掌握并使用理解他人的关键词汇——共情（empathy）、视角（perspective）、友善（kind）、公平（fair）、社区（community）、相似（similar）、不同（different）和关怀（care）——并理解这些词汇描述了真实的思维与感受习惯。
evidenceZh: 正确使用'共情（empathy）'一词，并将其与'同情（sympathy）'区分开来——例如：'共情意味着我努力去体会他们的感受'
解释'视角（perspective）'和'观点（point of view）'的含义，并通过描述两个人如何看待同一事件的不同之处来加以说明
在谈论学校或社区时，准确使用'社区（community）'、'归属感（belonging）'和'包容（inclusion）'等词汇
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 看到有人似乎悲伤或被孤立时，他们能否使用'共情'或'视角'等词汇来描述那个人可能的感受——这表明他们在为他人着想，而不仅仅是考虑自己？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Different Lives and Experiences
topics.description: Understand that people's lives and experiences can be very different from their own — that some children face challenges like disability, poverty, family difficulties, or being new to a country — and develop compassion rather than judgement
evidence: Describe at least two ways another child's life experience might differ significantly from their own
Explain why it's important not to judge someone based on their circumstances
Suggest a kind action they could take to help someone facing a difficult situation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a new child joins {{name}}'s class who doesn't speak much English or whose family situation is very different, does {{name}} show understanding and try to include them rather than avoiding them?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解人们的生活和经历可能与自己大不相同——有些孩子面临着残疾、贫困、家庭困难或初到异国等挑战——并培养同情心而非评判心理
evidenceZh: 至少描述两种其他孩子的生活经历与自己显著不同的情况
解释为什么不应根据他人的处境来评判他们
建议一项可以采取的友善行动，以帮助面临困难处境的人
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果班里来了一位不太会说英语或家庭情况非常不同的新同学，{{name}}是否能表现出理解并主动接纳对方，而不是刻意回避？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Fairness, Equality and Equity
topics.description: Understand what fairness means and why it matters — recognising that fair doesn't always mean equal (everyone getting the same) but can mean equitable (everyone getting what they need), and applying this understanding in group situations
evidence: Explain the difference between treating everyone the same and treating everyone fairly
Give an example of a situation where equal treatment wouldn't be fair
Apply fairness thinking when sharing resources or making group decisions
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a child with a broken arm gets extra time to finish a task at school, can {{name}} explain why that's fair even though other children don't get extra time?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解公平的含义及其重要性——认识到公平并不总是意味着平等（每个人得到相同的待遇），也可以是公正（每个人得到他们真正需要的），并能在团队活动中运用这一理解。
evidenceZh: 解释平等对待（给每个人一样的东西）和公平对待（给每个人适合的东西）之间的区别
举出一个平等对待反而不公平的例子
在分享资源或进行团队决策时运用公平思维
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果一个手臂骨折的孩子在学校获得了额外的时间来完成一项任务，{{name}} 能否解释为什么这样做是公平的，即使其他孩子没有得到额外的时间？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Seeing Someone Else's Point of View
topics.description: Practise perspective-taking by imagining how someone else might feel in a given situation — using prompts like 'How would you feel if that happened to you?' and applying this when reading stories or during real interactions
evidence: Describe how a character in a story feels and give reasons based on the plot
Predict how another child would feel in a described scenario
Use perspective-taking during a real disagreement to understand the other person's view
topics.assessmentPrompt: When reading a story together, can {{name}} pause and explain how a character might be feeling and why — putting themselves in the character's shoes?
topics.descriptionZh: 通过想象他人在特定情境下的感受来练习换位思考（perspective-taking）——使用诸如‘如果这事发生在你身上，你会有什么感觉？’的引导语，并在阅读故事或真实互动中应用这一技巧。
evidenceZh: 描述故事中角色的感受，并根据故事情节说明理由
预测另一个孩子在特定情境描述中会有怎样的感受
在真实的意见分歧中运用换位思考，以理解对方的观点
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在共同阅读故事时，{{name}} 能否停下来，设身处地地代入角色，解释该角色可能的感受及其原因？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Vocabulary: social awareness
topics.description: Know and use the vocabulary of social awareness — including stereotype, prejudice, discrimination, equality, equity, bias, compassion, and fairness — and understand what distinguishes these closely related concepts
evidence: Explain what 'stereotype' and 'prejudice' mean and give an example of each from everyday life
Use words like 'equality', 'equity', and 'bias' correctly when discussing a scenario — e.g. 'That's not equity because not everyone got what they needed'
Identify an example of discrimination in a story or news article and explain why it is unfair using the correct vocabulary
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears a classmate say something that groups all people of a certain background together, can they explain why that's a stereotype and how it differs from a fact about an individual person?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解并使用社会意识（social awareness）相关的词汇——包括刻板印象（stereotype）、偏见（prejudice）、歧视（discrimination）、平等（equality）、公平（equity）、偏差（bias）、同情（compassion）和公正（fairness）——并理解这些密切相关概念之间的区别。
evidenceZh: 解释“刻板印象”（stereotype）和“偏见”（prejudice）的含义，并分别举出日常生活中的例子。
在讨论特定情境时正确使用“平等”（equality）、“公平”（equity）和“偏差”（bias）等词汇——例如：“那不是公平（equity），因为并不是每个人都得到了他们所需要的”。
在故事或新闻报道中找出一个“歧视”（discrimination）的例子，并使用正确的词汇解释为什么这是不公平的。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 听到同学说了一些将某种特定背景的所有人归为一类的话，他们能否解释为什么这是一个“刻板印象”（stereotype），以及它与关于个人的事实有何不同？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Prejudice and Discrimination
topics.description: Understand the impact of prejudice and discrimination on individuals and communities — that treating people unfairly because of their identity causes real harm — and recognise their own responsibility to stand against it
evidence: Define prejudice and discrimination in their own words with examples
Describe the emotional and social impact of discrimination on the person experiencing it
Identify at least one action they can personally take to challenge unfair treatment
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees someone at school being excluded or teased because of their race, religion, or disability, can they explain why that's wrong and describe what they could do about it?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解偏见和歧视对个人及社区的影响——明白因身份而受到不公平对待会造成实质性的伤害——并认识到自己有责任挺身反对这种行为。
evidenceZh: 用自己的话定义偏见和歧视并举例说明
描述歧视对受害者造成的情感和社会影响
找出至少一项他们个人可以采取的抵制不公平对待的行动
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}在学校看到有人因为种族、宗教或残疾而受到排挤或嘲笑，他们能否解释为什么这样做是错的，并描述他们可以采取什么行动？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Questioning Your Own Biases
topics.description: Reflect on their own assumptions and biases — recognising that everyone carries unconscious assumptions about others, and that actively questioning these assumptions is an ongoing practice that leads to greater fairness and empathy
evidence: Describe a time they made an assumption about someone that turned out to be wrong
Explain what unconscious bias means in simple terms
Describe a strategy for checking their own assumptions, such as asking questions before judging
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} catch themselves making an assumption about someone — like assuming a quiet child is unfriendly — and then question whether that assumption is fair?
topics.descriptionZh: 反思自己的预设（assumptions）和偏见（biases）——认识到每个人对他人都有无意识的预设（unconscious assumptions），并且积极质疑这些预设是一个持续的过程，能培养更大的公平心和同理心（empathy）。
evidenceZh: 描述一次自己对某人做出预设结果却被证明是错误的经历
用简单的语言解释“无意识偏见”（unconscious bias）的含义
描述一种检验自身预设的策略，例如在做出评判前先提问
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否察觉到自己对某人做出了预设——比如认为一个安静的孩子不友善——并进而质疑这种预设是否公平？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Stereotypes and Individual Differences
topics.description: Recognise stereotypes — oversimplified beliefs about groups of people based on gender, race, age, or other characteristics — and understand that stereotypes are unfair because they ignore individual differences
evidence: Define what a stereotype is in their own words
Identify a common stereotype and explain why it is inaccurate
Challenge a stereotype they encounter by giving a counter-example
topics.assessmentPrompt: If someone says 'boys don't cry' or 'girls aren't good at maths', can {{name}} explain why those statements are unfair stereotypes that don't apply to everyone?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识刻板印象——基于性别、种族、年龄或其他特征对人群产生的过度简化的观念——并理解刻板印象是不公平的，因为它们忽视了个体差异。
evidenceZh: 用自己的话定义什么是刻板印象
指出一个常见的刻板印象并解释为什么它是不准确的
通过举出反例来挑战遇到的刻板印象
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果有人说“男孩不哭”或“女孩不擅长数学”，{{name}}能解释为什么这些说法是不公平的刻板印象，并不适用于所有人吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: The world contains many cultures, traditions
topics.description: Understand that the world contains many cultures, traditions, and belief systems, and that learning about others' perspectives enriches our own understanding — developing genuine curiosity about and respect for cultural diversity
evidence: Describe a cultural practice different from their own and explain what they find interesting about it
Ask respectful questions to learn about someone else's traditions or beliefs
Explain why understanding different cultures makes communities stronger
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} show genuine interest when learning about how families from different cultures celebrate, eat, or worship — asking questions respectfully rather than dismissing things that are unfamiliar?
topics.nameZh: 世界包含多元的文化与传统
topics.descriptionZh: 理解世界上存在着多种文化、传统和信仰体系，了解他人的视角能丰富我们自身的认知——培养对文化多样性的真正好奇心和尊重。
evidenceZh: 描述一种不同于自身的文化习俗，并解释他们觉得有趣的地方
怀着尊重之心提问，了解他人的传统或信仰
解释为什么理解不同的文化能让社区变得更加强大
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 了解不同文化背景的家庭如何庆祝节日、日常饮食或进行信仰活动时，是否表现出真正的兴趣——以尊重的方式提问，而不是排斥不熟悉的事物？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Systemic Inequality and Allyship
topics.description: Move beyond 'treating everyone the same' to understand that structural advantages and disadvantages exist regardless of individual effort or intention; explore concrete examples of systemic inequality (educational attainment gaps, gender pay gap, representation in leadership); distinguish between individual prejudice and structural discrimination; understand intersectionality — how multiple aspects of identity interact; develop informed compassion rooted in evidence rather than pity; explore what being a genuine ally means in practice
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between treating everyone 'the same' and actually making things fair — and give a real example of a structural barrier that means two people starting in different positions face unequal opportunities even if they try equally hard?
topics.nameZh: 系统性不平等与同盟支持 (Systemic Inequality and Allyship)
topics.descriptionZh: 超越“对所有人一视同仁”的简单观念，理解无论个人多努力，结构性的优势与劣势（structural advantages and disadvantages）都客观存在；探讨系统性不平等（systemic inequality）的具体例子（如教育成就差距、性别薪酬差距、领导层中的代表性差异）；区分个人偏见（individual prejudice）与结构性歧视（structural discrimination）；理解交叉性（intersectionality），即多重身份特征如何相互交织影响；培养基于事实和证据的理性共情，而非单纯的怜悯；探索在实际生活中成为一名真正盟友（ally）的具体行动。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释对所有人“一视同仁”与真正实现“公平”之间的区别，并给出一个结构性障碍（structural barrier）的真实例子，说明即使两个人付出同样的努力，处于不同起点的人仍会面临不平等的机会？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Sympathy Versus Empathy
topics.description: Distinguish sympathy ('I feel sorry for you') from empathy ('I understand what you're experiencing'); develop active listening skills: reflecting, paraphrasing, asking open questions, resisting the urge to problem-solve too quickly; understand empathic curiosity as genuine interest in another person's inner world; practise being present for someone in distress without trying to fix or minimise their experience; understand vicarious trauma and compassion fatigue, and how empathetic people can protect their own wellbeing while staying present for others
topics.assessmentPrompt: When a friend is going through something really difficult, can {{name}} describe what makes a listener genuinely helpful — and explain the difference between empathy and sympathy, using an example of something that sounds supportive but actually isn't?
topics.descriptionZh: 区分同情（“我为你感到难过”）与共情（“我理解你的经历”）；培养积极倾听技巧：情感反映（reflecting）、内容释义（paraphrasing）、提出开放式问题、克制过早提供解决方案的冲动；理解“共情好奇心”（empathic curiosity），即对他人内心世界的真诚关注；练习陪伴处于痛苦中的人，而不急于解决问题或淡化其感受；理解替代性创伤（vicarious trauma）和同情疲劳（compassion fatigue），并学习富有共情能力的人如何在陪伴他人的同时保护自己的身心健康。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当朋友经历非常艰难的时期时，{{name}}能否描述出什么样的倾听者才是真正有帮助的——并解释共情与同情的区别，同时举出一个听起来像在支持对方但实际上并非如此的例子？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Global Citizenship
topics.description: Understand what it means to be a citizen in an interconnected world where decisions in one place affect people elsewhere; explore global issues (climate justice, forced migration, global health, poverty) through an empathy lens, distinguishing facts from value judgements; engage with the ethical tension between obligations to those close to us and obligations to distant strangers; introduce evidence-based giving and effective altruism as one framework for thinking about global responsibility; develop a personal, reasoned stance on global citizenship that acknowledges complexity
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads about a crisis happening in another country, can they describe how they think about their own responsibility — and name one practical thing young people can genuinely do about large-scale problems rather than just feeling helpless?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解在相互联系的世界中成为公民的意义，即一个地方的决策会影响其他地方的人们；通过同理心视角探讨全球性问题（气候正义、被迫迁移、全球健康、贫困），区分事实与价值判断；探讨对身边之人与远方陌生人的义务之间的伦理张力；引入基于证据的捐赠（evidence-based giving）和有效利他主义（effective altruism）作为思考全球责任的框架之一；培养一种承认复杂性的、个人的、经过深思熟虑的全球公民立场
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}读到发生在其他国家的危机时，他们能否描述自己是如何思考自身责任的——并说出年轻人可以采取的一件切实可行的事情来应对大规模问题，而不是仅仅感到无助？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Asking for Help
topics.description: Ask for help when they need it — from a friend, teacher, or family member — and understand that asking for help is a sign of strength, not weakness
evidence: Approach an appropriate person and ask for help clearly
Identify who to go to for different kinds of help (academic, emotional, practical)
Explain why asking for help is sensible rather than something to be embarrassed about
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is stuck on something at school or feeling worried about something, will they ask a teacher or friend for help rather than struggling in silence?
topics.descriptionZh: 在需要时寻求帮助——向朋友、老师或家庭成员求助——并明白寻求帮助是力量的体现，而非软弱的表现。
evidenceZh: 找到合适的人并清晰地提出求助
识别在需要不同帮助（学业、情感、实际）时应向谁求助
解释为什么寻求帮助是明智之举，而非令人难堪之事
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}在学校遇到难题或对某事感到担忧，他们会向老师或朋友求助，而不是独自默默承受吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Listening to Others
topics.description: Listen to others when they are speaking — looking at the speaker, waiting until they finish, and showing they have heard by responding to what was said rather than just talking about their own ideas
evidence: Face the speaker and maintain attention while someone else is talking
Wait until the other person has finished before responding
Respond to what was actually said rather than changing the subject to their own idea
topics.assessmentPrompt: When a friend is telling {{name}} about their weekend, does {{name}} actually listen and ask questions about it — rather than immediately jumping in to talk about their own weekend?
topics.descriptionZh: 当别人讲话时认真倾听——注视说话者，耐心等待对方讲完，并通过回应对方所说的内容来表明自己认真听了，而不是只顾着谈论自己的想法
evidenceZh: 面向说话者，在别人讲话时保持注意力集中
等对方完全讲完后再做出回应
针对对方实际所说的内容进行回应，而不是把话题转移到自己的想法上
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当朋友向{{name}}讲述他们的周末时，{{name}}是否真的在倾听并就相关内容提问——而不是立刻插嘴谈论自己的周末？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Makes someone a good friend
topics.description: Understand what makes someone a good friend — being kind, honest, reliable, and including others — and recognise behaviours that are not friendly, such as being bossy, leaving people out, or saying mean things
evidence: List at least four qualities of a good friend
Identify unfriendly behaviour in a story or real situation
Reflect on a time they were a good friend and explain what they did
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what makes a good friend and recognise when someone — including themselves — isn't being a good friend?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解是什么让一个人成为好朋友——善良、诚实、可靠和包容他人——并识别不友好的行为，如发号施令、孤立他人或说刻薄的话
evidenceZh: 列出至少四项好朋友的品质
在故事或真实情境中识别不友好的行为
反思自己曾经成为好朋友的一次经历，并说明自己是怎么做的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否描述好朋友的品质，并识别出何时有人（包括他们自己）没有表现出好朋友的特质？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Taking Turns and Sharing
topics.description: Take turns, share materials, and play cooperatively with others — understanding that group activities work better when everyone gets a fair go and that waiting for your turn is part of being a good friend
evidence: Take turns in a game or group activity without needing adult reminders
Share materials willingly during a shared task or playtime
Explain why taking turns makes games and group work more fun for everyone
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is playing a board game with friends or siblings, can they wait for their turn and share the pieces without grabbing or getting upset?
topics.descriptionZh: 轮流、分享材料，并与他人合作玩耍——理解当每个人都能获得公平机会时，集体活动会进行得更顺利，并且等待轮到自己也是做个好朋友的一部分。
evidenceZh: 在游戏或集体活动中能主动轮流，无需成年人提醒
在共同完成任务或玩耍时，乐意分享材料
能解释为什么轮流会让游戏和集体活动对每个人都更有趣
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}和朋友或兄弟姐妹玩桌面游戏时，他们能耐心等待轮到自己并分享游戏配件，而不是一味抢夺或发脾气吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Vocabulary: working with others
topics.description: Know and use the vocabulary of working with others — cooperate, share, take turns, team, listen, agree, disagree respectfully, and include — and understand that these words describe habits that friendships and group work depend on
evidence: Use 'cooperate' and 'compromise' correctly — e.g. 'We cooperated by taking turns choosing the game'
Explain what 'active listening' means and demonstrate it: facing the speaker, not interrupting, responding to what was said
Use 'share', 'take turns', and 'include' to describe how they work with others in a group activity
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is working on something with a friend or sibling, can they use words like 'cooperate' or 'take turns' to describe what they're doing — and actually practise those things?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解并使用与他人合作相关的词汇——合作（cooperate）、分享（share）、轮流（take turns）、团队（team）、倾听（listen）、同意（agree）、尊重地表达不同意见（disagree respectfully）以及包容（include）——并理解这些词汇描述了友谊和团队合作所依赖的行为习惯。
evidenceZh: 正确使用‘合作’（cooperate）和‘妥协/折中’（compromise）——例如：‘我们通过轮流挑选游戏来合作’
解释‘积极倾听’（active listening）的含义并做出示范：面向说话者，不打断对方，并对听到的内容做出回应
使用‘分享’（share）、‘轮流’（take turns）和‘包容’（include）来描述他们在小组活动中如何与他人协作
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}与朋友或兄弟姐妹一起做事时，他们能使用‘合作’或‘轮流’等词语来描述自己的做法，并实际践行这些行为吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Communication Vocabulary
topics.description: Know and use the vocabulary of healthy communication and conflict — assertive, passive, aggressive, compromise, conflict, resolution, mediate, bystander, upstander, and peer pressure — and understand the difference between these contrasting approaches
evidence: Use 'assertive' correctly and distinguish it from 'aggressive' — e.g. 'Being assertive means saying what I need calmly'
Explain what 'conflict resolution' means and describe one strategy such as using 'I feel...' statements
Use words like 'negotiate', 'boundary', and 'respect' accurately in a discussion about friendships
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} and a friend have a disagreement, can they describe it using words like 'conflict' or 'compromise' — and explain how assertive communication is different from aggressive or passive behaviour?
topics.descriptionZh: 掌握并使用健康沟通与冲突相关的词汇——自信（assertive）、被动（passive）、攻击性（aggressive）、妥协（compromise）、冲突（conflict）、解决（resolution）、调解（mediate）、旁观者（bystander）、挺身而出者（upstander）和同辈压力（peer pressure）——并理解这些不同应对方式之间的区别
evidenceZh: 正确使用“自信表达”（assertive）并将其与“攻击性”（aggressive）区分开来——例如：“自信表达意味着平静地说出我的需求”
解释“冲突解决”（conflict resolution）的含义，并描述一种策略，例如使用“我感到……”（I feel...）的句式
在关于友谊的讨论中准确使用“协商”（negotiate）、“边界”（boundary）和“尊重”（respect）等词汇
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 和朋友产生了分歧，他们能否使用“冲突”（conflict）或“妥协”（compromise）等词汇来描述这一情况——并解释自信沟通（assertive communication）与攻击性或被动行为有何不同？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Friendships change over time
topics.description: Understand that friendships change over time — that it's normal for friends to drift apart or for new friendships to form — and develop strategies for making new friends and handling friendship changes without feeling like something is wrong with them
evidence: Explain that friendships changing is normal and doesn't mean something is wrong
Describe a strategy for making new friends, such as joining a club or inviting someone to play
Talk about a friendship that changed and how they handled it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s best friend starts spending more time with someone else, can they handle it without falling apart — understanding that friendships shift and they can make new friends too?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解友谊会随着时间的推移而发生变化——朋友间渐行渐远或结交新朋友都是正常现象——并掌握结交新朋友和应对友谊变化的策略，从而不认为这代表自己有问题。
evidenceZh: 能够解释友谊发生变化是正常的，并不意味着自己有问题
描述结交新朋友的策略，例如加入社团或邀请他人一起玩耍
谈论一段发生变化的友谊以及他们是如何应对的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 的好朋友开始花更多时间和别人在一起，他们能否在不崩溃的情况下妥善处理——理解友谊会发生转变，并且自己也可以结交新朋友？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Resolving Disagreements with Friends
topics.description: Resolve simple disagreements with peers by talking it through — explaining how they feel, listening to the other person's side, and finding a compromise or solution that both can accept
evidence: Explain their own point of view calmly during a disagreement
Listen to the other person's perspective without interrupting
Suggest a compromise or solution that addresses both sides
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} and a friend disagree about which game to play at break time, can they talk it through and find a compromise — rather than one person always getting their way or the argument escalating?
topics.descriptionZh: 通过沟通解决与同伴之间的简单分歧——表达自己的感受，倾听对方的想法，并找到双方都能接受的妥协或解决方案。
evidenceZh: 在分歧中平静地表达自己的观点
不打断对方，倾听他人的观点
提出能兼顾双方的妥协或解决方案
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 和朋友在课间休息时玩什么游戏上产生了分歧，他们能否通过沟通找到妥协方案——而不是一方总是如愿以偿或导致争吵升级？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Roles in a Group
topics.description: Understand different roles people play in groups — leader, supporter, mediator, idea-generator — and recognise that effective groups need a mix of roles, not everyone trying to be the leader
evidence: Name at least three different roles people can play in a group
Identify their own preferred role and describe its strengths
Explain why groups work better when different people take different roles
topics.assessmentPrompt: In a group project, can {{name}} recognise that they don't always have to be in charge — and that sometimes the group works better when they support someone else's idea rather than pushing their own?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解人们在团队中扮演的不同角色——领导者（leader）、支持者（supporter）、调解者（mediator）、创意生成者（idea-generator）——并认识到高效的团队需要不同角色的组合，而不是每个人都争当领导者。
evidenceZh: 说出人们在团队中至少能扮演的三种不同角色
找出自己偏好的角色并描述其优势
解释为什么不同的人承担不同的角色会让团队运转得更好
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在小组项目中，{{name}} 能否认识到自己不必总是掌控全局——并且有时支持他人的想法而不是强推自己的想法，会让团队运作得更好？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Working Well in a Group
topics.description: Work effectively as part of a small group — contributing their own ideas, listening to others' ideas, taking on a fair share of the work, and supporting the group to reach a shared goal
evidence: Contribute at least one idea during a group discussion
Listen to and build on another group member's idea
Complete their assigned part of a group task on time
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} has to do a group project at school, do they pull their weight — sharing ideas and doing their part — rather than sitting back or trying to take over?
topics.descriptionZh: 作为小组成员进行高效协作——主动贡献自己的想法，认真倾听他人的意见，承担自己应尽的工作份额，并协助团队达成共同目标。
evidenceZh: 在小组讨论中至少提出一个想法
倾听并补充其他小组成员的想法
按时完成分配给自己的小组任务
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 在学校需要做小组项目时，他们是否能尽自己的一份力——分享想法并完成自己的任务——而不是袖手旁观或试图包揽一切？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Assertive Communication
topics.description: Use assertive communication — expressing needs, opinions, and boundaries clearly and respectfully without being aggressive (pushy/demanding) or passive (giving in/staying silent) — including saying no when something doesn't feel right
evidence: Explain the difference between assertive, aggressive, and passive responses
Role-play saying no in a peer pressure scenario
Express a personal boundary clearly and respectfully in a real situation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If friends want {{name}} to do something they're uncomfortable with — like excluding another child or breaking a rule — can {{name}} say 'I don't want to do that' firmly but politely?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用自信沟通（Assertive communication）——清晰且尊重地表达需求、观点和边界，既不咄咄逼人（aggressive，强迫/苛求），也不消极退缩（passive，妥协/沉默），包括在感觉不对劲时勇敢地说“不”。
evidenceZh: 解释自信（assertive）、咄咄逼人（aggressive）和消极被动（passive）这三种回应方式的区别
在同伴压力（peer pressure）场景下进行说“不”的角色扮演
在真实情境中清晰且尊重地表达个人边界（personal boundary）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果朋友们想让 {{name}} 做一件让他们感到不舒服的事——比如排挤另一个孩子或违反规则——{{name}} 能否坚定而有礼貌地说“我不想那样做”？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Giving and Receiving Feedback
topics.description: Give and receive constructive feedback — telling someone what they did well and what could be improved in a way that is helpful rather than hurtful, and receiving feedback about their own work without becoming defensive
evidence: Give feedback that includes both a specific positive point and a constructive suggestion
Receive feedback about their own work without getting upset or dismissive
Explain why constructive feedback helps people improve
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reviews a classmate's story and finds mistakes, can they give feedback that's helpful — like 'I loved this part, and this bit could be clearer' — rather than just saying 'it's wrong'?
topics.descriptionZh: 给予和接受建设性反馈（constructive feedback）——告诉别人他们做得好的地方以及可以改进的地方，方式要具有帮助性而非伤害性，并且在接受关于自己作品的反馈时不产生防御心理
evidenceZh: 提供包含具体优点和建设性建议的反馈
接受关于自己作品的反馈时不产生抵触情绪或轻视态度
解释为什么建设性反馈（constructive feedback）能帮助人们进步
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 审阅同学的故事并发现了错误，他们能否给出有帮助的反馈——比如“我很喜欢这部分，而这一点可以写得更清楚些”——而不是仅仅说“这写错了”？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Helping Others Resolve Conflicts
topics.description: Mediate conflicts between others — helping two friends who are arguing by listening to both sides, helping them see each other's perspective, and guiding them toward a fair resolution
evidence: Listen to both sides of a conflict without taking sides initially
Help each person articulate their perspective to the other
Suggest a fair resolution or compromise that both parties can accept
topics.assessmentPrompt: If two of {{name}}'s friends are arguing and both come to {{name}} for support, can {{name}} help them talk it out fairly rather than just taking one side?
topics.descriptionZh: 调解他人之间的冲突——当两个朋友争吵时，通过倾听双方的意见，帮助他们理解彼此的立场，并引导他们达成公平的解决方案来提供帮助。
evidenceZh: 倾听冲突双方的意见，初期不偏袒任何一方
帮助双方各自向对方表达清楚自己的立场
提出双方都能接受的公平解决方案或折中办法
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 的两个朋友在争吵，并且都来找 {{name}} 寻求支持，{{name}} 能否帮助他们公平地沟通解决问题，而不是单纯地偏袒其中一方？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Self-Reflection in Relationships
topics.description: Reflect on their own role and behaviour in relationships — recognising patterns in how they interact with others, understanding what they contribute to friendships, and identifying areas where they could improve as a friend or team member
evidence: Identify a pattern in their own social behaviour, such as always wanting to lead or avoiding confrontation
Describe what they do well in relationships and one area they'd like to improve
Set a specific social goal, such as 'I will ask others for their ideas before sharing mine'
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} honestly reflect on their friendships and say something like 'I think I sometimes take over in group work and I'm trying to listen more' — showing awareness of their own social patterns?
topics.nameZh: 人际关系中的自我反思
topics.descriptionZh: 反思自己在人际关系中的角色和行为——认识自己与他人互动的模式，理解自己对友谊的贡献，并找出自己作为朋友或团队成员可以改进的地方。
evidenceZh: 识别自己社交行为中的一种模式，例如总是想占主导地位或回避冲突
描述自己在人际关系中做得好的地方以及一个想要改进的方面
设定一个具体的社交目标，例如“在分享自己的想法之前，我会先询问别人的意见”
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否诚实地反思自己的友谊，并说出类似“我觉得我在小组合作中有时过于强势，我正在努力多倾听”这样的话——从而展现出对自己社交模式的认知？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Social Cues and Group Dynamics
topics.description: Understand subtext, indirect communication, and social cues in adolescent peer groups; analyse the psychology of in-group and out-group dynamics and why belonging can come at the cost of exclusion; understand gossip as a social bonding and status mechanism, and its costs; develop strategies for navigating social hierarchies without compromising values; distinguish between assertiveness and aggression in peer settings; understand how to respond to exclusion — whether experiencing it or witnessing it
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} senses tension or unspoken 'undercurrents' in a group of friends, can they describe what social cues they pick up on and explain the difference between being assertive and being aggressive when they choose to address it?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解青少年同伴群体中的言外之意、间接沟通和社交线索 (social cues)；分析内群体和外群体动态 (in-group and out-group dynamics) 的心理学原理，以及为什么归属感可能会以排斥他人为代价；理解八卦 (gossip) 作为一种社交纽带和地位机制的作用及其代价；制定在不妥协个人价值观的情况下应对社交等级 (social hierarchies) 的策略；区分同伴环境中的自信果断 (assertiveness) 与攻击性 (aggression)；理解如何应对排斥——无论是自己遭受排斥还是目睹他人被排斥。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 察觉到朋友群体中的紧张气氛或未言明的“暗流”时，他们能否描述自己捕捉到了哪些社交线索，并解释在尝试解决这些问题时，自信果断 (assertiveness) 和攻击性 (aggression) 之间的区别？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Honest Conversations and Conflict Repair
topics.description: Understand how to have honest, direct conversations that address problems without attacking the person; apply the principles of non-violent communication (observation, feeling, need, request); understand the repair process after significant conflicts: taking responsibility without defensiveness, offering a genuine apology (without blame-shifting), and rebuilding trust through consistent behaviour over time; distinguish between a real apology and a face-saving 'sorry'; understand how friendships survive and deepen through navigated conflict rather than avoidance
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} falls out seriously with a friend, can they describe what makes an apology actually repair a relationship — and what the difference is between a genuine apology and just saying sorry to end the awkwardness?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解如何进行诚实、直接的对话以解决问题而不攻击个人；应用非暴力沟通（non-violent communication）的原则（观察、感受、需要、请求）；理解重大冲突后的修复过程：不带防御地承担责任，提供真诚的道歉（不推卸责任），并通过长期一致的行为重建信任；区分真正的道歉和为了保全面子而说的“对不起”；理解友谊是如何通过妥善应对冲突而非逃避来维系和加深的。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 与朋友发生严重争吵时，他们能否描述出是什么让道歉真正修复了关系——以及真诚的道歉与仅仅为了结束尴尬而说“对不起”之间有什么区别？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
