topics.name: Leadership Styles and Influence
topics.description: Distinguish different leadership styles (directive, democratic, servant, transformational) and understand when each is appropriate; understand that influence in a group comes with responsibility, and explore the difference between leading through inspiration versus coercion; practise inclusive leadership: actively creating space for quieter voices and diverse perspectives; understand the ethics of influence and the boundary between persuasion and manipulation; explore concepts of consent and coercion in peer relationships; reflect on what kind of influence they want to have in their communities
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were leading a group project where one person was dominating all the decisions, can they describe two different leadership approaches they could take and explain why the most authoritative person in a group isn't always the best leader?
topics.descriptionZh: 区分不同的领导风格（指令型、民主型、服务型、变革型），并理解每种风格适用的场景；理解在团队中拥有影响力意味着承担责任，并探索通过启发与通过强迫进行领导之间的区别；实践包容性领导：积极为安静的声音和多元的观点创造表达空间；理解影响力的道德规范以及说服与操纵之间的界限；探索同伴关系中的同意与强迫概念；反思他们希望在社区中产生怎样的影响力。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 正在负责一个小组项目，而其中一个人包揽了所有的决定，他们能否描述出两种可以采取的不同领导方法，并解释为什么团队中最具权威的人并不总是最好的领导者？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Actions and Their Consequences
topics.description: Understand that actions have consequences — that what you choose to do affects both yourself and other people — and begin to think about what might happen before they act
evidence: Describe what happened as a consequence of a specific action they took
Predict what might happen if they choose a particular action before doing it
Explain that actions can have good or bad consequences for themselves and others
topics.assessmentPrompt: Before {{name}} does something — like taking a toy from a sibling or running in the corridor — can they stop and think about what might happen as a result?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解行为会产生后果——即自己的选择会影响自己和他人——并开始在行动前思考可能发生的事情。
evidenceZh: 描述自己采取的特定行为所带来的后果
预测在行动前选择特定行为可能会引发的结果
解释行为对自己和他人可能产生好的或坏的后果
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在 {{name}} 做某事之前——比如从兄弟姐妹那里拿玩具或在走廊里奔跑——他们能停下来思考一下这样做可能会导致什么结果吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Everyday Safety Awareness
topics.description: Keep themselves safe in everyday situations — knowing basic safety rules about roads, strangers, water, and the internet — and understanding who their trusted adults are and when to tell them something
evidence: State at least three basic safety rules and explain why each matters
Name their trusted adults and describe when they should tell them something
Demonstrate safe behaviour in a familiar everyday situation without being reminded
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know their basic safety rules — like not going off with someone they don't know, looking both ways before crossing, and telling you if something online makes them uncomfortable?
topics.descriptionZh: 在日常生活中保护自己——了解关于道路、陌生人、水域和网络的基本安全规则——并明白谁是值得信赖的成年人，以及在何时应该向他们报告情况
evidenceZh: 至少说出三条基本安全规则，并解释每条规则为何重要
说出值得信赖的成年人的名字，并描述在什么情况下应该告诉他们
在熟悉的日常情境中，无需提醒即可表现出安全的行为
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否了解基本的安全规则——例如不跟不认识的人走、过马路前左右观察，以及在网络上遇到令人不适的内容时告诉您？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Right and Wrong Choices
topics.description: Know the difference between right and wrong in familiar everyday situations — understanding basic rules about honesty, not hurting others, respecting others' property, and being fair — and choose to do the right thing even when it's harder
evidence: Identify the right and wrong choice in a simple moral scenario
Choose to be honest even when lying would avoid trouble
Explain why rules about not hurting others and being honest matter
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} accidentally breaks something at a friend's house, do they tell the truth about it rather than hiding it or blaming someone else?
topics.descriptionZh: 在熟悉的日常情境中明辨是非——理解关于诚实、不伤害他人、尊重他人财产和公平公正的基本规则——并在遇到困难时依然选择做正确的事
evidenceZh: 在简单的道德场景中识别正确与错误的选择
即使撒谎能避免麻烦，也选择保持诚实
解释为什么关于不伤害他人和诚实的规则很重要
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在朋友家不小心弄坏了东西，他们会如实相告，而不是隐瞒或责怪别人吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Rules and agreements exist
topics.description: Understand why rules and agreements exist — that they help keep people safe, make things fair, and help groups work well together — and follow agreed rules willingly rather than only when being watched
evidence: Explain the reason behind at least two rules at home or school
Follow a rule consistently without needing to be reminded or monitored
Describe what would happen if nobody followed the rules in a specific context
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} follow the class rules or family agreements even when no adult is watching — not because they're scared of punishment but because they understand why the rules matter?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解规则与约定为何存在——它们能保障人们的安全、维护公平，并帮助团队良好协作——并且自愿遵守已达成的规则，而非仅在有人监督时才遵守。
evidenceZh: 能解释家里或学校至少两条规则背后的原因
能在无需提醒或监督的情况下始终如一地遵守规则
能描述在特定情境下如果不遵守规则会发生什么
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}在没有成年人监督时，是否依然遵守班级规则或家庭约定——不是因为害怕惩罚，而是因为他们理解规则的重要性？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Vocabulary: making decisions and keeping safe
topics.description: Know and use the vocabulary of making decisions and keeping safe — choice, consequence, rule, safe, fair, honest, trusted adult, and right and wrong — and understand that naming these ideas clearly helps make better choices
evidence: Explain what 'consequence' means and give an example of a positive and a negative consequence of a choice
Use 'responsible' and 'safe' correctly when talking about everyday decisions — e.g. 'The responsible choice is to tell an adult'
Define 'rule' and 'fairness' and explain why rules exist using their own examples from school or home
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} faces a situation where they need to make a choice — like whether to tell the truth about something that went wrong — can they talk through what might happen using words like 'consequence' and 'fair'?
topics.nameZh: 词汇：做决定与保持安全
topics.descriptionZh: 掌握并运用关于做决定和保持安全的词汇——选择 (choice)、后果 (consequence)、规则 (rule)、安全 (safe)、公平 (fair)、诚实 (honest)、可信赖的成年人 (trusted adult) 以及是非对错 (right and wrong)——并理解清晰地表达这些概念有助于做出更好的选择。
evidenceZh: 解释“后果 (consequence)”的含义，并举出一个选择带来的积极后果和消极后果的例子。
在谈论日常决定时正确使用“负责任的 (responsible)”和“安全的 (safe)”——例如：“负责任的选择是告诉成年人”。
定义“规则 (rule)”和“公平 (fairness)”，并用自己来自学校或家庭的例子解释为什么需要制定规则。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 面临需要做出选择的情况——比如是否要对做错的事情说出真相——他们能否使用“后果 (consequence)”和“公平 (fair)”等词语来探讨可能会发生的事情？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Basic digital citizenship
topics.description: Understand basic digital citizenship — being kind online, protecting personal information, recognising that people behind screens are real people with real feelings, and knowing what to do if something online makes them uncomfortable
evidence: State at least three rules for staying safe and being kind online
Explain why hurtful messages online are just as harmful as saying them in person
Describe what they should do if someone online makes them feel uncomfortable or asks for personal information
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is chatting with friends online or playing multiplayer games, do they treat people kindly and know not to share personal details like their address or school name?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解基础数字公民素养——在网上友善待人，保护个人信息，认识到屏幕背后是拥有真实情感的真人，并知道如果在网上遇到让人不舒服的情况该怎么做
evidenceZh: 说出至少三条在网上保持安全和友善待人的规则
解释为什么网上的伤人信息和当面说出来的伤害一样大
描述如果在网上有人让他们感到不舒服或索要个人信息时，他们应该怎么做
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}在网上和朋友聊天或玩多人游戏时，他们是否能友善待人，并且知道不要分享家庭住址或学校名称等个人详细信息？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Bystanders and Upstanders
topics.description: Understand the bystander role — that when someone witnesses unkind or unfair behaviour, they have a choice: they can be a passive bystander (doing nothing), join in, or be an upstander (speaking up or getting help) — and develop the confidence to be an upstander
evidence: Explain the difference between a bystander and an upstander
Describe at least two safe actions an upstander can take
Give an example of a time they or someone they know stood up for someone else
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a group of children being mean to someone at school, do they have the courage to say something, walk away with the person being targeted, or tell a teacher — rather than just watching?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解旁观者的角色——当目睹不友善或不公平的行为时，人们面临选择：可以做消极的旁观者（无所作为）、参与其中，或者做挺身而出的人（勇敢发声或寻求帮助）——并培养成为挺身而出者的勇气
evidenceZh: 解释旁观者与挺身而出者之间的区别
描述挺身而出者可以采取的至少两种安全行动
举例说明他们自己或认识的人曾为他人挺身而出的经历
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在学校看到一群孩子对某人不友善，他们是否有勇气发声、和被针对的人一起走开，或者告诉老师——而不是仅仅在一旁旁观？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Stop, Think, Then Choose
topics.description: Use a simple decision-making process when faced with a choice — stopping to think, identifying the options, considering the consequences of each option, and then choosing — rather than acting impulsively
evidence: Describe at least two options when facing a decision
Predict a likely consequence for each option
Explain which option they chose and why, showing they considered the consequences
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} faces a tricky choice — like whether to tell the teacher that a friend cheated — can they think through their options and the consequences rather than just reacting?
topics.descriptionZh: 面临选择时，使用简单的决策过程——停下来思考、明确各种选项、考虑每个选项的后果，然后再做出选择——而不是冲动行事
evidenceZh: 面临决定时，至少描述两个选项
预测每个选项可能导致的后果
说明自己选择了哪个选项及原因，以表明其考虑了后果
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 面临棘手的选择时——比如是否要向老师报告朋友作弊——他们能否深思熟虑地权衡各种选项及后果，而不是仅仅做出冲动反应？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Understanding Bullying
topics.description: Understand what bullying is — repeated behaviour intended to hurt someone, including physical, verbal, social (exclusion, spreading rumours), and cyberbullying — and know that it is always wrong and what to do if they experience or witness it
evidence: Define bullying and distinguish it from a one-off conflict
Name at least three forms of bullying including cyberbullying
Describe the steps they should take if they experience or witness bullying
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} understand the difference between a one-off argument and bullying, and do they know what to do if they see someone being bullied — rather than just ignoring it?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解什么是欺凌——即旨在伤害他人的重复性行为，包括身体欺凌、言语欺凌、社交欺凌（孤立、散布谣言）和网络欺凌——并明白这种行为永远是错误的，以及在亲身经历或目睹欺凌时应该怎么做。
evidenceZh: 定义欺凌，并将其与单次冲突区分开来
列举至少三种欺凌形式，包括网络欺凌
描述在亲身经历或目睹欺凌时应采取的步骤
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否理解单次争吵与欺凌之间的区别，并且在看到他人受到欺凌时是否知道该怎么做——而不是仅仅置之不理？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Vocabulary: ethics and citizenship
topics.description: Know and use the vocabulary of ethics and citizenship — bullying, cyberbullying, bystander, upstander, peer pressure, digital citizenship, rights, responsibility, and ethical — and understand the distinctions between these closely related terms
evidence: Explain what 'ethics' means in their own words and give an example of an ethical dilemma
Use 'citizen', 'rights', and 'responsibilities' correctly — e.g. 'A citizen has the right to vote and the responsibility to follow laws'
Define 'consent' and 'integrity' and explain why they matter in relationships and online behaviour
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw someone being treated unkindly online and you asked them about it, could they explain the difference between being a bystander and an upstander — and what 'digital citizenship' means?
topics.descriptionZh: 掌握并使用道德与公民素养（ethics and citizenship）相关的词汇——欺凌（bullying）、网络欺凌（cyberbullying）、旁观者（bystander）、挺身而出者（upstander）、同辈压力（peer pressure）、数字公民（digital citizenship）、权利（rights）、责任（responsibility）以及符合道德的（ethical）——并理解这些密切相关词汇之间的区别。
evidenceZh: 用自己的话解释‘道德（ethics）’的含义，并举出一个道德困境（ethical dilemma）的例子。
正确使用‘公民（citizen）’、‘权利（rights）’和‘责任（responsibilities）’——例如：‘公民有投票的权利，也有遵守法律的责任’。
定义‘同意（consent）’和‘正直（integrity）’，并解释它们在人际交往和网络行为中为何重要。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}在网上看到有人受到不友善的对待，而你问起这件事，他们能否解释‘旁观者（bystander）’和‘挺身而出者（upstander）’的区别，以及‘数字公民（digital citizenship）’的含义？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Community Rights and Responsibilities
topics.description: Understand their rights and responsibilities as a member of a community — that everyone has a right to be treated with respect and to feel safe, and that with rights come responsibilities to treat others the same way
evidence: Name at least three rights that every child has (e.g., safety, education, respect)
Describe the responsibilities that go along with those rights
Give an example of how exercising their own rights responsibly supports the community
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that they have a right to feel safe at school AND a responsibility to help make school safe for others — understanding that rights and responsibilities go together?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解作为社区成员的权利与责任——每个人都有受到尊重和享有安全的权利，同时享有权利也意味着必须承担以同样方式对待他人的责任。
evidenceZh: 列举每个儿童至少拥有的三项权利（例如：人身安全、接受教育、受到尊重）
描述与这些权利相对应的责任
举例说明负责任地行使自己的权利是如何帮助和支持社区的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释他们在学校享有感到安全的权利，并且有责任帮助他人确保学校的安全——从而理解权利与责任是密不可分的？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Difficult Ethical Choices
topics.description: Understand that ethical decisions are not always black and white — that sometimes there is no perfect answer and reasonable people can disagree — and practise weighing up competing values when making difficult choices
evidence: Describe a moral dilemma where both sides have valid points
Explain the values in tension (e.g., loyalty vs safety, honesty vs kindness)
Describe how they would make a decision in such a situation and justify their reasoning
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s friend tells them a secret but the secret involves something dangerous, can {{name}} think through the tension between loyalty to their friend and the need to keep someone safe?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解道德（伦理）决策并不总是非黑即白的——有时并没有完美的答案，理智的人也会有不同的意见——并在做出艰难选择时练习权衡相互冲突的价值观。
evidenceZh: 描述一个双方都有合理立场的道德（伦理）困境
解释产生冲突的价值观（例如：忠诚与安全、诚实与善良之间的冲突）
描述在这种情况下的决策过程，并证明其推理的合理性
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}的朋友告诉其一个秘密，但这个秘密涉及危险的事情，{{name}}能否理清对朋友的忠诚与保护他人安全的需求之间的冲突？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Ethics in Real-World Issues
topics.description: Evaluate the ethical dimensions of real-world issues they encounter — such as environmental responsibility, fairness in sport, digital ethics, or social justice — considering multiple perspectives and forming a reasoned personal position
evidence: Identify an ethical issue and describe at least two different perspectives on it
Explain which perspective they agree with most and give reasons for their position
Acknowledge that the other perspective has some validity even if they disagree
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} discuss a real issue — like whether it's fair that some children have more than others, or whether animals should be kept in zoos — considering different viewpoints and explaining their own position thoughtfully?
topics.descriptionZh: 评估他们遇到的现实问题的伦理维度——如环境责任、体育公平、数字伦理（digital ethics）或社会正义（social justice）——考虑多方视角并形成有理有据的个人立场。
evidenceZh: 识别一个伦理问题并描述至少两种不同的观点
解释他们最赞同哪种观点，并给出支持其立场的理由
承认即使他们不同意，另一种观点也具有一定的合理性
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否讨论一个现实问题——例如某些孩子拥有的东西比别人多是否公平，或者动物是否应该被关在动物园里——在考虑不同观点的同时，深思熟虑地解释自己的立场？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Peer Pressure and Resisting It
topics.description: Understand peer pressure — the influence friends and peers can have on your choices and behaviour — and develop strategies for resisting pressure to do something they know is wrong or that makes them uncomfortable
evidence: Define peer pressure in their own words and give a real-world example
Describe at least two strategies for resisting peer pressure, such as walking away or using humour
Explain why going along with something wrong to fit in usually makes things worse
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s friends dare them to do something risky or unkind — like shoplifting a sweet or posting an embarrassing photo of someone — can they resist the pressure and explain why they won't do it?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解同伴压力（Peer Pressure）——即朋友和同龄人对你选择和行为的影响——并制定策略来抵制去做那些明知是错误或让你感到不适的事情的压力。
evidenceZh: 用自己的话定义同伴压力，并举一个现实生活中的例子
描述至少两种抵制同伴压力的策略，例如走开或使用幽默
解释为什么为了融入群体而盲从错误的事情通常会使情况变得更糟
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}的朋友怂恿他们去做一些有风险或不友善的事情——比如偷拿一颗糖果或发布某人的尴尬照片——他们能抵制这种压力并解释为什么自己不会这么做吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Risk, Uncertainty, and Cognitive Bias
topics.description: Distinguish between risk (decisions with known probabilities) and uncertainty (decisions with unknown outcomes); identify cognitive biases that distort risk assessment: availability heuristic (judging likelihood by how easily examples come to mind), present bias (overvaluing the immediate over the future), optimism bias (underestimating personal risk), and groupthink; understand why adolescent brains are biologically calibrated toward higher risk tolerance; apply a structured decision-making framework to real choices; understand the role of personal values in decisions where facts alone cannot determine the answer
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why taking a risk isn't always irrational — and describe one cognitive bias that causes people to misjudge risk in their everyday decisions, such as why teenagers tend to underestimate certain dangers?
topics.nameZh: 风险、不确定性与认知偏差 (Risk, Uncertainty, and Cognitive Bias)
topics.descriptionZh: 区分风险（已知概率的决策）与不确定性（结果未知的决策）；识别会扭曲风险评估的认知偏差：可得性启发式 (availability heuristic，根据想起例子的容易程度来判断可能性)、现时偏差 (present bias，过度看重眼前而忽视未来)、乐观偏差 (optimism bias，低估个人风险) 以及群体思维 (groupthink)；理解为什么青少年的大脑在生物学上被设定为具有更高的风险承受力；将结构化的决策框架应用于实际选择；理解在仅凭事实无法得出结论的决策中，个人价值观所扮演的角色。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么承担风险并不总是非理性的——并描述一种导致人们在日常生活中误判风险的认知偏差，例如为什么青少年往往会低估某些危险？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Online Identity and Misinformation
topics.description: Understand the ethics of online identity and the importance of consistency between who you are online and offline; explain how recommendation algorithms and filter bubbles narrow information exposure; evaluate the psychology of misinformation: why it spreads, why smart people believe it, and how to apply source evaluation (lateral reading, checking evidence, recognising emotional manipulation); understand digital consent around sharing images or personal information; explore the ethics of AI, surveillance, and data privacy as they affect everyday life; reflect on responsible content creation and online influence
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} sees a convincing claim shared on social media, can they describe their process for deciding whether to believe or share it — and explain why even intelligent people are regularly misled online?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解网络身份的道德规范以及线上线下形象一致性的重要性；解释推荐算法（recommendation algorithms）和过滤气泡（filter bubbles）如何限制信息获取；分析虚假信息的心理机制：为何传播、为何聪明人也会轻信，以及如何应用来源评估（如横向阅读 lateral reading、核查证据、识别情感操纵）；理解分享图像或个人信息时的数字同意（digital consent）；探讨人工智能（AI）、监控和数据隐私的伦理及其对日常生活的影响；反思负责任的内容创作与网络影响力。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 在社交媒体上看到令人信服的说法时，他们能否描述自己决定相信或分享该信息的判断过程——并解释为什么即使是聪明人也经常在网上被误导？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Ethical Frameworks and Moral Reasoning
topics.description: Introduce the three main ethical frameworks: consequentialism (judge actions by outcomes and overall welfare), deontology (judge actions by adherence to rules and duties regardless of consequences), and virtue ethics (judge actions by the character they reflect); apply each framework to real-world moral dilemmas: climate responsibility, AI ethics, civil disobedience, wealth inequality, healthcare rationing; understand the strengths and limitations of each framework; develop the capacity for careful moral reasoning — the ability to think through ethical questions systematically rather than relying only on intuition or group opinion
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} take a real ethical dilemma — like whether it's ever right to break a rule to help someone — and explain how a consequentialist, a deontologist, and someone focused on virtue ethics would each think about it differently, and which approach they find most persuasive?
topics.descriptionZh: 介绍三大主要伦理框架：结果主义（consequentialism，根据行为的结果和整体福祉来评判行为）、义务论（deontology，无论后果如何，根据对规则和责任的遵守来评判行为）以及美德伦理学（virtue ethics，根据行为所反映的品格来评判行为）；将每种框架应用于现实世界的道德困境：气候责任、人工智能伦理、公民不服从、财富不平等、医疗资源分配；理解每种框架的优势和局限性；培养审慎的道德推理能力——即系统思考伦理问题的能力，而不是仅仅依靠直觉或群体意见。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否选取一个真实的伦理困境——比如为了帮助别人而打破规则是否正确——并解释结果主义者（consequentialist）、义务论者（deontologist）和美德伦理学倡导者会如何从不同角度思考这个问题，以及{{name}}自己认为哪种方法最有说服力？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Naming Your Feelings
topics.description: Notice what you are feeling and put a name to it — being able to label an emotion is the first step to understanding and managing it
evidence: emotional literacy research
Fostering Emotional Literacy in Young Children (HeadStart.gov)
emotion vocabulary development 4-11 years (PMC)
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} seems upset, excited, or frustrated, can they stop and tell you what emotion they're feeling — even if they can't fully explain why?
topics.descriptionZh: 留意自己的感受并为之命名——能够准确标记（label）情绪，是理解和调节情绪的第一步。
evidenceZh: 情绪素养（emotional literacy）研究
《培养幼儿的情绪素养》（HeadStart.gov）
4-11岁情绪词汇发展（PMC）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 显得难过、兴奋或沮丧时，他们能停下来告诉你自己正感受到什么情绪吗——即使他们无法完全解释原因？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Vocabulary: self
topics.description: Know and use the vocabulary of self-reflection — self-awareness, reflect, pattern, trigger, assumption, impact, perspective, and notice — and understand that having precise words for these inner experiences makes them easier to understand and talk about
evidence: Use words like 'reflect', 'pattern', and 'trigger' accurately when describing their own behaviour — e.g. 'I notice a pattern: I get frustrated when I rush'
Explain what 'self-awareness' means in their own words and give a personal example
Use the word 'perspective' correctly — e.g. 'From my perspective it felt unfair, but I can see theirs too'
topics.assessmentPrompt: After a difficult moment — a falling-out with a friend or a frustrating task — can {{name}} talk about what happened using words like 'trigger' or 'reflect', showing they're thinking about their own reactions rather than just what the other person did?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解并使用自我反思（self-reflection）的词汇——自我意识（self-awareness）、反思（reflect）、模式（pattern）、触发因素（trigger）、假设（assumption）、影响（impact）、视角（perspective）和察觉（notice）——并理解拥有精确的词汇来表达这些内心体验，能使其更容易被理解和探讨。
evidenceZh: 在描述自己的行为时，能准确使用“反思（reflect）”、“模式（pattern）”和“触发因素（trigger）”等词汇——例如：“我察觉到一个模式：当我匆忙时就会感到沮丧。”
能用自己的话解释“自我意识（self-awareness）”的含义，并举出一个个人生活中的例子。
能正确使用“视角（perspective）”一词——例如：“从我的视角来看，这件事显得不公平，但我也能理解他们的视角。”
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在经历了一段艰难的时刻——比如与朋友发生争执或遇到令人受挫的任务之后，{{name}} 能否使用“触发因素（trigger）”或“反思（reflect）”等词汇来谈论发生的事情，展现出他们正在思考自己的反应，而不仅仅关注对方做了什么？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Feelings Versus Actions
topics.description: Understand that feelings and actions are separate — you can feel something strongly without having to act on it straight away
evidence: emotion regulation development research
Effects of Age and Gender in Emotion Regulation (PMC 2020)
expressive control to emotion regulation (PMC)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} understand that feeling angry, scared, or jealous doesn't mean they have to act on it immediately — that there's a gap between the feeling and what they choose to do next?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解情绪和行动是相互独立的——即使感受非常强烈，也不必立刻付诸行动。
evidenceZh: 情绪调节发展研究 (emotion regulation development research)
年龄与性别对情绪调节的影响 (Effects of Age and Gender in Emotion Regulation, PMC 2020)
表达控制与情绪调节 (expressive control to emotion regulation, PMC)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否明白，感到生气、害怕或嫉妒并不意味着必须立刻采取行动——在情绪感受和后续选择的行为之间存在着一段缓冲空间？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Patterns in Your Own Reactions
topics.description: Notice patterns in your own reactions — 'I tend to respond like this when I'm tired, left out, or put on the spot'
evidence: middle childhood self-reliance in emotion regulation
7-year developmental shift in self-understanding research
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} ever noticed a pattern in how they react — for example, that they get more upset at certain times of day, or that a particular type of situation reliably triggers a strong feeling?
topics.descriptionZh: 留意自身反应的模式——‘当我感到疲惫、被冷落或被突然点名时，我往往会做出这样的反应’
evidenceZh: 童年中期情绪调节的自主性 (self-reliance in emotion regulation)
7岁自我理解的发展转变研究 (developmental shift in self-understanding)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否曾注意到自己反应的模式——例如，在一天中的某些特定时间更容易感到烦躁，或者某种特定类型的情境总能引发强烈的情绪？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Your Impact on Others
topics.description: Reflect on how your behaviour lands on others — consider not just what you intended but what the actual impact was on the other person
evidence: Describe how something they said or did affected someone else — e.g. 'When I didn't include them, they looked upset'
Predict what might happen before acting — e.g. 'If I take the last one without asking, they'll feel it's unfair'
After a conflict, explain what they could have done differently and what effect that would have had
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} think about how something they said or did might have felt to the other person — not just what they meant by it, but what the impact actually was?
topics.descriptionZh: 反思你的行为对他人产生的影响——不仅要考虑你的初衷，还要考虑对他人造成的实际影响。
evidenceZh: 描述自己说的话或做的事如何影响了他人——例如：‘当我不带他们一起玩时，他们看起来很不高兴。’
在行动前预测可能发生的情况——例如：‘如果我不问一声就拿走最后一个，他们会觉得这不公平。’
在发生冲突后，解释自己本可以怎么做以及那样做会产生什么效果。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否思考自己说的话或做的事可能会让对方产生怎样的感受——不仅考虑自己的本意，还要考虑实际产生的影响？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Questioning First Impressions
topics.description: Notice when your first reading of a social situation might be wrong — your assumptions about why someone acted a certain way are not always facts
evidence: Pause before reacting to a classmate's behaviour and consider an alternative explanation — e.g. 'Maybe they bumped me by accident, not on purpose'
Describe a time they assumed the worst about someone's intention and later found out they were wrong
When told about an ambiguous social situation, suggest at least two possible reasons for the other person's behaviour instead of jumping to one conclusion
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} felt sure someone was being unfair or unkind, could they pause and consider whether there might be another explanation for what happened?
topics.descriptionZh: 留意自己对社交情境的第一印象是否会有误——你对他人行为动机的假设并不总是事实
evidenceZh: 在对同学的行为做出反应前先停顿一下，考虑其他可能的解释——例如：‘也许他是不小心碰到我的，而不是故意的’
描述一次你对他人的意图做最坏假设，但后来发现自己完全想错了的经历
当听别人讲述一个模糊的社交情境时，为对方的行为提出至少两种可能的理由，而不是草率地得出一个结论
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}确信某人做事不公或态度恶劣，他们能否先冷静一下，想想这件事是否还有其他解释？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Personal Growth Over Time
topics.description: Reflect on your own growth over time — the things that challenge you now are not fixed, and noticing how you have already changed builds genuine self-knowledge
evidence: emotion vocabulary development continues to age 11 (PMC)
self-reflection importance in children research
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} look back over the past year or two and point to something they used to find really difficult that they now handle better — and explain what changed?
topics.descriptionZh: 反思自己随时间的成长——现在让你感到挑战的事物并非固定不变的，注意到自己已经发生的改变能建立真正的自我认知。
evidenceZh: 情绪词汇发展（emotion vocabulary development）持续至11岁（PMC）
儿童研究中自我反思（self-reflection）的重要性
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否回顾过去一两年，指出他们曾经觉得非常困难但现在能更好应对的事情——并解释发生了什么改变？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Coping with Life Changes
topics.description: Understand that change is a normal part of life — such as starting school, getting a new teacher, a new baby arriving, or moving house — and identify simple strategies that help them cope with changes
evidence: Name at least two changes they have experienced and how they felt
Identify a person they can talk to when a change feels hard
Describe one strategy that helps them cope with change, such as keeping a familiar routine
topics.assessmentPrompt: When something changes in {{name}}'s life — like getting a new teacher at school — can they talk about how it makes them feel and think of ways to help themselves adjust?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解变化是生活中正常的一部分——例如开始上学、换了一位新老师、家里迎来了新宝宝或者搬家——并能识别出帮助他们应对变化的简单策略。
evidenceZh: 说出至少两件他们经历过的变化以及他们的感受
找出当变化让人感到困难时，可以倾诉的人
描述一种帮助他们应对变化的策略，例如保持熟悉的日常作息
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 的生活中发生了一些变化——比如在学校换了新老师——他们能否谈论这让他们有什么感受，并想出帮助自己适应的方法？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Learning from Mistakes
topics.description: Understand that making mistakes is a normal part of learning and that everyone — including adults — makes mistakes, and begin to see mistakes as opportunities to learn rather than reasons to give up
evidence: Describe a time they made a mistake and what they learned from it
Respond to a mistake by trying again rather than giving up
Explain why mistakes help people learn
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets an answer wrong in class or messes up during a game, do they bounce back and keep trying rather than shutting down or saying 'I can't do it'?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解犯错是学习过程中的正常部分，并且每个人——包括成年人——都会犯错，并开始将错误视为学习的机会，而不是放弃的理由。
evidenceZh: 描述一次他们犯错的经历以及从中学到了什么
面对错误时选择重试而不是放弃
解释为什么错误能帮助人们学习
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在课堂上答错了问题或在游戏中犯了错，他们是否会重新振作并继续尝试，而不是退缩或说“我做不到”？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Patience and Delayed Gratification
topics.description: Wait for things they want without becoming very distressed — practising patience and delayed gratification in everyday situations like waiting their turn, waiting for a treat, or waiting for help
evidence: Wait for their turn in a game or activity without constant complaints
Describe what they do to help themselves wait, such as thinking about something else
Explain why sometimes we have to wait and that it is a skill they can practise
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has to wait their turn for something they really want — like a go on the iPad or being served dinner — can they wait without a big fuss?
topics.descriptionZh: 在等待想要的事物时不会变得非常焦躁——在日常情境中练习耐心和延迟满足（如等待轮流、等待奖励或等待帮助）
evidenceZh: 在游戏或活动中等待轮到自己时，不会不停地抱怨
能描述他们为了帮助自己等待所做的事情，例如想些其他事情
能解释为什么有时我们必须等待，并明白这是一项可以练习的技能
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}必须等待轮到自己来做他们非常想要的事情——比如玩一会儿iPad或等上晚餐——他们能在不大吵大闹的情况下耐心等待吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Simple Calming Strategies
topics.description: Use simple calming strategies when feeling upset or overwhelmed — such as taking deep breaths, counting to ten, or going to a quiet space — and understand that these help the body and mind settle down
evidence: Demonstrate at least two calming strategies when prompted
Choose to use a calming strategy independently during a real upset
Explain in simple terms why calming down helps them think better
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} gets really upset — say they lose a game or argue with a sibling — can they use a strategy like deep breaths to calm themselves down rather than staying in meltdown mode?
topics.descriptionZh: 在感到心烦或不知所措时，使用简单的冷静策略——例如深呼吸、数到十，或去一个安静的地方——并理解这些方法有助于让身心平静下来
evidenceZh: 在提示下展示至少两种冷静策略
在真正心烦意乱时，能独立选择使用冷静策略
能用简单的语言解释为什么冷静下来有助于更好地思考
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}感到非常心烦意乱时——比如输了游戏或和兄弟姐妹吵架——他们能否使用深呼吸等策略让自己平静下来，而不是继续处于情绪崩溃的状态？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Words for Big Feelings
topics.description: Know and use the key words for managing big feelings — calm, strategy, cope, settle, patience, overwhelmed, and breathe — and understand that having words for these ideas is the first step to using them
evidence: Use words like 'frustrated', 'anxious', 'overwhelmed', and 'disappointed' accurately to describe how they feel in difficult moments
Explain what 'calm down' strategies are in their own words and name at least two they have tried (e.g. deep breaths, counting, walking away)
Distinguish between similar feelings — e.g. explain the difference between being angry and being disappointed
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is feeling really upset or frustrated, can they use words like 'I need to calm down' or 'I'm feeling overwhelmed' instead of just acting out?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解并使用管理强烈情绪的关键词汇——平静（calm）、策略（strategy）、应对（cope）、平复（settle）、耐心（patience）、不堪重负（overwhelmed）和呼吸（breathe）——并理解掌握这些词汇是运用它们的第一步。
evidenceZh: 能够准确使用“沮丧（frustrated）”、“焦虑（anxious）”、“不堪重负（overwhelmed）”和“失望（disappointed）”等词汇来描述自己在困难时刻的感受。
能用自己的话解释什么是“冷静下来”的策略，并说出至少两种他们尝试过的方法（例如：深呼吸、数数、离开现场）。
能够区分相似的情绪——例如，解释生气和失望之间的区别。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}感到非常难过或沮丧时，他们能否使用诸如“我需要冷静一下”或“我感到不堪重负”之类的词语来表达，而不是直接发脾气或行为失控？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Breaking Tasks into Steps
topics.description: Break a challenging task into smaller, manageable steps rather than feeling overwhelmed by the whole thing — and celebrate progress along the way
evidence: Take a challenging task and list at least three smaller steps to complete it
Start with the first step rather than procrastinating on the whole task
Acknowledge progress after completing each step
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has a big school project that feels overwhelming, can they break it down into smaller steps — like 'first I'll research, then I'll write the introduction' — rather than panicking about the whole thing?
topics.descriptionZh: 将具有挑战性的任务分解为更小、更易掌控的步骤，而不是被整体任务压得喘不过气——并在过程中为取得的每一步进展庆祝。
evidenceZh: 面对一项有挑战性的任务，列出至少三个完成它的较小步骤
从第一步开始做起，而不是对整个任务拖延不决
在完成每一个步骤后，肯定自己取得的进展
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}面对一个让人感到压力巨大的学校大项目，他们能把任务拆解成更小的步骤——比如“第一步我先查阅资料，第二步我再写前言”——而不是被整个任务吓倒吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Choosing the Right Coping Strategy
topics.description: Understand that different situations require different coping strategies — what works for anger might not work for sadness, and what helps at school might be different from what helps at home
evidence: Name at least two different coping strategies and explain when each one is most useful
Choose an appropriate strategy based on the specific situation and emotion
Reflect on a time a strategy didn't work and explain what they might try instead
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} recognise that when they're angry they need to do something physical like walk around, but when they're worried they need to talk it through — rather than using the same approach for every difficult feeling?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解不同的情境需要不同的应对策略（coping strategies）——对愤怒有效的方法可能对悲伤无效，在学校有帮助的方法在家里也可能不同
evidenceZh: 至少说出两种不同的应对策略，并解释每种策略在何时最有用
根据具体的情境和情绪选择合适的应对策略
反思一次某种策略不起作用的情况，并解释接下来可能会尝试的其他方法
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否能认识到，当他们生气时需要进行一些身体活动（如四处走动），而当他们感到担忧时则需要倾诉和沟通——而不是对每种难以处理的情绪都使用同一种应对方法？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Growth Mindset
topics.description: Understand the concept of a growth mindset — that abilities and intelligence can grow with effort, practice, and good strategies — as opposed to a fixed mindset where you believe you're either good at something or you're not
evidence: Explain the difference between growth mindset and fixed mindset in their own words
Use 'yet' language when describing something they find difficult
Give an example of something they got better at through practice and effort
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} finds something difficult like learning to ride a bike or mastering times tables, do they say 'I can't do it YET' rather than 'I'm just not good at this'?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解成长型思维（Growth Mindset）的概念——即能力和智力可以通过努力、练习和好的策略来增长——这与固定型思维（Fixed Mindset）相反，后者认为你要么天生擅长某事，要么就完全不擅长。
evidenceZh: 用自己的话解释成长型思维和固定型思维的区别
在描述觉得困难的事情时，使用‘尚未’（yet）的表达方式
举一个通过练习和努力而取得进步的具体例子
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 遇到像学骑自行车或掌握乘法口诀表（times tables）这样困难的事情时，他们会说‘我还做不到（YET）’而不是‘我就是不擅长这个’吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Positive Self-Talk
topics.description: Use positive self-talk to manage difficult situations — replacing unhelpful thoughts like 'I'm stupid' or 'I'll never be able to do this' with encouraging ones like 'This is hard but I can keep trying' or 'I've done hard things before'
evidence: Give an example of an unhelpful thought and rephrase it as a helpful one
Use positive self-talk aloud or in writing when facing a challenge
Explain how the words we say to ourselves affect how we feel and perform
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is struggling with homework and starts saying 'I'm rubbish at this', can they catch that thought and replace it with something more helpful like 'I just need to try a different approach'?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用积极自我对话来应对困难情况——将“我很笨”或“我永远也做不到”等无益的想法，替换为“这很难，但我可以继续尝试”或“我以前做成过困难的事”等鼓励性的想法。
evidenceZh: 举一个无益想法的例子，并将其重新表述为有益的想法
在面对挑战时，大声说出或在纸上写下积极的自我对话
解释我们对自己说的话如何影响我们的感受和表现
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 在做作业时遇到困难并开始说“我在这方面太差了”时，他们能察觉到这种想法，并用更有益的想法（比如“我只需要尝试一种不同的方法”）来替换它吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Vocabulary: resilience and self
topics.description: Know and use the vocabulary of resilience and self-management — including regulate, resilience, growth mindset, fixed mindset, self-talk, trigger, setback, persevere, and distress — and understand what each word means in practice
evidence: Explain what 'resilience' means in their own words and give an example of a time they kept going when something was hard
Use 'growth mindset' correctly — e.g. 'I can't do it yet, but I can improve with practice'
Define 'self-regulation' and describe a strategy they use to manage frustration or setbacks
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s team loses a match or they fail a test, can they talk about what happened using words like 'resilience' or 'growth mindset' — showing they understand the difference between giving up and bouncing back?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解并使用有关韧性和自我管理的词汇——包括调节（regulate）、韧性（resilience）、成长型思维（growth mindset）、固定型思维（fixed mindset）、自我对话（self-talk）、触发点（trigger）、挫折（setback）、坚持（persevere）和困扰（distress）——并理解每个词在实际中的含义。
evidenceZh: 用自己的话解释“韧性（resilience）”的含义，并举一个在困难时坚持到底的例子
正确使用“成长型思维（growth mindset）”——例如：“我现在还不会，但通过练习我可以提高”
定义“自我调节（self-regulation）”，并描述他们用来管理挫败感或应对挫折的策略
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}的团队输掉了一场比赛或考试不及格，他们能否使用“韧性（resilience）”或“成长型思维（growth mindset）”等词汇来谈论发生的事情——从而表明他们理解放弃与重新振作（bouncing back）之间的区别？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Personal Coping Toolkit
topics.description: Reflect on which self-regulation and coping strategies work best for them personally, building a 'toolkit' of approaches they can draw on in different situations and sharing what works with others
evidence: Describe at least three personal coping strategies and when each is most effective
Recommend a strategy to a friend based on the friend's specific situation
Evaluate whether a strategy they tried worked well and explain their reasoning
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you 'When I'm stressed about exams I go for a walk and that helps, but when I'm sad I need to talk to someone' — showing they know their own coping toolkit?
topics.descriptionZh: 反思哪些自我调节（self-regulation）和应对策略对自己最有效，建立一个可以在不同情境下使用的“工具箱”，并与他人分享有效的经验。
evidenceZh: 描述至少三种个人应对策略，并说明每种策略在何时最有效
根据朋友的具体情况，向其推荐一种应对策略
评估他们尝试过的某种策略是否有效，并解释其理由
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能告诉你“当我因为考试感到压力时，我会去散步，这很有帮助；但当我难过时，我需要找人倾诉”——这表明他们了解并使用自己的个人应对工具箱吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Personal Goal-Setting
topics.description: Set realistic personal goals, create a simple plan to achieve them, monitor their own progress, and adjust their approach when things aren't working
evidence: Write or state a specific, achievable personal goal with a timeframe
Describe the steps they will take to reach the goal
Review their progress and adjust their plan when something isn't working
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} set themselves a goal — like improving their swimming or finishing a book series — and actually work towards it step by step, adjusting their plan if needed?
topics.descriptionZh: 设定切实可行的个人目标，制定简单的实现计划，监控自身进度，并在方法不奏效时及时调整。
evidenceZh: 写下或说出一个具体、可实现的个人目标，并设定时间期限
描述他们为达成目标将采取的步骤
回顾自己的进度，并在某些方法不奏效时调整计划
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否为自己设定一个目标——比如提高游泳技能或读完一套系列丛书——并切实地一步一步向目标努力，在需要时调整自己的计划？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Resilience and Bouncing Back
topics.description: Understand resilience as the ability to recover from setbacks, adapt to difficult circumstances, and keep going — recognising that resilience is a skill that develops through experience, not a trait you either have or don't
evidence: Define resilience in their own words and explain why it matters
Describe a time they bounced back from a setback and what helped them recover
Explain that resilience grows through experience and that struggling doesn't mean you're weak
topics.assessmentPrompt: After a real disappointment — like not getting a part in the school play or failing a test they studied for — can {{name}} feel upset but then pick themselves up and figure out what to do next?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解韧性是从挫折中恢复、适应困难环境并继续前进的能力——认识到韧性是一种通过经验培养的技能，而不是天生具备或不具备的特质。
evidenceZh: 用自己的话定义韧性，并解释它的重要性
描述一次从挫折中重新振作的经历，以及是什么帮助他们恢复了状态
解释韧性是通过经验成长的，并且遇到困难并不意味着软弱
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在经历真正的失望之后——比如没有在学校戏剧中获得角色，或者考砸了努力复习过的考试——{{name}} 能否在感到难过之后重新振作起来，并思考接下来该怎么办？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Time and Attention Management
topics.description: Manage their own time and attention effectively — prioritising tasks, minimising distractions, and maintaining focus on important work even when it's not the most exciting option
evidence: Create a simple plan for completing multiple tasks in a sensible order
Identify their own common distractions and describe strategies to manage them
Complete a less enjoyable task before a more enjoyable one without constant reminders
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} has homework to finish but also wants to play a game, can they manage their time — doing the homework first or setting a timer — rather than always needing you to enforce it?
topics.descriptionZh: 有效地管理自己的时间和注意力——确定任务的优先级、最大限度地减少干扰，并在重要工作并非最有趣的选择时也能保持专注。
evidenceZh: 制定一个简单的计划，以合理的顺序完成多项任务
识别自己常见的干扰因素，并描述应对这些干扰的策略
在无需不断提醒的情况下，先完成较不喜欢的任务，再去做更喜欢的任务
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}需要完成作业但又想玩游戏时，他们能管理好自己的时间——先写作业或设定计时器——而不是总需要您来督促执行吗？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Good Stress and Bad Stress
topics.description: Distinguish between eustress (the productive, motivating kind of stress) and distress (harmful, overwhelming stress); explain the physiological stress response (fight-flight-freeze, HPA axis) and how chronic stress affects the body and mind; identify common adolescent stressors (academic pressure, social comparison, physical change, uncertainty about the future); evaluate evidence-based coping strategies (exercise, sleep, mindfulness, social support, expressive writing); recognise warning signs that stress has crossed into anxiety or depression and know where to get help
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is under pressure from exams or social situations, can they name two or three strategies that genuinely help them manage the stress — and explain why each one actually works, not just that it 'makes them feel better'?
topics.descriptionZh: 区分良性压力（eustress，具有生产力和激励作用的积极压力）与不良压力（distress，有害且令人不堪重负的压力）；解释生理压力反应（战斗-逃跑-僵死反应（fight-flight-freeze）、下丘脑-垂体-肾上腺轴（HPA axis））以及慢性压力如何影响身心；识别青少年常见的压力源（学业压力、社会比较、生理变化、对未来的不确定性）；评估基于证据的应对策略（锻炼、睡眠、正念、社会支持、表达性书写）；识别压力已转化为焦虑或抑郁的预警信号，并知道在何处寻求帮助
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 面临考试或社交环境的压力时，他们能否说出两三种真正帮助他们管理压力的策略——并解释每一种策略为什么真正有效，而不仅仅是因为它“让他们感觉好些”？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Habits and Motivation
topics.description: Understand habit formation through the cue-routine-reward loop and how to design new habits intentionally; distinguish intrinsic motivation (doing something for its own value) from extrinsic motivation (rewards/punishments) and understand when each is more effective; understand procrastination as primarily an emotion regulation problem (avoiding discomfort) rather than a time management failure; apply self-determination theory (autonomy, competence, relatedness) to boost intrinsic motivation; design environments that reduce friction for desired behaviours
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} keeps meaning to do something important but finds themselves putting it off, can they explain the real reason people procrastinate — it's not laziness — and describe one practical change they could make to their environment to make starting easier?
topics.descriptionZh: 通过“提示-惯例-奖励”（cue-routine-reward）循环理解习惯的形成，以及如何有意识地设计新习惯；区分内在动机（因事物本身的价值而做某事）和外在动机（奖励/惩罚），并理解在何种情况下各自更有效；理解拖延主要是一个情绪调节问题（逃避不适感），而不是时间管理失败；应用自我决定理论（自主性 autonomy、胜任力 competence、归属感 relatedness）来提升内在动机；设计能够减少期望行为阻力的环境。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 一直打算做某件重要的事情，却发现自己一再拖延，他们能否解释人们拖延的真正原因——这并不是因为懒惰——并描述他们可以对环境做出的一个实际改变，从而让开始变得更容易？

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Growth Through Adversity
topics.description: Understand that facing serious challenges can lead to genuine growth in three domains: new perspectives on life, improved relationships, and a strengthened sense of personal capability (post-traumatic growth); distinguish genuine growth from toxic positivity ('everything happens for a reason') and from denial; understand that resilience does not mean being unaffected by adversity but recovering and growing through it; develop a personal philosophy for handling setbacks based on meaning-making; explore how to support others going through serious difficulty without minimising their experience
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} ever come through something genuinely hard and found it changed them in a meaningful way? Can they explain what post-traumatic growth means and how it differs from just 'getting over it' or pretending something difficult was fine?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解面临严峻挑战能在三个领域带来真正的成长：对生活的新视角、改善的人际关系以及增强的个人能力感（创伤后成长 post-traumatic growth）；区分真正的成长与“有毒的积极”（toxic positivity，如“一切发生皆有原因”）及否认现实；理解心理韧性（resilience）并不意味着不受逆境影响，而是从中恢复并获得成长；基于意义建构（meaning-making），培养个人应对挫折的理念；探索如何在不轻视他人经历的情况下，支持正在经历严重困难的人。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否曾经历过真正艰难的事情，并发现它在有意义的方面改变了他们？他们能否解释创伤后成长（post-traumatic growth）的含义，以及它与仅仅“熬过去”或假装困难的事情没问题有何不同？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Animal Camouflage
topics.description: Know that many animals use camouflage — colours and patterns that help them blend into their surroundings — to hide from predators or to sneak up on prey, like a leaf insect that looks like a leaf or an Arctic hare that turns white in winter
evidence: Explains that camouflage means blending in with surroundings
Gives at least 3 examples of camouflaged animals
Explains that camouflage helps animals hide from predators or sneak up on food
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} tries to spot a grasshopper in the garden, can they explain that it's hard to see because its green colour helps it hide in the grass — and give other examples of animals that use camouflage?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解许多动物会使用伪装（camouflage）——即帮助它们融入周围环境的颜色和图案——来躲避捕食者或悄悄靠近猎物，例如看起来像树叶的叶子虫（leaf insect）或在冬天变白的北极兔（Arctic hare）。
evidenceZh: 解释伪装意味着融入周围环境
给出至少3种具有伪装能力的动物的例子
解释伪装能帮助动物躲避捕食者或悄悄靠近食物
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 试图在花园里寻找蚱蜢（grasshopper），他们能否解释很难看到它是因为它的绿色帮助它隐藏在草丛中——并给出其他使用伪装（camouflage）的动物的例子？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Animal Homes
topics.description: Know that animals make or find many different kinds of homes — birds build nests, rabbits dig burrows, bees live in hives, hermit crabs use empty shells, spiders spin webs — and that these shelters protect them and their young
evidence: Names at least 4 different types of animal homes (nest, burrow, hive, web, shell, den, lodge)
Explains that animals need homes for shelter and to keep their babies safe
Matches common animals to their homes
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} where different animals live, can they describe several animal homes — like a bird's nest, a rabbit's burrow, or a bee's hive — and say why animals need shelter?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解动物会建造或寻找各种各样的家——鸟儿筑巢，兔子挖洞，蜜蜂住在蜂巢里，寄居蟹使用空贝壳，蜘蛛结网——并懂得这些庇护所（shelters）能保护它们和它们的幼崽。
evidenceZh: 至少能说出4种不同类型的动物住所（巢穴、地洞、蜂巢、蛛网、贝壳、兽穴、小屋）
能解释动物需要家来获得庇护，并保护宝宝的安全
能将常见动物与它们的家正确匹配
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果您问{{name}}不同的动物住在哪里，他们能描述出几种动物的家吗——比如鸟儿的巢穴、兔子的地洞或蜜蜂的蜂巢——并说出动物为什么需要庇护所（shelter）吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Animal Record-Holders
topics.description: Know some of the world's animal record-holders — the blue whale is the largest animal ever, the cheetah is the fastest land animal, the bee hummingbird is the smallest bird, the giraffe is the tallest — and compare their sizes to familiar objects
evidence: Names at least 4 animal record-holders with their record (fastest, biggest, tallest, smallest, etc.)
Compares an animal's size or ability to a familiar reference
Shows enthusiasm for superlative animal facts
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} which animal is the fastest or the biggest in the world, can they name some record-holders like the cheetah or blue whale and compare their size to something familiar, like 'a blue whale is as long as three buses'?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解世界上一些动物纪录保持者——蓝鲸（blue whale）是有史以来最大的动物，猎豹（cheetah）是陆地上跑得最快的动物，吸蜜蜂鸟（bee hummingbird）是最小的鸟类，长颈鹿（giraffe）是最高的——并将它们的体型与熟悉的物体进行比较。
evidenceZh: 能说出至少4种动物纪录保持者及其保持的纪录（最快、最大、最高、最小等）
能将动物的体型或能力与熟悉的参照物进行比较
对动物的“世界之最”事实表现出热情
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你问{{name}}世界上哪种动物跑得最快或体型最大，他们能说出猎豹或蓝鲸等纪录保持者，并将它们的体型与熟悉的事物进行比较吗？比如“蓝鲸有三辆公交车那么长”？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Animals Everywhere
topics.description: Know that animals live all over the world — on land, in water, and in the air — and that every continent, even icy Antarctica, is home to animals, each suited to the conditions where they live
evidence: Names at least 3 animals from different environments (e.g., forest, ocean, desert)
States that animals live on land, in water, and some can fly
Recognises that animals live on every continent
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you show {{name}} pictures of a polar bear, a parrot, a camel, and a penguin, can they tell you that animals live in all sorts of different places around the world?
topics.descriptionZh: 知道动物生活在世界各地——在陆地上、水里和空中——并且每个大洲，甚至是冰雪覆盖的南极洲，都有动物栖息，每种动物都适应其生存的环境条件。
evidenceZh: 能说出至少3种来自不同环境的动物（例如：森林、海洋、沙漠）
说明动物生活在陆地上、水里，有些还能飞
认识到动物生活在每个大洲
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你给{{name}}看北极熊、鹦鹉、骆驼和企鹅的图片，他们能告诉你动物生活在世界各地各种各样的地方吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How Animals Have Babies
topics.description: Know that different animals have their babies in different ways — some lay eggs (birds, reptiles, fish, insects), some give birth to live young (most mammals) — and that babies may look like miniature adults or look very different from their parents
evidence: Gives examples of animals that lay eggs and animals that give birth to live young
Describes at least one example of a baby that looks different from its parent (e.g., tadpole/frog, caterpillar/butterfly)
Shows curiosity about how different animals have their babies
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a nest with eggs in a nature programme, can they explain that birds lay eggs and the babies hatch out, but dogs and cats have their babies born alive?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解不同动物繁衍后代的方式不同——有些动物产卵（卵生，如鸟类、爬行动物、鱼类、昆虫），有些动物直接生出幼崽（胎生，大多数哺乳动物）——并了解幼崽可能看起来像微缩版的成年动物，或者与父母长得非常不同。
evidenceZh: 能举出卵生动物（产卵）和胎生动物（直接生出幼崽）的例子
能描述至少一个幼崽与父母长相不同的例子（例如：蝌蚪/青蛙、毛毛虫/蝴蝶）
对不同动物繁衍后代的方式表现出好奇心
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在自然节目中看到有蛋的鸟巢，他们能否解释鸟类是产卵的且幼崽是从蛋中孵化出来的，而狗和猫则是直接生出活的幼崽？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Nocturnal Animals
topics.description: Know that some animals are nocturnal — active at night and sleeping during the day — and that nocturnal animals often have special features like big eyes (owls, tarsiers), large ears (bats, fennec foxes), or sensitive whiskers to help them find food in the dark
evidence: Explains what 'nocturnal' means
Names at least 3 nocturnal animals (e.g., owl, bat, fox, hedgehog, moth)
Describes one feature that helps a nocturnal animal (e.g., big eyes, echolocation, whiskers)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears an owl hooting at bedtime, can they explain that owls are nocturnal — meaning they sleep during the day and come out at night — and that their big eyes help them see in the dark?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解有些动物是夜行动物——它们在夜间活动，白天睡觉——并且夜行动物通常具有特殊的身体特征，如大眼睛（猫头鹰、眼镜猴）、大耳朵（蝙蝠、耳廓狐）或敏感的胡须，以帮助它们在黑暗中寻找食物。
evidenceZh: 能解释“夜行性 (nocturnal)”的含义
能说出至少3种夜行动物的名字（例如：猫头鹰、蝙蝠、狐狸、刺猬、飞蛾）
能描述一种有助于夜行动物生存的身体特征（例如：大眼睛、回声定位 (echolocation)、胡须）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在就寝时间听到猫头鹰叫，他们能解释猫头鹰是夜行动物——也就是白天睡觉、晚上出来活动——并且它们的大眼睛能帮助它们在黑暗中看清东西吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Wild, Farm & Pet Animals
topics.description: Understand the difference between wild animals, farm animals, and pets — wild animals find their own food and shelter in nature; farm animals are kept by people for food, wool, or eggs; pets are animals people keep for companionship — and know that wild animals should be observed from a distance
evidence: Sorts animals into wild, farm, and pet categories with examples
Explains one key difference between each category
Understands that wild animals should be observed, not approached
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a fox in the garden, can they explain that it's a wild animal — different from their pet cat or a farm sheep — and that wild animals look after themselves and shouldn't be touched?
topics.nameZh: 野生动物、农场动物与宠物
topics.descriptionZh: 理解野生动物、农场动物和宠物之间的区别——野生动物在自然界中自己寻找食物和住所；农场动物由人类饲养，用于提供食物、羊毛或鸡蛋；宠物是人类饲养用来陪伴的动物——并知道应该保持距离观察野生动物。
evidenceZh: 能将动物分为野生、农场和宠物三类并举例
能解释各类别之间的一个主要区别
懂得对野生动物应保持观察，不可靠近
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在花园里看到一只狐狸，他们能解释这是一只野生动物——不同于他们的宠物猫或农场的绵羊——并且明白野生动物会自己照顾自己，不能去触摸吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Animal Communication
topics.description: Understand that animals communicate in many different ways — birds sing to attract mates and defend territory, whales call across vast ocean distances, bees dance to show other bees where food is, wolves howl to keep the pack together, and fireflies flash light signals — and that communication is essential for survival
evidence: Describes at least 4 different methods of animal communication (sound, dance, light, scent, body language)
Gives a specific animal example for each method
Explains that animals communicate to find mates, warn of danger, or share food locations
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears birds singing in the morning, can they explain that birdsong is a way of communicating — and describe at least two other ways different animals send messages to each other?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解动物通过多种不同的方式进行交流——鸟儿歌唱以吸引伴侣和保卫领地，鲸鱼在广阔的海洋中远距离呼唤，蜜蜂跳舞以告诉其他蜜蜂食物的位置，狼群嚎叫以保持群体聚集，萤火虫闪烁光信号——并且交流对于生存至关重要。
evidenceZh: 描述至少4种不同的动物交流方式（声音、舞蹈、光、气味、肢体语言）
为每种方式提供一个具体的动物示例
解释动物交流是为了寻找伴侣、警告危险或分享食物位置
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}在早晨听到鸟儿唱歌，他们能解释鸟鸣是一种交流方式吗——并描述至少两种不同动物之间传递信息的其他方式？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Animal Migration
topics.description: Know that many animals make incredible journeys called migrations — Arctic terns fly from pole to pole, monarch butterflies travel thousands of miles across North America, wildebeest cross the Serengeti following rain, and humpback whales swim between polar feeding grounds and tropical breeding waters — and that these journeys are linked to food, breeding, and seasons
evidence: Defines migration as a regular long journey animals make
Names at least 3 migratory animals with their routes or destinations
Explains that migration is driven by food availability, breeding, or seasonal changes
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learns about the monarch butterfly's journey, can they explain what migration means and name at least two other animals that make long journeys — and say why they travel?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解许多动物会进行被称为迁徙（Migration）的不可思议的旅程——北极燕鸥（Arctic terns）从地球一极飞到另一极，黑脉金斑蝶（monarch butterflies）穿越北美大陆飞行数千英里，角马（wildebeest）追随雨水穿越塞伦盖蒂大草原，座头鲸（humpback whales）在极地觅食区和热带繁殖水域之间游动——并了解这些旅程与食物、繁殖和季节变化有关。
evidenceZh: 将迁徙定义为动物定期进行的一段漫长旅程
说出至少3种迁徙动物及其迁徙路线或目的地
解释迁徙是由食物供应、繁殖或季节变化所驱动的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 了解了黑脉金斑蝶的旅程，他们能解释迁徙的含义，并说出至少另外两种进行长途旅程的动物，以及说明它们为什么要进行迁徙吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Desert Animals
topics.description: Explore animals of the desert — camels, fennec foxes, scorpions, rattlesnakes, meerkats — and understand how desert animals survive extreme heat and lack of water through being active at night, storing water or fat, burrowing underground during the day, and having large ears to lose heat
evidence: Names at least 4 desert animals
Explains at least two desert survival adaptations (nocturnal behaviour, water storage, burrowing, large ears for cooling)
Knows deserts can be hot or cold but are always dry
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads about camels in a desert, can they explain at least two ways desert animals cope with the heat and lack of water — like being active at night or having special body features?
topics.descriptionZh: 探索沙漠中的动物——骆驼、耳廓狐 (fennec foxes)、蝎子、响尾蛇、猫鼬 (meerkats)——并了解沙漠动物如何通过夜间活动、储存水分或脂肪、白天在地下挖洞以及拥有散热的大耳朵，来在极端高温和缺水的环境中生存。
evidenceZh: 能说出至少4种沙漠动物的名字
能解释至少两种沙漠生存适应特征（如夜行性行为 nocturnal behaviour、储水 water storage、挖洞 burrowing、大耳朵散热 large ears for cooling）
知道沙漠可能很热也可能很冷，但总是非常干燥的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 阅读了关于沙漠中骆驼的内容，他们能否解释沙漠动物应对高温和缺水的至少两种方法——比如夜间活动或拥有特殊的身体特征？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Polar Animals
topics.description: Explore animals of the Arctic and Antarctic — polar bears, Arctic foxes, and walruses in the north; penguins, seals, and albatrosses in the south — and understand how polar animals survive extreme cold through thick fur or blubber, huddling behaviour, and seasonal changes like white winter coats
evidence: Names at least 3 animals each from the Arctic and Antarctic
Explains at least two adaptations for surviving cold (blubber, thick fur, huddling, white camouflage)
Knows polar bears live only in the Arctic and penguins only in the Antarctic/Southern Hemisphere
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a nature programme about the Arctic, can they explain how polar bears stay warm in freezing temperatures and name at least two differences between Arctic animals (north) and Antarctic animals (south)?
topics.descriptionZh: 探索北极和南极的动物——北方的北极熊、北极狐和海象；南方的企鹅、海豹和信天翁——并了解极地动物如何通过厚厚的皮毛或脂肪（blubber）、群聚保暖行为（huddling behaviour）以及季节性变化（如换上白色的冬装）来在极寒环境中生存。
evidenceZh: 能说出北极和南极各自至少3种动物的名称
能解释至少两种适应寒冷环境的特征（如脂肪层 blubber、厚皮毛、群聚保暖 huddling 或白色伪装 white camouflage）
知道北极熊只生活在北极，而企鹅只生活在南极/南半球
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 观看了一部关于北极的自然纪录片，他们能解释北极熊如何在冰天雪地中保暖，并说出北极（北方）动物和南极（南方）动物之间的至少两个区别吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Predator Hunting Strategies
topics.description: Understand that predators have evolved hunting strategies — wolves hunt in packs, chameleons use their long tongues, spiders build webs, crocodiles ambush at water's edge — and prey animals have evolved defences — porcupine spines, skunk spray, poison dart frog toxins, zebra stripes confusing predators, playing dead
evidence: Describes at least 3 predator hunting strategies with examples
Describes at least 3 prey defence mechanisms with examples
Understands the concept of an 'arms race' between predators and prey
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watches a nature programme showing a lion hunting, can they describe at least two different ways predators catch food and two ways prey animals defend themselves?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解捕食者（predators）进化出的狩猎策略——狼群合作捕猎、变色龙使用长舌、蜘蛛结网、鳄鱼在水边伏击——以及猎物（prey）进化出的防御机制——豪猪的刺、臭鼬的喷雾、箭毒蛙的毒素、斑马条纹迷惑捕食者、装死。
evidenceZh: 能举例描述至少3种捕食者的狩猎策略
能举例描述至少3种猎物的防御机制
理解捕食者与猎物之间“军备竞赛”（arms race）的概念
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}观看了一档展示狮子捕猎的自然节目，他们能否描述出至少两种捕食者捕捉食物的不同方式，以及两种猎物防御自己的方式？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rainforest Animals
topics.description: Explore animals of the tropical rainforest — the most species-rich habitat on Earth — learning that the forest has layers (canopy, understory, forest floor) with different animals at each level: toucans and monkeys in the canopy, jaguars and frogs on the floor, and that rainforests are found near the equator
evidence: Names at least 4 rainforest animals from different layers
Describes the rainforest as having layers (canopy, understory, forest floor)
Explains that rainforests are near the equator and are hot and wet
Recognises that rainforests have more species than almost any other habitat
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watches a documentary about rainforests, can they describe at least three animals that live there and explain that different animals live at different heights in the forest — some in the treetops and some on the ground?
topics.descriptionZh: 探索热带雨林（地球上物种最丰富的栖息地）中的动物，了解森林分为不同层次（树冠层 canopy、林下层 understory、林地层 forest floor），每个层次都有不同的动物：树冠层有巨嘴鸟和猴子，地面上有美洲豹和青蛙，并了解热带雨林分布在赤道附近。
evidenceZh: 至少说出4种来自不同层次的雨林动物
描述热带雨林具有不同的层次（树冠层 canopy、林下层 understory、林地层 forest floor）
解释热带雨林靠近赤道，气候炎热潮湿
认识到热带雨林的物种数量几乎超过地球上任何其他栖息地
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 观看了一部关于热带雨林的纪录片，他们能描述至少三种生活在那里的动物，并解释不同的动物生活在森林的不同高度——有的在树顶上，有的在地面上吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Savanna & Grassland Animals
topics.description: Explore animals of the grasslands and savanna — lions, zebras, wildebeest, elephants, cheetahs in African savanna; bison and prairie dogs in American grasslands — understanding why large herds form on open grasslands and how predators and prey interact in these wide-open spaces
evidence: Names at least 5 grassland/savanna animals
Explains that herding provides safety in numbers against predators
Describes the predator-prey relationship (e.g., lions hunt zebras)
Knows grasslands/savannas are wide-open habitats with few trees
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees pictures of the African savanna, can they name at least four animals that live there and explain why some animals like zebras live in large herds?
topics.descriptionZh: 探索草原和稀树草原的动物——非洲稀树草原的狮子、斑马、角马、大象、猎豹；美洲草原的美洲野牛和草原犬鼠——理解为什么在开阔的草原上会形成大型兽群，以及捕食者和猎物在这些开阔地带如何互动。
evidenceZh: 能说出至少5种草原/稀树草原动物
解释群居能通过数量优势提供安全保护以抵御捕食者
描述捕食者与猎物的关系（例如：狮子捕猎斑马）
知道草原/稀树草原是树木稀少的开阔栖息地
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到非洲稀树草原的图片，他们能说出至少四种生活在那里的动物，并解释为什么像斑马这样的一些动物会成群生活吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The World of Minibeasts
topics.description: Know that insects and other minibeasts (spiders, worms, snails, centipedes) are the most numerous and diverse group of animals on Earth — there are more species of beetle than any other animal — and that they play vital roles as pollinators (bees, butterflies), decomposers (woodlice, worms), and food for other animals
evidence: Knows that insects/minibeasts are the most numerous animal group
Names at least 3 roles minibeasts play: pollinators, decomposers, food source
Distinguishes insects (6 legs) from spiders (8 legs) from other minibeasts
Shows appreciation for the importance of invertebrates
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} spots a bee in the garden, can they explain why bees are important — and name at least two other jobs that insects and minibeasts do that help the natural world?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解昆虫和其他微小生物（蜘蛛、蠕虫、蜗牛、蜈蚣）是地球上数量最多、种类最丰富的动物群体——甲虫的物种数量比其他任何动物都多——并且它们作为传粉者（蜜蜂、蝴蝶）、分解者（鼠妇、蠕虫）以及其他动物的食物，发挥着至关重要的作用。
evidenceZh: 知道昆虫和微小生物是数量最多的动物群体
能说出微小生物扮演的至少3种角色：传粉者、分解者、食物来源
能区分昆虫（6条腿）、蜘蛛（8条腿）和其他微小生物
认识到无脊椎动物的重要性
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在花园里发现一只蜜蜂，他们能否解释蜜蜂为什么重要——并说出昆虫和微小生物对自然界有帮助的至少另外两项作用？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Animal Intelligence
topics.description: Explore animal intelligence and complex behaviour — chimpanzees and crows use tools, dolphins recognise themselves in mirrors, octopuses solve puzzles and escape enclosures, elephants mourn their dead, meerkats teach their young to handle scorpions — understanding that many animals think, learn, and have social lives more complex than once believed
evidence: Gives at least 4 examples of animal intelligence or complex behaviour
Explains what 'tool use' means and names at least 2 tool-using animals
Discusses how scientists test animal intelligence (mirror test, puzzle boxes, observation)
Shows understanding that intelligence takes different forms in different species
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watches a video of a crow using a stick to get food from a tube, can they explain that this shows animal intelligence and give other examples of animals that use tools, solve problems, or show complex behaviour?
topics.descriptionZh: 探索动物智力和复杂行为（Complex behaviour）——黑猩猩和乌鸦会使用工具，海豚能在镜子中认出自己，章鱼能解开谜题并逃出围栏，大象会哀悼死去的同伴，狐獴会教幼崽如何处理蝎子——理解许多动物会思考、学习，并且拥有比过去认为的更复杂的社会生活。
evidenceZh: 能列举至少4个动物智力或复杂行为的例子
能解释“工具使用（Tool use）”的含义，并说出至少2种会使用工具的动物
能讨论科学家如何测试动物智力（如镜子测试（Mirror test）、谜题盒（Puzzle boxes）、观察（Observation））
能理解智力在不同物种中有着不同的表现形式
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 观看了一段乌鸦用树枝从管子里获取食物的视频，他们能否解释这说明动物具有智力，并给出其他使用工具、解决问题或表现出复杂行为的动物的例子？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Biodiversity
topics.description: Understand that biodiversity — the variety of different species in an ecosystem — is essential for healthy ecosystems, and that keystone species (like wolves in Yellowstone, sea otters in kelp forests, or bees as pollinators) have an outsized impact on their ecosystem, so that losing one key species can cause a cascade of changes affecting many others
evidence: Defines biodiversity as the variety of species in an ecosystem
Explains why biodiversity matters (stability, resilience, ecosystem services)
Defines keystone species and gives at least 2 examples
Describes a trophic cascade or chain reaction from removing/adding a species
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learns about how wolves were brought back to Yellowstone and the whole ecosystem changed, can they explain what a 'keystone species' is and why having many different species in an area matters?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解生物多样性——即生态系统中不同物种的多样性——对于维持健康的生态系统至关重要；同时理解关键物种（Keystone species）（例如黄石公园的狼、海藻林中的海獭或作为传粉者的蜜蜂）对其生态系统有着不成比例的巨大影响，以至于失去某一个关键物种就会引发一连串的变化，从而影响到许多其他物种。
evidenceZh: 将生物多样性定义为生态系统中物种的多样性
解释生物多样性为何重要（如：稳定性、恢复力、生态系统服务）
定义关键物种（Keystone species）并给出至少2个例子
描述移除或引入某个物种后引发的营养级联（Trophic cascade）或连锁反应
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 学习了狼被重新引入黄石公园以及整个生态系统随之发生变化的案例，他们能解释什么是“关键物种”（Keystone species），以及为什么一个地区拥有众多不同的物种很重要吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Endangered & Extinct Species
topics.description: Understand why some animal species become endangered or go extinct — habitat destruction, hunting/poaching, pollution, climate change, and invasive species — and know examples like the giant panda, mountain gorilla, Amur leopard, and the now-extinct dodo and thylacine, using the IUCN Red List as the system scientists use to track threatened species
evidence: Defines endangered as a species at risk of extinction
Names at least 3 causes of species becoming endangered
Gives at least 3 examples of endangered or extinct animals
Knows the IUCN Red List exists as a tracking system
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a news story about an endangered animal, can they explain what 'endangered' means and describe at least three reasons why some animals are at risk of disappearing forever?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解为什么某些动物物种会濒危或灭绝——栖息地破坏、狩猎与偷猎、污染、气候变化和入侵物种——并认识大熊猫、山地大猩猩、远东豹（阿穆尔豹），以及已经灭绝的渡渡鸟和袋狼等例子，了解世界自然保护联盟濒危物种红色名录（IUCN Red List）是科学家用来追踪受威胁物种的系统。
evidenceZh: 将濒危（endangered）定义为面临灭绝风险的物种
列举至少3个导致物种濒危的原因
给出至少3个濒危或灭绝动物的例子
知道世界自然保护联盟濒危物种红色名录（IUCN Red List）作为一个追踪系统的存在
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到关于濒危动物的新闻报道，他们能解释“濒危”是什么意思，并描述至少三个为什么有些动物面临永远消失（灭绝）风险的原因吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Invasive Species
topics.description: Understand that invasive species are animals (or plants) that have been introduced to a place where they don't naturally belong — like grey squirrels outcompeting red squirrels in the UK, cane toads poisoning native predators in Australia, or rabbits devastating ecosystems in Australia — and that they can cause serious harm to native wildlife by competing for food, spreading disease, or having no natural predators
evidence: Defines invasive species as non-native animals introduced to a new environment
Names at least 2 examples of invasive species and their impacts
Explains at least 2 reasons invasive species are harmful (no predators, outcompete natives, spread disease)
Understands the difference between a species naturally expanding its range and being introduced by humans
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learns that grey squirrels were brought to the UK from America, can they explain why introduced animals can be a problem for the animals that were already living there?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解入侵物种是指被引入到非自然栖息地的动物（或植物）——例如灰松鼠在英国抢占红松鼠的生存空间，蔗蟾蜍在澳大利亚毒害本土捕食者，或者兔子在澳大利亚破坏生态系统——并且明白它们会通过争夺食物、传播疾病或缺乏天敌等方式，对本土野生动植物造成严重危害。
evidenceZh: 将入侵物种定义为被引入新环境的非本土动物（或植物）
说出至少2个入侵物种的例子及其造成的影响
解释入侵物种造成危害的至少2个原因（没有天敌、排挤本土物种、传播疾病）
理解物种自然扩大分布范围与被人类引入之间的区别
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 了解到灰松鼠是从美洲被引入英国的，他们能否解释为什么这些被引入的动物会对当地原有的动物造成问题？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Protecting Endangered Animals
topics.description: Know how people work to protect endangered animals — through national parks and marine reserves, captive breeding programmes (like those that saved the California condor and Arabian oryx), anti-poaching patrols, wildlife corridors connecting habitats, and laws banning trade in endangered species — and understand that children can contribute through habitat-friendly choices
evidence: Describes at least 3 conservation strategies with specific examples
Names an animal saved from near-extinction by conservation efforts
Suggests at least one action children or families can take to help wildlife
Understands that conservation requires both protecting habitats and helping individual species
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visits a zoo with a breeding programme, can they explain how zoos help save endangered species and describe at least two other ways people protect wildlife?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解人们如何保护濒危动物——通过建立国家公园和海洋保护区、圈养繁殖计划（captive breeding programmes，如拯救加州神鹫（California condor）和阿拉伯大羚羊（Arabian oryx）的计划）、反盗猎巡逻、连接栖息地的野生动物走廊（wildlife corridors），以及禁止濒危物种贸易的法律——并理解儿童可以通过选择对栖息地友好的生活方式来贡献力量。
evidenceZh: 描述至少3种保护策略并举出具体例子
说出一种因保护工作而从濒临灭绝边缘被拯救回来的动物
提出至少一项儿童或家庭可以帮助野生动物的具体行动
理解保护工作既需要保护栖息地，也需要帮助具体的物种
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 参观了一个开展繁殖计划的动物园，他们能解释动物园是如何帮助拯救濒危物种的，并描述人们保护野生动物的至少其他两种方法吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Structural Adaptations
topics.description: Understand that animals have structural adaptations (body features like the giraffe's long neck, eagle's talons, dolphin's streamlined shape), behavioural adaptations (migration, hibernation, tool use), and physiological adaptations (antifreeze in Arctic fish blood, echolocation in bats) — and that these developed over many generations through natural selection
evidence: Defines adaptation as a feature or behaviour that helps an animal survive in its environment
Gives examples of structural, behavioural, and physiological adaptations
Explains that adaptations develop over many generations, not during one animal's lifetime
Connects adaptations to the concept of natural selection at a basic level
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a woodpecker pecking a tree, can they explain that its strong beak, long tongue, and shock-absorbing skull are all adaptations — and describe what the word 'adaptation' means with other examples?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解动物具有结构适应（身体特征，如长颈鹿的长脖子、老鹰的利爪、海豚的流线型体型）、行为适应（如迁徙、冬眠、使用工具）以及生理适应（如北极鱼类血液中的抗冻物质、蝙蝠的回声定位）——并且明白这些适应性是通过自然选择 (natural selection) 经过许多世代逐渐发展而来的。
evidenceZh: 将适应 (adaptation) 定义为帮助动物在所处环境中生存的特征或行为
给出结构适应、行为适应和生理适应的例子
解释适应是经过许多世代逐渐发展形成的，而不是在单只动物的一生中获得的
在基础层面上将适应与自然选择 (natural selection) 的概念联系起来
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到啄木鸟在啄树干，他们能否解释它强壮的喙、长长的舌头和能减震的头骨都是适应 (adaptations) ——并且能用其他例子来说明‘适应’是什么意思吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Symbiosis
topics.description: Understand symbiosis — close relationships between different species — including mutualism (both benefit, like clownfish and anemones), commensalism (one benefits without harming the other, like remora fish riding sharks), and parasitism (one benefits at the other's expense, like ticks on deer) — and recognise these relationships in nature
evidence: Defines symbiosis as a close relationship between different species
Distinguishes mutualism, commensalism, and parasitism with an example of each
Identifies symbiotic relationships when presented with new scenarios
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a nature programme showing a small bird picking insects off a buffalo's back, can they explain that both animals benefit from this relationship and name the type of symbiosis?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解共生现象——即不同物种之间建立的密切关系，包括互利共生（双方都受益，例如小丑鱼和海葵）、偏利共生（一方受益而另一方不受影响，例如䲟鱼搭乘鲨鱼）以及寄生（一方受益而以损害另一方为代价，例如鹿身上的蜱虫）——并能够识别自然界中的这些共生关系。
evidenceZh: 将共生定义为不同物种之间的密切关系
区分互利共生、偏利共生和寄生，并为每种类型举出一个例子
在遇到新场景时，能够识别其中的共生关系
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到一档自然节目，节目中一只小鸟正在啄食水牛背上的昆虫，他们能否解释这两种动物是如何从这种关系中获益的，并说出这种共生关系的类型？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Red Queen Hypothesis
topics.description: Introduce the Red Queen hypothesis — species must keep evolving just to maintain fitness relative to co-evolving partners; describe predator-prey arms races (cheetah speed vs gazelle speed, bat echolocation vs moth hearing jamming) and parasite-host co-evolution (myxomatosis in rabbits); explain Darwin's hawk moth and orchid as a classic example of mutualistic co-evolution predicting an unknown species; understand that co-evolution is a major driver of biological diversification
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the idea of an evolutionary arms race — how a predator and its prey keep evolving better attack and defence strategies in response to each other, never quite getting ahead?
topics.descriptionZh: 介绍红皇后假说——物种必须不断进化，才能保持相对于共同进化伙伴的适应度（fitness）；描述捕食者与猎物之间的军备竞赛（如猎豹的速度与瞪羚的速度、蝙蝠的回声定位与飞蛾的听觉干扰）以及寄生者与宿主之间的协同进化（co-evolution，如兔子的粘液瘤病）；解释达尔文的天蛾与兰花作为互利协同进化的经典案例，并以此预测了一种当时未知的物种；理解协同进化是生物多样性演化的主要驱动力。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释进化军备竞赛的概念——即捕食者和猎物如何为了应对彼此而不断进化出更好的攻击和防御策略，却始终无法彻底占据绝对优势？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Deep-Sea Survival
topics.description: Explain how deep-sea animals cope with crushing pressure (no gas-filled spaces, flexible proteins, pressure-adapted enzymes); describe thermoregulation extremes — antifreeze glycoproteins in Antarctic fish, supercooling in wood frogs; introduce tardigrades and cryptobiosis (surviving desiccation, extreme temperatures, radiation, vacuum); survey other extremophiles (thermophiles at hydrothermal vents, halophiles in salt flats); consider what these organisms tell us about the limits of life
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe an animal that can survive being frozen solid, completely dried out, or exposed to the vacuum of space — and explain roughly how it manages to survive conditions that would kill almost any other living thing?
topics.descriptionZh: 探索深海动物如何抵御巨大的水压（它们没有充满气体的空腔，拥有柔韧的蛋白质和适应高压的酶 pressure-adapted enzymes）；了解极端的御寒绝招——比如南极鱼体内的抗冻糖蛋白 antifreeze glycoproteins，以及林蛙的过冷现象 supercooling；认识神奇的水熊虫 tardigrades 和它的隐生绝技 cryptobiosis（能在极度干燥、极端温度、强辐射甚至太空中存活）；探索其他极端微生物 extremophiles（如生活在海底热液喷口的嗜热菌 thermophiles，以及盐湖里的嗜盐菌 halophiles）；最后，让我们一起思考：这些神奇的生物是如何打破我们对生命极限的认知的？
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能描述一种被完全冻成冰棍、彻底干透，或者暴露在太空真空中依然能存活的动物吗？并且能简单解释一下，它是如何在这些足以杀死其他几乎所有生物的极端条件下存活下来的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Sexual Selection
topics.description: Explain sexual selection as a form of natural selection: runaway selection for peacock tails, bird of paradise displays, and frog calls; explain kin selection and altruistic behaviour — why worker bees die to protect the hive, why meerkats stand guard at personal risk (Hamilton's rule, inclusive fitness); introduce game theory in animal behaviour using the hawk-dove model; define cognitive ethology and survey evidence for animal emotions, play, and culture
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a worker bee dying to protect the hive actually makes evolutionary sense — even though the bee never has its own offspring? What's the logic that makes this a successful strategy?
topics.descriptionZh: 把性选择解释为自然选择的一种形式：比如孔雀的尾巴、极乐鸟的华丽展示和青蛙的叫声是如何通过“失控选择”（Runaway selection）进化而来的；解释亲缘选择（Kin selection）和利他行为——为什么工蜂会为了保护蜂巢而牺牲自己，为什么狐獴会冒着生命危险站岗放哨（汉密尔顿法则/Hamilton's rule，广义适合度/Inclusive fitness）；通过“鹰鸽模型”（Hawk-dove model）简单介绍动物行为中的博弈论（Game theory）；定义认知动物行为学（Cognitive ethology），并介绍证明动物也有情感、会玩耍以及拥有自己“文化”的科学证据。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能解释一下为什么工蜂为了保护蜂巢而牺牲，在进化上其实是合理的吗——尽管这只工蜂永远不会有自己的后代？这种策略之所以能成功，背后的逻辑是什么呢？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Biodiversity Crisis
topics.description: Quantify the current biodiversity crisis: extinction rates 100-1000x the background rate; explain methods for measuring biodiversity loss (species-area relationship, population viability analysis, IUCN Red List categories); evaluate rewilding case studies — Yellowstone wolf reintroduction triggering a trophic cascade that changed river courses; Iberian lynx recovery; describe minimum viable population theory and conservation triage; examine ethical debates in deciding which species to prioritise
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what happened to Yellowstone National Park after wolves were reintroduced — what unexpected changes rippled through the whole ecosystem, including effects on rivers, as a result of one predator coming back?
topics.descriptionZh: 量化当前的生物多样性危机：灭绝率是背景灭绝率的100到1000倍；解释衡量生物多样性丧失的方法（物种-面积关系 (species-area relationship)、种群生存力分析 (population viability analysis)、IUCN红色名录等级 (IUCN Red List categories)）；评估“再野化”案例研究——黄石公园重新引入狼引发了营养级联 (trophic cascade)，甚至改变了河流的走向，以及伊比利亚猞猁的恢复；描述最小存活种群 (minimum viable population) 理论和保护分流 (conservation triage)；探讨在决定优先保护哪些物种时的伦理争论。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能描述一下黄石国家公园在重新引入狼之后发生了什么吗——由于一种捕食者的回归，整个生态系统产生了哪些意想不到的连锁反应，包括对河流产生了什么影响？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Grouping Species Using DNA
topics.description: Explain cladistics: organisms are grouped by shared derived characters, not just similarity; how phylogenetic trees are built using molecular data (DNA sequence alignment) and the molecular clock; explain why birds are technically a group within dinosaurs (crown Avemetatarsalia); distinguish convergent evolution (unrelated species evolving similar traits) from parallel evolution; introduce horizontal gene transfer and why the tree of life is more accurately a web; explain why classification systems keep changing as new data emerge
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why biologists now say that birds ARE a type of dinosaur — not just their descendants but literally within the dinosaur family tree? What does that tell us about how scientists classify animals?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释分支分类学（cladistics）：生物是根据共有衍征（shared derived characters）来分组的，而不仅仅是看外表相似；讲解如何利用分子数据（DNA序列比对，DNA sequence alignment）和分子钟（molecular clock）来构建系统发育树（phylogenetic trees）；解释为什么鸟类在分类上其实是恐龙的一个分支（冠龙形类，crown Avemetatarsalia）；区分趋同进化（convergent evolution，没有亲缘关系的物种演化出相似的特征）和平行进化（parallel evolution）；介绍水平基因转移（horizontal gene transfer），并解释为什么“生命之树”更准确地说应该是一张“生命之网”；最后说明为什么随着新数据的发现，生物分类系统会不断发生变化。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能不能解释一下，为什么现在的生物学家认为鸟类“就是”恐龙的一种——它们不仅仅是恐龙的后代，而是真真切切地包含在恐龙的家谱里？这说明了科学家在给动物分类时是怎样的思路？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Dinosaur Sizes
topics.description: Compare dinosaur sizes to familiar things — some dinosaurs were as tall as a house, others were as small as a chicken — and understand that dinosaurs came in a huge range of sizes
evidence: Compare the size of a large dinosaur to a familiar object like a bus or house
