Name a very large dinosaur (e.g. Brachiosaurus) and a small one (e.g. Compsognathus)
Use words like 'taller than', 'longer than', 'heavier than' when comparing
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you that some dinosaurs were enormous and others were tiny — maybe using comparisons like 'as tall as a building' or 'as small as a cat'?
topics.descriptionZh: 将恐龙的大小与熟悉的事物进行比较——有些恐龙有房子那么高，有些则像小鸡一样小——并理解恐龙的体型大小差异巨大。
evidenceZh: 将大型恐龙的大小与公交车或房子等熟悉的物体进行比较
说出一种非常大的恐龙（如腕龙 Brachiosaurus）和一种小型恐龙（如美颌龙 Compsognathus）
在比较时使用“比……更高”、“比……更长”、“比……更重”等词语
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能告诉你有些恐龙巨大无比，而有些却非常微小吗——也许会用“像大楼一样高”或“像猫一样小”这样的比较？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Dinosaurs Were Real
topics.description: Understand that dinosaurs were real animals that lived on Earth a very long time ago and are now extinct — none are alive today
evidence: State that dinosaurs were real animals, not made up
Explain that 'extinct' means no living ones are left anywhere
Distinguish between 'a long time ago' and recent events like last year
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a dinosaur toy, can they tell you that real dinosaurs lived long ago but aren't alive any more?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解恐龙是很久以前生活在地球上的真实动物，现在它们已经灭绝了——今天没有任何恐龙还活着。
evidenceZh: 能够说出恐龙是真实的动物，不是虚构的
能够解释“灭绝（extinct）”意味着地球上再也没有存活的恐龙了
能够区分“很久以前”和“去年”等近期事件
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到恐龙玩具，他们能告诉你真实的恐龙生活在很久以前，但现在再也没有活着的恐龙了吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Famous Dinosaur Species
topics.description: Recognise and name common well-known dinosaur species: Tyrannosaurus rex, Triceratops, Stegosaurus, and Brachiosaurus/Diplodocus, describing a basic feature of each
evidence: Name at least four common dinosaur species from pictures or models
Describe one visible feature of each (e.g. T. rex has tiny arms, Triceratops has three horns)
Match a dinosaur name to a picture or model without help
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees pictures of different dinosaurs, can they name at least three — like T. rex, Triceratops, and Stegosaurus?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别并命名常见的著名恐龙物种：霸王龙（Tyrannosaurus rex）、三角龙（Triceratops）、剑龙（Stegosaurus）和腕龙/雷龙（Brachiosaurus/Diplodocus），并描述它们各自的一个基本特征。
evidenceZh: 能够根据图片或模型说出至少四种常见恐龙的名称
描述每种恐龙的一个明显特征（例如：霸王龙的手臂很小，三角龙有三只角）
能够在没有帮助下将恐龙名称与图片或模型相匹配
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到不同恐龙的图片，他们能说出至少三种恐龙的名字吗？比如霸王龙、三角龙和剑龙。

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Fossils & Palaeontologists
topics.description: Understand that fossils are the remains of ancient living things preserved in rock, and that scientists called palaeontologists study fossils to learn about dinosaurs
evidence: Describe a fossil as the remains of a living thing preserved in rock
Name the job of a palaeontologist as someone who studies fossils
Identify examples of fossils: bones, teeth, footprints in rock
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} found a fossil-shaped rock on a beach or at a museum, could they explain what a fossil is and who studies them?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解化石是保存在岩石中的古代生物遗骸，并知道被称为古生物学家（palaeontologists）的科学家通过研究化石来了解恐龙。
evidenceZh: 描述化石是保存在岩石中的生物遗骸
说出古生物学家（palaeontologist）的工作是研究化石
识别化石的例子：岩石中的骨骼、牙齿和脚印
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在海滩或博物馆发现一块化石形状的石头，他们能解释什么是化石以及是谁在研究它们吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Plant-Eaters vs Meat-Eaters
topics.description: Sort dinosaurs into plant-eaters (herbivores) and meat-eaters (carnivores) by looking at clues like tooth shape — flat teeth for plants, sharp teeth for meat
evidence: Sort a set of dinosaur pictures or models into herbivore and carnivore groups
Explain that sharp pointed teeth are for tearing meat and flat teeth are for grinding plants
Give an example of one herbivore and one carnivore dinosaur
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you showed {{name}} a picture of a dinosaur's teeth, could they guess whether it ate plants or meat?
topics.descriptionZh: 通过观察牙齿形状等线索，将恐龙分为植食动物（herbivores）和肉食动物（carnivores）——扁平的牙齿用于咀嚼植物，锋利的牙齿用于撕裂肉类
evidenceZh: 将一组恐龙图片或模型分类为植食动物和肉食动物组
解释尖锐的牙齿用于撕裂肉类，扁平的牙齿用于研磨植物
举出一个植食恐龙和一个肉食恐龙的例子
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你给 {{name}} 看一张恐龙牙齿的图片，他们能猜出这只恐龙是吃植物还是吃肉吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Real Dinosaurs vs Fiction
topics.description: Distinguish real dinosaurs from fictional or commonly confused creatures — pterosaurs (flying reptiles) and plesiosaurs (marine reptiles) were not dinosaurs, and movie dinosaurs are not always accurate
evidence: State that pterosaurs could fly but were not dinosaurs
State that plesiosaurs lived in the sea but were not dinosaurs
Identify at least one way a movie or cartoon dinosaur differs from the real animal
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a flying reptile in a dinosaur book, can they tell you it's actually not a dinosaur but a different kind of prehistoric animal?
topics.descriptionZh: 区分真实的恐龙与虚构或常被混淆的生物——翼龙（飞行爬行动物）和蛇颈龙（海洋爬行动物）并不是恐龙，而且电影中的恐龙形象并不总是准确的
evidenceZh: 说明翼龙会飞但并不是恐龙
说明蛇颈龙生活在海洋中但并不是恐龙
指出电影或卡通中的恐龙与真实动物至少一个不同之处
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}在一本恐龙书里看到一种会飞的爬行动物，他们能告诉你它其实不是恐龙，而是另一种史前动物吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Dinosaurs Around the World
topics.description: Understand that different dinosaurs lived on different continents and that fossil discoveries around the world show dinosaurs were a global phenomenon, with some species found only in certain regions
evidence: State that dinosaur fossils have been found on every continent including Antarctica
Name at least one dinosaur discovery location (e.g. T. rex in North America, Velociraptor in Mongolia)
Suggest a reason why the same type of dinosaur is sometimes found on continents now far apart
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you showed {{name}} a world map, could they tell you that dinosaur fossils have been found on every continent — and maybe name a place where a famous dinosaur was discovered?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解不同的恐龙生活在不同的大陆上，并且世界各地的化石发现表明恐龙是一种全球性现象，有些物种仅在特定地区被发现。
evidenceZh: 能够说出在包括南极洲在内的每个大陆都发现了恐龙化石
至少说出一个恐龙发现地点（例如：北美洲的霸王龙 (Tyrannosaurus rex)、蒙古的迅猛龙 (Velociraptor)）
能够推测为什么现在相隔甚远的大陆上有时会发现同一种恐龙
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你给 {{name}} 看一张世界地图，他们能告诉你恐龙化石在每个大陆都有发现吗——也许还能说出一个著名恐龙的发现地？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Fossilised Dinosaur Dung
topics.description: Describe what coprolites are (fossilised dinosaur dung) and how palaeontologists analyse them to discover what dinosaurs ate, including plant fragments, bones, and seeds
evidence: Define a coprolite as fossilised dung (animal droppings preserved as rock)
Explain that scientists cut coprolites open to find plant seeds, bone fragments, or fish scales inside
State one example of what coprolite contents reveal about a dinosaur's diet
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know what a coprolite is? Can they explain — with a giggle — how fossilised poo helps scientists figure out what a dinosaur ate?
topics.descriptionZh: 介绍什么是粪化石（coprolites，即石化的恐龙粪便），以及古生物学家如何对其进行分析，从而发现恐龙的食性，包括其中包含的植物碎片、骨骼和种子。
evidenceZh: 将粪化石定义为石化的粪便（保存为岩石状的动物排泄物）
解释科学家们如何切开粪化石，以在里面寻找植物种子、骨骼碎片或鱼鳞
举一个例子，说明粪化石的内容物能揭示关于恐龙饮食的什么信息
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}知道什么是粪化石（coprolite）吗？他们能否带着咯咯的笑声，解释石化的便便如何帮助科学家弄清楚恐龙吃了什么？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Fossils Reveal Ancient Environments
topics.description: Understand that fossils tell us not only about ancient animals but also about ancient environments — for example, marine fossils found on a mountaintop show that area was once underwater
evidence: Give an example of a fossil that reveals a past environment different from today's
Explain that finding marine fossils inland means that area was once covered by sea
State that plant fossils can show whether an area was once a forest, desert, or swamp
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that seashell fossils were found on a mountain, could they explain what that tells us about what the area used to be like?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解化石不仅能告诉我们关于古代动物的信息，还能揭示古代环境——例如，在山顶发现海洋化石（marine fossils）表明该地区曾经在水下。
evidenceZh: 举出一个化石揭示过去环境与今天不同的例子
解释在内陆发现海洋化石意味着该地区曾经被海水覆盖
说明植物化石（plant fossils）可以显示一个地区曾经是森林、沙漠还是沼泽
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}听说在山上发现了贝壳化石，他们能解释这告诉我们该地区过去的环境是什么样的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How Fossils Form
topics.description: Explain in simple terms how fossils form: an organism dies and is quickly buried in sediment; over millions of years minerals replace the remains and the sediment turns to rock, preserving the shape
evidence: Describe the basic sequence: organism dies, buried in sediment, minerals replace remains over time
Explain why fossilisation is rare — most organisms decompose before being buried
Use the words 'sediment', 'minerals', and 'rock' correctly when explaining
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} made a salt-dough fossil at school, could they explain how real fossils form underground over millions of years?
topics.descriptionZh: 用简单的语言解释化石是如何形成的：生物死后被迅速掩埋在沉积物（sediment）中；经过数百万年，矿物质（minerals）替换了遗骸，沉积物变成了岩石（rock），从而保留了其形状。
evidenceZh: 描述基本过程：生物死亡，被掩埋在沉积物（sediment）中，随着时间的推移，矿物质（minerals）替换了遗骸。
解释为什么化石形成很罕见——大多数生物在被掩埋前就已经分解了。
在解释时正确使用“沉积物（sediment）”、“矿物质（minerals）”和“岩石（rock）”这几个词。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}在学校用盐面团制作了一个化石，他们能解释真实的化石是如何在地下经过数百万年形成的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Mary Anning, Fossil Hunter
topics.description: Know who Mary Anning was — a pioneering fossil hunter from Lyme Regis, England, who discovered ichthyosaur and plesiosaur skeletons in the early 1800s and contributed to our understanding of prehistoric life
evidence: State that Mary Anning lived in England in the early 1800s and hunted for fossils along the coast
Name at least one of her major discoveries (ichthyosaur or plesiosaur)
Explain why her work was important — she helped scientists understand that extinct creatures once lived on Earth
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} heard of Mary Anning? Can they tell you who she was and why she was important to the study of fossils?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解玛丽·安宁是谁——她是一位来自英国莱姆里吉斯的先驱化石猎人，在19世纪初发现了鱼龙（ichthyosaur）和蛇颈龙（plesiosaur）的骨骼，为我们理解史前生命做出了贡献。
evidenceZh: 说明玛丽·安宁生活在19世纪初的英格兰，并沿着海岸寻找化石
说出她至少一项重大发现（鱼龙或蛇颈龙）
解释她的工作为何重要——她帮助科学家认识到地球上曾经生活过已经灭绝的生物
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 听说过玛丽·安宁吗？他们能告诉你她是谁以及她为什么对化石研究很重要吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Reading Dinosaur Trackways
topics.description: Use dinosaur trackways (fossilised footprints) to make inferences about a dinosaur's size, speed, and behaviour — widely spaced prints suggest running, closely spaced suggest walking
evidence: Explain that larger footprints generally mean a larger dinosaur
Compare spacing between prints to infer walking versus running
Suggest what a set of parallel trackways might mean (e.g. dinosaurs travelling in a group)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a line of dinosaur footprints at a museum, could they figure out whether the dinosaur was walking or running based on how far apart the prints are?
topics.descriptionZh: 利用恐龙足迹（化石脚印）来推断恐龙的体型、速度和行为——足迹间距较大通常意味着恐龙在奔跑，间距较小则说明在行走。
evidenceZh: 解释较大的足迹通常意味着恐龙的体型更大
通过比较足迹之间的间距来推断恐龙是在行走还是在奔跑
推测一组平行的足迹可能意味着什么（例如：恐龙成群结队地行走）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在博物馆看到一排恐龙足迹，他们能根据足迹之间的距离来判断恐龙是在行走还是在奔跑吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Mesozoic Era
topics.description: Place the three periods of the Mesozoic Era — Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous — in order and understand that different dinosaurs lived in different periods, not all at the same time
evidence: List Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous in the correct chronological order
Assign at least one well-known dinosaur to the correct period
Explain that millions of years separated these periods and different species lived in each
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that T. rex and Stegosaurus didn't actually live at the same time — and can they name the three dinosaur time periods in order?
topics.descriptionZh: 将中生代的三个时期——三叠纪 (Triassic)、侏罗纪 (Jurassic) 和白垩纪 (Cretaceous)——按正确顺序排列，并理解不同的恐龙生活在不同的时期，而不是所有恐龙都生活在同一时间。
evidenceZh: 按正确的时间顺序列出三叠纪、侏罗纪和白垩纪
将至少一种著名的恐龙归入其正确的生存时期
解释这些时期之间相隔数百万年，并且每个时期都生活着不同的物种
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否知道霸王龙 (T. rex) 和剑龙 (Stegosaurus) 实际上并没有生活在同一时代——并且他们能否按顺序说出这三个恐龙时期？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Types of Fossils
topics.description: Distinguish body fossils (preserved bones, teeth, shells) from trace fossils (footprints, trackways, eggs, burrows, coprolites) and explain what each type can tell scientists
evidence: Sort examples into body fossils (bones, teeth, shells) and trace fossils (footprints, eggs, dung)
Explain that body fossils show what an animal looked like physically
Explain that trace fossils show how an animal behaved — how it moved, what it ate, where it nested
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a dinosaur footprint in rock at a museum, could they explain how it's different from a fossil bone and what scientists can learn from it?
topics.descriptionZh: 区分实体化石（保存的骨骼、牙齿、贝壳）与遗迹化石（脚印、足迹、蛋、洞穴、粪化石），并解释每种化石能告诉科学家什么信息。
evidenceZh: 将示例分为实体化石（骨骼、牙齿、贝壳）和遗迹化石（脚印、蛋、粪便）
解释实体化石展示了动物生前的身体外貌
解释遗迹化石展示了动物的行为方式——如何移动、吃什么、在哪里筑巢
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在博物馆看到岩石中的恐龙脚印，他们能解释这与化石骨骼有何不同，以及科学家能从中了解到什么吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Fossils as Evidence
topics.description: Analyse and interpret data from fossils to provide evidence of organisms and environments that existed long ago
evidence: Explain that fossils are preserved remains or traces of organisms that lived long ago
Use fossil evidence to make inferences about past organisms and their environments
Describe how comparing fossils with living organisms helps us understand how life has changed
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a fossil of a fish in a rock on a hillside, can they explain that the area must have been underwater millions of years ago?
topics.descriptionZh: 分析和解读化石数据，为远古时期存在的生物和环境提供证据
evidenceZh: 解释化石是远古生物遗留下来的保存完好的遗骸或痕迹
利用化石证据对过去的生物及其生存环境进行合理推断
描述将化石与现存生物进行比较，如何帮助我们理解生命是如何演变的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在山坡的岩石中发现了一块鱼类化石，他们能解释出这片区域在数百万年前一定是在水下吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Birds Evolved from Dinosaurs
topics.description: Understand that modern birds evolved from a group of small feathered theropod dinosaurs, using evidence such as the fossil Archaeopteryx, feathered dinosaur fossils from China, and shared skeletal features
evidence: State that birds evolved from small theropod dinosaurs
Name Archaeopteryx or Chinese feathered dinosaurs as key fossil evidence
List at least two features birds share with theropods (e.g. hollow bones, wishbone, three-toed feet)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why scientists say birds are actually living dinosaurs — and point to evidence like feathered dinosaur fossils?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解现代鸟类是由一群长有羽毛的小型兽脚类恐龙（theropod dinosaurs）演化而来的，并利用始祖鸟（Archaeopteryx）化石、中国发现的带羽毛恐龙化石以及共同的骨骼特征等证据来认识这一过程。
evidenceZh: 说明鸟类是由小型兽脚类恐龙（theropod dinosaurs）演化而来的
说出始祖鸟（Archaeopteryx）或中国发现的带羽毛恐龙作为关键的化石证据
列出鸟类与兽脚类恐龙共有的至少两个特征（例如：中空骨、叉骨、三趾足）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能解释为什么科学家说鸟类实际上是活着的恐龙，并指出带羽毛恐龙化石等证据吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Changing Scientific Knowledge
topics.description: Evaluate competing scientific explanations about dinosaurs by weighing fossil evidence — understanding that scientific knowledge changes as new fossils are discovered and new methods of analysis are developed
evidence: Give an example of a scientific idea about dinosaurs that changed when new evidence was found
Explain that different scientists may interpret the same fossil evidence differently
State that the best scientific explanation is the one supported by the most evidence from multiple sources
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read two different explanations for why dinosaurs went extinct, could they discuss what evidence supports each idea and why scientists sometimes change their minds?
topics.descriptionZh: 通过权衡化石证据来评估关于恐龙的不同科学解释——理解科学知识会随着新化石的发现以及新分析方法的发展而不断更新
evidenceZh: 举例说明一个关于恐龙的科学观点在发现新证据后发生了怎样的改变
解释不同的科学家可能会对相同的化石证据做出不同的解读
说明最合理的科学解释是得到多个来源的充足证据支持的那个
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}阅读了两种关于恐龙灭绝原因的不同解释，他们能否讨论支持每种观点的证据，以及科学家为什么有时会改变观点？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Dinosaur Hip Groups
topics.description: Classify dinosaurs into the two major groups based on hip structure: Saurischia (lizard-hipped, including theropods and sauropods) and Ornithischia (bird-hipped, including Triceratops and Stegosaurus)
evidence: Name the two major dinosaur groups: Saurischia and Ornithischia
Explain the difference is based on hip bone structure (lizard-hipped vs bird-hipped)
Correctly classify at least two dinosaurs into each group (e.g. T. rex = Saurischia, Triceratops = Ornithischia)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that scientists divide dinosaurs into two big groups based on their hip bones — and tell you which group includes T. rex?
topics.descriptionZh: 根据骨盆结构将恐龙分为两大主要类群：蜥臀目（Saurischia，骨盆类似蜥蜴，包括兽脚亚目和蜥脚亚目）和鸟臀目（Ornithischia，骨盆类似鸟类，包括三角龙和剑龙）。
evidenceZh: 说出恐龙的两大主要类群：蜥臀目（Saurischia）和鸟臀目（Ornithischia）
解释分类的区别基于骨盆骨骼结构（类似蜥蜴的骨盆与类似鸟类的骨盆）
将至少两种恐龙正确分类到对应的类群中（例如：霸王龙 = 蜥臀目，三角龙 = 鸟臀目）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释科学家是如何根据骨盆骨骼将恐龙分为两大类群的，并告诉你霸王龙属于哪个类群？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How Palaeontologists Work
topics.description: Describe how palaeontologists work in the field and lab: prospecting for exposed fossils, careful excavation with hand tools, plaster jacketing for transport, preparation in the lab, and scientific description and publication
evidence: List the main stages: prospecting, excavation, jacketing, transport, preparation, study, display
Explain why careful excavation with small tools is necessary to avoid damaging the fossil
Describe plaster jacketing as wrapping fossils in plaster for safe transport to a lab
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the steps a palaeontologist goes through from first spotting a fossil in a cliff to it ending up on display in a museum?
topics.nameZh: 古生物学家是如何工作的
topics.descriptionZh: 描述古生物学家在野外和实验室的工作方式：寻找裸露的化石、使用手工工具小心挖掘、制作石膏包（plaster jacketing）以便运输、在实验室进行化石清修（preparation）、以及进行科学描述和发表成果。
evidenceZh: 列出主要阶段：勘探（prospecting）、挖掘（excavation）、制作石膏包（jacketing）、运输（transport）、清修（preparation）、研究（study）、展示（display）
解释为什么必须使用小工具小心挖掘，以避免损坏化石
描述制作石膏包（plaster jacketing）是指用石膏包裹化石，以便安全运输到实验室
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否描述古生物学家从最初在岩壁上发现化石，到最终将其展示在博物馆里所经历的各个步骤？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Palaeoart & Speculation
topics.description: Understand that palaeoart — scientific illustrations and models of dinosaurs — is based on fossil evidence but involves informed speculation about skin colour, feathers, and soft tissues that don't usually fossilise
evidence: Explain that bones and teeth are known from fossils but skin colour and soft tissues usually are not
State that recent discoveries of preserved skin impressions and feather fossils have improved reconstructions
Give an example of how our picture of a dinosaur has changed over time (e.g. feathered vs scaly Velociraptor)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} understand that pictures of dinosaurs are educated guesses? Can they explain what parts are based on evidence and what parts scientists have to imagine?
topics.nameZh: 古生物艺术 (Palaeoart) 与科学推测 (Speculation)
topics.descriptionZh: 了解古生物艺术（恐龙的科学插图和模型）是基于化石证据的，但也包含对通常不会形成化石的皮肤颜色、羽毛和软组织的有依据的推测。
evidenceZh: 解释骨骼和牙齿可以通过化石得知，但皮肤颜色和软组织通常无法形成化石。
说明近期发现的保存完好的皮肤印痕和羽毛化石改善了恐龙的复原工作。
举例说明我们对某种恐龙的认知是如何随时间变化的（例如，长羽毛的伶盗龙 (Velociraptor) 与长鳞片的伶盗龙）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否理解恐龙的图片是基于科学依据的推测？他们能否解释哪些部分是基于证据的，哪些部分是科学家们必须想象出来的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Reading Cladograms
topics.description: Read and create simple cladograms (branching diagrams) that show how groups of dinosaurs are related based on shared features, understanding that species sharing more features are more closely related
evidence: Explain that a cladogram shows evolutionary relationships based on shared features
Read a simple cladogram to identify which two dinosaurs share the most recent common ancestor
Add a new species to a partially completed cladogram based on its listed features
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a branching tree diagram showing dinosaur relationships, could they explain which dinosaurs are most closely related by looking at where the branches split?
topics.descriptionZh: 阅读并绘制简单的分支图（Branching diagrams），展示恐龙类群如何基于共同特征相互关联，理解拥有更多共同特征的物种亲缘关系更近
evidenceZh: 解释分支图（Cladogram）展示了基于共同特征的进化关系
阅读简单的分支图，找出哪两种恐龙拥有最近的共同祖先（Common ancestor）
根据列出的特征，将新物种添加到未完成的分支图中
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到一张展示恐龙关系的分支树图，他们能通过观察树枝的分叉点来解释哪些恐龙的亲缘关系最近吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rock Layers & Relative Dating
topics.description: Understand that rock layers (strata) form in sequence with the oldest at the bottom and the youngest at the top, and that fossils found in deeper layers are older — this is the principle of relative dating
evidence: Explain that sedimentary rock forms in layers with the oldest at the bottom
Use a diagram of rock strata to determine which fossil is older based on its position
Define relative dating as working out the age of something by comparing its position in rock layers
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a cliff with layers of rock, could they explain that the bottom layers are the oldest and that fossils found deeper down lived longer ago?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解岩层（地层，strata）是按顺序形成的，最古老的在底部，最年轻的在顶部，并且在更深层发现的化石更古老——这就是相对定年的原理。
evidenceZh: 解释沉积岩（sedimentary rock）是一层层形成的，最古老的岩层在最底部
使用岩层示意图，根据化石所在的位置来判断哪个化石更古老
将相对定年定义为通过比较某物在岩层中的位置来确定其年龄
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到一座有岩层的悬崖，他们能否解释最底部的岩层最古老，并且在更深处发现的化石生活在更久远的过去？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The K-Pg Extinction Event
topics.description: Describe the Cretaceous–Palaeogene (K-Pg) extinction event approximately 66 million years ago, including the asteroid impact theory and its evidence (iridium layer, Chicxulub crater), and understand that this ended the reign of non-avian dinosaurs
evidence: State that the K-Pg extinction happened about 66 million years ago and wiped out non-avian dinosaurs
Describe the asteroid impact hypothesis and name the Chicxulub crater in Mexico
Explain one piece of evidence: the iridium-rich layer found worldwide in rocks from that time
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what scientists think caused the dinosaurs to go extinct — and describe at least one piece of evidence for the asteroid theory?
topics.nameZh: 白垩纪-古近纪（K-Pg）灭绝事件
topics.descriptionZh: 描述大约6600万年前发生的白垩纪-古近纪（K-Pg）灭绝事件，包括小行星撞击理论及其证据（富铱层、希克苏鲁伯陨石坑），并理解这一事件终结了非鸟恐龙（non-avian dinosaurs）的统治。
evidenceZh: 说明白垩纪-古近纪（K-Pg）灭绝事件发生在大约6600万年前，并导致了非鸟恐龙（non-avian dinosaurs）的灭绝。
描述小行星撞击假说，并指出位于墨西哥的希克苏鲁伯陨石坑（Chicxulub crater）。
解释一项关键证据：在全球范围内该时期岩石中发现的富含铱（iridium）的地层。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释科学家们认为是什么导致了恐龙灭绝，并描述至少一项支持小行星撞击理论的证据？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Life Changed Over Time
topics.description: Recognise that living things have changed over time and that fossils provide information about organisms that inhabited the Earth millions of years ago
evidence: State that living things have changed (evolved) over millions of years
Describe how fossils form and what information they provide about the past
Compare a fossil organism with a modern relative, noting similarities and differences
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that the animals and plants alive today are different from those that lived millions of years ago, and that we know this from fossils?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识到生物随着时间的推移而发生变化，并且化石（fossils）提供了关于数百万年前栖息在地球上的生物（organisms）的信息。
evidenceZh: 说明生物在数百万年间发生了改变（进化，evolved）
描述化石（fossils）是如何形成的，以及它们提供了哪些关于过去的信息
将化石生物（fossil organism）与现代近亲（modern relative）进行比较，指出其相似之处与差异
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释今天存活的动植物与数百万年前的动植物不同，并且我们是通过化石（fossils）了解到这一点的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Dinosaur-to-Bird Transition
topics.description: Trace the evidence for the dinosaur-to-bird transition in depth: feathered theropods from the Liaoning Formation (China), the mix of dinosaur and bird features in Archaeopteryx, and the competing ground-up versus trees-down hypotheses for the origin of flight
evidence: Describes at least three specific feathered theropod fossils (e.g. Microraptor, Anchiornis, Sinosauropteryx) and what each tells us
Describes Archaeopteryx as showing a mix of bird features (feathers, wishbone) and dinosaur features (teeth, clawed wings, long bony tail)
Outlines the ground-up (running and leaping) and trees-down (gliding from trees) hypotheses for flight origin and the evidence supporting each
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was told that a sparrow is technically a living dinosaur, could they explain the chain of fossil evidence that supports this — naming at least one key transitional fossil and describing what makes it part dinosaur, part bird?
topics.descriptionZh: 深入追踪恐龙向鸟类过渡的证据：来自中国辽宁群的带羽毛兽脚类恐龙（feathered theropods），始祖鸟（Archaeopteryx）身上恐龙与鸟类特征的混合，以及关于飞行起源相互竞争的“地起假说”（ground-up）与“树起假说”（trees-down）。
evidenceZh: 描述至少三种具体的带羽毛兽脚类恐龙化石（如小盗龙 Microraptor、近鸟龙 Anchiornis、中华龙鸟 Sinosauropteryx），并说明每种化石揭示了什么信息
描述始祖鸟（Archaeopteryx）如何展示鸟类特征（羽毛、叉骨 wishbone）与恐龙特征（牙齿、带爪的翅膀、长骨质尾巴）的混合
概述飞行起源的“地起假说”（奔跑和跳跃，ground-up）和“树起假说”（从树上滑翔，trees-down），以及支持每种假说的证据
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果告诉 {{name}} 麻雀在生物学上是一种现存的恐龙，他们能否解释支持这一观点的化石证据链——至少命名一种关键的过渡化石，并描述它为何同时具备恐龙和鸟类的特征？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Radiometric Dating
topics.description: Explain how radiometric dating works — radioactive isotopes decay at a known rate (half-life), so measuring the ratio of parent to daughter isotope in a rock or fossil gives an absolute age; distinguish between carbon-14 (useful up to ~50,000 years) and uranium-lead (useful for millions to billions of years)
evidence: Defines half-life as the time for half the radioactive parent isotope to decay to the daughter isotope
Explains that the parent:daughter ratio in a sample gives an estimate of absolute age
Distinguishes carbon-14 (for recent organic material) from uranium-lead or potassium-argon (for deep geological time), explaining why carbon-14 cannot be used for dinosaur bones
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was told a dinosaur bone was dated using uranium-lead radiometric dating, could they explain what that means — what is decaying, why the rate of decay is useful, and roughly why scientists don't use carbon-14 for 70-million-year-old bones?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释放射性测年法的工作原理——放射性同位素 (radioactive isotopes) 以已知速率衰变（即半衰期 (half-life)），因此测量岩石或化石中母体同位素 (parent isotope) 与子体同位素 (daughter isotope) 的比例即可得出绝对年龄 (absolute age)；区分碳-14 (Carbon-14，适用于约5万年以内的样本) 与铀-铅 (Uranium-lead，适用于数百万至数十亿年的样本) 测年法的适用范围。
evidenceZh: 将半衰期 (half-life) 定义为放射性母体同位素衰变一半成为子体同位素所需的时间
解释样本中母体与子体同位素的比例 (parent:daughter ratio) 可用来估算绝对年龄
区分用于近期有机物的碳-14 (Carbon-14) 与用于深地质时代的铀-铅 (Uranium-lead) 或钾-氩 (Potassium-argon) 测年法，并解释为什么碳-14不能用于测定恐龙骨骼的年代
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果告诉 {{name}} 一块恐龙骨骼是用铀-铅 (Uranium-lead) 放射性测年法测定年代的，他们能解释这意味着什么吗——是什么在衰变，为什么衰变速率很有用，以及为什么科学家不对7000万年前的骨骼使用碳-14 (Carbon-14) 测年法？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Mass Extinctions in Earth History
topics.description: Compare the five major mass extinction events in Earth history (End-Ordovician, Late Devonian, End-Permian, End-Triassic, K-Pg), describe proposed kill mechanisms for each (glaciation, oceanic anoxia, volcanic mega-eruptions, asteroid impact), and explain why mass extinctions, while catastrophic, also open ecological space for subsequent evolutionary radiations
evidence: Names all five major mass extinctions in chronological order with approximate dates
Describes the End-Permian extinction as the most severe and links it to the Siberian Traps volcanic eruption and its atmospheric consequences
Explains how each mass extinction was followed by an adaptive radiation — e.g. the K-Pg extinction removing non-avian dinosaurs allowed mammals to diversify and eventually produce humans
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs was actually the fifth mass extinction in Earth history — and describe what happened in the worst one, which killed over 90% of all species?
topics.nameZh: 地球历史上的生物大灭绝 (Mass Extinctions in Earth History)
topics.descriptionZh: 比较地球历史上的五次重大生物大灭绝事件（奥陶纪末期 End-Ordovician、泥盆纪晚期 Late Devonian、二叠纪末期 End-Permian、三叠纪末期 End-Triassic、白垩纪-古近纪 K-Pg），描述每次事件推测的灭绝机制（冰川作用、海洋缺氧、超级火山喷发、小行星撞击），并解释为什么生物大灭绝虽然具有灾难性，但也为随后的进化辐射 (adaptive radiation) 腾出了生态空间。
evidenceZh: 按时间顺序列出所有五次重大生物大灭绝的名称并附带大致年代
描述二叠纪末期大灭绝 (End-Permian) 是最严重的一次，并将其与西伯利亚暗色岩 (Siberian Traps) 火山喷发及其对大气环境的影响联系起来
解释每次大灭绝之后如何伴随着一次适应辐射——例如，白垩纪-古近纪 (K-Pg) 大灭绝消灭了非鸟类恐龙，使得哺乳动物得以多样化并最终演化出人类
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能解释一下导致恐龙灭绝的小行星撞击实际上是地球历史上的第五次生物大灭绝吗？并且能描述一下最严重的那次大灭绝发生了什么吗（那次灭绝导致了超过90%的物种死亡）？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Reconstructing Ancient Ecosystems
topics.description: Reconstruct an ancient ecosystem using multiple independent lines of evidence: isotope analysis of teeth to infer diet and migration, bone histology (growth rings) to estimate age and growth rate, coprolite chemistry for diet, and palaeobotany for habitat — understanding that palaeontology is an evidence-synthesis discipline
evidence: Explains how stable oxygen isotope ratios in teeth shift with geographic location, allowing detection of seasonal migration
Explains how annual growth rings in bone cross-sections reveal growth rate and approximate age at death
Describes how combining evidence from teeth isotopes, coprolites, and fossil plant assemblages builds a richer picture of ancient ecology than any single source alone
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked how scientists know a large dinosaur migrated hundreds of kilometres every year, could they explain what kind of evidence they look for and how they rule out alternative explanations?
topics.descriptionZh: 利用多条独立的证据线索重建古代生态系统：通过牙齿同位素分析（isotope analysis）推断饮食和迁徙，通过骨组织学（bone histology）的生长环估算年龄和生长速率，通过粪化石化学（coprolite chemistry）分析饮食，以及通过古植物学（palaeobotany）研究栖息地——从而理解古生物学是一门证据综合学科。
evidenceZh: 解释牙齿中稳定的氧同位素比率（stable oxygen isotope ratios）如何随地理位置变化，从而检测出季节性迁徙
解释骨骼横截面中的年生长环如何揭示生长速率和死亡时的大致年龄
描述如何将牙齿同位素、粪化石和化石植物组合的证据结合起来，从而构建出比单一来源更丰富的古代生态图景
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 被问到科学家是如何知道大型恐龙每年要迁徙数百公里的，他们能否解释科学家寻找的是哪些证据，以及他们是如何排除其他可能性的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Megafauna Extinction & De-Extinction
topics.description: Evaluate the debate over what drove Pleistocene megafauna to extinction — human overkill, climate change, or a combination — using evidence from fossil records, ancient DNA, and archaeological sites; connect to the present-day sixth mass extinction and consider the ethics and feasibility of de-extinction using ancient DNA
evidence: Summarises the overkill hypothesis (human hunting pressure) and the climate hypothesis (rapid warming) for Pleistocene megafauna extinction, citing specific evidence for each
Explains how ancient DNA sequencing from permafrost-preserved specimens provides information about genetics, diet, and relatedness of extinct species
Evaluates the de-extinction concept — describing what it would take technically and raising at least two substantive scientific or ecological arguments for and against
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that scientists are trying to bring back the woolly mammoth using ancient DNA, could they explain what ancient DNA is, what challenges exist, and why some scientists think reviving extinct species might actually help ecosystems?
topics.nameZh: 巨型动物灭绝与物种“复活”（De-Extinction）
topics.descriptionZh: 探讨是什么导致了更新世（Pleistocene）巨型动物的灭绝——是人类过度捕杀、气候变化，还是两者共同作用？通过学习化石记录、古DNA（ancient DNA）和考古遗址的证据来寻找答案；并将这一话题与当今的第六次生物大灭绝联系起来，思考利用古DNA“复活”灭绝物种的科学可行性与伦理问题。
evidenceZh: 总结导致更新世巨型动物灭绝的“过度捕杀假说”（overkill hypothesis，即人类的狩猎压力）和“气候变化假说”（climate hypothesis，即气候快速变暖），并列举具体的证据。
解释如何通过对永久冻土中保存的标本进行古DNA（ancient DNA）测序，来获取关于灭绝物种的遗传信息、饮食习性以及物种间亲缘关系的信息。
评估物种“复活”（de-extinction）的概念——描述实现它所需的技术条件，并至少提出两个支持或反对该概念的科学或生态学实质性论据。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 听说科学家们正试图利用古DNA让猛犸象“复活”，他们能解释什么是古DNA、面临哪些挑战，以及为什么有些科学家认为复活灭绝物种实际上可能对生态系统有帮助吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How Organisms Shape Habitats
topics.description: Construct an argument supported by evidence for how plants and animals can change the environment to meet their needs
evidence: Give at least three examples of organisms changing their environment (beaver dams, bird nests, plant roots breaking rock)
Explain why organisms change their environment (to meet needs for shelter, food, water)
Construct an argument with evidence showing how a specific organism changes its environment
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a beaver builds a dam that changes a river into a pond, or how tree roots can crack rocks apart?
topics.descriptionZh: 运用证据构建论点，说明植物和动物如何改变环境以满足自身需求
evidenceZh: 给出至少三个生物改变环境的例子（如海狸筑坝、鸟类筑巢、植物根系破碎岩石）
解释生物为何改变环境（为了满足对住所、食物和水的需求）
运用证据构建论点，展示某种特定生物如何改变其环境
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释海狸是如何筑坝将河流变成池塘的，或者树根是如何将岩石裂开的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Local weather patterns
topics.description: Use and share observations of local weather conditions to describe patterns over time, recording temperature, rainfall, and other conditions
evidence: Observe and record daily weather conditions (temperature, cloud cover, precipitation, wind)
Identify patterns in weather data over days or weeks
Use observations to make simple predictions about upcoming weather
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} kept a weather diary for a week or more, recording whether it was sunny, rainy, or windy, and noticed any patterns?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用和分享对当地天气状况的观察，以描述随时间变化的模式，记录温度、降雨量和其他状况
evidenceZh: 观察并记录每日天气状况（温度、云量、降水量、风力）
识别数天或数周内天气数据中的模式
利用观察结果对未来天气进行简单预测
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否坚持记录了一周或更长时间的天气日记，记录天气是晴天、雨天还是刮风，并发现了任何天气模式？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Seasonal changes
topics.description: Observe changes across the four seasons and describe weather associated with each season, including how day length varies
evidence: Name the four seasons and describe typical weather for each
Describe how day length changes through the year (longer in summer, shorter in winter)
Give examples of changes in the natural world associated with each season (e.g. leaves, flowers, animal behaviour)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what happens in each season — like leaves falling in autumn, snow in winter — and notice that days are shorter in winter and longer in summer?
topics.descriptionZh: 观察四季的变化，描述每个季节的天气特征，包括白昼长度的变化。
evidenceZh: 说出四季的名称并描述每个季节的典型天气。
描述一年中白昼长度的变化（夏季白天较长，冬季白天较短）。
举例说明每个季节自然界的变化（如树叶、花朵、动物行为等）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否描述每个季节发生的现象——例如秋天落叶、冬天下雪——并注意到冬天白天较短而夏天白天较长？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Evaporation and condensation
topics.description: Name and use vocabulary for the water cycle — evaporation, condensation, precipitation, collection, transpiration, water vapour, runoff, groundwater — and describe each stage of the cycle using these terms in the correct sequence
evidence: Describe the complete water cycle using at least four correct technical terms in the right order
Distinguish 'evaporation' from 'condensation' and explain where each occurs in the water cycle
Use 'water vapour' and 'precipitation' correctly in descriptions of weather and the water cycle
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain where the puddle goes after it stops raining — using words like 'evaporation' or 'water vapour' rather than just 'it dries up'?
topics.descriptionZh: 说出并使用水循环的专业词汇——蒸发 (evaporation)、凝结 (condensation)、降水 (precipitation)、汇集 (collection)、蒸腾 (transpiration)、水蒸气 (water vapour)、地表径流 (runoff)、地下水 (groundwater)——并按正确顺序使用这些术语描述水循环的每个阶段。
evidenceZh: 使用至少四个正确的专业术语按正确顺序描述完整的水循环
区分“蒸发 (evaporation)”与“凝结 (condensation)”，并解释它们各自发生在水循环的哪个阶段
在描述天气和水循环时，正确使用“水蒸气 (water vapour)”和“降水 (precipitation)”
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释雨后水坑里的水去哪儿了——使用“蒸发 (evaporation)”或“水蒸气 (water vapour)”等词汇，而不是仅仅说“水干了”？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How fossils form
topics.description: Describe in simple terms how fossils are formed when things that have lived are trapped within rock over millions of years
evidence: Describe the basic process: organism dies, gets buried in mud/sand, layers build up, material turns to rock over millions of years
Explain that the organism's shape is preserved as a fossil within the rock
Give examples of common fossils (shells, bones, leaf imprints, footprints)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a shell or bone from an ancient creature ended up preserved inside a rock?
topics.descriptionZh: 用简单易懂的语言描述化石是如何形成的：当曾经生活过的生物被包裹在岩石中，经过数百万年的时间，就会形成化石。
evidenceZh: 描述基本过程：生物死亡后，被埋在泥土或沙子里，沉积层不断堆积，经过数百万年的时间，这些物质变成了岩石。
解释生物的形状是如何作为化石保存在岩石中的。
举出常见化石的例子（如贝壳、骨骼、树叶印痕、脚印）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释远古生物的贝壳或骨骼是如何最终保存在岩石中的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Preventing Erosion
topics.description: Compare multiple solutions designed to slow or prevent wind or water from changing the shape of the land
evidence: Describe how wind and water can change the shape of land (erosion)
Compare at least two design solutions for reducing erosion (e.g. retaining walls, plants, windbreaks)
Evaluate which solution works best based on evidence from tests or observations
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a sandcastle being washed away by waves, can they think of ways to protect it — like building a wall or planting grass to hold the sand?
topics.descriptionZh: 比较多种旨在减缓或防止风或水改变地形（侵蚀）的解决方案。
evidenceZh: 描述风和水是如何改变地形（侵蚀）的。
比较至少两种减少侵蚀的设计方案（例如：挡土墙、种植植物、防风林）。
根据测试或观察的证据，评估哪种方案的效果最好。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到沙堡被海浪冲毁，他们能想出保护它的方法吗——比如筑起一道墙或者种草来固定沙子？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Properties of materials
topics.description: Compare and group different kinds of rocks based on their appearance and simple physical properties such as hardness, texture, and colour
evidence: Describe at least three observable properties of rocks: hardness, texture, colour, grain size
Sort a collection of rocks into groups based on chosen properties
Compare two rocks and describe how their properties differ
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} examine a collection of rocks and sort them by whether they're hard or crumbly, rough or smooth, and light or dark?
topics.descriptionZh: 根据岩石的外观及其硬度（hardness）、质地（texture）和颜色（colour）等简单物理性质，对各类岩石进行比较与分类。
evidenceZh: 描述岩石至少三种可观察的性质：硬度、质地、颜色和颗粒大小（grain size）
根据选定的性质将收集到的岩石进行分组
比较两块岩石，并描述它们的性质差异
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否观察一组岩石，并根据它们是坚硬还是易碎、粗糙还是光滑、颜色浅还是深来进行分类？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rocks and soil
topics.description: Recognise that soils are made from rocks and organic matter, and that different soils have different properties
evidence: State that soil is a mixture of broken-down rock particles and decomposed organic matter (humus)
Compare at least two types of soil (sandy, clay, loam) and describe their different properties
Explain that soil formation takes a very long time as rocks gradually break down
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that soil isn't just dirt — it's made from tiny broken-down bits of rock mixed with dead leaves and other organic material?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识到土壤是由岩石和有机物质组成的，并且不同的土壤具有不同的特性
evidenceZh: 说明土壤是风化岩石颗粒和分解的有机物质（腐殖质 humus）的混合物
比较至少两种类型的土壤（沙质土 sandy soil、黏土 clay、壤土 loam）并描述它们的不同特性
解释土壤的形成需要很长的时间，因为岩石是逐渐风化破碎的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释土壤不仅仅是泥土——它是由微小的风化岩石碎屑与枯叶及其他有机物质混合而成的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Shapes of land and water
topics.description: Develop a model to represent the shapes and kinds of land (mountains, valleys, plains) and bodies of water (rivers, lakes, oceans) in an area
evidence: Name and describe at least four types of landforms (mountain, valley, plain, hill, cliff)
Name and describe at least three types of water bodies (river, lake, ocean, pond)
Create or interpret a simple model or map showing land and water features of an area
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} look at a map or build a model showing mountains, rivers, and oceans, and explain what each type of land or water feature is?
topics.descriptionZh: 制作模型来表现特定区域内陆地（山脉、山谷、平原）和水体（河流、湖泊、海洋）的形状与种类。
evidenceZh: 命名并描述至少四种地形（山地、山谷、平原、丘陵、悬崖）
命名并描述至少三种水体（河流、湖泊、海洋、池塘）
制作或解读展示某区域陆地与水体特征的简单模型或地图
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否观察地图或制作一个展示山脉、河流和海洋的模型，并解释每种陆地或水体特征分别是什么？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Where water is found on Earth
topics.description: Identify where water is found on Earth and understand that water can exist as solid (ice) or liquid, recognising water in oceans, rivers, glaciers, and underground
evidence: List where water is found on Earth: oceans, rivers, lakes, glaciers, underground, atmosphere
Explain that water exists as liquid (rivers, oceans) and solid (ice, glaciers, snow)
Recognise that most of Earth's water is in the oceans
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name the different places water is found on Earth — in oceans, rivers, ice caps, and even underground — and explain that ice is just frozen water?
topics.descriptionZh: 找出地球上哪里有水，并了解水可以以固体（冰）或液体的形式存在，认识海洋、河流、冰川和地下的水
evidenceZh: 列出地球上哪里有水：海洋、河流、湖泊、冰川、地下、大气层
解释水以液体（河流、海洋）和固体（冰、冰川、雪）的形式存在
认识到地球上大部分的水都在海洋中
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能说出水在地球上的不同分布地点——如海洋、河流、冰盖，甚至地下——并解释冰只是冻结的水吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Seasonal changes (age 8+)
topics.description: Represent data in tables and graphical displays to describe typical weather conditions expected during a particular season
evidence: Collect and organise weather data in a table (temperature, precipitation, cloud cover)
Create a graphical display (bar chart, pictogram) showing weather patterns for a season
Use the data to describe typical weather conditions for that season and compare with other seasons
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} collect weather data over several weeks, put it in a chart, and use it to describe what weather is typical for that time of year?
topics.descriptionZh: 在表格和图形展示（graphical displays）中表示数据，以描述特定季节预期的典型天气状况
evidenceZh: 在表格中收集和整理天气数据（温度(temperature)、降水量(precipitation)、云量(cloud cover)）
制作图形展示（条形图(bar chart)、象形统计图(pictogram)）以显示一个季节的天气模式
使用数据描述该季节的典型天气状况，并与其他季节进行比较
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否在几周内收集天气数据，将其制成图表，并用来描述一年中这个时候的典型天气？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Weather vs climate
topics.description: Obtain and combine information to describe climates in different regions of the world, distinguishing between weather and climate
evidence: Define weather as day-to-day conditions and climate as the long-term pattern of weather in an area
Describe at least three different climate types (tropical, temperate, polar, desert) with examples
Explain that climate varies by region due to factors like distance from the equator
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between weather and climate, and describe why the Arctic is always cold while tropical areas are always warm?
topics.descriptionZh: 获取并整合信息以描述世界不同地区的气候，区分天气与气候
evidenceZh: 将天气定义为日常的大气状况，将气候定义为一个地区长期的天气模式
描述至少三种不同的气候类型（如热带、温带、极地、沙漠气候）并举例说明
解释气候因地区而异，其原因包括距离赤道的远近等因素
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释天气和气候的区别，并描述为什么北极总是很冷，而热带地区总是很暖和？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Erosion and weathering
topics.description: Make observations and measurements to provide evidence of the effects of weathering or the rate of erosion by water, ice, wind, or vegetation
evidence: Define weathering (breaking down of rock in place) and erosion (movement of broken rock/soil)
Describe the effects of at least three agents of weathering/erosion: water, ice, wind, vegetation
Provide evidence from observations showing how weathering or erosion has changed a landscape
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} look at a crumbling cliff or a river bank and explain how water, wind, or ice has slowly worn away the rock or soil over time?
topics.descriptionZh: 通过观察和测量，提供水、冰、风或植物对风化影响或侵蚀速率的证据。
evidenceZh: 定义风化（岩石在原地的破碎）和侵蚀（破碎岩石/土壤的移动）
描述至少三种风化/侵蚀因素（水、冰、风、植物）的影响
提供观察证据，说明风化或侵蚀如何改变了地貌
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否观察崩塌的悬崖或河岸，并解释水、风或冰是如何随着时间的推移慢慢侵蚀掉岩石或土壤的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Finding patterns in data
topics.description: Analyse and interpret data from maps to describe patterns of Earth's features, recognising that many features result from processes that occur over long periods
evidence: Use a map to identify patterns in the location of mountains, rivers, lakes, and other features
Describe patterns observed (e.g. mountains in chains, rivers flow from high to low ground)
Explain that Earth's features result from processes like erosion, volcanic activity, and plate movement over long periods
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} look at a map and notice patterns like mountains running in lines, rivers flowing to the sea, or deserts clustered near the equator?
topics.descriptionZh: 分析和解读地图数据，描述地球表面特征的分布规律，并认识到许多特征是经过漫长时期的地质过程形成的。
evidenceZh: 使用地图识别山脉、河流、湖泊和其他地理特征的位置规律
描述观察到的规律（例如：山脉呈链条状分布，河流从高处流向低处）
解释地球特征是由侵蚀、火山活动和板块运动等经过漫长时期的过程形成的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否观察地图并注意到山脉呈线状延伸、河流汇入海洋或沙漠集中在赤道附近等规律？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Types of rocks
topics.description: Use vocabulary for Earth's geological processes and rock types — igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic, erosion, weathering, deposition, fossil, sediment, strata, permeable, impermeable — and apply these when explaining how rocks form and how landscapes change over time
evidence: Correctly classify igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks and explain in one sentence how each type forms
Use 'erosion', 'weathering', and 'deposition' correctly as three distinct stages in a sequence
Explain how fossils form using 'sediment' and 'sedimentary rock' correctly
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain the difference between a rock being weathered and being eroded — those are actually two different things?
topics.descriptionZh: 运用地球地质过程和岩石类型的词汇——火成岩（igneous）、沉积岩（sedimentary）、变质岩（metamorphic）、侵蚀（erosion）、风化（weathering）、沉积作用（deposition）、化石（fossil）、沉积物（sediment）、地层（strata）、透水性（permeable）、不透水性（impermeable）——并应用这些词汇解释岩石的形成过程以及地貌随时间的变化。
evidenceZh: 正确分类火成岩（igneous）、沉积岩（sedimentary）和变质岩（metamorphic），并用一句话解释每种岩石的形成过程。
按顺序正确地将风化（weathering）、侵蚀（erosion）和沉积作用（deposition）作为三个不同的阶段来使用。
使用沉积物（sediment）和沉积岩（sedimentary rock）正确解释化石的形成过程。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释一下岩石被风化和被侵蚀之间的区别吗？这实际上是两件不同的事情。

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Earth's atmosphere
topics.description: Develop a model to describe ways the geosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere, and atmosphere interact as connected Earth systems
evidence: Name the four Earth systems: geosphere (rock/land), hydrosphere (water), atmosphere (air), biosphere (living things)
Describe at least two interactions between different Earth systems with examples
Create or interpret a model showing how a change in one system affects others
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how rain (atmosphere) falls on mountains (geosphere), flows into rivers (hydrosphere), and provides water for plants and animals (biosphere)?
topics.descriptionZh: 建立模型，描述岩石圈（geosphere）、生物圈（biosphere）、水圈（hydrosphere）和大气圈（atmosphere）作为相互联系的地球系统是如何相互作用的。
evidenceZh: 说出四个地球系统的名称：岩石圈（geosphere/岩石和陆地）、水圈（hydrosphere/水）、大气圈（atmosphere/空气）、生物圈（biosphere/生物）
举例描述不同地球系统之间至少两种相互作用
创建或解释一个模型，展示一个系统的变化如何影响其他系统
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释雨水（大气圈）如何降落在山脉（岩石圈）上，流入河流（水圈），并为动植物（生物圈）提供水分？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rock layers and Earth's history
topics.description: Interpret cross-section diagrams of the Earth's interior, geological strata, and rock cycle; read and label layers (crust, mantle, outer core, inner core); understand that deeper layers in sedimentary sequences are older
evidence: Label the four layers of the Earth on a cross-section diagram using the correct terms
Interpret a diagram of sedimentary rock layers and identify which layer was deposited first
Read a rock cycle diagram and trace the pathway of a rock from igneous to sedimentary to metamorphic
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a cut-away diagram of the Earth, can they point to and name the different layers — and if shown stacked rock layers, can they say which layer formed first?
topics.descriptionZh: 解读地球内部、地质地层和岩石循环的剖面图；识别并标注各圈层（地壳、地幔、外核、内核）；理解在沉积序列中，越深层的岩层年代越久远
evidenceZh: 在剖面图上使用正确的术语标注地球的四个圈层
解读沉积岩层图，并识别出哪一层是最先沉积的
阅读岩石循环图，追踪岩石从火成岩到沉积岩再到变质岩的转化路径
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到一张地球的剖面图，他们能指出并说出不同圈层的名称吗？如果给他们看层层叠放的岩层，他们能说出哪一层最先形成吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Salt Water vs Fresh Water
topics.description: Describe and graph the amounts of salt water and fresh water in various reservoirs to provide evidence about the distribution of water on Earth
evidence: State that about 97% of Earth's water is salt water in the oceans
Describe where fresh water is found: glaciers/ice caps, groundwater, rivers, lakes
Create or interpret a graph showing the relative amounts of salt water vs fresh water
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that most of Earth's water is salty ocean water, and only a tiny fraction is the fresh water we drink, and show this on a graph?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述并绘制不同储水体 (reservoirs) 中咸水和淡水的数量图表，为地球上的水资源分布提供证据。
evidenceZh: 说明地球上约97%的水是海洋中的咸水
描述淡水的分布位置：冰川/冰盖 (glaciers/ice caps)、地下水 (groundwater)、河流和湖泊
绘制或解读展示咸水与淡水相对数量的图表
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释地球上大部分的水是海洋里的咸水，只有极小一部分是我们饮用的淡水，并通过图表展示这一点？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Plants and animals in their habitats
topics.description: Use a model to represent the relationship between the needs of different plants and animals and the places they live, connecting organism needs to habitat features
evidence: Use a simple model (drawing, diagram) to show how a habitat provides what an organism needs
Match at least three organisms to their habitats and explain why each needs that specific place
Describe what would happen if an organism were placed in a habitat that doesn't meet its needs
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a fish needs to live in water but a cactus can live in a desert, by matching what each living thing needs to where it lives?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用模型来表示不同动植物的需求与其居住地之间的关系，将生物需求与栖息地特征联系起来
evidenceZh: 使用简单的模型（绘画、图表）展示栖息地如何提供生物生存所需的条件
将至少三种生物与其栖息地相匹配，并解释为什么每种生物都需要该特定环境
描述如果将生物置于无法满足其需求的栖息地中会发生什么
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否通过将每种生物的需求与其生活环境相匹配，来解释为什么鱼需要生活在水中，而仙人掌可以生活在沙漠中？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Reducing Human Impact
topics.description: Communicate solutions that will reduce the impact of humans on the land, water, air, and other living things in the local environment
evidence: Identify at least three ways humans negatively impact the local environment (litter, pollution, habitat destruction)
Propose at least three solutions to reduce human impact (recycling, reducing waste, conserving water, planting trees)
Explain how each solution helps protect land, water, air, or living things
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} suggest ways people can help the environment — like recycling, not littering, saving water, or planting trees?
topics.descriptionZh: 提出能够减少人类对当地环境中的土地、水、空气及其他生物影响的解决方案
evidenceZh: 识别至少三种人类对当地环境产生负面影响的方式（乱扔垃圾、污染、栖息地破坏）
提出至少三种减少人类影响的解决方案（回收利用、减少浪费、节约用水、植树造林）
解释每种解决方案如何帮助保护土地、水、空气或生物
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否提出人们可以帮助保护环境的方法——例如回收利用、不乱扔垃圾、节约用水或植树造林？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Habitats & Basic Needs
topics.description: Identify that most living things live in habitats to which they are suited and describe how habitats provide for basic needs and how organisms depend on each other
evidence: Define a habitat as a place where an organism lives that provides what it needs
Give examples of how specific habitats meet organisms' needs (e.g. pond provides water and food for frogs)
Describe at least one way organisms in a habitat depend on each other (e.g. bees pollinate flowers, flowers feed bees)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a polar bear lives in the Arctic and not in a desert, and how the animals and plants in a habitat help each other?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识到大多数生物都生活在适合它们的栖息地中，并描述栖息地如何提供基本生存需求，以及生物之间是如何相互依存的。
evidenceZh: 将栖息地（Habitat）定义为生物生活并获取所需资源的地方
举例说明特定的栖息地是如何满足生物需求的（例如：池塘为青蛙提供水和食物）
描述栖息地中生物相互依存的至少一种方式（例如：蜜蜂为花朵传粉，花朵为蜜蜂提供食物）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释为什么北极熊生活在北极而不是沙漠，以及栖息地里的动植物是如何互相帮助的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Habitat Vocabulary
topics.description: Name and use vocabulary for where living things are found — habitat, environment, microhabitat, conditions, woodland, ocean, desert, rainforest, pond — and use terms to describe what animals need to survive: food, water, shelter, space, and suitable conditions
evidence: Match animals to their habitats and explain the match using 'adapted to', 'conditions', or 'shelter'
Correctly use 'habitat' and 'microhabitat' to describe different scales of environment with examples
Name at least three contrasting habitats and describe what makes each distinctive
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a polar bear couldn't survive in a rainforest — using the word 'habitat' or 'conditions' rather than just 'it's too hot'?
topics.descriptionZh: 命名并使用描述生物生存环境的词汇——栖息地（habitat）、环境（environment）、微栖息地（microhabitat）、条件（conditions）、林地（woodland）、海洋（ocean）、沙漠（desert）、雨林（rainforest）、池塘（pond）——并使用术语描述动物生存所需的要素：食物、水、庇护所、空间以及适宜的条件。
evidenceZh: 将动物与其栖息地进行匹配，并使用“适应于”（adapted to）、“条件”（conditions）或“庇护所”（shelter）等词汇解释匹配原因。
正确使用“栖息地”（habitat）和“微栖息地”（microhabitat）并举例描述不同尺度的环境。
说出至少三种截然不同的栖息地，并描述使它们各具特色的因素。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么北极熊无法在雨林中生存——要求使用“栖息地”（habitat）或“条件”（conditions）这样的词汇，而不仅仅是说“太热了”？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Living, Dead & Never Alive
topics.description: Explore and compare the differences between things that are living, dead, and things that have never been alive
evidence: Sort a collection of objects into three groups: living, dead (was once alive), never alive
Give reasons for each sorting decision (e.g. 'the leaf was on a tree so it was alive once')
List characteristics of living things such as growing, breathing, reproducing, and moving
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you show {{name}} a rock, a fallen leaf, and a caterpillar, can they tell you which is alive, which was once alive, and which was never alive?
topics.nameZh: 有生命的、曾存活过的与从未有生命的
topics.descriptionZh: 探索并比较有生命的、已死亡的以及从未有过生命的事物之间的区别
evidenceZh: 将一组物品分为三类：有生命的、曾存活过的（已死亡的）和从未有生命的
说明每个分类的理由（例如：树叶曾长在树上，所以它曾经活过）
列出有生命事物的特征，如生长、呼吸、繁殖和移动
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你给 {{name}} 看一块石头、一片落叶和一条毛毛虫，他们能分辨出哪个是活着的，哪个是曾存活过的，哪个是从未有生命的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Local Plants & Animals
topics.description: Identify and name a variety of plants and animals in their habitats, including microhabitats such as under a log or in a pond
evidence: Name at least three animals and plants found in a specific local habitat
Explain what a microhabitat is (a very small habitat within a larger one)
Describe conditions in a microhabitat (e.g. 'under a stone is damp and dark, woodlice like that')
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you turn over a log in the garden with {{name}}, can they name the little creatures they find and explain why they live there?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别并命名其栖息地中的各种动植物，包括微栖息地（microhabitats），如木头下或池塘里
evidenceZh: 说出在特定本地栖息地中找到的至少三种动物和植物
解释什么是微栖息地（即较大栖息地内的一个非常小的栖息地）
描述微栖息地中的条件（例如：‘石头下面潮湿阴暗，鼠妇喜欢那样的环境’）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你和{{name}}一起在花园里翻开一块木头，他们能说出找到的小生物的名字，并解释它们为什么住在那里吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Simple Food Chains
topics.description: Describe how animals obtain their food from plants and other animals, using the idea of a simple food chain, and identify different sources of food
evidence: Draw a simple food chain with at least three organisms using arrows to show energy flow
Explain that food chains always start with a plant (producer) that makes its own food
Use the terms 'producer' and 'consumer' correctly when describing a food chain
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw a food chain showing how a caterpillar eats a leaf and then a bird eats the caterpillar?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述动物如何从植物和其他动物获取食物，运用简单食物链的概念，并识别不同的食物来源。
evidenceZh: 绘制一条至少包含三种生物（organisms）的简单食物链，使用箭头表示能量流动（energy flow）。
解释食物链总是从能够自己制造食物的植物（生产者，producer）开始。
在描述食物链时，正确使用“生产者”（producer）和“消费者”（consumer）这两个术语。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否画出一条食物链，展示毛毛虫吃树叶，然后小鸟吃掉毛毛虫的过程？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Animal Groups & Survival
topics.description: Construct an argument that some animals form groups that help members survive, such as herds, packs, or colonies
evidence: Give at least two examples of animals that live in groups (e.g. wolves, ants, fish schools)
Explain how group living provides survival advantages (protection, finding food, raising young)
Construct a simple argument with evidence for why a specific animal benefits from group behaviour
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why wolves hunt in packs or why fish swim in schools, and how being in a group helps them survive?
topics.descriptionZh: 构建论点，证明某些动物会形成群体（如兽群 (herds)、狼群 (packs) 或群落 (colonies)）以帮助成员生存。
evidenceZh: 给出至少两个群居动物的例子（例如狼、蚂蚁、鱼群）
解释群居生活如何提供生存优势（如保护自己、寻找食物、抚育后代）
用证据构建一个简单的论点，说明为什么某种特定动物会从群体行为中获益
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么狼要成群结队地狩猎，或者为什么鱼要成群游动，以及群体生活如何帮助它们生存？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Changing Environments
topics.description: Recognise that environments can change and that this can sometimes pose dangers and challenges to living things
evidence: Give at least two examples of environmental changes (natural and human-caused)
Describe how a specific change affects the organisms in that environment
Explain why some organisms may not survive if their environment changes too quickly
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} give examples of how changes like pollution, building, or drought can make it harder for animals and plants to survive?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识到环境会发生变化，并且这些变化有时会给生物带来危险和挑战。
evidenceZh: 给出至少两个环境变化的例子（包括自然原因和人为原因）
描述某种具体的变化如何影响该环境中的生物
解释如果环境变化过快，为什么一些生物可能无法生存
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否举例说明像污染、建筑施工或干旱这样的变化是如何让动植物的生存变得更加困难的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Classification Keys
topics.description: Explore and use classification keys to identify, group, and name living things in local and wider environments
evidence: Follow a branching classification key to identify an unknown organism
Create a simple yes/no classification key for a set of 6-8 organisms
Use a key to identify organisms in the local environment during a field activity
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} use a simple yes/no key chart to work out the name of an insect or plant they've found outside?
topics.descriptionZh: 探索并使用分类检索表（Classification Keys）来识别、分组和命名当地及更广泛环境中的生物。
evidenceZh: 遵循分支分类检索表（Branching classification key）来识别未知的生物体
为6至8种生物创建简单的‘是/否’分类检索表
在实地考察活动中使用检索表识别当地环境中的生物
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否使用简单的‘是/否’检索表来确定他们在户外发现的昆虫或植物的名称？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Ecology Vocabulary
topics.description: Use vocabulary for feeding relationships and ecological roles — producer, consumer, predator, prey, herbivore, carnivore, omnivore, decomposer, food chain, food web, nutrient cycle — and describe how energy and matter flow through ecosystems using these terms
evidence: Construct a food chain correctly using producer, consumer, predator, and prey in the right positions
Distinguish between herbivore, carnivore, and omnivore with correct examples from a given ecosystem
Explain what a decomposer does and why it matters, using the correct vocabulary
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw a food chain from a plant to a top predator and label each animal as a producer, consumer, predator, or prey?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用关于捕食关系和生态角色的词汇——生产者 (producer)、消费者 (consumer)、捕食者 (predator)、猎物 (prey)、草食动物 (herbivore)、肉食动物 (carnivore)、杂食动物 (omnivore)、分解者 (decomposer)、食物链 (food chain)、食物网 (food web)、营养循环 (nutrient cycle)——并运用这些词汇描述能量和物质如何在生态系统中流动。
evidenceZh: 正确使用生产者 (producer)、消费者 (consumer)、捕食者 (predator) 和猎物 (prey) 在正确的位置上构建食物链 (food chain)。
在特定的生态系统中，通过正确的例子区分草食动物 (herbivore)、肉食动物 (carnivore) 和杂食动物 (omnivore)。
使用正确的词汇解释分解者 (decomposer) 的作用及其重要性。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否画出一条从植物到顶级捕食者 (top predator) 的食物链 (food chain)，并将每种动物标记为生产者 (producer)、消费者 (consumer)、捕食者 (predator) 或猎物 (prey)？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Food Chains & Energy Transfer
topics.description: Construct and interpret food chains identifying producers, predators, and prey, and understand energy transfer between trophic levels
evidence: Construct a food chain with at least four organisms, labelling producer, primary consumer, predator
Define producer, predator, and prey with examples
Interpret a given food chain to predict what happens if one organism is removed
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} build a food chain for a woodland and point out which organisms are producers, which are predators, and which are prey?
topics.descriptionZh: 构建并解释食物链，识别生产者（producers）、捕食者（predators）和猎物（prey），并理解营养级（trophic levels）之间的能量传递。
evidenceZh: 构建一条包含至少四种生物的食物链，并标注生产者（producer）、初级消费者（primary consumer）和捕食者（predator）
结合实例定义生产者、捕食者和猎物
解释给定的食物链，并预测如果移除其中一种生物会发生什么
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否为林地构建一条食物链，并指出哪些生物是生产者，哪些是捕食者，哪些是猎物？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Grouping Living Things
topics.description: Recognise that living things can be grouped in a variety of ways based on observable features
evidence: Group a set of organisms using at least two different criteria (e.g. by habitat, by body covering, by diet)
Explain the reasoning behind each grouping choice
Recognise that the same organism can belong to different groups depending on the criteria used
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} sort a set of animals or plants into groups using their own criteria, like 'has wings' or 'lives in water'?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识到可以根据可观察的特征，以多种方式对生物进行分组
evidenceZh: 使用至少两种不同的标准对一组生物进行分组（例如，按栖息地、按体表覆盖物、按食性）
解释每次分组选择背后的理由
认识到同一种生物可以根据所使用的不同标准被归入不同的组
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否使用自己的标准（如“有翅膀”或“生活在水里”）将一组动物或植物进行分组？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Human impact on environments
topics.description: Use vocabulary for human impact on the environment — pollution, habitat destruction, deforestation, biodiversity, conservation, renewable energy, non-renewable energy, fossil fuel, carbon footprint, sustainability, endangered, extinct — and apply these when discussing environmental issues and human choices
evidence: Distinguish between renewable and non-renewable energy sources using the correct terms and give examples of each
Use 'biodiversity' and 'conservation' correctly in discussing why protecting habitats matters
Apply 'carbon footprint' and 'sustainability' correctly in a discussion about everyday human choices
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what a carbon footprint is — not just that it's about pollution, but what it actually measures?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用描述人类对环境影响的词汇——污染 (pollution)、栖息地破坏 (habitat destruction)、森林砍伐 (deforestation)、生物多样性 (biodiversity)、环境保护 (conservation)、可再生能源 (renewable energy)、不可再生能源 (non-renewable energy)、化石燃料 (fossil fuel)、碳足迹 (carbon footprint)、可持续性 (sustainability)、濒危 (endangered)、灭绝 (extinct)——并在讨论环境问题和人类选择时应用这些词汇。
evidenceZh: 使用正确的术语区分可再生能源和不可再生能源，并给出每种能源的例子
在讨论保护栖息地的重要性时，正确使用“生物多样性”和“环境保护”
在讨论日常人类选择时，正确应用“碳足迹”和“可持续性”
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释什么是碳足迹——不仅仅是说它与污染有关，而是说明它实际衡量的是什么？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Reading Food Web Diagrams
topics.description: Read and interpret food web diagrams — identify producers, primary and secondary consumers, and decomposers; trace energy flow along food chains within the web; predict the effect of removing or adding a species
evidence: Identify the producer, herbivore, and carnivore in a food web from a diagram
Trace two food chains through the same food web and identify shared species
Predict what would happen to fox numbers if rabbits were removed from a food web diagram
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is shown a diagram with arrows connecting plants, insects, frogs, and hawks, can they trace which animals eat which and explain what would happen if the frogs disappeared?
topics.descriptionZh: 阅读并解释食物网图解——识别生产者（producers）、初级和次级消费者（primary and secondary consumers）以及分解者（decomposers）；追踪网内食物链的能量流动（energy flow）；预测移除或添加某一物种的影响
evidenceZh: 从图解中识别食物网中的生产者（producer）、食草动物（herbivore）和食肉动物（carnivore）
在同一个食物网中追踪两条食物链，并识别共有物种
预测如果从食物网图解中移除兔子，狐狸的数量会发生什么变化
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果给 {{name}} 展示一个带有连接植物、昆虫、青蛙和老鹰的箭头的图解，他们能否追踪哪些动物吃哪些动物，并解释如果青蛙消失会发生什么？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Animal Life Cycles
topics.description: Describe differences in the life cycles of mammals, amphibians, insects, and birds, comparing metamorphosis with direct development
evidence: Describe the life cycle of a mammal, amphibian, insect, and bird with key stages for each
Compare metamorphosis (complete change of form) with direct development (gradual growth)
Identify which groups undergo metamorphosis and which do not
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a butterfly's life cycle (egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly) is completely different from how a puppy grows into a dog?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述哺乳动物、两栖动物、昆虫和鸟类生命周期的差异，比较变态发育（metamorphosis，形态的完全改变）与直接发育（direct development，逐渐生长）
evidenceZh: 描述哺乳动物、两栖动物、昆虫和鸟类的生命周期及各自的关键阶段
比较变态发育（metamorphosis，形态的完全改变）与直接发育（direct development，逐渐生长）
识别哪些动物类群经历变态发育，哪些不经历
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释蝴蝶的生命周期（卵、毛毛虫、蛹、蝴蝶）与小狗长成成年犬的过程有何根本不同吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Plant & Animal Reproduction
topics.description: Describe the life process of reproduction in some plants and animals, including sexual and asexual reproduction in plants
evidence: Describe sexual reproduction in plants: pollination, fertilisation, seed production
Give examples of asexual reproduction in plants: runners (strawberries), bulbs, cuttings
Compare reproduction in egg-laying animals (birds, frogs) vs live-bearing mammals
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain different ways plants reproduce — not just from seeds but also from cuttings or runners — and how animals reproduce by having babies or laying eggs?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述部分动植物的繁殖生命过程，包括植物的有性繁殖（sexual reproduction）和无性繁殖（asexual reproduction）。
evidenceZh: 描述植物的有性繁殖（sexual reproduction）：传粉（pollination）、受精（fertilisation）、产生种子（seed production）
举例说明植物的无性繁殖（asexual reproduction）：匍匐茎（runners，如草莓）、鳞茎（bulbs）、扦插（cuttings）
比较卵生动物（egg-laying animals，如鸟类、青蛙）与胎生哺乳动物（live-bearing mammals）的繁殖方式
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释植物不同的繁殖方式——不仅包括通过种子繁殖，还包括通过扦插（cuttings）或匍匐茎（runners）繁殖——以及动物如何通过产卵或生育幼崽来繁殖？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Classifying Organisms
topics.description: Describe how living things are classified into broad groups (micro-organisms, plants, animals) according to common observable characteristics, similarities, and differences
evidence: Name the broad classification groups: micro-organisms, plants, animals (and fungi if known)
Describe observable characteristics used for classification (e.g. plants make own food, animals move and eat)
Give examples of organisms in each group, including micro-organisms like bacteria
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the big groups that scientists sort all living things into — like plants, animals, and tiny micro-organisms — and give examples of each?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述生物是如何根据共同的可观察特征、相似点和不同点，被划分到大的类别中（如微生物 (micro-organisms)、植物 (plants) 和动物 (animals)）的。
evidenceZh: 说出广泛的分类群体：微生物 (micro-organisms)、植物 (plants)、动物 (animals)（如果知道的话，还包括真菌 (fungi)）
描述用于分类的可观察特征（例如，植物自己制造食物，动物会移动和进食）
给出每个群体中生物的示例，包括像细菌 (bacteria) 这样的微生物 (micro-organisms)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能解释科学家将所有生物分成的主要大类（比如植物、动物和微小的微生物 (micro-organisms)），并给出每类的例子吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Communities Protecting Resources
topics.description: Obtain and combine information about ways individual communities use science ideas to protect the Earth's resources and environment
evidence: Describe at least three real-world examples of communities protecting resources or the environment
Explain the science ideas behind each example (e.g. solar panels convert sunlight to electricity, reducing fossil fuel use)
Discuss how individual actions and community efforts combine to make a difference
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe real examples of how communities protect the environment — like using solar panels, creating nature reserves, or cleaning up rivers?
topics.descriptionZh: 获取并整合关于各个社区如何运用科学理念来保护地球资源与环境的相关信息。
evidenceZh: 描述至少三个社区保护资源或环境的真实案例。
解释每个案例背后的科学原理（例如：太阳能电池板将阳光转化为电能，从而减少化石燃料的使用）。
探讨个人行动与社区努力如何结合并产生积极影响。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否描述社区保护环境的真实案例——例如使用太阳能电池板、建立自然保护区或清理河流？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Evidence-Based Classification
topics.description: Give reasons for classifying plants and animals based on specific characteristics, using evidence to justify classification decisions
evidence: Classify an unfamiliar organism using specific observable characteristics with reasoning
Compare two similar organisms and explain which characteristics distinguish their classification
Justify a classification decision using at least two pieces of evidence from observation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} finds an unusual creature, can they explain step by step how they'd work out what group it belongs to based on its features?
topics.descriptionZh: 根据动植物的具体特征说明分类理由，并用证据来支持分类决定。
evidenceZh: 运用具体的可观察特征对陌生的生物 (organism) 进行分类，并说明推理过程
比较两种相似的生物，并解释是哪些特征决定了它们属于不同的分类
利用至少两条观察到的证据，来证明自己做出的分类决定是合理的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 发现了一种奇特的生物，他们能一步一步地解释，如何根据它的特征来判断它属于哪一类吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Matter Cycling in Ecosystems
topics.description: Develop a model to describe the movement of matter among plants, animals, decomposers, and the environment in an ecosystem
evidence: Describe the role of decomposers (fungi, bacteria, worms) in breaking down dead matter
Trace the movement of matter: plant grows using soil nutrients → animal eats plant → animal dies → decomposers return nutrients to soil
Create or interpret a simple diagram showing matter cycling through an ecosystem
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happens to a fallen leaf on the forest floor — how tiny organisms break it down and the nutrients go back into the soil to help new plants grow?
topics.nameZh: 生态系统中的物质循环
topics.descriptionZh: 建立模型，描述生态系统中植物、动物、分解者与环境之间物质的运动
evidenceZh: 描述分解者（真菌、细菌、蠕虫）在分解死亡物质中的作用
追踪物质的运动：植物利用土壤养分生长 → 动物吃植物 → 动物死亡 → 分解者将养分返还给土壤
绘制或解读展示生态系统中物质循环的简单图表
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释森林地面上的一片落叶会发生什么——微小的生物如何将其分解，以及养分如何回到土壤中帮助新植物生长？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Energy Loss Between Levels
topics.description: Explain how energy is transferred between trophic levels in a food chain, why energy is lost at each stage, and use pyramids of biomass/numbers to represent this
evidence: Explains that only about 10% of energy passes from one trophic level to the next
Constructs a pyramid of biomass from data and explains its shape
Identifies where energy is lost at each trophic level (heat, movement, waste)
Explains why food chains rarely have more than five trophic levels
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why there are so many more plants than foxes in a field, could they explain how energy gets lost at every step of a food chain and what that means for the size of each population?
topics.nameZh: 营养级间的能量损耗 (Energy Loss Between Levels)
topics.descriptionZh: 解释在食物链中能量是如何在营养级（trophic levels）之间传递的，为什么在每个阶段会有能量损耗，并使用生物量金字塔（pyramid of biomass）和数量金字塔（pyramid of numbers）来表示这一过程。
evidenceZh: 解释只有大约10%的能量能从一个营养级传递到下一个营养级
根据数据构建生物量金字塔（pyramid of biomass），并解释其形状
指出在每个营养级中能量流失的去向（热量、运动、废物）
解释为什么食物链通常很少超过五个营养级
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果问{{name}}为什么田野里的植物比狐狸多得多，他们能否解释能量在食物链的每一步是如何流失的，以及这对每个种群（population）的规模意味着什么？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Food Webs & Interdependence
topics.description: Construct and interpret food webs showing the interdependence of organisms in an ecosystem, explaining how a change in one population affects others
evidence: Draws a food web from given data with arrows showing energy flow direction
Predicts how the population of one species would change if another species increased or decreased
Distinguishes a food web from a food chain and explains why webs are more realistic
Identifies producers, primary consumers, secondary consumers, and apex predators
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was shown a diagram with lots of animals connected by arrows, could they explain what it means — tracing what eats what — and predict what would happen if one animal disappeared from the web?
topics.nameZh: 食物网与相互依存关系
topics.descriptionZh: 构建并解读展示生态系统中生物相互依存关系的食物网，解释一个种群数量的变化如何影响其他种群
evidenceZh: 根据给定数据绘制食物网，并用箭头标出能量流动 (energy flow) 的方向
预测如果一个物种的数量增加或减少，另一个物种的种群数量会发生怎样的变化
区分食物网与食物链，并解释为什么食物网更符合现实情况
识别生产者 (producers)、初级消费者 (primary consumers)、次级消费者 (secondary consumers) 和顶级捕食者 (apex predators)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果给 {{name}} 看一张画满动物并用箭头相连的图，他们能解释这代表什么意思吗——理清谁吃谁的关系——并预测如果其中一种动物从食物网中消失会发生什么？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Pollination & Pollinator Decline
topics.description: Explain the importance of insect pollination for plant reproduction and human food security, and discuss the consequences of pollinator decline
evidence: Explains why many food crops depend on insect pollination to produce fruit and seeds
Names examples of crops that require insect pollination (e.g. apples, almonds, oilseed rape)
Discusses the potential impact of bee population decline on food production
Connects to plant reproduction — flowers are adapted to attract specific pollinators
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a news story about bees dying out, could they explain what that would actually mean for the food in your kitchen — which foods would be affected and why?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释昆虫授粉（pollination）对植物繁殖和人类粮食安全的重要性，并讨论传粉者（pollinator）减少带来的后果。
evidenceZh: 解释为什么许多农作物需要依赖昆虫授粉才能结出果实和种子
列举需要昆虫授粉的农作物实例（如苹果、杏仁、油菜）
讨论蜜蜂种群数量下降对粮食生产的潜在影响
联系植物繁殖——说明花朵是如何通过适应来吸引特定传粉者的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到关于蜜蜂濒临灭绝的新闻，他们能否解释这对你厨房里的食物究竟意味着什么——哪些食物会受到影响，为什么？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Water Cycle
topics.description: Describe the water cycle, tracing water through evaporation, condensation, precipitation, surface runoff, and transpiration in plants, explaining how the sun drives the cycle
evidence: Labels a water cycle diagram correctly
Explains what drives each stage of the water cycle (e.g. solar energy drives evaporation)
Explains the role of transpiration (plants releasing water vapour) in the water cycle
Discusses how human activities (deforestation, paving) affect the water cycle
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watched rain falling outside and was asked where that water had been before it fell, could they trace its journey through the water cycle from the sea to the clouds to the rain and back?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述水循环，追踪水经历蒸发 (evaporation)、凝结 (condensation)、降水 (precipitation)、地表径流 (surface runoff) 以及植物蒸腾 (transpiration) 的过程，并解释太阳如何驱动这一循环。
evidenceZh: 正确标注水循环示意图
解释水循环每个阶段的驱动力（例如：太阳能驱动蒸发）
解释蒸腾作用 (transpiration，即植物释放水蒸气) 在水循环中的作用
讨论人类活动（如森林砍伐、铺设硬化路面）如何影响水循环
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看着外面的雨落下，并被问到这些水在落下之前去过哪里，他们能追溯它在水循环中的旅程，从海洋到云层，再到降雨，然后返回吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Biodiversity & Resilience
topics.description: Explain what biodiversity means, why high biodiversity makes ecosystems more resilient, and describe the ways human activity threatens biodiversity (habitat destruction, pollution, invasive species, climate change)
evidence: Defines biodiversity at the species, genetic, and ecosystem levels
Explains why high biodiversity makes an ecosystem more stable and resilient to disruption
Identifies at least three human activities that reduce biodiversity
Discusses why biodiversity loss matters for humans as well as wildlife
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why it matters if a rainforest is cut down even if lots of species survive elsewhere, could they explain what biodiversity means and why losing it makes whole ecosystems more fragile?
topics.nameZh: 生物多样性与生态韧性
topics.descriptionZh: 解释生物多样性的含义，说明为什么高生物多样性能使生态系统更具韧性，并描述人类活动威胁生物多样性的方式（栖息地破坏、污染、外来物种入侵、气候变化）
evidenceZh: 在物种、基因和生态系统层面定义生物多样性
解释为什么高生物多样性能使生态系统更稳定，并更能抵御干扰
指出至少三种会降低生物多样性的人类活动
探讨生物多样性丧失为何不仅关乎野生动物，对人类也至关重要
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果有人问{{name}}，即使许多物种能在其他地方存活，砍伐雨林为什么仍然会造成严重后果，他们能否解释生物多样性的含义，以及为什么失去它会使整个生态系统变得更加脆弱？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Chromosomes, Genes & DNA
topics.description: Describe the relationship between chromosomes, genes, and DNA in heredity, including the double helix structure of DNA and the historical roles of Watson, Crick, Franklin, and Wilkins
evidence: Explains the hierarchy: DNA → gene → chromosome → nucleus → cell
Describes what a gene is and what it codes for
States that human body cells contain 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs
Describes the contributions of Watson, Crick, Franklin, and Wilkins to the discovery of DNA structure
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked what DNA actually is and where it is in the body, could they explain the relationship between DNA, genes, and chromosomes — and say roughly how many chromosomes a human cell has?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述遗传学中染色体（Chromosomes）、基因（Genes）和DNA之间的关系，包括DNA的双螺旋结构（Double helix structure），以及沃森（Watson）、克里克（Crick）、富兰克林（Franklin）和威尔金斯（Wilkins）在发现DNA结构中的历史贡献。
evidenceZh: 解释结构层级：DNA → 基因（Gene） → 染色体（Chromosome） → 细胞核（Nucleus） → 细胞（Cell）
描述基因（Gene）是什么以及它编码（Code for）什么
说明人体细胞含有23对共46条染色体（Chromosomes）
描述沃森（Watson）、克里克（Crick）、富兰克林（Franklin）和威尔金斯（Wilkins）对发现DNA结构的贡献
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果问{{name}} DNA到底是什么以及它在身体的哪个部位，他们能解释DNA、基因（Genes）和染色体（Chromosomes）之间的关系，并说出一个人体细胞大约有多少条染色体吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Evidence for Evolution
topics.description: Describe the main types of evidence for evolution: the fossil record (change over time), comparative anatomy (homologous structures), and the geographic distribution of related species
evidence: Explains how fossils form and what they can tell us about past life
Uses the fossil record as evidence that species have changed over time
Describes homologous structures (e.g. pentadactyl limb) as evidence for common ancestry
Explains why island species provide evidence for evolution (e.g. Darwin's finches, Galapagos)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visited a natural history museum and saw fossils and skeletons of different animals, could they explain how scientists use those to build up evidence that species change over time — and that different animals are related?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述进化的主要证据类型：化石记录（随时间的变化）、比较解剖学（同源结构）以及相关物种的地理分布。
evidenceZh: 解释化石是如何形成的，以及它们能告诉我们关于过去生命的哪些信息
利用化石记录作为物种随时间发生变化的证据
描述同源结构（例如五趾型附肢 (pentadactyl limb)）作为拥有共同祖先的证据
解释为什么岛屿物种能提供进化的证据（例如加拉帕戈斯群岛的达尔文雀 (Darwin's finches)）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 参观自然历史博物馆并看到了不同动物的化石和骨骼，他们能解释科学家如何利用这些证据来证明物种会随时间变化——以及不同动物之间存在亲缘关系吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Extinction & Rapid Change
topics.description: Explain how environmental change can outpace a species' ability to adapt through natural selection, leading to extinction, using historical and contemporary examples
evidence: Explains why extinction occurs when environmental change is faster than the rate of adaptation
Gives a historical example (e.g. woolly mammoth, dodo) and a contemporary example of threatened extinction
Distinguishes between background extinction rates and mass extinctions
Explains how human activity (habitat loss, hunting, climate change) is driving current species loss
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why woolly mammoths no longer exist while other large mammals survived, could they explain what conditions led to the mammoth's extinction — and connect it to what's happening with endangered species today?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释环境变化如何超越物种通过自然选择（natural selection）适应的能力，从而导致灭绝，并使用历史和当代的例子进行说明
evidenceZh: 解释当环境变化速度快于适应速度时为什么会发生灭绝
给出历史案例（如长毛象 woolly mammoth、渡渡鸟 dodo）和当代面临灭绝威胁的案例
区分背景灭绝率（background extinction rates）和大规模灭绝（mass extinctions）
解释人类活动（栖息地丧失、捕猎、气候变化）如何导致当前的物种丧失
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果有人问 {{name}} 为什么长毛象（woolly mammoths）已经灭绝而其他大型哺乳动物却存活了下来，他们能否解释导致长毛象灭绝的环境条件——并将其与当今濒危物种的现状联系起来？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Genetic Mutation
topics.description: Explain genetic mutation as a random change in DNA sequence, describe causes of mutation (e.g. radiation, chemicals, copying errors), and explain that most mutations are neutral, some harmful, and a few beneficial
evidence: Defines mutation as a change to DNA sequence
Names at least two things that can cause mutations (mutagens)
