Explains that mutations are the original source of all genetic variation
Explains that beneficial mutations can be selected for by natural selection
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that DNA can get damaged or changed, could they explain what a mutation is, what might cause one, and why most mutations don’t actually cause problems — but occasionally one leads to something new?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释基因突变是DNA序列 (DNA sequence) 的随机变化，描述导致突变的原因（例如辐射、化学物质、复制错误），并解释大多数突变是中性的，有些是有害的，只有少数是有益的。
evidenceZh: 将突变定义为DNA序列 (DNA sequence) 的改变
说出至少两种能引起突变的因素（诱变因素 mutagens）
解释突变是所有遗传变异 (genetic variation) 的最初来源
解释有益突变可以通过自然选择 (natural selection) 被保留下来
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 听说DNA可能会受损或发生改变，他们能否解释什么是突变 (mutation)、可能是什么原因引起的，以及为什么大多数突变实际上不会引起问题——但偶尔会导致新事物的产生？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How Natural Selection Works
topics.description: Explain natural selection as the mechanism of evolution: heritable variation + competition for resources + differential survival and reproduction = change in allele frequency over generations
evidence: Describes the four conditions required for natural selection to operate (variation, heritability, competition, selection)
Applies the concept to a specific example (e.g. antibiotic resistance in bacteria, peppered moth)
Explains why individuals with advantageous traits leave more offspring
Distinguishes natural selection from evolution (selection is the mechanism; evolution is the result over many generations)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard about bacteria becoming resistant to antibiotics, could they explain how that happened using natural selection — without the bacteria ‘choosing’ to change?
topics.descriptionZh: 将自然选择解释为生物进化的机制：可遗传的变异（heritable variation）加上对资源的竞争（competition for resources），导致差异化的生存与繁殖（differential survival and reproduction），最终等于世代之间等位基因频率（allele frequency）的改变。
evidenceZh: 描述自然选择运作所需的四个条件（变异 variation、遗传性 heritability、竞争 competition、选择 selection）
将该概念应用于具体实例（例如细菌的抗生素抗性 antibiotic resistance 或椒花蛾 peppered moth）
解释为什么拥有有利性状（advantageous traits）的个体会留下更多的后代
区分自然选择与进化（选择是机制 mechanism；进化是经过许多世代后产生的结果 result）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 听说细菌对抗生素产生了抗药性，他们能用自然选择的原理来解释这是如何发生的吗——并且说明细菌并没有‘主动选择’去改变？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Species Distribution & Change
topics.description: Explain how environmental change (climate change, habitat loss, pollution) affects the distribution of species, including range shifts, local extinction, and invasive species
evidence: Describes at least two ways environmental change can affect species distribution
Gives a real example of a species whose range has shifted due to climate change
Explains what an invasive species is and how environmental change can enable invasions
Discusses why some species are more vulnerable to environmental change than others
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that wild plants in the UK are now flowering weeks earlier than they did 50 years ago, could they explain why that happens and what problems it might cause for the other animals that depend on those plants?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释环境变化（如气候变化 climate change、栖息地丧失 habitat loss、污染 pollution）如何影响物种的分布，包括分布区转移（range shifts）、局部灭绝（local extinction）和入侵物种（invasive species）。
evidenceZh: 描述至少两种环境变化影响物种分布的方式
给出一个因气候变化而导致分布区转移（range shift）的真实物种例子
解释什么是入侵物种（invasive species），以及环境变化如何促成物种入侵
探讨为什么有些物种比其他物种更容易受到环境变化的影响
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 听说英国的野生植物现在比50年前提前了几周开花，他们能解释为什么会发生这种情况，以及这可能给依赖这些植物的其他动物带来什么问题吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Carbon Cycle
topics.description: Describe the carbon cycle, tracing carbon through photosynthesis, respiration, feeding, decomposition, and combustion, and explain the role of each process
evidence: Draws or labels a diagram of the carbon cycle showing the main processes
Explains how photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere
Explains how respiration, combustion, and decomposition return carbon dioxide to the atmosphere
Discusses how human activities (burning fossil fuels, deforestation) disrupt the carbon cycle
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked where the carbon in a wooden table came from originally, could they trace its journey through the carbon cycle — from the atmosphere, through a plant, into the tree, and back out again?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述碳循环，追踪碳在光合作用（photosynthesis）、呼吸作用（respiration）、摄食（feeding）、分解（decomposition）和燃烧（combustion）过程中的流动，并解释每个过程的作用。
evidenceZh: 绘制或标注展示主要过程的碳循环图
解释光合作用如何从大气中去除二氧化碳
解释呼吸作用、燃烧和分解如何将二氧化碳返回大气中
讨论人类活动（如燃烧化石燃料、砍伐森林）如何破坏碳循环
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果问{{name}}木桌里的碳最初来自哪里，他们能否追踪其在碳循环中的旅程——从大气中，通过植物，进入树木，最后又回到大气中？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Toxins Building Up in Food Chains
topics.description: Explain how organisms affect and are affected by their environment, including the bioaccumulation of toxic materials (e.g. pesticides, heavy metals) through food chains
evidence: Defines bioaccumulation and explains why toxins increase in concentration higher up the food chain
Gives a real example of bioaccumulation (e.g. DDT in peregrine falcons, mercury in tuna)
Explains how organisms can change their habitat (e.g. earthworms aerating soil, beavers creating wetlands)
Discusses why top predators are most at risk from bioaccumulation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that large fish like tuna can contain more mercury than small fish, could they explain why that is — even though the tuna didn’t encounter mercury directly?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释生物如何影响环境并受环境影响，包括有毒物质（如农药、重金属）在食物链中的生物富集（bioaccumulation）过程。
evidenceZh: 定义生物富集（bioaccumulation），并解释为什么毒素在食物链越高层级浓度越高
举出生物富集的真实案例（例如游隼体内的DDT、金枪鱼体内的汞）
解释生物如何改变其栖息环境（例如蚯蚓疏松土壤、河狸建造湿地）
探讨为什么顶级捕食者面临最大的生物富集风险
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 听说像金枪鱼这样的大型鱼类体内含有的汞比小型鱼类多，即使金枪鱼没有直接接触汞，他们能解释这是为什么吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Variation in Species
topics.description: Explain variation within and between species, distinguishing between continuous variation (e.g. height) and discontinuous variation (e.g. blood group), and between genetic and environmental causes
evidence: Gives examples of continuous and discontinuous variation in humans
Distinguishes between genetic causes of variation (inherited differences) and environmental causes (diet, sunlight, etc.)
Explains why sexual reproduction produces greater variation than asexual reproduction
Draws or interprets a frequency graph showing continuous variation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked around a classroom and noticed that everyone has slightly different heights, hair colours, and eye colours, could they explain why these differences exist — and which ones are inherited, which are down to the environment, and which are both?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释物种内部及物种之间的变异，区分连续变异（continuous variation，如身高）与不连续变异（discontinuous variation，如血型），并区分导致变异的遗传原因与环境原因。
evidenceZh: 能举出人类连续变异和不连续变异的例子
能区分导致变异的遗传原因（遗传差异）和环境原因（饮食、阳光等）
能解释为什么有性繁殖比无性繁殖产生更多的变异
能绘制或解读展示连续变异的频率图（frequency graph）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 环顾教室，注意到每个人的身高、发色和瞳色都略有不同，他们能解释为什么存在这些差异吗——哪些是遗传的，哪些是环境造成的，哪些是两者共同作用的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Predicting Inherited Traits
topics.description: Explain how alleles are inherited in sexual reproduction and use Punnett squares to predict the probability of offspring inheriting a characteristic, including dominant and recessive alleles
evidence: Defines allele, dominant, and recessive in the context of inheritance
Constructs a Punnett square for a monohybrid cross and calculates probability ratios
Explains the difference between genotype and phenotype
Gives an example of a human characteristic controlled by dominant/recessive alleles
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why two brown-eyed parents can have a blue-eyed child, could they explain what dominant and recessive alleles are and show how it works using a Punnett square?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释在有性生殖中等位基因(alleles)是如何遗传的，并使用庞尼特方格(Punnett squares)来预测后代遗传某一特征的概率，包括显性(dominant)和隐性(recessive)等位基因。
evidenceZh: 在遗传学背景下定义等位基因(allele)、显性(dominant)和隐性(recessive)
构建单因子杂交(monohybrid cross)的庞尼特方格(Punnett square)并计算概率比
解释基因型(genotype)和表型(phenotype)之间的区别
举例说明受显性/隐性等位基因控制的人类特征
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果有人问{{name}}为什么两个棕色眼睛的父母能生出蓝色眼睛的孩子，他们能否解释什么是显性和隐性等位基因(alleles)，并使用庞尼特方格(Punnett square)展示其遗传过程？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Building shade from the sun
topics.description: Use tools and materials to design and build a structure that will reduce the warming effect of sunlight on an area, such as a shade or shelter
evidence: Design a structure intended to reduce the warming effect of sunlight on an area
Build the structure using available materials and test whether it reduces temperature
Compare the temperature in the shaded area vs an unshaded area as evidence of effectiveness
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} design and build a simple shade — like an umbrella or canopy — and test whether it keeps an area cooler in the sun?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用工具和材料设计并搭建一个结构，以减少阳光对某一区域的加热效应（warming effect），例如遮阳篷或庇护所（shelter）
evidenceZh: 设计一个旨在减少阳光对某一区域加热效应（warming effect）的结构
使用现有材料搭建该结构，并测试其是否能降低温度
比较遮阳区域（shaded area）与无遮阳区域（unshaded area）的温度，以此作为有效性的证据
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否设计并搭建一个简单的遮阳设施——比如雨伞或顶篷（canopy）——并测试它是否能让该区域在阳光下保持更凉爽？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Sunlight warms things up
topics.description: Make observations to determine the effect of sunlight on Earth's surface, noticing that sunlight warms the ground, water, and objects
evidence: Observe that surfaces in sunlight feel warmer than those in shade
Describe that sunlight provides warmth (heat energy) to Earth's surface
Compare temperatures of surfaces in sun vs shade using touch or a thermometer
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} feel the difference between a sunny pavement and a shady one, and explain that sunlight warms up surfaces it shines on?
topics.descriptionZh: 通过观察来确定阳光对地球表面的影响，注意到阳光会使地面、水和物体变暖。
evidenceZh: 观察到阳光照射下的表面比阴影处的表面感觉更暖和
描述阳光为地球表面提供温暖（热能）
使用触摸或温度计比较阳光下和阴影处表面的温度
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否感受到阳光照射的路面和阴凉处的路面之间的温差，并解释阳光会使其照射到的表面变暖？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Naming types of energy
topics.description: Name and use vocabulary for types of energy and energy transfer — kinetic energy, potential energy, heat energy, light energy, sound energy, electrical energy, chemical energy, stored energy, energy transfer, energy transformation — and describe energy changes in familiar situations using these terms
evidence: Name the type of energy stored in a battery, a stretched spring, and a moving ball
Use 'energy transfer' or 'energy transformation' to describe what happens in a simple device such as a torch or a toaster
Distinguish between 'stored energy' and 'transferred energy' with a correct example of each
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} stretches a rubber band and lets it go, can they name what type of energy it had when stretched — and what it changed into?
topics.descriptionZh: 命名并使用能量及能量传递的词汇——动能 (kinetic energy)、势能 (potential energy)、热能 (heat energy)、光能 (light energy)、声能 (sound energy)、电能 (electrical energy)、化学能 (chemical energy)、储存能 (stored energy)、能量传递 (energy transfer)、能量转化 (energy transformation)——并使用这些术语描述熟悉情境中的能量变化。
evidenceZh: 说出电池、拉伸的弹簧和运动的球所储存的能量类型
使用“能量传递 (energy transfer)”或“能量转化 (energy transformation)”来描述手电筒或烤面包机等简单设备中发生的现象
区分“储存能 (stored energy)”和“传递能 (transferred energy)”，并为每种能量提供正确的例子
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 拉伸一根橡皮筋然后松开，他们能说出橡皮筋在拉伸时具有什么类型的能量——以及它转化成了什么能量吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Building a simple circuit
topics.description: Construct a simple series electrical circuit, identifying and naming its basic parts: cells, wires, bulbs, switches, and buzzers
evidence: Build a complete series circuit that lights a bulb or sounds a buzzer
Name each component: cell (battery), wire, bulb, switch, buzzer
Explain the role of each component in making the circuit work
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} build a working circuit with a battery, wires, and a light bulb, and name each part they're using?
topics.descriptionZh: 搭建一个简单的串联电路（series circuit），识别并命名其基本部件：电池（cell）、导线（wire）、灯泡（bulb）、开关（switch）和蜂鸣器（buzzer）。
evidenceZh: 搭建一个完整的串联电路（series circuit），使其能够点亮灯泡或使蜂鸣器发声
命名每个组件：电池（cell/battery）、导线（wire）、灯泡（bulb）、开关（switch）、蜂鸣器（buzzer）
解释每个组件在使电路工作（circuit）中所起的作用
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否使用电池、导线和灯泡搭建一个可工作的电路，并说出他们所使用的每个部件的名称？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Conductors and insulators
topics.description: Recognise some common conductors and insulators, and associate metals with being good conductors of electricity
evidence: Define conductors (allow electricity to flow through) and insulators (block electricity)
Test at least six materials and correctly classify them as conductors or insulators
State that metals are generally good conductors and explain why wires are made of metal with plastic coating
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} test objects in a circuit and explain why metal objects let electricity through but rubber and plastic don't?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识一些常见的导体和绝缘体，并了解金属是良好的电导体
evidenceZh: 定义导体（允许电流通过）和绝缘体（阻断电流）
测试至少六种材料，并将它们正确分类为导体或绝缘体
说明金属通常是良好的导体，并解释为什么电线是由金属制成并带有塑料涂层的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否在电路中测试物体，并解释为什么金属物体能让电流通过，而橡胶和塑料不能？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How switches work
topics.description: Recognise that a switch opens and closes a circuit, controlling whether a lamp lights or a buzzer sounds
evidence: Explain that a closed switch completes the circuit (current flows) and an open switch breaks it (current stops)
Demonstrate adding a switch to a circuit and using it to control a bulb or buzzer
Relate the switch concept to everyday switches in the home
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happens inside the wall when they flip a light switch — that it completes or breaks the electrical loop?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识到开关可以断开和闭合电路，从而控制灯泡是否发光或蜂鸣器是否发声
evidenceZh: 解释闭合的开关能接通电路（电流通过），而断开的开关能切断电路（电流停止）
演示在电路中加入开关，并用它来控制灯泡或蜂鸣器
将开关的概念与家中日常使用的开关联系起来
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释当他们拨动电灯开关时，墙壁里面发生了什么——也就是它接通还是断开了电路回路？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: What uses electricity at home
topics.description: Identify common appliances that run on electricity and understand that electricity is a form of energy that powers devices in everyday life
evidence: Name at least ten common appliances that run on electricity
Distinguish between mains-powered and battery-powered appliances
Explain that electricity provides the energy that makes these devices work
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} walk around the house and point out which things use electricity to work, like the fridge, TV, and lights?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识日常生活中使用电的常见电器，并理解电是一种能量，能为各种家用电器提供动力。
evidenceZh: 说出至少十种使用电的常见电器
区分使用市电（mains-powered）和电池（battery-powered）供电的电器
解释电提供了使这些设备运转的能量
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否在屋里走一圈，指出哪些东西是靠电工作的，比如冰箱、电视和电灯？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Will the bulb light up?
topics.description: Identify whether or not a lamp will light in a simple series circuit, based on whether the lamp is part of a complete loop with a battery
evidence: Predict whether a lamp will light by tracing the circuit for a complete loop
Explain that a gap anywhere in the circuit breaks the loop and the bulb won't light
Identify the fault in a non-working circuit (e.g. loose wire, missing connection)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looks at a circuit diagram, can they tell you whether the bulb will light up or not, based on whether there's a complete loop?
topics.descriptionZh: 判断在简单的串联电路（simple series circuit）中灯泡是否会亮，依据是灯泡是否与电池构成了一个完整的回路（complete loop）。
evidenceZh: 通过追踪电路是否形成完整回路，来预测灯泡是否会亮。
解释电路中任何地方的断开都会破坏回路，导致灯泡不亮。
找出不工作电路中的故障（例如：导线松动、连接缺失）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看一个电路图，他们能根据是否有完整回路来判断灯泡是否会亮吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Building an energy-converting device
topics.description: Apply scientific ideas to design, test, and refine a device that converts energy from one form to another
evidence: Design a device that converts one form of energy to another (e.g. electrical to light, kinetic to sound)
Build, test, and identify what works well and what needs improvement
Explain the energy conversion taking place in the device
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} design and build a simple device — like a rubber-band car or a solar oven — that changes energy from one form to another?
topics.descriptionZh: 运用科学知识设计、测试并改进一个能将能量从一种形式转化为另一种形式的装置
evidenceZh: 设计一个能将一种形式的能量转化为另一种形式的装置（例如：电能 (electrical energy) 转化为光能 (light energy)，动能 (kinetic energy) 转化为声能 (sound energy)）
制作、测试该装置，并找出哪些部分效果好、哪些部分需要改进
解释装置中发生的能量转换 (energy conversion) 过程
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否设计并制作一个简单的装置（如橡皮筋动力车或太阳能烤箱），将能量从一种形式转化为另一种形式？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Circuit vocabulary
topics.description: Use technical vocabulary for electrical circuits — circuit, component, cell, battery, current, voltage, resistance, conductor, insulator, switch, series circuit, parallel circuit — and apply these when describing, drawing, and designing working circuits
evidence: Use 'series' and 'parallel' correctly to describe two different circuit configurations and explain the key difference
Apply 'current', 'voltage', and 'resistance' correctly in a written description of how a circuit works
Name at least six standard circuit components and describe what each one does
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know the difference between a series circuit and a parallel circuit — not just which one, but what actually makes them different electrically?
topics.descriptionZh: 运用电路专业词汇——电路（circuit）、元件（component）、电芯（cell）、电池（battery）、电流（current）、电压（voltage）、电阻（resistance）、导体（conductor）、绝缘体（insulator）、开关（switch）、串联电路（series circuit）、并联电路（parallel circuit）——并在描述、绘制和设计实用电路时应用这些词汇。
evidenceZh: 正确使用“串联”和“并联”来描述两种不同的电路配置，并解释它们的关键区别
在书面描述电路工作原理时，正确运用“电流”、“电压”和“电阻”
说出至少六种标准电路元件的名称，并描述它们各自的作用
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否了解串联电路和并联电路的区别——不仅是能分辨哪个是串联、哪个是并联，而是真正明白它们在电学原理上的本质不同？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How energy travels around
topics.description: Observe and provide evidence that energy can be transferred from place to place by sound, light, heat, and electric currents
evidence: Give at least one example of energy transfer by each: sound, light, heat, electric current
Explain that energy moves from a source to a destination through these means
Describe how electric currents transfer energy from a battery to a bulb through wires
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} give examples of how energy moves around — like heat from a radiator warming a room, light from a lamp reaching your eyes, or electricity flowing through a wire?
topics.descriptionZh: 观察并提供证据，证明能量可以通过声音、光、热和电流（electric currents）从一个地方传递到另一个地方。
evidenceZh: 为声音、光、热和电流（electric current）的能量传递各举至少一个例子。
解释能量是如何通过这些方式从源头（source）传递到目的地（destination）的。
描述电流如何通过导线将能量从电池（battery）传递到灯泡（bulb）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能举出能量是如何传递的例子吗——比如散热器散发的热量温暖了房间，台灯发出的光进入你的眼睛，或者电流在导线中流动？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Reading and drawing circuit diagrams
topics.description: Draw and read simple circuit diagrams using standard symbols for cells, bulbs, switches, buzzers, and wires; identify whether a circuit is complete or broken from a diagram; match circuit diagrams to physical circuits
evidence: Draw a circuit diagram for a cell, switch, and bulb using standard symbols
Identify from a diagram whether a switch is open or closed and predict whether the bulb lights
Match a photograph of a physical circuit to the correct circuit diagram from a set of options
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a circuit diagram with symbols for a battery, switch, and light bulb, can they tell you whether the bulb would light up — and draw the diagram for a simple circuit you describe?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用电池（cell）、灯泡、开关、蜂鸣器和导线的标准符号绘制和阅读简单电路图；从电路图中识别电路是闭合（complete）还是断开（broken）；将电路图与实际物理电路进行匹配
evidenceZh: 使用标准符号绘制包含电池、开关和灯泡的电路图
从电路图中识别开关是断开（open）还是闭合（closed），并预测灯泡是否会亮起
将实际电路的照片与一组选项中的正确电路图进行匹配
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到一张包含电池、开关和灯泡符号的电路图，他们能告诉你灯泡是否会亮起吗？并且，能否根据你对简单电路的描述画出相应的电路图？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Speed and energy
topics.description: Use evidence to construct an explanation relating the speed of an object to the energy of that object
evidence: Explain that a moving object has energy, and the faster it moves the more energy it has
Provide evidence from observations (e.g. faster ball causes more damage/movement)
Use the term 'kinetic energy' or 'energy of motion' appropriately
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a fast-moving ball knocks down more skittles than a slow one, using the idea that faster things have more energy?
topics.descriptionZh: 运用证据构建解释，说明物体的运动速度与其能量之间的关系。
evidenceZh: 解释运动的物体具有能量，且运动速度越快，能量越大。
提供基于观察的证据（例如：速度更快的球会造成更大的破坏或使物体移动得更远）。
恰当使用“动能（kinetic energy）”或“运动能量（energy of motion）”这一术语。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否运用“速度越快的物体具有的能量越大”这一概念，解释为什么快速移动的球比慢速移动的球能击倒更多的木瓶？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: What happens when things collide
topics.description: Ask questions and predict outcomes about the changes in energy that occur when objects collide
evidence: Predict the outcome of a collision based on the speeds and sizes of the objects
Explain that energy transfers from one object to another during a collision
Describe observable changes: one object speeds up, the other slows down, sound is produced
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} rolls two balls towards each other, can they predict what will happen when they hit and explain that energy transfers between them?
topics.nameZh: 物体碰撞时会发生什么
topics.descriptionZh: 提出问题，并预测物体碰撞时能量（energy）的变化与结果。
evidenceZh: 根据物体的速度和大小，预测碰撞（collision）的结果。
解释在碰撞过程中，能量（energy）会从一个物体转移到另一个物体。
描述能观察到的变化：一个物体变快，另一个物体变慢，还会发出声音。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 把两个球相对滚出去，他们能预测球撞在一起时会发生什么，并解释能量（energy）在它们之间转移了吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Drawing circuits with proper symbols
topics.description: Use recognised symbols when representing a simple circuit in a diagram, including cell, wire, bulb, switch, buzzer, and motor
evidence: Draw a circuit diagram using standard symbols for at least five components
Interpret a circuit diagram drawn by someone else and describe what the circuit does
Convert between a physical circuit and its diagram representation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw a circuit diagram using the proper symbols for batteries, bulbs, switches, and wires instead of drawing pictures?
topics.nameZh: 使用标准符号绘制电路图
topics.descriptionZh: 在电路图中使用公认的标准符号来表示简单电路，包括电池（cell）、导线（wire）、灯泡（bulb）、开关（switch）、蜂鸣器（buzzer）和电动机（motor）。
evidenceZh: 能够使用标准符号为至少五种元件绘制电路图
能够解读他人绘制的电路图，并描述该电路的作用
能够在实物电路与其电路图表示之间进行转换
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否使用电池、灯泡、开关和导线的标准符号来绘制电路图，而不是直接画实物图片？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: More batteries, brighter bulb
topics.description: Associate the brightness of a lamp or volume of a buzzer with the number and voltage of cells used in a series circuit
evidence: Describe the pattern: more cells (or higher voltage) = brighter bulb / louder buzzer
Explain that more cells provide more energy to the circuit
Predict the effect of changing the number of cells on a component's behaviour
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why adding a second battery makes the bulb brighter, and predict what happens with three batteries?
topics.descriptionZh: 将灯泡的亮度或蜂鸣器的音量与串联电路（series circuit）中使用的电池数量及电压（voltage）联系起来
evidenceZh: 描述规律：更多电池（cells）或更高电压（voltage）= 更亮的灯泡 / 更响的蜂鸣器
解释更多电池能为电路提供更多能量
预测改变电池数量对元件行为（component's behaviour）的影响
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能解释为什么增加第二节电池会使灯泡更亮，并预测使用三节电池时会发生什么吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Why circuit components behave differently
topics.description: Compare and give reasons for variations in how circuit components function, including brightness of bulbs, loudness of buzzers, and switch positions
evidence: Explain why adding more components in series reduces brightness/loudness (energy shared)
Compare circuits with different configurations and predict component behaviour
Give reasoned explanations for observed variations in component function
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} adds a second bulb to a series circuit and it gets dimmer, can they explain why the energy is being shared between the two bulbs?
topics.nameZh: 为什么电路元件（circuit components）的表现不同
topics.descriptionZh: 比较并说明电路元件（circuit components）功能变化的原因，包括灯泡（bulbs）的亮度、蜂鸣器（buzzers）的响度以及开关（switches）的位置。
evidenceZh: 解释为什么在串联电路（series circuit）中增加更多元件会降低亮度或响度（能量被分配 shared）
比较不同连接方式（configurations）的电路并预测元件的表现
对观察到的元件功能变化给出有理有据的解释
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}在串联电路（series circuit）中增加第二个灯泡导致其变暗，他们能解释为什么能量在两个灯泡之间被分配（shared）吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Current, voltage, and what they measure
topics.description: Understand that electric current is the rate of flow of charge (measured in amperes using an ammeter), and that potential difference (voltage) is the energy transferred per unit charge (measured in volts using a voltmeter)
evidence: States that current is measured in amperes (A) and is the rate at which charge flows around a circuit
States that potential difference (voltage) is measured in volts (V) and represents energy transferred per unit charge
Correctly connects an ammeter in series and a voltmeter in parallel when building or interpreting a circuit
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sets up a circuit with an ammeter and a voltmeter, can they explain what each one is measuring and describe the difference between current and voltage?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解电流（electric current）是电荷（charge）流动的速率（使用电流表以安培（amperes）为单位进行测量），并且电势差（电压，potential difference / voltage）是每单位电荷所转移的能量（使用电压表以伏特（volts）为单位进行测量）。
evidenceZh: 说明电流（current）以安培（A）为单位进行测量，它是电荷（charge）在电路中流动的速率
说明电势差或电压（potential difference / voltage）以伏特（V）为单位进行测量，代表每单位电荷转移的能量
在搭建或分析电路时，能够正确地将电流表（ammeter）串联、电压表（voltmeter）并联接入电路
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 搭建了一个包含电流表（ammeter）和电压表（voltmeter）的电路，他们能否解释这两个仪表分别测量什么，并描述电流（current）和电压（voltage）之间的区别？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Energy can't be created or destroyed
topics.description: Explain the principle of conservation of energy (energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred between stores), and describe how energy is dissipated as thermal energy to the surroundings in all real processes
evidence: States the law of conservation of energy
Explains why the total energy in a closed system is always the same even though it changes form
Explains what dissipation means and why it happens in real machines (friction, air resistance)
Gives an example showing why 'wasted' energy is not lost but transferred to the surroundings
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} charged their phone overnight and was asked where the electrical energy goes, could they explain what conservation of energy means — and why the charger gets warm even though that heat isn’t doing any useful work?
topics.nameZh: 能量不能被创造或毁灭（能量守恒 / Conservation of Energy）
topics.descriptionZh: 解释能量守恒原理（能量不能被创造或毁灭，只能在不同的能量库（stores）之间转移），并描述在所有实际过程中，能量是如何以热能（thermal energy）的形式耗散（dissipation）到周围环境中的。
evidenceZh: 阐述能量守恒定律（Law of Conservation of Energy）
解释为什么封闭系统（closed system）中的总能量始终不变，即使它的形式发生了改变
解释耗散（dissipation）的含义，以及为什么在实际机械中会发生耗散（如摩擦力 friction 和空气阻力 air resistance）
举例说明为什么“浪费”的能量并没有消失，而是转移到了周围环境中
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}整夜给手机充电，并被问到电能（electrical energy）去哪儿了，他们能解释能量守恒（conservation of energy）的意思吗——并且解释为什么充电器会变热，即使这些热量并没有做任何有用的功（work）？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Energy stores and transfers
topics.description: Identify the main energy stores (kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic potential, thermal, chemical, nuclear, electromagnetic) and the pathways by which energy is transferred between stores (mechanically, electrically, by heating, by radiation)
evidence: Names and describes at least five energy stores with a real-world example of each
Identifies the energy stores at the start and end of a given process (e.g. a falling ball, a burning match)
Describes the transfer pathway connecting two energy stores in a given scenario
Traces energy through a system identifying all stores and transfers involved
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watched a ball being thrown upward and then falling back down, could they describe what type of energy the ball has at the top of its arc and at the bottom — and explain what happened to the energy between those two points?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别主要的能量储存形式（动能（kinetic）、重力势能（gravitational potential）、弹性势能（elastic potential）、热能（thermal）、化学能（chemical）、核能（nuclear）、电磁能（electromagnetic））以及能量在各储存形式之间传递的途径（机械方式（mechanically）、电学方式（electrically）、加热方式（by heating）、辐射方式（by radiation））。
evidenceZh: 命名并描述至少五种能量储存形式，并为每种形式提供一个现实生活中的实例
识别特定过程开始和结束时的能量储存形式（例如：下落的球、燃烧的火柴）
描述特定场景中连接两种能量储存形式的传递途径
追踪能量在系统中的流动，识别所有涉及的储存形式和传递过程
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 观察一个被向上抛出然后又落下的球，他们能否描述球在最高点（抛物线顶端）和最低点时分别具有哪种类型的能量，并解释在这两点之间能量发生了怎样的传递与转化？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Static electricity and sparks
topics.description: Explain static electricity as the build-up of electric charge through friction, describe how charged objects attract or repel each other, and relate static discharge to everyday phenomena such as lightning
evidence: Explains that rubbing transfers electrons from one material to another, creating opposite charges
States that like charges repel and unlike charges attract
Links the concept of static discharge to the formation of lightning as a large-scale electric spark
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a balloon rubbed on hair sticks to the wall, and connect this to the science of how lightning forms during a thunderstorm?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释静电是通过摩擦积累电荷的现象，描述带电物体如何相互吸引或排斥，并将静电放电 (static discharge) 与闪电等日常现象联系起来。
evidenceZh: 解释摩擦会将电子 (electrons) 从一种材料转移到另一种材料上，从而产生正负电荷
说明同种电荷相互排斥，异种电荷相互吸引
将静电放电 (static discharge) 的概念与闪电的形成联系起来，说明闪电是一种大规模的电火花现象
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释为什么在头发上摩擦过的气球会粘在墙上，并将其与雷暴天气中闪电形成的科学原理联系起来？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Conduction, convection, and radiation
topics.description: Describe and compare the three mechanisms of heat transfer — conduction (particle vibration through solids), convection (fluid movement in liquids/gases), and radiation (infrared waves) — and explain that the rate of transfer depends on temperature difference
evidence: Explains the particle-level mechanism for conduction and why metals are good conductors
Describes a convection current using particle theory and gives a real-world example
Explains that all objects emit and absorb infrared radiation and how surface colour affects this
States that a greater temperature difference increases the rate of heat transfer
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was heating soup on a hob and also warming their hands by a radiator, could they explain which type of heat transfer is happening in each case — and why the soup pot gets hot throughout even though it’s only heated at the bottom?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述并比较三种热传递 (Heat transfer) 方式：传导（固体中粒子的振动）、对流（液体或气体中流体的运动）和辐射（红外波/Infrared waves），并解释热传递的速度取决于温差 (Temperature difference)。
evidenceZh: 解释传导 (Conduction) 在粒子层面的原理，以及为什么金属是热的良导体。
运用粒子理论 (Particle theory) 描述对流 (Convection) 现象，并举一个生活中的实际例子。
解释所有物体都会发射和吸收红外辐射 (Infrared radiation)，以及物体表面颜色对此的影响。
说明温差 (Temperature difference) 越大，热传递的速度就越快。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在炉子上热汤，同时又在暖气片旁边烤手，他们能解释这两种情况分别属于哪种热传递方式吗？另外，他们能解释为什么汤锅只在底部受热，整个锅却都能变热吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Efficiency, Sankey diagrams, and work done
topics.description: Calculate energy efficiency as the ratio of useful output energy to total input energy, construct and interpret Sankey diagrams, and calculate work done using work = force × distance
evidence: Calculates efficiency as a percentage from given input and useful output energy values
Draws a Sankey diagram to represent energy transfers in a device, with arrow widths proportional to energy amounts
Uses W = Fd to calculate work done when a force moves through a distance
Identifies which energy transformations in a Sankey diagram are useful and which are wasted
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that a light bulb is 10% efficient and uses 60 J of energy, could they work out how much of that energy actually becomes light — and where the rest goes?
topics.nameZh: 效率、桑基图（Sankey diagrams）与做功（Work done）
topics.descriptionZh: 计算能量效率（energy efficiency），即有用输出能量与总输入能量之比；构建并解读桑基图（Sankey diagrams）；使用公式“功=力×距离”（work = force × distance）计算做功
evidenceZh: 根据给定的输入能量和有用输出能量值，计算效率（efficiency）百分比
绘制桑基图（Sankey diagram）来表示设备中的能量转移（energy transfers），且箭头宽度与能量大小成正比
使用公式 W = Fd 计算力作用一段距离时所做的功（work done）
识别桑基图（Sankey diagram）中哪些能量转换（energy transformations）是有用的，哪些是浪费的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}听说一个灯泡的效率是10%，并且消耗了60焦耳（J）的能量，他们能算出这些能量中有多少实际上转化为了光能吗——剩下的能量又去了哪里？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Heating experiments and Q = mcΔT
topics.description: Plan and carry out experiments to measure energy transferred during heating, including using the equation Q = mcΔT, recording temperature changes over time, and evaluating sources of error
evidence: Uses a thermometer and stopwatch to record temperature change over time in a heating experiment
Applies Q = mcΔT to calculate the energy transferred to a substance being heated
Identifies sources of energy loss in a heating experiment (e.g. heat to surroundings) and suggests improvements
Plots a temperature-time graph and identifies the energy transfer rate from its gradient
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heated 100 ml of water in a beaker and recorded the temperature every minute, could they plot the results on a graph and use the data to work out roughly how much energy was transferred to the water?
topics.descriptionZh: 规划并开展实验以测量加热过程中转移的能量，包括使用公式 Q = mcΔT，记录温度随时间的变化，并评估误差来源。
evidenceZh: 在加热实验中使用温度计和秒表记录温度随时间的变化
应用 Q = mcΔT 计算传递给被加热物质的能量
识别加热实验中的能量损失来源（如向周围环境散热）并提出改进建议
绘制温度-时间图表，并通过其斜率识别能量转移速率
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在烧杯中加热 100 毫升水并每分钟记录一次温度，他们能将结果绘制成图表并利用这些数据粗略计算出传递给水多少能量吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Ohm's Law: voltage, current, resistance
topics.description: Apply Ohm's Law (V = IR) to calculate current, voltage, or resistance in a simple circuit, and explain that resistance opposes the flow of current
evidence: States Ohm's Law as V = IR and identifies the units for each quantity
Rearranges V = IR to find the unknown value given the other two
Explains that resistance opposes current flow and identifies factors that affect resistance (material, length, thickness)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} doubles the resistance in a circuit while keeping the battery the same, can they predict what happens to the current and explain using the V = IR formula?
topics.nameZh: 欧姆定律 (Ohm's Law)：电压 (voltage)、电流 (current)、电阻 (resistance)
topics.descriptionZh: 应用欧姆定律 (V = IR) 计算简单电路中的电流 (current)、电压 (voltage) 或电阻 (resistance)，并解释电阻会阻碍电流的流动
evidenceZh: 表述欧姆定律为 V = IR，并指出每个物理量的单位
对公式 V = IR 进行变形，在已知另外两个量的情况下求出未知量
解释电阻 (resistance) 会阻碍电流 (current) 流动，并指出影响电阻的因素：材料 (material)、长度 (length)、粗细 (thickness)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在保持电池不变的情况下将电路中的电阻 (resistance) 增加一倍，他们能预测电流 (current) 会发生什么变化，并使用 V = IR 公式进行解释吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Power: watts and energy per second
topics.description: Define power as the rate of energy transfer (power = energy ÷ time, measured in watts), and compare energy transfer rates in different everyday contexts
evidence: States the definition of power and gives its unit (watt)
Uses P = E/t to calculate power, energy, or time given the other two quantities
Compares the power ratings of common appliances and explains what the rating means
Explains why a higher-powered device does the same job faster but uses more energy
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was comparing a 100 W light bulb with a 10 W LED, could they explain what those numbers mean and calculate how much energy each uses in an hour?
topics.nameZh: 功率 (Power)：瓦特 (Watt) 与每秒能量 (Energy per second)
topics.descriptionZh: 将功率 (Power) 定义为能量 (Energy) 转移的速率（功率 = 能量 ÷ 时间，以瓦特 (Watt) 为单位），并比较不同日常生活场景中的能量转移速率。
evidenceZh: 能够陈述功率 (Power) 的定义并说出其单位（瓦特 (Watt)）
能够使用公式 P = E/t，在已知另外两个量的情况下计算功率 (Power)、能量 (Energy) 或时间 (Time)
能够比较常见家用电器的功率额定值 (Power ratings)，并解释该额定值的含义
能够解释为什么功率 (Power) 更高的设备能更快完成相同的工作，但会消耗更多的能量 (Energy)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 正在比较一个 100 W（瓦特）的灯泡和一个 10 W（瓦特）的 LED 灯，他们能解释这些数字的含义，并计算出每个灯在一小时内消耗了多少能量 (Energy) 吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Renewable vs non-renewable energy
topics.description: Distinguish between renewable energy resources (solar, wind, hydroelectric, tidal, geothermal, biomass) and non-renewable resources (coal, oil, gas, nuclear), comparing their advantages, disadvantages, and environmental impacts
evidence: Lists at least four renewable and three non-renewable energy resources
Explains what makes a resource renewable or non-renewable
Compares the environmental impact of at least two different energy sources (e.g. wind vs coal)
Discusses trade-offs between cost, reliability, and environmental impact in choosing energy resources
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard about a plan to build a new wind farm in your area, could they explain what the advantages and disadvantages would be compared to a gas-fired power station — both for the environment and for reliability?
topics.nameZh: 可再生能源与不可再生能源
topics.descriptionZh: 区分可再生能源资源（太阳能 solar、风能 wind、水力发电 hydroelectric、潮汐能 tidal、地热能 geothermal、生物质能 biomass）和不可再生能源资源（煤炭 coal、石油 oil、天然气 gas、核能 nuclear），并比较它们的优缺点及环境影响。
evidenceZh: 列出至少四种可再生能源和三种不可再生能源资源
解释是什么使一种资源成为可再生或不可再生资源
比较至少两种不同能源（例如风能 wind 与煤炭 coal）的环境影响
讨论在选择能源资源时，成本、可靠性和环境影响之间的权衡 (trade-offs)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 听说计划在你所在的地区建设一个新的风力发电场 (wind farm)，他们能否解释与燃气发电站 (gas-fired power station) 相比，在环境和可靠性方面各有什么优缺点？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Series vs parallel circuits
topics.description: Describe and apply the rules for current, voltage, and resistance in series and parallel circuits, and explain the practical uses of each circuit type
evidence: States the rules for current and voltage in series circuits (current same everywhere; voltages add up)
States the rules for current and voltage in parallel circuits (voltages same across each branch; currents add up)
Explains why household wiring uses parallel circuits and identifies the advantage of each type
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the lights in your home don't all switch off when you turn off one room's light, but a string of old-fashioned Christmas lights does go off if one bulb breaks?
topics.nameZh: 串联电路与并联电路 (Series vs parallel circuits)
topics.descriptionZh: 描述并应用串联电路和并联电路中电流（current）、电压（voltage）和电阻（resistance）的规律，并解释每种电路类型的实际应用
evidenceZh: 阐述串联电路中电流和电压的规律（电流处处相等；各部分电压之和等于总电压）
阐述并联电路中电流和电压的规律（各支路电压相等；各支路电流之和等于总电流）
解释家庭电路为何采用并联电路，并指出每种电路类型的优势
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释一下，为什么关掉家里一个房间的灯时，其他房间的灯不会全灭，而一串老式圣诞彩灯如果坏了一个灯泡就会全灭吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Forces Vocabulary
topics.description: Name and describe forces using precise vocabulary — force, push, pull, twist, stretch, squash, contact force, non-contact force, gravity, weight, friction, air resistance, upthrust — and distinguish between forces that require physical contact and forces that act at a distance
evidence: Correctly name the force acting in at least five given scenarios (e.g. 'friction slows the sledge', 'gravity pulls the apple')
Distinguish between contact forces (friction, upthrust) and non-contact forces (gravity, magnetism) using the correct terms
Use 'weight' correctly as a force — distinct from 'mass' — in descriptions
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} slides down a slide and slows near the bottom, can they name the force responsible and spell it correctly?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用精确的词汇来命名和描述力——力（force）、推（push）、拉（pull）、扭转（twist）、拉伸（stretch）、挤压（squash）、接触力（contact force）、非接触力（non-contact force）、重力（gravity）、重量（weight）、摩擦力（friction）、空气阻力（air resistance）、向上托力（upthrust）——并区分需要物理接触的力和远距离作用的力。
evidenceZh: 在至少五个给定场景中正确命名作用的力（例如，‘摩擦力使雪橇减速’，‘重力使苹果下落’）
使用正确的术语区分接触力（摩擦力、向上托力）和非接触力（重力、磁力）
在描述中正确地将‘重量’（weight）作为一种力来使用——将其与‘质量’（mass）区分开来
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 从滑梯上滑下并在靠近底部时减速，他们能说出导致减速的力并正确拼写该术语吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Pushes & Pulls
topics.description: Understand that pushes and pulls are forces that can change the speed or direction of an object's motion, and compare the effects of different strengths and directions
evidence: Describe a push and a pull as types of force that make objects move, speed up, slow down, or change direction
Compare the effects of a gentle push versus a strong push on the same object
Predict the direction an object will move based on the direction of the applied force
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that pushing a toy car harder makes it go faster, and pushing it sideways makes it change direction?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解推和拉是能够改变物体运动速度或方向的力（forces），并比较不同大小和方向的力所产生的效果
evidenceZh: 描述推和拉作为力的类型，说明它们如何使物体运动、加速、减速或改变方向
比较对同一个物体轻轻推和用力推所产生的不同效果
根据施加力的方向，预测物体将会移动的方向
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释更用力地推玩具小车会让它跑得更快，而侧着推它会使其改变方向？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Testing Push & Pull Designs
topics.description: Analyse data to determine if a design solution works as intended to change the speed or direction of an object with a push or pull
evidence: Test a simple design (e.g. ramp, launcher) and collect data on whether it meets the goal
Analyse results to determine if the design works as intended
Suggest modifications based on the data to improve the design's performance
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} builds a ramp to make a ball go into a cup, can they test it and figure out what to change if the ball misses?
topics.descriptionZh: 分析数据以确定设计方案是否能按预期通过推（push）或拉（pull）来改变物体的速度（speed）或方向（direction）。
evidenceZh: 测试简单的设计（如斜面、发射器），并收集数据以确认其是否达到目标
分析结果以确定该设计是否按预期发挥作用
根据数据提出修改建议，以提高设计的性能
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 搭建了一个斜面想让球滚进杯子里，他们能进行测试，并在球没进杯子时找出需要调整的地方吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Contact & Non-Contact Forces
topics.description: Notice that some forces need contact between two objects (contact forces) while magnetic forces can act at a distance (non-contact forces)
evidence: Define contact forces as those needing objects to touch (e.g. push, pull, friction)
Define non-contact forces as those acting at a distance (e.g. magnetism)
Sort examples of forces into contact and non-contact categories
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why you have to touch a ball to kick it, but a magnet can pull a paperclip without touching it?
topics.descriptionZh: 请注意，有些力需要两个物体相互接触才能产生（接触力，Contact forces），而磁力等可以在不接触的情况下隔空作用（非接触力，Non-contact forces）。
evidenceZh: 将接触力（Contact forces）定义为需要物体相互接触才能产生的力（例如：推力、拉力、摩擦力）
将非接触力（Non-contact forces）定义为可以隔空作用的力（例如：磁力）
将各种力的例子分类到接触力和非接触力类别中
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释一下为什么踢足球时必须接触到球，而磁铁却能在不接触的情况下吸起回形针吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Drawing Force Diagrams
topics.description: Draw and interpret force diagrams showing forces as labelled arrows — where the arrow's length represents the force's magnitude and its direction shows which way the force acts; show multiple forces on one object; identify from the diagram whether forces are balanced (equal arrows in opposite directions, no resultant) or unbalanced (arrows of different sizes, producing a resultant); represent the resultant with a single arrow
evidence: Draw a force diagram with labelled arrows showing direction and relative size for at least two forces acting on an object
Use their diagram to explain whether forces are balanced or unbalanced and what will happen to the object
Add a resultant force arrow to a diagram and explain how they calculated it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is asked to draw a diagram of all the forces acting on a stationary book on a table, can they draw two arrows — one pointing down for gravity and one pointing up from the table — and explain why, if they're balanced, the book doesn't move?
topics.nameZh: 绘制力的示意图 (Drawing Force Diagrams)
topics.descriptionZh: 绘制并解读力的示意图，用带标签的箭头来表示力——箭头的长度代表力的大小（magnitude），箭头的方向代表力的作用方向；在一个物体上画出多个力；通过示意图判断力是平衡的（方向相反且长度相等的箭头，没有合力）还是不平衡的（长度不同的箭头，会产生合力）；并用一个箭头来表示合力（resultant force）。
evidenceZh: 绘制一个力的示意图，用带标签的箭头表示作用在物体上的至少两个力的方向和相对大小
利用绘制的示意图来解释力是平衡的还是不平衡的，以及物体接下来会发生什么
在示意图上添加一个合力（resultant force）箭头，并解释是如何计算出该合力的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果让 {{name}} 画出一本静止在桌子上的书所受的所有力的示意图，他们能画出两个箭头吗——一个指向下方表示重力（gravity），一个指向上方表示桌子的支持力——并且解释为什么在力平衡的情况下，书不会移动？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Friction & Surfaces
topics.description: Compare how things move on different surfaces, noticing that some surfaces create more friction than others
evidence: Observe and compare how the same object moves on at least three different surfaces
Describe that rough surfaces slow objects down more than smooth surfaces
Use the word 'friction' to explain why movement differs on different surfaces
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a toy car rolls further on a smooth wooden floor than on carpet?
topics.descriptionZh: 比较物体在不同表面上的运动情况，注意有些表面产生的摩擦力比其他表面更大。
evidenceZh: 观察并比较同一物体在至少三种不同表面上的运动情况
描述粗糙表面比光滑表面更能减缓物体的运动
使用“摩擦力 (friction)”一词来解释为什么在不同表面上的运动会有所不同
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么玩具车在光滑的木地板上比在地毯上滚得更远？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Magnetic Materials
topics.description: Observe how magnets attract or repel each other and attract some materials and not others
evidence: Demonstrate that magnets attract some materials (iron, steel, nickel) but not others (wood, plastic, copper)
Show that two magnets can either attract (pull together) or repel (push apart)
Test at least six objects and correctly predict which are magnetic
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} test a magnet on different objects around the house and predict which ones will stick?
topics.descriptionZh: 观察磁铁如何相互吸引或排斥，以及它们如何吸引某些材料而不吸引其他材料。
evidenceZh: 证明磁铁能吸引某些材料（铁 iron、钢 steel、镍 nickel），但不能吸引其他材料（木头、塑料、铜 copper）。
展示两块磁铁既可以相互吸引（吸在一起 attract），也可以相互排斥（推开 repel）。
测试至少六件物品，并正确预测哪些具有磁性（magnetic）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能用磁铁测试家里的不同物品，并预测哪些会被吸住吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Magnetic Poles
topics.description: Describe magnets as having two poles (north and south) and predict whether two magnets will attract or repel based on which poles face each other
evidence: Identify and label the north and south poles of a magnet
State the rule: like poles repel, opposite poles attract
Predict the outcome of bringing two magnets together based on their pole orientation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} hold two magnets together and explain why they sometimes snap together and sometimes push apart, based on which ends are facing?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述磁铁具有两个磁极（北极和南极），并根据相对的磁极预测两块磁铁是会相互吸引 (attract) 还是相互排斥 (repel)
evidenceZh: 识别并标出磁铁的北极和南极
说明规律：同极相斥 (like poles repel)，异极相吸 (opposite poles attract)
根据磁极的朝向预测两块磁铁靠近时的结果
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否将两块磁铁拿在一起，并根据哪两端相对，解释为什么它们有时会吸在一起，有时会推开？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Balanced & Unbalanced Forces
topics.description: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence of the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces on the motion of an object
evidence: Define balanced forces (equal in size, opposite in direction — no change in motion) and unbalanced forces (cause motion to change)
Plan a fair test investigating how different force sizes affect an object's motion
Use results as evidence to explain when forces are balanced versus unbalanced
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a book sitting on a table doesn't move (balanced forces) but slides when you push it (unbalanced forces)?
topics.descriptionZh: 计划并实施调查，提供证据证明平衡力和非平衡力对物体运动的影响
evidenceZh: 定义平衡力（大小相等、方向相反——运动状态不改变）和非平衡力（导致运动状态改变）
设计公平测试，探究不同大小的力如何影响物体的运动
利用实验结果作为证据，解释何时物体受力平衡，何时受力不平衡
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释为什么放在桌子上的书不会移动（平衡力），但推它时就会滑动（非平衡力）？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Predicting Motion Patterns
topics.description: Make observations and measurements of an object's motion to provide evidence that a pattern can be used to predict future motion
evidence: Measure an object's motion (distance, speed, direction) under different conditions
Identify a pattern in the data (e.g. steeper ramp = further roll)
Use the pattern to make and test a prediction about future motion
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} rolls a ball down ramps of different heights, can they spot the pattern and predict how far it will roll from a new height?
topics.nameZh: 预测运动模式（Predicting Motion Patterns）
topics.descriptionZh: 对物体的运动进行观察和测量，以提供证据表明可以利用模式（pattern）来预测未来的运动
evidenceZh: 在不同条件下测量物体的运动（距离 distance、速度 speed、方向 direction）
在数据中识别出模式（pattern）（例如：斜坡越陡 = 滚得越远）
利用该模式（pattern）对未来的运动做出预测并进行测试
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 让球从不同高度的斜坡上滚下，他们能发现其中的模式（pattern）并预测球从新高度滚下时会滚多远吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Air Resistance & Friction
topics.description: Identify the effects of air resistance, water resistance, and friction, and understand that these forces act between moving surfaces to oppose motion
evidence: Define air resistance, water resistance, and friction as forces that oppose motion
Give everyday examples of each force and explain how they slow things down
Describe how these forces depend on factors like speed, surface area, or surface texture
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a parachute slows you down, why swimming is harder than walking, and why bike brakes use rubber pads?
topics.nameZh: 空气阻力 (Air Resistance) 与摩擦力 (Friction)
topics.descriptionZh: 识别空气阻力、水阻力和摩擦力的影响，并理解这些力作用于运动表面之间以阻碍运动
evidenceZh: 将空气阻力、水阻力和摩擦力定义为阻碍运动的力
给出每种力的日常例子，并解释它们是如何使物体减速的
描述这些力如何依赖于速度、表面积或表面纹理等因素
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么降落伞能让人减速，为什么游泳比走路更费力，以及为什么自行车刹车使用橡胶垫？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Force & Motion Vocabulary
topics.description: Use technical vocabulary for force and motion — balanced forces, unbalanced forces, resultant force, acceleration, deceleration, speed, moment, lever, fulcrum, mechanical advantage — and apply these when explaining and predicting how forces affect the motion and position of objects
evidence: Distinguish between balanced and unbalanced forces and describe the effect of each on an object's motion
Use 'resultant force' correctly when describing the net effect of two or more forces acting on an object
Apply 'moment', 'lever', and 'fulcrum' correctly when describing how simple machines work
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a seesaw stays level when two people of different weights sit at different distances — using words like 'balanced forces' or 'moment'?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用力与运动的专业词汇——平衡力（balanced forces）、非平衡力（unbalanced forces）、合力（resultant force）、加速度（acceleration）、减速度（deceleration）、速度（speed）、力矩（moment）、杠杆（lever）、支点（fulcrum）、机械效益（mechanical advantage）——并在解释和预测力如何影响物体的运动和位置时运用这些词汇。
evidenceZh: 区分平衡力和非平衡力，并描述它们各自对物体运动的影响
在描述两个或多个力作用于物体的净效果时，正确使用‘合力’（resultant force）
在描述简单机械的工作原理时，正确应用‘力矩’（moment）、‘杠杆’（lever）和‘支点’（fulcrum）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否使用‘平衡力’（balanced forces）或‘力矩’（moment）等词汇，解释为什么两个体重不同的人坐在不同距离时，跷跷板能保持水平？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Gravity & Falling Objects
topics.description: Explain that unsupported objects fall towards the Earth because of the force of gravity acting between the Earth and the falling object
evidence: Define gravity as a force of attraction between the Earth and objects
Explain that unsupported objects fall because gravity pulls them towards the Earth
Give examples showing gravity in action (dropping objects, jumping, water flowing downhill)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why everything falls downwards when you let go of it, and name the force that causes this?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释没有支撑的物体会落向地球，这是因为地球与下落物体之间存在重力（Gravity）的作用。
evidenceZh: 将重力（Gravity）定义为地球与物体之间的吸引力
解释没有支撑的物体会下落，是因为重力将它们拉向地球
举出展示重力作用的例子（掉落物体、跳跃、水往低处流）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么松开手后所有东西都会往下掉，并说出导致这一现象的力（重力）的名称？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Levers, Pulleys & Gears
topics.description: Recognise that some mechanisms including levers, pulleys, and gears allow a smaller force to have a greater effect
evidence: Describe how a lever works: effort at one end moves a load at the other, with a pivot in between
Explain how a pulley changes the direction of a force and can make lifting easier
Describe how gears transfer and change the size or direction of forces
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a see-saw, a pulley on a flagpole, or the gears on a bicycle make it easier to move heavy things with less effort?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解一些机械装置，包括杠杆、滑轮和齿轮，能够用较小的力产生更大的效果。
evidenceZh: 描述杠杆 (Lever) 是如何工作的：在中间的支点 (Pivot) 两边，一端施加动力 (Effort)，另一端移动重物 (Load)。
解释滑轮 (Pulley) 如何改变力的方向，并使提升重物变得更轻松。
描述齿轮 (Gears) 如何传递并改变力的大小或方向。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释跷跷板、旗杆上的滑轮或自行车上的齿轮是如何让我们用更少的力气移动重物的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Reading Distance-Time Graphs
topics.description: Read and plot distance-time graphs for moving objects; interpret the gradient (steepness) of a line as speed; identify stationary periods (horizontal sections), constant speed (straight diagonal lines), and relative speeds by comparing gradients; calculate average speed from the gradient of a straight-line segment using speed = distance ÷ time
evidence: Read a distance-time graph and describe what is happening at each stage — moving, stopped, returning
Calculate speed from the gradient of a straight section of a distance-time graph
Sketch a distance-time graph from a written description of a journey with stops and speed changes
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a distance-time graph of a journey with a flat section in the middle, can they explain what was happening then — and point to which part of the graph shows the fastest speed?
topics.descriptionZh: 阅读和绘制运动物体的距离-时间图像；将线条的斜率（陡峭程度）解释为速度；识别静止时段（水平线段）、匀速运动（直线段），并通过比较斜率来比较相对速度；使用速度 = 距离 ÷ 时间，从直线段的斜率计算平均速度
evidenceZh: 阅读距离-时间图像，并描述每个阶段发生的情况——运动、停止、返回
从距离-时间图像的直线段斜率计算速度
根据包含停顿和速度变化的旅程文字描述，绘制距离-时间图像
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到一段旅程的距离-时间图像，其中间有一段水平的部分，他们能解释当时发生了什么吗——并指出图像的哪一部分显示了最快的速度？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Magnetic Fields
topics.description: Describe magnetic poles (north and south), explain attraction and repulsion between poles, describe magnetic field lines plotted using a compass, and explain the Earth's magnetic field and its practical uses
evidence: States the rule for attraction and repulsion of magnetic poles
Draws the magnetic field pattern around a bar magnet from memory or compass readings
Explains why a compass needle points north
Explains that the Earth has a magnetic field and describes how it is used for navigation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} used a compass and iron filings to map the magnetic field around a bar magnet, could they describe what pattern the field lines make and explain why a compass needle always points roughly north?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述磁极（南极和北极），解释磁极之间的吸引与排斥，描述使用指南针绘制的磁感线（magnetic field lines），并解释地球磁场（Earth's magnetic field）及其实际应用。
evidenceZh: 阐述磁极吸引与排斥的规律
凭记忆或根据指南针读数，绘制条形磁铁（bar magnet）周围的磁场分布图
解释指南针指针为何指向北方
解释地球存在磁场，并描述其如何应用于导航
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 使用指南针和铁屑（iron filings）来绘制条形磁铁（bar magnet）周围的磁场，他们能否描述磁感线（magnetic field lines）形成的图案，并解释为什么指南针指针总是大致指向北方？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Mass vs Weight
topics.description: Distinguish between mass (amount of matter, measured in kg) and weight (gravitational force, measured in N), use the equation weight = mass × gravitational field strength, and explain why g differs on other planets and stars
evidence: Explains the difference between mass and weight with correct units for each
Calculates weight using W = mg with g = 10 N/kg on Earth
Predicts what would happen to an object's weight on the Moon or Jupiter
Explains why mass stays constant but weight changes in different gravitational fields
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} weighed themselves on bathroom scales and was then asked what they would weigh on the Moon, could they explain the difference between mass and weight and work out a rough answer?
topics.descriptionZh: 区分质量（物质的量，以千克 kg 为单位）和重量（重力，以牛顿 N 为单位），使用公式：重量 = 质量 × 重力场强度 (gravitational field strength)，并解释为什么重力 (g) 在其他行星和恒星上会有所不同。
evidenceZh: 能解释质量和重量的区别，并使用正确的单位
能在地球上使用 W = mg 公式（其中 g = 10 N/kg）计算重量
能预测物体在月球或木星上的重量会发生什么变化
能解释为什么在不同重力场中质量保持不变，而重量会发生变化
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 用体重秤称了自己的体重，然后被问到在月球上会多重，他们能解释质量和重量的区别并计算出一个大概的答案吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Relative Motion
topics.description: Explain relative motion — how the apparent speed and direction of an object depends on the observer's own motion — using everyday examples such as trains and cars passing
evidence: Explains why a train moving at the same speed in the same direction as another appears stationary to passengers on that train
Calculates relative speed when two objects move towards or away from each other
Explains why the frame of reference matters when describing motion
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was on a train and another train passed going the same direction but faster, could they explain why it looks slow even if it's actually travelling at high speed?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释相对运动——即一个物体看起来的速度和方向是如何受到观察者自身运动影响的——并通过火车和汽车擦肩而过等生活中的小例子来说明。
evidenceZh: 解释为什么一列与另一列火车同向同速行驶时，在车上乘客看来它仿佛是静止的
计算两个物体相向或背向运动时的相对速度 (Relative Speed)
解释为什么在描述运动时参考系 (Frame of Reference) 的选择非常重要
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}坐在一列火车上，另一列同向但速度更快的火车从旁边驶过，他们能解释为什么那列火车看起来开得很慢，即使它实际上正以极高的速度行驶吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Resultant Forces
topics.description: Describe forces as vector quantities with both magnitude and direction, distinguish between balanced forces (zero resultant, no change in motion) and unbalanced forces (non-zero resultant, causes acceleration or deceleration)
evidence: Explains what a vector quantity is and why force is a vector
Calculates the resultant force when two forces act in the same or opposite directions on an object
Explains what happens to an object's motion when forces are balanced vs unbalanced
Draws free body diagrams showing all forces on a stationary object (e.g. a book on a table)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was pushing a heavy box along the floor but it wasn't moving, could they explain all the forces acting on it and why it stays still even though you're pushing?
topics.descriptionZh: 将力描述为同时具有大小和方向的矢量（vector quantity），并区分平衡力（合力为零，运动状态不变）与非平衡力（合力不为零，会引起加速或减速）。
evidenceZh: 解释什么是矢量（vector quantity）以及为什么力是矢量
计算当两个力沿相同或相反方向作用于物体时的合力（resultant force）
解释当力平衡与不平衡时物体的运动状态会发生什么变化
绘制受力分析图（free body diagrams），显示静止物体（例如桌子上的书）所受的所有力
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 正在地板上推一个沉重的箱子但箱子没有移动，他们能解释作用在箱子上的所有力，并说明为什么即使你在推它，它仍然保持静止吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Speed & Distance-Time Graphs
topics.description: Calculate average speed using the equation speed = distance ÷ time, represent journeys on distance-time graphs, and interpret gradient as speed and flat sections as stationary periods
evidence: Uses speed = distance ÷ time to calculate average speed with correct units (m/s, km/h)
Draws a distance-time graph for a given journey with correct axes and labels
Reads a distance-time graph to determine speed, stopping points, and direction of travel
Identifies which section of a distance-time graph represents the fastest speed
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} tracked a cycle ride on a map and knew how far they went and how long it took, could they calculate the average speed — and then sketch a rough graph showing the journey including a stop for lunch?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用公式 速度 = 距离 ÷ 时间 (speed = distance ÷ time) 计算平均速度，在距离-时间图像 (distance-time graphs) 上表示行程，并将斜率 (gradient) 解释为速度，将平缓部分解释为静止时段
evidenceZh: 使用 速度 = 距离 ÷ 时间 计算平均速度，并使用正确的单位（米/秒 (m/s)、千米/小时 (km/h)）
为给定的行程绘制距离-时间图像，具有正确的坐标轴和标签
读取距离-时间图像以确定速度、停靠点和行驶方向
识别距离-时间图像的哪一部分代表最高的速度
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在地图上记录了一次骑行，知道骑行了多远以及花了多长时间，他们能计算出平均速度吗？——然后能画出一个粗略的图像，展示出包括午餐休息在内的整个行程吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Deformation & Fluid Pressure
topics.description: Explain forces associated with deforming objects (elastic and inelastic deformation), thermal expansion and contraction of materials, and how fluid pressure acts in all directions and increases with depth
evidence: Distinguishes elastic deformation (returns to shape) from inelastic/plastic deformation (permanently changed)
Explains why bridges and railway tracks have expansion gaps
Explains why pressure increases with depth in a liquid (e.g. why deep-sea divers need pressure suits)
Gives an everyday example of thermal expansion causing a problem or being used usefully
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} noticed the lid on a jar was very tight, could they explain why running it under hot water helps — and what's happening to the metal as it heats up?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释与物体形变（弹性形变和非弹性/塑性形变）相关的力、材料的热胀冷缩现象，以及流体压强如何向各个方向作用并随深度增加。
evidenceZh: 区分弹性形变（恢复原状）与非弹性/塑性形变（永久变形）
解释为什么桥梁和铁轨留有伸缩缝（膨胀间隙）
解释为什么液体中的压强随深度增加而增大（例如，为什么深海潜水员需要抗压潜水服）
给出一个日常生活中热胀冷缩引起问题或被巧妙利用的例子
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 注意到罐头瓶盖得很紧，他们能解释为什么在热水下冲洗会有帮助——以及金属在受热时发生了什么变化吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Electromagnets
topics.description: Describe the magnetic effect of an electric current (a current-carrying wire produces a magnetic field), and investigate how the strength of an electromagnet depends on current, number of coil turns, and core material
evidence: Describes that a current-carrying wire produces a circular magnetic field
Lists three factors that affect electromagnet strength: current size, number of coil turns, and core material
Explains why an electromagnet can be switched on and off, unlike a permanent magnet
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} built an electromagnet using a battery, wire, and iron nail, could they describe two ways to make it pick up more paperclips — and explain why it stops working when the circuit is switched off?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述电流的磁效应（通电导线会产生磁场），并探究电磁铁的磁性强弱如何取决于电流大小、线圈匝数（number of coil turns）和铁芯材料（core material）。
evidenceZh: 描述通电导线会产生环形磁场（circular magnetic field）
列出影响电磁铁磁性强弱的三个因素：电流大小、线圈匝数和铁芯材料
解释为什么电磁铁可以控制磁性的通断，而永磁体（permanent magnet）则不能
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 用电池、导线和铁钉制作了一个电磁铁，他们能说出两种让它吸起更多回形针的方法吗？——并能解释为什么断开电路后它就不工作了吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Investigating Forces
topics.description: Plan and carry out investigations into forces, including measuring force with a newton meter, investigating Hooke's Law, and collecting and interpreting motion data to test Newton's laws
evidence: Uses a newton meter correctly to measure forces in newtons
Sets up and conducts a Hooke's Law investigation, recording force and extension and plotting a graph
Identifies and controls variables in a force investigation
Calculates acceleration from force and mass data and compares with experimental results
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} set up an experiment hanging weights on a spring and measuring how much it stretched, could they describe how they would make it a fair test, record the results, and show what Hooke's Law looks like on a graph?
topics.descriptionZh: 计划并开展关于力的探究活动，包括使用测力计（newton meter）测量力、探究胡克定律（Hooke's Law），以及收集和解读运动数据以验证牛顿定律（Newton's laws）。
evidenceZh: 正确使用测力计（newton meter）以牛顿（newtons）为单位测量力
搭建并开展胡克定律（Hooke's Law）探究实验，记录力和伸长量，并绘制图表
在力的探究实验中识别并控制变量
根据力和质量数据计算加速度（acceleration），并与实验结果进行比较
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 设计了一个实验，把重物挂在弹簧上并测量它伸长了多少，他们能描述如何设计一个公平实验（fair test）、记录结果，并在图表上展示胡克定律（Hooke's Law）的规律吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Moments, Pressure & Hooke's Law
topics.description: Calculate the turning effect (moment = force × perpendicular distance), explain how pressure is transmitted equally in liquids (Pascal's principle) and the concept of atmospheric pressure, and describe Hooke's Law (extension ∝ force up to the elastic limit)
evidence: Calculates the moment of a force and uses the principle of moments to solve lever problems
Explains why hydraulic systems can multiply force (pressure transmitted equally)
States Hooke's Law and plots force-extension graphs identifying the elastic limit
Calculates spring constant k from a force-extension graph (k = F/x)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was using a long spanner to loosen a tight bolt, could they explain why a longer spanner makes it easier — and work out what force would be needed with a spanner of a specific length?
topics.descriptionZh: 计算转动效果（力矩 = 力 × 垂直距离），解释液体中压强如何均匀传递（帕斯卡定律）以及大气压强的概念，并描述胡克定律（在弹性限度内，伸长量 ∝ 力）
evidenceZh: 计算力的力矩，并利用力矩原理解决杠杆问题
解释为什么液压系统可以放大作用力（压强均匀传递）
阐述胡克定律并绘制力-伸长量图像以识别弹性限度
根据力-伸长量图像计算弹簧劲度系数 k（k = F/x）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 正在使用一把长扳手拧松一个紧固的螺栓，他们能否解释为什么更长的扳手会更省力——并计算出如果使用特定长度的扳手需要施加多大的力？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Newton's First & Second Laws
topics.description: State and apply Newton's First Law (an object stays at rest or constant velocity unless acted on by a resultant force) and Second Law (force = mass × acceleration), including the relationship between mass, force, and acceleration
evidence: States Newton's First Law and gives a real example (e.g. why a moving spacecraft doesn't need engines in space)
Uses F = ma to calculate force, mass, or acceleration given the other two quantities
Explains why a heavier object requires more force to achieve the same acceleration
Explains why seatbelts are needed in cars using Newton's First Law
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why you need a seatbelt in a car but not when sitting still, could they explain what Newton's First Law says about moving objects — and then calculate how much force a 60 kg person experiences in a sudden stop?
topics.nameZh: 牛顿第一定律与第二定律
topics.descriptionZh: 阐述并应用牛顿第一定律（物体在不受合外力作用时保持静止或匀速直线运动状态）和第二定律（力 = 质量 × 加速度），包括质量、力和加速度之间的关系
evidenceZh: 阐述牛顿第一定律并给出实际例子（例如：为什么在太空中飞行的航天器不需要开启发动机）
使用 F = ma 在已知另外两个量的情况下计算力、质量或加速度
解释为什么质量更大的物体需要更大的力才能获得相同的加速度
运用牛顿第一定律解释为什么乘车时需要系安全带
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果有人问 {{name}} 为什么在汽车里需要系安全带，而静止坐着时却不需要，他们能否解释牛顿第一定律对运动物体的描述——然后计算一个60公斤的人在急刹车时会受到多大的力？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Newton's Third Law
topics.description: State and apply Newton's Third Law: every force has an equal and opposite reaction force acting on a different object, distinguishing action-reaction pairs from balanced forces
evidence: States Newton's Third Law correctly, identifying both the action and reaction force and the objects they act on
Gives at least two real-world examples (e.g. rocket propulsion, swimmer pushing off a wall)
Distinguishes a Newton's Third Law pair from balanced forces on the same object
Explains why a gun recoils when fired using Newton's Third Law
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a video of a rocket launching into space, could they explain what force is pushing the rocket upward and where that force comes from — and which law of motion that demonstrates?
topics.descriptionZh: 陈述并应用牛顿第三定律：每一个力都有一个大小相等、方向相反的反作用力作用在不同的物体上，并能区分作用力与反作用力对和平衡力
evidenceZh: 正确陈述牛顿第三定律，指出作用力和反作用力以及它们各自作用的物体
给出至少两个现实生活中的例子（例如火箭推进、游泳者蹬壁）
区分牛顿第三定律中的作用力与反作用力对和作用于同一物体上的平衡力
运用牛顿第三定律解释开枪时枪身后坐的原因
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到一段火箭发射升空的视频，他们能否解释是什么力在向上推火箭，这个力来自哪里——以及这体现了哪条运动定律？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Motors & the Motor Effect
topics.description: Explain the motor effect as the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field, and describe how this principle is used in electric motors and loudspeakers
evidence: Explains that a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field experiences a force (the motor effect)
Predicts how reversing the current or reversing the magnetic field affects the direction of the force
Describes how the motor effect is applied in an electric motor and in a loudspeaker
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked inside an electric motor or the back of a loudspeaker, could they explain why the coil of wire moves — and what would happen to the movement if you reversed the direction of the current?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释电动机效应（Motor Effect），即磁场中载流导体所受到的力，并描述这一原理是如何在电动机（Electric Motors）和扬声器（Loudspeakers）中应用的。
evidenceZh: 解释磁场中的载流导体（Current-carrying Conductor）会受到力的作用（即电动机效应）
预测反转电流方向或反转磁场（Magnetic Field）方向会如何影响力的方向
描述电动机效应是如何应用于电动机和扬声器中的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 观察电动机的内部或扬声器的背面，他们能解释为什么线圈（Coil）会移动吗——如果反转电流方向，它的移动会发生什么变化？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Caring for minibeasts
topics.description: Caring for minibeasts: observing minibeasts gently, handling them carefully, putting them back where you found them. Why minibeasts matter — they help gardens grow, break down dead leaves, and feed other animals.
evidence: Demonstrate careful handling of a minibeast such as letting a woodlouse walk onto a hand rather than grabbing it
Explain one reason why minibeasts are important, such as bees helping flowers grow or worms helping soil
State that minibeasts should be returned to where they were found after observing them
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} finds a minibeast, do they handle it gently and put it back — and can they tell you why minibeasts are important for the garden?
topics.descriptionZh: 关爱微小生物（minibeasts）：温柔地观察微小生物，小心地对待它们，观察后将它们放回原处。微小生物的重要性——它们帮助花园植物生长、分解枯叶，并为其他动物提供食物。
evidenceZh: 展示对微小生物的小心处理，例如让鼠妇（woodlouse）爬到手心上，而不是直接抓取它
解释微小生物重要的一个原因，例如蜜蜂帮助花朵生长或蚯蚓帮助改善土壤
说明观察完微小生物后，应将它们放回发现它们的地方
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 发现微小生物时，他们是否会温柔地对待它并将其放回原处——并且能告诉你微小生物对花园为什么重要吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Caterpillar to butterfly
topics.description: Caterpillar to butterfly: the life cycle of a butterfly as an observable transformation. Egg → caterpillar → chrysalis → butterfly. The idea that one creature can change its whole form. Classroom butterfly kits, The Very Hungry Caterpillar.
evidence: Describe the four stages of a butterfly's life in order: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly
Explain that the caterpillar and the butterfly are the same creature at different stages of life
Retell or draw the transformation from caterpillar to butterfly after reading a story or watching it happen
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watched a caterpillar make a chrysalis — or read The Very Hungry Caterpillar — could they tell you what happens next and how it becomes a butterfly?
topics.descriptionZh: 毛毛虫变蝴蝶：将蝴蝶的生命周期作为一种可观察的转变过程。卵（egg）→ 毛毛虫（caterpillar）→ 蛹（chrysalis）→ 蝴蝶（butterfly）。理解同一个生物能够完全改变其形态的概念。课堂蝴蝶观察套装，绘本《好饿的毛毛虫》。
evidenceZh: 按顺序描述蝴蝶生命的四个阶段：卵（egg）、毛毛虫（caterpillar）、蛹（chrysalis）、蝴蝶（butterfly）
解释毛毛虫和蝴蝶是同一个生物在不同生命阶段的形态
在阅读相关故事或观察其变化过程后，复述或画出从毛毛虫到蝴蝶的转变过程
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 观察到毛毛虫结蛹——或者阅读了《好饿的毛毛虫》——他们能告诉你接下来会发生什么，以及它是如何变成蝴蝶的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Common minibeasts: naming and recognising
topics.description: Recognising and naming common minibeasts: ladybird, ant, bee, butterfly, spider, snail, worm, woodlouse, caterpillar, beetle. Building positive attitudes toward all minibeasts, not just the 'pretty' ones.
evidence: Name and identify at least six common minibeasts from pictures or real encounters
Describe one visible feature that helps tell a ladybird from a beetle or a spider from an ant
Show interest or curiosity toward less popular minibeasts like woodlice, worms, or spiders rather than only butterflies
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} spots a creepy-crawly in the garden or at the park, can they tell you what it is — even the less cute ones like woodlice or worms?
topics.nameZh: 常见小虫子（微型动物）：命名与识别
topics.descriptionZh: 识别并命名常见的小虫子（微型动物）：瓢虫、蚂蚁、蜜蜂、蝴蝶、蜘蛛、蜗牛、蚯蚓、鼠妇（潮虫）、毛毛虫、甲虫。培养对所有小虫子的积极态度，而不仅仅是那些‘漂亮’的。
evidenceZh: 能够通过图片或实际接触，命名并识别至少六种常见的小虫子（微型动物）
描述一个可见特征，帮助区分瓢虫与甲虫，或蜘蛛与蚂蚁
对鼠妇、蚯蚓或蜘蛛等不太受欢迎的小虫子表现出兴趣或好奇心，而不仅仅是对蝴蝶感兴趣
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}在花园或公园里发现爬行的小虫子时，他们能告诉你那是什么吗——即使是像鼠妇或蚯蚓这样不那么可爱的虫子？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How minibeasts move
topics.description: How minibeasts move: crawling (ants, beetles), flying (butterflies, bees), slithering (worms, slugs), jumping (grasshoppers, fleas), burrowing (earthworms). Counting legs as a first step toward grouping creatures.
evidence: Describe at least three different ways minibeasts move such as crawling, flying, and slithering
Match a minibeast to its way of moving, for example grasshoppers jump and worms slither
Count legs on a minibeast and notice that ants have six while spiders have eight
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} watch a few minibeasts and describe how each one moves differently — like ants crawling, butterflies flying, and worms wriggling?
topics.descriptionZh: 小虫子是如何移动的：爬行（蚂蚁、甲虫）、飞行（蝴蝶、蜜蜂）、蠕动（蠕虫、蛞蝓）、跳跃（蚱蜢、跳蚤）、钻洞（蚯蚓）。数腿的数量是对生物进行分类的第一步。
evidenceZh: 描述小虫子至少三种不同的移动方式，例如爬行、飞行和蠕动
将小虫子与其移动方式相匹配，例如蚱蜢会跳跃，而蠕虫会蠕动
数一数小虫子的腿，并注意到蚂蚁有六条腿，而蜘蛛有八条腿
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否观察几只小虫子，并描述它们各自不同的移动方式——比如蚂蚁爬行、蝴蝶飞行和蚯蚓蠕动？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Minibeast Habitats
topics.description: Where minibeasts live: micro-habitats. Different minibeasts prefer different conditions — under logs (damp, dark), in soil (underground), on leaves (sunny), in pond water (wet). The idea that you find different creatures in different places.
evidence: Name at least two micro-habitats where minibeasts live such as under logs, in soil, or on leaves
Predict what type of minibeast might be found in a damp dark place versus a sunny leaf
Explain that different minibeasts prefer different conditions like wet, dry, dark, or light
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you asked {{name}} where to look for woodlice or worms in the garden, could they tell you the kind of spot those creatures prefer — like somewhere damp and dark?
topics.descriptionZh: 微小生物生活的地方：微栖息地（micro-habitats）。不同的微小生物偏好不同的环境条件——在原木下（潮湿、黑暗），在土壤中（地下），在树叶上（阳光充足），在池塘水中（湿润）。核心理念是：在不同的地方会发现不同的生物。
evidenceZh: 说出至少两个微小生物生活的微栖息地，例如原木下、土壤中或树叶上
预测在潮湿黑暗的地方与阳光充足的树叶上分别可能发现哪种微小生物
解释不同的微小生物偏好不同的环境条件，如湿润、干燥、黑暗或明亮
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你问 {{name}} 在花园里哪里可以找到鼠妇（woodlice）或蚯蚓，他们能告诉你这些生物偏好的环境吗——比如潮湿阴暗的地方？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Minibeasts in the food chain
topics.description: Minibeasts in the food chain: simple garden food chains. A caterpillar eats a leaf, a bird eats the caterpillar. The idea that minibeasts are food for other animals, and that minibeasts eat things too.
evidence: Describe a simple food chain such as leaf → caterpillar → bird
Explain that minibeasts eat plants or other tiny creatures and are eaten by bigger animals
Give an example of what a specific minibeast eats, such as caterpillars eating leaves or ladybirds eating aphids
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you asked {{name}} what a caterpillar eats and what eats the caterpillar, could they describe that chain — leaf, caterpillar, bird?
topics.descriptionZh: 食物链中的小型动物（Minibeasts）：简单的花园食物链。毛毛虫吃树叶，小鸟吃毛毛虫。理解小型动物是其他动物的食物，同时它们自己也会进食。
evidenceZh: 描述一个简单的食物链，例如：树叶 → 毛毛虫 → 小鸟
解释小型动物（Minibeasts）吃植物或其他微小生物，并且会被更大的动物吃掉
举例说明某种特定的小型动物（Minibeasts）吃什么，例如毛毛虫吃树叶，或瓢虫吃蚜虫
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你问{{name}}毛毛虫吃什么，以及什么动物吃毛毛虫，他们能描述出这条食物链吗——树叶、毛毛虫、小鸟？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: What is a minibeast?
topics.description: What is a minibeast? Small creatures without backbones, found in gardens, parks, and woodland. Bug hunts — searching under logs, stones, and leaves using magnifying glasses to observe minibeasts up close.
evidence: Explain that minibeasts are small animals without a backbone found in gardens and parks
Find at least three different minibeasts during a garden bug hunt under logs, stones, or leaves
Use a magnifying glass to observe and describe one minibeast's appearance in detail
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you went on a bug hunt in the garden with {{name}}, could they find creatures under logs and stones and tell you what makes something a minibeast?
topics.descriptionZh: 什么是微型动物？它们是没有脊椎的小型生物，常见于花园、公园和林地。寻虫活动（bug hunt）——在枯木、石头和树叶下寻找，并使用放大镜近距离观察微型动物。
evidenceZh: 能够解释微型动物是生活在花园和公园里、没有脊椎的小型动物
在花园的寻虫活动中，能够在枯木、石头或树叶下找到至少三种不同的微型动物
能够使用放大镜观察并详细描述其中一种微型动物的外观
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你和{{name}}一起去花园里参加寻虫活动，他们能在枯木和石头下找到小虫子，并告诉你什么样的特征才算作微型动物吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Bees and pollination
topics.description: Bees and pollination: how flowers and insects depend on each other. Bees visit flowers for nectar, pollen sticks to their bodies and transfers to the next flower. Without pollination many plants cannot make seeds or fruit. Why bees matter for the food we eat.
evidence: Describe how pollen moves from one flower to another when a bee visits to collect nectar
Explain that many fruits and vegetables depend on bees or other insects for pollination
State what would happen to a garden or farm if there were no pollinating insects
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a bee buzzing around flowers in the garden, could they explain how the bee is helping the plant — and why that matters for the food we eat?
topics.descriptionZh: 蜜蜂与授粉 (Pollination)：花朵和昆虫如何相互依存。蜜蜂为了采集花蜜 (nectar) 而拜访花朵，花粉 (pollen) 会粘在它们身上并传递到下一朵花。如果没有授粉，许多植物就无法结出种子或果实。为什么蜜蜂对我们吃的食物至关重要。
evidenceZh: 描述当蜜蜂拜访采集花蜜 (nectar) 时，花粉 (pollen) 如何从一朵花移动到另一朵花
解释许多水果和蔬菜依赖蜜蜂或其他昆虫进行授粉 (pollination)
说明如果没有授粉昆虫，花园或农场会发生什么
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到一只蜜蜂在花园里的花丛中嗡嗡飞舞，他们能解释这只蜜蜂是如何帮助植物的吗——以及为什么这对我们吃的食物很重要？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Camouflage, warning colours, and mimicry
topics.description: Camouflage, warning colours, and mimicry: how insects survive by hiding or sending visual signals. Stick insects look like twigs, leaf insects look like leaves. Wasps have warning stripes; hoverflies mimic wasps but are harmless. The 'can you spot it?' challenge.
evidence: Give at least two examples of insect camouflage such as stick insects resembling twigs or leaf insects resembling leaves
Explain why bright warning colours like a wasp's yellow and black stripes help the insect survive
Describe mimicry by explaining that a harmless insect like a hoverfly copies a dangerous one like a wasp to trick predators
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you showed {{name}} pictures of stick insects hiding on branches or hoverflies pretending to be wasps, could they explain why those insects look the way they do?
topics.nameZh: 伪装、警戒色与拟态 (Camouflage, warning colours, and mimicry)
topics.descriptionZh: 伪装（Camouflage）、警戒色（Warning colours）与拟态（Mimicry）：昆虫如何通过隐藏自己或发出视觉信号来生存。竹节虫看起来像树枝，叶䗛看起来像树叶。黄蜂长有警戒条纹；食蚜蝇会拟态黄蜂，但它们其实无害。快来参与“你能发现它吗？”的挑战吧！
evidenceZh: 给出至少两个昆虫伪装（Camouflage）的例子，例如竹节虫像树枝或叶䗛像树叶
解释为什么像黄蜂黄黑条纹这样鲜艳的警戒色（Warning colours）能帮助昆虫生存
描述拟态（Mimicry），解释像食蚜蝇这样无害的昆虫如何模仿像黄蜂这样危险的昆虫来欺骗捕食者
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你给 {{name}} 看竹节虫隐藏在树枝上或食蚜蝇伪装成黄蜂的图片，他们能解释为什么这些昆虫看起来是那个样子吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Incredible insects: record-breakers
topics.description: Incredible insects — record-breakers and superpowers. Dung beetles are the strongest animals relative to body weight. Dragonflies are among the fastest flying insects. Fleas can jump over 150 times their own body length. Bombardier beetles spray boiling chemicals. The 'wow factor' of the insect world.
evidence: Name at least three insect record-breakers and their extreme abilities such as dung beetle strength or flea jumping
Compare an insect's ability to a human scale, for example a flea's jump would be like a person leaping over a skyscraper
Explain why being very small helps insects achieve extreme feats of strength or speed relative to their size
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you about insect record-breakers — like which insect is the world's strongest for its size, or which one can jump the farthest?
topics.nameZh: 不可思议的昆虫：纪录保持者
topics.descriptionZh: 不可思议的昆虫——纪录保持者与超能力。蜣螂（屎壳郎）是相对于自身体重力气最大的动物。蜻蜓是飞行速度最快的昆虫之一。跳蚤的跳跃距离能超过自身体长的150倍。气步甲能喷射沸腾的化学物质。这就是昆虫世界令人惊叹的“超能力”。
evidenceZh: 说出至少三种昆虫纪录保持者及其极限能力，例如蜣螂的力量或跳蚤的跳跃
将昆虫的能力与人类的比例进行比较，例如跳蚤的跳跃就像一个人跳过摩天大楼
解释为什么体型微小能帮助昆虫实现相对于其体型的极限力量或速度壮举
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能给你讲讲昆虫界的纪录保持者吗？比如哪种昆虫是相对体型力气最大的，或者哪种昆虫跳得最远？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Insect life cycles: complete metamorphosis
topics.description: Insect life cycles — complete metamorphosis in detail. Egg → larva → pupa → adult. The larva (caterpillar, grub, maggot) looks completely different from the adult. Inside the pupa the body is rebuilt. Butterflies, beetles, flies, and ladybirds all undergo complete metamorphosis.
evidence: Name the four stages of complete metamorphosis using the correct terms: egg, larva, pupa, adult
Explain that the larva stage is when the insect eats and grows, and the pupa stage is when its body transforms
