Give at least two examples of insects that undergo complete metamorphosis such as butterflies and beetles
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the full life cycle of a beetle or butterfly using the proper words — egg, larva, pupa, adult — and tell you what happens at each stage?
topics.nameZh: 昆虫生命周期：完全变态
topics.descriptionZh: 昆虫生命周期——详细了解完全变态（complete metamorphosis）。卵（egg）→ 幼虫（larva）→ 蛹（pupa）→ 成虫（adult）。幼虫（如毛毛虫、蛴螬、蛆）的外观与成虫完全不同。在蛹的内部，身体会进行重组。蝴蝶、甲虫、苍蝇和瓢虫都会经历完全变态。
evidenceZh: 使用正确的术语说出完全变态的四个阶段：卵（egg）、幼虫（larva）、蛹（pupa）、成虫（adult）
解释幼虫阶段是昆虫进食和生长的时期，而蛹阶段是其身体发生转变的时期
举出至少两种经历完全变态的昆虫的例子，例如蝴蝶和甲虫
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否使用正确的词汇——卵（egg）、幼虫（larva）、蛹（pupa）、成虫（adult）——来解释甲虫或蝴蝶的完整生命周期，并告诉你每个阶段会发生什么？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Not all minibeasts are insects
topics.description: Not all minibeasts are insects: distinguishing insects from other minibeasts. Spiders have 8 legs and 2 body parts (arachnids), woodlice have 14 legs (crustaceans), worms have no legs, snails have a shell and one foot. The 'Is it an insect?' sorting game.
evidence: Sort a set of minibeasts into 'insect' and 'not insect' groups using the six-legs rule
Explain why a spider is not an insect by noting it has eight legs and two body parts
Name at least one difference between insects and another minibeast group such as worms having no legs or woodlice having fourteen
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you showed {{name}} a spider and asked whether it's an insect, could they explain why not — for example, that spiders have eight legs, not six?
topics.nameZh: 并非所有微小生物都是昆虫
topics.descriptionZh: 并非所有微小生物都是昆虫：区分昆虫与其他微小生物。蜘蛛有8条腿和2个身体部位（蛛形纲），鼠妇有14条腿（甲壳纲），蠕虫没有腿，蜗牛有外壳和一只腹足。进行“它是昆虫吗？”分类游戏。
evidenceZh: 利用“六条腿”规则，将一组微小生物分类为‘昆虫’和‘非昆虫’两组
通过指出蜘蛛有八条腿和两个身体部位，解释为什么蜘蛛不是昆虫
说出昆虫与另一类微小生物（例如没有腿的蠕虫或有十四条腿的鼠妇）之间的至少一个区别
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你给{{name}}看一只蜘蛛并问它是不是昆虫，他们能解释为什么不是吗——比如，指出蜘蛛有八条腿而不是六条？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Social insects: ants and bees
topics.description: Social insects: how ants and bees live and work together in colonies. Queens, workers, and drones. Division of labour — some gather food, some build, some guard. Ant tunnels and bee hives as organised homes. Parallels to human teamwork.
evidence: Describe at least two different roles within an ant colony or bee hive such as queen, worker, or guard
Explain that social insects live together in large groups and divide up the jobs needed to survive
Compare an ant colony or bee hive to a human team, describing how different members do different tasks
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watched a nature programme about ants or bees, could they tell you about the different jobs inside the colony — like the queen, the workers, and the guards?
topics.nameZh: 社会性昆虫：蚂蚁和蜜蜂
topics.descriptionZh: 社会性昆虫：蚂蚁和蜜蜂如何在群落 (colony) 中共同生活与工作。介绍蚁后/蜂后 (queen)、工蚁/工蜂 (worker) 和雄蚁/雄蜂 (drone)。劳动分工 (division of labour)——有些负责采集食物，有些负责建造，有些负责保卫。蚂蚁的地下通道 (ant tunnels) 和蜂巢 (bee hives) 是井然有序的家。探讨其与人类团队合作的相似之处。
evidenceZh: 描述蚂蚁群落或蜂巢中至少两种不同的角色，例如蚁后/蜂后 (queen)、工蚁/工蜂 (worker) 或守卫 (guard)
解释社会性昆虫如何群居并分工合作以完成生存所需的各项工作
将蚂蚁群落或蜂巢与人类团队进行比较，描述不同成员如何承担不同的任务
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 观看了一部关于蚂蚁或蜜蜂的自然纪录片，他们能告诉你群落内部不同的工作分工吗——比如蚁后/蜂后 (queen)、工蚁/工蜂 (worker) 和守卫 (guard) 的不同职责？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Sorting and Identifying Minibeasts
topics.description: Using classification keys to identify minibeasts. Branching yes/no questions: 'Does it have legs?' → 'How many legs?' → 'Does it have wings?' Dichotomous keys as a systematic tool for sorting and identifying creatures.
evidence: Follow a simple branching key to correctly identify at least four different minibeasts
Create a yes/no question that separates insects from spiders, such as 'Does it have six legs?'
Explain why asking questions in a set order helps identify a creature you have never seen before
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} found an unfamiliar minibeast, could they use a set of yes/no questions — like 'Does it have legs? How many?' — to work out what group it belongs to?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用分类检索表（classification keys）来识别小动物。分支式的是/否问题：‘它有腿吗？’→‘它有几条腿？’→‘它有翅膀吗？’二歧式检索表（dichotomous keys）作为对生物进行分类和识别的系统化工具。
evidenceZh: 遵循简单的分支检索表（branching key），正确识别至少四种不同的小动物
提出一个将昆虫与蜘蛛区分开来的是/否问题，例如‘它有六条腿吗？’
解释为什么按照固定顺序提问有助于识别从未见过的生物
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 发现了一只不熟悉的小动物，他们能否使用一组是/否问题——比如‘它有腿吗？有几条？’——来弄清它属于哪个类群？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The insect body plan
topics.description: The insect body plan: all insects share three body parts (head, thorax, abdomen), six legs attached to the thorax, and antennae on the head. Most have wings. They have an exoskeleton — a hard outer shell — instead of bones inside.
evidence: Label the three body parts of an insect — head, thorax, and abdomen — on a diagram or real specimen
State that all insects have exactly six legs and that the legs attach to the thorax
Explain that insects have an exoskeleton, a hard outer covering, instead of bones inside their body
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a picture of a beetle or ant, could they point out the head, thorax, and abdomen, and tell you that all insects have six legs and a hard outer shell?
topics.nameZh: 昆虫的身体结构 (Insect body plan)
topics.descriptionZh: 昆虫的身体结构 (Insect body plan)：所有昆虫都有三个共同的身体部位——头部 (head)、胸部 (thorax) 和腹部 (abdomen)，六条腿长在胸部，头上长着触角。大多数昆虫有翅膀。它们没有体内的骨头，而是拥有外骨骼 (exoskeleton)——一层坚硬的外壳。
evidenceZh: 在图表或真实标本上标注昆虫的三个身体部位——头部 (head)、胸部 (thorax) 和腹部 (abdomen)
说明所有昆虫都正好有六条腿，并且这些腿都长在胸部 (thorax) 上
解释昆虫拥有外骨骼 (exoskeleton)，即一层坚硬的外部覆盖物，而不是体内有骨头
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看一张甲虫或蚂蚁的图片，他们能指出头部 (head)、胸部 (thorax) 和腹部 (abdomen)，并告诉你所有昆虫都有六条腿和坚硬的外壳吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Insect Adaptations
topics.description: Adaptation and evolution in insects: peppered moths as a famous example of natural selection (dark moths survived better on soot-covered trees during the Industrial Revolution). Stick insects evolved to look like twigs. Ant-mimicking spiders evolved to fool predators. How small changes over many generations lead to remarkable disguises.
evidence: Retell the peppered moth story and explain how the environment changed which colour moth survived best
Describe how a stick insect's body shape is an adaptation that helps it avoid being eaten
Explain that adaptations develop over many generations through natural selection, not during one insect's lifetime
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why peppered moths changed colour during the Industrial Revolution — and how that's an example of how living things adapt over many generations?
topics.descriptionZh: 昆虫的适应与进化：桦尺蠖（peppered moths）是自然选择（natural selection）的著名例子（在工业革命期间，深色桦尺蠖在覆盖着煤烟的树上生存得更好）。竹节虫（stick insects）进化得像树枝一样。蚁蛛（ant-mimicking spiders）进化出蚂蚁的模样来欺骗捕食者。微小的变化经过许多代的积累，最终形成了令人惊叹的伪装。
evidenceZh: 讲述桦尺蠖的故事，并解释环境的变化是如何决定哪种颜色的桦尺蠖生存得最好的
描述竹节虫的身体形状是如何作为一种适应性特征（adaptation）来帮助它避免被吃掉的
解释适应性是通过自然选择在许多代中逐渐发展起来的，而不是在昆虫的一生中形成的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释为什么桦尺蠖在工业革命期间改变了颜色吗——以及这如何作为生物经过许多代进行适应（adaptation）的一个例子？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Insect anatomy in depth
topics.description: Insect anatomy in depth: compound eyes made of thousands of tiny lenses, spiracles (breathing holes along the body), diverse mouthparts (chewing mandibles in beetles, sucking proboscis in butterflies, sponging pad in flies), and moulting the exoskeleton to grow. Biomimicry — how engineers copy insect designs.
evidence: Describe at least two specialised insect structures such as compound eyes or spiracles and explain their function
Compare the mouthparts of a beetle (chewing) and a butterfly (sucking) and explain how each is suited to its food
Give one example of biomimicry where human technology is inspired by an insect structure or ability
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a close-up photo of an insect's eye or mouth, could they explain how those body parts work and why they look so different from ours?
topics.descriptionZh: 深入探索昆虫解剖学：由成千上万个微小晶状体组成的复眼 (compound eyes)、气门 (spiracles，沿身体分布的呼吸孔)、多样化的口器（甲虫用于咀嚼的大颚 (mandibles)、蝴蝶用于吸吮的虹吸式口器 (proboscis)、苍蝇用于海绵般舔吸的唇瓣 (sponging pad)），以及通过蜕去外骨骼 (exoskeleton) 来生长。仿生学 (Biomimicry) —— 工程师如何模仿昆虫的设计。
evidenceZh: 描述至少两种专门的昆虫身体结构，如复眼 (compound eyes) 或气门 (spiracles)，并解释它们的功能
比较甲虫（咀嚼式）和蝴蝶（吸吮式）的口器 (mouthparts)，并解释它们各自如何适应其食物
举出一个仿生学 (biomimicry) 的例子，说明人类技术是如何受昆虫身体结构或能力启发而发明的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看着一张昆虫眼睛或口器的特写照片，他们能解释这些身体部位是如何运作的，以及为什么它们看起来和我们的如此不同吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Insect communication and behaviour
topics.description: Insect communication and behaviour: bees perform a waggle dance to tell hive-mates where flowers are. Ants lay pheromone trails for others to follow. Fireflies flash light patterns to find mates. Crickets chirp by rubbing their wings. Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of miles across continents. How insects 'talk' without words.
evidence: Describe at least three ways insects communicate such as the bee waggle dance, ant pheromone trails, and firefly light signals
Explain what information a bee conveys through its waggle dance, including direction and distance to flowers
Describe the monarch butterfly migration and explain why it is remarkable in terms of distance and navigation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how bees tell each other where to find flowers, how ants leave invisible trails, or how fireflies use light to send messages?
topics.descriptionZh: 昆虫的交流与行为：蜜蜂跳起摇摆舞（waggle dance）告诉同伴哪里有花朵。蚂蚁留下信息素（pheromone）轨迹让同伴跟随。萤火虫闪烁特定的光信号来寻找伴侣。蟋蟀通过摩擦翅膀来鸣叫。帝王蝶（monarch butterfly）会跨越大陆，迁徙数千英里。来看看昆虫们是如何在没有语言的情况下“说话”的吧！
evidenceZh: 描述至少三种昆虫交流的方式，例如蜜蜂的摇摆舞（waggle dance）、蚂蚁的信息素（pheromone）轨迹和萤火虫的光信号
解释蜜蜂通过摇摆舞（waggle dance）传递了什么信息，包括花朵的方向和距离
描述帝王蝶（monarch butterfly）的迁徙，并解释为什么它的迁徙距离和导航能力如此令人惊叹
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释蜜蜂是如何互相告诉对方去哪里找花朵的、蚂蚁是如何留下隐形轨迹的，或者萤火虫是如何用光来发送信息的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Insects in ecosystems
topics.description: Insects in ecosystems: the many roles insects play. Pollinators (bees, butterflies, hoverflies), decomposers (dung beetles, fly larvae), food source for birds, bats, fish, and frogs, and pest controllers (ladybirds eating aphids). The thought experiment: what would happen if all insects disappeared?
evidence: Name at least three different ecological roles that insects play such as pollinator, decomposer, and food source
Explain how the removal of one insect group like bees would affect plants, other animals, and humans
Describe a specific example of insects as pest controllers such as ladybirds controlling aphid populations
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you asked {{name}} what would happen if all the insects in the world disappeared tomorrow, could they explain the chain of problems that would cause — for plants, animals, and people?
topics.descriptionZh: 生态系统中的昆虫：昆虫扮演的许多重要角色。它们是传粉者 (pollinators)（如蜜蜂、蝴蝶、食蚜蝇），是分解者 (decomposers)（如粪金龟、蝇蛆），是鸟类、蝙蝠、鱼类和青蛙的食物来源，也是害虫控制者 (pest controllers)（如七星瓢虫捕食蚜虫)。思想实验：如果世界上所有的昆虫都消失了，会发生什么？
evidenceZh: 说出昆虫扮演的至少三种不同的生态角色，例如传粉者 (pollinator)、分解者 (decomposer) 和食物来源 (food source)
解释移除某一昆虫群体（如蜜蜂）会如何影响植物、其他动物和人类
描述一个昆虫作为害虫控制者的具体例子，例如七星瓢虫控制蚜虫种群
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你问 {{name}}，如果明天世界上所有的昆虫都消失了会发生什么，他们能解释这会引发的一系列问题吗——对植物、动物和人类的影响？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The most successful animals on Earth
topics.description: The most successful animals on Earth: there are roughly one million described insect species, and scientists estimate 5–10 million may exist. More insect species than all other animal groups combined. Why so many? Small body size means less food needed, fast reproduction with many offspring, flight allows reaching new habitats, and the exoskeleton is incredibly versatile.
evidence: State that insects are the most species-rich group of animals with about one million known species
Give at least two reasons why insects are so successful such as small size, fast reproduction, or flight
Compare insect diversity to another animal group, explaining that there are far more insect species than mammals or birds
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know which group of animals has more species than any other on Earth — and can they explain why insects are so incredibly successful?
topics.descriptionZh: 地球上最成功的动物：目前已命名的昆虫物种大约有100万种，科学家估计实际存在的昆虫可能有500万到1000万种。昆虫的物种数量超过了所有其他动物类群的总和。为什么昆虫这么多呢？体型小意味着需要的食物更少，繁殖速度快且后代数量多，飞行能力让它们能到达新的栖息地，而且外骨骼（exoskeleton）的功能极其多样且强大。
evidenceZh: 指出昆虫是物种最丰富的动物类群，已知物种约有100万种
给出昆虫如此成功的至少两个原因，如体型小、繁殖快或会飞
将昆虫的多样性与其他动物类群进行比较，解释昆虫的物种数量远远多于哺乳动物或鸟类
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否知道地球上哪个动物类群的物种数量最多——他们能解释为什么昆虫能取得如此巨大的成功吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Threats to insects and conservation
topics.description: Threats to insects and conservation: insect populations are declining worldwide. Causes include habitat loss, pesticide use, light pollution disrupting nocturnal insects, and climate change. Pollinator decline threatens food production. What children can do: plant pollinator-friendly gardens, reduce pesticide use, participate in citizen science like the Big Butterfly Count.
evidence: Name at least three threats to insect populations such as habitat loss, pesticides, and light pollution
Explain why declining bee populations are a problem for humans and the food we eat
Suggest at least two actions that children or families can take to help insects such as planting wildflowers or joining a butterfly count
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you why insect numbers are falling around the world, why that matters for people too, and what your family could do to help?
topics.nameZh: 昆虫面临的威胁与保护
topics.descriptionZh: 昆虫面临的威胁与保护：全球昆虫数量正在不断减少。主要原因包括栖息地丧失（habitat loss）、农药滥用、光污染干扰夜行性昆虫以及气候变化。传粉昆虫（pollinator）数量的下降直接威胁到人类的粮食生产。孩子们可以采取的行动：种植吸引传粉昆虫的花园、减少农药的使用、参与“大蝴蝶计数”（Big Butterfly Count）等公民科学（citizen science）活动。
evidenceZh: 列举至少三种威胁昆虫种群的因素，例如栖息地丧失（habitat loss）、农药使用和光污染（light pollution）。
解释为什么蜜蜂数量的减少会对人类以及我们的食物供应造成问题。
提出至少两项儿童或家庭可以采取的帮助昆虫的具体行动，例如种植野花或参与蝴蝶计数（butterfly count）活动。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能告诉你为什么世界各地的昆虫数量正在减少，为什么这也会影响到人类，以及你的家庭可以采取哪些行动来帮助它们吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Types of Metamorphosis
topics.description: Complete vs incomplete metamorphosis. Complete: egg → larva → pupa → adult (butterflies, beetles, flies). Incomplete: egg → nymph → adult — the nymph looks like a small version of the adult and moults as it grows (grasshoppers, dragonflies, crickets). Why do some insects transform completely while others grow gradually?
evidence: Compare complete and incomplete metamorphosis by describing the stages of each on a diagram
Classify at least three insects into the correct metamorphosis type such as butterfly (complete) and grasshopper (incomplete)
Explain that nymphs resemble adults while larvae look completely different from their adult form
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between a butterfly's life cycle and a grasshopper's — why the caterpillar looks nothing like the butterfly, but a baby grasshopper already looks like a small grasshopper?
topics.nameZh: 变态发育的类型 (Types of Metamorphosis)
topics.descriptionZh: 完全变态 (Complete) 与不完全变态 (Incomplete) 发育。完全变态：卵 (egg) → 幼虫 (larva) → 蛹 (pupa) → 成虫 (adult)（如蝴蝶、甲虫、苍蝇）。不完全变态：卵 (egg) → 若虫 (nymph) → 成虫 (adult) —— 若虫看起来像是成虫的缩小版，并在生长过程中蜕皮 (moult)（如蚱蜢、蜻蜓、蟋蟀）。为什么有些昆虫会经历完全变态，而另一些则是逐渐长大的呢？
evidenceZh: 通过在图表上描述各个阶段，比较完全变态和不完全变态发育
将至少三种昆虫分类到正确的变态发育类型中，例如蝴蝶（完全变态）和蚱蜢（不完全变态）
解释若虫 (nymphs) 与成虫相似，而幼虫 (larvae) 看起来与成虫形态完全不同
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能解释蝴蝶和蚱蜢生命周期的区别吗——为什么毛毛虫看起来一点也不像蝴蝶，而小蚱蜢看起来已经像是一只缩小版的蚱蜢了呢？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Describing Material Properties
topics.description: Describe simple physical properties of everyday materials such as hard/soft, stretchy/stiff, shiny/dull, rough/smooth, waterproof/absorbent, transparent/opaque
evidence: Use at least five property words correctly: hard, soft, stretchy, shiny, rough, smooth, transparent, waterproof
Describe the properties of three different materials using at least two property words each
Explain why a property matters (e.g. 'waterproof means water doesn't soak through')
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} pick up different objects and describe their properties — like 'this is smooth and shiny' or 'this is rough and bendy'?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述日常材料的简单物理特性（physical properties），如：硬/软（hard/soft）、有弹性/硬挺（stretchy/stiff）、有光泽/无光泽（shiny/dull）、粗糙/光滑（rough/smooth）、防水/吸水（waterproof/absorbent）、透明/不透明（transparent/opaque）。
evidenceZh: 正确使用至少五个特性词汇：硬（hard）、软（soft）、有弹性（stretchy）、有光泽（shiny）、粗糙（rough）、光滑（smooth）、透明（transparent）、防水（waterproof）
使用至少两个特性词汇描述三种不同材料的特性
解释为什么某种特性很重要（例如：“防水意味着水无法渗透”）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否拿起不同的物品并描述它们的特性——比如“这个很光滑且有光泽”或“这个很粗糙且可弯曲”？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Grouping Materials
topics.description: Compare and group everyday materials based on their simple physical properties
evidence: Sort a set of materials into groups based on a chosen property (e.g. transparent vs opaque)
Compare two materials and state which properties they share and which differ
Explain the reasoning behind a grouping decision using property vocabulary
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} sort a pile of objects into groups based on their properties, like all the waterproof ones together or all the transparent ones?
topics.descriptionZh: 根据日常材料的简单物理属性进行比较和分类
evidenceZh: 根据选定的属性（如：透明与不透明）将一组材料进行分类
比较两种材料，并指出它们相同和不同的属性
使用属性词汇解释分类决定背后的理由
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否根据物品的属性（例如把所有防水的放在一起，或把所有透明的放在一起）对一堆物品进行分类？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Naming Everyday Materials
topics.description: Identify and name a variety of everyday materials including wood, plastic, glass, metal, water, and rock
evidence: Name at least six everyday materials: wood, plastic, glass, metal, water, rock
Identify the material of at least ten different objects around the home or classroom
Recognise that some objects are made from more than one material
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} look around a room and correctly name the materials things are made of — like glass in the window, metal in the radiator, and plastic in a pen?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别并命名各种日常材料，包括木材、塑料、玻璃、金属、水和岩石。
evidenceZh: 至少说出六种日常材料的名称：木材、塑料、玻璃、金属、水、岩石
识别家里或教室里至少十种不同物品的制作材料
认识到有些物品是由一种以上的材料制成的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否环顾房间，正确说出各种物品是由什么材料制成的——比如窗户上的玻璃、暖气片上的金属，以及笔上的塑料？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Objects vs Materials
topics.description: Distinguish between an object and the material from which it is made, understanding that objects can be made from different materials
evidence: Explain the difference between an object (e.g. a chair) and the material it is made from (e.g. wood)
Give examples of the same object made from different materials (e.g. plastic cup, glass cup)
Identify what material a given object is made from by looking at and touching it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you hold up a wooden spoon and a metal spoon, can {{name}} explain that both are spoons (the object) but made from different materials?
topics.descriptionZh: 区分物体（Object）及其制作材料（Material），理解同一个物体可以由不同的材料制成。
evidenceZh: 解释物体（如椅子）与其制作材料（如木头）之间的区别
举例说明由不同材料制成的相同物体（如塑料杯、玻璃杯）
通过观察和触摸来识别给定物体是由什么材料制成的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你拿出一把木勺和一把金属勺，{{name}} 能解释它们都是勺子（物体），但由不同的材料制成吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: States of Matter Vocabulary
topics.description: Name and distinguish the three states of matter — solid, liquid, and gas — using properties vocabulary: hard, rigid, runny, flows, keeps its shape, fills its container; use 'change of state' to describe what happens when materials are heated or cooled
evidence: Correctly sort a set of everyday materials as solid, liquid, or gas and give a reason for each
Use the terms solid, liquid, and gas accurately when describing everyday substances
Use 'change of state' to describe what happens when ice melts or water boils
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you point to water, ice, and steam from a kettle, can {{name}} correctly call each one a liquid, solid, or gas — and use those words naturally?
topics.descriptionZh: 命名并区分物质的三种状态——固体(solid)、液体(liquid)和气体(gas)——并使用描述特性的词汇：坚硬(hard)、有固定形状(rigid)、易流动(runny)、可流动(flows)、保持自身形状(keeps its shape)、充满容器(fills its container)；使用“物态变化(change of state)”来描述物质被加热或冷却时发生的情况。
evidenceZh: 能够将一组日常材料正确分类为固体、液体或气体，并给出每个分类的理由
在描述日常物质时，能准确使用固体、液体和气体这些术语
能使用“物态变化”来描述冰融化或水沸腾时发生的现象
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你指着水壶里的水、冰和蒸汽，{{name}}能正确地说出它们分别是液体、固体还是气体吗——并且能自然地使用这些词汇吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Changing Shapes of Solids
topics.description: Investigate how the shapes of solid objects can be changed by squashing, bending, twisting, and stretching
evidence: Demonstrate four ways to change the shape of a solid: squashing, bending, twisting, stretching
Compare how different materials respond to these forces (e.g. clay squashes easily, wood does not)
Explain that the material itself stays the same even when the shape changes
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} show you how to change the shape of clay by squashing it, twist a pipe cleaner, and explain that some materials bend while others snap?
topics.descriptionZh: 探究如何通过挤压（squashing）、弯曲（bending）、扭转（twisting）和拉伸（stretching）来改变固体物体的形状。
evidenceZh: 演示改变固体形状的四种方法：挤压、弯曲、扭转和拉伸
比较不同材料对这些力的反应（例如，黏土容易被挤压变形，而木头则不会）
解释即使形状发生改变，材料本身并没有发生变化
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能为你演示如何通过挤压来改变黏土的形状、扭转扭扭棒（pipe cleaner），并解释有些材料可以弯曲而有些材料会折断吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Choosing the Right Material
topics.description: Identify and compare the suitability of everyday materials for particular uses, explaining why specific materials are chosen for specific purposes
evidence: Explain why a specific material is chosen for a purpose based on its properties (e.g. glass for windows because it's transparent)
Compare two materials and decide which is more suitable for a given use with reasoning
Suggest an alternative material for an object and explain why it would or wouldn't work
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why windows are made of glass and not wood, or why wellies are made of rubber and not paper?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别并比较日常材料在特定用途中的适用性，解释为何针对特定目的选择特定材料。
evidenceZh: 根据材料的属性（properties）解释为何为特定目的选择某种材料（例如，因为玻璃透明（transparent），所以用玻璃做窗户）
比较两种材料，并通过推理说明哪种材料更适合特定用途
为某物品建议一种替代材料，并解释该替代材料是否可行及其原因
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么窗户是用玻璃而不是木头做的，或者为什么雨靴是用橡胶而不是纸做的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Changes & Separation Vocabulary
topics.description: Use process vocabulary for changes of state and material separation — dissolve, solution, soluble, insoluble, evaporate, condense, melt, freeze, filter, sieve, mixture, separate — and understand precisely what each term describes, including the important distinction between dissolving and melting
evidence: Distinguish 'dissolve' from 'melt' correctly in context and explain the difference
Use 'soluble' and 'insoluble' accurately when describing whether a material dissolves in water
Explain the difference between evaporation and condensation using the correct terms
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} stirs sugar into tea, can they explain whether the sugar dissolved or melted — and tell you those are different things?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用描述状态变化和物质分离的过程词汇——溶解 (dissolve)、溶液 (solution)、可溶的 (soluble)、不溶的 (insoluble)、蒸发 (evaporate)、凝结 (condense)、熔化 (melt)、凝固 (freeze)、过滤 (filter)、筛分 (sieve)、混合物 (mixture)、分离 (separate)——并准确理解每个术语所描述的含义，特别是要清楚溶解和熔化之间的重要区别。
evidenceZh: 在具体语境中正确区分“溶解 (dissolve)”和“熔化 (melt)”，并解释两者的区别
在描述物质是否在水中溶解时，准确使用“可溶的 (soluble)”和“不溶的 (insoluble)”
使用正确的术语解释“蒸发 (evaporation)”和“凝结 (condensation)”之间的区别
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 将糖搅入茶中，他们能解释糖是溶解了还是熔化了——并告诉你这是两件不同的事情吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Classifying Materials
topics.description: Plan and conduct an investigation to classify different kinds of materials by their observable properties
evidence: Design a simple test to compare one property across several materials
Record observations in a table or chart during the investigation
Classify the tested materials into groups based on the results
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} test a set of objects and sort them by properties like whether they float, conduct heat, or are magnetic?
topics.descriptionZh: 计划并开展探究活动，根据可观察的特征（observable properties）对各类材料进行分类。
evidenceZh: 设计一个简单的测试，比较多种材料的同一种特征（property）
在探究过程中，将观察结果记录在表格或图表中
根据测试结果将受测材料分组归类
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否测试一组物体，并根据它们是否会漂浮、是否导热或是否具有磁性等特征（properties）对其进行分类？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Drawing Particle Diagrams
topics.description: Draw and interpret particle diagrams — dot representations showing the arrangement, spacing, and movement of particles in solids (close, regular, vibrating in place), liquids (close, random, flowing past each other), and gases (widely spaced, moving rapidly in all directions) — and use these diagrams to explain observable properties such as fixed shape, fixed volume, and compressibility
evidence: Draw labelled particle diagrams for solids, liquids, and gases showing the correct arrangement and spacing of particles
Use their particle diagram to explain why solids keep their shape but liquids flow
Sketch what happens to particles during a change of state (e.g. melting) and explain the energy changes involved
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s science teacher draws a diagram with dots packed tightly in rows versus dots spread far apart and moving around, can {{name}} tell you which represents a solid and which a gas — and explain why, using the particles?
topics.descriptionZh: 绘制并解读粒子图（particle diagrams）——这是一种用点来表示固体（粒子紧密、排列规则、在原地振动）、液体（粒子紧密、排列无序、相互滑动）和气体（粒子间距大、向各个方向快速运动）中粒子的排列方式、间距和运动状态的图示，并利用这些图示来解释物质具有固定形状、固定体积以及可压缩性等可观察的特性。
evidenceZh: 绘制带有标签的固体、液体和气体粒子图，正确展示粒子的排列方式和间距
利用自己绘制的粒子图来解释为什么固体能保持固定的形状，而液体却会流动
画出物态变化（change of state，如熔化）过程中粒子发生的变化草图，并解释其中涉及的能量变化
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}的科学老师画了一幅图，图中的点紧密地排列成行，另一幅图中的点则分散得很开并且四处移动，{{name}}能分辨出哪一幅代表固体、哪一幅代表气体吗？并且能结合粒子的特性解释原因吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Heating & Cooling Changes
topics.description: Observe and describe that some materials change state when heated or cooled, and measure the temperature at which changes occur in degrees Celsius
evidence: Describe melting (solid to liquid) and freezing (liquid to solid) with everyday examples
State that water freezes at 0°C and boils at 100°C
Explain that heating adds energy causing particles to move more, leading to state changes
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happens to an ice cube when you heat it, and at what temperature water freezes and boils?
topics.descriptionZh: 观察并描述某些物质在加热或冷却时状态会发生改变，并用摄氏度（degrees Celsius）测量发生状态变化时的温度。
evidenceZh: 结合日常生活中的例子，描述熔化（melting，固体变为液体）和凝固（freezing，液体变为固体）现象
说明水在0°C时凝固（freezing），在100°C时沸腾（boiling）
解释加热会增加能量，使微粒（particles）运动加剧，从而导致物质状态发生变化
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释给冰块加热时会发生什么，以及水在什么温度下凝固和沸腾？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Taking Apart & Rebuilding
topics.description: Observe that an object made of a small set of pieces can be disassembled and made into a new object, understanding that the pieces still exist
evidence: Explain that taking apart an object and rebuilding it uses the same pieces in a new arrangement
Describe how the pieces themselves don't change even though the object looks different
Give an everyday example of reusing materials to make something new
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} builds a tower with building bricks and then takes it apart to build a car, can they explain that the same bricks are used but arranged differently?
topics.descriptionZh: 观察由少量部件组成的物体可以被拆解并重新组装成新物体，并理解这些部件依然存在。
evidenceZh: 解释拆解物体并重新组装时，使用的是相同的部件，只是排列方式不同。
描述即使物体外观改变，部件本身并没有发生变化。
举一个日常生活中重复利用材料制作新物品的例子。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 用积木搭建了一座塔，然后将其拆解并重新拼成一辆汽车，他们能否解释使用的是相同的积木，只是排列方式不同？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Testing Materials for Uses
topics.description: Give reasons, based on evidence from comparative and fair tests, for the particular uses of everyday materials including metals, wood, and plastic
evidence: Design a fair test to compare a specific property of two or more materials
Present test results as evidence for why a material is suited to a particular use
Explain the link between a material's tested properties and its real-world application
topics.assessmentPrompt: After testing different materials, can {{name}} explain with evidence why saucepans are made of metal but their handles are plastic?
topics.descriptionZh: 基于对比和公平测试（fair test）的证据，解释日常材料（包括金属、木材和塑料）特定用途的原因。
evidenceZh: 设计一个公平测试（fair test）来比较两种或多种材料的某项特定属性
展示测试结果作为证据，说明某种材料为何适合特定用途
解释材料的测试属性与其实际应用之间的联系
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在测试了不同的材料之后，{{name}} 能否用证据解释为什么锅身是金属做的，而把手却是塑料做的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Evaporation & the Water Cycle
topics.description: Identify the role of evaporation and condensation in the water cycle, and associate the rate of evaporation with temperature
evidence: Describe evaporation as liquid turning to gas and condensation as gas turning to liquid
Explain the water cycle: evaporation from seas/lakes → condensation into clouds → precipitation
Explain why evaporation happens faster at higher temperatures (e.g. puddles dry faster on hot days)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why puddles disappear on a sunny day and where the water goes, and why the bathroom mirror steams up after a hot shower?
topics.nameZh: 蒸发 (Evaporation) 与水循环 (Water Cycle)
topics.descriptionZh: 识别蒸发 (Evaporation) 和凝结 (Condensation) 在水循环 (Water Cycle) 中的作用，并理解蒸发速率与温度的关系。
evidenceZh: 描述蒸发 (Evaporation) 是液体变成气体，凝结 (Condensation) 是气体变成液体
解释水循环 (Water Cycle)：海洋/湖泊的水蒸发 (Evaporation) → 凝结 (Condensation) 成云 → 降水 (Precipitation)
解释为什么温度越高蒸发 (Evaporation) 越快（例如，水坑在炎热的晴天干得更快）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能解释为什么晴天水坑里的水会消失、水去了哪里，以及为什么洗完热水澡后浴室的镜子会起雾吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Solids, Liquids & Gases
topics.description: Compare and group materials as solids, liquids, or gases based on their observable properties and behaviour
evidence: Define solids (fixed shape, hard to compress), liquids (flow, take shape of container), gases (spread out, fill space)
Sort at least eight everyday materials into solid, liquid, or gas categories
Explain tricky cases like sand (solid particles) or steam (gas, not visible water droplets)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between a solid like ice, a liquid like water, and a gas like steam, and sort everyday things into these three groups?
topics.descriptionZh: 根据可观察的特性和行为，将材料比较并归类为固体（solid）、液体（liquid）或气体（gas）。
evidenceZh: 定义固体（固定形状，难以压缩）、液体（会流动，形状随容器改变）、气体（向外扩散，充满空间）
将至少八种日常材料分类为固体、液体或气体
解释一些容易混淆的情况，例如沙子（由固体颗粒组成）或水蒸气（是气体，而不是可见的水滴）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释像冰（固体）、水（液体）和水蒸气（气体）之间的区别，并将日常事物归入这三个类别中？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Advanced Material Properties
topics.description: Compare and group everyday materials based on advanced properties: hardness, solubility, transparency, electrical and thermal conductivity, and response to magnets
evidence: Define and test for at least four properties: hardness, solubility, conductivity, magnetism
Group a set of materials based on test results for each property
Use results to explain why certain materials are chosen for specific uses (e.g. copper for wires because it conducts electricity)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} test materials and sort them by whether they dissolve in water, conduct electricity, or are attracted to a magnet?
topics.descriptionZh: 根据进阶特性（如硬度 (hardness)、溶解度 (solubility)、透明度 (transparency)、导电与导热性 (electrical and thermal conductivity) 以及对磁铁的反应 (response to magnets)）来比较和分类日常材料。
evidenceZh: 定义并测试至少四种特性：硬度 (hardness)、溶解度 (solubility)、导电性 (conductivity)、磁性 (magnetism)
根据每项特性的测试结果对一组材料进行分类
利用测试结果解释为什么某些材料被选用于特定用途（例如，因为铜能导电，所以用铜制作导线）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否测试材料，并根据它们是否溶于水、是否导电或是否被磁铁吸引来进行分类？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Dissolving & Solutions
topics.description: Understand that some materials dissolve in liquid to form a solution, and describe how to recover a substance from a solution by evaporation
evidence: Explain that dissolving means a solid mixes completely into a liquid to form a solution
Describe how to recover a dissolved substance by evaporating the liquid
Distinguish between a mixture (can see separate parts) and a solution (looks clear, fully dissolved)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happens when sugar dissolves in tea, and figure out how to get the salt back from salty water?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解某些物质在液体中溶解形成溶液（solution），并描述如何通过蒸发（evaporation）从溶液中回收该物质。
evidenceZh: 解释溶解是指固体完全混合到液体中形成溶液（solution）
描述如何通过蒸发（evaporation）液体来回收已溶解的物质
区分混合物（能看到分离的部分）和溶液（看起来清澈，完全溶解）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释糖在茶中溶解时发生了什么，并想办法从盐水中把盐提取出来吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Irreversible Changes
topics.description: Explain that some changes result in the formation of new materials and are not usually reversible, such as burning, rusting, and reactions with acid
evidence: Define an irreversible change as one that creates new materials that cannot be changed back
Give at least three examples: burning, rusting, mixing bicarbonate of soda with vinegar
Describe observable signs of irreversible change: gas produced, colour change, heat given off, new substance formed
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why you can't un-burn a piece of toast or turn rust back into shiny iron, because a completely new material has been made?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释某些变化会导致新物质的形成，且通常不可逆，例如燃烧、生锈以及与酸的反应。
evidenceZh: 将不可逆变化定义为产生无法变回原状的新物质的变化
给出至少三个例子：燃烧、生锈、将小苏打（碳酸氢钠）与醋混合
描述不可逆变化的可观察迹象：产生气体、颜色改变、释放热量、形成新物质
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么无法让烤焦的面包片恢复原状，或者为什么铁锈不能变回闪亮的铁，因为已经生成了全新的物质？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Material Properties Vocabulary
topics.description: Use technical vocabulary to describe and compare material properties — conductor, insulator, thermal, electrical, transparent, opaque, translucent, soluble, insoluble, magnetic, flexible, rigid, density — and apply these terms precisely when selecting and justifying materials for particular purposes
evidence: Classify a set of materials as electrical conductors or insulators and explain why using the correct terms
Use 'transparent', 'translucent', and 'opaque' correctly and distinctly in descriptions
Apply at least four property terms correctly when justifying a material choice for a given purpose
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} had to choose a material to make a window, could they use words like 'transparent' and 'insulator' to explain their choice — not just say 'you can see through it'?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用专业词汇（导体 conductor、绝缘体 insulator、热学 thermal、电学 electrical、透明 transparent、不透明 opaque、半透明 translucent、可溶 soluble、不溶 insoluble、磁性 magnetic、柔性 flexible、刚性 rigid、密度 density）来描述和比较材料特性，并在为特定目的选择和论证材料时精准应用这些术语。
evidenceZh: 将一组材料分类为电的导体（electrical conductors）或绝缘体（insulators），并使用正确的术语解释原因
在描述中正确且明确地使用“透明的（transparent）”、“半透明的（translucent）”和“不透明的（opaque）”
在为特定目的论证材料选择时，正确应用至少四个特性术语
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 需要选择一种材料来制作窗户，他们能否使用“透明的（transparent）”和“绝缘体（insulator）”等词汇来解释其选择，而不是仅仅说“你能透过它看到外面”？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Reversible Changes
topics.description: Demonstrate that dissolving, mixing, and changes of state are reversible changes where no new materials are formed
evidence: Define a reversible change as one where the original materials can be recovered
Give at least three examples of reversible changes: melting, freezing, dissolving, evaporating
Explain how to reverse each example (e.g. freeze melted chocolate, evaporate a solution)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that melting chocolate or dissolving sugar can be undone — you can get the original material back — because these are reversible changes?
topics.descriptionZh: 证明溶解、混合和状态变化（changes of state）是可逆变化，且没有新物质生成
evidenceZh: 将可逆变化定义为能够恢复原始物质的变化
给出至少三个可逆变化的例子：熔化（melting）、凝固（freezing）、溶解（dissolving）、蒸发（evaporating）
解释如何逆转每个例子（例如，冷冻熔化的巧克力、蒸发溶液）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释熔化巧克力或溶解糖是可以逆转的——你可以恢复原始物质——因为这些是可逆变化？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Separating Mixtures
topics.description: Use knowledge of solids, liquids, and gases to decide how mixtures might be separated through filtering, sieving, and evaporating
evidence: Choose the correct separation method for a given mixture (sieving for large particles, filtering for small, evaporating for dissolved)
Describe a multi-step separation plan for a complex mixture like sand, salt, and water
Explain why each method works based on the properties of the materials
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has a mixture of sand, salt, and water, can they figure out a step-by-step plan to separate all three using a sieve, filter, and evaporation?
topics.descriptionZh: 运用固体、液体和气体的知识，决定如何通过过滤（filtering）、筛分（sieving）和蒸发（evaporating）来分离混合物
evidenceZh: 为指定的混合物选择正确的分离方法（大颗粒使用筛分（sieving），小颗粒使用过滤（filtering），已溶解物质使用蒸发（evaporating））
描述针对复杂混合物（如沙子、盐和水）的多步分离计划
根据物质的特性解释每种分离方法为何有效
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 有一杯沙子、盐和水的混合物，他们能制定一个分步计划，使用筛子（sieve）、滤纸（filter）和蒸发（evaporation）将这三种物质完全分离开来吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Conservation of Mass
topics.description: Measure and provide evidence that the total weight of matter is conserved regardless of the type of change (heating, cooling, or mixing)
evidence: State the principle that matter is neither created nor destroyed during physical or chemical changes
Describe an investigation weighing materials before and after a change to show mass is conserved
Explain why dissolved sugar still contributes to the total weight even though it can't be seen
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} dissolves sugar in water, can they explain why the total weight of the water and sugar stays the same even though the sugar seems to disappear?
topics.descriptionZh: 测量并提供证据，证明无论发生何种变化（加热、冷却或混合），物质的总质量 (mass) 都保持不变。
evidenceZh: 阐述在物理变化或化学变化 (physical or chemical changes) 中，物质既不会被创造也不会被消灭的原理。
描述一项探究活动，通过称量变化前后材料的质量 (mass)，来证明质量守恒。
解释为什么溶解的糖虽然看不见了，但仍然对总质量 (mass) 有贡献。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 把糖溶解在水里，他们能解释为什么即使糖好像消失了，水和糖的总重量 (weight) 仍然保持不变吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Matter Is Made of Particles
topics.description: Develop a model to describe that matter is made of particles too small to be seen, and that this explains properties of solids, liquids, and gases
evidence: Describe matter as made of particles too small to see with the naked eye
Use a particle model to explain differences: particles tightly packed (solid), loosely arranged (liquid), spread far apart (gas)
Use the particle model to explain a state change (e.g. heating makes particles move faster and spread apart)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that everything is made of tiny particles we can't see, and that how tightly packed they are determines whether something is a solid, liquid, or gas?
topics.nameZh: 物质是由微粒 (particles) 构成的
topics.descriptionZh: 建立模型来描述物质是由肉眼看不见的微粒构成的，并用此解释固体 (solids)、液体 (liquids) 和气体 (gases) 的性质。
evidenceZh: 描述物质是由肉眼看不见的微粒组成的
使用微粒模型来解释差异：微粒紧密排列（固体 solids）、松散排列（液体 liquids）、分散得很开（气体 gases）
使用微粒模型解释物态变化 (state change)（例如，加热使微粒运动加快并分散开来）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释一切事物都是由我们看不见的微小微粒构成的，并且它们的排列紧密程度决定了该物质是固体、液体还是气体？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Atoms, Elements & Compounds
topics.description: Explain the differences between atoms, elements, and compounds; describe the simple Bohr model of the atom (nucleus with protons and neutrons, electrons in shells); and write and interpret chemical symbols and simple formulae
evidence: Defines atom, element, and compound and distinguishes between them with examples
Draws a simple Bohr model of an atom labelling nucleus (protons/neutrons) and electron shells
Reads a chemical formula to identify the elements and number of each atom (e.g. H₂O, CO₂, NaCl)
Identifies the difference between a mixture and a compound
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw the formula H₂O on a label, could they explain what it means — which atoms are involved, how many of each, and why water is a compound rather than just a mixture of hydrogen and oxygen?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释原子、元素和化合物之间的区别；描述简单的原子玻尔模型（包含质子和中子的原子核，以及电子层）；并书写和解释化学符号及简单的化学式
evidenceZh: 定义原子、元素和化合物，并通过实例区分它们
绘制简单的原子玻尔模型，标注原子核（质子/中子）和电子层
解读化学式以识别所含元素及各原子的数量（如 H₂O、CO₂、NaCl）
识别混合物与化合物之间的区别
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在标签上看到化学式 H₂O，他们能解释其含义吗——涉及哪些原子，每种原子各有多少个，以及为什么水是化合物而不仅仅是氢和氧的混合物？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How Materials Change State
topics.description: Explain melting, freezing, boiling, condensing, and sublimation using the particle model, interpreting heating and cooling curves to identify melting and boiling points
evidence: Describes what happens to particles during each change of state
Reads a heating/cooling curve and identifies the melting point and boiling point from the flat regions
Explains why temperature stays constant during a change of state
Distinguishes between evaporation (from surface, any temperature) and boiling (throughout liquid, at boiling point)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was heating a block of ice in a pan and drew a graph of temperature over time, could they explain why the line goes flat at certain points — and what's happening to the particles when it does?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用粒子模型（particle model）解释熔化（melting）、凝固（freezing）、沸腾（boiling）、凝结（condensing）和升华（sublimation），并解读加热和冷却曲线（heating and cooling curves）以确定熔点（melting point）和沸点（boiling point）。
evidenceZh: 描述在每种物态变化中粒子（particles）发生了什么
读取加热/冷却曲线（heating/cooling curve），并从平缓区域识别熔点和沸点
解释为什么在物态变化期间温度保持不变
区分蒸发（evaporation，发生在液体表面，任何温度下）和沸腾（boiling，发生在整个液体内部，在沸点时）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在锅里加热一块冰，并绘制了温度随时间变化的图表，他们能解释为什么曲线在某些点会变平吗——以及此时粒子正在发生什么变化？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Metals vs Non-Metals
topics.description: Compare the physical and chemical properties of metals and non-metals, explaining metallic properties (malleability, lustre, conductivity) and how position in the periodic table predicts reactivity
evidence: Lists physical properties typical of metals (shiny, malleable, good conductor) and non-metals
Explains why metals are used in wires, cookware, and construction based on their properties
Uses the periodic table to predict whether an element is likely to be reactive or unreactive
Explains what lustre and malleability mean in terms of real-world observations
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} had an unknown substance that was shiny, could be bent without breaking, and conducted electricity, could they identify it as likely a metal and explain how each property points to that conclusion?
topics.descriptionZh: 比较金属与非金属的物理和化学性质，解释金属的特性（延展性 (malleability)、金属光泽 (lustre)、导电性 (conductivity)），以及如何根据元素在周期表 (periodic table) 中的位置预测其反应活性 (reactivity)。
evidenceZh: 列出金属（有光泽、具延展性、良导体）和非金属典型的物理性质
根据金属的性质，解释为什么它们被用于制造电线、炊具和建筑材料
利用元素周期表来预测某种元素可能具有反应活性还是缺乏反应活性
结合实际生活中的观察，解释“金属光泽”和“延展性”的具体含义
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}遇到一种未知物质，它闪闪发光、可以弯曲而不断裂，并且能导电，{{name}}能否判断它很可能是一种金属，并解释每种性质是如何指向这一结论的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Physical vs Chemical Changes
topics.description: Distinguish between physical changes (reversible, no new substances formed) and chemical changes (new substances formed, often irreversible), using conservation of mass to understand both types
evidence: Classifies given changes as physical or chemical with justification
Explains what conservation of mass means and why mass is conserved in chemical reactions
Names observable signs that a chemical reaction has occurred (colour change, gas produced, temperature change, precipitate)
Explains why dissolving is a physical change but burning is a chemical change
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} dissolved sugar in tea versus burnt toast in the toaster, could they explain which is a physical change and which is a chemical change — and what test would show that mass is conserved in both cases?
topics.nameZh: 物理变化与化学变化 (Physical vs Chemical Changes)
topics.descriptionZh: 区分物理变化（可逆，不生成新物质）和化学变化（生成新物质，通常不可逆），并利用质量守恒 (conservation of mass) 来理解这两种变化。
evidenceZh: 能够将给定的变化分类为物理变化或化学变化，并给出理由。
解释质量守恒 (conservation of mass) 的含义，以及为什么在化学反应中质量是守恒的。
列举发生化学反应时可观察到的迹象（颜色改变、产生气体、温度变化、生成沉淀 (precipitate)）。
解释为什么溶解 (dissolving) 是物理变化，而燃烧 (burning) 是化学变化。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}在茶水中溶解糖，或者在烤面包机里把面包烤焦，他们能否解释哪一个是物理变化，哪一个是化学变化——并且说明什么样的测试能证明在这两种情况下质量都是守恒的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Pure Substances & Mixtures
topics.description: Distinguish between pure substances and mixtures, identify formulations as useful mixtures with precise compositions, and use melting and boiling points to test for purity
evidence: Explains why a pure substance has a sharp, fixed melting point but a mixture melts over a range
Identifies common formulations (medicines, alloys, paints, fuels) as deliberate mixtures
Explains what impurities do to melting and boiling points
Distinguishes mixtures from compounds at the particle level
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was checking whether a sample of water was pure, could they explain one test they could do — and say what result would tell them it was definitely pure versus a mixture?
topics.descriptionZh: 区分纯净物与混合物，认识配方（formulations）作为具有精确成分的有用混合物，并利用熔点（melting points）和沸点（boiling points）来检验物质的纯度
evidenceZh: 解释为什么纯净物有固定且敏锐的熔点，而混合物在一个温度范围内熔化
识别常见的配方（如药品、合金、涂料、燃料）是人为刻意配制的混合物
解释杂质（impurities）对熔点和沸点会产生什么影响
在微粒（particle）层面上区分混合物与化合物（compounds）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 要检验一份水样是否为纯净物，他们能说出一种可以做的检验方法，并说明出现什么结果就能证明它绝对是纯净物而不是混合物吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Separating Mixtures
topics.description: Select and carry out appropriate separation techniques for different types of mixtures: filtration (insoluble solids), distillation (liquids by boiling point), crystallisation (dissolved solids), and chromatography (coloured substances)
evidence: Selects the correct separation technique for a given mixture with justification
Describes the steps of simple distillation and explains why it works
Interprets a chromatography result (Rf values, number of components)
Explains why filtration removes sand from water but not salt
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} needed to separate salt from sand mixed together in water, could they describe two stages of separation, the equipment needed, and explain why each step works?
topics.descriptionZh: 针对不同类型的混合物选择并进行合适的分离技术：过滤 (filtration，分离不溶性固体)、蒸馏 (distillation，根据沸点分离液体)、结晶 (crystallisation，分离溶解的固体) 和色谱法 (chromatography，分离有色物质)
evidenceZh: 能够为给定的混合物选择正确的分离技术并说明理由
描述简单蒸馏 (simple distillation) 的步骤并解释其原理
解释色谱法 (chromatography) 的结果（比移值 (Rf values)、组分数量）
解释为什么过滤 (filtration) 能去除水中的沙子，却不能去除盐
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 需要把混合在水中的盐和沙子分离开来，他们能否描述分离的两个阶段、所需的设备，并解释每个步骤为什么有效？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Particle Model
topics.description: Use the particle model to explain the properties of solids, liquids, and gases — including differences in arrangement, movement, and spacing — and apply the model to explain density, compressibility, and the anomalous expansion of water
evidence: Draws particle diagrams for solids, liquids, and gases showing correct arrangement and spacing
Explains why gases are compressible but liquids and solids are not
Explains why ice floats on water using the anomalous expansion of water
Uses particle spacing to explain why gases are much less dense than solids and liquids
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why you can squash a balloon but not a water bottle full of liquid, could they explain using the idea of particles what's different about gases and liquids?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用微粒模型（Particle Model）来解释固体、液体和气体的性质——包括排列、运动和间距的差异——并运用该模型来解释密度（Density）、可压缩性（Compressibility）以及水的反常膨胀（Anomalous Expansion）。
evidenceZh: 绘制固体、液体和气体的微粒图，展示正确的排列和间距
解释为什么气体可以被压缩，而液体和固体不能
利用水的反常膨胀解释为什么冰能浮在水面上
利用微粒间距解释为什么气体的密度远小于固体和液体
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果有人问{{name}}为什么可以压瘪气球却不能压瘪装满液体的水瓶，他们能用微粒的概念解释气体和液体有什么不同吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Periodic Table
topics.description: Describe the organisation of the periodic table into periods and groups, explain the contribution of Mendeleev, and use the table to identify metals, non-metals, and predict patterns in reactivity
evidence: Explains why the periodic table is arranged into periods (rows) and groups (columns)
States that elements in the same group have similar chemical properties
Locates metals, non-metals, and metalloids in the periodic table
Explains how Mendeleev ordered elements by atomic weight and predicted missing elements
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was looking at a periodic table, could they explain why elements in the same column tend to behave similarly — and say what Mendeleev did that made it so useful to chemists?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述元素周期表如何按周期（periods）和族（groups）进行组织，解释门捷列夫（Mendeleev）的贡献，并利用该表识别金属（metals）和非金属（non-metals），以及预测反应性（reactivity）的规律。
evidenceZh: 解释为什么元素周期表被排列成周期（行，rows）和族（列，columns）
说明同一族（group）中的元素具有相似的化学性质（chemical properties）
在元素周期表中找到金属（metals）、非金属（non-metals）和类金属（metalloids）的位置
解释门捷列夫（Mendeleev）是如何按原子量（atomic weight）对元素进行排序并预测缺失元素的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 正在观察元素周期表，他们能解释为什么同一列（族）里的元素往往表现出相似的性质吗？并且能说出是门捷列夫的什么发现让它对化学家如此有用吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Acid Reactions & Salts
topics.description: Describe and write word equations for the reactions of acids with metals, alkalis (neutralisation), and metal oxides/hydroxides, identifying the salt produced in each case
evidence: Writes word equations for: acid + metal → salt + hydrogen; acid + alkali → salt + water; acid + metal oxide → salt + water
Names the salt formed from a given acid and base (e.g. hydrochloric acid + sodium hydroxide → sodium chloride)
Describes the test for hydrogen gas (squeaky pop)
Explains what neutralisation means and gives a practical example (indigestion tablets, treating acidic soil)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked how an indigestion tablet works to relieve stomach acid, could they explain what type of chemical reaction is happening and write a simple word equation for it?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述并书写酸与金属、碱（中和反应 (neutralisation)）以及金属氧化物/氢氧化物反应的文字方程式 (word equations)，并指出每种情况下生成的盐。
evidenceZh: 写出以下文字方程式 (word equations)：酸 + 金属 → 盐 + 氢气；酸 + 碱 → 盐 + 水；酸 + 金属氧化物 → 盐 + 水
说出给定酸和碱反应生成的盐的名称（例如：盐酸 + 氢氧化钠 → 氯化钠）
描述氢气的检验方法（发出“噗”的爆鸣声 (squeaky pop)）
解释中和反应 (neutralisation) 的含义并给出实际例子（如服用抗酸胃药 (indigestion tablets)、处理酸性土壤）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果问 {{name}} 抗酸胃药 (indigestion tablet) 是如何缓解胃酸的，他们能否解释其中发生的化学反应类型，并写出一个简单的文字方程式 (word equation)？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Acids, Alkalis & pH
topics.description: Define acids and alkalis in terms of hydrogen ion concentration, describe the pH scale (0–14), and explain how indicators are used to identify and measure acidity or alkalinity
evidence: States that acids have pH below 7, alkalis have pH above 7, and neutral is pH 7
Explains what hydrogen ions (H⁺) have to do with acidity
Names common indicators (litmus, universal indicator) and describes colour changes
Identifies everyday acids (vinegar, lemon juice) and alkalis (bleach, bicarbonate of soda)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} used a piece of universal indicator paper to test lemon juice and baking soda solution, could they predict what colour each would turn and explain what that tells you about each substance?
topics.descriptionZh: 从氢离子（hydrogen ion）浓度的角度定义酸和碱，描述pH标度（pH scale, 0-14），并解释如何使用指示剂（indicators）来识别和测量酸度或碱度。
evidenceZh: 说明酸的pH值低于7，碱的pH值高于7，中性（neutral）物质的pH值为7。
解释氢离子（H⁺）与酸度的关系。
列举常见的指示剂（石蕊 litmus、通用指示剂 universal indicator）并描述其颜色变化。
识别日常生活中的酸（醋、柠檬汁）和碱（漂白剂、碳酸氢钠/小苏打）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 使用pH通用试纸（universal indicator paper）测试柠檬汁和小苏打溶液，他们能预测出每种溶液会变成什么颜色，并解释这说明了每种物质的什么性质吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Earth's Atmosphere & CO2
topics.description: Describe the composition of Earth's atmosphere (mainly nitrogen and oxygen, with small amounts of CO₂ and other gases), explain how human activity increases CO₂, and describe the impact on global climate
evidence: States the approximate percentages of nitrogen, oxygen, CO₂, and argon in the atmosphere
Explains how burning fossil fuels and deforestation increase atmospheric CO₂
Describes the greenhouse effect and how it leads to climate change
Discusses one specific consequence of climate change (e.g. rising sea levels, extreme weather)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why scientists are worried about CO₂ levels rising, could they explain what CO₂ does in the atmosphere, why human activities produce more of it, and what effects it's having on the planet?
topics.nameZh: 地球大气层与二氧化碳
topics.descriptionZh: 描述地球大气层的组成（主要为氮气和氧气，含有少量二氧化碳（CO₂）和其他气体），解释人类活动如何增加二氧化碳，并描述其对全球气候的影响。
evidenceZh: 说明大气中氮气、氧气、二氧化碳（CO₂）和氩气的大致百分比
解释燃烧化石燃料和砍伐森林如何增加大气中的二氧化碳
描述温室效应（greenhouse effect）及其如何导致气候变化
讨论气候变化的一个具体后果（例如海平面上升、极端天气）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果询问{{name}}为什么科学家对二氧化碳（CO₂）水平上升感到担忧，他们能否解释二氧化碳在大气中的作用、为什么人类活动会产生更多的二氧化碳，以及这对地球产生了什么影响？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Finite Resources & Recycling
topics.description: Explain that many raw materials (metals, fossil fuels, minerals) are finite resources, describe the environmental costs of extraction, and evaluate the benefits of recycling and the circular economy
evidence: Identifies examples of finite natural resources and explains why they are finite
Describes the environmental impact of mining and fossil fuel extraction
Explains why recycling metals saves energy compared to extraction from ores
Discusses trade-offs between the cost of recycling and the benefit of resource conservation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was deciding whether to recycle an aluminium drinks can or throw it away, could they explain what goes into making new aluminium from scratch — and why recycling it uses much less energy?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释许多原材料（如金属、化石燃料、矿物）是有限资源（finite resources），描述开采（extraction）带来的环境成本，并评估回收利用（recycling）和循环经济（circular economy）的益处。
evidenceZh: 列举有限自然资源的例子，并解释为什么它们是有限的
描述采矿和化石燃料开采对环境的影响
解释与从矿石中提炼相比，为什么回收金属能节省能源
讨论回收利用成本与资源保护效益之间的权衡（trade-offs）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}在决定是回收一个铝制饮料罐还是把它扔掉，他们能否解释从零开始制造新铝材需要经历哪些过程——以及为什么回收利用它消耗的能源要少得多？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Reactions That Release or Absorb Heat
topics.description: Distinguish between exothermic reactions (release energy, temperature rises) and endothermic reactions (absorb energy, temperature falls), with everyday and industrial examples
evidence: Defines exothermic and endothermic in terms of energy transfer to and from the surroundings
Gives two examples of each type from everyday life (e.g. combustion, hand warmers; photosynthesis, cold packs)
Explains energy changes during changes of state (melting is endothermic, freezing is exothermic)
Interprets a temperature change in an experiment to classify the reaction type
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} shook a sports cold pack to activate it and it got cold, or lit a match and it got hot, could they explain what type of reaction is happening in each case and why one gets hot while the other gets cold?
topics.nameZh: 释放或吸收热量的反应（放热与吸热反应）
topics.descriptionZh: 区分放热反应（exothermic reactions，释放能量，温度升高）和吸热反应（endothermic reactions，吸收能量，温度降低），并结合日常生活和工业中的实例进行说明。
evidenceZh: 根据能量向周围环境的释放和吸收情况，定义放热反应（exothermic）和吸热反应（endothermic）。
给出日常生活中每种反应类型的两个例子（例如：燃烧、暖宝宝；光合作用、冷敷袋）。
解释物态变化过程中的能量变化（熔化是吸热的，凝固是放热的）。
根据实验中观察到的温度变化来推断和分类反应的类型。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 摇晃运动冷敷袋使其激活并感觉到变冷，或者点燃一根火柴并感觉到变热，他们能解释每种情况下发生的是哪种类型的反应，以及为什么一个变热而另一个变冷吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Reactivity Series
topics.description: Order common metals in the reactivity series and explain how a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one; describe how carbon is used to extract metals from their oxides in industry
evidence: Recalls the order of common metals in the reactivity series (potassium to gold)
Predicts whether a displacement reaction will occur given two metals
Explains why carbon can be used to extract iron from iron oxide but not aluminium from aluminium oxide
Links the reactivity series to the history of metal use (gold found free, iron smelted, aluminium electrolytic)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why humans used gold and copper before iron and aluminium, could they explain how a metal's reactivity determines how easy it is to extract — and why carbon can extract some metals but not others?
topics.nameZh: 金属活动性顺序 (The Reactivity Series)
topics.descriptionZh: 将常见金属按活动性顺序排列，并解释活动性较强的金属如何置换出活动性较弱的金属；描述在工业上如何利用碳从金属氧化物 (oxides) 中提取金属。
evidenceZh: 能够记住常见金属在金属活动性顺序表中的排列顺序（从钾到金）
能够预测在给定两种金属的情况下是否会发生置换反应 (displacement reaction)
能够解释为什么可以用碳从氧化铁中提取铁，却不能从氧化铝中提取铝
能够将金属活动性顺序与金属使用的历史联系起来（金以游离态 (free state) 存在、铁通过冶炼获得、铝通过电解 (electrolysis) 获得）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果向 {{name}} 提问，为什么人类在铁和铝之前先使用了金和铜，{{name}} 能否解释金属的活动性如何决定了其提取的难易程度——以及为什么碳可以提取某些金属而不能提取其他金属？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Rock Cycle
topics.description: Explain the rock cycle: how igneous rocks form from magma, sedimentary rocks from compressed sediment, and metamorphic rocks from heat and pressure, and how all rock types can transform into one another over geological time
evidence: Describes how each rock type (igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic) is formed
Gives an example of each rock type and its formation (e.g. granite, limestone, marble)
Traces a rock sample through possible transitions in the rock cycle
Explains what geological time means and why rock cycle changes are slow
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} picked up a piece of marble on a school trip, could they explain how it was originally limestone, what changed it into marble, and how long that process took?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释岩石循环：火成岩（igneous rocks）如何由岩浆（magma）形成，沉积岩（sedimentary rocks）如何由压缩的沉积物形成，变质岩（metamorphic rocks）如何由热量和压力形成，以及所有岩石类型如何在地质时间（geological time）尺度上相互转化。
evidenceZh: 描述每种岩石类型（火成岩、沉积岩、变质岩）是如何形成的
给出每种岩石类型及其形成的例子（例如花岗岩、石灰岩、大理石）
追踪一块岩石样本在岩石循环中可能经历的转变过程
解释地质时间（geological time）的含义，以及为什么岩石循环的变化是缓慢的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在学校郊游时捡到了一块大理石，他们能否解释它最初是如何从石灰岩变来的，是什么把它变成了大理石，以及这个过程花了多长时间？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Types of Chemical Reaction
topics.description: Identify and describe four types of chemical reaction: combustion (burning in oxygen), oxidation (gain of oxygen), thermal decomposition (breaking down by heat), and displacement (more reactive metal replaces less reactive one)
evidence: Writes a word equation for each type of reaction with an example
Identifies the type of reaction from a given word equation or description
Explains what makes a displacement reaction happen (relative reactivity)
Distinguishes complete combustion (CO₂ and H₂O) from incomplete combustion (CO and soot)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw iron going rusty and a candle burning, could they explain what type of chemical reaction is happening in each case — and write a simple word equation for one of them?
topics.nameZh: 化学反应类型 (Types of Chemical Reaction)
topics.descriptionZh: 识别并描述四种化学反应类型：燃烧（在氧气中燃烧）(combustion)、氧化（得到氧）(oxidation)、热分解（受热分解）(thermal decomposition) 和置换反应（较活泼金属置换较不活泼金属）(displacement)。
evidenceZh: 为每种类型的反应写出文字方程式（word equation）并举例
根据给定的文字方程式或描述识别反应类型
解释是什么促使置换反应发生（相对活泼性 / relative reactivity）
区分完全燃烧（CO₂和H₂O）与不完全燃烧（CO和炭黑）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到铁生锈和蜡烛燃烧，他们能解释这两种情况下分别发生的是哪种类型的化学反应，并为其中一种写出一个简单的文字方程式（word equation）吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Ceramics, Polymers & Composites
topics.description: Describe the properties and uses of ceramics (hard, brittle, heat-resistant), polymers (flexible, lightweight, variable), and composites (combine properties of constituent materials), giving real-world examples of each
evidence: Gives the key properties of ceramics, polymers, and composites with examples of each
Explains why a composite material is used rather than a single material in a given application (e.g. carbon-fibre reinforced plastic in bikes)
Identifies natural and synthetic polymers
Explains why polymer properties can be tailored during manufacturing
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was looking at a racing bicycle made of carbon fibre, could they explain why neither carbon nor plastic alone would work as well — and what makes the combination a composite better than either material on its own?
topics.nameZh: 陶瓷、聚合物与复合材料
topics.descriptionZh: 描述陶瓷（ceramics：坚硬、易碎、耐热）、聚合物（polymers：柔韧、轻质、性质多变）和复合材料（composites：结合了组成材料的特性）的性质与用途，并给出每种材料在现实生活中的具体例子。
evidenceZh: 列出陶瓷、聚合物和复合材料的关键性质，并举出每种材料的例子
解释在特定应用中（例如自行车中的碳纤维增强塑料）为什么使用复合材料而不是单一材料
识别天然聚合物和合成聚合物
解释为什么在制造过程中可以调整聚合物的性质
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到一辆用碳纤维（carbon fibre）制成的赛车，他们能解释为什么单独的碳或单独的塑料都不如它好用吗？——并且能说明这种组合而成的复合材料（composite）为什么比任何一种单一材料都更优秀吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Coasts & Beaches
topics.description: Know what a coast or beach is — the place where land meets the ocean — and that different coasts can be sandy, rocky, or muddy, each with different plants and animals
evidence: Define a coast as where land meets the ocean
Describe at least two types of coast: sandy, rocky, or muddy
Name an animal likely found at each type of coast
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visited a sandy beach and then a rocky shore, could they describe how the two coasts look different and name animals you might find at each one?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解什么是海岸或海滩——即陆地与海洋交汇的地方——并知道不同的海岸可以是沙质的、岩石的或泥质的，每种海岸都有不同的植物和动物。
evidenceZh: 将海岸定义为陆地与海洋交汇的地方
描述至少两种海岸类型：沙质、岩石或泥质海岸
说出每种海岸类型上可能发现的动物名称
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 先去了一个沙质海滩，然后又去了一个岩石海岸，他们能描述出这两个海岸的外观有什么不同，并说出在各自那里可能找到的动物吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Ocean Animal Variety
topics.description: Recognise that the ocean is home to an amazing variety of animals — from tiny seahorses and colourful clownfish to enormous whales and sharks — and that ocean animals come in many shapes and sizes
evidence: Name at least five different ocean animals
Describe differences in size between small and large ocean creatures
Express curiosity or wonder about the variety of life in the ocean
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visited an aquarium or watched an ocean documentary, could they name at least five different ocean animals and describe how different they are from each other?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识到海洋是众多奇妙动物的家园——从微小的海马、色彩斑斓的小丑鱼，到巨大的鲸鱼和鲨鱼——并且海洋动物有着各种各样的形状和体型。
evidenceZh: 至少说出五种不同的海洋动物
描述小型和大型海洋生物在体型上的差异
对海洋中生命的多样性表达好奇或惊叹
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}参观了水族馆或观看了海洋纪录片，他们能说出至少五种不同的海洋动物，并描述它们之间的不同之处吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Ocean Food Chains
topics.description: Describe a simple ocean food chain: tiny plants (phytoplankton) are eaten by small animals, which are eaten by bigger fish, which are eaten by top predators like sharks — showing that all ocean life depends on others for food
evidence: Describe a food chain with at least three levels
Identify that ocean food chains start with tiny plants or algae
Explain that bigger animals eat smaller ones in a chain of dependence
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw or describe a chain showing how tiny ocean plants are eaten by small creatures, then by bigger fish, then by a shark — explaining that each animal depends on the one before it?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述一个简单的海洋食物链：微小的植物（浮游植物）被小动物吃掉，小动物被更大的鱼吃掉，大鱼又被鲨鱼等顶级捕食者吃掉——这表明所有海洋生物都依赖其他生物获取食物。
evidenceZh: 描述一个至少包含三个层级的食物链
指出海洋食物链从微小的植物或藻类开始
解释在相互依赖的食物链中，较大的动物会吃掉较小的动物
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否画出或描述这样一条食物链：微小的海洋植物被小生物吃掉，然后小生物被更大的鱼吃掉，最后大鱼被鲨鱼吃掉——并解释每种动物都依赖排在它前面的动物？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rock Pool Habitats
topics.description: Explore rock pools (tide pools) as small ocean habitats where crabs, anemones, starfish, and small fish can be found, and understand that these creatures are adapted to survive crashing waves and changing water levels
evidence: Name at least three creatures found in rock pools
Describe a rock pool as a small ocean habitat on the shore
Explain one way rock pool animals cope with waves or changing water levels
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} explored a rock pool at the beach, could they point out the creatures living there and explain how they hold on tight or hide in cracks when waves come?
topics.descriptionZh: 探索潮池（tide pools）这一小型海洋栖息地，了解那里生活着螃蟹、海葵（anemones）、海星和小鱼，并理解这些生物是如何适应汹涌的波浪和不断变化的水位而生存下来的。
evidenceZh: 说出至少三种在潮池中发现的生物
将潮池描述为海岸上的一个小型海洋栖息地
解释一种潮池动物应对波浪或水位变化的方法
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在海滩上探索潮池，他们能指出生活在那里的生物，并解释当海浪袭来时，这些生物是如何紧紧抓住物体或藏在裂缝里的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Whales & Dolphins Are Mammals
topics.description: Know that whales and dolphins are mammals, not fish — they breathe air, are warm-blooded, and feed their babies milk — even though they live in the ocean
evidence: State that whales and dolphins are mammals, not fish
Give at least two reasons why: they breathe air and feed babies milk
Explain that living in water does not make an animal a fish
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a dolphin jumping out of the water, could they explain that dolphins are mammals like us — they breathe air and feed their babies milk — not fish?
topics.nameZh: 鲸鱼和海豚是哺乳动物
topics.descriptionZh: 了解鲸鱼和海豚是哺乳动物(Mammals)，而不是鱼类——它们呼吸空气、是恒温动物(Warm-blooded)，并且用乳汁哺育幼崽——尽管它们生活在海洋中。
evidenceZh: 说明鲸鱼和海豚是哺乳动物(Mammals)，而不是鱼类
给出至少两个原因：它们呼吸空气并且用乳汁哺育幼崽
解释生活在水里并不能使动物变成鱼类
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}看到海豚跃出水面，他们能解释海豚和人类一样是哺乳动物(Mammals)——它们呼吸空气并用乳汁哺育幼崽——而不是鱼类吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: What Is the Ocean?
topics.description: Know that oceans are huge bodies of salt water that cover most of Earth's surface, and that the ocean is home to an enormous number of living things
evidence: State that oceans cover more of Earth than land does
Explain that ocean water is salty, unlike the fresh water in rivers and lakes
Describe the ocean as home to a huge variety of living things
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you asked {{name}} to point to the oceans on a globe, could they show you and explain that most of our planet is covered by salty water where millions of creatures live?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解海洋是覆盖地球大部分表面的巨大咸水（salt water）水体，并且海洋是无数生物（living things）的家园。
evidenceZh: 说明海洋覆盖地球的面积比陆地更大
解释海水是咸的，这与河流和湖泊里的淡水（fresh water）不同
描述海洋是种类繁多的大量生物的家园
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你让{{name}}在地球仪上指出海洋的位置，他们能指出来并解释我们星球的大部分被咸水覆盖，那里生活着数以百万计的生物吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: What Ocean Animals Need
topics.description: Understand that ocean animals need food, shelter, and the right conditions to survive — just like land animals — and that different parts of the ocean provide for different animals' needs
evidence: List basic needs of ocean animals: food, shelter, suitable water conditions
Give an example of how a specific ocean animal meets its needs
Compare an ocean animal's needs to a familiar land animal's needs
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that a clownfish needs a sea anemone for shelter and small creatures to eat, just like a bird needs a tree for a nest and seeds to eat?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解海洋动物和陆地动物一样，需要食物、庇护所和适宜的生存条件，并且海洋的不同区域为不同动物提供了它们所需的生存资源。
evidenceZh: 列出海洋动物的基本需求：食物、庇护所、适宜的水域条件
举例说明某种特定的海洋动物是如何满足其生存需求的
将某种海洋动物的需求与熟悉的陆地动物的需求进行比较
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释小丑鱼需要海葵来提供庇护所并捕食小型生物，就像鸟儿需要树木筑巢和吃种子一样？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Classifying Ocean Animals
topics.description: Classify ocean animals into major groups: fish (breathe through gills, have scales), marine mammals (breathe air, warm-blooded, feed milk), and invertebrates (no backbone — jellyfish, octopuses, crabs, starfish)
evidence: Sort ocean animals into fish, marine mammals, and invertebrates
Give defining features of each group (gills vs lungs, backbone vs none)
Correctly classify at least two animals in each group
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw pictures of a tuna, a seal, and a jellyfish, could they sort them into fish, marine mammals, and invertebrates, and explain what makes each group different?
topics.descriptionZh: 将海洋动物分为主要类群：鱼类 (fish)（用鳃 (gills) 呼吸，长有鳞片）、海洋哺乳动物 (marine mammals)（呼吸空气，恒温 (warm-blooded)，哺乳 (feed milk)）和无脊椎动物 (invertebrates)（没有脊椎骨 (backbone)——例如水母、章鱼、螃蟹和海星）。
evidenceZh: 将海洋动物分为鱼类 (fish)、海洋哺乳动物 (marine mammals) 和无脊椎动物 (invertebrates)
说出每个类群的显著特征（用鳃 (gills) 还是用肺 (lungs) 呼吸，有脊椎骨 (backbone) 还是无脊椎骨）
能正确地将每个类群中至少两种动物进行分类
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到金枪鱼 (tuna)、海豹 (seal) 和水母 (jellyfish) 的图片，他们能把它们分入鱼类 (fish)、海洋哺乳动物 (marine mammals) 和无脊椎动物 (invertebrates)，并解释每个类群有什么不同之处吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Coral Reefs
topics.description: Know that coral reefs are built by tiny living animals called coral polyps, that reefs are home to more species than almost any other ocean habitat, and that they are sometimes called the 'rainforests of the sea'
evidence: State that coral is built by tiny living animals called polyps, not made of rock
Describe coral reefs as one of the most biodiverse habitats in the ocean
Explain why reefs are compared to rainforests
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watched a documentary about coral reefs, could they explain that coral is actually made by tiny living animals, and that reefs are home to an incredible number of different species?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解珊瑚礁是由被称为珊瑚虫（coral polyps）的微小活体动物建造的，知道珊瑚礁栖息的物种比几乎所有其他海洋栖息地都多，并且它们有时被称为“海洋中的热带雨林”。
evidenceZh: 说明珊瑚是由被称为珊瑚虫（polyps）的微小活体动物建造的，而不是由岩石构成的
将珊瑚礁描述为海洋中生物多样性（biodiversity）最丰富的栖息地之一
解释为什么珊瑚礁常被比作热带雨林
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 观看了一部关于珊瑚礁的纪录片，他们能解释珊瑚实际上是由微小的活体动物建造的，并且珊瑚礁栖息着数量惊人的不同物种吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Ocean Animal Adaptations
topics.description: Understand that ocean animals have special adaptations for their environment: streamlined bodies for fast swimming, camouflage to hide from predators, blubber to keep warm in cold seas, and tentacles or suckers to catch prey
evidence: Name at least three different ocean animal adaptations
Explain how each adaptation helps the animal survive in its environment
Connect an adaptation to the specific challenge it addresses (cold, predators, catching food)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} pick an ocean animal and explain at least two ways its body is specially designed for life in the sea — like a seal's blubber for warmth or an octopus's camouflage for hiding?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解海洋动物对其环境具有特殊的适应性（adaptations）：用于快速游泳的流线型身体（streamlined bodies）、用于躲避捕食者的伪装（camouflage）、用于在寒冷海域保暖的鲸脂（blubber），以及用于捕捉猎物的触手或吸盘（tentacles or suckers）。
evidenceZh: 说出至少三种不同的海洋动物适应性（adaptations）
解释每种适应性如何帮助动物在其环境中生存
将某种适应性与它所应对的具体挑战（寒冷、捕食者、捕捉食物）联系起来
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否选择一种海洋动物，并解释其身体至少有哪两种特别设计以适应海洋生活——例如海豹的鲸脂（blubber）用于保暖，或章鱼的伪装（camouflage）用于隐藏？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Ocean Depth Zones
topics.description: Understand that the ocean has different zones depending on depth and light: the sunlight zone near the surface where most life lives, the twilight zone where light fades, and the midnight zone of total darkness
evidence: Name the three main ocean zones: sunlight, twilight, and midnight
Explain that light decreases with depth until it disappears completely
State that most ocean life is found in the sunlight zone because plants need light to grow
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a diagram showing the ocean getting darker as you go deeper, could they name the three main zones and explain why most ocean animals live near the sunlit surface?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解海洋根据深度和光线分为不同的区域：靠近表层、大多数生物居住的阳光带（Sunlight Zone），光线逐渐变暗的暮光带（Twilight Zone），以及完全黑暗的午夜带（Midnight Zone）。
evidenceZh: 说出三个主要的海洋带：阳光带（Sunlight Zone）、暮光带（Twilight Zone）和午夜带（Midnight Zone）
解释光线随着深度增加而减弱，直到完全消失
说明大多数海洋生物生活在阳光带，因为植物需要光线才能生长
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到一幅显示海洋越往深处越暗的图表，他们能说出三个主要的海洋带，并解释为什么大多数海洋动物生活在阳光充足的表层附近吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Ocean Food Webs
topics.description: Understand ocean food webs: multiple interconnected food chains where energy flows from phytoplankton (producers) through zooplankton, small fish, and large predators, and that removing one species affects the whole web
evidence: Distinguish a food web from a simple food chain
Trace at least two paths of energy through an ocean food web
Explain what could happen if one species in the web were removed
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why catching too many of one type of fish doesn't just affect that fish — it affects the whole food web, including the animals that eat it and the things it eats?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解海洋食物网：它是由多条相互连接的食物链组成的网络，能量从浮游植物（生产者）开始，流经浮游动物、小鱼和大型捕食者，并且移除其中任何一个物种都会影响整个食物网。
evidenceZh: 区分食物网与简单的食物链
在海洋食物网中追踪至少两条能量流动的路径
解释如果移除食物网中的某一个物种可能会发生什么
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释为什么过度捕捞某一种鱼类不仅仅影响该鱼类本身——它还会影响整个食物网，包括以它为食的动物和它所吃的生物？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Five Oceans
topics.description: Name and locate the five oceans — Pacific (largest), Atlantic, Indian, Southern, and Arctic (smallest and coldest) — on a world map, and understand that they are all connected as one global ocean
evidence: Name all five oceans: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic
Locate at least three oceans on a world map
Explain that the five named oceans are all connected as one continuous body of water
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a world map, could they point to each of the five oceans by name and explain that they're all connected into one big global ocean?
topics.descriptionZh: 在世界地图上说出并找出五大洋的位置——太平洋 (Pacific)（最大）、大西洋 (Atlantic)、印度洋 (Indian)、南大洋 (Southern) 和北冰洋 (Arctic)（最小且最冷），并理解它们相互连接，构成一个全球性的海洋。
evidenceZh: 说出所有五大洋的名称：太平洋 (Pacific)、大西洋 (Atlantic)、印度洋 (Indian)、南大洋 (Southern)、北冰洋 (Arctic)
在世界地图上指出至少三个大洋的位置
解释这五个被命名的大洋是如何相互连接，形成一个连续水体的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看着世界地图，他们能否按名称指出每个大洋的位置，并解释它们是如何连接成一个巨大的全球海洋的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Ocean Floor
topics.description: Know that the ocean floor is not flat — it has mountains, valleys, and the deepest trenches on Earth — and that the deepest point is the Mariana Trench, deeper than Mount Everest is tall
evidence: State that the ocean floor has varied terrain including mountains, ridges, and trenches
Name the Mariana Trench as the deepest point on Earth
Compare its depth to a familiar reference like Mount Everest's height
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that the ocean floor has mountains and valleys, could they explain that it's not flat and that the Mariana Trench is the deepest spot on Earth — deeper than Everest is tall?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解海底并非平坦无奇——它有着连绵的山脉、深邃的山谷和地球上最深的海沟——并且知道最深的地方是马里亚纳海沟（Mariana Trench），它的深度甚至超过了珠穆朗玛峰（Mount Everest）的高度。
evidenceZh: 说明海底拥有多变的地形，包括山脉、海岭（ridges）和海沟（trenches）。
说出马里亚纳海沟（Mariana Trench）是地球上的最深处。
将其深度与熟悉的参照物进行比较，比如珠穆朗玛峰（Mount Everest）的高度。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 听说海底有山脉和山谷，他们能否解释海底并不是平的，而且马里亚纳海沟（Mariana Trench）是地球上最深的地方——比珠穆朗玛峰（Mount Everest）的高度还要深？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Tides, Waves & Currents
topics.description: Know that the ocean has tides (water level rises and falls twice a day, caused mainly by the Moon's gravity), waves (caused by wind), and currents (rivers of water flowing through the ocean that carry warmth and nutrients around the world)
evidence: Describe tides as the regular rise and fall of water level, caused by the Moon's gravity
Explain that waves are caused by wind blowing across the water surface
Describe ocean currents as large flows of water that carry heat and nutrients around the globe
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} noticed the water level changing at the beach during the day, could they explain that tides are caused by the Moon's pull, and that the ocean also has waves from wind and currents that flow like underwater rivers?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解海洋有潮汐（水位每天涨落两次，主要由月球引力（gravity）引起）、海浪（由风引起）和洋流（在海洋中流动的“河流”，将温暖和营养物质输送到世界各地）
evidenceZh: 描述潮汐为水位的规律性涨落，这是由月球引力（gravity）引起的
解释海浪是由风吹过水面引起的
描述洋流为巨大的水流，它们将热量和营养物质输送到全球各地
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在海滩上注意到白天水位发生变化，他们能解释潮汐是由月球引力引起的，并且海洋中还有风吹起的海浪，以及像水下河流一样流动的洋流吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Deep-Sea Creatures
topics.description: Explore life in the deep sea: animals that make their own light (bioluminescence), creatures adapted to crushing pressure and total darkness, and hydrothermal vents where life thrives without sunlight
evidence: Define bioluminescence as the ability of some deep-sea creatures to produce their own light
Describe at least two adaptations deep-sea animals have for life in darkness and pressure
Explain that hydrothermal vents support life without sunlight through chemical energy
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw footage of glowing deep-sea creatures, could they explain how some animals make their own light and why life can exist even in the deepest, darkest parts of the ocean?
topics.descriptionZh: 探索深海生命：会自己发光的动物（生物发光 bioluminescence），适应巨大压力和完全黑暗的奇特生物，以及在没有阳光的情况下依然生机勃勃的海底热液喷口（hydrothermal vents）
evidenceZh: 将生物发光（bioluminescence）定义为某些深海生物自己发光的能力
描述深海动物为了适应黑暗和高压环境而具备的至少两种生理特征
解释海底热液喷口（hydrothermal vents）如何通过化学能量在没有阳光的情况下维持生命
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到发光深海生物的影像，他们能解释一些动物是如何自己发光的，以及为什么在海洋最深、最黑的地方依然有生命存在吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Exploring the Ocean
topics.description: Know that oceanographers and marine biologists study the ocean using submarines, remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), satellites, and diving, and that much of the ocean remains unexplored — we know more about the Moon's surface than the deep ocean floor
evidence: Name at least two tools scientists use to explore the ocean: submarines, ROVs, satellites
State that most of the deep ocean remains unexplored
Explain why ocean exploration is difficult: darkness, pressure, vastness
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how scientists explore the deep ocean using robots and submarines, and why we've still only explored a small fraction of the ocean floor — less than we know about the Moon?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解海洋学家（oceanographers）和海洋生物学家（marine biologists）如何使用潜水艇（submarines）、遥控潜水器（remotely operated vehicles, ROVs）、卫星（satellites）以及潜水来研究海洋，并且知道海洋的大部分仍未被探索——我们对月球表面的了解甚至多于对深海海底的了解。
evidenceZh: 说出至少两种科学家用来探索海洋的工具：潜水艇（submarines）、遥控潜水器（ROVs）、卫星（satellites）
说明深海的大部分区域仍未被探索
解释为什么海洋探索很困难：黑暗（darkness）、高压（pressure）、广阔（vastness）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释科学家如何使用机器人（robots）和潜水艇（submarines）探索深海，以及为什么我们至今只探索了海底的一小部分——甚至比我们对月球的了解还要少？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Ocean Animal Migrations
topics.description: Know that many ocean animals undertake remarkable migrations — humpback whales travel thousands of miles between feeding and breeding grounds, sea turtles return to the same beach where they hatched to lay eggs — and understand these journeys are linked to seasonal food supplies and reproduction
evidence: Describe at least one example of marine animal migration in detail
Explain that migrations are driven by seasonal food availability and breeding needs
Estimate the scale of these journeys (thousands of miles)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that a humpback whale swims from Antarctica to the tropics every year, could they explain why — that it's following food in summer and heading to warmer waters to have its baby?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解许多海洋动物会进行令人惊叹的迁徙（migration）——座头鲸（humpback whales）在觅食地和繁殖地之间跋涉数千英里，海龟会回到它们破壳而出的同一片海滩产卵——并理解这些旅程与季节性食物供应和繁殖需求密切相关。
evidenceZh: 详细描述至少一个海洋动物迁徙的例子
解释迁徙是由季节性食物供应和繁殖需求所驱动的
估算这些旅程的规模（数千英里）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 听说座头鲸每年从南极游到热带海域，他们能解释其中的原因吗——即夏天追随食物，然后前往温暖的水域孕育宝宝？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Ocean Ecosystems
topics.description: Understand ocean ecosystems as interconnected systems where living things (producers, consumers, decomposers) and non-living factors (temperature, salinity, light, currents) all interact, and that changes to one part affect the whole system
evidence: Describe an ocean ecosystem as a system of living and non-living parts that interact
Name key non-living factors that affect ocean life: temperature, salinity, light, currents
Explain how a change in one factor (like temperature) cascades through the whole ecosystem
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why warmer ocean temperatures don't just affect one species — they change the whole ecosystem, from the plankton at the bottom of the food web to the whales at the top?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解海洋生态系统是一个相互关联的系统，其中的生物（生产者 (producers)、消费者 (consumers)、分解者 (decomposers)）和非生物因素（温度 (temperature)、盐度 (salinity)、光照 (light)、洋流 (currents)）相互作用，且系统中任何一部分的变化都会影响整个系统。
evidenceZh: 描述海洋生态系统是一个由生物和非生物部分相互作用组成的系统。
说出影响海洋生物的关键非生物因素：温度 (temperature)、盐度 (salinity)、光照 (light)、洋流 (currents)。
解释一个因素（如温度）的变化如何引发整个生态系统的连锁反应 (cascade)。
