topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么海洋温度变暖不仅仅影响单一物种——它会改变整个生态系统，从食物网 (food web) 底部的浮游生物 (plankton) 到顶部的鲸鱼？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Ocean Pollution & Harm
topics.description: Identify ways humans harm the ocean — plastic pollution, overfishing, oil spills, and ocean acidification from carbon dioxide — and understand that most ocean pollution comes from land-based activities, not just ships
evidence: Name at least three ways humans harm the ocean
Explain that most ocean pollution originates on land, not from ships
Describe how plastic pollution or overfishing specifically harms marine animals
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw plastic washed up on a beach, could they explain where it came from, how it harms sea life, and name other ways humans damage the ocean like overfishing and pollution from factories?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解人类是如何伤害海洋的——比如塑料污染（plastic pollution）、过度捕捞（overfishing）、石油泄漏（oil spills）和二氧化碳导致的海洋酸化（ocean acidification）——并明白大部分的海洋污染其实来自陆地上的活动，而不仅仅是因为船只。
evidenceZh: 说出至少三种人类伤害海洋的方式
解释大部分海洋污染是源自陆地，而不是来自船只
描述塑料污染或过度捕捞具体是如何伤害海洋动物的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到海滩上冲上来塑料垃圾，他们能解释这些塑料是从哪里来的、是如何伤害海洋生物的，并说出人类破坏海洋的其他方式（比如过度捕捞和工厂污染）吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Oceans & Climate
topics.description: Understand the connection between the ocean and climate: the ocean absorbs heat and carbon dioxide, drives weather patterns through evaporation, and ocean currents distribute warmth around the planet — making the ocean Earth's climate engine
evidence: Explain that the ocean absorbs a large amount of the Sun's heat and atmospheric carbon dioxide
Describe the ocean's role in the water cycle through evaporation
Explain how ocean currents distribute warmth and affect weather patterns in distant places
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the ocean is sometimes called Earth's climate engine — that it absorbs heat, drives rain through evaporation, and moves warmth around the world through currents?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解海洋与气候之间的联系：海洋吸收热量和二氧化碳（carbon dioxide），通过蒸发（evaporation）影响天气变化，洋流（ocean currents）把温暖输送到世界各地——让海洋成为地球的“气候引擎（climate engine）”。
evidenceZh: 解释海洋如何吸收大量的太阳热量和大气中的二氧化碳（carbon dioxide）
描述海洋通过蒸发（evaporation）在水循环（water cycle）中发挥的作用
解释洋流（ocean currents）如何输送热量并影响遥远地区的天气模式
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么海洋有时被称为地球的“气候引擎（climate engine）”——即它吸收热量、通过蒸发（evaporation）带来降雨，并通过洋流（ocean currents）将温暖输送到世界各地？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Protecting the Ocean
topics.description: Understand how people protect the ocean: marine protected areas limit fishing and pollution, sustainable fishing prevents overharvesting, beach clean-ups reduce plastic, and international agreements aim to reduce carbon emissions that cause ocean acidification
evidence: Explain what a marine protected area is and why it helps
Describe sustainable fishing as taking only what the ocean can replace
Name at least two actions people can take to protect oceans: reducing plastic, marine reserves, cutting emissions
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard about a marine protected area where fishing is banned, could they explain why it helps — and name other ways people are working to protect the ocean from pollution, overfishing, and climate change?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解人们如何保护海洋：海洋保护区（marine protected areas）限制捕鱼和污染，可持续捕捞（sustainable fishing）防止过度捕捞，海滩清理减少塑料垃圾，国际协议旨在减少导致海洋酸化（ocean acidification）的碳排放。
evidenceZh: 解释什么是海洋保护区（marine protected area）以及它为什么有帮助
描述可持续捕捞（sustainable fishing）就是只捕捞海洋能够自然恢复的数量
说出人们可以采取的至少两项保护海洋的行动：减少塑料使用、建立海洋保护区、减少碳排放
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 听说了一个禁止捕鱼的海洋保护区（marine protected area），他们能解释这为什么有帮助吗——并说出人们还在用哪些其他方法来保护海洋免受污染、过度捕捞和气候变化的影响？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Deep-Sea Life Without Sunlight
topics.description: Contrast photosynthesis (energy from sunlight) with chemosynthesis (energy from oxidising chemicals like hydrogen sulphide); describe hydrothermal vent communities: chemoautotrophic bacteria form the base of a food web supporting tube worms, giant clams, and vent crabs with no sunlight; explore what deep-sea life tells us about the origin of life on Earth; explain why NASA studies ocean vents as analogues for potential life around hydrothermal activity on Europa and Enceladus
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe a community of animals living at the bottom of the ocean that gets its energy from volcanic chemicals rather than sunlight — and explain why scientists are excited about what this might mean for life on other planets?
topics.descriptionZh: 对比光合作用（利用阳光获取能量）与化能合成作用（chemosynthesis，利用氧化氢硫化氢等化学物质获取能量）；描述海底热液喷口（hydrothermal vent）群落：化能自养细菌（chemoautotrophic bacteria）构成了食物网的基础，在完全没有阳光的环境中滋养着管虫、巨蛤和喷口蟹；探索深海生命对地球生命起源的启示；解释为什么美国宇航局（NASA）将深海热液喷口作为木卫二（Europa）和土卫二（Enceladus）潜在生命的模拟环境（analogues）进行研究。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否描述一个生活在海底、依靠火山化学物质而不是阳光获取能量的动物群落，并解释为什么科学家对这一现象可能暗示其他星球上存在生命感到如此兴奋？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Ocean Currents and Global Heat
topics.description: Explain thermohaline circulation (the global conveyor belt) as driven by temperature and salinity differences that cause dense water to sink; describe how the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) transfers heat from the tropics toward Europe; explain that oceans absorb more than 90% of excess heat and ~25% of CO2 from human emissions; explore what would happen to Northern European climates if circulation weakened
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the UK has mild winters compared to parts of Canada at similar latitudes — what does ocean circulation have to do with it, and what might change if that circulation slows down?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释温盐环流（thermohaline circulation，即全球海洋输送带）是如何由温度和盐度差异导致高密度海水下沉而驱动的；描述大西洋经向翻转环流（AMOC）如何将热量从热带传输至欧洲；解释海洋吸收了超过90%的过剩热量以及人类排放的约25%的二氧化碳（CO2）；探讨如果该环流减弱，北欧气候将会发生怎样的变化。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释为什么与加拿大同纬度地区相比，英国的冬季更为温和——这与洋流有什么关系？如果该洋流减缓，可能会发生什么变化？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Coral Bleaching & Acidification
topics.description: Explain the mutualistic symbiosis between coral polyps and photosynthetic zooxanthellae; describe how heat stress causes bleaching (corals expel zooxanthellae and turn white); explain ocean acidification chemistry: CO2 dissolves in seawater to form carbonic acid, lowering pH and dissolving calcium carbonate skeletons; connect reef loss to the collapse of habitat for ~25% of marine species; evaluate current reef restoration efforts
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} heard of coral bleaching? Can they explain what's actually happening to the coral — what breaks down between the coral and the tiny algae living inside it, and why warmer or more acidic water triggers this?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释珊瑚虫（coral polyps）和进行光合作用的虫黄藻（zooxanthellae）之间的互利共生关系；描述高温压力如何导致白化（珊瑚排出虫黄藻并变成白色）；解释海洋酸化的化学原理：二氧化碳（CO2）溶解在海水中形成碳酸（carbonic acid），降低pH值，并溶解碳酸钙（calcium carbonate）骨骼；将珊瑚礁的消失与约25%海洋物种栖息地的崩溃联系起来；评估目前的珊瑚礁修复工作。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}听说过珊瑚白化吗？他们能解释珊瑚究竟发生了什么吗——珊瑚和生活在它体内的微小藻类之间的共生关系是如何破裂的，以及为什么海水变暖或变酸会引发这种现象？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Predator Loss and Ecosystem Effects
topics.description: Quantify energy transfer efficiency through trophic levels (~10% rule); explain trophic cascades: how removing an apex predator triggers a chain of ecosystem changes (sea otters → sea urchin explosion → kelp forest collapse); define 'fishing down the food web'; evaluate evidence for ocean rewilding — shark reintroduction, whale recovery driving nutrient cycling; understand why ecosystem-based fisheries management is needed
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} trace the chain of events that happened to Pacific kelp forests when sea otters were hunted almost to extinction — what domino effect did removing one species set off through the whole ecosystem?
topics.nameZh: 捕食者减少与生态系统效应
topics.descriptionZh: 量化能量在营养级（trophic levels）之间的传递效率（10%法则）；解释营养级联（trophic cascades）现象：移除顶级捕食者（apex predator）如何引发一连串的生态系统变化（海獭减少 → 海胆数量暴增 → 海带森林崩溃）；解释“向食物链底层捕捞”（fishing down the food web）的概念；评估海洋再野化（ocean rewilding）的证据——例如重新引入鲨鱼、鲸鱼种群恢复从而促进营养物质循环；理解为什么需要采用基于生态系统的渔业管理（ecosystem-based fisheries management）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否梳理出当海獭被猎杀至濒临灭绝时，太平洋海带森林所经历的一系列事件——移除单一物种在整个生态系统中引发了怎样的多米诺骨牌效应（domino effect）？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Deep-Ocean Exploration Technology
topics.description: Explain how crewed submersibles (Alvin, Deepsea Challenger) and remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) allow exploration of the deep; describe acoustic seafloor mapping using sonar and why only ~25% of the ocean floor has been mapped at high resolution; explore why the deep ocean is harder to explore than the surface of the Moon (pressure, cold, darkness, communication difficulties); survey astrobiology missions targeting ocean worlds in our solar system
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why more of the Moon's surface has been mapped in detail than Earth's ocean floor — what makes deep ocean exploration so much harder than looking at the Moon?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释载人潜水器（如“阿尔文”号、“深海挑战者”号）和遥控潜水器（ROV）是如何实现深海探测的；描述利用声呐（sonar）进行海底声学测绘的过程，以及为什么目前只有约25%的海底被进行了高分辨率测绘；探讨为什么深海探测比探测月球表面更加困难（涉及高压、极寒、黑暗和通信困难等因素）；概述我们太阳系中以“海洋世界”为目标的天体生物学（astrobiology）探测任务。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释为什么月球表面被详细测绘的比例比地球海底还要高——是什么使得深海探测比观测月球困难得多？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Animal Body Groups
topics.description: Describe and compare the external body structure of common animals across groups (fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals)
evidence: Describe key structural features of at least three animal groups (e.g. scales, feathers, fur)
Compare two animals from different groups, noting at least two differences
Use words like 'wings', 'fins', 'legs', 'tail' correctly when describing an animal
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how a fish's body is different from a bird's body and explain features like scales, feathers, or fins?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述并比较不同类群（鱼类、两栖动物、爬行动物、鸟类、哺乳动物）常见动物的外部身体结构。
evidenceZh: 描述至少三个动物类群的关键结构特征（如鳞片、羽毛、毛发）
比较来自不同类群的两种动物，指出至少两处不同点
在描述动物时，能正确使用“翅膀”、“鳍”、“腿”、“尾巴”等词汇
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否描述鱼的身体和鸟的身体有什么不同，并解释鳞片、羽毛或鳍等特征？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Body Parts & Senses
topics.description: Identify, name, and locate basic parts of the human body and associate each body part with its sense
evidence: Label eyes, ears, nose, mouth, and skin on a body outline
Match each sense organ to its sense: sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch
Describe a simple scenario for each sense (e.g. 'I use my nose to smell cookies baking')
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} point to their eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin and tell you which sense each one is used for?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别、命名并指出人体基本部位的位置，并将每个身体部位与其对应的感官联系起来
evidenceZh: 在人体轮廓图上标出眼睛、耳朵、鼻子、嘴巴和皮肤
将每个感觉器官与其对应的感官匹配：视觉、听觉、嗅觉、味觉、触觉
为每种感官描述一个简单的场景（例如：‘我用鼻子闻烤饼干的香味’）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否指出自己的眼睛、耳朵、鼻子、舌头和皮肤，并告诉你它们分别用于哪种感官？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Common Plants & Trees
topics.description: Identify and name common wild and garden plants, including deciduous and evergreen trees
evidence: Name at least five common wild or garden plants from direct observation
Sort trees into deciduous (loses leaves) and evergreen (keeps leaves) with examples
Match a plant to its name when shown a picture or real specimen
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you point to a tree in the park, can {{name}} tell you what kind it is and whether it keeps its leaves in winter?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别并说出常见野生植物和庭院植物的名称，包括落叶树 (deciduous) 和常绿树 (evergreen)。
evidenceZh: 通过直接观察，至少说出五种常见的野生或庭院植物名称
将树木分为落叶树 (deciduous，会落叶) 和常绿树 (evergreen，不落叶)，并能举例说明
看到图片或真实植物标本时，能准确说出该植物的名称
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你指着公园里的一棵树，{{name}}能告诉你它是什么树，以及它冬天是否落叶吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Herbivores, Carnivores & Omnivores
topics.description: Classify common animals as carnivores (eat meat), herbivores (eat plants), or omnivores (eat both)
evidence: Define carnivore, herbivore, and omnivore in own words
Sort at least six common animals into the three diet groups
Give a reason for each sorting decision based on what the animal eats
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a cat is a carnivore, a rabbit is a herbivore, and a bear is an omnivore?
topics.nameZh: 草食动物、肉食动物与杂食动物
topics.descriptionZh: 将常见动物分类为肉食动物（吃肉）、草食动物（吃植物）或杂食动物（两者都吃）
evidenceZh: 用自己的话定义肉食动物、草食动物和杂食动物
将至少六种常见动物分配到这三个饮食类别中
根据动物的饮食内容为每个分类决定提供理由
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释为什么猫是肉食动物，兔子是草食动物，而熊是杂食动物吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Living Things Vocabulary
topics.description: Name and use vocabulary for what makes something living — alive, dead, never been alive, movement, nutrition, growth, reproduction, sensitivity, excretion — and apply these terms when classifying objects and explaining why plants and animals count as living things
evidence: Correctly classify objects as living, dead, or never been alive and give a reason using one of the life process terms
Name at least five life processes using the correct vocabulary
Explain why a plant is alive using at least two life process words
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a rock is not alive but a weed is — using a science word like 'nutrition' or 'growth' rather than just saying 'it moves'?
topics.descriptionZh: 命名并使用描述生命特征的词汇——有生命的（alive）、已死亡的（dead）、从未有生命的（never been alive）、运动（movement）、营养（nutrition）、生长（growth）、繁殖（reproduction）、应激性（sensitivity）、排泄（excretion）——并在对物体进行分类以及解释为什么动植物属于生物时应用这些术语。
evidenceZh: 能够正确将物体分类为有生命的、已死亡的或从未有生命的，并使用其中一个生命过程术语说明理由
能够使用正确的词汇说出至少五个生命过程
能够使用至少两个生命过程词汇来解释为什么植物是有生命的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么石头没有生命而杂草有生命——并使用如“营养（nutrition）”或“生长（growth）”这样的科学词汇，而不仅仅是说“它会动”？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Naming Common Animals
topics.description: Identify and name common animals from major groups: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals
evidence: Name at least two animals from each group: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals
Sort a set of animal pictures into the five groups
Explain one feature of each group (e.g. 'birds have feathers', 'fish have gills')
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} sees a frog, a robin, or a goldfish, can they tell you which animal group each belongs to?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别并命名主要类群（鱼类、两栖动物、爬行动物、鸟类和哺乳动物）中的常见动物
evidenceZh: 说出每个类群（鱼类、两栖动物、爬行动物、鸟类、哺乳动物）中至少两种动物的名称
将一组动物图片分类到这五个类群中
解释每个类群的一个特征（例如：‘鸟类有羽毛’，‘鱼类有鳃’）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}看到青蛙、知更鸟或金鱼时，他们能告诉你每种动物分别属于哪个动物类群吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Parts of a Plant
topics.description: Identify and describe the basic structure of common flowering plants (roots, stem, leaves, flowers) and trees (roots, trunk, branches, leaves)
evidence: Label roots, stem, leaves, and flowers on a diagram of a flowering plant
Name the main parts of a tree: roots, trunk, branches, leaves
Explain that roots take in water and leaves catch sunlight
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you pick a flower from the garden, can {{name}} point to the roots, stem, leaves, and petals and say what each part does?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别并描述常见开花植物（根、茎、叶、花）和树木（根、树干、树枝、叶）的基本结构。
evidenceZh: 在开花植物的示意图上标注根、茎、叶和花
说出树木的主要部分：根、树干、树枝和叶
解释根负责吸收水分，叶负责捕捉阳光
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你从花园里摘一朵花，{{name}}能指出根、茎、叶和花瓣的位置，并说出每个部分的作用吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: What Living Things Need
topics.description: Understand what plants and animals (including humans) need to survive: water, food, air, and suitable conditions
evidence: List the basic needs of animals: water, food, air, shelter
List the basic needs of plants: water, light, air, suitable temperature
Explain what happens if one basic need is missing (e.g. 'the plant wilts without water')
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} what a pet dog or a garden plant needs to stay alive, can they list the basic things like water, food, and air?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解植物和动物（包括人类）生存所需的条件：水、食物、空气和适宜的环境。
evidenceZh: 列出动物的基本需求：水、食物、空气和庇护所（shelter）
列出植物的基本需求：水、光照、空气和适宜的温度
解释如果缺少某一项基本需求会发生什么（例如：“植物没有水会枯萎”）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你问{{name}}宠物狗或花园里的植物需要什么才能存活，他们能列出水、食物和空气等基本需求吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Animal Life Stages
topics.description: Recognise that animals, including humans, have offspring which grow into adults, and describe basic animal life stages
evidence: Describe the basic life stages of a human: baby, child, teenager, adult
Give examples of other animals and their young (e.g. kitten → cat, chick → hen)
Explain that offspring grow and change as they develop into adults
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how a kitten grows into a cat, or how a baby grows into an adult?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识到动物（包括人类）会繁衍后代（offspring），并且后代会长成成年个体，同时能描述基本的动物生命阶段（life stages）。
evidenceZh: 描述人类的基本生命阶段：婴儿（baby）、儿童（child）、青少年（teenager）、成年人（adult）
列举其他动物及其幼崽（young）的例子（例如：小猫（kitten）→ 猫（cat），小鸡（chick）→ 母鸡（hen））
解释后代（offspring）在发育成成年个体的过程中会生长和发生变化
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否描述小猫是如何长成猫的，或者婴儿是如何长成成年人的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Offspring resemble parents
topics.description: Observe that young plants and animals resemble their parents but are not identical, recognising inherited similarities and individual differences
evidence: Describe at least three features that offspring inherit from parents (e.g. eye colour, petal colour, fur type)
Explain that offspring are similar to parents but not identical copies
Give examples from both plants and animals showing resemblance with variation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} look at a family photo and point out features children share with their parents, while also noticing how each child looks a bit different?
topics.descriptionZh: 观察幼小的植物和动物与它们的父母相似但并不完全相同，认识到遗传的相似性和个体差异
evidenceZh: 描述至少三个后代从父母那里遗传的特征（例如：眼睛颜色、花瓣颜色、毛发类型）
解释后代与父母相似，但并非完全相同的复制品
列举植物和动物的例子，展示相似性中的变异
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否看着一张全家福照片，指出孩子们与父母共有的特征，同时也能注意到每个孩子看起来有些不同？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Seeds & Plant Growth
topics.description: Observe and describe how seeds and bulbs grow into mature plants through stages of germination and growth
evidence: Describe the stages: seed absorbs water → root appears → shoot pushes up → leaves open
Compare how a bulb and a seed start growing differently
Record observations of a growing plant over several days using drawings or a simple diary
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} planted a seed or bulb and been able to describe what happened as it grew — first a root, then a shoot, then leaves?
topics.descriptionZh: 观察并描述种子和鳞茎如何通过发芽和生长阶段长成成熟的植物
evidenceZh: 描述生长阶段：种子吸水 → 根出现 → 嫩芽向上长出 → 叶片展开
比较鳞茎和种子开始生长的不同方式
使用绘画或简单的日记记录植物在数日内的生长观察
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否种植过种子或鳞茎，并能够描述其生长过程——先长出根，然后长出嫩芽，最后长出叶子？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: What Plants Need to Grow
topics.description: Understand that plants need water, light, and a suitable temperature to grow and stay healthy
evidence: Name three things plants need to grow: water, light, suitable temperature
Predict what happens to a plant kept in the dark, with no water, or in freezing cold
Describe the results of a simple test comparing plants grown in different conditions
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a plant on the windowsill grows better than one left in a dark cupboard?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解植物需要水、光和适宜的温度才能生长并保持健康
evidenceZh: 说出植物生长需要的三种要素：水、光和适宜的温度
预测植物如果被放在黑暗中、没有水或者处于严寒中会发生什么
描述一项简单测试的结果，该测试比较了植物在不同条件下的生长情况
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释为什么窗台上的植物比放在黑暗橱柜里的植物长得更好吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Animal Classification Vocabulary
topics.description: Use vocabulary for classifying animals and describing life cycles — vertebrate, invertebrate, mammal, bird, reptile, amphibian, fish, insect, arachnid, larva, pupa, metamorphosis, gestation, offspring, complete metamorphosis, incomplete metamorphosis — and apply these correctly when sorting and comparing organisms
evidence: Correctly classify a set of animals as vertebrates or invertebrates, then into more specific groups
Use 'metamorphosis' correctly to describe insect and amphibian life cycles and distinguish complete from incomplete metamorphosis
Compare a mammal's life cycle with an insect's using precise vocabulary
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know the difference between a vertebrate and an invertebrate — and could they sort a list of animals into the right group?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用分类动物和描述生命周期的词汇——脊椎动物 (vertebrate)、无脊椎动物 (invertebrate)、哺乳动物 (mammal)、鸟类 (bird)、爬行动物 (reptile)、两栖动物 (amphibian)、鱼类 (fish)、昆虫 (insect)、蛛形纲动物 (arachnid)、幼虫 (larva)、蛹 (pupa)、变态发育 (metamorphosis)、妊娠期 (gestation)、后代 (offspring)、完全变态发育 (complete metamorphosis)、不完全变态发育 (incomplete metamorphosis)——并在对生物进行分类和比较时正确运用这些词汇。
evidenceZh: 正确地将一组动物分类为脊椎动物或无脊椎动物，然后再分入更具体的类别
正确使用“变态发育 (metamorphosis)”来描述昆虫和两栖动物的生命周期，并区分完全变态发育与不完全变态发育
使用精确的词汇比较哺乳动物与昆虫的生命周期
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否了解脊椎动物和无脊椎动物之间的区别——他们能否将一份动物列表正确分类到相应的组别中？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Animal Nutrition
topics.description: Understand that animals, including humans, need the right types and amounts of nutrition, and that animals cannot make their own food
evidence: Name the main food groups: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre, water
Explain that animals get energy from food they eat, unlike plants which make their own
Describe what happens with too much or too little of a food group (e.g. weak bones without calcium)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why people need to eat different types of food like fruit, protein, and carbohydrates to stay healthy?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解动物（包括人类）需要正确类型和数量的营养，并且动物不能自己制造食物。
evidenceZh: 说出主要食物类别：碳水化合物（carbohydrates）、蛋白质（proteins）、脂肪（fats）、维生素（vitamins）、矿物质（minerals）、膳食纤维（fibre）、水（water）
解释动物从它们吃的食物中获取能量，这与能自己制造食物的植物不同
描述摄入过多或过少某类食物会发生什么（例如，缺钙会导致骨骼脆弱）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释为什么人们需要吃水果、蛋白质和碳水化合物等不同种类的食物来保持健康？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Drawing Life Cycle Diagrams
topics.description: Draw and interpret life cycle diagrams for flowering plants, insects (complete and incomplete metamorphosis), birds, and mammals — labelling stages, describing transitions, and comparing cycles across species
evidence: Draw a labelled life cycle diagram for a flowering plant including seed, seedling, mature plant, and flower/fruit
Compare a butterfly life cycle (complete metamorphosis) with a grasshopper life cycle (incomplete metamorphosis) using diagrams
Label a blank life cycle diagram for a given organism correctly, including transitions between stages
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is given a blank circular diagram, can they fill in the stages of a butterfly's life cycle in the right order with labels — and explain what changes at each stage?
topics.nameZh: 绘制生命周期图 (Drawing Life Cycle Diagrams)
topics.descriptionZh: 绘制并解读开花植物、昆虫（完全变态 complete metamorphosis 与 不完全变态 incomplete metamorphosis）、鸟类和哺乳动物的生命周期图——标注各个发育阶段、描述阶段间的过渡变化，并比较不同物种的生命周期。
evidenceZh: 绘制一幅带有标注的开花植物生命周期图，包括种子（seed）、幼苗（seedling）、成熟植株（mature plant）以及花与果实（flower/fruit）。
利用图表比较蝴蝶的生命周期（完全变态 complete metamorphosis）与蝗虫的生命周期（不完全变态 incomplete metamorphosis）。
正确标注给定生物的空白生命周期图（Life Cycle Diagram），包括各阶段之间的过渡（transitions）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果给 {{name}} 一个空白的环形图（circular diagram），他们能否按正确顺序填入蝴蝶生命周期的各个阶段并加上标注——同时解释每个阶段发生了哪些变化？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How Plant Parts Work
topics.description: Identify and describe the functions of different parts of flowering plants: roots absorb water and nutrients, stems transport materials, leaves make food, flowers enable reproduction
evidence: Describe the function of roots (absorb water and minerals from soil)
Explain that the stem transports water up and food around the plant
State that leaves use sunlight to make food and flowers produce seeds for new plants
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a flower needs roots underground and leaves up top — what job does each part do?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别并描述开花植物不同部分的功能：根吸收水分和养分，茎运输物质，叶制造食物，花实现繁殖
evidenceZh: 描述根的功能（从土壤中吸收水分和矿物质）
解释茎将水向上运输并将食物输送到植物全身
说明叶利用阳光制造食物，花产生种子以繁衍新植物
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释为什么开花植物需要地下的根和顶部的叶——每个部分分别承担什么功能？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Life Cycles of Organisms
topics.description: Develop models to describe that organisms have unique and diverse life cycles but all share the common stages of birth, growth, reproduction, and death
evidence: Describe the life cycle of at least two different organisms (e.g. butterfly, frog, plant)
Identify the common stages all life cycles share: birth, growth, reproduction, death
Explain how life cycles can look very different (metamorphosis vs gradual growth) but follow the same pattern
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} compare the life cycle of a butterfly with that of a frog and explain what stages they all share — being born, growing, having babies, and dying?
topics.descriptionZh: 构建模型以描述生物具有独特且多样的生命周期，但所有生物都共享出生、生长、繁殖（reproduction）和死亡这些共同阶段。
evidenceZh: 描述至少两种不同生物（如蝴蝶、青蛙、植物）的生命周期
识别所有生命周期共有的阶段：出生、生长、繁殖、死亡
解释生命周期（如变态发育（metamorphosis）与逐渐生长）外观上可能差异巨大，但遵循相同的规律
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否比较蝴蝶和青蛙的生命周期，并解释它们都经历了哪些共同阶段——出生、生长、繁育后代和死亡？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Pollination & Seed Dispersal
topics.description: Understand the life cycle of flowering plants including pollination, seed formation, and seed dispersal
evidence: Describe the stages: pollination → fertilisation → seed formation → seed dispersal
Explain at least two methods of seed dispersal (wind, animal, water, explosion)
Describe pollination as the transfer of pollen from one flower to another, often by insects or wind
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a flower turns into a fruit with seeds inside, and how those seeds get spread to grow new plants?
topics.nameZh: 传粉与种子传播 (Pollination & Seed Dispersal)
topics.descriptionZh: 了解开花植物的生命周期，包括传粉 (Pollination)、种子形成 (Seed formation) 和种子传播 (Seed dispersal) 的过程。
evidenceZh: 描述植物繁殖的各个阶段：传粉 (Pollination) → 受精 (Fertilisation) → 种子形成 (Seed formation) → 种子传播 (Seed dispersal)
解释至少两种种子传播 (Seed dispersal) 的方法（风力、动物、水流、弹射）
描述传粉 (Pollination) 是花粉从一朵花转移到另一朵花的过程，通常由昆虫或风作为媒介
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释一朵花是如何变成内部带有种子的果实的，以及这些种子是如何散播出去长成新植物的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Skeletons & Muscles
topics.description: Identify that humans and some other animals have skeletons and muscles for support, protection, and movement
evidence: Name the three functions of the skeleton: support, protection, movement
Identify that muscles are attached to bones and pull to create movement
Give examples of bones protecting organs (skull protects brain, ribs protect heart and lungs)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why we have a skeleton inside our body and what our muscles do when we bend an arm?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识人类和某些其他动物拥有骨骼（Skeletons）和肌肉（Muscles），用于支撑身体、保护内脏和产生运动。
evidenceZh: 说出骨骼的三个功能：支撑（Support）、保护（Protection）和运动（Movement）
认识肌肉附着在骨骼（Bones）上，通过牵拉产生运动
举例说明骨骼如何保护器官（例如：颅骨保护大脑，肋骨保护心脏和肺部）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释为什么我们体内有骨骼（Skeleton），以及弯曲手臂时肌肉（Muscles）是如何工作的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Water Transport in Plants
topics.description: Investigate how water is transported within plants, using observations such as coloured water being drawn up through a stem
evidence: Describe an investigation using coloured water to track water movement in a plant
Explain that water travels from roots through the stem to the leaves and flowers
Draw or label a diagram showing the path of water through a plant
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} seen a white flower turn a different colour in coloured water and been able to explain that the stem carries water up to the petals?
topics.descriptionZh: 探究水分在植物体内的运输过程，通过观察有色水被吸入茎中等现象进行实验。
evidenceZh: 描述一项使用有色水追踪植物体内水分移动的实验
解释水分从根部经过茎运输到叶片和花朵的过程
绘制或标注展示水分在植物体内运输路径的示意图
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否观察过白花在有色的水中变成其他颜色，并且能够解释是茎将水分向上输送到了花瓣？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: What Plants Need to Thrive
topics.description: Explore and compare the requirements of plants for life and growth: air, light, water, nutrients from soil, and room to grow
evidence: List five requirements for plant growth: air, light, water, nutrients, space
Explain how needs vary between plants (e.g. cacti need less water than ferns)
Predict what happens when one requirement is removed or limited
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you why a crowded pot of seedlings doesn't grow as well as one with just a few plants?
topics.nameZh: 植物茁壮成长所需的条件
topics.descriptionZh: 探索并比较植物生存和生长所需的条件：空气、光照、水分、土壤中的养分以及生长空间
evidenceZh: 列出植物生长的五个必需条件：空气、光照、水分、养分和空间
解释不同植物需求之间的差异（例如，仙人掌比蕨类植物需要的水分少）
预测当其中一个必需条件被移除或受限时会发生什么
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能告诉你为什么种满幼苗的拥挤花盆里，植物长得不如只种了几株的花盆好吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How animals adapt to environments
topics.description: Identify how animals and plants are adapted to suit their environment and understand that adaptation may lead to evolution over time
evidence: Define adaptation as a feature that helps an organism survive in its environment
Give at least three examples of adaptations in different organisms and explain how each helps survival
Explain that over many generations, organisms with helpful adaptations survive and reproduce more, leading to evolution
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a camel's humps, a cactus's thick skin, or a polar bear's white fur help them survive where they live, and how these adaptations developed over time?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别动植物如何适应其生存环境，并理解适应（Adaptation）可能随着时间的推移导致进化（Evolution）。
evidenceZh: 将适应（Adaptation）定义为帮助生物在其环境中生存的特征
给出不同生物至少三个适应环境的例子，并解释每种适应如何帮助它们生存
解释在许多世代中，具有有益适应特征的生物能更好地生存和繁衍，从而导致进化（Evolution）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释骆驼的驼峰、仙人掌的厚皮或北极熊的白毛是如何帮助它们在各自的生活环境中生存的，以及这些适应特征是如何随着时间的推移而发展出来的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Inheritance Vocabulary
topics.description: Use vocabulary for variation and inheritance — inherited characteristic, acquired characteristic, variation, offspring, trait, species, breed, genetic, environment — and apply these when comparing organisms and explaining similarities and differences within and between species
evidence: Distinguish between inherited and acquired characteristics with a correct example of each
Use 'variation' correctly to describe differences within a species and explain what causes variation
Use 'offspring', 'species', and 'trait' correctly in written descriptions of living things
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why children look similar to but not exactly like their parents — using words like 'inherited' or 'variation'?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用关于变异和遗传的词汇——遗传特征 (inherited characteristic)、后天获得特征 (acquired characteristic)、变异 (variation)、后代 (offspring)、性状 (trait)、物种 (species)、品种 (breed)、遗传的 (genetic)、环境 (environment)——并在比较生物体以及解释物种内部和物种之间的相似性与差异时应用这些词汇。
evidenceZh: 能够区分遗传特征和后天获得特征，并为每种特征提供正确的示例。
能够正确使用“变异 (variation)”一词来描述同一物种内部的差异，并解释引起变异的原因。
能够在书面描述生物时，正确使用“后代 (offspring)”、“物种 (species)”和“性状 (trait)”。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么孩子看起来与父母相似但并不完全一样——并使用诸如“遗传的 (inherited)”或“变异 (variation)”等词汇？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Inherited characteristics
topics.description: Analyse and interpret data to provide evidence that plants and animals have traits inherited from parents and that variation of these traits exists in a group of similar organisms
evidence: Define inherited traits as characteristics passed from parents to offspring
Collect or interpret data showing variation within a group (e.g. different heights, colours, sizes)
Explain that while traits are inherited, there is natural variation among individuals of the same species
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} measures the height of all the sunflowers in the garden, can they see that they're all sunflowers but each one is a slightly different height?
topics.descriptionZh: 分析和解读数据，提供证据证明动植物具有从父母（亲代）遗传的特征，并且在同类生物群体中这些特征存在变异 (variation)。
evidenceZh: 将遗传特征 (inherited traits) 定义为从父母传递给后代（子代）的特征
收集或解读显示群体内变异 (variation) 的数据（例如不同的身高、颜色、大小）
解释虽然特征是遗传的，但同一物种的个体之间存在自然变异 (natural variation)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 测量花园里所有向日葵的高度，他们能不能看出它们虽然都是向日葵，但每一株的高度都略有不同？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Digestive System
topics.description: Describe the simple functions of the basic parts of the human digestive system: mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine
evidence: Name the main organs in order: mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine
Describe the function of each (mouth chews, stomach breaks down, small intestine absorbs nutrients)
Draw or label a simple diagram of the digestive system
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} trace the journey of a sandwich through the body — from chewing in the mouth all the way to the intestines?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述人体消化系统基本部位的简单功能：口腔（mouth）、食道（oesophagus）、胃（stomach）、小肠（small intestine）、大肠（large intestine）。
evidenceZh: 按顺序说出主要器官的名称：口腔（mouth）、食道（oesophagus）、胃（stomach）、小肠（small intestine）、大肠（large intestine）。
描述每个器官的功能（口腔咀嚼食物、胃分解食物、小肠吸收营养）。
绘制或标注消化系统的简单示意图。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否追踪一个三明治在体内的旅程——从在口腔咀嚼一直到进入肠道？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Traits: inherited and environmental
topics.description: Use evidence to support the explanation that traits can be influenced by the environment as well as inheritance
evidence: Explain that traits result from both inheritance and environmental factors
Give examples of environmental influence on traits (e.g. sunlight affects plant growth, diet affects animal size)
Distinguish between inherited traits (e.g. eye colour) and environmentally influenced traits (e.g. muscle strength from exercise)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why two identical seeds might grow into different-sized plants if one gets more sunlight than the other?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用证据支持以下解释：性状既可以受遗传影响，也可以受环境影响
evidenceZh: 解释性状是由遗传和环境因素共同作用的结果
举例说明环境对性状的影响（例如，阳光影响植物生长，饮食影响动物体型）
区分遗传性状（例如眼睛颜色）和受环境影响的性状（例如通过锻炼增强的肌肉力量）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释为什么如果一颗种子比另一颗种子获得更多的阳光，两颗相同的种子可能会长成不同大小的植物？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Types of Teeth
topics.description: Identify the different types of human teeth (incisors, canines, molars) and describe their functions in eating
evidence: Name three types of teeth: incisors, canines, molars
Describe the function of each: incisors cut, canines tear, molars grind
Relate tooth type to diet (e.g. herbivores have flat molars, carnivores have sharp canines)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} point to different teeth in their mouth and explain that front teeth cut food while back teeth grind it?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别人类牙齿的不同种类（切牙、犬齿、臼齿），并描述它们在进食过程中的功能。
evidenceZh: 说出三种牙齿的名称：切牙（门齿）、犬齿（尖牙）、臼齿（磨牙）
描述每种牙齿的功能：切牙切割食物，犬齿撕裂食物，臼齿研磨食物
将牙齿类型与饮食联系起来（例如：食草动物有平坦的臼齿，食肉动物有锋利的犬齿）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否指出嘴里不同种类的牙齿，并解释前面的牙齿用来切断食物，而后面的牙齿用来研磨食物？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Variation & Survival Advantage
topics.description: Use evidence to explain how variations in characteristics among individuals of the same species may provide advantages in surviving, finding mates, and reproducing
evidence: Explain that variation within a species means some individuals have traits better suited to their environment
Give examples of advantageous variations (e.g. camouflage, speed, drought resistance in plants)
Connect variation to survival advantage: individuals with beneficial traits are more likely to survive and reproduce
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a faster rabbit in a group might survive longer because it can escape predators better than slower ones?
topics.descriptionZh: 运用证据解释同种生物个体之间的特征变异（variation）如何为生存、寻找配偶和繁衍后代提供优势。
evidenceZh: 解释物种内的变异意味着某些个体拥有更适应其环境的特征（traits）。
举例说明有利的变异（例如：保护色（camouflage）、奔跑速度、植物的耐旱性（drought resistance））。
将变异与生存优势联系起来：具有有利特征的个体更有可能生存下来并繁衍后代（reproduce）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释为什么一群兔子中跑得更快的那只可能存活得更久，因为它能比跑得慢的兔子更好地逃避捕食者（predators）？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Human Life Stages
topics.description: Describe the changes as humans develop to old age, including the stages of the human life cycle
evidence: Name the main stages of human development: baby, toddler, child, teenager, adult, elderly
Describe key changes at puberty (growth spurt, body changes)
Explain that old age brings changes like reduced strength, greying hair, and slower healing
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the main stages of a human life — from baby to toddler to child to teenager to adult to old age — and some changes at each stage?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述人类发育至老年的变化过程，包括人类生命周期的各个阶段。
evidenceZh: 说出人类发展的主要阶段：婴儿、幼儿、儿童、青少年、成人、老年
描述青春期的关键变化（身高突增、身体变化）
解释老年带来的变化，如体力下降、头发变白和伤口愈合变慢
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否描述人类生命的主要阶段——从婴儿到幼儿、儿童、青少年、成人再到老年——以及每个阶段的一些变化？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Organ Systems Vocabulary
topics.description: Use technical vocabulary for the major organ systems — organ, organ system, circulatory system, digestive system, respiratory system, skeletal system, muscular system, nutrient, oxygen, carbon dioxide, blood vessel, artery, vein, capillary, enzyme — and describe the function of each system using these terms
evidence: Name the main organs in at least two body systems and state their functions using the correct vocabulary
Use 'circulatory', 'digestive', and 'respiratory' correctly in written descriptions of the body
Explain the difference between an artery and a vein using the correct anatomical terms
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the circulatory system does — not just 'the heart pumps blood', but using words like 'oxygen', 'artery', and 'blood vessel'?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用主要器官系统的专业词汇——器官 (organ)、器官系统 (organ system)、循环系统 (circulatory system)、消化系统 (digestive system)、呼吸系统 (respiratory system)、骨骼系统 (skeletal system)、肌肉系统 (muscular system)、营养物质 (nutrient)、氧气 (oxygen)、二氧化碳 (carbon dioxide)、血管 (blood vessel)、动脉 (artery)、静脉 (vein)、毛细血管 (capillary)、酶 (enzyme)——并使用这些词汇描述各个系统的功能。
evidenceZh: 说出至少两个身体系统中的主要器官，并使用正确的专业词汇说明其功能
在书面描述人体时，正确使用“循环 (circulatory)”、“消化 (digestive)”和“呼吸 (respiratory)”等词汇
使用正确的解剖学术语解释动脉 (artery) 和静脉 (vein) 之间的区别
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释循环系统 (circulatory system) 的作用——不仅仅是说“心脏泵血”，而是能使用“氧气 (oxygen)”、“动脉 (artery)”和“血管 (blood vessel)”等词汇？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Senses, Brain & Responses
topics.description: Use a model to describe that animals receive information through their senses, process it in their brain, and respond in different ways
evidence: Describe the pathway: sense organ detects stimulus → brain processes information → body responds
Give examples of different animal senses (sight, smell, hearing, echolocation, vibration)
Explain how the same stimulus can produce different responses in different animals
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a dog uses its senses to detect a squirrel and then decides to chase it?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用模型来描述动物如何通过感官接收信息，在大脑中进行处理，并做出不同的反应。
evidenceZh: 描述路径：感觉器官检测刺激（stimulus） → 大脑处理信息 → 身体做出反应
举例说明动物不同的感官（视觉、嗅觉、听觉、回声定位（echolocation）、振动感知（vibration））
解释同一种刺激如何在不同动物身上引发不同的反应
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释小狗是如何利用感官发现松鼠，然后决定去追逐它的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Structures for Survival
topics.description: Construct an argument that plants and animals have internal and external structures that function to support survival, growth, behaviour, and reproduction
evidence: Give examples of external structures and their survival functions (e.g. thorns for protection, claws for catching prey)
Give examples of internal structures and their functions (e.g. heart pumps blood, lungs take in air)
Construct a reasoned argument linking a specific structure to how it helps the organism survive or reproduce
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a cactus's thick stem helps it survive in a desert, or how a bird's wings help it find food?
topics.descriptionZh: 构建论点，说明动植物具有支持生存、生长、行为和繁殖的内部结构（internal structures）和外部结构（external structures）。
evidenceZh: 举例说明外部结构（external structures）及其生存功能（例如：刺用于保护，爪子用于捕捉猎物）
举例说明内部结构（internal structures）及其功能（例如：心脏泵血，肺部吸入空气）
构建有理有据的论点，说明特定结构如何帮助生物体生存或繁殖
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释仙人掌粗壮的茎如何帮助它在沙漠中生存，或者鸟类的翅膀如何帮助它寻找食物？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Diet, Exercise & Lifestyle
topics.description: Recognise the impact of diet, exercise, drugs, and lifestyle on the way human bodies function
evidence: Describe how a balanced diet provides energy and nutrients the body needs
Explain the positive effects of regular exercise on the heart, muscles, and mental health
Describe harmful effects of drugs, alcohol, or tobacco on the body
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why eating well and exercising regularly helps the body stay healthy, and why drugs and smoking are harmful?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识饮食、运动、毒品及生活方式对人体机能的影响
evidenceZh: 描述均衡饮食如何为身体提供所需的能量和营养物质
解释规律运动对心脏、肌肉和心理健康的积极影响
描述毒品、酒精或烟草对身体的危害
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释为什么均衡饮食和规律运动有助于保持身体健康，以及为什么毒品和吸烟是有害的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Energy from Food & the Sun
topics.description: Use models to describe that energy in animals' food was once energy from the sun, transferred through plants or other organisms
evidence: Explain that plants capture energy from sunlight to make food (photosynthesis)
Trace an energy pathway: sun → plant → animal → another animal
Explain that animals use food energy for body repair, growth, movement, and warmth
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} trace the energy in their breakfast cereal all the way back to the sun, explaining each step?
topics.nameZh: 来自食物和太阳的能量
topics.descriptionZh: 使用模型描述动物食物中的能量最初来自太阳，并通过植物或其他生物传递而来。
evidenceZh: 解释植物通过捕获阳光中的能量来制造食物（光合作用）
追踪能量传递路径：太阳 → 植物 → 动物 → 另一种动物
解释动物利用食物能量进行身体修复、生长、运动和保持体温
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否追踪他们早餐麦片中的能量，一直追溯到太阳，并解释每一个步骤？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Evolution vocabulary
topics.description: Use technical vocabulary for evolution and natural selection — adaptation, evolution, natural selection, extinct, extinction, fossil record, species, common ancestor, mutation, variation — and explain the mechanism of natural selection using these terms in the correct sequence
evidence: Use 'adaptation' correctly to describe a feature that helps an organism survive in its environment
Explain natural selection using 'variation', 'selection pressure', and 'reproduction' correctly in sequence
Use 'extinct' and 'extinction' correctly and distinguish them from 'endangered'
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in their own words why giraffes have long necks — using words like 'adaptation' or 'natural selection' rather than just 'so they can reach leaves'?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用进化和自然选择的专业词汇——适应（adaptation）、进化（evolution）、自然选择（natural selection）、已灭绝（extinct）、灭绝（extinction）、化石记录（fossil record）、物种（species）、共同祖先（common ancestor）、突变（mutation）、变异（variation）——并按照正确的逻辑顺序使用这些术语来解释自然选择的机制。
evidenceZh: 正确使用“适应（adaptation）”来描述帮助生物在其环境中生存的特征
按照正确的顺序使用“变异（variation）”、“选择压力（selection pressure）”和“繁殖（reproduction）”来解释自然选择
正确使用“已灭绝（extinct）”和“灭绝（extinction）”，并能将它们与“濒危（endangered）”区分开来
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否用自己的话解释为什么长颈鹿有长脖子——使用“适应（adaptation）”或“自然选择（natural selection）”等词汇，而不仅仅是说“为了能吃到树叶”？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Nutrient Transport in Animals
topics.description: Describe how nutrients and water are transported within animals, including the role of the circulatory system in delivering nutrients from digestion
evidence: Describe how nutrients from digested food pass through the wall of the small intestine into the blood
Explain that blood transports dissolved nutrients and water to all parts of the body
Connect the digestive system and circulatory system as working together to deliver nourishment
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the sandwich they ate at lunch actually gets to their muscles — from the stomach into the blood and then around the body?
topics.nameZh: 动物体内的营养运输 (Nutrient Transport in Animals)
topics.descriptionZh: 描述营养物质和水分如何在动物体内运输，包括循环系统（circulatory system）在输送消化后营养物质中的作用。
evidenceZh: 描述消化食物中的营养物质如何穿过小肠壁（small intestine）进入血液
解释血液如何将溶解的营养物质和水分输送到身体的各个部位
将消化系统（digestive system）和循环系统（circulatory system）联系起来，说明它们如何协同工作来输送养分
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能解释一下他们午餐吃的三明治究竟是如何到达肌肉的吗——从胃部进入血液，然后再输送到全身各处？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Plants Grow from Air & Water
topics.description: Support an argument that plants get the materials they need for growth chiefly from air and water, not from the soil
evidence: Explain that plants take in carbon dioxide from air and water from soil to make food (photosynthesis)
Argue that most of a plant's mass comes from air (CO₂) and water, not soil minerals
Describe a simple investigation showing soil mass barely changes while a plant grows significantly
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} knows plants need water and sunlight, can they also explain that most of a plant's 'building material' actually comes from air and water rather than dirt?
topics.nameZh: 植物从空气和水中生长
topics.descriptionZh: 支持以下论点：植物获取生长所需物质的主要来源是空气和水，而不是土壤
evidenceZh: 解释植物从空气中吸收二氧化碳（carbon dioxide），从土壤中吸收水分来制造食物（光合作用，photosynthesis）
论证植物的大部分质量（mass）来自空气（CO₂）和水，而不是土壤矿物质
描述一个简单的探究实验，展示在植物显著生长的同时，土壤质量几乎不发生变化
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}知道植物需要水和阳光，他们还能解释植物的大部分“建筑材料”实际上来自空气和水，而不是泥土吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Circulatory System
topics.description: Identify and name the main parts of the human circulatory system and describe the functions of the heart, blood vessels, and blood
evidence: Name the main components: heart, arteries, veins, capillaries, blood
Describe the heart as a pump that pushes blood around the body in a continuous loop
Explain that blood carries oxygen and nutrients to cells and removes waste products like carbon dioxide
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the heart does, why we have blood vessels throughout the body, and what blood actually carries?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别并命名人体循环系统的主要部分，并描述心脏、血管和血液的功能。
evidenceZh: 命名主要组成部分：心脏 (heart)、动脉 (arteries)、静脉 (veins)、毛细血管 (capillaries) 和血液 (blood)
将心脏描述为一个泵 (pump)，推动血液在体内进行连续的循环
解释血液将氧气 (oxygen) 和营养物质 (nutrients) 输送到细胞，并清除二氧化碳 (carbon dioxide) 等废物
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释心脏的作用、为什么我们全身都有血管，以及血液实际上输送了什么吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Calculating Dietary Energy
topics.description: Calculate and evaluate energy intake and requirements in a healthy daily diet, interpreting food labels and nutritional data
evidence: Reads and interprets a nutritional information label (kJ and kcal)
Estimates daily energy requirements for a person of a given age/activity level
Compares the energy content of different diets and identifies surpluses or deficits
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was reading food labels at the supermarket with you, could they work out roughly whether a meal gives too much, too little, or about the right amount of energy for a day?
topics.descriptionZh: 计算并评估健康日常饮食中的能量摄入与需求，解读食品标签和营养数据
evidenceZh: 阅读并解读营养信息标签（千焦 kJ 和 千卡 kcal）
估算特定年龄或活动水平人群的每日能量需求
比较不同饮食的能量含量，并识别能量过剩或缺乏
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}和你一起在超市看食品标签，他们能大致算出一顿饭提供的能量是太多、太少，还是刚好满足一天的需求吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Cells to Organ Systems
topics.description: Describe the hierarchical organisation of multicellular organisms: cells → tissues → organs → organ systems → organism
evidence: Places cells, tissues, organs, and organ systems in the correct order of organisation
Gives a specific example of each level (e.g. muscle cell → muscle tissue → heart → circulatory system → human)
Explains why specialised cells are needed in a multicellular organism
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked to explain how the body is built up from the smallest parts to the whole, could they describe the levels from individual cells all the way up to organ systems — with a real example at each level?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述多细胞生物的层次化组织结构：细胞 → 组织 → 器官 → 器官系统 → 生物体
evidenceZh: 将细胞、组织、器官和器官系统按正确的组织顺序排列
给出每个层级的具体例子（例如：肌肉细胞 → 肌肉组织 → 心脏 → 循环系统 → 人）
解释为什么多细胞生物需要特化细胞
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果要求 {{name}} 解释身体是如何从最小的部分构建到整体的，他们能否描述从单个细胞一直到器官系统的各个层级——并在每个层级提供一个具体的实例？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Cells Under the Microscope
topics.description: Understand that all living organisms are made of cells and use a light microscope to observe, interpret, and record cell structure
evidence: States that all living things are made of cells
Prepares or examines a slide of cells (e.g. onion skin, cheek cells) under a microscope
Draws and labels a diagram of cells observed
Identifies nucleus, cytoplasm, and cell membrane in a microscope image
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} prepared a slide of onion skin and looked at it through a school microscope, could they identify what they were seeing and explain that all living things are made of these tiny units?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解所有生物体都是由细胞 (Cells) 构成的，并使用光学显微镜 (Light microscope) 来观察、解读和记录细胞结构
evidenceZh: 能说出所有生物都是由细胞 (Cells) 构成的
能在显微镜下制备或观察细胞装片 (Slide)（例如洋葱表皮、口腔上皮细胞）
能绘制并标注所观察到的细胞结构图
能在显微镜图像中识别细胞核 (Nucleus)、细胞质 (Cytoplasm) 和细胞膜 (Cell membrane)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 制作了洋葱表皮装片 (Slide) 并通过学校的光学显微镜 (Microscope) 进行观察，他们能认出所看到的内容，并解释所有生物都是由这些微小单元（细胞）构成的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Diet Imbalance & Deficiency
topics.description: Explain the health consequences of an imbalanced diet including obesity (excess energy), starvation (severe energy deficit), and deficiency diseases (lack of specific nutrients, e.g. scurvy, rickets)
evidence: Defines obesity, starvation, and deficiency disease and links each to dietary imbalance
Identifies at least two specific deficiency diseases and the missing nutrient causing each
Explains why the impact of poor diet can be long-term
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard about conditions like obesity or vitamin deficiency diseases, could they explain how eating too much, too little, or the wrong mix of foods leads to those health problems?
topics.nameZh: 饮食不平衡与营养缺乏
topics.descriptionZh: 解释饮食不平衡对健康造成的后果，包括肥胖症（能量过剩）、饥饿（严重的能量缺乏）以及营养缺乏症（缺乏特定营养素，例如坏血病、佝偻病）
evidenceZh: 定义肥胖症、饥饿和营养缺乏症，并将每种情况与饮食不平衡联系起来
识别至少两种特定的营养缺乏症以及导致每种疾病的缺失营养素
解释为什么不良饮食的影响可能是长期的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 听说肥胖症或维生素缺乏症等疾病，他们能解释吃得过多、过少或食物搭配不当是如何导致这些健康问题的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Digestion & Enzymes
topics.description: Describe the organs of the human digestive system and how food is physically and chemically digested, including the role of enzymes as biological catalysts
evidence: Traces the journey of food from mouth to large intestine, naming each organ and its role
Explains what enzymes do and names where they are produced (salivary glands, stomach, small intestine)
Distinguishes physical digestion (chewing, churning) from chemical digestion
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} ate a meal with you, could they describe what happens to the food step by step as it travels through the body — naming the organs it passes through and what each one does?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述人体消化系统的各个器官，以及食物如何进行物理消化（physical digestion）和化学消化（chemical digestion），包括酶（enzymes）作为生物催化剂（biological catalysts）的作用。
evidenceZh: 追踪食物从口腔到大肠的旅程，说出每个器官的名称及其作用
解释酶的作用，并说明它们产生的部位（唾液腺、胃、小肠）
区分物理消化（咀嚼、搅拌）和化学消化（chemical digestion）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 和你一起吃饭，他们能否一步步描述食物在体内旅行时发生的变化——说出食物经过的每个器官以及它们各自的作用？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Joints, Tendons & Ligaments
topics.description: Explain biomechanics — the interaction between skeleton and muscles at joints, including the roles of tendons (attach muscle to bone) and ligaments (attach bone to bone)
evidence: Distinguishes between tendons and ligaments and gives the function of each
Describes how a synovial joint works (e.g. the knee or elbow)
Explains how force is transmitted from muscle through tendon to bone to produce movement
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hurt their knee playing sport, could they explain what a ligament and a tendon are, where each is found, and what would happen if one got damaged?
topics.nameZh: 关节、肌腱与韧带 (Joints, Tendons & Ligaments)
topics.descriptionZh: 解释生物力学 (biomechanics) —— 也就是骨骼和肌肉在关节处是如何相互配合的，包括肌腱 (tendons，负责将肌肉连接到骨骼) 和韧带 (ligaments，负责将骨骼连接到骨骼) 各自的作用。
evidenceZh: 能区分肌腱 (tendons) 和韧带 (ligaments)，并说明它们各自的功能
描述滑膜关节 (synovial joint) 是如何工作的（例如膝关节或肘关节）
解释力量是如何从肌肉通过肌腱 (tendon) 传递到骨骼，从而产生运动的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在运动中弄伤了膝盖，他们能解释什么是韧带 (ligament) 和肌腱 (tendon)，它们分别位于哪里，以及如果其中一个受损会发生什么情况吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Muscles Work in Pairs
topics.description: Explain that muscles work in antagonistic pairs — one contracts while the other relaxes — to produce movement, using the bicep and tricep as a key example
evidence: Explains why muscles can only pull, not push
Describes what happens to the bicep and tricep when the arm is bent and straightened
Gives another example of an antagonistic muscle pair
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} bent and straightened their arm, could they explain why two different muscles are needed — one to bend and one to straighten — and which muscle is which?
topics.nameZh: 肌肉成对工作 (Muscles Work in Pairs)
topics.descriptionZh: 解释肌肉以拮抗对（antagonistic pairs）的方式工作——一块收缩（contract）时另一块放松（relax）——从而产生运动，并以肱二头肌（bicep）和肱三头肌（tricep）作为主要例子。
evidenceZh: 解释为什么肌肉只能拉（pull），不能推（push）
描述当手臂弯曲和伸直时，肱二头肌（bicep）和肱三头肌（tricep）会发生什么变化
给出另一个拮抗肌肉对（antagonistic muscle pair）的例子
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 弯曲并伸直手臂，他们能解释为什么需要两块不同的肌肉——一块用于弯曲，一块用于伸直——并指出哪块是哪块吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Nutrients in a Healthy Diet
topics.description: Identify the seven components of a healthy diet — carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, vitamins, minerals, dietary fibre, and water — and explain the role of each in the body
evidence: Names all seven dietary components and a food source for each
Explains what each nutrient does in the body (e.g. proteins for growth and repair)
Identifies which nutrients provide energy and which do not
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was planning a packed lunch, could they explain what each food group does for the body — why we need protein, carbohydrates, fats, vitamins, and minerals?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别健康饮食的七大组成部分——碳水化合物（carbohydrates）、脂质（lipids）、蛋白质（proteins）、维生素（vitamins）、矿物质（minerals）、膳食纤维（dietary fibre）和水，并解释每种成分在人体中的作用。
evidenceZh: 说出所有七种饮食成分，并为每种成分列举一个食物来源
解释每种营养素在人体内的作用（例如：蛋白质用于生长和修复）
指出哪些营养素能提供能量，哪些不能
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 正在准备午餐便当，他们能解释每种食物类别对身体的作用吗——为什么我们需要蛋白质、碳水化合物、脂肪、维生素和矿物质？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Parts of Plant and Animal Cells
topics.description: Describe the functions of the main components of plant and animal cells: cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, vacuole, mitochondria, ribosomes, and chloroplasts
evidence: Names the main organelles in plant and animal cells
Explains the function of each organelle in their own words
Links organelle function to the needs of the whole cell (e.g. mitochondria produce energy for cell activities)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was shown a diagram of a plant cell, could they point to parts like the nucleus, chloroplasts, and cell wall and explain in plain words what each one does?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述动植物细胞主要组成部分的功能：细胞壁（cell wall）、细胞膜（cell membrane）、细胞质（cytoplasm）、细胞核（nucleus）、液泡（vacuole）、线粒体（mitochondria）、核糖体（ribosomes）和叶绿体（chloroplasts）。
evidenceZh: 能说出动植物细胞中的主要细胞器（organelles）
能用自己的话解释每个细胞器的功能
能将细胞器的功能与整个细胞的需求联系起来（例如，线粒体为细胞活动产生能量）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果给 {{name}} 看一张植物细胞的图解，他们能指出细胞核、叶绿体和细胞壁等部分，并用通俗易懂的话解释它们各自的作用吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Photosynthesis
topics.description: Explain photosynthesis as the process by which plants use light energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen, and describe how mineral nutrients are absorbed through roots
evidence: Writes and explains the word equation for photosynthesis
Identifies the raw materials needed and the products made
Explains the role of chlorophyll in capturing light energy
Distinguishes between what plants get from the air (CO₂), soil (water and minerals), and light
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why plants don't need to eat food like animals do, could they explain how plants make their own food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide — and write the equation?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释光合作用 (Photosynthesis) 是植物利用光能将二氧化碳和水转化为葡萄糖 (glucose) 和氧气的过程，并描述矿物质营养是如何通过根部吸收的。
evidenceZh: 写出并解释光合作用的文字表达式 (word equation)
识别所需的原料和生成的产物
解释叶绿素 (chlorophyll) 在捕获光能中的作用
区分植物从空气 (CO₂)、土壤 (水和矿物质) 以及光中获取的物质
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果有人问 {{name}} 为什么植物不需要像动物那样进食，他们能否解释植物是如何利用阳光、水和二氧化碳自己制造食物的——并写出文字表达式？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Plant Cells vs Animal Cells
topics.description: Compare plant and animal cells, identifying shared features and structures unique to plant cells (cell wall, vacuole, chloroplasts)
evidence: Lists features common to plant and animal cells
Identifies structures found only in plant cells and explains why
Draws and annotates labelled diagrams of both cell types showing similarities and differences
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was shown unlabelled diagrams of a plant cell and an animal cell side by side, could they spot which features are shared and which ones only appear in plant cells — and say why?
topics.descriptionZh: 比较植物细胞和动物细胞，找出它们共有的特征，并识别植物细胞独有的结构（如细胞壁 (cell wall)、液泡 (vacuole) 和叶绿体 (chloroplasts)）。
evidenceZh: 列出植物细胞和动物细胞共有的特征
识别仅存在于植物细胞中的结构并解释其原因
绘制并标注两种细胞的示意图，展示它们的相同点与不同点
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果给 {{name}} 并排展示没有标注的植物细胞和动物细胞图片，他们能分辨出哪些特征是两者共有的，哪些是植物细胞独有的吗——并能说出原因吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Single-Celled Organisms
topics.description: Explain how unicellular organisms such as bacteria and Amoeba carry out all the functions of life within a single cell
evidence: Names examples of unicellular organisms
Lists the seven life processes (MRS NERG) and explains how a single cell performs each one
Contrasts how unicellular organisms meet their needs compared to multicellular organisms
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learned that bacteria are made of just one cell, could they explain how that single cell still manages to feed, grow, and reproduce — doing everything a whole body does?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释细菌和变形虫（Amoeba）等单细胞生物如何在一个细胞内完成所有的生命功能。
evidenceZh: 列举单细胞生物的例子
列出七大生命过程（MRS NERG）并解释单细胞如何执行每一项
对比单细胞生物与多细胞生物满足自身需求的方式
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 了解到细菌仅由一个细胞组成，他们能解释这个单细胞是如何完成摄食、生长和繁殖——即完成整个生物体所有功能的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Human Skeleton
topics.description: Describe the structure and four main functions of the human skeleton: support, protection, movement, and production of blood cells in bone marrow
evidence: Lists and explains the four functions of the skeleton with examples
Names key bones and identifies which organs they protect (e.g. ribcage protects heart and lungs)
Explains what bone marrow is and where blood cells are made
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why we have bones, could they explain that bones do more than just hold us up — describing at least three different things the skeleton does for the body?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述人体骨骼的结构及其四个主要功能：支撑（support）、保护（protection）、运动（movement）以及在骨髓（bone marrow）中制造血细胞。
evidenceZh: 列举并结合实例解释骨骼的四种功能
说出主要骨骼的名称，并指出它们保护哪些器官（例如：肋骨保护心脏和肺部）
解释什么是骨髓（bone marrow）以及血细胞是在哪里生成的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果问 {{name}} 为什么我们会有骨头，他们能否解释骨头不仅仅是支撑我们的身体，还能描述骨骼为身体做的至少三件不同的事情？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Using a Microscope
topics.description: Use a light microscope correctly to prepare, focus, and examine biological specimens, including making accurate labelled drawings at an appropriate magnification
evidence: Sets up a light microscope safely and correctly (course focus then fine focus)
Prepares a wet mount slide with a biological specimen (e.g. onion skin)
Calculates the magnification of an image (magnification = image size ÷ actual size)
Draws an accurate labelled diagram of observed cells with a scale
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} had to use a school microscope to study a biological specimen, could they set it up correctly, find what they're looking for, and produce a labelled scientific drawing of what they see?
topics.descriptionZh: 正确使用光学显微镜（light microscope）来制备、对焦和观察生物标本，包括在合适的放大倍数下绘制准确的、带有标注的科学绘图
evidenceZh: 安全且正确地设置光学显微镜（先使用粗准焦螺旋进行粗调，再使用细准焦螺旋进行微调）
使用生物标本（如洋葱表皮）制备临时装片（wet mount slide）
计算图像的放大倍数（放大倍数 = 图像大小 ÷ 实际大小）
绘制观察到的细胞的准确图示，并带有比例尺（scale）和清晰的标注
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 需要使用学校的显微镜来研究生物标本，他们能否正确设置显微镜，找到需要观察的目标，并绘制出带有标注的科学绘图？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Aerobic Respiration
topics.description: Explain aerobic respiration as the process by which organisms release energy from glucose using oxygen, producing carbon dioxide and water; write and interpret the word equation: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water
evidence: Writes and explains the word equation for aerobic respiration
Explains where in the cell aerobic respiration takes place (mitochondria)
Links aerobic respiration to why breathing rate and heart rate increase during exercise
Explains that respiration is not the same as breathing
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} had just finished PE and was breathing hard, could they explain what aerobic respiration is doing inside their muscle cells — and write out the word equation that describes it?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释有氧呼吸是生物体利用氧气分解葡萄糖以释放能量的过程，并产生二氧化碳和水；写出并解释文字方程式：葡萄糖 (glucose) + 氧气 (oxygen) → 二氧化碳 (carbon dioxide) + 水 (water)
evidenceZh: 写出并解释有氧呼吸的文字方程式 (word equation)
解释有氧呼吸在细胞中的发生部位（线粒体 mitochondria）
将有氧呼吸与运动时呼吸加快、心跳加速的原因联系起来
解释呼吸作用 (respiration) 与日常的呼吸 (breathing) 并不相同
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 刚上完体育课并且正在大口喘气，他们能解释有氧呼吸在他们的肌肉细胞里正在发挥什么作用，并写出描述该过程的文字方程式吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Anaerobic Respiration
topics.description: Explain anaerobic respiration in animals as the incomplete breakdown of glucose to lactic acid when oxygen is in short supply, causing muscle fatigue; contrast this with aerobic respiration in terms of energy yield and products
evidence: Writes the word equation for anaerobic respiration in animals
Explains why lactic acid causes muscle pain and fatigue
Compares the energy released by aerobic and anaerobic respiration
Explains oxygen debt and recovery after vigorous exercise
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sprinted as fast as they could and their legs started to burn and ache afterwards, could they explain what's happening inside their muscles — why there isn't enough oxygen, and what the body produces instead?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释动物体内的无氧呼吸（anaerobic respiration）是在氧气供应不足时，葡萄糖（glucose）不完全分解成乳酸（lactic acid）的过程，这会导致肌肉疲劳；并从能量释放和产物的角度，将其与有氧呼吸（aerobic respiration）进行对比。
evidenceZh: 写出动物体内无氧呼吸的文字表达式（word equation）
解释为什么乳酸（lactic acid）会导致肌肉疼痛和疲劳
比较有氧呼吸和无氧呼吸释放的能量
解释剧烈运动后的氧债（oxygen debt）和身体恢复过程
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 拼尽全力冲刺，之后双腿开始感到灼烧和酸痛，他们能解释肌肉内部正在发生什么吗——为什么氧气供应不足，以及身体转而产生了什么物质？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Body Temperature Regulation
topics.description: Explain how the human body detects and responds to environmental changes including temperature, including the role of the skin in temperature regulation (sweating, shivering, vasodilation, vasoconstriction)
evidence: Explains what homeostasis means in the context of body temperature
Describes at least two mechanisms the body uses to cool down and two to warm up
Explains why maintaining a constant core body temperature is important for enzyme activity
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} got too hot on a summer day and started sweating, could they explain what the body is doing to cool itself down — and why it's so important to keep body temperature steady?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释人体如何感知并应对包括温度在内的环境变化，包括皮肤在体温调节（出汗(sweating)、寒颤(shivering)、血管舒张(vasodilation)、血管收缩(vasoconstriction)）中的作用。
evidenceZh: 解释在体温调节的语境下“稳态”(homeostasis)的含义
描述身体用来降温和升温的至少两种机制
解释为什么维持恒定的核心体温对酶活性(enzyme activity)很重要
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在夏日觉得太热并开始出汗，他们能解释身体正在做什么来给自己降温吗——以及为什么保持体温稳定如此重要？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Gas Exchange & Breathing
topics.description: Describe the structure of the human gas exchange system (trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, alveoli) and explain how the mechanism of breathing — using pressure changes from rib and diaphragm movement — moves air in and out of the lungs
evidence: Labels a diagram of the lungs showing trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, and alveoli
Explains that breathing in lowers air pressure in the chest and air rushes in
Describes how the structure of alveoli (large surface area, thin walls, good blood supply) aids gas exchange
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} took a deep breath after running, could they explain what's happening in their lungs — how the air gets in, where the oxygen crosses into the blood, and how carbon dioxide leaves?
topics.nameZh: 气体交换与呼吸 (Gas Exchange and Breathing)
topics.descriptionZh: 描述人体气体交换系统的结构，包括气管 (trachea)、支气管 (bronchi)、细支气管 (bronchioles) 和肺泡 (alveoli)，并解释呼吸机制——即利用肋骨和膈肌 (diaphragm) 运动引起的压力变化——使空气进出肺部。
evidenceZh: 标注显示气管 (trachea)、支气管 (bronchi)、细支气管 (bronchioles) 和肺泡 (alveoli) 的肺部结构图
解释吸气时胸腔内气压降低，空气随之涌入
描述肺泡 (alveoli) 的结构（表面积大、管壁薄、血液供应丰富）如何促进气体交换
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在跑步后深吸了一口气，他们能解释肺部正在发生什么吗——空气是如何进入的，氧气 (oxygen) 在哪里进入血液，以及二氧化碳 (carbon dioxide) 是如何排出的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Gut Bacteria & Digestion
topics.description: Explain the role of gut microbiome bacteria in digestion, including breaking down dietary fibre and contributing to a healthy gut environment
evidence: Explains that many gut bacteria are beneficial, not harmful
Describes what gut bacteria do that human digestive enzymes cannot (e.g. break down fibre)
Explains what might happen if the gut microbiome is disrupted
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that there are billions of bacteria living in our gut, could they explain why that's actually helpful for digestion rather than something to worry about?
topics.nameZh: 肠道细菌与消化 (Gut Bacteria & Digestion)
topics.descriptionZh: 解释肠道微生物群（gut microbiome）在消化中的作用，包括分解膳食纤维（dietary fibre）以及维持健康的肠道环境。
evidenceZh: 解释许多肠道细菌是有益的，而不是有害的。
描述肠道细菌能做而人类消化酶（digestive enzymes）无法做到的事情（例如分解膳食纤维）。
解释如果肠道微生物群（gut microbiome）遭到破坏可能会发生什么。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 听说我们的肠道里生活着数十亿个细菌，他们能解释为什么这对消化实际上非常有益，而不是什么让人担忧的事情吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Heart Structure & Double Circulation
topics.description: Describe the structure of the heart (four chambers, valves, coronary arteries) and explain how it pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs and oxygenated blood to the body in a double circulatory system
evidence: Labels a diagram of the heart showing atria, ventricles, valves, aorta, vena cava, and pulmonary vessels
Traces the route of blood through the double circulatory system
Explains the role of valves in preventing backflow
Compares arteries, veins, and capillaries
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} felt their heartbeat, could they describe what the heart is doing — explaining the two sides of the heart, where the blood goes from each side, and why we need a double loop?
topics.nameZh: 心脏结构与双循环系统
topics.descriptionZh: 描述心脏的结构（四个腔室、瓣膜、冠状动脉），并解释在双循环系统（double circulatory system）中，心脏如何将缺氧血泵入肺部，将富氧血泵送到全身。
evidenceZh: 在心脏结构图上标注心房（atria）、心室（ventricles）、瓣膜（valves）、主动脉（aorta）、腔静脉（vena cava）和肺血管（pulmonary vessels）
描绘血液在双循环系统（double circulatory system）中的流动路径
解释瓣膜（valves）在防止血液倒流（backflow）中的作用
比较动脉（arteries）、静脉（veins）和毛细血管（capillaries）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 感受到了自己的心跳，他们能描述心脏正在做什么吗——解释心脏的两侧分别做什么，血液从每一侧流向哪里，以及为什么我们需要一个双循环（double loop）系统？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How Diffusion Works
topics.description: Explain diffusion as the net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to lower concentration, and describe its role in moving materials (oxygen, carbon dioxide, glucose) in and between cells
evidence: Defines diffusion using particle theory
Explains the direction of diffusion of oxygen and carbon dioxide at the alveoli
Explains how cells get glucose from the blood using diffusion
Identifies factors that affect the rate of diffusion (concentration gradient, surface area, distance)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why oxygen moves from the lungs into the blood without the body needing to pump it, could they explain what diffusion is and why it always moves in one particular direction?
topics.nameZh: 扩散作用是如何运作的
topics.descriptionZh: 将扩散作用解释为微粒从高浓度区域向低浓度区域的净移动，并描述其在物质（如氧气、二氧化碳、葡萄糖）进出细胞以及在细胞之间移动时所起的作用。
evidenceZh: 用微粒理论（particle theory）定义扩散作用
解释氧气和二氧化碳在肺泡（alveoli）处的扩散方向
解释细胞如何通过扩散作用从血液中获取葡萄糖
识别影响扩散速率的因素（浓度梯度（concentration gradient）、表面积、距离）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果有人问{{name}}，为什么氧气从肺部进入血液不需要身体去“泵”它，{{name}}能否解释什么是扩散作用，以及为什么它总是朝着一个特定的方向移动？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Human Reproduction
topics.description: Describe the structure and function of the male and female human reproductive systems, and explain the processes of fertilisation, gestation, and birth including the role of the placenta
evidence: Labels diagrams of the male and female reproductive systems
Explains the roles of gametes (sperm and egg) in sexual reproduction
Describes what happens during fertilisation and where it occurs
Explains the function of the placenta and the impact of maternal lifestyle on foetal development
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was studying human reproduction, could they describe how the male and female reproductive systems work together and explain what happens between fertilisation and birth?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述男性和女性人体生殖系统的结构和功能，并解释受精（fertilisation）、妊娠（gestation）和分娩（birth）的过程，包括胎盘（placenta）的作用
evidenceZh: 标注男性和女性生殖系统的图表
解释配子（精子和卵子）在有性生殖中的作用
描述受精过程中发生的事情及其发生的位置
解释胎盘的功能以及母体生活方式对胎儿发育的影响
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 正在学习人类生殖，他们能否描述男性和女性生殖系统是如何协同工作的，并解释从受精到分娩之间发生的事情？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Pathogens & the Immune System
topics.description: Explain how pathogens (bacteria, viruses, and fungi) cause disease and describe how the immune system responds, including the roles of white blood cells (phagocytosis, antibody production) and the concept of immunity
evidence: Distinguishes between bacteria, viruses, and fungi as pathogens with examples of each
Explains two ways white blood cells destroy pathogens (engulfing and antibodies)
Explains how vaccination works and why it prevents disease
Explains the difference between being infected and being ill
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} got a cold, could they explain what type of pathogen caused it, how the immune system tries to fight it off, and why a vaccine for flu won't protect you from all colds?
topics.nameZh: 病原体(Pathogens)与免疫系统(Immune System)
topics.descriptionZh: 解释病原体（细菌、病毒和真菌）如何引发疾病，并描述免疫系统如何作出反应，包括白细胞（white blood cells）的作用（如吞噬作用(phagocytosis)、产生抗体(antibody production)）以及免疫(immunity)的概念。
evidenceZh: 区分细菌、病毒和真菌作为病原体的不同，并给出各自的例子
解释白细胞破坏病原体的两种方式（吞噬(engulfing)和产生抗体(antibodies)）
解释疫苗接种(vaccination)如何起作用以及为什么它能预防疾病
解释被感染(infected)和生病(ill)之间的区别
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}感冒了，他们能否解释是哪种类型的病原体(pathogen)引起的，免疫系统(immune system)是如何尝试将其击退的，以及为什么流感疫苗(flu vaccine)不能预防所有的感冒？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Plant Reproduction
topics.description: Describe the structure of a flower and explain the processes of wind and insect pollination, fertilisation, seed and fruit formation, and seed dispersal in plants
evidence: Labels the main parts of a flower (sepals, petals, stamens, carpel, ovary, ovule)
Compares wind-pollinated and insect-pollinated flowers and explains adaptations of each
Traces the journey from pollination to seed dispersal
Identifies and explains at least two methods of seed dispersal
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watched bees visiting flowers in a garden, could they explain what role the bees are playing and trace the full journey from pollination through to seed dispersal?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述花的结构，并解释植物中风力传粉 (wind pollination) 和昆虫传粉 (insect pollination)、受精 (fertilisation)、种子与果实形成以及种子传播 (seed dispersal) 的过程。
evidenceZh: 标记花的主要部分（萼片 (sepals)、花瓣 (petals)、雄蕊 (stamens)、雌蕊 (carpel)、子房 (ovary)、胚珠 (ovule)）
比较风媒花和虫媒花，并解释它们各自的适应性特征
追踪从传粉 (pollination) 到种子传播 (seed dispersal) 的完整过程
识别并解释至少两种种子传播的方法
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在花园里观察蜜蜂访花，他们能解释蜜蜂在其中扮演的角色，并追踪从传粉到种子传播的完整过程吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Effects of Drugs & Alcohol
topics.description: Explain the effects of recreational drugs including alcohol, tobacco, and illegal substances on behaviour, health, and body systems, and distinguish between depressants, stimulants, and hallucinogens
evidence: Categorises common recreational drugs as depressants, stimulants, or hallucinogens
Explains specific effects of alcohol and tobacco on the body (e.g. liver damage, lung cancer)
Discusses the difference between physical and psychological dependence
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a news story about drug misuse, could they explain what different types of drugs do to the body and behaviour — and why some are more harmful than others?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释消遣性药物（recreational drugs，包括酒精、烟草和非法物质）对行为、健康和身体系统的影响，并区分抑制剂（depressants）、兴奋剂（stimulants）和致幻剂（hallucinogens）。
evidenceZh: 将常见的消遣性药物分类为抑制剂（depressants）、兴奋剂（stimulants）或致幻剂（hallucinogens）。
解释酒精和烟草对身体的具体影响（如肝损伤、肺癌）。
探讨生理依赖（physical dependence）与心理依赖（psychological dependence）之间的区别。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到一则关于药物滥用的新闻报道，他们能否解释不同类型的药物对身体和行为会产生什么影响——以及为什么有些药物比其他药物危害更大？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Arctic vs Antarctic
topics.description: Know that the Arctic (North Pole) and Antarctic (South Pole) are very different — the Arctic is a frozen ocean surrounded by land where people and polar bears live, while the Antarctic is a huge ice-covered continent surrounded by ocean where penguins live but no people live permanently
evidence: State that the Arctic is a frozen ocean surrounded by land, while the Antarctic is a continent covered in ice surrounded by ocean
Explain that polar bears live in the Arctic and penguins live in the Antarctic, not the other way around
Know that people (like the Inuit) live in the Arctic but nobody lives permanently in Antarctica
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the big difference between the two poles — that the Arctic is frozen sea with land around it, while the Antarctic is a frozen continent with sea around it?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解北极（北极点）和南极（南极点）有很大的不同——北极是被陆地包围的冰冻海洋，那里生活着人类和北极熊；而南极是被海洋包围的巨大陆地（南极洲），上面覆盖着冰雪，那里生活着企鹅，但没有人类永久居住。
evidenceZh: 说明北极是被陆地包围的冰冻海洋，而南极是被海洋包围的冰雪覆盖的大陆。
解释北极熊生活在北极，企鹅生活在南极，而不是反过来。
了解人类（如因纽特人 Inuit）生活在北极，但没有人永久居住在南极洲（Antarctica）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释这两个极地之间的巨大差异——北极是被陆地包围的冰冻海洋，而南极是被海洋包围的冰冻大陆？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Brave Polar Explorers
topics.description: Know simple stories of brave polar explorers — Robert Falcon Scott and Roald Amundsen who raced to the South Pole, and Ernest Shackleton whose ship Endurance was crushed by ice but who brought all his men home safely — and understand that polar exploration required incredible courage and endurance
evidence: Name at least two polar explorers: Scott, Amundsen, or Shackleton
Tell the basic story of Scott and Amundsen's race to the South Pole in simple terms
Describe what happened to Shackleton's ship Endurance and how he brought his crew home safely
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you the story of explorers who went to the South Pole — like Scott and Amundsen's race, or Shackleton whose ship got trapped in the ice but who saved all his crew?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解勇敢的极地探险家的简单故事——罗伯特·法尔肯·斯科特（Robert Falcon Scott）和罗尔德·阿蒙森（Roald Amundsen）竞相前往南极（South Pole），以及欧内斯特·沙克尔顿（Ernest Shackleton）的“坚忍号”（Endurance）被冰层压碎，但他却带领所有船员安全回家——并理解极地探险需要非凡的勇气和毅力。
evidenceZh: 至少说出两位极地探险家的名字：斯科特、阿蒙森或沙克尔顿
用简单的语言讲述斯科特和阿蒙森竞逐南极（South Pole）的基本故事
描述沙克尔顿的“坚忍号”（Endurance）遭遇了什么，以及他是如何带领船员安全回家的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能给你讲讲去南极（South Pole）探险家的故事吗——比如斯科特和阿蒙森的竞赛，或者沙克尔顿的船被困在冰中但他却救出了所有船员的故事？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Ice & Snow
topics.description: Know that water can be solid (ice and snow) or liquid, that snow is made of tiny frozen ice crystals, that icebergs are huge chunks of ice floating in the ocean with most of their bulk hidden underwater, and that ice floats because it is lighter than liquid water
evidence: Explain that ice and snow are frozen water (solid) and that water can change between solid and liquid
Describe an iceberg as a huge piece of ice floating in the ocean with most of it hidden below the surface
State that ice floats because frozen water is lighter than liquid water
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that icebergs are like floating ice mountains with most of the ice hidden under the water — and that the polar regions are covered in ice because it's so cold the water stays frozen?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解水可以呈固态（冰和雪）或液态，雪是由微小的冻结冰晶（ice crystals）组成的，冰山是漂浮在海洋中的巨大冰块，其大部分体积隐藏在水下，以及冰会漂浮是因为固态水比液态水轻（密度较小）。
evidenceZh: 解释冰和雪是冻结的水（固态），并且水可以在固态和液态之间相互转化
描述冰山是漂浮在海洋中的巨大冰块，其大部分隐藏在水面以下
说明冰会漂浮是因为固态水比液态水轻
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否知道冰山就像漂浮在水面上的冰雪山脉，大部分冰体隐藏在水下——并且知道极地地区被冰覆盖是因为那里非常寒冷，水一直处于冻结状态？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Midnight Sun & Polar Night
topics.description: Know that at the poles, daylight and darkness are extreme — in summer the Sun never fully sets (midnight sun) and in winter the Sun never rises (polar night lasting months) — and that this is very different from what we experience at home, where every day has both daylight and darkness
evidence: Describe midnight sun: in polar summer, the Sun stays above the horizon all day and night
Describe polar night: in polar winter, the Sun stays below the horizon for weeks or months
Compare this to normal day-night patterns at home, noting the dramatic difference
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know the amazing fact that at the poles, the Sun doesn't set at all in summer and doesn't rise at all in winter — so there can be months of daylight or months of darkness?
topics.nameZh: 极昼与极夜 (Midnight Sun & Polar Night)
topics.descriptionZh: 了解在地球两极，白昼和黑夜的现象非常极端——夏天太阳完全不落下（极昼 Midnight Sun），而冬天太阳完全不升起（极夜 Polar Night，持续数月）——这与我们在家里经历的每天都有白天和黑夜的情况非常不同。
evidenceZh: 描述极昼 (Midnight Sun)：在极地夏季，太阳全天24小时都停留在地平线以上
描述极夜 (Polar Night)：在极地冬季，太阳连续数周或数月都停留在地平线以下
将此与我们在家乡经历的正常昼夜交替模式进行对比，指出其中的巨大差异
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否知道这个神奇的科学事实：在地球两极，夏天太阳完全不落山，冬天太阳完全不升起——因此可能会出现连续数月的白昼或连续数月的黑夜？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Penguins
topics.description: Know key facts about penguins — they live in the Antarctic and Southern Hemisphere, they cannot fly but are excellent swimmers, Emperor penguins are the largest and huddle together in winter to keep warm, and penguin parents take turns keeping their egg warm on their feet in freezing temperatures
evidence: State at least three facts about penguins: they can't fly, they're excellent swimmers, and Emperor penguins are the biggest
Describe how Emperor penguins huddle together in winter to keep warm
Explain that penguin parents take turns keeping their egg warm on their feet in freezing temperatures
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you about penguins — that they can't fly but swim brilliantly, that Emperor penguins huddle in huge groups to stay warm, and that the dad balances the egg on his feet for weeks?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解关于企鹅的关键知识——它们生活在南极和南半球，虽然不会飞却是游泳健将，体型最大的帝企鹅在冬天会紧紧挤在一起取暖，而且企鹅爸爸妈妈在严寒中会轮流把蛋放在脚背上保暖。
evidenceZh: 说出至少三个关于企鹅的事实：它们不会飞、是游泳健将，以及帝企鹅体型最大
描述帝企鹅在冬天是如何挤在一起取暖的
解释企鹅父母在严寒中是如何轮流把蛋放在脚上保暖的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能给你讲讲关于企鹅的知识吗——比如它们不会飞却是游泳健将，帝企鹅会挤成一大群来保暖，还有企鹅爸爸会把蛋稳稳地顶在脚背上好几个星期？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Polar Animals
topics.description: Know about other polar animals besides penguins and polar bears — seals that swim under ice, walruses with long tusks, Arctic foxes that turn white in winter, snowy owls, narwhals with their unicorn-like tusk, and whales that migrate to polar waters to feed — and that all these animals have special features to survive extreme cold
evidence: Name at least four polar animals beyond penguins and polar bears, such as seals, walruses, Arctic foxes, snowy owls, or narwhals
Describe one way each named animal survives the cold (e.g. walrus blubber, Arctic fox white winter coat)
State that narwhals have a long spiral tusk and live in Arctic waters
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name several animals that live in the freezing polar regions — like walruses, Arctic foxes, snowy owls, or narwhals — and explain how they cope with the cold?
