topics.descriptionZh: 了解企鹅和北极熊之外的其他极地动物——在冰层下游动的海豹、长着长牙的海象、冬天会变白的北极狐、雪鸮、长着类似独角兽长牙的独角鲸，以及洄游到极地水域觅食的鲸鱼——并认识到这些动物都拥有在极寒环境中生存的特殊本领。
evidenceZh: 说出至少四种企鹅和北极熊之外的极地动物，如海豹、海象、北极狐、雪鸮或独角鲸
描述每种提到的动物抵御寒冷的一种方法（例如海象的脂肪层、北极狐白色的冬毛）
说明独角鲸长着长长的螺旋状长牙，并且生活在北极水域
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能说出几种生活在极寒地区的动物吗——比如海象、北极狐、雪鸮或独角鲸——并解释它们是如何抵御寒冷的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Polar Bears
topics.description: Know key facts about polar bears — they live only in the Arctic (not the Antarctic), they have thick white fur and a layer of fat (blubber) to keep warm, they are excellent swimmers, and they hunt seals by waiting at holes in the sea ice
evidence: State that polar bears live in the Arctic, not the Antarctic
Describe at least two ways polar bears stay warm: thick white fur and a layer of blubber (fat)
Explain how polar bears hunt seals by waiting at breathing holes in the sea ice
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you about polar bears — that they live only in the Arctic, their thick fur and blubber keep them warm, and they hunt seals by waiting patiently at holes in the ice?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解关于北极熊的关键事实：它们只生活在北极（Arctic）而非南极（Antarctic）；它们有厚厚的白毛和一层用来保暖的脂肪（blubber）；它们是出色的游泳健将；它们通过在冰面的孔洞旁等待来捕猎海豹。
evidenceZh: 说明北极熊生活在北极（Arctic），而不是南极（Antarctic）
描述北极熊保暖的至少两种方式：厚厚的白毛和一层脂肪（blubber）
解释北极熊如何通过在冰面的呼吸孔旁守候来捕猎海豹
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能告诉你关于北极熊的知识吗？比如它们只生活在北极（Arctic），它们厚厚的毛发和脂肪（blubber）能帮它们保暖，以及它们会在冰洞旁耐心守候来捕猎海豹。

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Where Are the Poles?
topics.description: Know that Earth has a North Pole and a South Pole — the two coldest places on the planet — and be able to find them on a globe, understanding that they are at the very top and very bottom of the Earth, as far from the Equator as possible
evidence: Point to the North Pole and South Pole on a globe or world map
Explain that the poles are the coldest places on Earth because they are farthest from the Equator
State that the North Pole is at the top and the South Pole is at the bottom of the Earth
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you hand {{name}} a globe, can they point to the North Pole and the South Pole and tell you they're the coldest places on Earth?
topics.descriptionZh: 知道地球有北极（North Pole）和南极（South Pole）——这是地球上最冷的两个地方——并能够在地球仪上找到它们，理解它们位于地球的最顶端和最底端，距离赤道（Equator）最远。
evidenceZh: 在地球仪或世界地图上指出北极和南极的位置
解释两极是地球上最冷的地方，因为它们距离赤道最远
说明北极在地球的最顶端，南极在地球的最底端
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你把地球仪递给{{name}}，他们能指出北极和南极，并告诉你它们是地球上最冷的地方吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Cold-Weather Adaptations
topics.description: Understand how polar animals are adapted to survive extreme cold — blubber (thick fat layer) insulates seals and whales, hollow fur traps air for warmth in polar bears, counter-current heat exchange in penguin flippers prevents heat loss, Arctic foxes grow thick white winter coats for camouflage and warmth, and some animals migrate to avoid the harshest months
evidence: Describe at least three cold-weather adaptations: blubber, hollow fur, counter-current heat exchange, white winter coats, or migration
Explain the purpose of each adaptation (e.g. blubber insulates against cold water, white fur provides camouflage in snow)
Use the word adaptation correctly to mean a feature that helps an animal survive in its environment
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain several ways polar animals survive the freezing cold — like a polar bear's hollow fur trapping warm air, a seal's thick blubber, or an Arctic fox changing colour in winter?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解极地动物如何适应极端严寒——海豹和鲸鱼依靠厚厚的脂肪层（blubber）来保暖，北极熊的中空毛发能锁住空气来保持体温，企鹅脚蹼中的逆流热交换（counter-current heat exchange）机制防止热量流失，北极狐长出厚实的白色冬毛用于伪装和保暖，还有些动物会通过迁徙来躲避最严寒的月份。
evidenceZh: 描述至少三种寒冷天气的适应性特征：厚厚的脂肪层（blubber）、中空毛发、逆流热交换（counter-current heat exchange）、白色冬毛或迁徙
解释每种适应性特征的作用（例如：厚厚的脂肪层能抵御冷水，白色冬毛能在雪中提供伪装）
正确使用“适应性（adaptation）”一词，表示帮助动物在其环境中生存的特征
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释极地动物抵御严寒的几种方法——比如北极熊的中空毛发如何锁住暖空气、海豹厚厚的脂肪层，或者北极狐在冬季改变毛色？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Comparing Arctic & Antarctic
topics.description: Compare the Arctic and Antarctic in detail — the Arctic is an ocean covered by floating sea ice with surrounding land masses (Canada, Russia, Greenland, Scandinavia), while Antarctica is a continent larger than Europe buried under ice up to 4 km thick; polar bears, Arctic foxes, and walruses live only in the Arctic while penguins, leopard seals, and albatrosses are found only in the Antarctic
evidence: State that the Arctic is a frozen ocean surrounded by land (name at least two bordering countries), while Antarctica is a continent covered by ice sheet up to 4 km thick
Correctly assign at least three animals to the Arctic and three to the Antarctic
Name at least two differences in human presence: indigenous peoples in the Arctic vs research stations only in Antarctica
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in detail how the Arctic and Antarctic are different — which animals live where, that one is frozen ocean and the other is a frozen continent, and which countries border the Arctic?
topics.descriptionZh: 详细比较北极和南极——北极是被周围陆地（加拿大、俄罗斯、格陵兰、斯堪的纳维亚）包围的、覆盖着浮冰的海洋，而南极是一个比欧洲还大的大陆，被厚达4公里的冰层覆盖；北极熊、北极狐和海象仅生活在北极，而企鹅、豹海豹和信天翁仅生活在南极
evidenceZh: 说明北极是被陆地包围的冰冻海洋（至少说出两个接壤国家），而南极是被厚达4公里冰盖覆盖的大陆
正确地将至少三种动物分配到北极，三种动物分配到南极
说出人类存在的至少两个差异：北极有原住民，而南极只有科考站
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否详细解释北极和南极有什么不同——哪些动物生活在哪里，哪个是冰冻的海洋而哪个是冰冻的大陆，以及哪些国家与北极接壤？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Ice & States of Matter
topics.description: Understand ice in different forms and states of matter — sea ice forms when ocean water freezes (it's salty and relatively thin), glacial ice forms from compacted snow over centuries (fresh water, very thick), and icebergs break off from glaciers and float in the sea; know that water exists as solid (ice), liquid (water), and gas (water vapour), and that salt lowers the freezing point of water
evidence: Distinguish between sea ice (frozen ocean, salty, thin) and glacial ice (compacted snow, fresh water, thick)
Explain that icebergs break off from glaciers and float because ice is less dense than liquid water
Describe the three states of water (solid, liquid, gas) and explain that salt lowers the freezing point
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between sea ice and glacier ice, and describe how water changes between solid, liquid, and gas — maybe by doing a simple freezing experiment with salt and fresh water?
topics.nameZh: 冰与物质状态 (States of Matter)
topics.descriptionZh: 了解不同形态的冰和物质状态：海水结冰形成海冰（含盐且相对较薄），积雪经过数百年压实形成冰川冰（淡水，非常厚），冰山从冰川断裂并漂浮在海中；了解水以固态（冰）、液态（水）和气态（水蒸气）存在，并知道盐会降低水的冰点 (Freezing point)。
evidenceZh: 区分海冰（海水冻结、含盐、较薄）和冰川冰（积雪压实、淡水、很厚）
解释冰山从冰川断裂并漂浮，因为冰的密度小于液态水
描述水的三种状态（固态、液态、气态）并解释盐会降低冰点 (Freezing point)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释海冰和冰川冰的区别，并描述水如何在固态、液态和气态之间变化——也许可以通过用盐水和淡水做一个简单的结冰实验？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Inuit & Sami Peoples
topics.description: Know that indigenous peoples have lived in the Arctic for thousands of years — the Inuit across Canada, Alaska, and Greenland, and the Sami in northern Scandinavia — developing remarkable knowledge of the environment, using dog sleds and kayaks for transport, wearing animal-skin clothing for warmth, and building igloos as temporary shelters, with a deep respect for the animals and land they depend on
evidence: Name the Inuit (Canada, Alaska, Greenland) and Sami (northern Scandinavia) as Arctic indigenous peoples
Describe at least three aspects of traditional Arctic life: dog sleds, kayaks, animal-skin clothing, igloos, or hunting practices
Explain that indigenous Arctic peoples have deep knowledge of their environment developed over thousands of years
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you about the Inuit and Sami peoples who have lived in the Arctic for thousands of years — how they travel by dog sled, wear animal-skin clothing, and know the ice and animals incredibly well?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解原住民在北极地区生活了数千年——因纽特人（Inuit）分布在加拿大、阿拉斯加和格陵兰岛，萨米人（Sami）居住在北欧斯堪的纳维亚半岛北部。他们发展出了对自然环境的卓越认知，使用狗拉雪橇和皮划艇作为交通工具，穿着动物皮毛衣服保暖，并建造冰屋（igloo）作为临时住所，对他们赖以生存的动物和土地怀有深深的尊重。
evidenceZh: 说出因纽特人（加拿大、阿拉斯加、格陵兰岛）和萨米人（北欧斯堪的纳维亚半岛北部）是北极地区的原住民
描述北极传统生活的至少三个方面：如狗拉雪橇、皮划艇、动物皮毛服装、冰屋或狩猎习俗
解释北极原住民在数千年的生活中积累了对其生存环境的深刻认知
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能给你讲讲在北极生活了数千年的因纽特人和萨米人吗？比如他们如何乘坐狗拉雪橇出行、穿着动物皮毛衣服，以及对冰雪和动物有着极其深刻的了解？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Polar Food Chains
topics.description: Understand polar food chains — in the Antarctic, phytoplankton are eaten by krill, krill are eaten by fish and penguins, and penguins are eaten by leopard seals and orcas; in the Arctic, algae under ice feeds zooplankton, which feeds fish, which feeds seals, which feeds polar bears — and that tiny organisms like krill and plankton are the foundation of all polar life
evidence: Construct an Antarctic food chain: phytoplankton → krill → penguin → leopard seal or orca
Construct an Arctic food chain: algae → zooplankton → fish → seal → polar bear
Explain why krill and plankton are critical — without them, the entire food chain collapses
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain a polar food chain — starting from tiny plankton, through krill and fish, up to seals and polar bears or orcas — and explain why the tiny creatures at the bottom are so important?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解极地食物链——在南极，浮游植物（phytoplankton）被磷虾吃掉，磷虾被鱼类和企鹅吃掉，企鹅被豹海豹和虎鲸吃掉；在北极，冰下的藻类喂养浮游动物（zooplankton），浮游动物喂养鱼类，鱼类喂养海豹，海豹喂养北极熊——并了解像磷虾和浮游生物这样微小的生物是所有极地生命的基础。
evidenceZh: 构建南极食物链：浮游植物（phytoplankton） → 磷虾（krill） → 企鹅 → 豹海豹或虎鲸
构建北极食物链：藻类 → 浮游动物（zooplankton） → 鱼类 → 海豹 → 北极熊
解释为什么磷虾和浮游生物至关重要——如果没有它们，整个食物链就会崩溃
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释一条极地食物链——从微小的浮游生物开始，经过磷虾和鱼类，直到海豹和北极熊或虎鲸——并解释为什么处于底层的这些微小生物如此重要？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Arctic Tundra
topics.description: Know what the Arctic tundra is — a vast, treeless landscape with permafrost (permanently frozen ground) just below the surface, a very short growing season in summer when mosses, lichens, and tough grasses burst into life, and home to caribou/reindeer, musk oxen, lemmings, and snowy owls
evidence: Describe the tundra as a treeless landscape with permafrost (permanently frozen ground) beneath the surface
Explain that the tundra has a very short summer growing season when mosses, lichens, and grasses grow quickly
Name at least three tundra animals: caribou/reindeer, musk oxen, lemmings, or snowy owls
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know what tundra is — the huge flat landscape near the Arctic with no trees, frozen ground underneath, and short summers where everything bursts into life?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解什么是北极苔原——一片广阔无树的景观，地表下刚好有永久冻土（permafrost），夏季有一个非常短暂的生长季节，此时苔藓、地衣和坚韧的草类焕发生机，这里也是驯鹿（caribou/reindeer）、麝牛（musk oxen）、旅鼠（lemmings）和雪鸮（snowy owls）的家园
evidenceZh: 将苔原描述为一种地表之下存在永久冻土（permanently frozen ground）的无树景观
解释苔原的夏季生长季非常短暂，此时苔藓、地衣和草类会迅速生长
说出至少三种苔原动物：驯鹿（caribou/reindeer）、麝牛（musk oxen）、旅鼠（lemmings）或雪鸮（snowy owls）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否了解什么是苔原——北极附近广阔平坦、没有树木、地下有冻土，且夏季短暂、万物焕发生机的景观？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Race to the South Pole
topics.description: Know the story of the race to the South Pole in detail — Norwegian Roald Amundsen and British Robert Falcon Scott both set out in 1911, Amundsen arrived first on 14 December using dog sleds and careful planning, Scott arrived 34 days later using man-hauled sledges and tragically died with his team on the return journey; also know about Ernest Shackleton's 1914 Endurance expedition where the ship was trapped and crushed by ice, and Shackleton's extraordinary boat journey to South Georgia to rescue his crew
evidence: Describe the Scott vs Amundsen race: Amundsen arrived 14 December 1911 using dog sleds; Scott arrived 34 days later and died on the return
Explain at least two reasons Amundsen succeeded: better planning, dog sleds, polar experience, and lighter supplies
Narrate the key events of the Endurance expedition: ship crushed, camps on ice, boat journey to South Georgia, all crew rescued
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you the detailed story of Amundsen and Scott's race to the South Pole — who won and why, what went wrong for Scott, and the incredible survival story of Shackleton's Endurance?
topics.descriptionZh: 详细了解南极探险竞速的故事：挪威人罗尔德·阿蒙森（Roald Amundsen）和英国人罗伯特·法尔肯·斯科特（Robert Falcon Scott）均在1911年出发。阿蒙森依靠狗拉雪橇和周密的计划，于12月14日率先抵达；斯科特则使用人力拉拽的雪橇，在34天后抵达，并在返回途中与队员不幸遇难；此外，还要了解欧内斯特·沙克尔顿（Ernest Shackleton）1914年的“坚忍号”（Endurance）探险，当时船只被浮冰困住并压碎，沙克尔顿还完成了一次非凡的乘船航行前往南乔治亚岛（South Georgia），最终成功营救了他的全体船员。
evidenceZh: 描述斯科特与阿蒙森的竞速：阿蒙森于1911年12月14日使用狗拉雪橇抵达；斯科特在34天后抵达，并在返回途中遇难
解释阿蒙森成功的至少两个原因：更好的计划、使用狗拉雪橇、丰富的极地经验以及更轻的补给
讲述“坚忍号”探险的关键事件：船只被压碎、在冰上扎营、乘小船前往南乔治亚岛、全体船员获救
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能为你详细讲述阿蒙森和斯科特争夺南极点的故事吗——谁赢了，为什么赢，斯科特出了什么差错，以及沙克尔顿“坚忍号”不可思议的求生故事？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Why Polar Seasons Are Extreme
topics.description: Understand why the poles have extreme seasons — Earth's axis is tilted at about 23.5°, so as it orbits the Sun, each pole spends half the year tilted toward the Sun (continuous daylight, warmer summer) and half tilted away (continuous darkness, bitter winter); this tilt also drives the annual cycle of sea ice expanding in winter and retreating in summer, and triggers animal behaviours like migration and breeding
evidence: Explain that Earth's axis is tilted at about 23.5° and this tilt causes the extreme polar seasons
Describe how the tilt means each pole faces toward the Sun for half the year (summer/daylight) and away for the other half (winter/darkness)
Connect the seasonal cycle to at least one animal behaviour, such as migration or sea ice retreat affecting hunting
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain WHY the poles have months of daylight in summer and months of darkness in winter — that it's because Earth is tilted on its axis as it goes around the Sun?
topics.nameZh: 为什么极地季节如此极端
topics.descriptionZh: 理解为什么极地季节如此极端——地球地轴倾斜约23.5°，因此在绕太阳公转时，每个极点有一半时间朝向太阳倾斜（持续白昼，较暖的夏季），另一半时间背向太阳倾斜（持续黑夜，严酷的冬季）；这种倾斜还驱动了海冰在冬季扩张、夏季消退的年度循环，并引发了动物的迁徙和繁殖等行为。
evidenceZh: 解释地球地轴倾斜约23.5°，且这种倾斜导致了极地的极端季节变化
描述这种倾斜如何意味着每个极点在一半的时间里（夏季/白昼）朝向太阳，而在另一半时间里（冬季/黑夜）背向太阳
将季节循环与至少一种动物行为联系起来，例如迁徙或海冰消退影响捕猎
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释为什么极地在夏季有数月的白昼，在冬季有数月的黑夜——这是因为地球在绕太阳公转时地轴是倾斜的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Antarctic Treaty & Research
topics.description: Know that Antarctica is governed by the Antarctic Treaty (signed 1959, in force since 1961) — which sets Antarctica aside for peaceful purposes and scientific research, bans military activity and mining, and is signed by over 50 countries; understand that international research stations study climate, astronomy, biology, and geology, and that Antarctica is the closest thing on Earth to a continent for science rather than politics
evidence: State that the Antarctic Treaty (1959) sets Antarctica aside for peace and science, banning military activity and mining
Know that over 50 countries have signed the treaty and that many operate research stations
Name at least two areas of scientific research conducted in Antarctica: climate, astronomy, biology, or geology
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know about the Antarctic Treaty — that over 50 countries agreed Antarctica should be used only for science and peace, not war or mining — and that research stations there study everything from ice to stars?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解南极洲受《南极条约》（Antarctic Treaty，1959年签署，1961年生效）管辖——该条约将南极洲划为和平与科学研究的专属区域，禁止军事活动和采矿，目前已有50多个国家签署；理解国际科考站（research stations）在此研究气候（climate）、天文学（astronomy）、生物学（biology）和地质学（geology），并认识到南极洲是地球上最纯粹致力于科学而非政治的大陆。
evidenceZh: 说明《南极条约》（1959年）将南极洲划定为和平与科学研究的区域，并禁止军事活动和采矿。
知道已有50多个国家签署了该条约，并且许多国家在此设立了科考站。
能说出至少两个在南极洲进行的科学研究领域：气候（climate）、天文学（astronomy）、生物学（biology）或地质学（geology）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否了解《南极条约》——即50多个国家同意南极洲只能用于科学和和平，而不是战争或采矿——并且知道那里的科考站研究从冰雪到星空的各种事物？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Climate Change at the Poles
topics.description: Understand how climate change is affecting polar regions — Arctic sea ice is shrinking dramatically (losing about 13% per decade since 1979), the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets are losing mass and contributing to sea level rise, permafrost is thawing and releasing methane (a powerful greenhouse gas), and these changes create positive feedback loops where melting leads to more warming which leads to more melting
evidence: State that Arctic sea ice has been declining at roughly 13% per decade since 1979
Explain the positive feedback loop: warming → ice melts → dark ocean absorbs more heat → more warming → more melting
Describe at least two consequences of polar ice loss: sea level rise and permafrost thawing releasing methane
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how climate change is melting polar ice — that Arctic sea ice is shrinking, ice sheets are losing mass, and that melting actually makes more melting happen in a vicious cycle?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解气候变化如何影响极地地区——北极海冰正在急剧减少（自1979年以来每十年约减少13%），格陵兰岛和南极冰盖正在流失质量并导致海平面上升，永久冻土正在融化并释放甲烷（一种强效温室气体），这些变化形成了正反馈循环（positive feedback loops），即融化导致更多变暖，进而导致更多融化。
evidenceZh: 说明自1979年以来，北极海冰每十年大约减少13%
解释正反馈循环：变暖→冰融化→深色海洋吸收更多热量→进一步变暖→更多融化
描述极地冰层流失的至少两个后果：海平面上升以及永久冻土融化释放甲烷
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释气候变化是如何融化极地冰层的——包括北极海冰正在缩小、冰盖正在流失质量，以及融化实际上是如何在一个恶性循环中导致更多融化的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Earth's Frozen Water
topics.description: Understand the cryosphere and its role in Earth's water system — the cryosphere is all frozen water on Earth (ice sheets, glaciers, sea ice, permafrost, snow cover); polar ice sheets hold about 69% of Earth's fresh water; if all polar ice melted, sea levels would rise over 65 metres; and the water cycle connects polar ice to the global system through evaporation, precipitation, and meltwater flowing into oceans
evidence: Define the cryosphere as all frozen water on Earth and name its components: ice sheets, glaciers, sea ice, permafrost, snow
State that polar ice sheets hold approximately 69% of Earth's fresh water
Explain how polar ice connects to the global water cycle and what would happen if it all melted (65m+ sea level rise)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that most of Earth's fresh water is actually locked up as ice at the poles — and that if it all melted, the sea would rise over 65 metres, flooding coastal cities worldwide?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解冰冻圈（cryosphere）及其在地球水系统中的作用——冰冻圈是指地球上所有的冰冻水（冰盖 ice sheets、冰川 glaciers、海冰 sea ice、永久冻土 permafrost、积雪 snow cover）；极地冰盖储存了地球约69%的淡水；如果所有极地冰融化，海平面将上升超过65米；水循环通过蒸发（evaporation）、降水（precipitation）和融水流入海洋，将极地冰与全球系统连接起来。
evidenceZh: 将冰冻圈（cryosphere）定义为地球上所有的冰冻水，并说出其组成部分：冰盖（ice sheets）、冰川（glaciers）、海冰（sea ice）、永久冻土（permafrost）、雪（snow）
说明极地冰盖储存了地球上约69%的淡水
解释极地冰如何与全球水循环相连，以及如果它们全部融化会发生什么（海平面上升65米以上）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否知道地球上大部分淡水实际上被冻结在两极的冰中——并且如果这些冰全部融化，海平面将上升超过65米，淹没世界各地的沿海城市？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Glaciers & Ice Sheets
topics.description: Understand how glaciers and ice sheets form and behave — snow accumulates over centuries and compresses into dense ice, glaciers flow slowly downhill under their own weight carving U-shaped valleys and depositing moraines; the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets together hold enough ice to raise sea levels by over 65 metres; and ice cores drilled from these sheets contain trapped air bubbles that reveal Earth's climate history going back 800,000 years
evidence: Describe how glaciers form: snow accumulates, compresses, and becomes dense ice that flows slowly under its own weight
Explain that the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets hold enough water to raise sea levels dramatically if melted
Describe how ice cores reveal climate history through trapped air bubbles from hundreds of thousands of years ago
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how glaciers form from layers of snow pressed into ice, how they slowly carve valleys, and that scientists drill into ice sheets to learn about Earth's climate thousands of years ago?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解冰川和冰盖的形成与运动——积雪经过数百年压实成致密的冰，冰川在自身重力作用下缓慢向下滑动，雕刻出U型谷（U-shaped valleys）并留下冰碛物（moraines）；格陵兰岛和南极洲的冰盖储存了足够的冰，如果全部融化，会使海平面上升超过65米；从这些冰盖中钻取的冰芯含有被困住的气泡，能够揭示地球长达80万年的气候历史。
evidenceZh: 描述冰川的形成过程：积雪不断堆积、压实，变成在自身重力下缓慢流动的致密冰层
解释格陵兰岛和南极洲冰盖储存了大量水分，如果融化会导致海平面大幅上升
描述冰芯如何通过封存数十万年前的空气气泡来揭示地球的气候历史
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释冰川是如何由层层积雪压实成冰而形成的，它们如何缓慢地雕刻山谷，以及科学家是如何钻探冰盖来了解数千年前地球气候的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Polar Climate Zone
topics.description: Understand that polar regions belong to the polar climate zone — one of Earth's five main climate zones (tropical, arid, temperate, continental, polar) — characterised by temperatures rarely above 10°C even in summer, low precipitation (polar deserts receive less rain than the Sahara), and strong winds; know that latitude is the key factor determining climate zones, with polar regions above 60°N/S
evidence: Name the five main climate zones and place polar regions correctly within them
State that polar regions are above approximately 60° latitude and explain that distance from the Equator is the main reason they are cold
Describe polar climate characteristics: rarely above 10°C in summer, very low precipitation, strong winds
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain where the polar climate zone fits among Earth's five climate zones, and why the poles are so cold — linking it to their position at high latitudes far from the Equator?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解极地地区属于极地气候带（Polar Climate Zone）——这是地球五大主要气候带（热带、干旱、温带、大陆性、极地）之一——其特点是即使在夏季气温也很少超过10°C，降水量低（极地沙漠的降雨量少于撒哈拉沙漠），且风力强劲；知道纬度（Latitude）是决定气候带的关键因素，极地地区位于南北纬60°以上。
evidenceZh: 说出五大主要气候带，并将极地地区正确归入其中
说明极地地区大约位于南北纬60°以上，并解释距离赤道（Equator）遥远是其寒冷的主要原因
描述极地气候特征：夏季气温极少超过10°C，降水量极低，风力强劲
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释极地气候带在地球五大气候带中的位置，以及为什么极地如此寒冷——并将其与它们位于远离赤道的高纬度地区这一位置联系起来？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Polar Conservation & Future
topics.description: Understand the conservation challenges facing polar regions — marine protected areas in the Southern Ocean aim to preserve Antarctic ecosystems, Arctic nations dispute sovereignty over northern sea routes and resources as ice retreats, indigenous peoples fight for land rights and voice in environmental decisions, and international cooperation (Paris Agreement, Antarctic Treaty) is essential but difficult to maintain as economic pressures grow
evidence: Describe at least two conservation measures: marine protected areas in the Southern Ocean and the Antarctic Treaty
Explain why Arctic sovereignty is contested as ice retreats and shipping routes open
Describe the role of indigenous peoples in Arctic environmental decisions and why their knowledge matters
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} discuss the big challenges facing the poles — like countries arguing over Arctic resources as ice melts, the push for marine protected areas in Antarctica, and why indigenous peoples' voices matter in these decisions?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解极地面临的保护挑战——南大洋的海洋保护区（Marine Protected Areas）旨在保护南极生态系统；随着冰层退缩，北极国家就北方海航道和资源主权产生争议；原住民（Indigenous peoples）为争取土地权和环境决策发言权而奋斗；随着经济压力增加，国际合作（如《巴黎协定》和《南极条约》）至关重要但难以维持。
evidenceZh: 描述至少两项保护措施：南大洋的海洋保护区和《南极条约》（Antarctic Treaty）
解释为什么随着冰层退缩和航运路线的开放，北极的主权（Sovereignty）会受到争议
描述原住民在北极环境决策中的作用，以及为什么他们的传统知识至关重要
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否讨论极地面临的重大挑战——比如随着冰雪融化，各国对北极资源的争夺、推动在南极建立海洋保护区，以及为什么原住民的声音在这些决策中如此重要？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Polar Ecosystems Compared
topics.description: Compare Arctic and Antarctic ecosystems — the Arctic has both terrestrial (tundra) and marine ecosystems supporting large land mammals and indigenous human communities, while the Antarctic is almost entirely marine-based with virtually no land plants or mammals; both regions have short, intense food chains anchored by phytoplankton and krill, and both are disproportionately affected by climate change and human activity
evidence: Compare Arctic (terrestrial + marine, land mammals, human communities) with Antarctic (almost entirely marine, no land mammals)
Explain that both polar food chains depend on phytoplankton and krill at the base
Describe why polar ecosystems are particularly vulnerable to climate change (short food chains, specialised organisms)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} compare the Arctic and Antarctic ecosystems — explaining that the Arctic has land animals and people while Antarctica's life is almost all in the sea, and that both depend on tiny creatures like krill?
topics.descriptionZh: 对比北极和南极生态系统——北极拥有陆地（苔原 tundra）和海洋生态系统，养育着大型陆地哺乳动物和原住民社区；而南极几乎完全依赖海洋，几乎没有陆地植物或哺乳动物；这两个地区都有以浮游植物（phytoplankton）和磷虾（krill）为起点的短小且紧密的食物链，并且都受到气候变化和人类活动的严重影响。
evidenceZh: 对比北极（陆地与海洋、陆地哺乳动物、人类社区）和南极（几乎全为海洋、无陆地哺乳动物）
解释两极食物链的底层都依赖于浮游植物（phytoplankton）和磷虾（krill）
描述极地生态系统为何对气候变化尤为脆弱（食物链短、物种高度特化）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否对比北极和南极生态系统——解释北极有陆地动物和人类，而南极的生命几乎都在海洋中，并且两者都依赖于像磷虾（krill）这样的微小生物？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Polar Exploration Then & Now
topics.description: Compare historical polar exploration with modern polar science — the Heroic Age (1897–1922) relied on ships, dogs, and human endurance with many fatalities, while today's polar scientists use GPS, satellites, icebreaker ships, heated research stations, and aircraft; understand that modern challenges include studying climate change data, and that polar science now includes diverse international teams including women scientists like glaciologist Liz Thomas and marine biologist Sylvia Earle
evidence: Compare Heroic Age exploration (dog sleds, man-hauling, many deaths) with modern science (GPS, satellites, icebreakers, heated stations)
Name at least two technologies that make modern polar science possible
Name a modern polar scientist and explain that today's polar teams are diverse and international
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} compare old polar exploration — dog sleds, freezing camps, real danger of death — with modern polar science using satellites, heated research stations, and diverse international teams?
topics.descriptionZh: 比较历史上的极地探索与现代极地科学——“英雄时代”（1897-1922年）依靠船只、狗和人类耐力，导致许多人丧生；而今天的极地科学家使用全球定位系统（GPS）、卫星、破冰船（icebreaker）、供暖研究站和飞机；了解现代挑战包括研究气候变化数据，并且极地科学现在包含多元化的国际团队，包括冰川学家（glaciologist）莉兹·托马斯（Liz Thomas）和海洋生物学家（marine biologist）西尔维娅·厄尔（Sylvia Earle）等女性科学家。
evidenceZh: 比较“英雄时代”的探索（狗拉雪橇、人力拖拽、大量伤亡）与现代科学（GPS、卫星、破冰船、供暖研究站）
说出至少两项使现代极地科学成为可能的技术
说出一位现代极地科学家的名字，并解释今天的极地团队是多元化且国际化的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否将早期的极地探索——狗拉雪橇、严寒营地、真实的死亡危险——与使用卫星、供暖研究站和多元化国际团队的现代极地科学进行比较？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Polar Oceans and World Climate
topics.description: Understand how polar oceans connect to the global climate system — cold, dense polar water sinks and drives thermohaline circulation (a global conveyor belt of ocean currents), sea ice reflects sunlight back to space (the albedo effect) helping regulate Earth's temperature, and the Southern Ocean around Antarctica is one of the most productive marine ecosystems on Earth due to upwelling nutrients
evidence: Explain that cold, dense polar water sinks and drives global ocean circulation (thermohaline circulation)
Describe the albedo effect: white ice reflects sunlight back to space, while dark ocean absorbs heat
State that the Southern Ocean is extremely productive because upwelling brings nutrients to the surface
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how cold polar water sinks and drives a global conveyor belt of ocean currents, and how white sea ice reflects sunlight to help keep the planet cool?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解极地海洋如何与全球气候系统相连：寒冷、高密度的极地海水下沉并驱动温盐环流（thermohaline circulation，即全球海洋洋流的传送带）；海冰将阳光反射回太空（反照率效应，albedo effect），帮助调节地球温度；此外，由于上升流（upwelling）带来丰富的营养物质，南极洲周围的南大洋成为了地球上最具活力的海洋生态系统之一。
evidenceZh: 解释寒冷、高密度的极地海水下沉并驱动全球海洋环流（温盐环流，thermohaline circulation）。
描述反照率效应（albedo effect）：白色的冰将阳光反射回太空，而深色的海洋则吸收热量。
说明南大洋具有极高的生产力，因为上升流（upwelling）将营养物质带到了海洋表层。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释寒冷的极地海水如何下沉并驱动全球海洋洋流的传送带，以及白色的海冰如何反射阳光来帮助地球保持凉爽？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Everyday Foods from Rainforests
topics.description: Know that many everyday foods come from rainforests — chocolate is made from cacao beans, bananas grow in tropical forests, coffee berries ripen in forest shade, and Brazil nuts fall from giant trees — connecting our daily lives to faraway forests
evidence: Name at least three foods that come from rainforests, such as chocolate (cacao), bananas, and Brazil nuts
Explain that cacao beans grow on trees in the rainforest and are made into chocolate
Connect their own food choices to rainforest origins by identifying a product they eat that comes from the forest
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is eating a chocolate bar or a banana, can they tell you that those foods originally come from rainforests?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解许多日常食物来自雨林——巧克力由可可豆（cacao beans）制成，香蕉生长在热带森林中，咖啡浆果（coffee berries）在森林荫凉处成熟，巴西坚果（Brazil nuts）从巨树上落下——将我们的日常生活与远方的森林联系起来
evidenceZh: 说出至少三种来自雨林的食物，例如巧克力（可可）、香蕉和巴西坚果
解释可可豆（cacao beans）生长在雨林的树上，并被制成巧克力
通过找出一种他们食用的来自森林的产品，将自己的食物选择与雨林的起源联系起来
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}正在吃巧克力棒或香蕉，他们能告诉你这些食物最初来自雨林吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Indigenous Rainforest Peoples
topics.description: Know that indigenous peoples such as the Yanomami have lived in rainforests for thousands of years, building homes from forest materials, finding food by hunting, fishing, and gathering, and knowing the forest and its plants and animals deeply
evidence: Explain that indigenous peoples like the Yanomami have lived in rainforests for thousands of years
Describe how they use the forest for shelter, food, and medicine
Show respect for indigenous knowledge by explaining that these communities understand the forest very deeply
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that some people have lived in rainforests for thousands of years — building their homes from the trees and knowing which plants are food and which are medicine?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解像亚诺马米人（Yanomami）这样的原住民已经在热带雨林中生活了数千年。他们利用森林里的材料建造房屋，通过打猎、捕鱼和采集来获取食物，并且非常深入地了解森林及其动植物。
evidenceZh: 解释像亚诺马米人（Yanomami）这样的原住民已经在热带雨林中生活了数千年
描述他们如何利用森林来建造住所、寻找食物和获取药材
解释这些原住民群体对森林有着极其深刻的了解，以此表达对原住民传统知识的尊重
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否知道有些人已经在热带雨林中生活了数千年——他们用树木建造房屋，并且知道哪些植物可以作为食物，哪些植物可以用作药材？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Inside a Rainforest
topics.description: Describe what it feels like inside a rainforest — hot and sticky (humid), dark on the ground because the treetops block the light, loud with animal calls and insect buzzing, and dripping with water from rain and condensation
evidence: Describe the air inside a rainforest as hot and sticky (humid)
Explain that the forest floor is dark because tall trees block most of the sunlight
Name at least two sounds you would hear in a rainforest, such as bird calls, insect buzzing, or rain dripping
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watches a rainforest video clip, can they describe what it would feel, sound, and look like to stand inside — the heat, the noise, the darkness on the ground?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述身处雨林内部的感受——空气炎热又潮湿（湿度高），由于树冠遮挡了阳光，地面十分阴暗；四周十分喧闹，充满了动物的叫声和昆虫的嗡嗡声；雨水和凝结的水滴让四周湿漉漉的，到处都在滴水。
evidenceZh: 描述雨林里的空气，说明它炎热又黏糊糊的（湿度高）
解释为什么森林地面很暗，说明是因为高大的树木挡住了大部分阳光
说出至少两种在雨林里能听到的声音，比如鸟叫声、昆虫的嗡嗡声或雨水滴落的声音
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}观看一段雨林的视频片段，他们能否描述出站在雨林里的触觉、听觉和视觉感受——比如炎热、嘈杂的声音以及地面的阴暗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rainforest Animals
topics.description: Name and recognise iconic rainforest animals — jaguars, toucans, sloths, poison dart frogs, howler monkeys, macaws, and butterflies — and know which layer of the rainforest each lives in
evidence: Name at least five iconic rainforest animals such as jaguars, toucans, sloths, poison dart frogs, and howler monkeys
Match at least three animals to the rainforest layer where they live (e.g. monkeys in the canopy, jaguars on the forest floor)
Describe one distinctive feature of each named animal
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name at least five animals that live in the rainforest and tell you something about each — like a toucan's big colourful beak or a sloth hanging upside down in the trees?
topics.descriptionZh: 命名并识别标志性的雨林动物——美洲豹、巨嘴鸟、树懒、箭毒蛙、吼猴、金刚鹦鹉和蝴蝶——并了解它们分别生活在雨林的哪个层次（layer）
evidenceZh: 命名至少五种标志性的雨林动物，如美洲豹、巨嘴鸟、树懒、箭毒蛙和吼猴
将至少三种动物与其生活的雨林层次相匹配（例如：猴子生活在树冠层（canopy），美洲豹生活在森林地表（forest floor））
描述每种命名动物的一个显著特征
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否说出至少五种生活在雨林中的动物，并告诉你关于它们的一些特点——比如巨嘴鸟巨大而色彩鲜艳的喙，或者倒挂在树上的树懒？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rainforest Insects
topics.description: Know that rainforests are home to millions of insects — leaf-cutter ants that farm fungus, giant beetles, jewel-coloured butterflies, enormous spiders, and stick insects — and that insects are the most numerous animals in the rainforest
evidence: Name at least three types of insect or minibeast found in the rainforest, such as leaf-cutter ants, morpho butterflies, and giant beetles
Explain that insects are the most numerous animals in the rainforest
Describe one interesting behaviour, such as leaf-cutter ants carrying leaf pieces back to grow fungus
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that rainforests are packed with insects — like leaf-cutter ants that carry bits of leaf in a long line, or butterflies as big as a dinner plate?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解雨林是数百万昆虫的家园——包括会培育真菌的切叶蚁（leaf-cutter ants）、巨大的甲虫、色彩如宝石般的蝴蝶、巨大的蜘蛛和竹节虫——并知道昆虫是雨林中数量最多的动物。
evidenceZh: 说出至少三种在雨林中发现的昆虫或微型动物（minibeast），例如切叶蚁、闪蝶（morpho butterflies）和巨型甲虫
解释昆虫是雨林中数量最多的动物
描述一种有趣的行为，例如切叶蚁搬运树叶碎片回去培育真菌
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否知道雨林里挤满了昆虫——比如排成长队搬运碎树叶的切叶蚁，或者像餐盘一样大的蝴蝶？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rainforest Layers
topics.description: Know that a rainforest has four layers from ground to sky — the forest floor (dark, damp, full of decomposing leaves), the understory (small trees and shrubs in the shade), the canopy (a thick roof of treetops where most animals live), and the emergent layer (the tallest trees poking above the canopy into bright sunlight)
evidence: Name the four rainforest layers in order from ground to sky: forest floor, understory, canopy, emergent
Describe one key feature of each layer, such as the canopy being a thick roof of leaves or the forest floor being dark and damp
Explain that most rainforest animals live in the canopy because that is where there is food and light
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} draws a rainforest, can they show the four layers — the dark forest floor, the shady understory, the leafy canopy, and the tallest emergent trees poking into the sky?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解雨林从地面到天空分为四个层次——森林地表 (forest floor)（阴暗、潮湿，布满腐烂的落叶），林下层 (understory)（阴影中的小树和灌木），树冠层 (canopy)（由茂密树顶组成的厚实“屋顶”，是大多数动物居住的地方），以及露生层 (emergent layer)（穿过树冠伸入明亮阳光中的最高树木）。
evidenceZh: 按从地面到天空的顺序说出雨林的四个层次：森林地表 (forest floor)、林下层 (understory)、树冠层 (canopy)、露生层 (emergent layer)
描述每个层次的一个主要特征，例如树冠层 (canopy) 是厚厚的树叶“屋顶”，或者森林地表 (forest floor) 阴暗潮湿
解释为什么大多数雨林动物生活在树冠层 (canopy)，因为那里有充足的食物和阳光
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 画一片雨林，他们能画出这四个层次吗——阴暗的森林地表 (forest floor)、背光的林下层 (understory)、枝叶茂密的树冠层 (canopy)，以及伸向天空的最高的露生层 (emergent layer) 树木？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rainforest Plants
topics.description: Know that rainforests contain an enormous variety of plants — towering kapok and Brazil nut trees, climbing vines called lianas, colourful orchids that grow on tree branches, giant water lilies, and huge leaves that funnel rainwater
evidence: Name at least three types of rainforest plant, such as kapok trees, lianas (climbing vines), and orchids
Explain that rainforest plants grow very tall because they compete for sunlight
Describe one unusual feature, such as orchids growing on tree branches or lianas climbing up trunks
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name some plants that grow in the rainforest — like giant trees, climbing vines, or orchids that grow on branches — and explain why they grow so big and tall?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解热带雨林中包含种类繁多的植物——高耸的木棉树（Kapok）和巴西坚果树（Brazil nut tree）、被称为木质藤本植物（Lianas）的攀援藤蔓、生长在树枝上的色彩斑斓的兰花（Orchids）、巨大的王莲（Giant water lilies），以及能将雨水汇聚起来的大叶子。
evidenceZh: 说出至少三种热带雨林植物的名称，例如木棉树（Kapok）、攀援藤蔓（Lianas）和兰花（Orchids）
解释热带雨林植物长得非常高大是因为它们需要争夺阳光
描述一种奇特的特征，例如兰花生长在树枝上，或者藤蔓攀附着树干向上生长
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能说出一些生长在热带雨林里的植物吗——比如巨大的树木、攀援的藤蔓，或者生长在树枝上的兰花——并解释它们为什么长得如此高大吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: What Is a Rainforest?
topics.description: Know that a rainforest is a thick, tall forest found in hot, wet places near the Equator where it rains almost every day, creating a warm, damp environment where plants and animals thrive
evidence: Describe a rainforest as a forest that is hot and wet, located near the Equator
Explain that it rains very often in a rainforest, which is why the plants grow so tall and thick
Point to the Equator on a globe and say that rainforests are found in the hot belt near it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a picture of a thick, green jungle with huge trees and dangling vines, can they tell you it's a rainforest and explain that it's hot and rainy there almost every day?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解热带雨林是一种茂密高大的森林，分布在赤道附近炎热潮湿的地区。那里几乎天天下雨，形成了一个温暖湿润的环境，让动植物能够茁壮成长。
evidenceZh: 描述热带雨林是一个炎热潮湿、位于赤道附近的森林。
解释热带雨林经常下雨，这就是为什么那里的植物长得如此高大茂密。
在地球仪上指出赤道的位置，并说明热带雨林分布在赤道附近的炎热地带。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到一张茂密绿色丛林的图片，里面有巨大的树木和垂吊的藤蔓，他们能告诉你那是热带雨林，并解释那里几乎每天都很热且经常下雨吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Where Rainforests Are
topics.description: Know that rainforests are found in a belt around the middle of the Earth — in South America (the Amazon), Central Africa (the Congo), and Southeast Asia — and that they appear on every continent except Antarctica and Europe
evidence: Point to the Amazon, Congo, and Southeast Asian rainforest regions on a world map
Explain that rainforests grow near the Equator where it is hot and wet all year
Name at least two continents that have large rainforests
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you show {{name}} a world map, can they point to where rainforests grow — near the middle of the Earth in places like South America, Africa, and Asia?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解热带雨林分布在地球中部的环状地带——包括南美洲（亚马逊）、中非（刚果）和东南亚——并且它们出现在除南极洲和欧洲之外的每个大洲。
evidenceZh: 在世界地图上指出亚马逊、刚果和东南亚的热带雨林区域
解释热带雨林生长在赤道（Equator）附近，那里全年炎热多雨
说出至少两个拥有大片热带雨林的大洲
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你给 {{name}} 展示一张世界地图，他们能指出热带雨林生长的地方吗——即地球中部附近的地方，如南美洲、非洲和亚洲？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Classifying Rainforest Organisms
topics.description: Classify rainforest organisms into major groups — mammals (jaguars, monkeys, bats), birds (toucans, macaws, hummingbirds), reptiles (snakes, lizards, caimans), amphibians (tree frogs, poison dart frogs), insects (butterflies, ants, beetles), and plants (trees, epiphytes, ferns) — using observable features to sort them
evidence: Sort at least eight rainforest organisms into correct groups: mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, insects, or plants
State the key feature that defines each group (e.g. mammals have fur and feed milk to their young)
Explain why classification helps scientists understand and study the huge variety of life in rainforests
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looks at pictures of different rainforest creatures, can they sort them into groups like mammals, birds, reptiles, and insects, and explain why each one belongs in its group?
topics.descriptionZh: 利用可观察的特征将雨林生物归类为主要类群：哺乳动物（mammals，如美洲豹、猴子、蝙蝠）、鸟类（birds，如巨嘴鸟、金刚鹦鹉、蜂鸟）、爬行动物（reptiles，如蛇、蜥蜴、凯门鳄）、两栖动物（amphibians，如树蛙、箭毒蛙）、昆虫（insects，如蝴蝶、蚂蚁、甲虫）和植物（plants，如树木、附生植物、蕨类植物）。
evidenceZh: 将至少八种雨林生物正确分类到相应的类群中：哺乳动物、鸟类、爬行动物、两栖动物、昆虫或植物
说出定义每个类群的关键特征（例如，哺乳动物长有毛发并用乳汁哺育幼崽）
解释为什么分类能帮助科学家理解和研究雨林中种类繁多的生命
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 观看不同雨林动物的图片，他们能否将它们分入哺乳动物、鸟类、爬行动物和昆虫等类群，并解释每种动物属于其所在类群的原因？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Indigenous Ecological Knowledge
topics.description: Understand that indigenous peoples of the rainforest have developed deep ecological knowledge over thousands of years — using plants for medicine, food, and building materials, practising sustainable farming methods like shifting cultivation, and understanding animal behaviour and forest ecology in ways that modern science is only beginning to appreciate
evidence: Give at least two examples of indigenous knowledge, such as using specific plants as medicine or practising sustainable farming
Explain what shifting cultivation is and why it is less harmful to the forest than permanent clearing
Describe how indigenous knowledge and modern science can work together to protect rainforests
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that indigenous rainforest peoples know an enormous amount about forest plants and animals — like which plants cure illnesses — and that scientists are learning from this knowledge?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解热带雨林的原住民在数千年的历史中积累了丰富的生态知识——他们将植物用于医药、食物和建筑材料，实践轮耕（shifting cultivation）等可持续农业方法，并且对动物行为和森林生态的理解，是现代科学才刚刚开始领会的。
evidenceZh: 列举至少两个原住民知识的例子，例如使用特定植物入药或实践可持续农业
解释什么是轮耕（shifting cultivation），以及为什么它比永久性砍伐（permanent clearing）对森林的危害更小
描述原住民知识如何与现代科学相结合，共同保护热带雨林
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释热带雨林的原住民对森林里的动植物有着极其丰富的了解——比如哪些植物能治病——而且科学家们正在向这些知识学习？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rainforest Animal Survival Tricks
topics.description: Know how rainforest animals are adapted to their environment — camouflage helps leaf insects and tree frogs hide, bright warning colours (aposematism) signal that poison dart frogs are toxic, prehensile tails let monkeys grip branches, toucans' large beaks help reach distant fruit, and many animals are nocturnal to avoid daytime heat
evidence: Describe at least three animal adaptations such as camouflage, warning colours, and prehensile tails
Explain how each adaptation helps the animal survive (e.g. camouflage hides prey from predators)
Give a specific example for each adaptation, linking the animal to its rainforest layer
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a poison dart frog is so brightly coloured — that it's warning predators it's dangerous — or why a sloth moves so slowly that algae grows on its fur, helping it blend in?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解雨林动物是如何适应环境的——保护色（camouflage）帮助叶䗛和树蛙隐藏自己；鲜艳的颜色（警戒色，aposematism）警告捕食者箭毒蛙有毒；卷尾（prehensile tails）让猴子能紧紧抓住树枝；巨嘴鸟的大嘴巴帮助它们吃到远处的果实；许多动物为了避开白天的炎热，选择在夜间活动（夜行性，nocturnal）。
evidenceZh: 描述至少三种动物的适应性特征，例如保护色、警戒色和卷尾
解释每种适应性特征如何帮助动物生存（例如，保护色能帮助猎物躲避捕食者）
为每种适应性特征提供一个具体的例子，并将动物与其所在的雨林层次联系起来
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释为什么箭毒蛙的颜色那么鲜艳——这是在警告捕食者它们很危险吗？或者能解释为什么树懒移动得那么慢，以至于皮毛上会长出藻类，从而帮助它们更好地融入环境隐藏自己吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rainforest Food Webs
topics.description: Understand how energy and nutrients flow through a rainforest food web — from plants (producers) to herbivores (primary consumers) to predators (secondary consumers) — and that decomposers like fungi and insects break down dead material on the forest floor, recycling nutrients back into the soil for plants to use again
evidence: Construct a simple rainforest food chain with at least three levels: producer → herbivore → predator
Explain the role of decomposers in breaking down dead material and returning nutrients to the soil
Use the terms producer, consumer, and decomposer correctly
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain a rainforest food chain — like how a fruit tree feeds a monkey, the monkey might be hunted by a jaguar, and when things die, tiny organisms break them down to feed the trees again?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解能量和营养物质是如何在雨林食物网中流动的——从植物（生产者 / Producers）到食草动物（初级消费者 / Primary Consumers），再到捕食者（次级消费者 / Secondary Consumers）；同时了解真菌和昆虫等分解者（分解者 / Decomposers）会分解森林地面上的动植物遗体，将营养物质重新循环回土壤中，供植物再次吸收利用。
evidenceZh: 构建一条包含至少三个营养级的简单雨林食物链：生产者（Producer） → 食草动物（Herbivore） → 捕食者（Predator）
解释分解者（Decomposer）在分解死亡物质并将营养物质归还给土壤中的作用
正确使用生产者（Producer）、消费者（Consumer）和分解者（Decomposer）这些术语
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释一条雨林食物链——比如果树如何喂养猴子，猴子可能会被美洲豹捕食，以及当生物死亡时，微小的生物如何将它们分解，从而再次滋养树木？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rainforest Plant Adaptations
topics.description: Know how rainforest plants are adapted to their environment — drip-tip leaves channel water off quickly to prevent rot, buttress roots spread wide to support tall trees in thin soil, epiphytes (like orchids and bromeliads) grow on tree branches to reach sunlight without needing soil, and lianas climb trunks to reach the canopy
evidence: Describe at least three plant adaptations: drip-tip leaves, buttress roots, and epiphytes
Explain the purpose of each adaptation (e.g. drip-tips shed water to prevent rot)
Use the word adaptation to mean a feature that helps an organism survive in its environment
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why some rainforest trees have huge roots spreading out like wings, or why leaves have pointy tips that water drips off — that these are clever adaptations to life in a hot, wet forest?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解雨林植物如何适应其环境——滴水叶尖（drip-tip leaves）能快速导流雨水以防止腐烂，板状根（buttress roots）向四周伸展以在贫瘠的土壤中支撑高大的树木，附生植物（epiphytes）（如兰花和凤梨科植物）生长在树枝上以获取阳光而不需要土壤，以及藤本植物（lianas）沿着树干攀爬以到达树冠层。
evidenceZh: 描述至少三种植物适应性特征：滴水叶尖（drip-tip leaves）、板状根（buttress roots）和附生植物（epiphytes）
解释每种适应性特征的作用（例如，滴水叶尖可以排走水分以防止腐烂）
使用“适应性”（adaptation）一词来指代帮助生物在其环境中生存的特征
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释为什么有些雨林树木长有像翅膀一样向外伸展的巨大板状根，或者为什么树叶有让水滴滑落的尖尖叶尖——并说明这些都是它们在炎热潮湿的森林中生存的巧妙适应性（adaptations）吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rainforest Water Cycle
topics.description: Understand how the water cycle works in a rainforest — trees absorb water through their roots and release it through their leaves (transpiration), this moisture forms clouds above the canopy, and the clouds produce rain that falls back into the forest — creating a self-sustaining cycle that generates much of the rainforest's own rainfall
evidence: Describe the sequence: trees absorb water → release it through leaves (transpiration) → moisture rises → clouds form → rain falls
Explain that rainforests generate much of their own rainfall through this cycle
Use the word transpiration correctly when describing how water leaves a plant through its leaves
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how rainforest trees help make their own rain — by releasing water from their leaves, which forms clouds, which rain back down on the forest?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解雨林中的水循环是如何运作的——树木通过根部吸收水分，并通过叶片将其释放（蒸腾作用 transpiration），这些水分在树冠上方形成云层，云层产生的降雨又落回森林中——从而形成一个自我维持的循环，产生了雨林大部分的降雨。
evidenceZh: 描述这一过程：树木吸收水分 → 通过叶片释放水分（蒸腾作用 transpiration） → 水汽上升 → 形成云层 → 降雨落下
解释雨林通过这一循环产生自身大部分降雨的原理
在描述水分如何通过叶片离开植物时，正确使用“蒸腾作用（transpiration）”一词
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释雨林中的树木是如何帮助制造降雨的——它们通过叶片释放水分形成云层，这些云层再将雨水降回森林中？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Amazon Rainforest
topics.description: Know that the Amazon is Earth's greatest rainforest — spanning nine countries across South America, containing the world's largest river by water volume, and home to an estimated 10% of all species on Earth including 40,000 plant species, 1,300 bird species, and 3,000 types of fish
evidence: Locate the Amazon rainforest on a map of South America and name at least two countries it spans
State that the Amazon contains the world's largest river by volume and is home to roughly 10% of all species on Earth
Give at least two specific numbers showing the Amazon's biodiversity, such as 40,000 plant species or 1,300 bird species
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you about the Amazon — that it's the biggest rainforest in the world, spread across nine countries, with more types of animals and plants than almost anywhere else on Earth?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解亚马逊热带雨林（rainforest）是地球上最大的雨林——它横跨南美洲的九个国家，拥有世界上水量最大的河流，并且孕育了地球上约10%的物种，包括40,000种植物、1,300种鸟类和3,000种鱼类
evidenceZh: 在南美洲地图上找到亚马逊雨林的位置，并说出它至少横跨的两个国家
说明亚马逊拥有世界上水量最大的河流，并且栖息着地球上大约10%的物种
给出至少两个展示亚马逊生物多样性（biodiversity）的具体数字，例如40,000种植物或1,300种鸟类
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能给你讲讲亚马逊吗？它是世界上最大的雨林，横跨九个国家，拥有比地球上几乎任何其他地方都多的动植物种类？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Tropical Rainforest Climate
topics.description: Understand that rainforests have a tropical climate — consistently hot (25–30°C) with over 2000 mm of rainfall per year — and that this combination of heat and moisture creates ideal conditions for rapid plant growth and extraordinary biodiversity
evidence: State that tropical rainforests are hot (25–30°C) and wet (over 2000 mm rain per year) all year round
Explain that the constant heat and moisture create ideal growing conditions for plants
Compare tropical rainforest climate to the UK or local climate, noting key differences in temperature and rainfall
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why rainforests grow so well — that it's the combination of being really hot and really rainy all year round that makes everything grow so fast?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解雨林具有热带气候——全年持续高温（25–30°C），年降水量超过2000 mm——并且这种热量与水分的结合为植物的快速生长和极高的生物多样性（biodiversity）创造了理想条件。
evidenceZh: 说明热带雨林全年高温（25–30°C）且多雨（年降水量超过2000 mm）
解释持续的热量和水分如何为植物创造理想的生长条件
将热带雨林气候与英国或当地气候进行比较，指出温度和降水量的主要差异
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释为什么雨林里的植物生长得如此茂盛——即全年持续的高温和充沛的降雨是如何让万物快速生长的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Deforestation Causes & Scale
topics.description: Understand the causes and scale of rainforest deforestation — cattle ranching (largest driver in the Amazon), soy and palm oil plantations, logging for timber, and mining — and know that approximately 10 million hectares of forest are lost globally each year, with devastating consequences for biodiversity, climate, and indigenous communities
evidence: Name at least three major causes of deforestation: cattle ranching, palm oil, soy, logging, and mining
State that approximately 10 million hectares of forest are lost globally each year
Explain the impact of deforestation on at least two of: biodiversity, climate, and indigenous peoples
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why rainforests are being cut down — naming causes like cattle farming, palm oil, and logging — and say roughly how fast it's happening?
topics.nameZh: 森林砍伐的原因与规模
topics.descriptionZh: 了解热带雨林砍伐（deforestation）的原因与规模——包括养牛业（亚马逊地区最大的驱动因素）、大豆和棕榈油种植园、木材采伐（logging）以及采矿业——并知道全球每年大约损失1000万公顷的森林，这对生物多样性（biodiversity）、气候和原住民社区造成了毁灭性的后果
evidenceZh: 列举至少三个导致森林砍伐的主要原因：养牛业、棕榈油、大豆、木材采伐和采矿
说明全球每年大约损失1000万公顷的森林
解释森林砍伐对以下至少两个方面的影响：生物多样性、气候和原住民
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么热带雨林正在被砍伐——指出养牛、棕榈油和木材采伐等原因——并说明其大致的发生速度？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Nutrient Cycling in Thin Soil
topics.description: Understand the paradox of nutrient cycling in rainforests — despite lush growth, rainforest soil is typically thin and nutrient-poor because most nutrients are locked in living organisms, not the soil; decomposition is rapid in the warm, wet conditions, and nutrients released from dead material are immediately absorbed by plant roots and fungi, creating a fast, closed-loop recycling system
evidence: Explain that rainforest soil is thin and nutrient-poor despite the lush growth above
Describe the rapid decomposition cycle: dead material → decomposers → nutrients released → immediately absorbed by roots
Explain why clearing rainforest for farming fails after a few years — once the trees are gone, the nutrients are lost
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the surprising fact that rainforest soil is actually poor and thin — that the nutrients aren't in the ground but locked inside the living plants and animals, constantly being recycled?
topics.nameZh: 浅薄土壤中的养分循环 (Nutrient Cycling)
topics.descriptionZh: 了解雨林中养分循环的悖论——尽管地表植被繁茂，但雨林土壤通常很浅且贫瘠 (nutrient-poor)，因为大多数养分储存在生物体内，而不是土壤中；在温暖潮湿的环境下，分解作用 (decomposition) 非常迅速，死亡物质释放的养分会立即被植物根系和真菌吸收，从而形成了一个快速、闭环的循环系统
evidenceZh: 解释为什么尽管地表植被繁茂，但雨林土壤却很浅薄且贫瘠
描述快速的分解循环：死亡物质 → 分解者 (decomposers) → 释放养分 → 被根系立即吸收
解释为什么砍伐雨林进行农业耕作几年后就会失败——一旦树木消失，养分就会流失
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释这个令人惊讶的事实：雨林土壤实际上非常贫瘠且浅薄——养分并不在泥土中，而是锁在活的动植物体内，并不断地被循环利用？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rainforest Biodiversity
topics.description: Understand that rainforests are biodiversity hotspots — covering just 6% of Earth's land surface but containing over 50% of all known plant and animal species — and that this extraordinary richness makes them irreplaceable for global biodiversity and a priority for conservation
evidence: State that rainforests cover about 6% of Earth's land but hold over 50% of all species
Explain why this concentration of species makes rainforests a conservation priority
Give specific examples of rainforest biodiversity, such as one hectare containing more tree species than all of northern Europe
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the mind-boggling fact that rainforests cover only a tiny fraction of Earth but are home to more than half of all species — and why that makes protecting them so important?
topics.nameZh: 热带雨林生物多样性 (Rainforest Biodiversity)
topics.descriptionZh: 了解热带雨林是生物多样性热点 (biodiversity hotspots) ——它们仅占地球陆地面积的6%，却包含了超过50%的已知动植物物种——并理解这种极其丰富的物种资源使其对全球生物多样性具有不可替代的作用，是生态保护的重中之重。
evidenceZh: 说明热带雨林仅占地球陆地面积的约6%，却拥有超过50%的物种
解释为什么这种物种的高度集中使热带雨林成为生态保护的首要任务
举出热带雨林生物多样性的具体例子，例如一公顷 (hectare) 内的树种比整个北欧还要多
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释这个令人惊叹的事实：热带雨林仅占地球极小一部分，却居住着超过一半的物种——以及为什么这使得保护它们变得如此重要？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rainforest Conservation
topics.description: Know the main approaches to rainforest conservation — protected areas and national parks, reforestation and rewilding programmes, sustainable certification schemes (Rainforest Alliance, FSC), recognition of indigenous land rights as the most effective form of forest protection, and international agreements like REDD+ that pay countries to keep forests standing
evidence: Name at least three conservation approaches: protected areas, reforestation, sustainable certification, and indigenous land rights
Explain why protecting indigenous territories is one of the most effective ways to prevent deforestation
Describe what certification labels like Rainforest Alliance or FSC mean and how they help
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what people are doing to save the rainforests — like creating nature reserves, planting new trees, supporting indigenous land rights, and buying certified sustainable products?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解热带雨林保护的主要方法——建立保护区和国家公园、植树造林与生态恢复（rewilding）项目、可持续认证计划（如雨林联盟 Rainforest Alliance、森林管理委员会 FSC）、承认原住民土地权作为最有效的森林保护形式，以及诸如减少毁林和森林退化所致排放（REDD+）等通过向国家提供资金来保护森林的国际协议。
evidenceZh: 说出至少三种保护方法：建立保护区、植树造林、可持续认证以及原住民土地权
解释为什么保护原住民领地是防止森林砍伐（deforestation）最有效的方法之一
描述雨林联盟（Rainforest Alliance）或森林管理委员会（FSC）等认证标签的含义及其如何发挥作用
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否描述人们正在采取哪些措施来拯救热带雨林——例如建立自然保护区、种植新树木、支持原住民土地权以及购买经过认证的可持续产品？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rainforest Futures & Trade-Offs
topics.description: Understand that the future of rainforests depends on balancing competing needs — economic development for local communities, indigenous peoples' rights to their ancestral lands, global biodiversity conservation, and climate stability — and that there are no simple answers, requiring cooperation between governments, businesses, scientists, indigenous leaders, and consumers worldwide
evidence: Name at least three competing interests: economic development, indigenous rights, biodiversity, and climate stability
Explain why there is no single simple solution to rainforest protection
Suggest how different groups (governments, businesses, consumers, scientists) can each contribute to a better outcome
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} discuss the tricky problem of rainforest protection — that farmers need land, companies want resources, indigenous people have rights, and the whole planet needs the forests for climate — and there's no easy answer?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解雨林的未来取决于如何平衡相互竞争的需求——当地社区的经济发展、原住民对其祖传土地的权利、全球生物多样性(biodiversity)保护以及气候稳定——并且明白这没有简单的答案，需要全球各国政府、企业、科学家、原住民领袖和消费者之间的合作。
evidenceZh: 至少说出三种相互竞争的利益诉求：经济发展、原住民权利、生物多样性(biodiversity)和气候稳定
解释为什么保护雨林没有单一简单的解决方案
提出建议，说明不同群体（政府、企业、消费者、科学家）如何各自为更好的结果做出贡献
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否讨论一下雨林保护这个棘手的问题——农民需要土地，公司想要资源，原住民拥有权利，而整个地球都需要森林来维持气候——并且说明这没有简单的答案？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rainforest Products in Daily Life
topics.description: Understand how rainforest products connect to everyday life through global supply chains — palm oil is in snacks, soap, and cosmetics; soy feeds livestock worldwide; cocoa becomes chocolate; rubber is in tyres and gloves; timber becomes furniture; and many medicines originate from rainforest plants — and that consumer choices can drive either destruction or sustainable practices
evidence: Name at least four products linked to rainforests: palm oil, soy, cocoa, rubber, timber, and medicines
Explain how a product like palm oil travels from a rainforest region to a supermarket shelf
Describe how consumer choices (e.g. buying Rainforest Alliance certified products) can reduce deforestation pressure
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} check ingredient labels at the supermarket and spot products linked to rainforests — like palm oil in biscuits or cocoa in chocolate — and explain why choosing sustainable versions helps protect forests?
topics.nameZh: 日常生活中的雨林产品
topics.descriptionZh: 了解雨林产品如何通过全球供应链（global supply chains）与我们的日常生活紧密相连——棕榈油（palm oil）存在于零食、肥皂和化妆品中；大豆（soy）喂养着全球的牲畜；可可（cocoa）变成巧克力；橡胶（rubber）用于制造轮胎和手套；木材（timber）变成家具；许多药物（medicines）也源自雨林植物——并认识到消费者的选择既能导致环境破坏，也能促进可持续发展（sustainable practices）。
evidenceZh: 至少说出四种与雨林有关的产品：棕榈油、大豆、可可、橡胶、木材和药物
解释像棕榈油这样的产品是如何从雨林地区运输到超市货架上的
描述消费者的选择（例如购买雨林联盟（Rainforest Alliance）认证产品）如何减轻森林砍伐（deforestation）的压力
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能在超市查看成分标签，找出与雨林有关的产品——比如饼干中的棕榈油或巧克力中的可可——并解释为什么选择可持续产品有助于保护森林吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rainforests & Global Climate
topics.description: Understand the connection between rainforests and global climate — rainforests absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen through photosynthesis, store enormous amounts of carbon in their biomass, and generate rainfall through transpiration; when forests are burned or cleared, stored carbon is released as CO₂, accelerating climate change and disrupting regional rainfall patterns
evidence: Explain that rainforests absorb CO₂ and store carbon in their trees, acting as a carbon sink
Describe how deforestation releases stored carbon back into the atmosphere, accelerating climate change
Explain that transpiration from rainforest trees generates rainfall, and losing trees disrupts rain patterns
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how rainforests help fight climate change by absorbing carbon dioxide — and how cutting them down makes climate change worse by releasing all that stored carbon?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解热带雨林与全球气候之间的联系——热带雨林通过光合作用（photosynthesis）吸收二氧化碳并释放氧气，在其生物量（biomass）中储存大量的碳，并通过蒸腾作用（transpiration）产生降雨；当森林被焚烧或砍伐时，储存的碳会以二氧化碳（CO₂）的形式释放，加速气候变化并破坏区域降雨模式。
evidenceZh: 解释热带雨林吸收二氧化碳（CO₂）并将碳储存在树木中，充当碳汇（carbon sink）的作用
描述森林砍伐（deforestation）如何将储存的碳释放回大气中，从而加速气候变化
解释热带雨林树木的蒸腾作用（transpiration）如何产生降雨，以及失去树木会如何破坏降雨模式
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释热带雨林如何通过吸收二氧化碳（CO₂）来帮助应对气候变化——以及砍伐它们如何通过释放所有储存的碳来使气候变化恶化？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Temperate Rainforests
topics.description: Know that not all rainforests are tropical — temperate rainforests exist in cooler, wet regions like the Pacific Northwest of North America, western Scotland and Wales, southern Chile, and New Zealand — with similar features (high rainfall, moss-draped trees, dense canopy) but different species, including ancient oaks, giant redwoods, and tree ferns
evidence: Name at least two locations of temperate rainforests, such as the Pacific Northwest, western Scotland, or southern Chile
Compare temperate and tropical rainforests: both have high rainfall and dense canopy, but differ in temperature and species
Name species found in temperate rainforests, such as ancient oaks, giant redwoods, or tree ferns
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that rainforests aren't only in hot places — that there are cool, misty rainforests in places like Wales, Scotland, and the Pacific Northwest, with mossy trees and ferns instead of monkeys and parrots?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解并非所有雨林都是热带的——温带雨林存在于较凉爽、湿润的地区，如北美太平洋西北部、苏格兰西部和威尔士、智利南部以及新西兰——它们具有相似的特征（高降水量、长满苔藓的树木、茂密的树冠），但物种不同，包括古老的橡树、巨大的红杉和树蕨。
evidenceZh: 说出至少两个温带雨林的位置，例如太平洋西北部、苏格兰西部或智利南部
比较温带雨林和热带雨林：两者都有高降水量和茂密的树冠，但在温度和物种上有所不同
说出在温带雨林中发现的物种，例如古老的橡树、巨大的红杉或树蕨
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否知道雨林不仅存在于炎热的地方——在威尔士、苏格兰和太平洋西北部等地还有凉爽、多雾的雨林，那里有长满苔藓的树木和蕨类植物，而不是猴子和鹦鹉？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Asking scientific questions
topics.description: Ask simple scientific questions and recognise that they can be answered in different ways including observation, testing, and research
evidence: Ask at least three 'how' or 'why' questions about the natural world
Suggest different ways to answer a question: observing, testing, asking an expert, reading a book
Choose an appropriate method to investigate a specific question
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} wonders about something — like 'why do leaves change colour?' — can they suggest how to find the answer, whether by looking closely, doing a test, or looking it up?
topics.descriptionZh: 提出简单的科学问题，并认识到可以通过观察、测试和研究等不同的方式来解答这些问题。
evidenceZh: 针对自然界至少提出三个“如何”或“为什么”的问题
提出解答问题的不同方法：观察、测试、请教专家、阅读书籍
选择合适的方法来探究特定的问题
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}对某件事感到好奇时——比如“为什么树叶会变色？”——他们能否提出寻找答案的方法，无论是通过仔细观察、进行测试还是查阅资料？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Comparing Design Solutions
topics.description: Analyse data from tests of two objects designed to solve the same problem to compare the strengths and weaknesses of each design
evidence: Test two designs that address the same problem and collect data on their performance
Compare the results, identifying strengths and weaknesses of each design
Use data as evidence to recommend which design works better and suggest improvements
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} tests two different paper aeroplane designs, can they compare the results and explain which one flew better and why?
topics.descriptionZh: 分析为解决同一问题而设计的两个物品的测试数据，以比较每种设计的优点和缺点
evidenceZh: 测试解决同一问题的两种设计，并收集它们的表现数据
比较测试结果，找出每种设计的优点和缺点
用数据作为证据，推荐哪种设计效果更好，并提出改进建议
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 测试了两种不同的纸飞机设计，他们能比较结果并解释哪一种飞得更好以及为什么吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Modelling with Sketches
topics.description: Develop a simple sketch, drawing, or physical model to illustrate how the shape of an object helps it function as needed to solve a given problem
evidence: Create a sketch, drawing, or physical model of a design solution
Explain how the shape or structure of the design helps solve the problem
Relate the model to the real-world problem it addresses
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw or build a model to show how they'd design something — like a boat shape that floats well — and explain why the shape matters?
topics.descriptionZh: 绘制简单的草图、图画或制作实物模型 (physical model)，以说明物体的形状如何帮助其发挥所需功能，从而解决给定的问题。
evidenceZh: 为设计解决方案制作草图、图画或实物模型
解释设计的形状或结构如何帮助解决问题
将模型与其解决的实际问题联系起来
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否绘制草图或搭建模型来展示他们的设计——比如设计一个能良好漂浮的船体形状——并解释为什么这个形状很重要？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Observing with simple equipment
topics.description: Observe closely using simple equipment such as hand lenses, and use observations to describe, compare, and identify things
evidence: Use a hand lens or other simple equipment to make detailed observations
Describe observations using specific vocabulary (colour, shape, size, texture, pattern)
Compare two objects based on careful observation, noting similarities and differences
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} use a magnifying glass to look carefully at something like a leaf or an insect and describe in detail what they see?
topics.nameZh: 使用简单器材进行观察
topics.descriptionZh: 使用手持放大镜等简单器材进行近距离观察，并利用观察结果来描述、比较和识别事物
evidenceZh: 使用手持放大镜或其他简单器材进行细致观察
使用特定词汇（颜色、形状、大小、质地、纹理）描述观察结果
基于细致观察比较两个物体，指出它们的相似之处与不同之处
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否使用放大镜仔细观察树叶或昆虫等事物，并详细描述他们所看到的内容？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Recording Data
topics.description: Gather and record data using simple methods such as tables, tally charts, and drawings to help answer questions
evidence: Record observations and measurements in a simple table or tally chart
Use drawings or labelled diagrams to record what was observed
Explain how the recorded data helps answer the original question
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} collect information during an experiment — like counting, measuring, or drawing — and put it into a simple table or chart?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用简单的方法（如表格 (tables)、正字图 (tally charts) 和绘画）收集和记录数据，以帮助回答问题。
evidenceZh: 在简单的表格 (table) 或正字图 (tally chart) 中记录观察结果和测量数据
使用绘画或标注图示 (labelled diagrams) 来记录观察到的内容
解释记录的数据如何帮助回答最初的问题
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否在实验过程中收集信息——例如计数、测量或绘画——并将其整理成简单的表格 (table) 或图表 (chart)？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Simple tests and experiments
topics.description: Perform simple tests and use observations and ideas to suggest answers to questions
evidence: Carry out a simple test with one thing changing at a time
Observe what happens and describe the result
Use the result to suggest an answer to the original question
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} do a simple experiment — like testing which paper towel absorbs the most water — and use what they find out to answer the question?
topics.descriptionZh: 进行简单的测试，并利用观察结果和想法为问题提出解答。
evidenceZh: 每次只改变一个条件（变量）进行简单的测试
观察发生的情况并描述结果
利用结果为最初的问题提出解答
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否做一个简单的实验——比如测试哪种纸巾吸水最多——并利用他们的发现来回答问题？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Changing Your Mind with Evidence
topics.description: Be willing to change your mind when evidence doesn't support your prediction — a result that surprises you is more valuable than one that confirms what you already thought
evidence: belief revision in children research (PMC 2020)
hypothesis testing and argumentation from evidence in young children
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} predicts what will happen in an experiment and gets a different result, do they accept the evidence rather than deciding the experiment must have gone wrong?
topics.descriptionZh: 当证据不支持你的预测时，要乐于改变自己的想法——一个让你感到意外的结果，往往比一个证实你原有想法的结果更有价值。
evidenceZh: 儿童信念修正研究 (belief revision in children research, PMC 2020)
幼儿基于证据的假设检验与论证 (hypothesis testing and argumentation from evidence in young children)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 预测了实验中会发生什么，却得到了不同的结果，他们会接受证据，而不是认定实验肯定出错了吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Observation vs Interpretation
topics.description: Notice the difference between what you observed and what you think it means — 'the ice melted' is an observation; 'the ice melted because of the heat' is an interpretation
evidence: observation vs interpretation in primary science
BERA: children's observation skills in nature
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} does a science activity, can they tell the difference between what they actually saw or measured — and what they think caused it or what it means?
topics.descriptionZh: 注意区分你观察到的事实和你认为的含义——“冰融化了”是观察 (Observation)；“冰因为受热而融化”是解释 (Interpretation)。
evidenceZh: 小学科学中的观察与解释 (observation vs interpretation in primary science)
BERA：儿童在自然中的观察技能 (BERA: children's observation skills in nature)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 进行科学活动时，他们能否区分自己实际看到或测量到的事实，与他们认为是原因或含义的解释？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Classifying living things
topics.description: Gather, record, classify, and present data in a variety of ways including tables, bar charts, labelled diagrams, and keys
evidence: Organise data into a clear table with appropriate headings
Create a bar chart or pictogram from collected data
Use labelled diagrams and classification keys to present findings
topics.assessmentPrompt: After doing an experiment, can {{name}} put their results into a neat table, draw a bar chart, and add labels to a diagram to show what they found?
topics.descriptionZh: 收集、记录、分类并以多种方式呈现数据，包括表格（tables）、柱状图（bar charts）、带标签的示意图（labelled diagrams）和检索表（keys）
evidenceZh: 将数据整理成带有适当标题的清晰表格
根据收集到的数据制作柱状图或象形图
使用带标签的示意图和分类检索表来展示研究结果
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在完成实验后，{{name}}能把实验结果整理成整齐的表格，绘制柱状图，并在示意图上添加标签来展示他们的发现吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Could there be another explanation?
topics.description: For any result, ask: is there another explanation? — the first explanation that fits isn't always the right one, and good scientists actively look for alternatives
evidence: prompts to consider alternative possible worlds research (6-7 year olds)
scientific thinking promotes critical thinking (MDPI 2025)
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} comes up with an explanation for something they observed, do they try to think of at least one other possible explanation before deciding they've found the answer?
topics.descriptionZh: 面对任何结果，都要问一问：会不会还有其他解释？——第一个看似合理的解释不一定就是正确的，优秀的科学家会积极寻找其他可能的解释。
evidenceZh: 促使考虑其他可能世界（alternative possible worlds）的研究（6-7岁儿童）
科学思维促进批判性思维（MDPI 2025）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 对他们观察到的现象提出解释时，在认定找到答案之前，他们是否会尝试想出至少一个其他的解释？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Drawing conclusions from evidence
topics.description: Report on findings from enquiries using oral and written explanations, draw simple conclusions, make predictions, and suggest improvements
evidence: Write or present a clear report of findings from an investigation
Draw a conclusion that answers the original question, supported by data
Make a prediction for a new situation based on the results, and suggest improvements to the method
topics.assessmentPrompt: After finishing an experiment, can {{name}} explain what they found out, what it means, what they'd predict for next time, and how they could improve the test?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用口头和书面解释报告探究的发现，得出简单结论，进行预测，并提出改进建议
evidenceZh: 撰写或展示清晰的探究发现报告
得出有数据支持的结论以回答最初的问题
根据结果对新情况做出预测并对方法提出改进建议
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 完成实验后，{{name}}能解释他们发现了什么、这意味着什么、下次会预测什么，以及如何改进测试吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Fair testing
topics.description: Set up simple practical enquiries, comparative tests, and fair tests, understanding the importance of changing only one variable at a time
evidence: Explain what makes a test 'fair' (only one variable changes, everything else stays the same)
Identify the variable to change, the variable to measure, and the variables to keep the same
Set up and carry out a comparative or fair test with support
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to find out which soil is best for growing beans, can they set up a fair test where only the soil changes and everything else stays the same?
topics.descriptionZh: 设计简单的实践探究、对比实验和公平实验，理解每次只改变一个变量（variable）的重要性
evidenceZh: 解释什么使实验“公平”（只有一个变量改变，其他所有条件保持不变）
识别需要改变的变量（自变量）、需要测量的变量（因变量）以及需要保持不变的变量（控制变量）
在指导下设计并开展对比或公平实验
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}想知道哪种土壤最适合种植豆子，他们能否设计一个公平实验，确保只有土壤条件改变，而其他所有条件都保持不变？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Measuring accurately
topics.description: Make systematic and careful observations, take accurate measurements using standard units and equipment including thermometers and data loggers
evidence: Use at least three types of measuring equipment correctly (ruler, thermometer, measuring jug, scales)
Read measurements in standard units (cm, ml, °C, g) with reasonable accuracy
Make systematic observations by following a planned method consistently
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} use a thermometer to measure temperature accurately, read a ruler in centimetres, and record measurements carefully during an experiment?
topics.descriptionZh: 进行系统和细致的观察，使用标准单位和设备（包括温度计 (thermometer) 和数据记录仪 (data loggers)）进行准确测量。
evidenceZh: 正确使用至少三种测量设备（直尺 (ruler)、温度计 (thermometer)、量杯 (measuring jug)、秤 (scales)）
以合理的准确度读取标准单位（厘米 (cm)、毫升 (ml)、摄氏度 (°C)、克 (g)）的测量值
始终遵循计划的方法进行系统性观察
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否在实验中使用温度计 (thermometer) 准确测量温度、以厘米 (cm) 为单位读取直尺 (ruler) 刻度，并仔细记录测量数据？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Using evidence to answer questions
topics.description: Identify differences, similarities, or changes related to scientific ideas and use straightforward scientific evidence to answer questions or support findings
evidence: Identify at least one pattern (similarity, difference, or trend) in a set of scientific data
Explain how the pattern relates to the scientific idea being investigated
Use specific data points as evidence when answering a scientific question
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} looks at their experiment results, can they spot patterns — like things that are similar, different, or changing — and use the evidence to back up their answer?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别与科学概念相关的差异、相似性或变化，并运用直观的科学证据来回答问题或支持结论
evidenceZh: 识别一组科学数据中的至少一个规律（pattern：相似性、差异性或趋势）
解释该规律与所研究的科学概念之间的关系
在回答科学问题时，使用具体的数据点（data points）作为证据
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 查看实验结果时，他们能否发现规律——比如事物是相似、不同还是正在发生变化——并运用证据来支持自己的答案？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Comparing Possible Solutions
topics.description: Generate and compare multiple possible solutions to a problem based on how well each is likely to meet the criteria and constraints
evidence: Generate at least three possible solutions to a defined design problem
Compare solutions against the specified criteria and constraints
Select the most promising solution with reasoning for the choice
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} brainstorm several different solutions to a design challenge and then compare them to decide which one best meets the requirements?
topics.descriptionZh: 根据每个方案满足标准（criteria）和约束条件（constraints）的可能程度，生成并比较解决问题的多个可能方案。
evidenceZh: 针对已定义的设计问题（design problem）生成至少三个可能的解决方案
根据指定的标准（criteria）和约束条件（constraints）对解决方案进行比较
选择最有前景的解决方案，并说明选择的理由
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否针对设计挑战（design challenge）进行头脑风暴，想出几种不同的解决方案，然后对它们进行比较，以决定哪一个最符合要求？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Correlation vs Causation
topics.description: Two things happening together doesn't mean one caused the other — recognise the difference between correlation and causation before drawing conclusions
evidence: developmental changes in children's recognition of evidence relevance to causal explanations
causal learning research
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} noticed that children who eat breakfast tend to do better at school, would they understand that breakfast might not be the cause — there could be another reason both things are true?
topics.nameZh: 相关性 vs 因果性 (Correlation vs Causation)
topics.descriptionZh: 两件事同时发生并不意味着其中一件导致了另一件——在得出结论之前，要认识到相关性（correlation）与因果性（causation）的区别。
evidenceZh: 儿童对证据与因果解释相关性的认知发展变化
因果学习研究（causal learning research）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 注意到吃早餐的孩子往往在学校表现更好，他们能理解早餐可能并不是原因——可能有其他原因使得这两件事同时成立吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Fair testing (age 8+)
topics.description: Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved
evidence: Plan a fair test of a prototype with clearly identified variables to control
Carry out the test and identify failure points or weaknesses in the design
Propose specific improvements based on test results and retest
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} builds and tests a prototype, can they run a fair test, find what didn't work, and figure out how to make it better?
topics.descriptionZh: 计划并执行公平测试（fair test），在测试中控制变量（variables）并考虑失败点（failure points），以识别模型或原型（prototype）中可以改进的方面
evidenceZh: 计划对原型（prototype）进行公平测试，明确需要控制的变量（variables）
执行测试并识别设计中的失败点（failure points）或薄弱环节
根据测试结果提出具体的改进方案并进行重新测试
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 制作并测试原型（prototype）时，他们能进行公平测试、找出不起作用的地方，并想出改进的方法吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Simple Design Problems
topics.description: Define a simple design problem reflecting a need or want that includes specified criteria for success and constraints on materials, time, or cost
evidence: Define a design problem by describing the need or want it addresses
Specify at least two criteria for a successful solution (e.g. must hold X weight, must cost less than Y)
Identify constraints such as available materials, time limits, or cost
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} clearly state what problem they're trying to solve with a design, what would make it successful, and what limits they have on materials or time?
topics.descriptionZh: 定义一个反映实际需求或愿望的简单设计问题，其中包含明确的成功标准以及对材料、时间或成本的限制条件。
evidenceZh: 通过描述该问题所满足的需求或愿望来定义设计问题
明确至少两项成功方案的标准（例如：必须承受X重量，成本必须低于Y）
识别可用材料、时间期限或成本等限制条件
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否清晰说明他们试图通过设计解决什么问题、什么样的结果才算成功，以及他们在材料或时间方面有哪些限制？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Accurate Measurement
topics.description: Take measurements with increasing accuracy and precision using a range of scientific equipment, taking repeat readings when appropriate
evidence: Use scientific equipment (scales, thermometers, measuring cylinders, stopwatches) with increasing precision
Explain why repeat readings improve reliability and take at least three readings
Identify and deal with anomalous results (measurements that don't fit the pattern)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} measure things precisely during experiments, know when to take repeat readings for reliability, and spot when a measurement seems wrong?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用各种科学设备进行测量，不断提高测量的准确性和精确度，并在必要时进行重复测量。
evidenceZh: 越来越精确地使用科学设备（如秤、温度计、量筒、秒表）进行测量
解释为什么重复测量能提高可靠性，并至少进行三次测量
识别并处理异常结果（不符合规律的测量值）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能在实验中精确测量物体，知道何时需要重复测量以保证可靠性，并能发现看似错误的测量结果吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Classifying living things (age 9+)
topics.description: Record data and results of increasing complexity using scientific diagrams, classification keys, tables, scatter graphs, bar and line graphs
evidence: Choose and create an appropriate graph type for the data (bar chart, line graph, scatter graph)
Draw graphs with correctly labelled axes, appropriate scales, and accurate plotting
Use classification keys and scientific diagrams to present complex findings
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} choose the right type of graph for their data — a bar chart for categories or a line graph for continuous data — and draw it accurately?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用科学图表、分类检索表 (classification keys)、表格、散点图 (scatter graphs)、柱状图 (bar graphs) 和折线图 (line graphs) 记录日益复杂的数据与结果。
evidenceZh: 为数据选择并绘制合适的图表类型（柱状图 (bar chart)、折线图 (line graph)、散点图 (scatter graph)）
绘制图表，确保坐标轴标注正确 (axes)、比例尺合适 (scales) 且数据描绘准确 (plotting)
使用分类检索表 (classification keys) 和科学图表展示复杂的研究结果
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否为他们的数据选择合适的图表类型——分类数据用柱状图 (bar chart)，连续数据用折线图 (line graph)——并准确绘制出来？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Controlling variables
topics.description: Plan different types of scientific enquiries to answer questions, recognising and controlling variables where necessary
evidence: Independently plan an investigation identifying the independent, dependent, and controlled variables
Choose the appropriate type of enquiry for the question (fair test, observation over time, pattern seeking, research)
Explain why controlling variables is essential for valid results
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} plan their own experiment from scratch — deciding what to test, what to measure, what to keep the same, and how many times to repeat it?
topics.descriptionZh: 规划不同类型的科学探究来解答问题，并在必要时识别和控制变量
evidenceZh: 独立设计探究方案，识别自变量、因变量和控制变量
为问题选择合适的探究类型（公平测试、长期观察、寻找规律、查阅资料）
解释为什么控制变量对于获得有效结果至关重要
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否从零开始独立设计自己的实验——决定测试什么、测量什么、保持什么条件不变，以及需要重复多少次？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Drawing conclusions from evidence (age 9+)
topics.description: Report and present findings including conclusions, causal relationships, explanations, and a degree of trust in results using oral and written forms
evidence: Present findings clearly in written and oral form with appropriate scientific vocabulary
Identify causal relationships (X caused Y because...) supported by evidence
Discuss the degree of trust in results, considering sample size, repeat readings, and possible errors
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} write up or present their experiment results, explain what caused what, and discuss how confident they are in their findings?
topics.nameZh: 从证据中得出结论（9岁及以上）
topics.descriptionZh: 使用口头和书面形式报告和展示研究发现，包括结论、因果关系（causal relationships）、解释以及对结果的可信度（degree of trust）评估。
evidenceZh: 使用恰当的科学词汇，以书面和口头形式清晰地展示研究发现。
识别由证据支持的因果关系（causal relationships，例如X导致Y，因为...）。
讨论对结果的可信度，需考虑样本量（sample size）、重复读数（repeat readings）以及可能的误差（errors）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否撰写或展示其实验结果，解释其中的因果关系（causal relationships），并讨论他们对其发现的置信度（confidence）？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Evidence Supporting Ideas
