topics.description: Identify scientific evidence that has been used to support or refute ideas or arguments, evaluating the strength of evidence
evidence: Distinguish between a claim and the evidence supporting it
Evaluate whether evidence is strong (fair test, multiple trials) or weak (single observation, no controls)
Identify when evidence supports or refutes a scientific idea and explain why
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads a science claim — like 'plants grow faster with music' — can they evaluate whether the evidence actually supports it or if the test wasn't fair?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别用于支持或反驳观点或论点的科学证据（scientific evidence），并评估证据的强度。
evidenceZh: 区分主张（claim）和支持该主张的证据
评估证据是强（如公平测试 fair test、多次试验 multiple trials）还是弱（如单次观察 single observation、无对照组 no controls）
识别证据何时支持或反驳科学观点，并解释原因
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当 {{name}} 阅读一个科学主张（science claim）——例如‘听音乐能让植物长得更快’——时，他们能评估证据是否真的支持该主张，或者判断该测试是否公平吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Fair testing (age 9+)
topics.description: Use test results to make predictions and set up further comparative and fair tests to investigate new questions
evidence: Use results from an investigation to make a specific, testable prediction
Design a follow-up test to verify the prediction
Explain the reasoning linking the original results to the new prediction
topics.assessmentPrompt: After getting results from one experiment, can {{name}} use the pattern to predict what would happen in a new situation and then design a follow-up test to check?
topics.descriptionZh: 利用测试结果进行预测，并设计进一步的对比测试（comparative tests）和公平测试来探究新问题
evidenceZh: 利用探究结果做出具体、可验证的预测（testable prediction）
设计后续测试（follow-up test）以验证该预测
解释将原始结果与新预测联系起来的推理过程
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在获得一次实验的结果后，{{name}} 能否利用其中的规律来预测在新情况下会发生什么，并设计一个后续测试来进行验证？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Science Can Be Revised
topics.description: Scientific knowledge is provisional — it is the best current explanation based on available evidence, and it can and should be revised when better evidence arrives
evidence: Give an example of a scientific idea that changed when new evidence was found — e.g. people once thought the Sun orbited the Earth
Explain that scientists update their ideas when experiments give unexpected results, and that this is a strength not a weakness
Describe why it is important to keep testing ideas rather than just accepting them because an expert said so
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} understand that scientific facts can be revised as new discoveries are made — and that this is science working properly, not a sign that scientists were wrong?
topics.nameZh: 科学知识可以不断修正
topics.descriptionZh: 科学知识是暂时性的（provisional）——它是基于现有证据得出的当前最佳解释，当有更好的证据出现时，它可以而且应该被修正。
evidenceZh: 举一个科学观点在发现新证据后发生改变的例子——例如，人们曾经认为太阳绕着地球转。
解释当实验得出意想不到的结果时，科学家会更新他们的观点，并说明这是科学的优势，而不是弱点。
描述为什么不断验证观点很重要，而不是仅仅因为专家说了就盲目接受。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否理解科学事实可以随着新发现而被修正——并且这是科学正常运作的表现，而不是说明科学家犯了错？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Controlling variables (age 11+)
topics.description: Form a testable scientific hypothesis linking an independent variable to a predicted outcome, plan a full investigation identifying independent, dependent, and control variables, sample size, and risk assessment
evidence: Writes a hypothesis in the form 'I predict that [IV] will affect [DV] because...' supported by scientific reasoning
Identifies and labels the independent variable, dependent variable, and at least three control variables
Plans repeat readings and an appropriate sample size, and identifies relevant hazards with control measures
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wanted to investigate whether temperature affects how quickly sugar dissolves, could they write a clear prediction, state exactly what they would change and measure, list three things to keep the same, and identify any safety steps?
topics.descriptionZh: 提出可验证的科学假设，将自变量（independent variable）与预期结果联系起来；规划完整的探究方案，明确自变量、因变量（dependent variable）和控制变量（control variables）、样本量（sample size）以及风险评估（risk assessment）。
evidenceZh: 以‘我预测[自变量]会影响[因变量]，因为……’的形式写出假设，并提供科学推理支持
识别并标明自变量、因变量以及至少三个控制变量
规划重复测量（repeat readings）和合适的样本量，并识别相关危害及相应的控制措施
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 想探究温度是否影响糖溶解的速度，他们能写出清晰的预测，准确说明要改变和测量的内容，列出三项需要保持不变的因素，并识别出相关的安全步骤吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Repeated tests for reliability
topics.description: Distinguish between precision (consistency of repeated readings) and accuracy (closeness to true value), use significant figures and standard form correctly, and choose and use appropriate measuring instruments to minimise uncertainty
evidence: Explains the distinction between precision and accuracy with examples
Rounds measurements to an appropriate number of significant figures
Selects a measuring instrument with appropriate resolution for the context (e.g. choosing a 10 ml measuring cylinder rather than a 1-litre measuring jug for a 5 ml measurement)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} weighed the same stone five times and got very similar answers but they were all slightly too high, could they explain the difference between being precise and being accurate — and why having lots of repeats doesn’t always fix the problem?
topics.nameZh: 重复测试以确保可靠性
topics.descriptionZh: 区分精密度（多次测量结果的一致性）(precision) 和准确度（测量值接近真实值的程度）(accuracy)，正确使用有效数字（significant figures）和标准形式（standard form），并选择和使用合适的测量仪器以尽量减少测量不确定度（uncertainty）
evidenceZh: 能通过举例说明精密度（precision）和准确度（accuracy）的区别
能将测量结果四舍五入保留适当位数的有效数字（significant figures）
能根据具体情境选择具有合适分辨率（resolution）的测量仪器（例如，测量5毫升液体时，选择10毫升量筒而不是1升量杯）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 对同一块石头称重了五次，得到了非常相似的结果，但这些结果都稍微偏高，他们能否解释精密度（precision）和准确度（accuracy）的区别——以及为什么仅仅进行多次重复测量并不总能解决这个问题？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Drawing conclusions from evidence (age 12+)
topics.description: Identify patterns and trends in data, draw conclusions that directly address the hypothesis with quantitative reference to evidence, and evaluate the investigation by distinguishing between systematic and random errors and proposing targeted improvements
evidence: Identifies the pattern or trend in a graph or data table using specific values
Writes a conclusion that references the hypothesis, states whether the prediction was supported, and quotes numerical evidence
Distinguishes between a systematic error (affects all readings in the same direction) and a random error, and proposes a specific procedural improvement to address each
topics.assessmentPrompt: After finishing an experiment, can {{name}} describe the trend in the results, write a conclusion that says whether their prediction was right (with figures), and suggest one specific improvement that would make the results more reliable — rather than just saying 'do more repeats'?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别数据中的模式和趋势，结合证据进行定量分析并得出直接回应假设的结论，并通过区分系统误差（systematic error）和随机误差（random error）来评估探究过程，同时提出有针对性的改进建议。
evidenceZh: 使用具体数值识别图表或数据表中的模式或趋势
撰写回应假设的结论，说明预测是否得到支持，并引用数值证据
区分系统误差（systematic error，使所有读数向同一方向偏移）和随机误差（random error），并针对每种误差提出具体的操作改进方案
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 实验结束后，{{name}} 能否描述结果的趋势，撰写说明其预测是否正确（包含具体数据）的结论，并建议一项能使结果更可靠的具体改进措施——而不是仅仅说“多做几次重复实验”？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Tables, charts, and graphs
topics.description: Construct data tables with correct headings and SI units, plot appropriate graph types (bar chart, line graph, scatter graph), draw a line of best fit, and calculate the gradient of a straight-line graph
evidence: Constructs a table with column headings that include quantity and unit (e.g. Mass / g)
Selects the appropriate graph type for the data and plots it accurately with labelled axes and scales
Draws a line of best fit for linear data and correctly calculates its gradient using two points
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} collected data on how spring length changes with the weight added, could they put it in a correct table, plot it as a line graph with axes labelled in the right units, draw a line of best fit, and calculate the gradient?
topics.descriptionZh: 构建带有正确标题和国际单位制（SI）单位的数据表格，绘制合适的图表类型（柱状图、折线图、散点图），绘制最佳拟合线，并计算直线图的斜率
evidenceZh: 构建包含物理量和单位的列标题的表格（例如：质量 / g）
为数据选择合适的图表类型，并准确绘制带有标注坐标轴和刻度的图表
为线性数据绘制最佳拟合线，并使用两个点正确计算其斜率
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 收集了弹簧长度随所加重量变化的数据，他们能否将其填入正确的表格中，绘制出坐标轴标注了正确单位的折线图，画出最佳拟合线，并计算出斜率？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Writing Science Reports
topics.description: Communicate scientific findings in a structured report using appropriate scientific vocabulary, SI units, and standard notation; describe how peer review and replication contribute to the reliability of scientific knowledge
evidence: Writes a structured scientific report including aim, hypothesis, method, results, conclusion, and evaluation using appropriate scientific vocabulary
Uses SI units and standard form consistently throughout a report
Explains what peer review is and why replication by independent researchers is essential for scientific claims to be accepted
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} write up an experiment with all the right sections and scientific language, and explain why a scientific discovery isn’t accepted straight away — describing what peer review means and why other scientists need to repeat the experiment?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用恰当的科学词汇、国际单位制（SI units）和标准记数法（standard form），在结构化的报告中交流科学发现；描述同行评审（peer review）和重复实验（replication）如何提升科学知识的可靠性。
evidenceZh: 撰写包含目的（aim）、假设（hypothesis）、方法（method）、结果（results）、结论（conclusion）和评估（evaluation）的结构化科学报告，并使用恰当的科学词汇
在整篇报告中始终如一地使用国际单位制（SI units）和标准记数法（standard form）
解释什么是同行评审（peer review），以及为什么独立研究者的重复实验（replication）对于科学论断被接受至关重要
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否用正确的结构和科学语言撰写一份实验报告，并解释为什么科学发现不能立刻被认可——描述同行评审的含义以及为什么其他科学家需要重复该实验？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Moon Phases
topics.description: Observe and describe the Moon's changing shape over about a month, recognising that it goes through a repeating cycle of phases from new moon (invisible) to full moon (complete circle) and back again
evidence: Describe that the Moon appears to change shape over about a month
Name or draw at least three phases: new moon (dark), half moon, and full moon
State that the pattern repeats — the Moon goes through the same shapes again and again
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you asked {{name}} to look at the Moon several nights in a row, could they notice that it changes shape and describe the pattern?
topics.descriptionZh: 观察并描述月亮在大约一个月内的形状变化，认识到它会经历一个不断重复的月相周期，从新月（完全看不见）到满月（完整的圆盘），然后再循环往复。
evidenceZh: 描述月亮在大约一个月内的形状看起来会发生变化
说出或画出至少三个月相：新月（黑暗）、半月和满月
说明这种规律是循环重复的——月亮会一次又一次地经历相同的形状变化
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你让{{name}}连续几个晚上观察月亮，他们能注意到月亮的形状变化并描述出其中的规律吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Our Solar System
topics.description: Know that there are other planets besides Earth and that our group of planets orbiting the Sun is called the solar system — and that space is the vast area beyond Earth's sky
evidence: State that Earth is a planet and there are other planets too
Use the term 'solar system' to describe the Sun and the planets that orbit it
Explain that space is the area beyond the Earth's sky, where the planets and stars are
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that Earth is one of several planets that go around the Sun, and that this group is called the solar system?
topics.descriptionZh: 知道除了地球之外还有其他行星，我们围绕太阳运行的行星群被称为太阳系（Solar System）——并且太空（Space）是地球天空之外的广阔区域。
evidenceZh: 说明地球是一颗行星，并且还有其他行星存在
使用“太阳系”（Solar System）一词来描述太阳及其围绕运行的行星
解释太空是地球天空之外的区域，那里有行星和恒星
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否知道地球是围绕太阳运行的众多行星之一，并且这个行星群被称为太阳系？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Spotting Constellations
topics.description: Recognise a few star patterns (constellations) in the night sky, starting with the Big Dipper (the Plough), and understand that the North Star (Polaris) can be found using the Big Dipper
evidence: Identify or draw the Big Dipper (the Plough) as a pattern of seven stars
Explain that the two end stars of the Big Dipper's bowl point towards the North Star
State that constellations are patterns of stars that people have named
topics.assessmentPrompt: On a clear night, could {{name}} find the Big Dipper in the sky — or draw its shape from memory?
topics.descriptionZh: 在夜空中识别一些星星组成的图案（星座），从北斗七星（Big Dipper）开始，并理解可以通过北斗七星找到北极星（Polaris）。
evidenceZh: 识别或画出由七颗星组成的北斗七星（Big Dipper）图案
解释北斗七星‘勺口’边缘的两颗星指向北极星
说明星座是人们为星星图案所起的名字
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在晴朗的夜晚，{{name}}能在天空中找出北斗七星吗——或者能凭记忆画出它的形状吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Sun, Moon & Stars
topics.description: Identify the Sun, Moon, and stars as objects in the sky and describe basic differences: the Sun gives light and heat during the day, stars are tiny points of light at night, and the Moon can appear in both the day and night sky
evidence: Name the Sun, Moon, and stars as objects in the sky
State that the Sun appears during the day and gives us light and heat
State that stars appear at night and the Moon can sometimes be seen during the day too
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} point out the Sun, Moon, and stars and tell you something simple about each one — like that the Sun gives us light and heat?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别太阳、月亮和星星为天空中的物体，并描述它们的基本区别：太阳在白天提供光和热，星星是夜间微小的光点，而月亮在白天和夜间的天空中都可以出现
evidenceZh: 说出太阳、月亮和星星是天空中的物体
说明太阳在白天出现，并为我们提供光和热
说明星星在夜间出现，而月亮有时在白天也能看到
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能指出太阳、月亮和星星，并告诉你关于它们的一些简单特征吗——比如太阳为我们提供光和热？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: What Astronauts Do
topics.description: Know that astronauts are people who travel to space in rockets, that humans have walked on the Moon (Apollo missions), and that astronauts today live and work on the International Space Station
evidence: Define an astronaut as a person who travels to space
State that humans landed on the Moon during the Apollo missions
Describe the International Space Station as a place where astronauts live and work in orbit around Earth
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you what an astronaut is, and that people have actually walked on the Moon and live on a space station?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解宇航员是乘坐火箭进入太空的人，人类曾登上月球（阿波罗计划 (Apollo missions)），以及如今的宇航员在国际空间站 (International Space Station) 生活和工作。
evidenceZh: 定义宇航员为进入太空的人
说明人类在阿波罗计划 (Apollo missions) 期间登上了月球
描述国际空间站 (International Space Station) 是宇航员在环绕地球的轨道上生活和工作的地方
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能告诉你宇航员是什么，并且知道人类确实曾在月球上行走，现在还居住在空间站上吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Asteroids, Comets & Dwarf Planets
topics.description: Identify other objects in the solar system beyond planets: asteroids (rocky bodies mostly between Mars and Jupiter), comets (icy bodies with tails when near the Sun), and meteoroids/meteors/meteorites (space rocks that enter Earth’s atmosphere)
evidence: Describe asteroids as rocky bodies mostly found in the belt between Mars and Jupiter
Describe comets as icy bodies that develop a glowing tail when they approach the Sun
Explain the difference between a meteoroid (in space), meteor (streak of light in atmosphere), and meteorite (lands on Earth)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a shooting star, could they explain that it’s actually a tiny space rock burning up in our atmosphere — and tell you the difference between that and a comet?
topics.nameZh: 小行星、彗星与矮行星（Asteroids, Comets & Dwarf Planets）
topics.descriptionZh: 识别太阳系中除行星外的其他天体：小行星（asteroids，主要位于火星和木星之间的岩石天体）、彗星（comets，靠近太阳时拖着尾巴的冰质天体），以及流星体/流星/陨石（meteoroids/meteors/meteorites，进入地球大气层的太空岩石）
evidenceZh: 描述小行星（asteroids）为主要分布在火星和木星之间小行星带中的岩石天体
描述彗星（comets）为靠近太阳时会产生发光尾巴的冰质天体
解释流星体（meteoroid，在太空中）、流星（meteor，大气层中的光迹）和陨石（meteorite，落在地球上）之间的区别
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到流星（shooting star），他们能否解释这实际上是一块在我们大气层中燃烧的微小太空岩石——并告诉你它与彗星（comet）的区别？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Earth's Spin & Orbit
topics.description: Understand that Earth moves in two ways: it rotates (spins) on its axis once every 24 hours causing day and night, and it orbits (travels around) the Sun once every 365 days, which is one year
evidence: Demonstrate with a globe or ball that Earth's rotation causes day on the Sun-facing side and night on the opposite side
State that one full rotation takes about 24 hours (one day)
State that one full orbit around the Sun takes about 365 days (one year)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that we have day and night because the Earth spins, and that a year is the time it takes Earth to go all the way around the Sun?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解地球有两种运动方式：它每24小时绕地轴自转（旋转）一圈，产生昼夜交替；它每365天绕太阳公转（环绕运行）一圈，这就是一年
evidenceZh: 用地球仪或小球演示，地球自转使得面向太阳的一面是白天，背向太阳的一面是黑夜
说明地球自转一圈大约需要24小时（一天）
说明地球绕太阳公转一圈大约需要365天（一年）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释因为有地球自转（旋转）所以我们才有昼夜交替，并且一年就是地球绕太阳公转（环绕运行）一整圈所需的时间？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How Telescopes Work
topics.description: Know that telescopes are instruments that help us see distant objects in space, and that space telescopes like Hubble and James Webb orbit above Earth’s atmosphere to get clearer views of the universe
evidence: Explain that a telescope magnifies distant objects so we can see them in more detail
State that Earth's atmosphere blurs the view, so space telescopes get clearer pictures
Name at least one space telescope (Hubble or James Webb) and describe what it does
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know what a telescope does and why some telescopes are sent into space — like the Hubble or James Webb telescopes?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解望远镜是帮助我们观察太空中遥远物体的仪器，并且像哈勃（Hubble）和詹姆斯·韦伯（James Webb）这样的太空望远镜在地球大气层（atmosphere）之外运行，以便更清晰地观测宇宙。
evidenceZh: 解释望远镜可以放大远处的物体，让我们能看清更多细节
说明地球的大气层（atmosphere）会使视线变得模糊，因此太空望远镜能拍摄到更清晰的照片
至少说出一架太空望远镜的名字（哈勃或詹姆斯·韦伯），并描述它的作用
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否知道望远镜的作用，以及为什么有些望远镜（比如哈勃或詹姆斯·韦伯望远镜）要被送入太空？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Planet Features
topics.description: Describe a key feature of each planet: Mercury is smallest and closest, Venus is the hottest, Mars is red with rust, Jupiter is the largest with a Great Red Spot, Saturn has rings, Uranus tilts on its side, Neptune is the farthest and very cold
evidence: State one distinctive feature for at least six of the eight planets
Compare at least two planets (e.g. Jupiter is much bigger than Earth, Venus is hotter than Mercury)
Explain why Mars appears red (iron oxide/rust in its rocks)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you named a planet, could {{name}} tell you one interesting fact about it — like Saturn's rings or Jupiter's Great Red Spot?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述每颗行星的一个主要特征：水星最小且距离最近，金星最热，火星因铁锈呈红色，木星最大且有大红斑，土星有星环，天王星侧着倾斜自转，海王星距离最远且非常寒冷。
evidenceZh: 说出八大行星中至少六颗行星的一个显著特征
比较至少两颗行星（例如：木星比地球大得多，金星比水星热）
解释火星为什么呈现红色（其岩石中含有氧化铁/铁锈 (iron oxide)）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你说出了一颗行星的名字，{{name}}能说出一个关于它的有趣事实吗——比如土星的星环或者木星的大红斑？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Space Robots & Rovers
topics.description: Describe how robots and rovers have explored places humans cannot easily go — Mars rovers like Curiosity and Perseverance drive across Mars taking photos, collecting rock samples, and searching for signs of past water
evidence: Name at least one Mars rover (Curiosity or Perseverance) and state it drives on Mars's surface
Explain that rovers take photos, analyse rocks, and look for evidence of water
State why we send robots instead of people: Mars is very far away and has no breathable air
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know about the Mars rovers? Can they tell you what Curiosity or Perseverance does on Mars?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述机器人和火星车如何探索人类无法轻易到达的地方——例如“好奇号”和“毅力号”等火星车在火星表面行驶，拍摄照片、收集岩石样本，并寻找过去存在水的迹象。
evidenceZh: 说出至少一辆火星车（“好奇号”或“毅力号”）的名称，并说明它在火星表面行驶
解释火星车会拍摄照片、分析岩石并寻找水的证据
说明我们为什么派遣机器人而不是人类：火星非常遥远，且没有可供呼吸的空气
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 了解火星车吗？他们能告诉你“好奇号”或“毅力号”在火星上做什么吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Eight Planets
topics.description: Name the eight planets in order from the Sun (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune), know that Pluto is a dwarf planet, and distinguish rocky inner planets from gas giant outer planets
evidence: List all eight planets in order from the Sun
State that Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006
Explain that the four inner planets are small and rocky while the four outer planets are large gas giants
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} list all eight planets in order from the Sun — maybe using a memory trick like 'My Very Eager Mother Just Served Us Nachos'?
topics.descriptionZh: 按距离太阳的远近顺序说出八大行星（水星、金星、地球、火星、木星、土星、天王星、海王星），了解冥王星是一颗矮行星（dwarf planet），并能区分岩石质地的内行星（inner planets）和气态巨行星（gas giants）组成的外行星（outer planets）
evidenceZh: 按距离太阳的远近顺序列出所有八大行星
说明冥王星在2006年被重新分类为矮行星（dwarf planet）
解释四颗内行星（inner planets）体积较小且为岩石质地，而四颗外行星（outer planets）是巨大的气态巨行星（gas giants）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否按距离太阳的远近顺序列出所有八大行星——也许可以使用像“我亲爱的妈妈刚给我们端上玉米片”（对应英文首字母记忆法：My Very Eager Mother Just Served Us Nachos）这样的记忆技巧？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Moon's Orbit
topics.description: Know that the Moon orbits Earth approximately once a month, that it does not make its own light but reflects sunlight, and that its changing appearance (phases) is caused by how much of the sunlit side we can see from Earth
evidence: State that the Moon orbits Earth roughly once every 28-30 days
Explain that the Moon reflects sunlight rather than producing its own light
Describe how Moon phases happen: we see different amounts of the lit-up side as the Moon orbits Earth
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the Moon seems to change shape — that it’s always round but we only see the part lit up by the Sun?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解月球大约每个月绕地球公转一圈，它本身不发光，而是反射太阳光，并且其外观的变化（月相）是由我们从地球上能看到多少被太阳照亮的面引起的。
evidenceZh: 说明月球大约每28到30天绕地球公转一圈。
解释月球是反射太阳光，而不是自己发光。
描述月相是如何形成的：随着月球绕地球公转，我们看到被照亮部分的大小不同。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释为什么月亮看起来会改变形状——它其实始终是圆的，但我们只能看到被太阳照亮的部分？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Sun is a star
topics.description: Know that the Sun is a star — the closest star to Earth — and that it is at the centre of our solar system, with all eight planets orbiting around it
evidence: State that the Sun is a star, not a unique type of object
Explain that the Sun appears bigger and brighter than other stars because it is much closer
Describe the solar system as the Sun at the centre with planets orbiting around it
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that the Sun is actually a star — just a very close one — and that the planets go around it?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解太阳是一颗恒星——离地球最近的恒星——并且它位于我们太阳系（solar system）的中心，八大行星都围绕着它运转。
evidenceZh: 说明太阳是一颗恒星，而不是一种独特的天体
解释太阳看起来比其他恒星更大更亮，是因为它距离我们更近
描述太阳系（solar system）是以太阳为中心，行星围绕其运行
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否知道太阳实际上是一颗恒星——只是一颗非常近的恒星——并且行星都围绕它运行？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Changing Ideas About Space
topics.description: Understand that ideas about the solar system changed over time: ancient people believed Earth was at the centre (geocentric model, Ptolemy), until Copernicus proposed the Sun was at the centre (heliocentric model), later confirmed by Galileo’s telescope observations
evidence: Describe the geocentric model (Earth at the centre) and name Ptolemy as its main proponent
Describe the heliocentric model (Sun at the centre) and name Copernicus as the person who proposed it
Explain that Galileo used a telescope to find evidence supporting the heliocentric model (e.g. moons orbiting Jupiter)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you that people used to think the Sun went around the Earth, and explain how scientists like Copernicus and Galileo changed our understanding?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解关于太阳系的观念是如何随时间变化的：古人认为地球位于中心（地心模型，托勒密），直到哥白尼提出太阳位于中心（日心模型），后来这一观点被伽利略的望远镜观测结果所证实。
evidenceZh: 描述地心模型（地球位于中心），并指出托勒密是其主要倡导者
描述日心模型（太阳位于中心），并指出哥白尼是提出该模型的人
解释伽利略如何使用望远镜找到了支持日心模型的证据（例如，发现围绕木星运行的卫星）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能告诉你人们过去认为太阳围绕地球转，并解释哥白尼和伽利略等科学家是如何改变我们这一认知的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Gravity Pulls Things Down
topics.description: Understand gravity as a force that pulls objects towards the centre of the Earth, that 'down' means towards Earth’s centre regardless of where you stand on the sphere, and that gravity keeps the Moon orbiting Earth and planets orbiting the Sun
evidence: Define gravity as a pulling force that attracts objects towards the centre of the Earth
Explain that 'down' points towards Earth's centre, so people on opposite sides of the globe both feel pulled 'down'
State that gravity keeps the Moon orbiting Earth and planets orbiting the Sun
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why things fall 'down' and that gravity is the same force keeping the Moon going around the Earth?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解重力是一种将物体拉向地球中心的力，理解‘下’是指向地球中心的方向，无论站在球体的哪个位置都是如此，并且理解重力使月球绕地球运行、使行星绕太阳运行。
evidenceZh: 将重力定义为一种将物体吸引向地球中心的拉力
解释‘下’指向地球中心，因此地球两端的人都会感觉到被向‘下’拉
说明重力使月球绕地球运行，并使行星绕太阳运行
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释为什么物体会向‘下’掉落，以及重力与使月球绕地球运行的力是同一种力？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Life Cycle of Stars
topics.description: Understand the basics of a star’s life cycle: stars are born in clouds of gas and dust (nebulae), shine for millions or billions of years by fusing hydrogen, and eventually die — massive stars explode as supernovae while smaller stars fade into white dwarfs
evidence: Describe that stars form from clouds of gas and dust called nebulae
State that stars produce energy by fusing hydrogen into helium in their cores
Explain that massive stars end in a supernova explosion while smaller stars shrink to become white dwarfs
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that stars are born, live for a very long time, and eventually die — and that really big stars can explode at the end?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解恒星生命周期的基础知识：恒星诞生于气体和尘埃组成的云（星云 nebulae）中，通过氢核聚变发光数百万或数十亿年，并最终走向死亡——大质量恒星会以超新星（supernovae）爆发的形式结束生命，而较小的恒星则会逐渐黯淡成为白矮星（white dwarfs）
evidenceZh: 描述恒星是由被称为星云（nebulae）的气体与尘埃云形成的
说明恒星通过在其核心将氢聚变为氦来产生能量
解释大质量恒星以超新星（supernova）爆炸的形式终结，而较小的恒星则收缩成为白矮星（white dwarfs）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释恒星会诞生，存活非常长的时间，并最终死亡——而且非常大的恒星在最后可能会发生爆炸？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Scale of the Solar System
topics.description: Use scale models, diagrams, or calculations to represent the relative sizes and distances of objects in the solar system, understanding that the distances between planets are enormously larger than the planets themselves
evidence: Explain that if the Sun were the size of a beach ball, Earth would be a pea about 26 metres away
State that the distances between planets are much greater than the sizes of the planets themselves
Create or interpret a scale model showing both relative sizes and distances
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} ever built or looked at a scale model of the solar system? Can they explain why the planets would need to be spread across a whole playing field to be the right distance apart?
topics.nameZh: 太阳系的比例尺（Scale of the Solar System）
topics.descriptionZh: 使用比例模型（scale models）、图表或计算来表示太阳系中天体的相对大小（relative sizes）和距离，理解行星之间的距离远大于行星本身的尺寸。
evidenceZh: 解释如果太阳有一个沙滩排球那么大，地球就会是一颗大约26米外的豌豆
说明行星之间的距离远大于行星本身的尺寸
创建或解读一个同时展示相对大小和距离的比例模型（scale model）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否曾经制作或观察过太阳系的比例模型？他们能否解释为什么行星需要分散在整个运动场上才能保持正确的距离？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Seasonal Constellations
topics.description: Recognise named constellations visible in different seasons and understand why we see different constellations at different times of year — because Earth’s orbit around the Sun changes which part of the sky we face at night
evidence: Name at least three constellations (e.g. Orion, Ursa Major/Big Dipper, Leo, Cassiopeia)
State that different constellations are visible in different seasons
Explain that this happens because Earth's orbit means we face different directions in space at different times of year
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that you can see different constellations in winter than in summer, and can they explain why?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识不同季节可见的命名星座，并理解为什么在一年中的不同时间我们会看到不同的星座——因为地球绕太阳公转（Earth's orbit）改变了我们在夜晚面向的星空区域。
evidenceZh: 说出至少三个星座的名称（例如：猎户座 Orion、大熊座/北斗七星 Ursa Major/Big Dipper、狮子座 Leo、仙后座 Cassiopeia）
说明在不同季节可以看到不同的星座
解释发生这种情况是因为地球公转（Earth's orbit）意味着我们在一年中的不同时间面向太空中的不同方向
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否知道在冬天和夏天可以看到不同的星座，并且能解释其中的原因吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Space Exploration Milestones
topics.description: Describe key milestones in human space exploration: the Space Race (Sputnik, Yuri Gagarin, Apollo 11 Moon landing), the Space Shuttle era, the International Space Station, and current missions (Artemis programme, Mars exploration plans, commercial spaceflight)
evidence: Name Sputnik as the first satellite (1957) and Yuri Gagarin as the first person in space (1961)
Describe the Apollo 11 Moon landing (1969) with Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin
Name at least one current space programme (Artemis, SpaceX, ISS) and describe its goal
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you about the history of space exploration — from the first satellite to the Moon landing to what’s happening now?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述人类太空探索的关键里程碑：太空竞赛（斯普特尼克号/Sputnik、尤里·加加林/Yuri Gagarin、阿波罗11号/Apollo 11登月）、航天飞机时代、国际空间站（International Space Station），以及当前的任务（阿尔忒弥斯计划/Artemis programme、火星探索计划、商业航天）
evidenceZh: 指出斯普特尼克号（Sputnik）是第一颗人造卫星（1957年），尤里·加加林（Yuri Gagarin）是第一位进入太空的人（1961年）
描述阿波罗11号（Apollo 11）登月（1969年），提及尼尔·阿姆斯特朗（Neil Armstrong）和巴兹·奥尔德林（Buzz Aldrin）
说出至少一个当前的太空计划（阿尔忒弥斯计划/Artemis、SpaceX、国际空间站/ISS）并描述其目标
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能给你讲讲太空探索的历史吗——从第一颗人造卫星到登月，再到现在正在发生的事情？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Vast Scale of Space
topics.description: Describe the scale of the universe in nested layers: Earth is one planet in our solar system, the Sun is one star among billions in the Milky Way galaxy, and the Milky Way is one galaxy among billions in the universe
evidence: State that the Milky Way is our galaxy and it contains billions of stars
Explain the hierarchy: planet → solar system → galaxy → universe
Use a comparison to convey cosmic scale (e.g. if the Sun were a football, Earth would be a peppercorn 26 metres away)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how our place in the universe works — that we’re on a planet in a solar system in a galaxy among billions of galaxies?
topics.descriptionZh: 以层层嵌套的方式描述宇宙的广阔尺度：地球是我们太阳系（Solar System）中的一颗行星，太阳是银河系（Milky Way）数十亿颗恒星中的一颗，而银河系又是宇宙中数十亿个星系（Galaxy）中的一个。
evidenceZh: 说明银河系（Milky Way）是我们的星系，其中包含数十亿颗恒星
解释层级关系：行星（Planet）→ 太阳系（Solar System）→ 星系（Galaxy）→ 宇宙（Universe）
运用对比来传达宇宙的广阔尺度（例如：如果太阳是一个足球，地球就是一粒胡椒籽，距离它26米远）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否描述我们在宇宙中的位置关系——即我们身处一颗行星（Planet）上，该行星属于太阳系（Solar System），太阳系属于银河系（Milky Way），而银河系只是数十亿个星系（Galaxy）中的一个？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Why the Sun Looks Brightest
topics.description: Explain why the Sun appears much brighter than other stars: it is the nearest star to Earth, not the biggest or brightest star in the universe — understanding the difference between apparent brightness (how bright something looks) and actual brightness
evidence: State that the Sun is a medium-sized star that appears brightest because it is the closest star to Earth
Explain the difference between apparent brightness (how bright it looks) and actual brightness (how much light it gives off)
Give an example: a torch held close looks brighter than a distant floodlight, even though the floodlight is more powerful
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} understand that the Sun looks so bright because it’s close, not because it’s the biggest star — and that some faraway stars are actually much larger?
topics.nameZh: 为什么太阳看起来最亮
topics.descriptionZh: 解释为什么太阳看起来比其他恒星亮得多：因为它是离地球最近的恒星，而不是宇宙中最大或最亮的恒星——理解视亮度（看起来有多亮）和实际亮度（实际发光强度）的区别
evidenceZh: 说明太阳是一颗中等大小的恒星，它看起来最亮是因为它是离地球最近的恒星
解释视亮度（看起来有多亮）和实际亮度（发出的光量）之间的区别
举个例子：拿在手里的手电筒看起来比远处的探照灯更亮，即使探照灯的功率更大
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否理解太阳看起来如此明亮是因为它距离近，而不是因为它是最大的恒星——并且知道一些遥远的恒星实际上要大得多？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Finding Exoplanets
topics.description: Describe how astronomers detect planets around other stars using transit photometry (dip in starlight as a planet crosses) and radial velocity (Doppler wobble of the star), explain the habitable zone concept, and discuss what atmospheric biosignatures — such as oxygen, methane, and water vapour detected together — would suggest about a planet
evidence: Explains transit photometry: the small, periodic dip in a star's brightness when a planet passes in front of it
Explains the habitable zone as the range of distances from a star where liquid water could exist on a planet's surface
Describes two or more atmospheric biosignatures and explains why their co-presence is significant (e.g. oxygen + methane together suggests active life replenishing both)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that a planet the size of Earth had been found in the habitable zone of a nearby star, could they explain how astronomers detected it, what the habitable zone means, and what they'd look for in its atmosphere to decide if life might exist there?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述天文学家如何利用凌星测光法（Transit photometry，即行星穿过恒星前方时星光的微小减弱）和径向速度法（Radial velocity，即恒星的 Doppler wobble/多普勒摆动）来探测其他恒星周围的行星，解释宜居带（Habitable zone）的概念，并讨论大气生物特征（Biosignatures）——如同时检测到氧气、甲烷和水蒸气——对一颗行星意味着什么。
evidenceZh: 解释凌星测光法（Transit photometry）：当行星从恒星前方经过时，恒星亮度出现的微小、周期性下降。
解释宜居带（Habitable zone）：指距离恒星一定范围的距离，在这个范围内行星表面可能存在液态水。
描述两种或多种大气生物特征（Biosignatures），并解释它们共存的重要意义（例如，氧气和甲烷同时存在表明有活跃的生命在源源不断地补充这两种气体）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}听说在附近一颗恒星的宜居带内发现了一颗地球大小的行星，他们能否解释天文学家是如何探测到它的、宜居带意味着什么，以及他们会在这颗行星的大气中寻找什么迹象来判断那里是否可能存在生命？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Observing with Light Waves
topics.description: Explain how the electromagnetic spectrum is the primary tool of modern astronomy — different wavelengths (radio, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma-ray) reveal different phenomena, why some telescopes must be in space, and what specific discoveries each wavelength range has enabled (e.g. CMB in microwave, black hole jets in X-ray, cold gas clouds in radio)
evidence: Lists at least four regions of the EM spectrum and gives a specific astronomical object or phenomenon observed in each
Explains why some telescopes must be placed in space (Earth's atmosphere blocks X-ray, gamma-ray, and much infrared radiation)
Describes the James Webb Space Telescope or Hubble and explains which part of the spectrum each primarily observes and why that was chosen
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was told that we can't see most of the universe with our eyes, could they explain why — and describe two types of telescope that detect something other than visible light, naming what they've helped us discover?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释电磁波谱（electromagnetic spectrum）如何成为现代天文学的主要工具——不同的波长（无线电波、红外线、可见光、紫外线、X射线、伽马射线）揭示不同的现象，为什么一些望远镜必须放置在太空中，以及每个波长范围促成了哪些具体发现（例如，微波波段发现了宇宙微波背景辐射（CMB），X射线（X-ray）波段发现了黑洞喷流，无线电波段发现了冷气体云）。
evidenceZh: 列出电磁波谱（EM spectrum）中至少四个区域，并给出在每个区域中观测到的特定天体或现象。
解释为什么有些望远镜必须放置在太空中（地球大气层会阻挡X射线（X-ray）、伽马射线（gamma-ray）以及大部分红外辐射）。
描述詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜（James Webb Space Telescope）或哈勃太空望远镜（Hubble），并解释它们各自主要观测波谱的哪个部分，以及为什么选择该部分。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果有人告诉 {{name}} 我们无法用肉眼看到宇宙的大部分，他们能否解释原因——并描述两种能探测可见光以外事物的望远镜，说出它们帮助我们发现了什么？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Orbital Mechanics
topics.description: Apply Newton's laws to explain orbital motion: why orbit is continuously falling sideways rather than floating; how a gravity assist (slingshot manoeuvre) transfers momentum from a planet to a spacecraft; and why rockets need to reach a specific speed to enter orbit — with a conceptual (not algebraic) treatment of the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation
evidence: Explains that orbit is a state of continuous freefall — the spacecraft is falling towards Earth but moving so fast horizontally that it keeps missing
Describes how a gravity assist works: a spacecraft flying past a planet gains speed by 'borrowing' from the planet's orbital momentum
Explains the key insight of the rocket equation: the ratio of fuel to final spacecraft mass grows exponentially with required Δv, explaining why large rockets are mostly fuel
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why astronauts in the ISS float even though they're still close to Earth and gravity hasn't disappeared, could they explain that they're actually in freefall and describe what 'being in orbit' really means physically?
topics.descriptionZh: 运用牛顿定律解释轨道运动：为什么轨道是持续向侧方坠落而不是漂浮；引力助推（Gravity Assist / Slingshot manoeuvre）如何将行星的动量传递给航天器；以及为什么火箭需要达到特定速度才能进入轨道——并对齐奥尔科夫斯基火箭方程（Tsiolkovsky rocket equation）进行概念性（非代数）的讲解。
evidenceZh: 解释轨道是一种持续的自由落体（Freefall）状态——航天器正在向地球坠落，但由于水平方向移动速度极快，使得它始终“错过”地球。
描述引力助推（Gravity Assist）的工作原理：航天器飞掠行星时，通过“借用”行星的轨道动量来获得加速。
解释火箭方程的核心洞察：燃料与航天器最终质量的比例随着所需速度增量（Δv）呈指数级增长，从而解释了为什么大型火箭大部分由燃料组成。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果有人问 {{name}}，为什么国际空间站（ISS）里的宇航员还在地球附近、重力也没有消失，却能漂浮起来？{{name}} 能否解释他们实际上处于自由落体（Freefall）状态，并从物理角度描述“在轨道上”到底意味着什么？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Where Elements Come From
topics.description: Explain stellar nucleosynthesis: the Big Bang produced mainly hydrogen and helium; main-sequence fusion builds elements up to iron; and supernovae produce elements heavier than iron and scatter them into space — meaning the atoms in our bodies were forged in ancient stars
evidence: States that the Big Bang produced primarily hydrogen and helium, and that all heavier elements were made later in stars
Explains that nuclear fusion in main-sequence stars converts hydrogen to helium and can continue building heavier elements up to iron

Explains why elements heavier than iron require supernova explosions to form, and describes how supernovae distribute these elements into interstellar space where they become the raw material for new stars, planets, and life
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was told that the calcium in their bones and the iron in their blood were made inside ancient stars that exploded billions of years ago, could they explain the chain of events from the Big Bang to the formation of those atoms to how they ended up on Earth?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释恒星核合成（stellar nucleosynthesis）：宇宙大爆炸（Big Bang）主要产生了氢（hydrogen）和氦（helium）；主序星（main-sequence star）内部的核聚变（nuclear fusion）可以合成直到铁（iron）的元素；而超新星（supernova）爆发则能产生比铁更重的元素，并将它们抛洒到宇宙空间中——这意味着我们身体里的原子，都是在远古恒星中锻造而成的。
evidenceZh: 说明宇宙大爆炸（Big Bang）主要产生了氢（hydrogen）和氦（helium），而所有更重的元素都是后来在恒星中产生的。
解释主序星（main-sequence star）内部的核聚变（nuclear fusion）将氢转化为氦，并能继续合成直到铁（iron）的更重元素。
解释为什么比铁更重的元素需要超新星（supernova）爆发才能形成，并描述超新星如何将这些元素散布到星际空间（interstellar space），使它们成为新恒星、行星和生命的原材料。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果告诉 {{name}}，他们骨骼中的钙（calcium）和血液中的铁（iron）是在数十亿年前爆炸的远古恒星内部产生的，他们能否解释从宇宙大爆炸（Big Bang）到这些原子形成，再到它们最终如何来到地球上的这一系列事件过程？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Journey to Mars
topics.description: Evaluate the engineering and human challenges of long-duration spaceflight to Mars — radiation exposure, muscle and bone loss, psychological isolation, communication delays — and assess the current state of the SETI programme: what methods are used, what has been detected so far, and what the Fermi Paradox is
evidence: Identifies and explains at least three major challenges of a Mars mission: radiation (no magnetosphere), bone/muscle loss from low gravity, psychological isolation, and delayed communications
Describes how SETI searches for intelligent life (radio signals, laser pulses, technosignatures) and explains why the lack of detection so far is not proof of absence
States the Fermi Paradox ('Where is everybody?') and discusses two contrasting proposed resolutions
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked whether they'd volunteer for a 3-year mission to Mars, could they describe at least three serious scientific or engineering challenges that would need to be solved first — and explain why the 20-minute communication delay alone changes almost everything about how the mission would operate?
topics.descriptionZh: 评估前往火星的长期太空飞行所面临的工程与人类挑战——包括辐射暴露、肌肉和骨骼流失、心理孤立以及通信延迟——并评估搜寻地外文明计划 (SETI) 的现状：使用了哪些方法、目前有何发现，以及什么是费米悖论 (Fermi Paradox)。
evidenceZh: 识别并解释火星任务的至少三个主要挑战：辐射（无磁层 (magnetosphere) 保护）、低重力导致的骨骼/肌肉流失、心理孤立以及通信延迟。
描述搜寻地外文明计划 (SETI) 如何搜寻外星智慧生命（无线电信号、激光脉冲、技术特征 (technosignatures)），并解释为何迄今为止缺乏发现并不能证明其不存在。
阐述费米悖论 (Fermi Paradox)（“大家都在哪儿呢？”），并讨论两种截然不同的拟议解释。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果问 {{name}} 是否愿意自愿参加为期3年的火星任务，他们能否描述至少三个需要首先解决的严重科学或工程挑战——并解释为什么仅仅20分钟的通信延迟就几乎改变了任务运作方式的方方面面？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Naming the Planets
topics.description: Name the planets in our solar system in order from the Sun and use vocabulary for space — planet, star, sun, moon, satellite, orbit, solar system, galaxy, universe, asteroid, comet — applying these correctly when describing the structure of the solar system and objects we see in the sky
evidence: Name the eight planets in order from the Sun without prompting
Use 'orbit' correctly to describe the movement of planets around the Sun and moons around planets
Distinguish between a planet, a moon, a star, and an asteroid using the correct vocabulary
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name the planets in order from the Sun — and explain the difference between a star, a planet, and a moon?
topics.descriptionZh: 按距离太阳由近及远的顺序说出太阳系中的行星，并掌握太空相关词汇——行星（planet）、恒星（star）、太阳（Sun）、月球（moon）、卫星（satellite）、轨道（orbit）、太阳系（solar system）、星系（galaxy）、宇宙（universe）、小行星（asteroid）、彗星（comet）——在描述太阳系结构以及我们在天空中看到的物体时，能够正确运用这些词汇。
evidenceZh: 无需提示，按距离太阳由近及远的顺序说出八大行星。
正确使用“轨道（orbit）”一词来描述行星绕太阳运行以及月球绕行星运行的运动。
使用正确的词汇区分行星（planet）、月球（moon）、恒星（star）和小行星（asteroid）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否按距离太阳由近及远的顺序说出各行星的名称，并解释恒星、行星和月球之间的区别？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Why seasons change
topics.description: Make observations at different times of year to relate the amount of daylight to the time of year, noticing longer days in summer and shorter days in winter
evidence: Describe the pattern: more daylight hours in summer, fewer in winter
Compare sunrise/sunset times at different points in the year
Relate amount of daylight to seasonal changes in weather and nature
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} noticed that it's still light at bedtime in summer but dark much earlier in winter, and can they explain this pattern?
topics.descriptionZh: 在一年中的不同时节进行观察，将日照时长与季节变化联系起来，注意到夏季白昼较长而冬季白昼较短
evidenceZh: 描述规律：夏季日照时间较长，冬季较短
比较一年中不同时间点的日出和日落时间
将日照时长与天气和自然的季节变化联系起来
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}是否注意到夏天就寝时天还亮着，而冬天天黑得早得多，并且能解释这一规律吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Sun, Moon, and stars
topics.description: Use observations of the sun, moon, and stars to describe predictable patterns such as the sun rising and setting, the moon changing shape, and stars appearing at night
evidence: Describe the daily pattern of sunrise and sunset
Describe the pattern of the moon's shape changing over about a month
Explain that stars are visible at night and describe any seasonal patterns observed
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe patterns they've noticed in the sky — like the sun rising in the east, the moon changing shape over weeks, and stars coming out at night?
topics.descriptionZh: 利用对太阳、月亮和星星的观察，描述可预测的规律，例如太阳的东升西落、月相（月亮形状）的变化以及星星在夜间的出现。
evidenceZh: 描述日出和日落的日常规律
描述月相（月亮形状）在大约一个月内变化的规律
解释星星在夜间可见，并描述观察到的任何季节性规律
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否描述他们在天空中注意到的规律——例如太阳从东方升起、月相在几周内发生变化，以及星星在夜晚出现？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rapid earth changes
topics.description: Use information from several sources to provide evidence that Earth events can occur quickly (earthquakes, volcanic eruptions) or slowly (erosion, mountain building)
evidence: Give at least two examples of rapid Earth events (earthquake, volcanic eruption, landslide, flood)
Give at least two examples of slow Earth processes (erosion, mountain formation, canyon carving)
Use evidence from text, images, or video to support the distinction between fast and slow changes
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} give examples of things that change the Earth quickly, like an earthquake, and things that change it very slowly, like a river carving a valley?
topics.descriptionZh: 利用多种来源的信息提供证据，证明地球事件可以迅速发生（如地震、火山喷发）或缓慢发生（如侵蚀、造山运动）。
evidenceZh: 给出至少两个地球快速变化的例子（地震、火山喷发、山体滑坡、洪水）
给出至少两个地球缓慢变化的例子（侵蚀、山脉形成、峡谷切割）
使用文本、图片或视频中的证据，来支持快速变化与缓慢变化之间的区别
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能举出快速改变地球的例子吗，比如地震；以及非常缓慢改变地球的例子，比如河流冲刷出峡谷？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Earth & Space Vocabulary
topics.description: Use technical vocabulary for Earth's motion and the wider universe — rotation, revolution, axis, tilt, orbit, light year, gravitational force, atmosphere, lunar phases, waxing, waning, solstice, equinox, eclipse — and apply these when explaining day and night, the seasons, and the Moon's phases
evidence: Use 'rotation' and 'revolution' correctly to describe Earth's two distinct types of movement and explain what each causes
Use 'waxing' and 'waning' to describe the Moon's phases and explain what causes them
Apply 'solstice' and 'equinox' correctly when explaining why seasons exist and why day length varies
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between the Earth rotating and the Earth orbiting the Sun — using the actual science words 'rotation' and 'revolution'?
topics.descriptionZh: 运用地球运动与宇宙相关的专业词汇——自转 (rotation)、公转 (revolution)、地轴 (axis)、倾角 (tilt)、轨道 (orbit)、光年 (light year)、引力 (gravitational force)、大气层 (atmosphere)、月相 (lunar phases)、盈 (waxing)、亏 (waning)、至日 (solstice)、分点 (equinox)、日食和月食 (eclipse)——来解释昼夜交替、四季更迭和月相变化。
evidenceZh: 正确使用“自转 (rotation)”和“公转 (revolution)”描述地球的两种不同运动方式，并解释它们分别产生的影响
使用“盈 (waxing)”和“亏 (waning)”描述月相变化，并解释其成因
在解释四季成因及昼夜长短变化时，正确应用“至日 (solstice)”和“分点 (equinox)”
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释地球自转与绕日公转的区别——并使用“自转 (rotation)”和“公转 (revolution)”这两个科学术语？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Earth's rotation and day/night
topics.description: Use the idea of the Earth's rotation to explain day and night and the apparent movement of the sun across the sky
evidence: Explain that the Earth rotates (spins) on its axis once every 24 hours
Describe how this rotation causes day (facing the sun) and night (facing away)
Explain that the sun appears to move across the sky because we are rotating, not the sun
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that the sun doesn't actually move across the sky — it's the Earth spinning that makes it look like it does, and that's what causes day and night?
topics.descriptionZh: 运用地球自转的概念，解释昼夜的形成以及太阳在天空中的视运动 (apparent movement)。
evidenceZh: 解释地球每24小时绕其自转轴 (axis) 旋转一周
描述这种自转如何产生白昼（面向太阳）和黑夜（背向太阳）
解释太阳看似在天空中移动是因为地球在自转，而不是太阳本身在移动
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释太阳实际上并没有在天空中移动——是地球的自转让我们觉得它在动，并且正是这造成了昼夜交替？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How fossils form
topics.description: Identify evidence from patterns in rock formations and fossils in rock layers to support an explanation for changes in a landscape over time
evidence: Explain that rock layers (strata) form over time, with the oldest at the bottom
Describe how fossils in different layers provide evidence of organisms that lived at different times
Use patterns in rock formations to explain how a landscape has changed over millions of years
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees layers of rock in a cliff face, can they explain that the bottom layers are oldest and any fossils tell us what lived there long ago?
topics.descriptionZh: 通过观察岩石构造的规律（patterns）和岩层中的化石来寻找证据，以支持对地表景观随时间变化的解释。
evidenceZh: 解释岩层（strata）是随时间逐渐形成的，最古老的岩层位于最底部
描述不同岩层中的化石如何为生活在不同时代的生物提供证据
利用岩石构造的规律（patterns）来解释地表景观在数百万年间是如何发生变化的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到悬崖面上的岩层，他们能否解释底部的岩层最古老，并且其中的化石能告诉我们很久以前那里生活着什么样的生物？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The solar system
topics.description: Describe the sun, Earth, and moon as approximately spherical bodies, and describe the movement of the Earth and other planets orbiting the sun in the solar system
evidence: State that the sun, Earth, and moon are approximately spherical
Name the planets in order from the sun and explain they all orbit the sun
Describe the moon orbiting the Earth while both orbit the sun
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the solar system — how Earth and the other planets orbit the sun, and how the moon orbits Earth, and that they're all roughly ball-shaped?
topics.descriptionZh: 将太阳、地球和月球描述为近似球体（spherical bodies），并描述太阳系中地球和其他行星绕太阳公转（orbit）的运动。
evidenceZh: 说明太阳、地球和月球是近似球体（spherical）
按距离太阳由近及远的顺序说出各行星的名称，并解释它们都绕太阳公转（orbit）
描述月球绕地球公转（orbit），同时两者又共同绕太阳公转的现象
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否描述太阳系——地球和其他行星如何绕太阳公转（orbit），月球如何绕地球公转，以及它们大致都是球形的（roughly ball-shaped）？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Shadows
topics.description: Represent data in graphical displays to reveal patterns of daily changes in shadow length and direction, day and night cycles, and seasonal star patterns
evidence: Measure and record shadow length and direction at different times of day
Create a graph showing how shadow length changes throughout the day
Connect shadow patterns to the sun's apparent position and Earth's rotation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} measure their shadow at different times of day, plot it on a chart, and explain why it's longest in the morning and evening but shortest at midday?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用图表展示数据，以揭示影子长度和方向的日常变化规律、昼夜交替以及季节性星空模式。
evidenceZh: 在不同时间测量并记录影子的长度和方向
制作图表展示一天中影子长度的变化
将影子的变化规律与太阳的视位置 (apparent position) 和地球自转 (Earth's rotation) 联系起来
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否在一天中的不同时间测量自己的影子，将其绘制在图表上，并解释为什么影子在早晨和傍晚最长，而在正午最短？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Star Brightness & Distance
topics.description: Support an argument that the apparent brightness of the sun and stars is due to their relative distances from Earth, understanding the sun is a relatively close star
evidence: Explain that the sun is a star, and it appears much brighter because it is much closer to Earth
Describe how a torch looks brighter close up and dimmer far away as an analogy
Argue that differences in apparent brightness of stars are mainly due to their different distances from Earth
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the sun looks so much brighter than other stars, even though many stars are actually bigger — it's because the sun is much closer to us?
topics.descriptionZh: 论证太阳和恒星的视亮度（apparent brightness）是由它们相对于地球的距离决定的，并理解太阳是一颗距离地球相对较近的恒星。
evidenceZh: 解释太阳是一颗恒星，它看起来明亮得多是因为它距离地球近得多
用手电筒靠近时看起来更亮、远离时变暗的现象作为类比进行描述
论证恒星视亮度（apparent brightness）的差异主要是由它们与地球的距离不同造成的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释为什么太阳看起来比其他恒星亮得多吗，尽管实际上许多恒星比太阳更大——这是因为太阳距离我们要近得多吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Phases of the Moon
topics.description: Explain the phases of the Moon as the changing angle of sunlight on the lunar surface as seen from Earth, and describe how solar and lunar eclipses occur
evidence: Explains that the phases of the Moon arise from the changing geometry of Sun, Earth, and Moon, not Earth's shadow
Describes the sequence of Moon phases over approximately 28 days
Distinguishes between a solar eclipse (Moon between Sun and Earth) and a lunar eclipse (Earth between Sun and Moon)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} noticed the Moon looking like a thin crescent one night and a full circle two weeks later, could they explain what has changed and why — and describe what happens during a lunar eclipse?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释月相（Phases of the Moon）是如何由于从地球上观察到的月球表面阳光照射角度变化而产生的，并描述日食（Solar eclipse）和月食（Lunar eclipse）是如何发生的。
evidenceZh: 解释月相的产生是由于太阳、地球和月球之间相对几何位置（geometry）的变化，而不是地球阴影造成的。
描述在大约28天（朔望月周期）内月相的演变顺序。
区分日食（月球位于太阳和地球之间）和月食（地球位于太阳和月球之间）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 注意到某天晚上的月亮像一弯细细的蛾眉月（crescent），而两周后变成了一个圆盘状的满月（full moon），他们能解释发生了什么变化以及为什么吗——并能描述月食（lunar eclipse）期间会发生什么吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The solar system (age 11+)
topics.description: Describe the detailed structure of the solar system, including moons, asteroids, and comets, compare orbital periods and distances of the planets, and distinguish between planets, dwarf planets, and other bodies
evidence: Names the eight planets in order and gives one distinguishing fact about each
Describes the difference between a planet, a dwarf planet, an asteroid, and a comet
Explains the relationship between distance from the Sun and orbital period (planets further out take longer)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was making a model of the solar system, could they describe the difference between a planet, a moon, an asteroid, and a comet — and explain why planets closest to the Sun take less time to complete an orbit?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述太阳系的详细结构，包括卫星（moons）、小行星（asteroids）和彗星（comets），比较行星的公转周期（orbital periods）和距离，并区分行星、矮行星（dwarf planets）和其他天体。
evidenceZh: 按顺序说出八大行星的名称，并给出关于每颗行星的一个显著特征
描述行星（planet）、矮行星（dwarf planet）、小行星（asteroid）和彗星（comet）之间的区别
解释与太阳的距离和公转周期（orbital period）之间的关系（距离太阳越远的行星公转周期越长）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 正在制作一个太阳系模型，他们能否描述行星（planet）、卫星（moon）、小行星（asteroid）和彗星（comet）之间的区别——并解释为什么距离太阳最近的行星完成一次公转（orbit）所需的时间更短？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Why We Have Seasons
topics.description: Explain that the seasons are caused by the tilt of Earth's axis during its orbit around the Sun, distinguishing this from the common misconception that seasons are caused by changing distance from the Sun
evidence: Explains that Earth's axis is tilted at about 23.5° relative to its orbit
Describes how the tilted axis causes one hemisphere to receive more direct sunlight in summer and less in winter
Refutes the misconception that distance from the Sun causes seasons by noting Earth is actually slightly closer to the Sun in January
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why the UK is hot in summer but Australia is cold at the same time, could they explain that it's not about being closer to the Sun but about which half of the Earth is tilted towards the Sun?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释四季的形成是因为地球在绕太阳公转 (orbit) 时地轴 (Earth's axis) 是倾斜的，并澄清一个常见的误解：四季并不是因为地球与太阳的距离变化而产生的。
evidenceZh: 解释地球的地轴 (Earth's axis) 相对于其公转轨道倾斜了约23.5°
描述倾斜的地轴如何导致一个半球 (hemisphere) 在夏季接收到更多直射阳光 (direct sunlight)，而在冬季接收较少
驳斥距离导致四季的误解，指出地球实际上在一月份离太阳更近一些
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果有人问{{name}}为什么英国夏天很热而澳大利亚在同一时间却很冷，他们能否解释这不是因为离太阳更近，而是因为地球的哪一半倾斜朝向太阳？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Galaxies and the universe
topics.description: Describe the scale of the universe, including the structure of galaxies, the position of the Sun in the Milky Way, and the use of light years as a unit of distance, and appreciate why space exploration requires enormous timescales
evidence: Defines a light year as the distance light travels in one year
Describes the structure of a galaxy and states that the Sun is a star in the Milky Way galaxy
Compares the distances within the solar system with the distances between stars and between galaxies, expressing them in appropriate units
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that a star is 400 light years away, could they explain what a light year means, roughly how far that is, and why we will never be able to visit it with current spacecraft?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述宇宙的尺度，包括星系的结构、太阳在银河系中的位置以及光年作为距离单位的使用，并理解为什么太空探索需要极其漫长的时间尺度。
evidenceZh: 将光年定义为光在一年内传播的距离
描述星系的结构，并指出太阳是银河系中的一颗恒星
比较太阳系内的距离与恒星之间以及星系之间的距离，并用合适的单位表示
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 听说一颗恒星距离我们400光年，他们能解释光年是什么意思、这大概有多远，以及为什么以目前的航天器我们永远无法到达那里吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Universal Gravitation
topics.description: Describe gravity as a universal attractive force between all masses, explain that orbital motion arises because gravity provides the centripetal force keeping objects in orbit, and compare gravitational field strengths on different planets
evidence: States that gravity is a universal attractive force acting between all objects with mass
Explains that orbital motion occurs because gravity continuously deflects the path of the orbiting object
Compares gravitational field strength on different planets and explains how this affects weight
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why the Moon doesn't fly off into space but also doesn't crash into Earth, could they explain that gravity is constantly pulling it into a curved path — like swinging a ball on a string?
topics.descriptionZh: 将重力描述为所有质量之间普遍存在的吸引力，解释轨道运动的产生是因为重力提供了使物体保持在轨道上的向心力 (centripetal force)，并比较不同行星上的重力场强度 (gravitational field strength)
evidenceZh: 指出重力 (gravity) 是所有具有质量的物体之间普遍存在的吸引力
解释轨道运动的发生是因为重力不断改变绕转物体的运动轨迹
比较不同行星上的重力场强度 (gravitational field strength)，并解释这如何影响物体的重量
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 被问到为什么月球既不会飞入太空也不会撞向地球，他们能否解释这是因为重力不断地把它拉向一条弯曲的路径——就像用绳子拴着球旋转一样？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Life Cycle of a Star
topics.description: Describe the life cycle of a star from nebula through main sequence to its end state (white dwarf, neutron star, or black hole depending on mass), and relate the life cycle to the origin of elements heavier than hydrogen
evidence: Describes the main stages in the life cycle of a star similar to the Sun: nebula → protostar → main sequence → red giant → planetary nebula → white dwarf
Explains that more massive stars end as a supernova followed by a neutron star or black hole
States that nuclear fusion inside stars produces heavier elements from hydrogen and helium
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was told that the iron in their blood was forged inside a star that exploded billions of years ago, could they explain the life cycle of a star and how elements are made inside stars?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述恒星从星云 (nebula) 经过主序星 (main sequence) 到最终状态（根据质量不同，演化为白矮星 (white dwarf)、中子星 (neutron star) 或黑洞 (black hole)）的生命周期，并将该生命周期与比氢更重的元素的起源联系起来。
evidenceZh: 描述类似太阳的恒星生命周期的主要阶段：星云 (nebula) → 原恒星 (protostar) → 主序星 (main sequence) → 红巨星 (red giant) → 行星状星云 (planetary nebula) → 白矮星 (white dwarf)
解释质量更大的恒星最终会以超新星 (supernova) 爆发结束生命，随后形成中子星 (neutron star) 或黑洞 (black hole)
说明恒星内部的核聚变 (nuclear fusion) 将氢和氦聚变成更重的元素
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果告诉{{name}}，他们血液中的铁是在数十亿年前一颗爆炸的恒星内部锻造而成的，他们能解释恒星的生命周期以及元素是如何在恒星内部合成的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Basic Body Needs
topics.description: Know that the body needs food for energy, water to stay hydrated, sleep to rest and grow, and exercise to keep muscles and the heart strong — and that these are basic needs every human body has
evidence: List the four basic needs: food (energy), water (hydration), sleep (rest and growth), exercise (strength)
Explain that food gives the body energy to move, think, and grow
Describe what happens if one need isn't met (e.g. feeling tired without sleep, thirsty without water)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why their body needs food, water, sleep, and exercise — and what happens if they miss any of them?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解身体需要食物来获取能量，需要水来保持水分（补水），需要睡眠来休息和成长，需要锻炼来保持肌肉和心脏强健——并且这些是每个人类身体都具备的基本需求。
evidenceZh: 列出四大基本需求：食物（能量）、水（补水）、睡眠（休息与成长）、锻炼（力量）
解释食物为身体提供移动、思考和成长所需的能量
描述如果某一项需求未得到满足会发生什么（例如：缺乏睡眠会感到疲倦，缺乏水分会感到口渴）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么身体需要食物、水、睡眠和锻炼——以及如果缺少其中任何一项会发生什么？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Bones & Muscles
topics.description: Know that the body has a skeleton made of bones inside it that gives the body its shape and protects important organs like the brain (skull) and heart (ribcage), and that muscles attached to bones allow the body to move
evidence: State that bones give the body shape, support, and protection
Name at least three bones or bone groups (e.g. skull, ribcage, spine, leg bones)
Explain that muscles pull on bones to make the body move
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} feel their own ribs or skull and explain what those bones are protecting inside?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解人体内部有由骨骼（bones）组成的骨架，它赋予身体形状并保护大脑（颅骨/skull）和心脏（胸廓/ribcage）等重要器官，同时了解附着在骨骼上的肌肉（muscles）能让身体运动
evidenceZh: 说明骨骼赋予身体形状、提供支撑和保护作用
说出至少三种骨骼或骨骼群（例如：颅骨/skull、胸廓/ribcage、脊柱/spine、腿部骨骼/leg bones）
解释肌肉通过牵拉骨骼来使身体运动
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否摸到自己的肋骨（ribs）或颅骨（skull），并解释这些骨骼在保护内部的什么器官？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How Breathing Works
topics.description: Know that we breathe air into our lungs through the nose and mouth, that our lungs take in oxygen from the air which our body needs to stay alive, and that we breathe out carbon dioxide as waste
evidence: Trace the path of air: nose/mouth → windpipe → lungs
State that lungs take oxygen from the air, which the body needs
State that we breathe out carbon dioxide, which the body doesn't need
topics.assessmentPrompt: After running around, can {{name}} notice their faster breathing and explain that their lungs are taking in air that the body needs?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解我们通过鼻子和嘴巴将空气吸入肺部，肺部从空气中吸收身体维持生命所需的氧气（oxygen），并将二氧化碳（carbon dioxide）作为废物呼出。
evidenceZh: 追踪空气的路径：鼻子/嘴巴 → 气管（windpipe） → 肺部（lungs）
说明肺部从空气中吸收身体所需的氧气（oxygen）
说明我们呼出身体不需要的二氧化碳（carbon dioxide）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在跑动玩耍之后，{{name}} 能否注意到自己呼吸变快，并解释这是因为肺部正在吸入身体所需的空气？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Brain Controls the Body
topics.description: Understand that the brain is the body’s control centre: it receives messages from the senses, thinks and makes decisions, and sends messages through nerves to tell muscles what to do
evidence: State that the brain is inside the skull and controls the whole body
Describe the basic loop: senses send information to the brain, the brain decides what to do, and sends messages to muscles
Give an example (e.g. eyes see a ball coming, brain decides to catch it, nerves tell hands to move)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the brain does — that it’s in charge of thinking, feeling, and telling the body what to do?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解大脑是人体的控制中心：它接收来自感觉器官的信息，进行思考并做出决定，然后通过神经发送信号来指挥肌肉活动
evidenceZh: 说明大脑位于颅骨内，并控制着全身
描述基本的信息传递循环：感觉器官将信息发送给大脑，大脑决定如何应对，并向肌肉发送指令
举个例子（例如：眼睛看到球飞过来，大脑决定去接它，神经指挥手部移动）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释大脑的作用——即它负责思考、感知，并指挥身体做出反应？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Five Senses
topics.description: Explore the five senses in detail: sight uses eyes to detect light, hearing uses ears to detect sound, touch uses skin to feel pressure and temperature, taste uses the tongue to detect flavours, and smell uses the nose to detect odours
evidence: Name all five senses and match each to the correct body part
Describe what each sense detects (e.g. eyes detect light, ears detect sound waves)
Give an example of using each sense in everyday life (e.g. smelling food cooking, feeling hot water)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you blindfolded {{name}} and gave them something to smell, taste, and touch, could they name which sense they were using each time and which body part does the job?
topics.descriptionZh: 详细探索五感：视觉（sight）使用眼睛感知光线，听觉（hearing）使用耳朵感知声音，触觉（touch）使用皮肤感受压力和温度，味觉（taste）使用舌头感知味道，嗅觉（smell）使用鼻子感知气味
evidenceZh: 说出所有五种感觉，并将每种感觉与正确的身体部位相匹配
描述每种感觉能感知到什么（例如：眼睛感知光线，耳朵感知声波（sound waves））
举例说明在日常生活中如何使用每种感觉（例如：闻到正在烹饪的食物，触摸热水）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你蒙住 {{name}} 的眼睛，并让他们闻、尝和触摸一些东西，他们能每次都说出自己使用的是哪种感觉，以及是哪个身体部位在起作用吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Heart & Blood
topics.description: Understand that the heart is a muscle that pumps blood around the body through tubes called blood vessels, and that we can feel our heartbeat by placing a hand on our chest or fingers on our wrist
evidence: Locate their own heartbeat by touch (chest or pulse point)
State that the heart pumps blood through the body continuously
Describe blood vessels as tubes that carry blood to every part of the body
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find their own pulse on their wrist or neck, and explain that it’s their heart pumping blood?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解心脏（Heart）是一块肌肉，它通过名为血管（Blood vessels）的管道将血液泵送至全身，并且我们可以通过将手放在胸口或手指放在手腕上来感受自己的心跳（Heartbeat）。
evidenceZh: 通过触摸找到自己的心跳位置（胸部或脉搏点 Pulse point）
说明心脏在持续不断地将血液泵送至全身
描述血管（Blood vessels）是将血液输送到身体各个部分的管道
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否在自己的手腕或颈部找到自己的脉搏（Pulse），并解释这是心脏在泵血？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Balanced Diet & Food Groups
topics.description: Know the main food groups (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre, water) and understand that a balanced diet includes the right amounts from each group to keep the body healthy and provide energy, growth materials, and protection from illness
evidence: Name at least five food groups and give an example food for each (e.g. carbohydrates = bread, protein = chicken)
Explain what carbohydrates (energy), proteins (growth and repair), and fats (energy and warmth) do for the body
State that vitamins and minerals protect against illness and help the body work properly
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at their dinner plate, could they identify which foods give energy, which help muscles grow, and which keep them healthy?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解主要的食物类别（碳水化合物、蛋白质、脂肪、维生素、矿物质、膳食纤维、水），并理解均衡饮食包含从每个类别中摄入适量的食物，以保持身体健康，提供能量、生长所需的物质以及抵御疾病的保护。
evidenceZh: 说出至少五个食物类别，并为每个类别举出一个食物例子（例如：碳水化合物 = 面包，蛋白质 = 鸡肉）
解释碳水化合物（能量）、蛋白质（生长和修复）和脂肪（能量和保暖）对身体的作用
说明维生素和矿物质能抵御疾病并帮助身体正常运转
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看着自己的晚餐盘，他们能分辨出哪些食物提供能量，哪些食物帮助肌肉生长，哪些食物让他们保持健康吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Cells, Tissues & Organs
topics.description: Understand that the body is organised in a hierarchy: tiny cells are the building blocks, groups of similar cells form tissues, tissues combine into organs (like the heart or stomach), and organs work together in organ systems (like the circulatory system)
evidence: State that cells are the smallest building blocks of the body, too small to see without a microscope
Describe the hierarchy: cells → tissues → organs → organ systems
Give an example: muscle cells form muscle tissue, which forms the heart organ, which is part of the circulatory system
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that the body is made of tiny cells, and that cells group together to make tissues, which make organs, which make whole systems?
topics.nameZh: 细胞、组织与器官 (Cells, Tissues & Organs)
topics.descriptionZh: 了解人体按照层级结构进行组织：微小的细胞（Cells）是基本构建块，相似的细胞群形成组织（Tissues），组织结合成器官（Organs，如心脏或胃），器官协同工作形成器官系统（Organ systems，如循环系统）。
evidenceZh: 说明细胞是构成人体的最小基本单位，不用显微镜就看不见
描述层级结构：细胞（Cells）→ 组织（Tissues）→ 器官（Organs）→ 器官系统（Organ systems）
举例说明：肌肉细胞形成肌肉组织，肌肉组织构成心脏器官，心脏是循环系统的一部分
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释人体是由微小的细胞组成的，细胞聚集在一起形成组织，组织构成器官，器官再组成完整的系统？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How Muscles Move Bones
topics.description: Understand that muscles work in pairs to move bones: when one muscle contracts (gets shorter and pulls), the opposite muscle relaxes, and that some muscles are voluntary (we choose to use them) while others like the heart are involuntary (they work automatically)
evidence: Demonstrate or describe how biceps and triceps work as a pair to bend and straighten the arm
Explain the difference between voluntary muscles (we control them) and involuntary muscles (they work automatically)
Name the heart and muscles of the digestive system as examples of involuntary muscles
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} bend their arm and explain that one muscle is pulling while the other is relaxing — and that their heart muscle works without them thinking about it?
topics.nameZh: 肌肉如何带动骨骼运动
topics.descriptionZh: 理解肌肉成对工作以带动骨骼运动：当一块肌肉收缩（contract，变短并产生拉力）时，相对的肌肉会舒张（relax）；并且了解有些肌肉是随意肌（voluntary muscles，受意识控制），而另一些如心脏肌肉则是不随意肌（involuntary muscles，自动工作）。
evidenceZh: 演示或描述肱二头肌（biceps）和肱三头肌（triceps）如何成对协同工作，使手臂弯曲和伸直
解释随意肌（voluntary muscles，可自主控制）与不随意肌（involuntary muscles，自动工作）之间的区别
列举心脏和消化系统肌肉作为不随意肌（involuntary muscles）的例子
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否弯曲手臂，并解释在此过程中一块肌肉在收缩牵引而另一块在舒张——并且能说明他们的心肌是在无需刻意思考的情况下自动工作的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How the Eye Works
topics.description: Describe how the eye works: light enters through the pupil, the lens focuses it onto the retina at the back of the eye, and the retina sends signals along the optic nerve to the brain, which interprets the image
evidence: Name the main parts: pupil (lets light in), lens (focuses light), retina (detects light), optic nerve (sends signals to brain)
Describe the sequence: light enters → lens focuses → retina detects → nerve signals brain → brain interprets image
Explain that the pupil gets bigger in dim light and smaller in bright light to control how much light enters
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happens inside their eye when they look at something — how light comes in through the pupil and the brain turns it into a picture?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述眼睛是如何工作的：光线通过瞳孔 (pupil) 进入，晶状体 (lens) 将其聚焦到眼睛后部的视网膜 (retina) 上，视网膜沿着视神经 (optic nerve) 向大脑发送信号，大脑负责解读图像。
evidenceZh: 说出主要部分：瞳孔 (pupil，让光线进入)、晶状体 (lens，聚焦光线)、视网膜 (retina，感知光线)、视神经 (optic nerve，向大脑发送信号)
描述过程：光线进入 → 晶状体聚焦 → 视网膜感知 → 神经向大脑发送信号 → 大脑解读图像
解释瞳孔在昏暗的光线下会变大，在明亮的光线下会变小，以此来控制进入眼睛的光线量
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释当他们看东西时眼睛内部发生了什么——光线是如何通过瞳孔进入，以及大脑如何将其转化为图像的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Naming Major Bones
topics.description: Identify major bones of the human skeleton by name (skull, spine/vertebrae, ribcage, pelvis, femur, humerus) and explain the skeleton’s three jobs: supporting the body’s shape, protecting organs, and enabling movement with muscles
evidence: Name and locate at least six major bones or bone groups on a diagram or their own body
Explain the three functions: support (holds us upright), protection (skull protects brain, ribs protect heart/lungs), movement (bones work with muscles)
State that not all animals have internal skeletons — some have shells or exoskeletons
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} point to different parts of their body and name the bones underneath — like the femur in the thigh or the vertebrae in the spine?
topics.descriptionZh: 通过名称识别人体骨骼的主要部分（如头骨(skull)、脊柱/脊椎(spine/vertebrae)、胸廓(ribcage)、骨盆(pelvis)、股骨(femur)、肱骨(humerus)），并解释骨骼的三大作用：支撑身体形态、保护内脏器官，以及与肌肉协同实现运动。
evidenceZh: 在示意图或自身身体上，说出并指出至少六块主要骨骼或骨骼群的名称和位置。
解释骨骼的三大功能：支撑作用（使我们保持直立）、保护作用（头骨保护大脑，肋骨保护心脏和肺部）、运动作用（骨骼与肌肉协同工作）。
说明并非所有动物都有内骨骼——有些动物拥有外壳或外骨骼(exoskeletons)。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否指出自己身体的不同部位并说出其下方骨骼的名称——例如大腿处的股骨(femur)或脊柱处的脊椎(vertebrae)？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Digestive Journey
topics.description: Trace the journey of food through the digestive system: food enters the mouth where teeth break it down and saliva begins digestion, travels down the oesophagus to the stomach, passes through the small intestine where nutrients are absorbed, and waste moves through the large intestine
evidence: List the organs in order: mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine
Describe what happens at each stage (teeth chew, stomach churns with acid, small intestine absorbs nutrients)
State that the small intestine is where most nutrients pass into the blood, and the large intestine removes water from waste
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} ate a sandwich, could they describe the journey it takes through their body — from mouth to stomach to intestines?
topics.descriptionZh: 追踪食物在消化系统（digestive system）中的奇妙旅程：食物首先进入口腔（mouth），牙齿将其嚼碎，唾液（saliva）开始初步消化；接着食物顺着食管（oesophagus）滑入胃（stomach）；然后进入小肠（small intestine），在这里大部分营养被吸收；最后，食物残渣进入大肠（large intestine）并排出体外。
evidenceZh: 按顺序列出食物经过的器官：口腔（mouth）、食管（oesophagus）、胃（stomach）、小肠（small intestine）、大肠（large intestine）
描述每个阶段发生的变化（牙齿咀嚼食物、胃部分泌胃酸进行蠕动、小肠吸收营养）
说明大部分营养是在小肠（small intestine）进入血液（blood）的，而大肠（large intestine）负责吸收食物残渣中的水分
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 吃了一个三明治，他们能描述出这个三明治在身体里的旅行过程吗——从口腔到胃，再到肠道？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Types of Teeth
topics.description: Identify the four types of human teeth (incisors for cutting, canines for tearing, premolars and molars for grinding) and understand that tooth shape is linked to function, just as in other animals — herbivores have flat teeth, carnivores have sharp teeth
evidence: Name the four tooth types and describe each one's job: incisors cut, canines tear, premolars/molars grind
Compare human teeth to herbivore teeth (flat, for grinding plants) and carnivore teeth (sharp, for tearing meat)
Explain that humans have all types because we are omnivores — we eat both plants and meat
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} look in a mirror, point out their different types of teeth, and explain what each type is for?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别人类牙齿的四种类型（门齿 (incisors) 用于切割，犬齿 (canines) 用于撕裂，前臼齿 (premolars) 和臼齿 (molars) 用于研磨），并理解牙齿的形状与其功能相关，正如其他动物一样——食草动物拥有扁平的牙齿，食肉动物拥有尖锐的牙齿。
evidenceZh: 说出四种牙齿的类型并描述它们各自的功能：门齿 (incisors) 切割，犬齿 (canines) 撕裂，前臼齿 (premolars) 和臼齿 (molars) 研磨
将人类牙齿与食草动物的牙齿（扁平，用于研磨植物）和食肉动物的牙齿（尖锐，用于撕裂肉类）进行比较
解释人类拥有所有这些类型的牙齿，因为我们是杂食动物 (omnivores) ——我们既吃植物也吃肉
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否照照镜子，指出他们不同类型的牙齿，并解释每种牙齿的用途？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Circulation & Breathing Together
topics.description: Understand how the circulatory and respiratory systems work together: the lungs oxygenate the blood, the heart pumps it around the body, cells use the oxygen and produce carbon dioxide waste, and the blood carries the waste back to the lungs to be breathed out
evidence: Describe the cycle: lungs add oxygen to blood → heart pumps oxygenated blood to body → cells use oxygen → blood returns CO₂ to lungs
Explain why heart rate and breathing rate increase during exercise (muscles need more oxygen)
Measure their own resting and post-exercise heart rate and explain the difference
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why their heart beats faster when they run — and how their heart and lungs are working together to deliver more oxygen to their muscles?
topics.nameZh: 血液循环与呼吸的协同作用
topics.descriptionZh: 了解循环系统（circulatory system）和呼吸系统（respiratory system）是如何协同工作的：肺部为血液充氧（oxygenate），心脏将血液泵送至全身，细胞利用氧气并产生二氧化碳（carbon dioxide）废物，然后血液将这些废物运回肺部呼出体外。
evidenceZh: 描述循环过程：肺部为血液增加氧气 → 心脏将充氧血液泵送至全身 → 细胞利用氧气 → 血液将二氧化碳 (CO₂) 运回肺部
解释为什么运动时心率 (heart rate) 和呼吸频率 (breathing rate) 会增加（肌肉需要更多氧气）
测量自己静息和运动后的心率，并解释两者的差异
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么他们跑步时心跳会加快——以及他们的心脏和肺部是如何协同工作，为肌肉输送更多氧气的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Growing Up & Puberty
topics.description: Describe the stages of human development from birth to old age: baby, toddler, child, adolescent (puberty), young adult, middle-aged adult, elderly — understanding the physical changes that happen at each stage, especially during puberty
evidence: Name and order at least six life stages from birth to old age
Describe key physical changes during puberty (growth spurts, body shape changes, development of adult features)
Explain that puberty is triggered by hormones — chemical messengers released by glands
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how a person’s body changes as they grow from a baby to an adult to an elderly person — and explain what happens during puberty?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述人类从出生到老年的发展各个阶段：婴儿、幼儿、儿童、青少年（青春期 puberty）、青年、中年、老年——了解每个阶段发生的身体变化，尤其是青春期的变化。
evidenceZh: 说出并排列从出生到老年的至少六个生命阶段
描述青春期的关键身体变化（生长突增 growth spurts、体型变化、成年特征的发育）
解释青春期是由激素（hormones）引发的——即由腺体释放的化学信使。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否描述一个人的身体从婴儿成长到成年、再到老年时发生的变化，并解释青春期会发生什么？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Healthy Lifestyle Choices
topics.description: Understand how lifestyle choices affect the body’s health: a balanced diet, regular exercise, adequate sleep, and avoiding harmful substances (tobacco, alcohol, drugs) help body systems function well, while poor choices increase the risk of disease
evidence: Explain how regular exercise strengthens the heart, lungs, and muscles
Describe how a poor diet high in sugar and fat can lead to obesity, tooth decay, and heart problems
State at least two harmful effects of smoking (damages lungs, increases heart disease risk) or alcohol (damages liver, affects brain)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how what they eat, how much they exercise, and how much they sleep affects how their body works — and why smoking or drugs are harmful?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解生活方式的选择如何影响身体健康：均衡饮食 (balanced diet)、规律运动 (regular exercise)、充足睡眠以及避免有害物质（烟草、酒精、毒品）有助于身体各系统良好运转，而不良选择则会增加患病风险。
evidenceZh: 解释规律运动如何增强心脏 (heart)、肺 (lungs) 和肌肉 (muscles)
描述高糖高脂的不良饮食如何导致肥胖 (obesity)、蛀牙 (tooth decay) 和心脏问题 (heart problems)
说出吸烟（损害肺部、增加心脏病 (heart disease) 风险）或饮酒（损害肝脏、影响大脑）的至少两个有害影响
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释他们的饮食、运动量和睡眠时长如何影响身体机能，以及为什么吸烟或毒品是有害的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Heart & Blood Circulation
topics.description: Describe the circulatory system in detail: the heart has four chambers (two atria, two ventricles) that pump blood in a double loop — one to the lungs for oxygen and one to the rest of the body to deliver it — through arteries, veins, and tiny capillaries
evidence: Name the four heart chambers and describe the double-loop pathway (heart → lungs → heart → body)
Distinguish arteries (carry blood away from heart), veins (carry blood back to heart), and capillaries (tiny vessels where exchange happens)
Name the components of blood: red blood cells (carry oxygen), white blood cells (fight infection), platelets (help clotting), plasma (liquid)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} trace the path blood takes through the heart and body — explaining that it goes to the lungs first for oxygen, then out to the rest of the body?
topics.nameZh: 心脏与血液循环 (Heart & Blood Circulation)
topics.descriptionZh: 详细描述循环系统：心脏有四个腔室（两个心房 Atria，两个心室 Ventricles），它们泵动血液进行双循环（Double loop）——一条路线去肺部获取氧气，另一条路线去身体其他部位输送氧气——血液流经动脉（Arteries）、静脉（Veins）和微小的毛细血管（Capillaries）。
evidenceZh: 说出心脏的四个腔室名称，并描述双循环路径（心脏 → 肺部 → 心脏 → 身体）
区分动脉（将血液输送出心脏）、静脉（将血液输送回心脏）和毛细血管（进行物质交换的微小血管）
说出血液的组成部分：红细胞（携带氧气）、白细胞（抵抗感染）、血小板（帮助凝血）和血浆（液体）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否追踪血液流经心脏和身体的路径——并解释它先去肺部获取氧气，然后再流向身体其他部位？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How the Lungs Work
topics.description: Explain how the respiratory system works in detail: air travels through the nose/mouth, down the trachea, into bronchi and bronchioles, reaching tiny air sacs (alveoli) in the lungs where oxygen passes into the blood and carbon dioxide passes out
evidence: Trace the air pathway: nose/mouth → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli
Explain gas exchange in the alveoli: oxygen passes into blood capillaries, carbon dioxide passes out
Describe the mechanical process: the diaphragm contracts to pull air in and relaxes to push air out
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what happens to the air they breathe in — how it travels deeper and deeper into the lungs until oxygen swaps into the blood?
topics.descriptionZh: 详细解释呼吸系统的工作原理：空气通过鼻子/嘴巴进入，顺着气管（trachea）向下，进入支气管（bronchi）和细支气管（bronchioles），到达肺部微小的气囊（肺泡 alveoli），在这里氧气进入血液，二氧化碳排出体外。
evidenceZh: 追踪空气的路径：鼻子/嘴巴 → 气管（trachea） → 支气管（bronchi） → 细支气管（bronchioles） → 肺泡（alveoli）
解释肺泡（alveoli）中的气体交换：氧气进入毛细血管，二氧化碳排出体外
描述呼吸的机械过程：膈肌（diaphragm）收缩将空气吸入，舒张时将空气排出
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否描述吸入的空气经历了什么过程——它是如何一步步深入肺部，直到氧气交换进入血液的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Immune System
topics.description: Know that the body has an immune system that protects against illness: the skin acts as a barrier, white blood cells identify and destroy germs (bacteria and viruses), and vaccines train the immune system to recognise specific diseases before they cause illness
evidence: Describe the skin as the body's first line of defence against germs
Explain that white blood cells detect and fight bacteria and viruses inside the body
Describe how vaccines work: they contain weakened or inactive germs that train the immune system to recognise the real disease
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how their body fights off germs — and why getting a vaccine helps protect them from getting sick?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解身体拥有一个抵御疾病的免疫系统（Immune System）：皮肤作为屏障，白细胞（White blood cells）识别并消灭病菌（细菌和病毒），而疫苗（Vaccines）则能在疾病引发症状前训练免疫系统识别特定的疾病。
evidenceZh: 描述皮肤是身体抵御病菌的第一道防线
解释白细胞如何在体内发现并对抗细菌（Bacteria）和病毒（Viruses）
描述疫苗的作用原理：它们含有减弱或失去活性的病菌，用于训练免疫系统识别真正的疾病
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释他们的身体是如何抵御病菌的——以及为什么接种疫苗能帮助他们免受疾病侵扰？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Nervous System
topics.description: Understand that the nervous system has two parts — the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord) and nerves that branch throughout the body — and that nerve signals travel at high speed to coordinate senses, thought, and movement
evidence: Name the two parts of the nervous system: central (brain + spinal cord) and peripheral (nerves throughout the body)
Describe the reflex arc: stimulus → sensory nerve → spinal cord/brain → motor nerve → muscle response
State that nerve signals travel extremely fast, which is why reflexes happen almost instantly
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a message travels from their finger to their brain when they touch something hot, and then back to their hand to pull it away?
