topics.descriptionZh: 了解神经系统分为两部分——中枢神经系统（Central Nervous System，包含大脑 brain 和脊髓 spinal cord）和周围神经（Peripheral Nerves），并知道神经信号传递速度极快，能够协调我们的感觉、思考和运动。
evidenceZh: 说出神经系统的两个部分：中枢神经系统（central，包含大脑 brain 和脊髓 spinal cord）和周围神经系统（peripheral，遍布全身的神经 nerves）。
描述反射弧（reflex arc）：刺激（stimulus）→ 感觉神经（sensory nerve）→ 脊髓/大脑（spinal cord/brain）→ 运动神经（motor nerve）→ 肌肉反应（muscle response）。
说明神经信号传递速度极快，这就是为什么反射动作（reflexes）几乎是瞬间发生的。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释当触摸到烫的东西时，信息是如何从手指传递到大脑，然后再传回手部将其缩回的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Immunity & Vaccines
topics.description: Distinguish innate (non-specific, immediate) from adaptive (specific, memory-forming) immunity; explain how B cells produce antibodies that recognise specific antigens, how T cells destroy infected cells, and why immunological memory makes vaccines work; and describe the gut microbiome as a community of trillions of microbes that significantly influences immune function
evidence: Distinguishes innate immunity (rapid, non-specific barriers and inflammation) from adaptive immunity (slow, specific, memory-forming)
Explains how B cells produce antibodies that bind to specific antigens on pathogens, targeting them for destruction
Explains immunological memory: after first exposure, memory B and T cells remain, making subsequent response faster and stronger — the basis of vaccine protection
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why they don't get chickenpox twice, could they explain the difference between just fighting off a germ and actually 'remembering' it — and describe how a vaccine trains the immune system without causing the disease?
topics.descriptionZh: 区分先天免疫（非特异性、即时反应）与适应性免疫（特异性、形成记忆）；解释B细胞如何产生识别特定抗原（antigens）的抗体，T细胞如何摧毁受感染的细胞，以及免疫记忆（immunological memory）为何能让疫苗发挥作用；并描述肠道微生物群（gut microbiome）这一由数万亿微生物组成的庞大群落是如何显著影响免疫功能的。
evidenceZh: 能够区分先天免疫（快速的、非特异性的屏障和炎症反应）与适应性免疫（较慢的、特异性的、能形成记忆的反应）
能够解释B细胞如何产生抗体，这些抗体会结合病原体上的特定抗原（antigens），从而将其标记并摧毁
能够解释免疫记忆（immunological memory）：在首次接触病原体后，记忆B细胞和T细胞会留存下来，使得再次接触时的免疫反应更快、更强——这也是疫苗提供保护的基础
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果问 {{name}} 为什么不会得两次水痘，他们能否解释“仅仅击退病菌”和真正“记住”病菌之间的区别——并描述疫苗是如何在不引发疾病的情况下训练免疫系统的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Neurons & Brain Structure
topics.description: Explain how neurons transmit signals as electrochemical impulses across synapses, describe how the brain is organised (lobes and functions, limbic system for emotion), and explain neuroplasticity — why learning and practice physically change brain structure — connecting to optical illusions as evidence that the brain constructs reality rather than passively recording it
evidence: Describes the neuron-to-neuron signal pathway: electrical impulse travels along axon, neurotransmitter crosses the synapse, new impulse begins in the next neuron
Names the four lobes of the cerebral cortex (frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital) and gives one function for each
Explains neuroplasticity: repeated neural pathways become stronger and faster — this is the biological mechanism of learning and skill development
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why practising a skill like piano or football makes you better over time, could they explain what's actually happening physically in the brain — and describe what it means to say the brain 'rewires itself'?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释神经元如何以电化学冲动（electrochemical impulses）的形式跨突触（synapses）传递信号，描述大脑的组织结构（脑叶及其功能、负责情绪的边缘系统（limbic system）），并解释神经可塑性（neuroplasticity）——为什么学习和练习会实际改变大脑的物理结构——并结合视觉错觉（optical illusions）作为证据，说明大脑是主动构建现实，而不是被动记录现实。
evidenceZh: 描述神经元之间的信号传递路径：电信号沿轴突（axon）传导，神经递质（neurotransmitter）穿过突触，在下一个神经元中引发新的电信号
说出大脑皮层（cerebral cortex）的四个脑叶（额叶 frontal lobe、顶叶 parietal lobe、颞叶 temporal lobe、枕叶 occipital lobe）的名称，并分别给出一个对应的功能
解释神经可塑性（neuroplasticity）：反复使用的神经通路会变得更强大、更快速——这是学习和技能发展的生物学机制
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果有人问 {{name}}，为什么练习弹钢琴或踢足球等技能会让我们随着时间推移变得更好，他们能否解释大脑中实际发生的物理变化——并描述说大脑“重新布线/重塑（rewires itself）”是什么意思？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: DNA & Genes
topics.description: Describe the double helix structure of DNA (base pairs, complementarity), explain how genes are sections of DNA that code for proteins, introduce the central dogma (DNA → mRNA → protein) conceptually, and discuss the ethical implications of CRISPR gene editing — including potential benefits (genetic disease treatment) and concerns (germline editing, 'designer babies')
evidence: Describes DNA as a double helix with four bases (A, T, C, G) where A pairs with T and C pairs with G
Explains that a gene is a section of DNA that codes for a specific protein, and that proteins carry out most of the body's functions
Describes CRISPR as a molecular tool that can cut and edit DNA sequences, and raises at least two distinct ethical considerations about its use in humans
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that scientists have edited a human gene to prevent a hereditary disease, could they explain what DNA actually is, how genes work, and why some people think editing human DNA raises serious ethical questions?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述DNA的双螺旋结构（碱基对、互补性），解释基因是DNA中负责编码蛋白质的片段，从概念上介绍中心法则（DNA → mRNA → 蛋白质），并探讨CRISPR基因编辑的伦理影响——包括其潜在益处（如治疗遗传疾病）以及引发的担忧（如生殖系编辑和“定制婴儿”）。
evidenceZh: 将DNA描述为具有四种碱基（A、T、C、G）的双螺旋结构，其中A与T配对，C与G配对
解释基因是DNA中编码特定蛋白质的片段，并且蛋白质执行着人体的大部分功能
将CRISPR描述为一种可以切割和编辑DNA序列的分子工具，并至少提出两项关于其在人类身上使用的不同伦理考量
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}听说科学家编辑了人类基因以预防一种遗传疾病，他们能否解释DNA究竟是什么，基因是如何工作的，以及为什么有些人认为编辑人类DNA会引发严重的伦理问题？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How the Body Stays in Balance
topics.description: Explain homeostasis as the process of maintaining a stable internal environment; describe the main feedback loop systems (negative feedback) using blood glucose regulation (insulin/glucagon) and body temperature as concrete examples; and connect the endocrine system (hormone-secreting glands) to the nervous system as two complementary communication systems with different speeds and durations
evidence: Defines homeostasis and explains why maintaining a stable internal environment is essential for survival
Describes the blood glucose negative feedback loop: glucose rises → pancreas releases insulin → cells take up glucose → glucose falls → insulin release stops
Compares the nervous system (fast, electrical, short-duration signals) with the endocrine system (slower, chemical, longer-duration signals) and gives an example where each is more appropriate
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} ate a large meal of sugary food and was asked what their body does to keep blood sugar from getting dangerously high, could they explain the role of insulin and describe how the feedback system brings levels back to normal?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释稳态（homeostasis）是维持内部环境稳定的过程；以血糖调节（胰岛素/胰高血糖素）和体温调节为具体例子，描述主要的反馈循环系统（负反馈/negative feedback）；并将内分泌系统（endocrine system，分泌激素的腺体）与神经系统（nervous system）联系起来，说明它们是两种速度和持续时间不同、但相互补充的通讯系统。
evidenceZh: 定义稳态（homeostasis），并解释为什么维持稳定的内部环境对生存至关重要
描述血糖负反馈（negative feedback）循环：血糖升高 → 胰腺释放胰岛素（insulin） → 细胞吸收葡萄糖 → 血糖下降 → 胰岛素释放停止
比较神经系统（nervous system，快速、电信号、持续时间短的信号）和内分泌系统（endocrine system，较慢、化学信号、持续时间长的信号），并举例说明在什么情况下各自更适用
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}吃了一顿富含糖分的大餐，并被问到身体会如何防止血糖变得过高，他们能否解释胰岛素（insulin）的作用，并描述反馈系统（feedback system）如何将血糖水平恢复正常？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Cancer & Stem Cells
topics.description: Explain that cancer occurs when mutations in DNA disable normal cell-cycle controls, causing uncontrolled cell division and tumour formation; describe how stem cells differ from specialised cells and their potential for regenerative medicine; and evaluate the ethical debates around embryonic stem cell research and genetic testing
evidence: Explains cancer as the result of DNA mutations that disable tumour suppressor genes or activate oncogenes, causing unchecked mitosis
Distinguishes stem cells (unspecialised, can differentiate) from specialised cells (fixed function) and explains why stem cells are medically valuable
Presents the embryonic stem cell debate with at least two specific scientific arguments in favour and two ethical objections against, without simply asserting one side is correct
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked to explain what cancer actually is at a cellular level, could they describe what goes wrong with cell division — and explain why some people object to using stem cells from embryos for medical research, even if it could save lives?
topics.nameZh: 癌症与干细胞 (Cancer & Stem Cells)
topics.descriptionZh: 解释癌症的发生是由于DNA突变使正常的细胞周期（Cell cycle）控制失效，导致细胞不受控制地分裂并形成肿瘤（Tumour）；描述干细胞与特化细胞（Specialised cells）的区别及其在再生医学（Regenerative medicine）中的潜力；并评估围绕胚胎干细胞研究和基因检测的伦理争议。
evidenceZh: 解释癌症是DNA突变导致抑癌基因（Tumour suppressor genes）失活或致癌基因（Oncogenes）激活的结果，从而引发不受控制的有丝分裂（Mitosis）
区分干细胞（未特化、可分化）与特化细胞（功能固定），并解释干细胞在医学上的重要价值
呈现关于胚胎干细胞的争议，至少提出两个支持的具体科学论据和两个反对的伦理理由，而不是简单地断言某一方绝对正确
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果让{{name}}在细胞层面上解释癌症究竟是什么，他们能否描述细胞分裂（Cell division）过程中哪里出了问题——并解释为什么有些人反对使用胚胎干细胞进行医学研究，即使这可能会拯救生命？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Earth Is Made of Rock
topics.description: Understand that Earth is made of rock and other solid materials
evidence: State that the ground beneath us is made of rock
Identify rocks and stones as pieces of the Earth
Explain that Earth is solid and made of natural materials
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} picks up a stone in the garden, can they tell you that the whole Earth is made of rock and other materials like that stone?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解地球是由岩石和其他固体物质组成的
evidenceZh: 说明我们脚下的地面是由岩石构成的
认出岩石和石头是地球的一部分
解释地球是固体的，并且由自然材料构成
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在花园里捡起一块石头，他们能告诉你整个地球都是由岩石和像那块石头一样的其他材料构成的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Earthquake Safety
topics.description: Know basic earthquake safety: drop, cover, and hold on; move away from windows; tell a trusted adult
evidence: Demonstrate the drop, cover, and hold on procedure
Explain why to move away from windows and shelves during shaking
Name a trusted adult to tell if they feel an earthquake
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you asked {{name}} what to do if the ground started shaking, could they show you 'drop, cover, and hold on' and say they'd move away from windows?
topics.descriptionZh: 掌握基本的地震安全知识：伏地、遮挡、手抓牢（drop, cover, and hold on）；远离窗户；告诉可信赖的成年人
evidenceZh: 演示“伏地、遮挡、手抓牢”（drop, cover, and hold on）的步骤
解释在地震摇晃时为什么要远离窗户和书架
说出如果感觉到地震，会告诉哪位可信赖的成年人
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你问{{name}}地面开始摇晃时该怎么办，他们能向你演示“伏地、遮挡、手抓牢”并说他们会远离窗户吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Fast & Slow Earth Changes
topics.description: Understand that Earth's surface changes: some changes are quick (eruptions, earthquakes) and some are slow (wind, water wearing away rock)
evidence: Give an example of a quick change to Earth's surface like a volcanic eruption
Give an example of a slow change to Earth's surface like erosion by wind or water
Compare quick and slow changes and explain the difference
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you point out a cliff being worn away by waves, can {{name}} explain that this happens slowly, while a volcanic eruption or earthquake changes the land quickly?
topics.nameZh: 快速与缓慢的地球变化
topics.descriptionZh: 理解地球表面是不断变化的：有些变化是快速的（如火山喷发、地震），而有些变化则是缓慢的（如风和水对岩石的侵蚀）。
evidenceZh: 举一个地球表面快速变化的例子，如火山喷发（volcanic eruption）
举一个地球表面缓慢变化的例子，如风或水造成的侵蚀（erosion）
比较快速变化和缓慢变化，并解释它们之间的区别
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你指出一处被海浪侵蚀的悬崖，{{name}} 能否解释这是一个缓慢发生的过程，而火山喷发或地震则会迅速改变地貌？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Power of Eruptions
topics.description: Appreciate that volcanic eruptions are powerful events that can change the landscape
evidence: Describe an eruption as a powerful, dramatic event
Give examples of how an eruption changes the area around a volcano
Compare the landscape before and after an eruption using pictures
topics.assessmentPrompt: After watching a video of a volcano erupting, does {{name}} show excitement and talk about how powerful it is and how it changes the land around it?
topics.descriptionZh: 体会火山喷发（volcanic eruptions）的巨大威力，了解其能够改变地貌（landscape）。
evidenceZh: 将火山喷发描述为一场强大而剧烈的事件
举例说明火山喷发如何改变火山周围的区域
通过图片对比火山喷发前后的地貌变化
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在观看火山喷发（volcanic eruption）的视频后，{{name}}是否表现出兴奋，并谈论它有多么强大的力量以及它是如何改变周围土地的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: What Is an Earthquake
topics.description: Know what an earthquake is: a sudden shaking of the ground that can be strong or weak
evidence: Describe an earthquake as the ground shaking suddenly
Explain that earthquakes vary in strength from barely noticeable to very strong
Describe what it might feel like during an earthquake
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that an earthquake is when the ground suddenly shakes, and that some earthquakes shake harder than others?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解什么是地震：地面突然发生的摇晃，有时轻微有时强烈
evidenceZh: 把地震描述为地面的突然摇晃
解释地震的摇晃程度各不相同，从几乎感觉不到到非常强烈
描述在地震发生时可能会有什么样的感觉
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释地震就是地面突然摇晃，并且有些地震摇晃得比其他地震更厉害？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: What Is a Volcano
topics.description: Know what a volcano is: an opening in Earth's surface where hot melted rock (lava) comes out
evidence: Describe a volcano as a place where hot material comes out of the Earth
Explain that lava is rock so hot it has melted
Point to a volcano in a picture and describe what is happening
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a picture of a volcano erupting, can they explain that it's an opening in the ground where very hot melted rock comes out?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解什么是火山：地球表面的一个开口，炽热的熔化岩石（熔岩，lava）会从这里喷发出来。
evidenceZh: 将火山描述为地球内部炽热物质喷出的地方
解释熔岩（lava）是温度极高而熔化的岩石
指出图片中的火山并描述正在发生的事情
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到一张火山喷发的图片，他们能解释这是地面上的一个开口，非常炽热的熔化岩石会从这里喷发出来吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Active, Dormant & Extinct
topics.description: Classify volcanoes as active (could erupt any time), dormant (sleeping but could wake up), or extinct (will not erupt again)
evidence: Define active, dormant, and extinct volcanoes
Explain that a dormant volcano is not safe just because it has not erupted recently
Classify a given volcano based on its eruption history
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you told {{name}} about a volcano that last erupted 500 years ago, could they explain whether it's active, dormant, or extinct, and why a dormant volcano might still be dangerous?
topics.nameZh: 活火山、休眠火山与死火山
topics.descriptionZh: 将火山分为活火山（随时可能喷发）、休眠火山（在“睡觉”但可能“醒来”）或死火山（不会再喷发）。
evidenceZh: 定义活火山、休眠火山和死火山
解释休眠火山即使最近没有喷发，也不代表它是安全的
根据火山的喷发历史对特定火山进行分类
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你告诉 {{name}} 有一座火山在500年前最后一次喷发，他们能判断出它是活火山、休眠火山还是死火山，并解释为什么休眠火山仍然可能很危险吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Earth's Layers
topics.description: Know that Earth has layers — a thin outer crust, a thick hot mantle, and a core at the centre — and that the inside of the Earth is extremely hot
evidence: Name Earth's three main layers: crust, mantle, and core
Explain that the crust is thin compared to the other layers
State that Earth's interior is extremely hot — hot enough to melt rock
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} cracks open a hard-boiled egg, can they compare it to Earth and name the three layers — crust on the outside, mantle in the middle, and core at the centre?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解地球是分层的——外部有薄薄的地壳（crust），中间有厚厚的炽热地幔（mantle），以及位于中心的地核（core），并且知道地球内部极其炎热。
evidenceZh: 说出地球的三个主要圈层：地壳（crust）、地幔（mantle）和地核（core）
解释与其他圈层相比，地壳非常薄
说明地球内部极其炎热——热得足以熔化岩石
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 剥开一个煮熟的鸡蛋，他们能将其与地球进行对比，并说出这三个圈层吗——最外面的地壳（crust）、中间的地幔（mantle）和中心的地核（core）？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Inside a Volcano
topics.description: Understand the inside of a volcano: magma is hot melted rock underground, lava is the same material after it reaches the surface, and volcanoes have a magma chamber, vent, and crater
evidence: Explain that magma is melted rock underground and lava is the same material above ground
Label a magma chamber, vent, and crater on a volcano cross-section
Describe the path magma takes from underground to the surface during an eruption
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looks at a cross-section diagram of a volcano, can they point to the magma chamber, vent, and crater, and explain the difference between magma underground and lava on the surface?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解火山的内部结构：岩浆（magma）是地下高温熔化的岩石，熔岩（lava）是同种物质到达地表后的状态，火山具有岩浆房（magma chamber）、火山通道（vent）和火山口（crater）。
evidenceZh: 解释岩浆是地下熔化的岩石，而熔岩是同种物质到达地表后的状态。
在火山剖面图（cross-section）上标出岩浆房（magma chamber）、火山通道（vent）和火山口（crater）。
描述火山喷发时岩浆从地下到地表所经过的路径。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 观察火山的剖面图（cross-section），他们能指出岩浆房（magma chamber）、火山通道（vent）和火山口（crater），并解释地下岩浆（magma）和地表熔岩（lava）的区别吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Pompeii & Vesuvius
topics.description: Know the story of Pompeii: a Roman city buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD, preserved under volcanic ash, and rediscovered by archaeologists centuries later
evidence: Retell the key events: Vesuvius erupted, Pompeii was buried under ash
Explain that the ash preserved the city, its buildings, and even people's shapes
Describe how archaeologists uncovered the city and what we can learn from it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a picture of the ruins of Pompeii, can they tell the story of how a Roman city was buried by a volcanic eruption and then found again hundreds of years later?
topics.nameZh: 庞贝古城与维苏威火山 (Pompeii & Vesuvius)
topics.descriptionZh: 了解庞贝古城的故事：这是一座在公元79年被维苏威火山爆发 (volcanic eruption) 掩埋的罗马城市，在火山灰 (volcanic ash) 下保存完好，并在几个世纪后被考古学家 (archaeologists) 重新发现。
evidenceZh: 复述关键事件：维苏威火山爆发，庞贝古城被掩埋在火山灰下
解释火山灰如何保存了这座城市、它的建筑，甚至是人们的身影
描述考古学家是如何发掘这座城市的，以及我们能从中学到什么
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到一张庞贝古城废墟的图片，他们能讲述这座罗马城市是如何被火山爆发掩埋，又在数百年后再次被发现的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Ring of Fire
topics.description: Recognise that volcanoes and earthquakes tend to happen in certain places — especially around the edges of the Pacific Ocean (Ring of Fire) — not randomly across the Earth
evidence: Describe the pattern that volcanoes and earthquakes cluster in certain zones
Locate the Ring of Fire on a world map
Explain that the locations of earthquakes and volcanoes are not random
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a world map showing where earthquakes and volcanoes happen, could they spot the pattern — that they cluster in certain lines and bands rather than being scattered everywhere?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识到火山和地震往往发生在特定的地方——尤其是太平洋边缘（火环）——而不是在地球上随机分布。
evidenceZh: 描述火山和地震聚集在特定区域的分布规律
在世界地图上找到火环 (Ring of Fire) 的位置
解释火山和地震的分布并不是随机的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 观察一张标有地震和火山分布的世界地图，他们能发现其中的规律吗——即它们聚集在特定的线条和带状区域，而不是到处散落？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Tsunamis
topics.description: Know what a tsunami is: a very large, fast ocean wave caused by an earthquake or volcanic eruption under the sea, which can cause great damage when it reaches land
evidence: Explain that a tsunami is caused by an earthquake or eruption under the sea
State that tsunamis travel very fast across the ocean
Describe the damage a tsunami can cause when it reaches the coast
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears the word 'tsunami' on the news, can they explain that it's a huge wave caused by an earthquake or eruption under the ocean, and that it can travel very fast across the sea?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解什么是海啸：海啸是一种由海底地震或火山爆发引起的巨大且移动迅速的海浪，当它到达陆地时会造成巨大的破坏。
evidenceZh: 解释海啸是由海底地震或火山爆发引起的
说明海啸在海洋中传播速度极快
描述海啸到达海岸时可能造成的破坏
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在新闻里听到“海啸”这个词，他们能解释这是由海底地震或火山爆发引起的巨大海浪，并且它能在海面上极速传播吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Types of Rock
topics.description: Know the three main types of rock — igneous (formed when lava or magma cools), sedimentary (formed from layers pressed together), and metamorphic — and that fossils are found in sedimentary rock
evidence: Name the three main rock types: igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic
Explain that igneous rock forms when lava or magma cools and hardens
State that fossils are preserved in sedimentary rock because it forms in layers
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} finds different rocks on a beach walk, can they sort them and explain that some formed from cooled lava, some from layers pressed together over time, and that fossils are found in the layered ones?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解三种主要的岩石类型——火成岩（由熔岩或岩浆冷却形成）、沉积岩（由层层沉积物压实形成）和变质岩，并知道化石保存在沉积岩中。
evidenceZh: 说出三种主要的岩石类型：火成岩（igneous）、沉积岩（sedimentary）和变质岩（metamorphic）
解释火成岩是在熔岩或岩浆冷却并硬化时形成的
说明化石保存在沉积岩中，因为它是分层形成的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在海滩散步时发现了不同的岩石，他们能对这些岩石进行分类，并解释有些是由冷却的熔岩形成的，有些是由沉积层随时间推移压实形成的，而且化石存在于那些分层的岩石中吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Why Earthquakes Happen
topics.description: Understand that earthquakes happen when rocks underground suddenly move or break, releasing energy that shakes the ground
evidence: Explain that earthquakes are caused by rocks underground suddenly moving
Describe how this movement sends shaking through the surrounding ground
Distinguish between the underground cause and the surface effects of an earthquake
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} felt a small tremor or saw footage of an earthquake, could they explain that it happens because rocks deep underground suddenly shift or crack?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解地震是由于地下岩石突然移动或断裂，释放出能量（Energy）并引起地面震动而发生的。
evidenceZh: 解释地震是由地下岩石突然移动引起的
描述这种移动如何将震动传递到周围的地面
区分地震的地下原因和地表效应（Surface effects）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 感觉到轻微的震动或看到了地震的画面，他们能解释这是因为地下深处的岩石突然移动或破裂而引起的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Earthquake-Resistant Design
topics.description: Know that buildings can be designed to resist earthquakes, tsunami warning systems alert coastal communities, and communities prepare through evacuation plans and drills
evidence: Describe at least one feature that makes buildings more earthquake-resistant
Explain how tsunami warning systems detect danger and alert communities
Describe how communities prepare for earthquakes and eruptions through drills and evacuation plans
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a documentary about earthquake-proof buildings in Japan, could they explain how engineers design buildings to withstand shaking and how tsunami warnings give people time to evacuate?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解建筑物可以通过特定设计来抵抗地震，海啸预警系统能及时警报沿海社区，以及社区可以通过疏散计划和演练来做好防灾准备。
evidenceZh: 描述至少一种让建筑物更抗震的设计特点
解释海啸预警系统是如何探测危险并向社区发出警报的
描述社区是如何通过演练和疏散计划来为地震和火山喷发做准备的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看了一部关于日本抗震建筑的纪录片，ta能解释工程师是如何设计建筑来抵御地震摇晃，以及海啸预警是如何为人们争取疏散时间的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Eruption Types & Volcano Shape
topics.description: Understand that not all volcanic eruptions are the same: some flow gently (effusive) and some explode violently (explosive), depending on the properties of the magma, and that volcano shape is related to eruption type
evidence: Contrast effusive eruptions (gentle lava flows) with explosive eruptions (violent blasts of ash and rock)
Explain that eruption type depends on properties of the magma such as thickness and gas content
Connect volcano shape to eruption style: shield volcanoes from runny lava, steep cones from thick explosive magma
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared pictures of a gently oozing Hawaiian volcano and a violently erupting one like Mount St Helens, could they explain why eruptions look so different and how that relates to the volcano's shape?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解并非所有火山喷发都一样：有的岩浆会平缓地流淌（溢流式喷发 effusive），有的则会猛烈地爆炸（爆发式喷发 explosive）。这取决于岩浆（magma）的特性，而且火山的形状也和喷发类型息息相关。
evidenceZh: 对比溢流式喷发（平缓的熔岩流 effusive eruptions）与爆发式喷发（火山灰和岩石的猛烈喷发 explosive eruptions）。
解释喷发类型取决于岩浆（magma）的特性，如粘稠度（thickness）和气体含量（gas content）。
将火山形状与喷发方式联系起来：盾状火山（shield volcanoes）由流动性强的熔岩形成，而陡峭的锥形火山由粘稠的爆发式岩浆形成。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 比较了平缓渗出熔岩的夏威夷火山和像圣海伦斯火山（Mount St Helens）那样猛烈喷发的火山的图片，他们能解释为什么喷发看起来如此不同，以及这与火山的形状有何关系吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Famous Eruptions & Pangaea
topics.description: Know about famous eruptions and their global effects: Mount St Helens (1980), Eyjafjallajökull (2010), and how large eruptions can affect weather and climate worldwide; understand that continents were once joined (Pangaea) and have slowly drifted apart
evidence: Describe at least one famous volcanic eruption and its key effects
Explain how volcanic ash and gases in the atmosphere can cool global temperatures
State that continents were once joined in a supercontinent and have slowly moved apart over millions of years
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you about a famous volcanic eruption like Mount St Helens and explain how a really big eruption can send so much ash into the sky that it affects weather around the whole world?
topics.nameZh: 著名火山喷发与盘古大陆 (Pangaea)
topics.descriptionZh: 了解著名的火山喷发及其全球影响：圣海伦斯火山（1980年）、艾雅法拉火山（2010年），以及大型喷发如何影响全球天气和气候；理解大陆曾经连在一起（盘古大陆/Pangaea），并缓慢漂移分开。
evidenceZh: 描述至少一次著名的火山喷发及其主要影响
解释大气中的火山灰和气体如何降低全球气温
说明大陆曾经连接在一个超大陆中，并在数百万年间缓慢漂移分开
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能给你讲讲像圣海伦斯火山这样的著名火山喷发，并解释一次非常大的喷发是如何将大量火山灰送入天空，从而影响全球天气的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Measuring Earthquake Strength
topics.description: Know that scientists measure earthquakes using seismometers, that earthquakes release energy that travels as waves through the ground, and that a magnitude scale describes their strength
evidence: Explain that a seismometer is an instrument that detects and records ground shaking
Describe earthquake energy as waves that travel outward from where rocks broke
Interpret a magnitude number as a measure of an earthquake's strength
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard a news report about a magnitude 6 earthquake, could they explain what a seismometer is, that earthquakes send waves through the ground, and that higher numbers mean stronger quakes?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解科学家使用地震仪（seismometer）测量地震，地震释放的能量会以波（waves）的形式在地层中传播，并且震级（magnitude scale）用来描述其强度。
evidenceZh: 解释地震仪（seismometer）是一种探测并记录地面震动的仪器
把地震能量描述为从岩石破裂处向外扩散的波（waves）
将震级（magnitude）数值理解为衡量地震强度的标准
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 听到关于6级（magnitude 6）地震的新闻报道，他们能解释什么是地震仪（seismometer）、地震波会在地面下传播，并且震级数字越大代表地震越强吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Monitoring Volcanoes
topics.description: Understand how volcanologists monitor volcanoes by looking for warning signs — gas emissions, ground swelling, small earthquakes — and that prediction involves evidence and uncertainty, not certainty
evidence: Name at least two warning signs scientists look for before an eruption
Explain that volcanologists combine multiple types of evidence to assess risk
Discuss why volcanic prediction involves uncertainty and cannot guarantee exact timing
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how scientists watch for signs that a volcano might erupt — like gas, ground bulging, or tiny earthquakes — and why they can warn people but can't predict the exact moment?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解火山学家如何通过寻找预警信号——比如气体排放（gas emissions）、地面隆起（ground swelling）和微小地震（small earthquakes）——来监测火山，并明白火山预测是基于证据和存在不确定性的，而不是绝对确定的。
evidenceZh: 说出科学家在火山喷发前寻找的至少两个预警信号
解释火山学家是如何结合多种类型的证据来评估风险的
讨论为什么火山预测存在不确定性，且无法保证准确的喷发时间
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能解释科学家是如何观察火山可能喷发的迹象（比如气体、地面隆起或微小地震）的，以及为什么他们能向人们发出警告，却无法预测确切的喷发时间吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Natural Disaster Solutions
topics.description: Generate and compare multiple solutions to reduce the impacts of natural Earth processes on humans, such as earthquakes, floods, or volcanic eruptions
evidence: Identify at least two natural hazards and their impacts on human life and property
Generate multiple solutions for reducing impacts (e.g. earthquake-resistant buildings, flood barriers, early warning systems)
Compare solutions based on criteria like effectiveness, cost, and feasibility
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} come up with different ideas for keeping people safe from earthquakes or floods, and compare which ones would work best?
topics.descriptionZh: 提出并比较多种解决方案，以减少地球自然过程（natural Earth processes）对人类的影响，如地震、洪水或火山爆发。
evidenceZh: 识别至少两种自然灾害及其对人类生命和财产的影响
提出多种减少影响的解决方案（例如：抗震建筑、防洪堤坝、早期预警系统）
根据有效性、成本和可行性等标准比较这些解决方案
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否想出不同的方法来保护人们免受地震或洪水的伤害，并比较哪些方法最有效？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Plate Boundaries
topics.description: Explain how plate boundaries cause earthquakes and volcanoes: plates pushing together, pulling apart, or sliding past each other create the forces that trigger these events, and mountains form where plates collide
evidence: Describe three types of plate boundary movement: convergent, divergent, and transform
Explain that earthquakes occur when plates grind or collide at boundaries
Explain that volcanoes form where plates pull apart or one slides under another, allowing magma to rise
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why most volcanoes and earthquakes happen at the edges of tectonic plates — where plates push together, pull apart, or slide past each other?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释板块边界如何引发地震和火山：板块相互挤压、分离或彼此错动所产生的力量会触发这些地质事件，而在板块相撞的地方则会形成山脉。
evidenceZh: 描述板块边界的三种运动类型：汇聚型 (convergent)、离散型 (divergent) 和转换型 (transform)
解释地震发生在板块边界相互摩擦或碰撞时
解释火山形成于板块分离或一个板块俯冲到另一个板块之下的地方，这使得岩浆 (magma) 得以涌升
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释为什么大多数火山和地震都发生在构造板块 (tectonic plates) 的边缘——也就是板块相互挤压、分离或彼此滑过的地方？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Tectonic Plates
topics.description: Understand that Earth's crust is broken into large pieces called tectonic plates that float on hotter, softer rock beneath and move very slowly — a few centimetres per year
evidence: Describe Earth's crust as broken into large plates
Explain that the plates float on hotter, partially melted rock underneath
State that plates move very slowly, typically a few centimetres per year
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you showed {{name}} a map of the tectonic plates, could they explain that Earth's surface is cracked into huge pieces that move very slowly — about as fast as their fingernails grow?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解地球的地壳 (Earth's crust) 破裂成被称为构造板块 (Tectonic Plates) 的巨大块体，这些板块漂浮在下方更热、更软的岩石上，并以非常缓慢的速度移动——每年几厘米。
evidenceZh: 描述地球的地壳破裂成巨大的板块
解释这些板块漂浮在下方更热、部分融化的岩石上
说明板块移动非常缓慢，通常每年只移动几厘米
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你给 {{name}} 看一张构造板块地图，他们能解释地球表面裂成了巨大的碎块，并且这些碎块移动得非常缓慢——大约和他们指甲生长的速度一样快吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Rock Cycle
topics.description: Understand the rock cycle: rocks slowly change from one type to another over millions of years — igneous rock weathers into sediment, sediment becomes sedimentary rock, heat and pressure create metamorphic rock, and melting starts the cycle again
evidence: Describe the rock cycle as a continuous process with no beginning or end
Trace at least one complete path through the cycle from igneous to sedimentary to metamorphic and back
Explain that the rock cycle operates over millions of years through weathering, pressure, heat, and melting
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw igneous rock, sandstone, and marble side by side, could they explain how each type forms and how rocks slowly transform from one type to another in a never-ending cycle?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解岩石循环：岩石会在数百万年的时间里，缓慢地从一种类型变成另一种类型——火成岩（igneous rock）风化变成沉积物，沉积物变成沉积岩（sedimentary rock），高温和高压形成变质岩（metamorphic rock），而熔化则再次开启循环。
evidenceZh: 将岩石循环描述为一个没有起点和终点的连续过程
描绘出循环中至少一条完整的转化路径，从火成岩到沉积岩，再到变质岩，最后回到起点
解释岩石循环是通过风化、压力、热量和熔化等作用，在数百万年的时间跨度中不断进行的
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}看到火成岩、砂岩和大理石并排放在一起，他们能解释每种岩石是如何形成的，以及岩石如何在一个永无止境的循环中从一种类型缓慢变成另一种类型吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How Tectonic Plates Move
topics.description: Understand that convection currents in the molten mantle drive the movement of rigid tectonic plates; distinguish between convergent (collision/subduction), divergent (spreading ridges), and transform (sliding) plate boundaries; explain why volcanoes, earthquakes, and mountain chains cluster at boundaries; introduce the Wilson cycle of supercontinent assembly and breakup
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looks at a world map showing where volcanoes and earthquakes happen, can they explain why these events follow specific ring-shaped patterns rather than occurring randomly around the globe?
topics.nameZh: 构造板块是如何运动的
topics.descriptionZh: 理解熔融地幔中的对流（convection currents）驱动着刚性构造板块（tectonic plates）的运动；区分汇聚型（convergent，碰撞/俯冲）、离散型（divergent，洋中脊扩张）和转换型（transform，滑动）板块边界；解释为什么火山、地震和山脉链会聚集在板块边界处；介绍超大陆聚合与裂解的威尔逊循环（Wilson cycle）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看着一张显示火山和地震发生地点的世界地图，他们能解释为什么这些事件会呈现出特定的环状分布模式，而不是在全球随机发生吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Seismic Waves & Earth's Interior
topics.description: Distinguish between P-waves (compression, travel through solids and liquids) and S-waves (shear, cannot pass through liquids); explain why a seismic shadow zone exists on the far side of an earthquake; describe how seismologists use wave refraction and reflection to infer that Earth has a solid inner core, liquid outer core, mantle, and crust
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how scientists know Earth has a liquid outer core if nobody has ever drilled that deep — what clues do earthquake waves give us about Earth's hidden interior?
topics.descriptionZh: 区分纵波（P-waves，压缩波，可在固体和液体中传播）和横波（S-waves，剪切波，无法在液体中传播）；解释为什么在地震的另一侧会存在地震影区（shadow zone）；描述地震学家如何利用波的折射（refraction）和反射（reflection）来推断地球具有固态内核（inner core）、液态外核（outer core）、地幔（mantle）和地壳（crust）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释一下科学家是如何知道地球有液态外核（liquid outer core）的吗，毕竟没有人能钻探到那么深的地方——地震波为我们揭示了地球隐藏内部的哪些线索呢？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Hazard Assessment & Evacuation
topics.description: Explain probabilistic hazard assessment using eruption recurrence intervals and fault slip rates; describe how volcano observatories monitor ground deformation, gas emissions, and seismicity to issue alert levels; explore why communities remain near active hazards (fertile volcanic soil, poverty, cultural ties); discuss the ethics and politics of evacuation decisions and the social justice dimensions of disaster risk
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read a news story about a town that refused to evacuate before a predicted volcanic eruption, can they describe at least two reasons — beyond just stubbornness — why people might genuinely choose to stay?
topics.nameZh: 灾害评估与疏散 (Hazard Assessment & Evacuation)
topics.descriptionZh: 解释如何利用火山喷发复发周期（eruption recurrence intervals）和断层滑动速率（fault slip rates）来进行概率性灾害评估（probabilistic hazard assessment）；描述火山观测站如何监测地面变形（ground deformation）、气体排放（gas emissions）和地震活动（seismicity）来发布预警级别；探讨为什么有些社区宁愿留在危险的活火山附近（如为了肥沃的火山土壤、经济贫困或文化羁绊）；讨论疏散决策背后的伦理与政治问题，以及灾害风险中的社会正义维度。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 读了一篇关于某个小镇在预测的火山喷发前拒绝疏散的新闻，他们能否说出至少两个原因——除了“固执”之外——来解释为什么人们可能会真心选择留下来？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Supervolcanoes & Volcanic Winter
topics.description: Describe calderas such as Yellowstone and Toba as supervolcanoes capable of erupting thousands of cubic kilometres of ash; explain how sulphur dioxide aerosols in the stratosphere scatter sunlight and cause volcanic winter; discuss the Toba catastrophe theory and how giant eruptions have interacted with ice ages; contrast supervolcano eruptions with ordinary eruptions in scale and climate impact
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} heard of a supervolcano? Can they describe how a single enormous eruption could cool the entire planet for years — what gets into the atmosphere and why does it block warmth?
topics.descriptionZh: 描述黄石公园和多巴湖等破火山口（calderas）作为超级火山，能够喷发出数千立方公里的火山灰；解释平流层中的二氧化硫气溶胶（sulphur dioxide aerosols）如何散射阳光并引发火山冬天；探讨多巴巨灾理论以及巨型火山喷发如何与冰河时期相互作用；对比超级火山喷发与普通火山喷发在规模和气候影响上的差异。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 听说过超级火山吗？他们能描述一次巨大的喷发是如何让整个地球冷却数年的吗——什么东西进入了大气层，它又是为什么能阻挡热量？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Volcanoes & Mass Extinctions
topics.description: Explain how large igneous provinces (LIPs) — massive outpourings of lava over millions of years — caused global warming and ocean acidification that drove mass extinctions; connect the Siberian Traps to the end-Permian extinction and the Deccan Traps to the end-Cretaceous event; explore how hydrothermal vents on the early Earth may have been the cradle of life; understand volcanoes as both destroyers and creators in the history of life
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how enormous volcanic eruptions millions of years ago may have triggered some of Earth's biggest mass extinctions — what's the chain of events from lava to species dying out?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释大火成岩省（LIPs）——数百万年间大规模涌出的熔岩——是如何引发全球变暖和海洋酸化，进而导致物种大灭绝的；将西伯利亚暗色岩（Siberian Traps）与二叠纪末期大灭绝联系起来，将德干暗色岩（Deccan Traps）与白垩纪末期大灭绝事件联系起来；探索早期地球的热液喷口（hydrothermal vents）是如何可能成为生命摇篮的；理解火山在生命历史中既是毁灭者又是创造者的双重角色。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能解释数百万年前巨大的火山喷发是如何可能引发地球上一些最大的物种大灭绝的吗——从熔岩喷发到物种灭绝，这一连串的事件是如何发生的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Communication with Light & Sound
topics.description: Design and build a device that uses light or sound to solve the problem of communicating over a distance
evidence: Design a device that uses light or sound to communicate over a distance (e.g. string telephone, torch signals)
Build and test the device, identifying what works and what could be improved
Explain how the device uses properties of light or sound to transmit information
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} design a simple device — like a string telephone or a mirror signalling system — to send a message to someone far away?
topics.descriptionZh: 设计并制作一个利用光或声音来解决远距离通信问题的装置
evidenceZh: 设计一个利用光或声音进行远距离通信的装置（例如：土电话、手电筒信号）
制作并测试该装置，找出其有效之处以及可以改进的地方
解释该装置如何利用光或声音的特性（properties）来传递信息
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否设计一个简单的装置——比如“土电话”或镜子信号系统——向远方的人发送信息？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Light & Seeing in the Dark
topics.description: Observe that objects in darkness can be seen only when illuminated by a light source
evidence: Explain that we need light to see objects — without any light source, it is completely dark
Describe an observation showing objects become visible only when light reaches them
Distinguish between light sources (sun, torch, lamp) and objects that just reflect light
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you go into a completely dark room with {{name}}, can they explain why they can't see anything until a torch is switched on?
topics.descriptionZh: 观察发现，黑暗中的物体只有在被光源照亮时才能被看见
evidenceZh: 解释我们需要光才能看见物体——没有任何光源时，周围就完全漆黑一片
描述一个观察现象，说明只有当光线照射到物体上时，我们才能看见它们
区分光源（如太阳、手电筒、台灯）和仅仅反射光线的物体
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你和{{name}}一起走进一个完全漆黑的房间，他们能解释为什么直到打开手电筒之前什么都看不见吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Light & Sound Vocabulary
topics.description: Name and use vocabulary for how light and sound behave — light source, transparent, translucent, opaque, shadow, reflect, vibration, pitch, volume — and apply these terms correctly when describing observations about how light travels and how sounds are made and changed
evidence: Correctly classify a set of materials as transparent, translucent, or opaque and explain each term
Explain what causes a shadow using the words 'opaque' and 'light source' correctly
Describe what changes the pitch or volume of a sound using vibration vocabulary
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you held up a piece of frosted glass, could {{name}} say whether it's transparent, translucent, or opaque — and explain what that word means?
topics.descriptionZh: 命名并使用描述光和声音行为的词汇——光源 (light source)、透明 (transparent)、半透明 (translucent)、不透明 (opaque)、影子 (shadow)、反射 (reflect)、振动 (vibration)、音高 (pitch)、音量 (volume)——并在描述关于光如何传播以及声音如何产生和变化的观察结果时正确应用这些术语。
evidenceZh: 正确地将一组材料分类为透明 (transparent)、半透明 (translucent) 或不透明 (opaque)，并解释每个术语的含义
正确使用“不透明 (opaque)”和“光源 (light source)”这两个词来解释影子形成的原因
使用振动 (vibration) 相关的词汇描述是什么改变了声音的音高 (pitch) 或音量 (volume)
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果你举起一块磨砂玻璃，{{name}} 能否说出它是透明 (transparent)、半透明 (translucent) 还是不透明 (opaque) 的——并解释这个词的意思？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Transparent, Translucent & Opaque
topics.description: Investigate the effect of placing objects made of different materials in the path of a beam of light, discovering transparent, translucent, and opaque materials
evidence: Test at least six materials and classify them as transparent, translucent, or opaque
Define transparent (light passes through clearly), translucent (some light passes, blurry), opaque (no light passes)
Predict whether a given material will let light through based on its appearance
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} test different materials with a torch and sort them into ones light goes through, ones that block light, and ones in between?
topics.descriptionZh: 探究将不同材料制成的物体放置在光束路径中的效果，从而发现透明（Transparent）、半透明（Translucent）和不透明（Opaque）的材料。
evidenceZh: 测试至少六种材料，并将它们分类为透明（Transparent）、半透明（Translucent）或不透明（Opaque）
定义透明（光线清晰穿过）、半透明（部分光线穿过，看东西模糊）和不透明（光线完全无法穿过）
根据材料的外观，预测给定的材料是否能让光线透过
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否用手电筒测试不同的材料，并将它们分为光线能透过的、光线被完全挡住的，以及介于两者之间的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Vibrations & Sound
topics.description: Understand that vibrating materials can make sound, and that sound can make materials vibrate
evidence: Describe that sounds are made when objects vibrate (move back and forth quickly)
Give at least three examples of vibrating objects making sound (drum skin, guitar string, voice box)
Demonstrate that sound can cause objects to vibrate (e.g. rice on a drum jumps when you shout near it)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} pluck a rubber band and explain that the vibrating band makes the sound, and then hold a ruler on a speaker and see it shake from the music?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解振动的物体可以产生声音，并且声音也能使物体产生振动
evidenceZh: 描述声音是在物体振动（快速来回运动）时产生的
举出至少三个振动物体发声的例子（鼓皮、吉他弦、声带）
演示声音能引起物体振动（例如，对着鼓大喊时，鼓面上的米粒会跳动）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否拨动橡皮筋并解释振动的橡皮筋产生了声音，然后将尺子放在扬声器上观察它随着音乐振动？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How Shadows Form
topics.description: Recognise that shadows are formed when light from a source is blocked by an opaque object, and find patterns in how shadow size changes
evidence: Explain that a shadow forms because an opaque object blocks light from reaching a surface
Describe the pattern: shadow gets larger when object moves closer to the light source
Predict the shape and relative size of a shadow given the position of light and object
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} make shadow puppets and explain why the shadow gets bigger when you move the puppet closer to the torch?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识到当光源发出的光被不透明物体（opaque object）挡住时就会形成影子，并找出影子大小变化的规律。
evidenceZh: 解释影子的形成是因为不透明物体（opaque object）挡住了光线，使其无法到达表面
描述规律：当物体靠近光源时，影子会变大
根据光源和物体的位置，预测影子的形状和相对大小（relative size）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能制作手影并解释为什么把手偶靠近手电筒（torch）时影子会变大吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Protecting Eyes from Sunlight
topics.description: Recognise that light from the sun can be dangerous and that there are ways to protect eyes
evidence: State that looking directly at the sun can damage eyes permanently
Name at least two ways to protect eyes from bright sunlight (sunglasses, hat, shade)
Explain that the sun is an extremely bright light source unlike any artificial light
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know why you should never look directly at the sun and what you can do to protect your eyes on bright days?
topics.nameZh: 保护眼睛免受阳光伤害
topics.descriptionZh: 认识到太阳光可能具有危险性，并了解保护眼睛的方法
evidenceZh: 说明直视太阳会对眼睛造成永久性伤害
说出至少两种在强烈阳光下保护眼睛的方法（如戴太阳镜、戴帽子、待在阴凉处）
解释太阳是一个极其明亮的光源，与任何人造光源都不同
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 是否知道为什么绝对不能直视太阳，以及在阳光强烈的日子里可以采取哪些措施来保护眼睛？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Reflecting Light
topics.description: Notice that light is reflected from surfaces, and that shiny smooth surfaces reflect light best
evidence: Explain that light bounces off surfaces, which is called reflection
Identify that smooth, shiny surfaces (mirrors, still water) reflect light best
Give everyday examples of reflection: mirror, puddle, polished floor
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why they can see themselves in a mirror or a shiny spoon, and why a rough wall doesn't reflect light the same way?
topics.descriptionZh: 注意到光会从物体表面反射（reflection）回来，并且光滑、闪亮的表面反射光的效果最好。
evidenceZh: 解释光从表面反弹回来的现象，这被称为反射（reflection）
识别出光滑、闪亮的表面（如镜子、平静的水面）反射光的效果最好
举出日常生活中反射现象的例子：镜子、水坑、抛光的地板
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么他们能在镜子或闪亮的勺子中看到自己，以及为什么粗糙的墙壁不能以同样的方式反射光？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Pitch of Sounds
topics.description: Find patterns between the pitch of a sound and features of the object that produced it
evidence: Describe the pattern: shorter/thinner/tighter objects produce higher-pitched sounds
Demonstrate pitch changes using at least one instrument or everyday object
Explain pitch as how high or low a sound is, determined by how fast the object vibrates
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a short guitar string makes a higher sound than a long one, or why a small drum sounds higher than a big one?
topics.descriptionZh: 发现声音的音高与发声物体特征之间的规律
evidenceZh: 描述规律：较短、较细或较紧的物体会产生音高（higher-pitched）更高的声音
使用至少一种乐器或日常物品演示音高的变化
解释音高是指声音的高低，由物体振动的快慢（频率/frequency）决定
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释为什么短的吉他弦比长的吉他弦发出的声音音高更高，或者为什么小鼓的声音比大鼓的声音音高更高？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Sound Fading with Distance
topics.description: Recognise that sounds get fainter as the distance from the sound source increases
evidence: State that sound gets quieter as distance from the source increases
Describe an observation or investigation demonstrating this pattern
Explain that vibrations spread out and get weaker as they travel further from the source
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a friend's voice gets harder to hear the further away they walk?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识到随着与声源距离的增加，声音会变得越来越微弱
evidenceZh: 说明随着与声源距离的增加，声音会变小
描述能证明这一规律的观察或探究活动
解释振动（vibrations）在远离声源传播时会扩散并减弱
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释为什么朋友走得越远，他们的声音就越难听清吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Sound Travels Through Materials
topics.description: Recognise that vibrations from sounds travel through a medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to the ear
evidence: Explain that sound vibrations need a material (medium) to travel through — they can't travel in a vacuum
Give examples of sound travelling through different media: air, water, solid objects
Describe how a string telephone works: voice vibrates the cup, vibrations travel along the string to the other cup
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why you can hear someone talking through a wall, and why sound travels through water when you're swimming underwater?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识到声音的振动需要通过介质（固体、液体或气体）传播到耳朵里。
evidenceZh: 解释声音的振动需要物质（介质）才能传播——它们无法在真空中传播
举例说明声音在不同介质中的传播：空气、水和固体物体
描述‘土电话’（线绳电话）的工作原理：说话声使杯子振动，振动顺着线绳传到另一个杯子
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释为什么隔着墙能听到别人说话，以及在水下游泳时为什么能听到水里的声音？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Volume & Vibrations
topics.description: Find patterns between the volume of a sound and the strength of the vibrations that produced it
evidence: Describe the pattern: stronger vibrations (larger movements) produce louder sounds
Demonstrate volume changes by varying the force applied to a sound-making object
Explain volume as how loud or quiet a sound is, determined by the size of vibrations
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why hitting a drum harder makes a louder sound, and what's happening to the drum skin differently?
topics.descriptionZh: 探索声音的音量与产生声音的振动强度之间的规律
evidenceZh: 描述规律：更强的振动（更大的运动幅度）会产生更响的声音
通过改变对发声物体施加的力来演示音量的变化
解释音量是指声音的响亮或轻柔程度，由振动的幅度大小决定
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释为什么更用力地敲鼓会产生更响的声音，以及鼓皮发生了什么不同的变化？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How We See Objects
topics.description: Develop a model to describe that light reflecting from objects and entering the eye allows objects to be seen
evidence: Draw a diagram showing light source → light hits object → reflects into eye
Explain that we see objects because reflected light enters our eyes, not because our eyes send out light
Use this model to explain why we can't see in total darkness (no light to reflect)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw a diagram showing how light bounces off a book and enters your eye, which is how you actually see the book?
topics.nameZh: 我们是怎样看到物体的
topics.descriptionZh: 建立模型，描述光线从物体反射并进入眼睛，从而使我们能够看到物体的过程。
evidenceZh: 绘制图表展示：光源 → 光线照射到物体 → 反射进入眼睛
解释我们能看见物体是因为反射光进入了我们的眼睛，而不是因为眼睛发出了光
运用该模型解释为什么我们在完全黑暗中看不见物体（因为没有光可以反射）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否绘制一幅图表，展示光线是如何从书本上反射并进入你的眼睛的，从而说明你是如何实际看到这本书的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Patterns & Codes for Information
topics.description: Generate and compare multiple solutions that use patterns to transfer information, such as codes and signals
evidence: Describe at least two systems that use patterns of light or sound to transfer information (e.g. Morse code, semaphore, drum signals)
Design a simple code using light or sound patterns to send a message
Compare the advantages and disadvantages of different information transfer methods
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} come up with different ways to send a secret message using patterns of light or sound, like Morse code or drum beats?
topics.descriptionZh: 生成并比较多种利用模式（如密码和信号）来传递信息的解决方案
evidenceZh: 描述至少两种利用光或声音模式来传递信息的系统（例如莫尔斯电码、旗语、鼓声信号）
设计一种简单的密码，利用光或声音模式来发送信息
比较不同信息传递方法的优缺点
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否想出不同的方法，利用光或声音的模式（如莫尔斯电码或鼓声）来发送秘密信息？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Wave Behaviour Vocabulary
topics.description: Use technical vocabulary for wave behaviour — refraction, absorption, reflection, scattering, amplitude, frequency, wavelength, echo, spectrum, angle of incidence, angle of reflection — and apply these when explaining how light and sound travel and interact with different materials
evidence: Use 'refraction' correctly to explain why a straw appears bent in a glass of water
Distinguish 'reflection' from 'refraction' using the correct definitions
Explain what an echo is using the vocabulary of sound reflection correctly
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a straw looks bent in a glass of water using a proper science word — or tell you what's actually happening when you hear an echo?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用波动行为的专业词汇——折射（refraction）、吸收（absorption）、反射（reflection）、散射（scattering）、振幅（amplitude）、频率（frequency）、波长（wavelength）、回声（echo）、光谱（spectrum）、入射角（angle of incidence）、反射角（angle of reflection）——并在解释光和声音如何传播以及与不同材料相互作用时应用这些词汇。
evidenceZh: 正确使用“折射”（refraction）来解释为什么水中的吸管看起来是弯曲的
使用正确的定义来区分“反射”（reflection）和“折射”（refraction）
正确使用声音反射（sound reflection）的词汇来解释什么是回声（echo）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否使用恰当的科学词汇解释为什么水中的吸管看起来是弯曲的——或者告诉你听到回声时实际发生了什么？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Waves & How They Move
topics.description: Develop a model of waves to describe patterns in terms of amplitude and wavelength, and understand that waves can cause objects to move
evidence: Describe a wave using the terms amplitude (height) and wavelength (distance between peaks)
Demonstrate that larger amplitude means more energy (bigger waves move objects more)
Model wave patterns using a slinky, rope, or water and describe what they observe
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} use a slinky or rope to show how waves work, and explain that bigger waves have more energy and can move things more?
topics.descriptionZh: 建立波的模型来描述其在振幅（amplitude）和波长（wavelength）方面的规律，并理解波可以引起物体的运动。
evidenceZh: 使用振幅（amplitude，即高度）和波长（wavelength，即波峰之间的距离）等术语来描述波
证明更大的振幅意味着更多的能量（更大的波能使物体移动得更多）
使用弹簧玩具（slinky）、绳子或水来模拟波的模式，并描述其观察到的现象
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否使用弹簧玩具（slinky）或绳子来展示波是如何运作的，并解释更大的波具有更多的能量且能更明显地移动物体？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Light Travels in Straight Lines
topics.description: Recognise that light appears to travel in straight lines and use this to explain how we see objects and why shadows have the same shape as the objects that cast them
evidence: State and demonstrate that light travels in straight lines (e.g. can't see around corners, laser pointer)
Use straight-line light to explain why shadows have the same outline shape as the object
Draw ray diagrams showing light travelling from source, being blocked by object, creating shadow on screen
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a shadow of a hand looks like a hand shape, using the idea that light travels in straight lines?
topics.descriptionZh: 认识光沿直线传播的现象，并运用这一原理解释我们是如何看见物体的，以及为什么影子的形状与投射它的物体形状相同。
evidenceZh: 陈述并证明光沿直线传播（例如：无法看到拐角后的物体、使用激光笔演示）
运用光沿直线传播的原理，解释为什么影子的轮廓形状与物体相同
绘制光路图 (ray diagrams)，展示光从光源发出、被物体阻挡并在屏幕上形成影子的过程
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否运用光沿直线传播的原理，解释为什么手的影子看起来是手的形状？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: How Sound Waves Travel
topics.description: Explain that sound is produced by vibrating objects and travels as a longitudinal pressure wave through solids, liquids, and gases; describe reflection of sound (echoes) and absorption; explain why sound cannot travel through a vacuum
evidence: Explains how a vibrating object creates regions of compression and rarefaction in air
Explains why sound travels fastest in solids and cannot travel in a vacuum
Describes how an echo is produced and gives a practical application (sonar, ultrasound)
Explains what sound absorption means and why soft furnishings reduce echoes
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard an echo in a large empty hall, could they explain what causes the echo, why the same sound in a carpeted living room doesn’t echo, and what would happen to sound in outer space?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释声音是由物体振动产生的，并作为纵波（纵向压力波）在固体、液体和气体中传播；描述声音的反射（回声）和吸收现象；解释为什么声音不能在真空中传播。
evidenceZh: 解释振动的物体如何在空气中产生密部（压缩）和疏部（稀疏）的区域
解释为什么声音在固体中传播速度最快，以及在真空中无法传播
描述回声是如何产生的，并列举实际应用（声呐、超声波）
解释声音吸收（吸声）的含义，以及为什么柔软的家具和装饰能减少回声
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}在一个空旷的大厅里听到了回声，他们能解释回声是如何产生的，为什么同样的声音在铺了地毯的客厅里不会产生回声，以及声音在外太空中会怎样吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Reflection & Refraction
topics.description: State the law of reflection (angle of incidence = angle of reflection) and explain refraction as the change in speed and direction when light crosses a boundary between two media; apply ray diagrams for plane mirrors and refracting surfaces
evidence: States the law of reflection and applies it to draw a reflected ray correctly
Draws a ray diagram for a plane mirror showing a virtual image
Explains why a pencil looks bent in a glass of water using refraction
Explains qualitatively why light bends towards the normal when entering a denser medium
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} put a straw in a glass of water and it looked bent at the surface, could they explain why that happens — drawing a diagram to show the path of light at the water’s surface?
topics.descriptionZh: 阐述反射定律（入射角等于反射角），并解释折射是光穿过两种介质交界面时速度和方向发生改变的现象；运用光线图（ray diagrams）绘制平面镜和折射表面的光路。
evidenceZh: 阐述反射定律并正确应用该定律绘制反射光线
绘制平面镜的光线图（ray diagram），展示虚像（virtual image）的形成
运用折射原理解释为什么铅笔在水杯中看起来是弯折的
定性解释为什么光进入较密介质时会向法线（normal）偏折
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 把一根吸管放进水杯里，发现它在水面处看起来弯折了，他们能解释这是为什么吗——能否画一张图来展示光在水面处的传播路径？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Wave Properties & Types
topics.description: Describe waves in terms of amplitude, wavelength, frequency, and wave speed; distinguish transverse waves (oscillation perpendicular to direction of travel) from longitudinal waves (oscillation parallel); and use the wave equation v = fλ
evidence: Labels a wave diagram with amplitude, wavelength, crest, and trough
Distinguishes transverse and longitudinal waves and gives an example of each
Uses v = fλ to calculate wave speed, frequency, or wavelength given the other two
Explains what happens to wavelength if frequency increases while wave speed stays constant
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked to describe a wave and how fast it travels, could they sketch one, label the wavelength and amplitude, and use the wave equation to work out speed from the frequency and wavelength?
topics.nameZh: 波的性质与类型 (Wave Properties & Types)
topics.descriptionZh: 用振幅 (amplitude)、波长 (wavelength)、频率 (frequency) 和波速 (wave speed) 来描述波；区分横波 (transverse waves，振动方向垂直于传播方向) 和纵波 (longitudinal waves，振动方向平行于传播方向)；并使用波动方程 (wave equation) v = fλ
evidenceZh: 在波图上标注振幅 (amplitude)、波长 (wavelength)、波峰 (crest) 和波谷 (trough)
区分横波 (transverse waves) 和纵波 (longitudinal waves)，并分别举例说明
使用 v = fλ 公式，在已知其中两个量的情况下计算波速 (wave speed)、频率 (frequency) 或波长 (wavelength)
解释在波速 (wave speed) 保持不变的情况下，如果频率 (frequency) 增加，波长 (wavelength) 会发生什么变化
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果要求 {{name}} 描述一种波及其传播速度，他们能否画出一个波，标注出波长 (wavelength) 和振幅 (amplitude)，并使用波动方程 (wave equation) 根据频率 (frequency) 和波长计算出波速？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: White Light & Colour
topics.description: Explain that white light is a mixture of all visible colours (ROYGBIV), describe dispersion through a prism, explain why objects appear coloured (selective reflection and absorption of wavelengths), and describe colour mixing with filters
evidence: Lists the colours of the visible spectrum in order of increasing frequency
Explains why a prism disperses white light into a spectrum
Explains why a red object looks red under white light but black under blue light
Predicts the colour of an object seen through a colour filter
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} shone white light through a prism, could they explain why a rainbow of colours appears — and then predict what colour a blue jumper would look under red light and why?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释白光是所有可见光颜色的混合（红橙黄绿蓝靛紫，ROYGBIV），描述光通过三棱镜的色散（dispersion），解释物体呈现颜色的原因（对波长的选择性反射和吸收 selective reflection and absorption），并描述使用滤光片进行颜色混合（colour mixing）的原理。
evidenceZh: 按频率递增的顺序列出可见光谱的颜色
解释三棱镜为何能将白光色散（dispersion）成光谱
解释为什么红色物体在白光下看起来是红色的，而在蓝光下看起来是黑色的
预测透过彩色滤光片观察到的物体颜色
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 让白光穿过三棱镜，他们能解释为什么会出现彩虹般的颜色吗——然后预测一件蓝色毛衣在红光下会呈现什么颜色以及为什么？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Drawing Ray Diagrams
topics.description: Draw ray diagrams to show reflection at a plane mirror (angle of incidence = angle of reflection) and refraction at a boundary between media; use ray diagrams to locate images and explain how lenses and mirrors work
evidence: Draw a ray diagram for a plane mirror showing the incident ray, normal, reflected ray, and virtual image
Draw a ray diagram showing a ray bending towards the normal when passing from air into glass
Use a ray diagram to locate the image formed by a convex lens and describe whether it is real or virtual
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw a diagram showing how a ray of light bounces off a mirror or bends when it passes from air into glass — labelling the angles correctly?
topics.descriptionZh: 绘制光路图以展示平面镜反射（入射角=反射角）和介质交界面的折射现象；利用光路图确定像的位置，并解释透镜和面镜的工作原理。
evidenceZh: 绘制平面镜的光路图，标注入射光线、法线、反射光线和虚像
绘制光路图，展示光线从空气进入玻璃时向法线偏折的现象
使用光路图确定凸透镜所成像的位置，并描述该像是实像还是虚像
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否绘制一张图，展示光线如何从镜面反射或在从空气进入玻璃时发生偏折，并正确标注各个角度？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Ray Diagrams & Images
topics.description: Construct ray diagrams to show the formation of images by plane mirrors and converging lenses, identifying whether images are real or virtual, magnified or diminished, upright or inverted
evidence: Draws an accurate ray diagram for a plane mirror showing a virtual, upright, same-size image
Draws a ray diagram for a converging lens to show image formation
Uses a ray diagram to determine whether the image is real or virtual and which side of the lens it forms
Applies ray diagram knowledge to explain how glasses, cameras, or projectors work
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked to show on a diagram where their reflection appears to be when they look in a mirror, could they draw the correct ray paths and explain whether the image is real or virtual — and where it actually appears to be located?
topics.nameZh: 光线图与成像 (Ray Diagrams & Images)
topics.descriptionZh: 绘制光线图 (ray diagrams) 以展示平面镜 (plane mirrors) 和会聚透镜 (converging lenses) 的成像过程，并识别图像是实像 (real image) 还是虚像 (virtual image)、放大 (magnified) 还是缩小 (diminished)、正立 (upright) 还是倒立 (inverted)。
evidenceZh: 绘制准确的平面镜光线图，展示虚像 (virtual image)、正立 (upright)、等大 (same-size) 的成像
绘制会聚透镜 (converging lens) 的光线图以展示成像过程
使用光线图判断图像是实像 (real image) 还是虚像 (virtual image)，以及它形成在透镜的哪一侧
运用光线图知识解释眼镜 (glasses)、相机 (cameras) 或投影仪 (projectors) 的工作原理
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果让 {{name}} 在图上标出他们照镜子时看到自己影像的位置，他们能画出正确的光路 (ray paths) 并解释这个像是实像 (real image) 还是虚像 (virtual image) 吗？还能说明它实际看起来在哪个位置吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Electromagnetic Spectrum
topics.description: Describe the full electromagnetic spectrum from radio waves to gamma rays, in order of increasing frequency and energy; explain that all EM waves travel at the same speed in a vacuum; and describe the uses and hazards of different regions
evidence: Lists the seven regions of the EM spectrum in order of increasing frequency
States that all EM waves travel at 3 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuum
Gives at least one use and one hazard for each region of the spectrum
Explains why some EM waves are more dangerous to living tissue than others (linked to frequency/energy)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard about microwaves, X-rays, and visible light all being part of the same family, could they explain what makes them different from each other and name one useful application and one risk for each?
topics.descriptionZh: 按频率和能量递增的顺序，描述从无线电波到伽马射线的完整电磁波谱（Electromagnetic Spectrum）；解释所有电磁波在真空中以相同的速度传播；并描述不同波段的用途和危害。
evidenceZh: 按频率递增的顺序列出电磁波谱的七个区域
说明所有电磁波在真空中的传播速度为 3 × 10⁸ m/s
为电磁波谱的每个区域至少提供一个用途和一个危害
解释为什么某些电磁波比其他电磁波对活体组织更危险（与频率/能量有关）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 听说微波（Microwaves）、X射线（X-rays）和可见光（Visible light）都属于同一个家族，他们能解释一下它们之间有什么不同，并分别说出每种电磁波的一个有用应用和一个风险吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Waves & Different Materials
topics.description: Explain how waves can be absorbed, transmitted, or reflected by different materials, and apply these interactions to explain colour perception, sight, communication technologies, and the effects of different surfaces on wave behaviour
evidence: Explains the difference between absorption, transmission, and reflection of waves
Uses the three interactions to explain how we see coloured objects
Explains how radio waves, visible light, and infrared are used in different communication technologies
Describes how the properties of a surface (colour, texture, material) determine how it interacts with radiation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was wearing a black t-shirt on a sunny day and a friend was wearing white, could they explain using wave interactions why the black shirt gets hotter — and which properties of materials determine how they absorb or reflect radiation?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释波是如何被不同材料吸收（absorption）、透射（transmission）或反射（reflection）的，并利用这些相互作用来解释颜色感知、视觉原理、通信技术，以及不同表面是如何影响波的行为的。
evidenceZh: 解释波的吸收（absorption）、透射（transmission）和反射（reflection）之间的区别。
运用这三种相互作用来解释我们是如何看到彩色物体的。
解释无线电波（radio waves）、可见光（visible light）和红外线（infrared）是如何应用于不同通信技术的。
描述物体表面的特性（颜色、纹理、材质）是如何决定它与辐射（radiation）相互作用方式的。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在晴朗的日子里穿着一件黑色T恤，而他的朋友穿着白色T恤，他们能否用波的相互作用来解释为什么黑T恤会更热——并且说出材料的哪些特性决定了它们吸收或反射辐射（radiation）的能力？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Dressing for the Weather
topics.description: Choose appropriate clothing and equipment for different weather conditions — coat and umbrella for rain, sun hat and sunscreen for hot sun, warm layers for cold — understanding that weather affects what we do and how we prepare each day
evidence: Select appropriate clothing for at least three different weather conditions
Explain why certain clothes or equipment are needed for specific weather
Describe how weather affects daily activities like playtime, walking to school, or outdoor events
topics.assessmentPrompt: Before going outside, can {{name}} check the weather and choose the right clothes — like grabbing a raincoat if it's cloudy or a sun hat if it's hot?
topics.descriptionZh: 为不同的天气状况选择合适的衣物和装备——下雨天穿外套打雨伞，烈日下戴太阳帽涂防晒霜，寒冷时穿保暖的层叠衣物——理解天气如何影响我们的日常活动以及每天应如何做好准备
evidenceZh: 能为至少三种不同的天气状况选择合适的衣物
能解释为什么在特定天气下需要某些衣物或装备
能描述天气如何影响日常活动，如玩耍时间、步行上学或户外活动
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在出门前，{{name}}能查看天气并选择正确的衣服吗——比如阴天时拿上雨衣，或者天气热时戴上太阳帽？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Rain & Puddles
topics.description: Know that rain falls from clouds in the sky, that puddles disappear because water goes back into the air, and that this is part of how water moves around — up into the sky and back down again
evidence: State that rain falls from clouds
Explain that puddles disappear because the water goes into the air
Describe the basic idea that water goes up and comes back down in a repeating process
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} notices a puddle has disappeared on a sunny afternoon, can they explain that the water went up into the air, and that it will come back down again as rain from a cloud?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解雨水从天空的云层中落下，水坑消失是因为水回到了空气中，并且这是水循环（water cycle）的一部分——水升上天空，然后再降落下来。
evidenceZh: 说明雨水从云层中落下
解释水坑消失是因为水进入了空气中
描述水升上去又降下来这一循环过程（repeating process）的基本概念
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在一个晴朗的下午注意到一个水坑消失了，他们能解释水升到了空气中，并且它会再次变成雨从云层中降落下来吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Seasons & Weather Patterns
topics.description: Know that weather changes with the seasons — spring brings rain and new growth, summer is warmest with long days, autumn brings cooling and falling leaves, winter is coldest with short days — and that this pattern repeats every year
evidence: Name the four seasons and describe typical weather for each
Explain that days are longer in summer and shorter in winter
State that the seasonal pattern repeats every year
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you what kind of weather to expect in each season and explain that summer has the longest days while winter has the shortest?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解天气会随季节变化：春天带来春雨和万物复苏，夏天最温暖且白昼最长，秋天天气转凉且落叶纷飞，冬天最寒冷且白昼最短，并且这种季节规律每年都会循环往复。
evidenceZh: 说出四季的名称并描述每个季节的典型天气
解释夏天白昼较长而冬天白昼较短
说明季节规律每年都会重复
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能告诉你每个季节会有怎样的天气，并解释夏天白昼最长而冬天白昼最短吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Storm Safety
topics.description: Know basic storm safety: during thunder and lightning, go indoors or into a car, stay away from trees and water; understand that storms can be frightening but there are ways to stay safe
evidence: State at least two safety rules for thunderstorms
Explain why going indoors is the safest option during lightning
Describe that storms are natural events and there are ways to stay safe
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard thunder while playing outside, would they know to come inside straight away and could they explain why standing under a tree isn't safe during a lightning storm?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解基本的风暴安全知识：在雷雨天气，应进入室内或车内，远离树木和水域；明白风暴虽然令人害怕，但有很多方法可以保持安全。
evidenceZh: 说出至少两条雷暴（thunderstorm）天气的安全规则
解释为什么在雷电（lightning）天气进入室内是最安全的选择
说明风暴是自然现象，并且有方法可以保持安全
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在外面玩耍时听到雷声，他们知道立刻回到室内吗？他们能解释为什么在雷暴天气站在树下不安全吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Temperature & Thermometers
topics.description: Understand temperature as how hot or cold something is, that a thermometer measures temperature, and use words like hot, warm, cool, and cold to describe how the air feels on different days
evidence: Explain that temperature describes how hot or cold something is
Identify a thermometer as the tool used to measure temperature
Use words like hot, warm, cool, and cold appropriately to describe air temperature
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a thermometer outside, could they explain that it tells us how hot or cold the air is, and describe today as hot, warm, cool, or cold?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解温度是指物体的冷热程度，知道温度计是用来测量温度的工具，并能使用“热”、“温暖”、“凉爽”和“冷”等词汇来描述不同天气里空气的冷热感觉。
evidenceZh: 解释温度是用来描述物体冷热程度的
辨认出温度计是用于测量温度的工具
能够恰当地使用“热”、“温暖”、“凉爽”和“冷”等词汇来描述气温
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在外面看到温度计，他们能否解释这是用来告诉我们空气有多热或多冷的，并能用“热”、“温暖”、“凉爽”或“冷”来描述今天的天气？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Types of Weather
topics.description: Identify and describe different types of weather — sunny, rainy, windy, snowy, cloudy, foggy, stormy — and describe what the weather is like today using simple vocabulary
evidence: Name at least five types of weather
Describe today's weather accurately using appropriate vocabulary
Match weather types to simple pictures or symbols
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} looks out the window in the morning, can they describe the weather using words like sunny, cloudy, rainy, or windy, and say whether it's a nice day or a wet day?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别并描述不同类型的天气——晴天、雨天、刮风、下雪、多云、有雾、暴风雨，并使用简单的词汇描述今天的天气情况。
evidenceZh: 说出至少五种天气类型
使用恰当的词汇准确描述今天的天气
将天气类型与简单的图片或符号相匹配
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当{{name}}早上向窗外望去时，他们能用晴天、多云、下雨或刮风等词语来描述天气，并说出今天是个好天气还是阴雨天吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Weather Forecasting & Safety
topics.description: Ask questions to obtain information about the purpose of weather forecasting and how people prepare for and respond to severe weather
evidence: Explain that weather forecasts help people plan and stay safe
Describe how people prepare for at least two types of severe weather (storm, flood, heat wave, blizzard)
Ask relevant questions about weather hazards and find answers from appropriate sources
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why we check the weather forecast and what people do to get ready for a big storm or very hot weather?
topics.descriptionZh: 通过提问获取有关天气预报的目的，以及人们如何准备和应对恶劣天气的信息。
evidenceZh: 解释天气预报如何帮助人们进行计划并保持安全。
描述人们如何为至少两种恶劣天气（风暴、洪水、热浪、暴风雪）做准备。
提出有关天气灾害的相关问题，并从合适的渠道寻找答案。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释我们为什么要查看天气预报，以及人们为应对大风暴或极热天气会做哪些准备？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: What Is Wind?
topics.description: Know that wind is moving air, that it can be gentle (a breeze) or very strong (a gale), and that wind can move things like leaves, kites, flags, and even push people
evidence: Define wind as air that is moving
Describe the difference between a gentle breeze and a strong wind
Give examples of things that wind can move or affect
topics.assessmentPrompt: On a windy day, can {{name}} explain that wind is air moving, point out things being blown around, and describe whether it's a gentle breeze or a strong gust?
topics.descriptionZh: 知道风是流动的空气，它既可以很轻柔（微风），也可以很强烈（狂风），并且风能够吹动树叶、风筝、旗帜等物体，甚至能推动人。
evidenceZh: 将风定义为流动的空气
描述轻柔的微风和强烈的狂风之间的区别
举例说明风能够吹动或影响的事物
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在刮风的日子里，{{name}} 能否解释风是流动的空气，指出被风吹动的物体，并描述当时是轻柔的微风还是强烈的阵风？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Cloud Types
topics.description: Identify the three main cloud types — cumulus (fluffy, fair weather), stratus (flat layers, overcast or drizzle), and cirrus (thin wisps, high up) — and understand that clouds form when water vapour in the air cools and condenses into tiny droplets
evidence: Name and describe the three main cloud types: cumulus, stratus, cirrus
Explain that clouds form when water vapour cools and condenses
Use cloud type to make a simple prediction about the weather
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked up at the sky, could they identify whether the clouds are fluffy cumulus, flat stratus, or wispy cirrus, and explain that clouds are made of tiny water droplets?
topics.descriptionZh: 识别三种主要的云类型——积云（cumulus，蓬松，预示晴天）、层云（stratus，呈平坦层状，预示阴天或毛毛雨）和卷云（cirrus，高空中纤细的丝缕）——并理解云是空气中的水蒸气（water vapour）冷却并凝结成小水滴时形成的。
evidenceZh: 说出并描述三种主要的云类型：积云（cumulus）、层云（stratus）、卷云（cirrus）
解释云是在水蒸气（water vapour）冷却并凝结（condenses）时形成的
利用云的类型对天气做出简单的预测
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}抬头看天空，他们能分辨出云是蓬松的积云（cumulus）、平坦的层云（stratus）还是丝缕状的卷云（cirrus），并解释云是由小水滴组成的吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Geography & Local Weather
topics.description: Know that different places around the world have very different typical weather — tropical places are hot and wet all year, deserts are very dry, polar regions are freezing cold — and that geography (distance from the equator, altitude, nearness to the sea) affects local weather
evidence: Describe typical weather in at least three different climate types
Explain that places near the equator tend to be hotter
Name at least one factor that affects a place's weather besides latitude
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared weather in a tropical rainforest, a desert, and the Arctic, could they describe how different each is and explain why — like distance from the equator?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解世界各地的典型天气差异很大——热带地区全年炎热潮湿，沙漠地区非常干燥，极地地区极其寒冷——并且地理因素（距赤道 (equator) 的距离、海拔 (altitude)、离海的远近）会影响当地天气。
evidenceZh: 描述至少三种不同气候类型的典型天气
解释靠近赤道 (equator) 的地方往往更热
说出至少一个除纬度 (latitude) 外影响某地天气的因素
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 比较热带雨林、沙漠和北极的天气，他们能否描述这三地的天气有何不同并解释原因——比如距离赤道 (equator) 的远近？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Water Cycle
topics.description: Understand the water cycle: the Sun heats water in oceans and lakes causing it to evaporate into water vapour, the vapour rises and cools to form clouds (condensation), and water falls back to Earth as rain, snow, or hail (precipitation) — then the cycle repeats
evidence: Name the three main stages: evaporation, condensation, precipitation
Explain the Sun's role in driving the water cycle
Describe the water cycle as a continuous loop with no beginning or end
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} trace the journey of a raindrop — from the ocean being heated by the Sun, rising as invisible vapour, forming a cloud, and falling back down as rain — and explain it keeps going round and round?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解水循环：太阳加热海洋和湖泊里的水，使其蒸发（evaporation）变成水蒸气；水蒸气上升并冷却形成云朵（凝结，condensation）；接着水以雨、雪或冰雹的形式落回地面（降水，precipitation）——然后这个循环不断重复。
evidenceZh: 说出三个主要阶段：蒸发（evaporation）、凝结（condensation）、降水（precipitation）
解释太阳在驱动水循环中的作用
将水循环描述为一个没有起点和终点的连续循环（continuous loop）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否追踪一滴雨的旅程——从海洋被太阳加热，变成看不见的水蒸气上升，形成云朵，然后再作为雨水落回地面——并解释它是如何不断循环往复的？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Thunder & Lightning
topics.description: Know that thunder and lightning happen during thunderstorms: lightning is a giant spark of electricity that forms in clouds, thunder is the sound the lightning makes, and we see lightning before hearing thunder because light travels faster than sound
evidence: Describe lightning as a large electrical discharge in clouds
Explain that thunder is the sound caused by lightning
State that we see lightning before hearing thunder because light travels faster than sound
topics.assessmentPrompt: During a thunderstorm, can {{name}} explain that lightning is electricity in the clouds, thunder is its sound, and that we see the flash before the boom because light is faster than sound?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解雷声和闪电发生在雷暴天气中：闪电是云层中形成的巨大电火花，雷声是闪电发出的声音，我们先看到闪电后听到雷声，因为光传播的速度比声音快（光速大于声速）
evidenceZh: 将闪电描述为云层中的大型放电现象（electrical discharge）
解释雷声是由闪电引起的声音
说明我们先看到闪电后听到雷声，因为光传播的速度比声音快（光速快于声速）
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 在雷暴天气中，{{name}} 能否解释闪电是云层中的电火花，雷声是它发出的声音，并且我们能先看到闪电后听到雷声是因为光速快于声速？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Using Weather Instruments
topics.description: Use weather instruments to measure and record weather data: thermometers for temperature in °C, rain gauges for rainfall, wind vanes for direction, and anemometers for wind speed — and keep a weather diary over time
evidence: Name at least three weather instruments and explain what each measures
Read a thermometer and record the temperature in degrees Celsius
Record weather data in a table or diary over several days
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} had a thermometer, rain gauge, and wind vane at school, could they take daily readings, record them in a table, and spot patterns over a week or month?
topics.descriptionZh: 使用气象仪器测量并记录天气数据：用温度计（thermometer）测量摄氏（°C）温度，用雨量计（rain gauge）测量降雨量，用风向标（wind vane）测量风向，用风速计（anemometer）测量风速——并持续记录天气日记。
evidenceZh: 说出至少三种气象仪器的名称，并解释每种仪器测量什么
读取温度计示数，并以摄氏度（°C）为单位记录温度
在连续几天内将天气数据记录在表格或日记中
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果{{name}}在学校里有温度计、雨量计和风向标，他们能每天进行测量读数，将数据记录在表格中，并在一周或一个月的时间里发现其中的规律吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Weather Forecasting
topics.description: Know that meteorologists are scientists who study and forecast the weather using satellites, radar, weather balloons, and computer models, and that weather forecasts help people plan their activities and prepare for dangerous weather
evidence: Define a meteorologist as a scientist who studies and predicts weather
Name at least three tools meteorologists use
Explain why weather forecasting is useful for safety and daily planning
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what a meteorologist does, name some tools they use like satellites and radar, and describe why weather forecasts are important for keeping people safe?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解气象学家（meteorologists）是利用卫星、雷达、气象探空气球（weather balloons）和计算机模型（computer models）来研究和预测天气的科学家，并且天气预报能帮助人们规划活动并为危险天气做好准备。
evidenceZh: 将气象学家定义为研究和预测天气的科学家
说出至少三种气象学家使用的工具
解释为什么天气预报对安全和日常规划很有用
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释气象学家的工作内容，说出他们使用的一些工具（如卫星和雷达），并描述天气预报对于保障人们安全的重要性？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Weather vs Climate
topics.description: Distinguish between weather and climate: weather is what the atmosphere is doing right now or today (it can change hour to hour), while climate is the typical pattern of weather in a place over many years
evidence: Define weather as short-term atmospheric conditions
Define climate as the long-term pattern of weather in a place
Give an example showing the difference: a cold day doesn't change the overall climate
topics.assessmentPrompt: If someone said 'It's raining today so climate change isn't real,' could {{name}} explain the difference between weather (today's conditions) and climate (patterns over many years)?
topics.descriptionZh: 区分天气和气候：天气是指大气层此刻或今天的状况（它可能每小时都在变化），而气候是指一个地方多年来典型的天气模式
evidenceZh: 将天气定义为短期的大气状况
将气候定义为一个地方长期的天气模式
举例说明两者的区别：一天的寒冷天气并不能改变整体的气候
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果有人说‘今天在下雨，所以气候变化不是真的’，{{name}}能解释一下天气（今天的状况）和气候（多年来的模式）之间的区别吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: What Causes Wind
topics.description: Understand what causes wind: the Sun heats the Earth's surface unevenly, warm air rises because it is lighter, and cooler air rushes in to take its place — this movement of air is wind
evidence: Explain that the Sun heats Earth's surface unevenly
State that warm air rises and cooler air moves in to replace it
Define this air movement as wind
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why wind blows — that the Sun warms some areas more than others, warm air floats upward, and cooler air rushes in to fill the gap?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解风的成因：太阳不均匀地加热地球表面，暖空气因为比较轻而上升，较冷的空气会涌过来填补它的位置——空气的这种流动就形成了风。
evidenceZh: 解释太阳不均匀地加热地球表面
说明暖空气上升，较冷空气会流过来补充
说明这种空气的流动就是风
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释风是怎么吹起来的——即太阳对某些地方的加热比其他地方多，暖空气向上升，而较冷的空气涌过来填补空缺？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Designing for Weather Hazards
topics.description: Make a claim about the merit of a design solution that reduces the impacts of a weather-related hazard such as flooding, wind damage, or extreme temperatures
evidence: Identify a specific weather-related hazard and its impacts on people
Describe at least two design solutions intended to reduce those impacts
Make a claim supported by evidence about which solution is most effective and why
topics.assessmentPrompt: If there's a risk of flooding in a town, can {{name}} evaluate different solutions like building levees, planting trees, or improving drainage and argue which works best?
topics.descriptionZh: 针对能够减轻洪水、风灾或极端气温等气象灾害影响的设计方案的价值提出主张。
evidenceZh: 识别一种特定的气象灾害及其对人类的影响
描述至少两种旨在减轻这些影响的设计方案
提出有证据支持的主张，说明哪种方案最有效及其原因
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果一个小镇面临洪水风险，{{name}}能否评估建造堤坝、植树造林或改善排水系统等不同的解决方案，并论证哪种方案效果最好？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Climate Change Basics
topics.description: Understand the basics of climate change: Earth’s atmosphere traps some of the Sun's heat (the greenhouse effect), burning fossil fuels adds extra greenhouse gases (especially CO₂), this is making Earth gradually warmer, and this warming changes weather patterns, melts ice, and raises sea levels
evidence: Describe the greenhouse effect: the atmosphere traps heat from the Sun
Explain that burning fossil fuels increases CO₂ in the atmosphere
Name at least two consequences of global warming: changing weather patterns, melting ice, rising seas
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the greenhouse effect in simple terms and describe how burning oil, gas, and coal adds extra CO₂ to the air, making Earth warmer and changing weather patterns?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解气候变化的基础知识：地球大气层会困住部分太阳的热量（温室效应），燃烧化石燃料会增加额外的温室气体（特别是二氧化碳(CO₂)），这使得地球逐渐变暖，而这种变暖会改变天气模式、融化冰雪并导致海平面上升。
evidenceZh: 描述温室效应：大气层困住来自太阳的热量
解释燃烧化石燃料会增加大气中的二氧化碳(CO₂)
列举全球变暖的至少两个后果：天气模式改变、冰雪融化、海平面上升
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能用简单的语言解释温室效应，并描述燃烧石油、天然气和煤炭如何向空气中增加额外的二氧化碳(CO₂)，从而使地球变暖并改变天气模式吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Climate Zones
