topics.description: Understand that Earth has distinct climate zones — tropical (hot and wet near the equator), temperate (moderate, with four seasons), polar (freezing cold), arid/desert (very dry), and mountain (cold at high altitude) — and that each zone supports different ecosystems and ways of life
evidence: Name and describe at least four climate zones
Explain what determines which zone a place belongs to (mainly latitude and geography)
Give an example of how a climate zone affects the plants, animals, or people living there
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a world map showing climate zones, could they explain why the Amazon rainforest, the Sahara desert, and the Arctic all have such different weather, plants, and animals?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解地球拥有不同的气候带——热带（赤道附近炎热多雨）、温带（气候温和，四季分明）、寒带/极地（终年严寒）、干旱/沙漠气候（非常干燥）和高山气候（高海拔地区寒冷）——并认识到每个气候带都孕育着不同的生态系统 (ecosystems) 与人类生活方式。
evidenceZh: 说出并描述至少四种气候带
解释决定一个地方属于哪个气候带的主要因素（主要是纬度 (latitude) 和地理特征 (geography)）
举例说明气候带如何影响当地动植物的生长以及人们的生活
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看着一张标有气候带的世界地图，他们能解释为什么亚马逊雨林、撒哈拉沙漠和北极地区的天气、动植物会有这么大的差异吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Extreme Weather Events
topics.description: Know about extreme weather events — hurricanes (spinning storms over warm ocean), tornadoes (violent rotating columns of air), floods, droughts, and blizzards — how they form, where they typically occur, and their effects on people and the environment
evidence: Describe how at least two types of extreme weather form
Explain where hurricanes and tornadoes typically occur and why
Describe the effects of extreme weather on communities and landscapes
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw news about a hurricane, could they explain how it forms over warm ocean water, why it spins, and what makes it so destructive when it reaches land?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解极端天气事件——飓风（在温暖海洋上旋转的风暴）、龙卷风（强烈旋转的空气柱）、洪水、干旱和暴风雪——了解它们是如何形成的，通常发生在哪些地方，以及它们对人类和环境的影响
evidenceZh: 描述至少两种极端天气是如何形成的
解释飓风和龙卷风通常发生在哪里以及为什么会发生在那里
描述极端天气对社区和自然景观的影响
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到关于飓风的新闻，他们能解释它是如何在温暖的海洋水面上形成的，为什么会旋转，以及在登陆时是什么让它具有如此大的破坏力吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Natural resources
topics.description: Obtain and combine information to describe that energy and fuels are derived from natural resources and that their uses affect the environment
evidence: Name natural resources used for energy and fuels (coal, oil, gas, wind, sun, water)
Describe how extracting and using these resources affects the environment (pollution, habitat loss, climate change)
Distinguish between renewable (wind, solar) and non-renewable (fossil fuels) energy sources
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain where petrol, electricity, and gas come from — that they come from natural resources like oil, coal, wind, or sunlight — and how using them affects the environment?
topics.descriptionZh: 收集并整合信息，说明能源和燃料来源于自然资源，并且它们的使用会影响环境。
evidenceZh: 列举用于能源和燃料的自然资源（煤炭 (coal)、石油 (oil)、天然气 (gas)、风 (wind)、太阳 (sun)、水 (water)）
描述开采和使用这些资源如何影响环境（污染 (pollution)、栖息地丧失 (habitat loss)、气候变化 (climate change)）
区分可再生（风能 (wind)、太阳能 (solar)）与不可再生（化石燃料 (fossil fuels)）能源
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释汽油、电力和天然气是从哪里来的——即它们来自石油、煤炭、风或阳光等自然资源——以及使用它们如何影响环境？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Reading Weather Maps
topics.description: Read and interpret weather maps, data tables, and graphs — identifying symbols for sun, rain, wind, and temperature; spotting trends and patterns in weather data over weeks, months, or seasons; and using data to make simple predictions
evidence: Interpret common weather map symbols for temperature, precipitation, and wind
Read a data table or graph of weather data and identify patterns
Use weather data to make a simple prediction about upcoming conditions
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a weather map with symbols on the news, could they read it and explain what weather is coming — and if shown a graph of monthly rainfall, could they spot the wettest and driest months?
topics.descriptionZh: 阅读并解释天气图、数据表 (data tables) 和图表 (graphs)——识别代表太阳、降雨、风和温度的符号；发现数周、数月或数季天气数据中的趋势和规律；并利用数据进行简单的预测。
evidenceZh: 解释天气图中代表温度、降水 (precipitation) 和风的常见符号
阅读天气数据的数据表或图表并识别其中的规律 (patterns)
利用天气数据对未来天气状况进行简单预测
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 在新闻中看到带有符号的天气图，他们能读懂并解释即将到来的天气吗？如果给他们看一张月降雨量图表，他们能找出最湿润和最干燥的月份吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Sun-Driven Weather Systems
topics.description: Understand how the Sun drives weather: the Sun heats Earth's surface unevenly (land heats faster than water, equator gets more heat than poles), creating differences in air pressure that cause wind patterns, ocean currents, and large-scale weather systems
evidence: Explain that the Sun heats land and water at different rates
Describe how temperature differences create air pressure differences that drive wind
Connect uneven heating to large-scale weather patterns
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why coastal areas often have sea breezes and why the equator is hotter than the poles, connecting it all back to the Sun heating Earth unevenly?
topics.descriptionZh: 理解太阳是如何驱动天气的：太阳对地球表面的加热是不均匀的（陆地升温比海洋快，赤道获得的热量比两极多），这会产生气压差（air pressure），进而引发风的模式（wind patterns）、洋流（ocean currents）以及大规模的天气系统。
evidenceZh: 解释太阳加热陆地和海洋的速率不同
描述温度差异如何产生气压差并驱动风的形成
将不均匀加热与大规模天气模式联系起来
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否解释为什么沿海地区经常有海风，以及为什么赤道比两极更热，并将这一切与太阳不均匀地加热地球联系起来？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Atmosphere
topics.description: Know that Earth is surrounded by a layer of air called the atmosphere, that air has weight and exerts pressure, that the atmosphere protects us from harmful radiation and keeps the planet warm enough for life, and that weather happens in the lowest layer (troposphere)
evidence: Define the atmosphere as the layer of air surrounding Earth
State that air has weight and exerts pressure
Explain that weather occurs in the troposphere, the lowest layer of the atmosphere
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that we're surrounded by a blanket of air called the atmosphere, that this air actually has weight and pushes on everything, and that all our weather happens in the lowest layer?
topics.descriptionZh: 了解地球被一层称为大气层（Atmosphere）的空气所包围，知道空气有重量并会产生压力（Pressure），了解大气层能保护我们免受有害辐射，并让地球保持适合生命生存的温度，还要知道天气现象都发生在最底层（对流层，Troposphere）。
evidenceZh: 定义大气层为包围地球的空气层
说明空气有重量并施加压力
解释天气发生在对流层（Troposphere），即大气层的最底层
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能否解释我们周围被一层像毯子一样称为大气层的空气所包围，这些空气实际上是有重量的并且会向各个方向施加压力，而且所有的天气现象都发生在大气层的最底层？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Weather-Resistant Engineering
topics.description: Understand that engineers design buildings, flood defences, and warning systems to protect communities from extreme weather — hurricane-resistant roofs, flood barriers, tornado shelters, and early-warning alert systems — and evaluate the merits of these solutions
evidence: Describe at least two engineering solutions designed to protect against extreme weather
Explain how a specific design feature reduces damage from a weather hazard
Evaluate the advantages and limitations of a weather protection solution
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw pictures of houses on stilts in a flood zone and a tornado shelter, could they explain how each design protects people and discuss whether one solution works better than another?
topics.nameZh: 抗极端天气工程学 (Weather-Resistant Engineering)
topics.descriptionZh: 了解工程师如何设计建筑物、防洪设施和预警系统来保护社区免受极端天气的侵袭——如抗飓风屋顶 (hurricane-resistant roofs)、防洪屏障 (flood barriers)、龙卷风避难所 (tornado shelters) 和早期预警系统 (early-warning alert systems)——并评估这些解决方案的优点。
evidenceZh: 描述至少两种旨在抵御极端天气的工程解决方案 (engineering solutions)
解释特定的设计特征如何减少天气灾害 (weather hazard) 带来的破坏
评估天气防护解决方案的优点和局限性
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 如果 {{name}} 看到洪水泛滥区的高脚屋 (houses on stilts) 和龙卷风避难所 (tornado shelter) 的图片，他们能解释每种设计是如何保护人们的，并讨论其中一种解决方案是否比另一种更有效吗？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Global Wind Patterns
topics.description: Explain that unequal solar heating drives large-scale atmospheric circulation: Hadley cells (0-30°), Ferrel cells (30-60°), and polar cells (60-90°) produce the trade winds, westerlies, and polar easterlies; describe how the Coriolis effect from Earth's rotation deflects winds rightward in the Northern Hemisphere; explain the jet stream as a fast high-altitude wind that steers weather systems; connect jet stream waviness and Arctic amplification to prolonged extreme weather
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the UK tends to get wet weather arriving from the west — what global pattern of winds is steering weather systems, and how does Earth's rotation contribute to this?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释太阳不均匀加热如何驱动大规模大气环流：哈德利环流圈（Hadley cells，0-30°）、费雷尔环流圈（Ferrel cells，30-60°）和极地环流圈（polar cells，60-90°）产生了信风（trade winds）、盛行西风（westerlies）和极地东风（polar easterlies）；描述地球自转产生的科里奥利效应（Coriolis effect）如何使北半球的风向右偏转；解释急流（jet stream）是引导天气系统的高空快速气流；并说明急流的波动与北极放大效应（Arctic amplification）如何导致持续的极端天气。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释为什么英国通常会迎来从西边吹来的湿润天气吗？——是什么全球风带模式在引导天气系统，地球的自转在其中起到了什么作用？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Greenhouse Gas Science
topics.description: Describe the electromagnetic spectrum and distinguish between short-wave solar radiation and long-wave infrared radiation emitted by Earth; explain how greenhouse gas molecules (CO2, CH4, N2O, H2O) absorb and re-emit infrared through molecular vibration while O2 and N2 do not; distinguish the natural greenhouse effect (which makes Earth habitable) from the enhanced greenhouse effect driven by human emissions; evaluate the relative potency of different greenhouse gases
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain, in terms of light and energy, why CO2 in the atmosphere traps heat but nitrogen and oxygen — which make up most of the air — don't? What's physically different about CO2 molecules?
topics.nameZh: 温室气体科学 (Greenhouse Gas Science)
topics.descriptionZh: 描述电磁波谱（electromagnetic spectrum），区分来自太阳的短波辐射（short-wave solar radiation）和地球发射的长波红外辐射（long-wave infrared radiation）；解释温室气体分子（二氧化碳 CO2、甲烷 CH4、一氧化二氮 N2O、水 H2O）如何通过分子振动（molecular vibration）吸收并重新释放红外线，而氧气（O2）和氮气（N2）则不能；区分让地球适宜生存的自然温室效应（natural greenhouse effect）与由人类排放引起的增强温室效应（enhanced greenhouse effect）；评估不同温室气体的相对效力（relative potency）。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}} 能否从光和能量的角度解释一下，为什么大气中的二氧化碳（CO2）能“困住”热量，而占空气大部分的氮气和氧气却做不到？二氧化碳分子在物理结构上有什么特别之处呢？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Hurricanes, Tornadoes & Monsoons
topics.description: Explain how hurricanes form and intensify over warm ocean water (latent heat release, low-pressure spiral); describe tornado formation within supercell thunderstorms; explain monsoon mechanics driven by temperature differences between land and sea; introduce attribution science — how scientists use climate models to calculate whether and by how much climate change increased the probability or intensity of a specific extreme weather event
topics.assessmentPrompt: When scientists say that climate change made a recent hurricane stronger, can {{name}} explain what they actually mean and how scientists figure that out — what kind of calculation lets them link a specific storm to climate change?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释飓风如何在温暖的海洋上空形成并增强（潜热释放、低压螺旋）；描述超级单体雷暴中龙卷风的形成过程；解释由海陆温差驱动的季风机制；引入归因科学（attribution science）——科学家如何使用气候模型来计算气候变化是否以及在多大程度上增加了特定极端天气事件的概率或强度。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: 当科学家说气候变化使最近的飓风变得更强时，{{name}} 能解释他们实际的意思以及科学家是如何得出结论的吗——什么样的计算能让他们将特定的风暴与气候变化联系起来？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Reading Ancient Climate Records
topics.description: Explain how ice cores preserve ancient air bubbles, isotope ratios, and volcanic markers allowing reconstruction of temperature and CO2 going back 800,000 years; describe tree rings, ocean sediment cores, coral skeletons, and pollen records as additional climate proxies; explain how climate models are built and validated against the palaeoclimate record; describe the IPCC process of synthesising scientific evidence across thousands of studies to produce consensus assessments
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how scientists know what the climate was like 500,000 years ago — what kind of 'time capsules' exist in nature that preserve ancient air and temperature records, and how do scientists read them?
topics.descriptionZh: 解释冰芯（ice cores）如何保存古代空气气泡、同位素比例（isotope ratios）和火山标记，从而帮助我们重建过去80万年的温度和二氧化碳（CO2）变化；介绍树木年轮（tree rings）、海洋沉积物岩芯（ocean sediment cores）、珊瑚骨骼（coral skeletons）和花粉记录（pollen records）等额外的气候代用指标（climate proxies）；解释气候模型（climate models）是如何建立并根据古气候记录（palaeoclimate record）进行验证的；描述联合国政府间气候变化专门委员会（IPCC）是如何综合数千项研究的科学证据，最终得出共识性评估的。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}能解释一下科学家是如何知道50万年前的气候状况的吗——大自然中存在哪些保存古代空气和温度记录的“时间胶囊”，科学家又是如何读取它们的呢？

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Net Zero & Energy Transition
topics.description: Evaluate the energy transition required to reach net zero: renewable energy scaling, electrification of transport and heat, green hydrogen; describe carbon capture and storage (CCS) and direct air capture (DAC); introduce proposed solar radiation management techniques (stratospheric aerosol injection, marine cloud brightening) and their potential risks and governance challenges; critically evaluate the role of individual behaviour change versus systemic policy in reducing emissions
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} heard of geoengineering? Can they describe one proposal for deliberately cooling the Earth and explain one potential risk of attempting it — and say whether they think individuals or governments bear more responsibility for tackling climate change?
topics.descriptionZh: 评估实现净零排放所需的能源转型：可再生能源规模化、交通和供暖电气化、绿氢；描述碳捕集与封存 (CCS) 和直接空气捕集 (DAC)；介绍提出的太阳辐射管理技术（平流层气溶胶注入、海洋云增亮）及其潜在风险与治理挑战；批判性地评估个人行为改变与系统性政策在减少排放方面的作用。
topics.assessmentPromptZh: {{name}}听说过地球工程 (geoengineering) 吗？他们能描述一项故意让地球降温的提案并解释尝试该提案的一个潜在风险吗——并说明他们认为个人还是政府在应对气候变化方面承担更多责任？
